# BIBLE-ASD-STE100

**The Holy Bible in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document | BIBLE-ASD-STE100 |
| Revision | 1.0 |
| Source text | King James Version (1769), public domain |
| Scope | 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,102 verses |
| Numbering | KJV chapter and verse numbers |

## 1 Scope

This document gives the full text of the Bible in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Each verse is a new rendering of the meaning of the KJV verse with the same number.

## 2 Conformance

- Sentences: max 25 words (descriptive), max 20 words (instructions).
- Verbs: simple present, simple past, simple future only. Active voice. No -ing verb forms.
- Modal verbs: can, could, must, will only.
- Technical names: proper names and religious terms with no STE equivalent (for example covenant, altar, Sabbath).

Grammar rules were checked by automated pattern rules. Vocabulary was not checked against the official ASD-STE100 dictionary. This document is not certified by, affiliated with, or endorsed by ASD.

# Genesis

## Chapter 1

**1** At the start, God made the heavens and the earth.

**2** The earth had no shape and it was empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep water. The Spirit of God moved above the water.

**3** God said, "Let there be light." Then there was light.

**4** God saw that the light was good. God divided the light from the darkness.

**5** God gave the light the name "day." He gave the darkness the name "night." The evening and the morning were the first day.

**6** God said, "Let there be an expanse in the middle of the water. Let the expanse divide the water from the water."

**7** God made the expanse. He divided the water below the expanse from the water above the expanse. The result was as God said.

**8** God gave the expanse the name "sky." The evening and the morning were the second day.

**9** God said, "Let the water below the sky come together into one place. Let the dry land appear." The result was as God said.

**10** God gave the dry land the name "earth." He gave the water that came together the name "seas." God saw that the result was good.

**11** God said, "Let the earth make plants grow. Let there be plants that make seeds. Let there be trees that make fruit with seeds in the fruit. Each plant and tree will make seeds of its own type." The result was as God said.

**12** The earth made plants grow. The plants made seeds of their own type. The trees made fruit with seeds of their own type. God saw that the result was good.

**13** The evening and the morning were the third day.

**14** God said, "Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky. Let the lights divide the day from the night. Let the lights be signs for the seasons, the days, and the years.

**15** Let the lights be in the expanse of the sky. Let them give light to the earth." The result was as God said.

**16** God made 2 large lights. The larger light controls the day. The smaller light controls the night. God also made the stars.

**17** God put the lights in the expanse of the sky. The lights give light to the earth.

**18** The lights control the day and the night. They divide the light from the darkness. God saw that the result was good.

**19** The evening and the morning were the fourth day.

**20** God said, "Let the water be full of live animals. Let birds fly above the earth, across the expanse of the sky."

**21** God made the large sea animals. He made all the live animals that move in the water, each of its own type. He made all the birds, each of its own type. God saw that the result was good.

**22** God blessed the animals. He said, "Have many young and increase in number. Fill the water in the seas. Let the birds increase in number on the earth."

**23** The evening and the morning were the fifth day.

**24** God said, "Let the earth make live animals, each of its own type. Let there be livestock, small animals that move on the ground, and wild animals, each of its own type." The result was as God said.

**25** God made the wild animals, each of its own type. He made the livestock, each of its own type. He made all the small animals that move on the ground, each of its own type. God saw that the result was good.

**26** God said, "We will make man in our image, similar to us. Man will control the fish of the sea and the birds of the sky. Man will control the livestock and all the earth. Man will control all the small animals that move on the earth."

**27** God made man in his own image. He made man in the image of God. He made them male and female.

**28** God blessed them. God said to them, "Have many children and increase in number. Fill the earth and control it. Control the fish of the sea and the birds of the sky. Control all the live animals that move on the earth."

**29** God said, "Look, I give you all the plants on the earth that make seeds. I give you all the trees that make fruit with seeds. The plants and the fruit will be your food.

**30** I give all the green plants as food to all the animals of the earth and to all the birds of the sky. I give the green plants to all the small animals that move on the earth. All these animals have life." The result was as God said.

**31** God saw all the things that he made. They were very good. The evening and the morning were the sixth day.

## Chapter 2

**1** Thus God completed the heavens and the earth and all the things in them.

**2** On the seventh day, God completed the work that he did. On the seventh day, he stopped all the work that he did.

**3** God blessed the seventh day and made the seventh day holy. On that day, God stopped all the work that he did when he made all things.

**4** This is the history of the heavens and the earth at the time when God made them. The LORD God made the earth and the heavens.

**5** At that time, no bush of the field was on the earth. No plant of the field grew yet. The LORD God did not cause rain to fall on the earth. There was no man to work the ground.

**6** But a mist went up from the earth. The mist put water on all the surface of the ground.

**7** The LORD God made man from the dust of the ground. He blew the breath of life into the nose of the man. Then the man became a live being.

**8** The LORD God put a garden in Eden, in the east. He put the man that he made in the garden.

**9** The LORD God caused all types of trees to grow from the ground. The trees were good to see and good for food. The tree of life was in the middle of the garden. The tree of the knowledge of good and evil was also there.

**10** A river went out from Eden to give water to the garden. From the garden, the river divided into 4 rivers.

**11** The name of the first river is Pishon. The Pishon flows around all the land of Havilah. There is gold in Havilah.

**12** The gold of that land is good. Bdellium and onyx stone are also in that land.

**13** The name of the second river is Gihon. The Gihon flows around all the land of Cush.

**14** The name of the third river is Tigris. The Tigris flows to the east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.

**15** The LORD God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden. The man had to work the garden and keep the garden safe.

**16** The LORD God gave a command to the man. He said, "You can eat from all the trees of the garden.

**17** But do not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. On the day that you eat from that tree, you will die."

**18** The LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper that is correct for him."

**19** The LORD God made all the animals of the field and all the birds of the sky from the ground. He brought them to the man to see what names the man will give them. The name that the man gave to each animal became the name of that animal.

**20** The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the sky, and to all the animals of the field. But there was no helper that was correct for Adam.

**21** The LORD God caused the man to sleep deeply. While the man slept, the LORD God took one of his ribs. Then he closed the flesh at that place.

**22** The LORD God made a woman from the rib that he took from the man. He brought the woman to the man.

**23** The man said, "Now this is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. Her name will be 'woman,' because she came out of man."

**24** Thus a man will leave his father and his mother. He will join with his wife. They will become one flesh.

**25** The man and his wife were both naked. They did not feel shame.

## Chapter 3

**1** The serpent was more clever than all the wild animals that the LORD God made. The serpent said to the woman, "Did God really tell you not to eat from all the trees of the garden?"

**2** The woman said to the serpent, "We can eat the fruit of the trees of the garden.

**3** But God said, 'Do not eat the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden. Do not touch that tree, or you will die.'"

**4** The serpent said to the woman, "You will not die.

**5** God knows that your eyes will open on the day you eat from that tree. You will be like God. You will know good and evil."

**6** The woman saw that the tree was good for food. She saw that the tree was pleasant to the eyes. She saw that the tree can make a person wise. She took some of its fruit and ate the fruit. She also gave some fruit to her husband, who was with her. He ate the fruit too.

**7** Then the eyes of the man and the woman opened. They knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together. They made coverings for themselves.

**8** They heard the sound of the LORD God, who walked in the garden in the cool part of the day. The man and his wife hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden.

**9** The LORD God called to the man. He said, "Where are you?"

**10** The man said, "I heard your sound in the garden. I was afraid because I was naked. Thus I hid."

**11** God said, "Who told you that you were naked? Did you eat from the tree that I told you not to eat from?"

**12** The man said, "You gave me the woman to be with me. She gave me fruit from the tree. Then I ate the fruit."

**13** The LORD God said to the woman, "What did you do?" The woman said, "The serpent deceived me. Then I ate the fruit."

**14** The LORD God said to the serpent, "You did this. Thus I curse you more than all the livestock and all the wild animals. You will move on your stomach. You will eat dust for all the days of your life.

**15** I will cause hate between you and the woman. I will cause hate between your offspring and her offspring. He will crush your head. You will bruise his heel."

**16** The LORD God said to the woman, "I will greatly increase your pain when you have children. You will have pain when you give birth to children. You will want your husband. He will control you."

**17** The LORD God said to Adam, "You obeyed your wife. You ate from the tree that I told you not to eat from. Thus I curse the ground because of you. You will work hard to get food from the ground for all the days of your life.

**18** The ground will grow thorns and thistles for you. You will eat the plants of the field.

**19** You will work hard and sweat to get your bread. You will do this work until you go back to the ground. I took you from the ground. You are dust, and you will go back to dust."

**20** The man gave his wife the name Eve. Eve became the mother of all the people who live.

**21** The LORD God made clothes of animal skins for Adam and his wife. He put the clothes on them.

**22** The LORD God said, "Look, the man became like one of us. He knows good and evil. He must not put out his hand and take fruit from the tree of life. If he eats that fruit, he will live forever."

**23** Thus the LORD God sent the man out of the Garden of Eden. The man had to work the ground. God took the man from that ground.

**24** God sent the man out. On the east side of the Garden of Eden, God put cherubim (angels). He also put a sword of fire there. The sword turned in all directions. The cherubim and the sword guarded the path to the tree of life.

## Chapter 4

**1** Adam had sexual relations with his wife Eve. She became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, "With the help of the LORD, I got a man."

**2** Then Eve gave birth to Abel, the brother of Cain. Abel kept sheep. Cain worked the ground.

**3** After some time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the ground to the LORD. Cain gave the fruit as an offering.

**4** Abel also brought an offering. He brought some of the first lambs of his sheep and their fat. The LORD accepted Abel and his offering.

**5** But the LORD did not accept Cain and his offering. Cain became very angry. His face showed that he was sad.

**6** The LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why does your face show that you are sad?

**7** If you do good things, I will accept you. If you do not do good things, sin waits at your door. Sin wants to control you. But you must control sin."

**8** Cain talked to his brother Abel. When they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel. Cain killed Abel.

**9** The LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" Cain said, "I do not know. Must I guard my brother?"

**10** The LORD said, "What did you do? The blood of your brother calls to me from the ground.

**11** Now I curse you and send you away from the ground. The ground opened its mouth. The ground received the blood of your brother from your hand.

**12** When you work the ground, the ground will not give you good crops again. You will move from place to place on the earth. You will have no home."

**13** Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is too large for me.

**14** Today you send me away from the surface of the ground. I will hide from your face. I will move from place to place on the earth, and I will have no home. Each person who finds me will kill me."

**15** The LORD said to Cain, "No. If a person kills Cain, I will punish that person 7 times." The LORD put a mark on Cain. The mark told people not to kill Cain when they found him.

**16** Cain went away from the LORD. He lived in the land of Nod, to the east of Eden.

**17** Cain had sexual relations with his wife. She became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Cain built a city. He gave the city the name of his son, Enoch.

**18** Enoch became the father of Irad. Irad became the father of Mehujael. Mehujael became the father of Methushael. Methushael became the father of Lamech.

**19** Lamech married 2 wives. The name of one wife was Adah. The name of the other wife was Zillah.

**20** Adah gave birth to Jabal. Jabal was the father of the people who live in tents and keep livestock.

**21** The name of his brother was Jubal. Jubal was the father of all the people who play the harp and the flute.

**22** Zillah gave birth to Tubal-Cain. Tubal-Cain made all types of tools from bronze and iron. The sister of Tubal-Cain was Naamah.

**23** Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice. Wives of Lamech, listen to my words. I killed a man because he wounded me. I killed a young man because he hit me.

**24** If a person kills Cain, God will punish that person 7 times. If a person kills Lamech, God will punish that person 77 times."

**25** Adam had sexual relations with his wife again. She gave birth to a son. She gave the son the name Seth. She said, "God gave me another son in the place of Abel, because Cain killed Abel."

**26** Seth also became the father of a son. Seth gave the son the name Enosh. At that time, people started to call on the name of the LORD.

## Chapter 5

**1** This is the book of the history of Adam. On the day that God made man, God made man similar to God.

**2** God made them male and female. He blessed them. On the day that he made them, he gave them the name "Man."

**3** When Adam was 130 years old, he became the father of a son. The son was similar to Adam. Adam gave the son the name Seth.

**4** After Adam became the father of Seth, Adam lived 800 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**5** Adam lived a total of 930 years. Then he died.

**6** When Seth was 105 years old, he became the father of Enosh.

**7** After Seth became the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**8** Seth lived a total of 912 years. Then he died.

**9** When Enosh was 90 years old, he became the father of Kenan.

**10** After Enosh became the father of Kenan, Enosh lived 815 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**11** Enosh lived a total of 905 years. Then he died.

**12** When Kenan was 70 years old, he became the father of Mahalalel.

**13** After Kenan became the father of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**14** Kenan lived a total of 910 years. Then he died.

**15** When Mahalalel was 65 years old, he became the father of Jared.

**16** After Mahalalel became the father of Jared, Mahalalel lived 830 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**17** Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years. Then he died.

**18** When Jared was 162 years old, he became the father of Enoch.

**19** After Jared became the father of Enoch, Jared lived 800 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**20** Jared lived a total of 962 years. Then he died.

**21** When Enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah.

**22** After Enoch became the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God for 300 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**23** Enoch lived a total of 365 years.

**24** Enoch walked with God. Then people did not see Enoch again, because God took him.

**25** When Methuselah was 187 years old, he became the father of Lamech.

**26** After Methuselah became the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**27** Methuselah lived a total of 969 years. Then he died.

**28** When Lamech was 182 years old, he became the father of a son.

**29** Lamech gave the son the name Noah. Lamech said, "This son will give us comfort in our work. We work hard with our hands because the LORD cursed the ground."

**30** After Lamech became the father of Noah, Lamech lived 595 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**31** Lamech lived a total of 777 years. Then he died.

**32** When Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

## Chapter 6

**1** The number of men started to increase on the surface of the earth. The men had daughters.

**2** The sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful. The sons of God took as wives the women that they chose.

**3** The LORD said, "My Spirit will not stay with man forever, because man is flesh. The days of man will be 120 years."

**4** The Nephilim (giants) were on the earth in those days and also after that time. The sons of God had sexual relations with the daughters of men. The women gave birth to children. These children became the strong men of old times. They were men with famous names.

**5** The LORD saw that the evil of man on the earth was very large. He saw that all the thoughts of the heart of man were evil all the time.

**6** The LORD was sorry that he made man on the earth. His heart felt much pain.

**7** The LORD said, "I will remove the men that I made from the surface of the ground. I will remove men, livestock, small animals, and birds of the sky. I am sorry that I made them."

**8** But the LORD was happy with Noah.

**9** This is the history of Noah. Noah was a righteous man. He did no wrong among the people of his time. Noah walked with God.

**10** Noah became the father of 3 sons. Their names were Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

**11** God saw that the earth was corrupt. The earth was full of violence.

**12** God looked at the earth. He saw that the earth was corrupt. All the people on the earth made their way of life corrupt.

**13** God said to Noah, "I will put an end to all people. The earth is full of violence because of them. I will destroy the people and the earth.

**14** Make an ark (a large boat) of gopher wood. Make rooms in the ark. Put pitch (tar) on the inside and the outside of the ark.

**15** Make the ark with these dimensions. The length of the ark will be 300 cubits. The width will be 50 cubits. The height will be 30 cubits.

**16** Make a roof for the ark. Make a space of 1 cubit below the roof. Put a door in the side of the ark. Make the ark with a lower deck, a second deck, and a third deck.

**17** I will cause a flood of water on the earth. The flood will destroy all flesh under the sky that has the breath of life. All things on the earth will die.

**18** But I will make my agreement (covenant) with you. You will go into the ark with your sons, your wife, and the wives of your sons.

**19** Bring into the ark 2 animals of each type, a male and a female. Keep the animals alive with you.

**20** 2 of each type of bird will come to you. 2 of each type of livestock will come to you. 2 of each type of small animal that moves on the ground will come to you. Keep them alive.

**21** Take all types of food. Keep the food with you. The food will be for you and for the animals."

**22** Noah did all the things that God told him to do.

## Chapter 7

**1** The LORD said to Noah, "Go into the ark with all your family. I see that you are righteous among the people of this time.

**2** Take 7 pairs of each type of clean animal, a male and its female. Take 1 pair of each type of animal that is not clean, a male and its female.

**3** Also take 7 pairs of each type of bird of the sky, male and female. Then their offspring will stay alive on the surface of all the earth.

**4** After 7 days, I will cause rain to fall on the earth for 40 days and 40 nights. I will remove all the live things that I made from the surface of the ground."

**5** Noah did all the things that the LORD told him to do.

**6** Noah was 600 years old when the flood of water came on the earth.

**7** Noah went into the ark with his sons, his wife, and the wives of his sons. They went into the ark to escape the water of the flood.

**8** Clean animals and animals that were not clean came to Noah. Birds and all the small animals that move on the ground also came.

**9** They came in pairs, male and female, and went into the ark. They came as God told Noah.

**10** After 7 days, the water of the flood came on the earth.

**11** In the 600th year of the life of Noah, on the 17th day of the second month, all the springs of the deep water opened. On that day, the windows of the sky opened.

**12** Rain fell on the earth for 40 days and 40 nights.

**13** On that same day, Noah went into the ark with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth. The wife of Noah and the 3 wives of his sons also went in with them.

**14** Each type of wild animal and each type of livestock went in with them. Each type of small animal that moves on the earth went in. Each type of bird went in.

**15** Pairs of all flesh that has the breath of life went into the ark with Noah.

**16** A male and a female of all flesh went in, as God told Noah. Then the LORD closed the door behind Noah.

**17** The flood continued on the earth for 40 days. The water increased and lifted the ark. The ark went up high above the earth.

**18** The water became very strong and increased much on the earth. The ark moved on the surface of the water.

**19** The water became very, very strong on the earth. The water covered all the high mountains under all the sky.

**20** The water went up 15 cubits above the mountains. The water covered the mountains.

**21** All flesh that moved on the earth died. Birds, livestock, wild animals, and all the small animals died. All the people died.

**22** All the things on the dry land that had the breath of life in their nose died.

**23** God removed all the live things from the surface of the ground. He removed people, livestock, small animals, and birds of the sky from the earth. Only Noah and the people and animals with him in the ark stayed alive.

**24** The water stayed strong on the earth for 150 days.

## Chapter 8

**1** God remembered Noah. He remembered all the wild animals and all the livestock with Noah in the ark. God caused a wind to blow over the earth. The water started to decrease.

**2** The springs of the deep water and the windows of the sky closed. The rain from the sky stopped.

**3** The water went back from the earth slowly. After 150 days, the water decreased.

**4** On the 17th day of the seventh month, the ark stopped on the mountains of Ararat.

**5** The water continued to decrease until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month, people can see the tops of the mountains.

**6** After 40 days, Noah opened the window that he made in the ark.

**7** Noah sent out a raven. The raven flew here and there until the water on the earth became dry.

**8** Then Noah sent out a dove. He wanted to see if the water decreased from the surface of the ground.

**9** The dove found no place to put its feet, because water covered the surface of all the earth. The dove came back to Noah in the ark. Noah put out his hand and took the dove. He brought the dove back into the ark.

**10** Noah waited 7 more days. Then he sent the dove out of the ark again.

**11** The dove came back to Noah in the evening. The dove had a fresh olive leaf in its beak. Then Noah knew that the water decreased from the earth.

**12** Noah waited 7 more days. Then he sent out the dove again. The dove did not come back to him.

**13** In the 601st year of the life of Noah, on the first day of the first month, the water on the earth became dry. Noah removed the cover of the ark. He looked out and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.

**14** On the 27th day of the second month, the earth was fully dry.

**15** Then God spoke to Noah. God said these words:

**16** "Go out of the ark with your wife, your sons, and the wives of your sons.

**17** Bring out all the live animals of all flesh with you. Bring out the birds, the livestock, and all the small animals that move on the earth. Let them have many young and increase in number on the earth."

**18** Noah went out with his sons, his wife, and the wives of his sons.

**19** All the animals, all the small animals, and all the birds went out of the ark. All the things that move on the earth went out. They went out in their families.

**20** Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took some of each type of clean animal and each type of clean bird. He gave them as burnt offerings on the altar.

**21** The LORD smelled the pleasant smell. The LORD said in his heart, "I will not curse the ground again because of man. The thoughts of the heart of man are evil from his youth. I will not destroy all the live things again, as I did.

**22** While the earth continues, the time to plant seeds and the time to collect crops will not stop. Cold and heat will not stop. Summer and winter will not stop. Day and night will not stop."

## Chapter 9

**1** God blessed Noah and his sons. He said to them, "Have many children and increase in number. Fill the earth.

**2** All the animals of the earth and all the birds of the sky will fear you. All the small animals that move on the ground and all the fish of the sea will fear you. I give them into your control.

**3** All the animals that move and live will be food for you. Before, I gave you the green plants as food. Now I give you all things.

**4** But do not eat meat that has its life in it. The life of the meat is its blood.

**5** Your blood is your life. I will make the killer pay for your blood. I will make each animal that kills a person pay. I will make each person who kills another person pay.

**6** If a person kills a man, another man will kill that person. God made man in his own image.

**7** You must have many children and increase in number. Fill the earth and increase on the earth."

**8** Then God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him. God said,

**9** "Look, I make my agreement (covenant) with you and with your offspring after you.

**10** I also make my agreement with all the live things that are with you. I make it with the birds, the livestock, and all the wild animals. I make it with all the animals that came out of the ark.

**11** I make my agreement with you. A flood of water will not kill all flesh again. A flood will not destroy the earth again."

**12** God said, "I give you a sign of the agreement between me and you. The agreement is also with all the live things with you. The agreement is for all the generations in the future.

**13** I put my rainbow in the cloud. The rainbow will be the sign of the agreement between me and the earth.

**14** I will bring clouds over the earth. Then people will see the rainbow in the clouds.

**15** I will remember my agreement between me and you and all the live animals of all flesh. Water will not become a flood to destroy all flesh again.

**16** The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will look at the rainbow. Then I will remember the agreement that continues forever. The agreement is between God and all the live animals of all flesh on the earth."

**17** God said to Noah, "The rainbow is the sign of the agreement between me and all flesh on the earth."

**18** The sons of Noah who went out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.

**19** These 3 men were the sons of Noah. All the people of the earth came from these 3 men.

**20** Noah started to work as a farmer. He planted a vineyard.

**21** Noah drank some of the wine and became drunk. He lay naked in his tent.

**22** Ham, the father of Canaan, saw that his father was naked. Ham went outside and told his 2 brothers.

**23** Shem and Japheth took a garment and put the garment on their shoulders. They walked backward and covered their naked father. They turned their faces away. They did not see their father naked.

**24** Noah woke up from the effect of the wine. He knew what his youngest son did to him.

**25** Noah said, "I curse Canaan. Canaan will be the lowest servant of his brothers."

**26** Noah also said, "Praise the LORD, the God of Shem. Canaan will be the servant of Shem.

**27** May God make the land of Japheth large. Japheth will live in the tents of Shem. Canaan will be the servant of Japheth."

**28** After the flood, Noah lived 350 years.

**29** Noah lived a total of 950 years. Then he died.

## Chapter 10

**1** This is the history of the sons of Noah. Their names were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. After the flood, they became the fathers of sons.

**2** The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

**3** The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

**4** The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

**5** The people of the coastlands came from these sons. They divided into their lands. Each group had its own language, family, and nation.

**6** The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

**7** The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.

**8** Cush became the father of Nimrod. Nimrod became the first powerful man on the earth.

**9** Nimrod was a powerful hunter in front of the LORD. Thus people say, "He is like Nimrod, a powerful hunter in front of the LORD."

**10** The first cities of his kingdom were Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh. These cities were in the land of Shinar.

**11** From that land, Nimrod went into Assyria. He built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah.

**12** He also built Resen, between Nineveh and Calah. Resen is a large city.

**13** Mizraim became the father of the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim, and the Naphtuhim.

**14** Mizraim also became the father of the Pathrusim, the Casluhim, and the Caphtorim. The Philistines came from the Casluhim.

**15** Canaan became the father of Sidon, his first son. Canaan also became the father of Heth.

**16** Canaan was also the father of the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites.

**17** He was the father of the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites.

**18** He was the father of the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. After that, the families of the Canaanites spread out.

**19** The border of the Canaanites went from Sidon toward Gerar, as far as Gaza. The border went toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

**20** These are the sons of Ham. Each group had its own family, language, land, and nation.

**21** Shem also became the father of children. Shem was the ancestor of all the children of Eber. Shem was the older brother of Japheth.

**22** The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.

**23** The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.

**24** Arpachshad became the father of Shelah. Shelah became the father of Eber.

**25** Eber became the father of 2 sons. The name of one son was Peleg, because people divided the earth in his time. The name of his brother was Joktan.

**26** Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.

**27** Joktan was the father of Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah.

**28** He was the father of Obal, Abimael, and Sheba.

**29** He was the father of Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these men were the sons of Joktan.

**30** Their land went from Mesha toward Sephar, the mountain in the east.

**31** These are the sons of Shem. Each group had its own family, language, land, and nation.

**32** These are the families of the sons of Noah, in their generations and nations. After the flood, the nations came from these families. The nations spread out on the earth.

## Chapter 11

**1** All the people of the earth had one language. They used the same words.

**2** The people traveled from the east. They found a plain in the land of Shinar. They lived there.

**3** They said to each other, "Come, we will make bricks and burn them fully." They used brick instead of stone. They used tar instead of mortar.

**4** Then they said, "Come, we will build a city and a tower. The top of the tower will be in the sky. We will make a famous name for us. Then we will not go to all parts of the earth."

**5** The LORD came down to see the city and the tower. The people built the city and the tower.

**6** The LORD said, "Look, they are one people, and they all have one language. This tower is only the start of their work. Now they will be able to do all the things that they plan.

**7** Come, we will go down and mix up their language. Then they will not understand each other."

**8** So the LORD sent the people from there to all parts of the earth. They stopped the construction of the city.

**9** Thus the name of the city is Babel. There the LORD mixed up the language of all the earth. From there the LORD sent the people to all parts of the earth.

**10** These are the descendants of Shem. Shem was 100 years old when he became the father of Arphaxad. This was 2 years after the flood.

**11** After Shem became the father of Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**12** Arphaxad lived 35 years. Then he became the father of Shelah.

**13** After Arphaxad became the father of Shelah, Arphaxad lived 403 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**14** Shelah lived 30 years. Then he became the father of Eber.

**15** After Shelah became the father of Eber, Shelah lived 403 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**16** Eber lived 34 years. Then he became the father of Peleg.

**17** After Eber became the father of Peleg, Eber lived 430 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**18** Peleg lived 30 years. Then he became the father of Reu.

**19** After Peleg became the father of Reu, Peleg lived 209 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**20** Reu lived 32 years. Then he became the father of Serug.

**21** After Reu became the father of Serug, Reu lived 207 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**22** Serug lived 30 years. Then he became the father of Nahor.

**23** After Serug became the father of Nahor, Serug lived 200 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**24** Nahor lived 29 years. Then he became the father of Terah.

**25** After Nahor became the father of Terah, Nahor lived 119 years. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**26** Terah lived 70 years. Then he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

**27** These are the descendants of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran became the father of Lot.

**28** Haran died before his father Terah. Haran died in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans.

**29** Abram and Nahor married wives. The name of the wife of Abram was Sarai. The name of the wife of Nahor was Milcah. Milcah was the daughter of Haran. Haran was the father of Milcah and of Iscah.

**30** Sarai could not have children. She had no child.

**31** Terah took his son Abram and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran. He also took his daughter-in-law Sarai, the wife of Abram. They went out together from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. They came to the city of Haran and lived there.

**32** Terah lived 205 years. Then Terah died in Haran.

## Chapter 12

**1** The LORD said to Abram, "Go from your country and from your relatives. Go from the house of your father. Go to the land that I will show you.

**2** I will make you into a great nation. I will bless you. I will make your name great. You will be a blessing to other people.

**3** I will bless the people who bless you. I will curse the person who curses you. All the families of the earth will get a blessing through you."

**4** So Abram went, as the LORD told him. Lot went with him. Abram was 75 years old when he went out of Haran.

**5** Abram took his wife Sarai and Lot, the son of his brother. They took all their possessions and the people that they got in Haran. They went out to go to the land of Canaan. Then they came into the land of Canaan.

**6** Abram traveled through the land to the place of Shechem. He came to the oak tree of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites lived in the land.

**7** The LORD appeared to Abram. The LORD said, "I will give this land to your descendants." So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who appeared to him.

**8** From there Abram moved to the mountain on the east of Bethel. He put up his tent there. Bethel was on the west, and Ai was on the east. There he built an altar to the LORD. He called on the name of the LORD.

**9** Abram continued to travel toward the South (the Negev).

**10** There was not sufficient food in the land (a famine). The famine in the land was very bad. So Abram went down into Egypt to live there for a short time.

**11** When Abram came near Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, "Look, I know that you are a beautiful woman.

**12** The Egyptians will see you. They will say, 'She is his wife.' Then they will kill me, but they will let you live.

**13** Please say that you are my sister. Then they will be good to me because of you. I will stay alive because of you."

**14** Abram came into Egypt. The Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.

**15** The officials of Pharaoh saw Sarai. They told Pharaoh good things about her. Then they took the woman into the house of Pharaoh.

**16** Pharaoh was good to Abram because of Sarai. Abram got sheep, cattle, and male donkeys. He also got male servants, female servants, female donkeys, and camels.

**17** But the LORD caused very bad diseases (plagues) on Pharaoh and his household. The LORD did this because of Sarai, the wife of Abram.

**18** Pharaoh called Abram and said, "What did you do to me? Why did you not tell me that she is your wife?

**19** Why did you say, 'She is my sister'? Because of your words, I took her as my wife. Now, here is your wife. Take her and go!"

**20** Pharaoh gave orders to his men about Abram. The men sent Abram away with his wife and all his possessions.

## Chapter 13

**1** Abram went up from Egypt into the South. His wife, all his possessions, and Lot went with him.

**2** Abram was very rich. He had many animals, much silver, and much gold.

**3** Abram traveled from the South to Bethel. He came to the place where his tent was at the start. That place was between Bethel and Ai.

**4** There was the altar that Abram made at the first. There Abram called on the name of the LORD.

**5** Lot traveled with Abram. Lot also had flocks of sheep, herds of cattle, and tents.

**6** The land could not give sufficient food for the animals of the two men together. They had too many possessions. So they could not live together.

**7** The herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot argued. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites also lived in the land.

**8** Abram said to Lot, "Please, we must not argue, you and I. Our herdsmen must not argue. We are relatives.

**9** All the land is in front of you. Please go away from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right. If you go to the right, I will go to the left."

**10** Lot looked up and saw all the plain of the Jordan River. All of the plain had much water. It was like the garden of the LORD and like the land of Egypt, in the direction of Zoar. This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.

**11** So Lot chose all the plain of the Jordan for himself. Lot traveled east. Thus the two men went away from each other.

**12** Abram lived in the land of Canaan. Lot lived among the cities of the plain. Lot moved his tent as far as Sodom.

**13** The men of Sodom were very bad. They did many sins against the LORD.

**14** After Lot went away from Abram, the LORD said to Abram, "Look up from the place where you are. Look north, south, east, and west.

**15** I will give all the land that you see to you and to your descendants for all time.

**16** I will make your descendants as many as the dust of the earth. If a person can count the dust of the earth, then he can also count your descendants.

**17** Get up and walk through the land. Walk through its length and its width. I will give the land to you."

**18** Abram moved his tent. He came and lived near the oak trees of Mamre, in Hebron. There he built an altar to the LORD.

## Chapter 14

**1** These events occurred in the time of four kings. The kings were Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim.

**2** These four kings made war against five kings. The five kings were Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, and Shinab king of Admah. The other two were Shemeber king of Zeboiim and the king of Bela (Zoar).

**3** These five kings joined together in the valley of Siddim. The valley of Siddim is now the Salt Sea.

**4** For 12 years the five kings served Chedorlaomer. In the 13th year they rebelled against him.

**5** In the 14th year, Chedorlaomer and the kings with him came. They defeated the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim and the Zuzim in Ham. They also defeated the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim.

**6** They defeated the Horites in the mountains of Seir. They went as far as El Paran, near the wilderness (desert).

**7** Then they went back and came to En Mishpat (Kadesh). They defeated all the country of the Amalekites. They also defeated the Amorites who lived in Hazazon Tamar.

**8** Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah went out. The king of Zeboiim and the king of Bela (Zoar) also went out. They prepared for battle in the valley of Siddim.

**9** They fought against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar. Four kings fought against five kings.

**10** The valley of Siddim had many pits of tar. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ran away. Some of their men fell into the pits. The other men ran away to the mountains.

**11** The four kings took all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah. They took all the food. Then they went away.

**12** They also took Lot, the son of the brother of Abram. Lot lived in Sodom. They took Lot and his possessions and went away.

**13** A man escaped and came to Abram the Hebrew. The man told Abram what occurred. Abram lived near the oak trees of Mamre the Amorite. Mamre was the brother of Eshcol and Aner. These men had an agreement with Abram.

**14** Abram heard that the enemy captured his relative Lot. Abram called his 318 trained men. The mothers of these men gave birth to them in his house. Abram followed the enemy as far as Dan.

**15** At night, Abram divided his men into groups against the enemy. He and his servants attacked the enemy and defeated them. Abram followed them as far as Hobah, on the north of Damascus.

**16** Abram brought back all the possessions. He also brought back his relative Lot and the possessions of Lot. He brought back the women and the other people too.

**17** Abram defeated Chedorlaomer and the kings with him. Then Abram came back. The king of Sodom went out to meet him in the valley of Shaveh (the King's Valley).

**18** Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. Melchizedek was the priest of God Most High.

**19** Melchizedek blessed Abram. He said, "Abram, God Most High blesses you. God Most High is the owner of heaven and earth.

**20** Praise God Most High. He gave your enemies into your control." Then Abram gave Melchizedek one tenth of all the possessions.

**21** The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give the people to me. Keep the possessions for yourself."

**22** But Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I lifted up my hand to the LORD, God Most High. He is the owner of heaven and earth. I made a promise to him.

**23** I will not take a thread or a sandal strap. I will take nothing that is yours. Then you cannot say, 'I made Abram rich.'

**24** I will take nothing for myself. I will only accept the food that my young men ate. Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre went with me. Let them take their part."

## Chapter 15

**1** After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision. The LORD said, "Abram, do not be afraid. I am your shield. Your reward will be very great."

**2** Abram said, "Lord GOD, what will you give me? I have no children. Eliezer of Damascus will get all that is in my house."

**3** Abram also said, "Look, you gave me no children. So a servant born in my house will be my heir."

**4** Then the word of the LORD came to Abram. The LORD said, "This man will not be your heir. A son from your own body will be your heir."

**5** The LORD brought Abram outside. The LORD said, "Look up at the sky. Count the stars, if you can count them." Then he said, "Your descendants will be as many as the stars."

**6** Abram believed the LORD. Because of this belief, the LORD considered Abram righteous.

**7** The LORD said to Abram, "I am the LORD. I brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans. I will give you this land as your possession."

**8** Abram said, "Lord GOD, how will I know that this land will be my possession?"

**9** The LORD said to him, "Bring me a female cow, a female goat, and a male sheep. Each animal must be 3 years old. Also bring a dove and a young pigeon."

**10** Abram brought all these animals to the LORD. He cut each animal into two halves. He put each half opposite the other half. But he did not cut the birds.

**11** Birds of prey came down on the dead animals. Abram made the birds go away.

**12** When the sun went down, Abram fell into a deep sleep. A very bad fear and a great darkness came on him.

**13** The LORD said to Abram, "Know this: Your descendants will be foreigners in a land that is not theirs. The people of that land will make them slaves. They will treat your descendants badly for 400 years.

**14** But I will judge the nation that makes them slaves. After that, your descendants will come out with many possessions.

**15** You will die in peace. You will be very old when people bury you.

**16** After 4 generations, your descendants will come back here. Now the sin of the Amorites is not yet complete."

**17** The sun went down and it was dark. Then a pot with smoke and a torch with fire went between the pieces of the animals.

**18** On that day, the LORD made an agreement (covenant) with Abram. The LORD said, "I give this land to your descendants. The land goes from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates.

**19** This land includes the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites.

**20** This land also includes the land of the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Rephaim.

**21** This land also includes the land of the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."

## Chapter 16

**1** Sarai, the wife of Abram, had no children. Sarai had a female servant from Egypt. The name of the servant was Hagar.

**2** Sarai said to Abram, "Look, the LORD does not let me have children. Please go to my servant. Possibly I can get children through her." Abram did what Sarai said.

**3** Abram lived in the land of Canaan for 10 years. Then Sarai took her servant Hagar the Egyptian. Sarai gave Hagar to her husband Abram as a wife.

**4** Abram had sexual relations with Hagar, and Hagar became pregnant. Hagar saw that she was pregnant. Then she did not respect Sarai.

**5** Sarai said to Abram, "You are responsible for this wrong to me. I gave my servant to you. She saw that she was pregnant. Then she did not respect me. The LORD will judge between you and me."

**6** Abram said to Sarai, "Look, your servant is under your control. Do to her what you think is good." Then Sarai treated Hagar badly. So Hagar ran away from Sarai.

**7** The angel of the LORD found Hagar near a spring of water in the wilderness. The spring was on the road to Shur.

**8** The angel said, "Hagar, servant of Sarai, where did you come from? Where will you go?" Hagar said, "I run away from Sarai, my mistress."

**9** The angel of the LORD said to her, "Go back to your mistress. Obey her."

**10** The angel of the LORD also said, "I will make your descendants very many. Nobody will be able to count them."

**11** The angel of the LORD said to her, "Look, you are pregnant. You will have a son. You will call him Ishmael, because the LORD heard about your trouble.

**12** Your son will be like a wild donkey. He will be against all men, and all men will be against him. He will live in opposition to all his brothers."

**13** Hagar gave a name to the LORD, who spoke to her. She said, "You are the God who sees me." She also said, "Here I saw the one who sees me."

**14** Because of this, people call the well Beer Lahai Roi. The well is between Kadesh and Bered.

**15** Hagar gave birth to a son for Abram. Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son of Hagar.

**16** Abram was 86 years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael.

## Chapter 17

**1** When Abram was 99 years old, the LORD appeared to him. The LORD said, "I am God Almighty. Obey me always. Do no wrong.

**2** I will make my agreement (covenant) between me and you. I will give you very many descendants."

**3** Abram bowed down with his face to the ground. God spoke to him and said,

**4** "Look, I make my agreement with you. You will be the father of many nations.

**5** Your name will not be Abram any more. Your name will be Abraham. I make you the father of many nations.

**6** I will give you very many descendants. I will make nations from you. Kings will come from you.

**7** I will make my agreement between me and you and your descendants. This agreement will continue through all their generations for all time. I will be your God and the God of your descendants.

**8** Now you live as a foreigner in the land of Canaan. I will give all the land of Canaan to you and your descendants. The land will be your possession for all time. I will be their God."

**9** God said to Abraham, "You must obey my agreement. You and your descendants must obey it through all their generations.

**10** This is my agreement between me and you and your descendants. You must obey this agreement. You must circumcise each male among you.

**11** You must cut away the foreskin of each male. This will be the sign of the agreement between me and you.

**12** Through all your generations, you must circumcise each male when he is 8 days old. Do this to each male born in your house. Also do this to each male that you buy with money from a foreigner.

**13** You must circumcise each male born in your house and each male that you buy with money. Thus my agreement will be in your bodies. It will be an agreement for all time.

**14** If you do not circumcise a male, you must remove him from his people. He broke my agreement."

**15** God said to Abraham, "Do not call your wife Sarai any more. Her name will be Sarah.

**16** I will bless her. I will give you a son from her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations. Kings of peoples will come from her."

**17** Abraham bowed down with his face to the ground and laughed. He thought, "Can a man who is 100 years old have a child? Can Sarah, who is 90 years old, give birth to a child?"

**18** Abraham said to God, "Please let Ishmael live under your blessing."

**19** God said, "No. Your wife Sarah will give birth to a son for you. You will call him Isaac. I will make my agreement with Isaac. It will be an agreement for all time for his descendants.

**20** I also heard your request about Ishmael. Look, I will bless him. I will give him very many descendants. He will be the father of 12 rulers. I will make him into a great nation.

**21** But I will make my agreement with Isaac. Sarah will give birth to Isaac at this time next year."

**22** God stopped his words to Abraham. Then God went up from Abraham.

**23** On that same day, Abraham took his son Ishmael and all the males born in his house. He also took all the males that he bought with his money. Abraham circumcised all the males of his household, as God told him.

**24** Abraham was 99 years old when he received circumcision.

**25** His son Ishmael was 13 years old when he received circumcision.

**26** Abraham and his son Ishmael received circumcision on that same day.

**27** All the men of the household of Abraham received circumcision with him. This included the men born in his house. It also included the men that he bought with money from foreigners.

## Chapter 18

**1** The LORD appeared to Abraham near the oak trees of Mamre. Abraham sat at the door of his tent. It was the hottest time of the day.

**2** Abraham looked up and saw three men. They stood near him. When Abraham saw them, he ran from the door of his tent to meet them. He bowed down to the ground.

**3** He said, "My lord, if you are happy with me, please do not go past your servant.

**4** Let me bring a little water. Then you can wash your feet and rest under the tree.

**5** I will bring some bread. The bread will give you strength. Then you can continue your journey. That is why you came to your servant." The men said, "Do as you say."

**6** Abraham went quickly into the tent to Sarah. He said, "Quickly, get 3 measures of fine flour. Make dough and bake bread."

**7** Then Abraham ran to the herd. He took a good, young calf. He gave the calf to a servant. The servant prepared it quickly.

**8** Abraham took butter, milk, and the meat of the calf. He put the food in front of the men. He stood near them under the tree while they ate.

**9** The men said to Abraham, "Where is your wife Sarah?" Abraham said, "She is in the tent."

**10** The LORD said, "I will certainly come back to you at this time next year. Then your wife Sarah will have a son." Sarah heard these words at the door of the tent, behind him.

**11** Abraham and Sarah were old. They lived many years. Sarah was too old to have children.

**12** So Sarah laughed to herself. She thought, "I am old, and my husband is old. Will I have this pleasure now?"

**13** The LORD said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh? Why did she say, 'Will I really have a child, now that I am old?'

**14** Is any thing too difficult for the LORD? I will come back to you at the set time next year. Then Sarah will have a son."

**15** Sarah was afraid. So she did not tell the truth. She said, "I did not laugh." But the LORD said, "No, you laughed."

**16** The men got up from there and looked toward Sodom. Abraham went with them to send them on their way.

**17** The LORD said, "I will not hide from Abraham what I will do.

**18** Abraham will certainly become a great and strong nation. All the nations of the earth will get a blessing through him.

**19** I chose Abraham. He will tell his children and his household to obey the way of the LORD. They will do what is right and fair. Then the LORD will do for Abraham all that he promised."

**20** Then the LORD said, "The complaint against Sodom and Gomorrah is very great. Their sin is very bad.

**21** I will go down now. I will see if they did all the bad things in the complaint that came to me. If not, I will know."

**22** The two men turned from there and went toward Sodom. But Abraham continued to stand in front of the LORD.

**23** Abraham came near and said, "Will you destroy the righteous people with the wicked people?

**24** Possibly there are 50 righteous people in the city. Will you destroy the city? Will you not save the city because of the 50 righteous people in it?

**25** Do not do such a thing! Do not kill the righteous people with the wicked people. Do not treat the righteous and the wicked the same. The Judge of all the earth must do what is right."

**26** The LORD said, "If I find 50 righteous people in the city of Sodom, I will save all the city because of them."

**27** Abraham said, "Look, I speak to the Lord again. But I am only dust and ashes.

**28** Possibly there will be 45 righteous people, 5 less than 50. Will you destroy all the city because of 5 people?" The LORD said, "If I find 45 there, I will not destroy the city."

**29** Abraham spoke to the LORD again. He said, "Possibly you will find 40 there." The LORD said, "I will not destroy the city because of the 40."

**30** Abraham said, "Lord, please do not be angry, and I will speak. Possibly you will find 30 there." The LORD said, "I will not destroy the city if I find 30 there."

**31** Abraham said, "Look, I speak to the Lord again. Possibly you will find 20 there." The LORD said, "I will not destroy the city because of the 20."

**32** Abraham said, "Lord, please do not be angry. I will speak only one more time. Possibly you will find 10 there." The LORD said, "I will not destroy the city because of the 10."

**33** The LORD stopped his words to Abraham. Then the LORD went away. Abraham went back to his home.

## Chapter 19

**1** The two angels came to Sodom in the evening. Lot sat at the gate of Sodom. When Lot saw the angels, he got up to meet them. He bowed down with his face to the ground.

**2** Lot said, "My lords, please come into the house of your servant. Stay the night and wash your feet. Then you can get up early and continue your journey." The angels said, "No, we will stay the night in the street."

**3** But Lot asked them very strongly. So they went with him into his house. Lot made a meal for them. He baked bread without yeast, and they ate.

**4** Before they lay down, the men of the city came. All the men of Sodom, young and old, came from all parts of the city. They stood around the house.

**5** They called to Lot. They said, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us. We want to have sexual relations with them."

**6** Lot went out to the men at the door. He closed the door behind him.

**7** He said, "Please, my brothers, do not do this wicked thing.

**8** Look, I have two daughters who are virgins. Let me bring them out to you. Do to them what you think is good. But do nothing to these men. They came into my house for protection."

**9** The men said, "Move away!" Then they said, "This man came here as a foreigner. Now he wants to be our judge! Now we will do worse things to you than to them." They pushed hard against Lot. They came near to break the door.

**10** But the two men inside put out their hands. They pulled Lot into the house and closed the door.

**11** Then the angels made the men at the door blind, the young and the old. So the men could not find the door.

**12** The two men said to Lot, "Do you have other relatives here? Take your sons-in-law, your sons, and your daughters. Take all your people in the city out of this place.

**13** We will destroy this place. The LORD heard the great complaint against the people of this city. The LORD sent us to destroy the city."

**14** Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law. These men had an agreement to marry his daughters. Lot said, "Get up! Go out of this place, because the LORD will destroy the city." But his sons-in-law thought that Lot made a joke.

**15** At dawn, the angels told Lot to go quickly. They said, "Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here. If you do not go, you will die when the LORD punishes the city."

**16** But Lot did not go quickly. So the men took the hand of Lot, the hand of his wife, and the hands of his two daughters. The LORD was merciful to Lot. The men brought them out and put them outside the city.

**17** When they were outside, one angel said, "Run away to save your lives! Do not look behind you. Do not stop anywhere in the plain. Run away to the mountains, or you will die."

**18** Lot said to them, "No, my lord, please!

**19** Look, you are kind to your servant. You show great mercy to me because you save my life. But I cannot run away to the mountains. The disaster will catch me, and I will die.

**20** Look, there is a city near here. I can run to it. The city is small. Please let me run away there. It is only a small city. Then I will live."

**21** The angel said to Lot, "Look, I agree to this request also. I will not destroy the city that you speak about.

**22** Go there quickly! I can do nothing until you get there." Because of this, people call the city Zoar.

**23** The sun was up over the earth when Lot came to Zoar.

**24** Then the LORD sent sulfur and fire from the sky. The sulfur and fire fell on Sodom and Gomorrah.

**25** The LORD destroyed those cities and all the plain. He destroyed all the people in the cities. He also destroyed all the plants on the ground.

**26** But the wife of Lot looked back from behind him. She became a pillar of salt.

**27** Abraham got up early in the morning. He went to the place where he stood in front of the LORD.

**28** Abraham looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and toward all the land of the plain. He saw smoke that went up from the land. The smoke was like the smoke of a furnace.

**29** When God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Abraham. So God sent Lot out of the destruction. God destroyed the cities where Lot lived.

**30** Lot was afraid to live in Zoar. So Lot went up from Zoar with his two daughters. They lived in the mountains. Lot and his two daughters lived in a cave.

**31** The older daughter said to the younger daughter, "Our father is old. There is no man in the land to marry us. All the people of the earth marry, but we cannot.

**32** Come, we will make our father drink wine. Then we will have sexual relations with him. Thus we will have children from our father."

**33** That night the daughters made their father drink wine. The older daughter went in and had sexual relations with her father. Lot did not know when she lay down. He did not know when she got up.

**34** On the next day, the older daughter said to the younger daughter, "Look, last night I had sexual relations with my father. Tonight we will make him drink wine again. Then you go in and have sexual relations with him. Thus we will have children from our father."

**35** That night the daughters again made their father drink wine. The younger daughter went in and had sexual relations with him. Lot did not know when she lay down. He did not know when she got up.

**36** Thus the two daughters of Lot became pregnant by their father.

**37** The older daughter gave birth to a son. She called him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites until today.

**38** The younger daughter also gave birth to a son. She called him Ben-Ammi. He is the father of the people of Ammon until today.

## Chapter 20

**1** Abraham traveled from there toward the land of the South. He lived between Kadesh and Shur. For a time he lived as a foreigner in Gerar.

**2** Abraham said about his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." So Abimelech king of Gerar sent men, and they took Sarah.

**3** But God came to Abimelech in a dream at night. God said to him, "Look, you will die because of the woman that you took. She is the wife of a man."

**4** Abimelech did not go near Sarah. Abimelech said, "Lord, will you kill a nation that did no wrong?

**5** Abraham said to me, 'She is my sister.' And Sarah also said, 'He is my brother.' I did this with a pure heart and clean hands."

**6** God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know that you did this with a pure heart. Thus I stopped you from sin against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.

**7** Now give the wife of the man back to him. He is a prophet. He will pray for you, and you will live. If you do not give her back, you will certainly die. You and all your people will die."

**8** Abimelech got up early in the morning. He called all his servants. He told them all these things. The men were very afraid.

**9** Then Abimelech called Abraham. He said to Abraham, "What did you do to us? What wrong did I do to you? You brought a great sin on me and on my kingdom. You did things to me that a person must not do."

**10** Abimelech also said to Abraham, "Why did you do this thing?"

**11** Abraham said, "I thought, 'The people in this place do not fear God. They will kill me because of my wife.'

**12** Also, Sarah is really my sister. She is the daughter of my father, but she is not the daughter of my mother. Then she became my wife.

**13** God caused me to travel away from the house of my father. Then I said to Sarah, 'Show me this kindness. At each place where we go, say about me, "He is my brother."'"

**14** Then Abimelech took sheep, cattle, male servants, and female servants. He gave them to Abraham. He also gave Sarah, the wife of Abraham, back to him.

**15** Abimelech said, "Look, my land is in front of you. Live where you want."

**16** Abimelech said to Sarah, "Look, I give your brother 1000 pieces of silver. This silver shows all the people with you that you did no wrong. All people will know that you are innocent."

**17** Then Abraham prayed to God. God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants. Then they could have children again.

**18** Before this, the LORD did not let any woman in the house of Abimelech have children. The LORD did this because of Sarah, the wife of Abraham.

## Chapter 21

**1** The LORD visited Sarah as he said. The LORD did for Sarah what he promised.

**2** Sarah became pregnant. She gave birth to a son for Abraham when Abraham was old. The birth occurred at the time that God told him.

**3** Abraham gave the name Isaac to his son. Sarah gave birth to Isaac for him.

**4** When Isaac was 8 days old, Abraham circumcised him. Abraham did as God commanded him.

**5** Abraham was 100 years old when Sarah gave birth to his son Isaac.

**6** Sarah said, "God caused me to laugh. All the people who hear about my son will laugh with me."

**7** She also said, "Nobody could tell Abraham that Sarah will feed children with her milk. But I gave birth to a son for him when he was old."

**8** The child grew, and Sarah stopped and did not feed him with her milk again. On that day, Abraham made a large feast.

**9** Hagar was the Egyptian woman who gave birth to a son for Abraham. Sarah saw that son laugh at Isaac.

**10** So Sarah said to Abraham, "Send away this female slave and her son. The son of this female slave will not get a part of your property with my son Isaac."

**11** Abraham was very sad about the words of Sarah, because Ishmael was his son.

**12** But God said to Abraham, "Do not be sad about the boy and about your female slave. Do all that Sarah tells you. The descendants that I promised to you will come from Isaac."

**13** "I will also make a nation from the son of the female slave, because he is your descendant."

**14** Early in the morning, Abraham got up. He took bread and a skin container of water. He gave them to Hagar and put them on her shoulder. He also gave her the boy and sent her away. Hagar went away. She walked without a direction in the desert of Beersheba.

**15** When all the water in the container was gone, she put the boy under a bush.

**16** Then she went and sat down opposite him, approximately one arrow shot away. She said, "I do not want to see the death of the boy." She sat opposite him, and she cried loudly.

**17** God heard the voice of the boy. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven. He said, "What is the problem, Hagar? Do not be afraid. God heard the voice of the boy where he lies."

**18** "Get up. Lift the boy and hold him with your hand. I will make him into a great nation."

**19** Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the container with water. She gave the boy water to drink.

**20** God was with the boy, and the boy grew. He lived in the desert. He became a man who shot arrows with a bow.

**21** He lived in the desert of Paran. His mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt.

**22** At that time, Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham. They said, "God is with you in all that you do."

**23** "So now, make a promise to me here in the name of God. Promise that you will not deceive me, my son, or my grandson. I was kind to you. Be kind to me and to the land where you live as a foreigner."

**24** Abraham said, "I make that promise."

**25** Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water. The servants of Abimelech took that well by force.

**26** Abimelech said, "I do not know who did that. You did not tell me. I did not hear about the well until today."

**27** Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech. The two men made an agreement (covenant).

**28** Abraham put 7 female lambs of the flock away from the other sheep.

**29** Abimelech asked Abraham, "Why did you put these 7 female lambs away from the other sheep?"

**30** Abraham said, "Take these 7 female lambs from my hand. They will show that I dug this well."

**31** So people called that place Beersheba, because the two men made a promise there.

**32** The two men made an agreement at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, got up. They went back to the land of the Philistines.

**33** Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba. There he prayed to the LORD, the God who lives forever.

**34** Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for many days.

## Chapter 22

**1** After these events, God tested Abraham. God said to him, "Abraham." Abraham said, "I am here."

**2** God said, "Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love. Go to the land of Moriah. Offer Isaac there as a burnt offering on a mountain. I will tell you which mountain."

**3** Early in the morning, Abraham got up and put a saddle on his donkey. He took 2 of his young men and his son Isaac with him. He cut the wood for the burnt offering. Then he went to the place that God told him about.

**4** On the third day, Abraham looked up. He saw the place far away.

**5** Abraham said to his young men, "Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there. We will worship, and then we will come back to you."

**6** Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and put the wood on his son Isaac. He held the fire and the knife in his hand. The two of them walked together.

**7** Isaac spoke to his father Abraham. He said, "My father." Abraham said, "I am here, my son." Isaac said, "Here are the fire and the wood. But where is the lamb for a burnt offering?"

**8** Abraham said, "My son, God will supply the lamb for a burnt offering." So the two of them walked together.

**9** They came to the place that God told Abraham about. Abraham built an altar there and put the wood on the altar. He tied his son Isaac. He put Isaac on the altar, on top of the wood.

**10** Then Abraham extended his hand and took the knife to kill his son.

**11** But the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven. The angel said, "Abraham, Abraham." Abraham said, "I am here."

**12** The angel said, "Do not put your hand on the boy. Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God. You did not keep your son, your only son, from me."

**13** Abraham looked up and saw a ram behind him. A bush held the horns of the ram. Abraham went and took the ram. He offered the ram as a burnt offering in the place of his son.

**14** Abraham gave the name "The LORD Will Supply" to that place. Today people say, "On the mountain of the LORD, the LORD will supply what is necessary."

**15** The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time.

**16** The angel said, "The LORD says this: I make a promise in my own name. You did this action. You did not keep your son, your only son, from me."

**17** "So I will bless you very much. I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky. They will be as many as the sand on the shore of the sea. Your descendants will take the cities of their enemies."

**18** "All the nations of the earth will get a blessing through your descendants, because you obeyed my voice."

**19** Then Abraham went back to his young men. They got up and went together to Beersheba. Abraham lived in Beersheba.

**20** After these events, a person told Abraham, "Milcah also gave birth to children for your brother Nahor."

**21** The first son was Uz. After him came his brother Buz, and Kemuel, the father of Aram.

**22** The other sons had the names Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.

**23** Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah gave birth to these 8 sons for Nahor, the brother of Abraham.

**24** Nahor also had a concubine (a secondary wife) with the name Reumah. She also gave birth to sons. Their names were Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

## Chapter 23

**1** Sarah lived for 127 years. That was the length of the life of Sarah.

**2** Sarah died at Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to cry for her.

**3** Abraham got up from the body of his dead wife. He spoke to the sons of Heth. He said,

**4** "I am a foreigner and a visitor among you. Give me land among you for a grave. Then I can bury my dead wife."

**5** The sons of Heth answered Abraham. They said,

**6** "Sir, listen to us. You are a powerful prince among us. Bury your dead wife in the best of our graves. None of us will refuse his grave to you."

**7** Abraham got up. He bowed down to the people of the land, the sons of Heth.

**8** He spoke to them. He said, "You agree that I bury my dead wife here. So listen to me. Speak for me to Ephron the son of Zohar."

**9** "Ask him to give me the cave of Machpelah. Ephron owns that cave. The cave is at the end of his field. Let him give the cave to me for the full price. Then I will have a grave among you."

**10** Ephron sat among the sons of Heth. Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham. All the sons of Heth at the gate of his city heard him. Ephron said,

**11** "No, sir, listen to me. I give you the field. I also give you the cave in the field. I give them to you in front of the sons of my people. Bury your dead wife."

**12** Abraham bowed down in front of the people of the land.

**13** He spoke to Ephron, and the people of the land heard him. He said, "Please listen to me. I will pay the price of the field. Take the money from me. Then I will bury my dead wife there."

**14** Ephron answered Abraham. He said,

**15** "Sir, listen to me. The land has a value of 400 shekels of silver. That is a small amount between you and me. Bury your dead wife."

**16** Abraham agreed with Ephron. Abraham weighed the silver for Ephron, as Ephron said in front of the sons of Heth. He weighed 400 shekels of silver by the standard of the merchants.

**17** So the field of Ephron in Machpelah, near Mamre, became the property of Abraham. The field, the cave in the field, and all the trees in the area of the field became his property.

**18** The sale occurred in front of the sons of Heth. All the people at the gate of the city of Ephron saw the sale.

**19** After that, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field of Machpelah. The field is near Mamre, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan.

**20** So the sons of Heth gave the field and its cave to Abraham. The field became his property for a grave.

## Chapter 24

**1** Abraham was very old. The LORD blessed Abraham in all things.

**2** Abraham spoke to his oldest servant. That servant controlled all the property of Abraham. Abraham said to him, "Put your hand under my thigh."

**3** "Make a promise in the name of the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth. Promise that you will not get a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites. I live among the Canaanites."

**4** "But go to my country and to my relatives. Get a wife for my son Isaac there."

**5** The servant said to Abraham, "Maybe the woman will not agree to come with me to this land. Then must I take your son back to the land that you came from?"

**6** Abraham said to him, "Make sure that you do not take my son back there."

**7** "The LORD, the God of heaven, took me from the house of my father and from the land of my relatives. He spoke to me and made a promise to me. He said, 'I will give this land to your descendants.' He will send his angel in front of you. You will get a wife for my son from there."

**8** "If the woman does not agree to come with you, then you are free from this promise. But do not take my son back there."

**9** So the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham. He made the promise to Abraham about this task.

**10** The servant took 10 of the camels of his master and left. He took all types of good things from his master with him. He went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.

**11** He made the camels kneel down outside the city, near the well of water. It was evening. That is the time when the women go out to get water.

**12** He said, "LORD, God of my master Abraham, please give me success today. Show kindness to my master Abraham."

**13** "Look, I stand here near the spring of water. The daughters of the men of the city come out to get water."

**14** "I will say to a young woman, 'Please lower your jar so that I can drink.' Maybe she will say, 'Drink, and I will also give water to your camels.' Then I will know that she is the woman that you chose for your servant Isaac. Then I will know that you showed kindness to my master."

**15** Before he stopped his words, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. Rebekah was the daughter of Bethuel. Bethuel was the son of Milcah. Milcah was the wife of Nahor, the brother of Abraham.

**16** The young woman was very beautiful. She was a virgin. No man slept with her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up.

**17** The servant ran to meet her. He said, "Please give me a small quantity of water from your jar."

**18** She said, "Drink, sir." Quickly she lowered her jar onto her hand and gave him a drink.
