**19** When she finished, she said, "I will also get water for your camels. I will give them all the water that they need."

**20** Quickly she emptied her jar into the water container for the animals. Then she ran again to the well to get more water. She got water for all his camels.

**21** The man looked at her and said nothing. He wanted to know if the LORD gave him success on his journey.

**22** When the camels finished their drink, the man took a gold ring for her nose. The weight of the ring was a half shekel. He also took 2 gold bracelets for her arms. The weight of the bracelets was 10 shekels.

**23** He said, "Please tell me, whose daughter are you? Is there space in the house of your father for us for the night?"

**24** She said to him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel. Bethuel is the son of Milcah. Milcah gave birth to Bethuel for Nahor."

**25** She also said to him, "We have much straw and food for animals. We also have space for you for the night."

**26** The man bowed his head and worshipped the LORD.

**27** He said, "I praise the LORD, the God of my master Abraham. The LORD did not stop his kindness and his truth to my master. The LORD guided me on the road to the house of the relatives of my master."

**28** The young woman ran to the house of her mother. She told the people there about these events.

**29** Rebekah had a brother with the name Laban. Laban ran out to the man at the spring.

**30** Laban saw the nose ring and the bracelets on the arms of his sister. He heard the words of his sister Rebekah: "The man spoke these words to me." So Laban went to the man. The man stood near the camels at the spring.

**31** Laban said, "Come in, man whom the LORD blesses. Why do you stand outside? I prepared the house and a place for the camels."

**32** So the man came into the house. Laban took the loads off the camels. He gave straw and food to the camels. He gave water to the man and to the men with him to wash their feet.

**33** Then they put food in front of the man. But he said, "I will not eat until I tell you my message." Laban said, "Speak."

**34** The man said, "I am the servant of Abraham."

**35** "The LORD blessed my master very much, and my master became rich. The LORD gave him sheep and cattle, silver and gold. He also gave him male servants, female servants, camels, and donkeys."

**36** "Sarah, the wife of my master, gave birth to a son for my master when she was old. My master gave all his property to that son."

**37** "My master caused me to make a promise. He said, 'Do not get a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites. I live in their land.'"

**38** "He said, 'Go to the house of my father and to my relatives. Get a wife for my son there.'"

**39** "I said to my master, 'Maybe the woman will not come with me.'"

**40** "He said to me, 'I live to obey the LORD. The LORD will send his angel with you. He will give you success on your journey. You will get a wife for my son from my relatives and from the house of my father.'"

**41** "'Then you will be free from my promise when you go to my relatives. If they do not give her to you, you will be free from my promise.'"

**42** "Today I came to the spring. I said, 'LORD, God of my master Abraham, please give me success on this journey.'"

**43** "'Look, I stand near the spring of water. A young woman will come out to get water. I will say to her, "Please give me a small quantity of water from your jar."'"

**44** "'She will say to me, "Drink, and I will also get water for your camels." Let that woman be the wife that the LORD chose for the son of my master.'"

**45** "Before I stopped my words in my heart, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and got water. I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'"

**46** "Quickly she lowered her jar from her shoulder. She said, 'Drink, and I will also give water to your camels.' So I drank. She also gave water to the camels."

**47** "I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' She said, 'I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor. Milcah gave birth to Bethuel for Nahor.' Then I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms."

**48** "I bowed my head and worshipped the LORD. I praised the LORD, the God of my master Abraham. The LORD guided me on the correct road. He brought me to the family of the brother of my master. Now I can take a wife from that family for the son of my master."

**49** "Now tell me if you will show kindness and truth to my master. If you will not, tell me. Then I will know where to go next."

**50** Laban and Bethuel answered, "The LORD caused this event. We cannot say anything bad or good to you."

**51** "Rebekah is here in front of you. Take her and go. Let her become the wife of the son of your master, as the LORD said."

**52** The servant of Abraham heard their words. He bowed down to the ground in front of the LORD.

**53** The servant brought out silver jewelry, gold jewelry, and clothes. He gave them to Rebekah. He also gave valuable gifts to her brother and to her mother.

**54** Then the servant and the men with him ate and drank. They stayed there for the night. In the morning they got up. The servant said, "Send me back to my master."

**55** Her brother and her mother said, "Let the young woman stay with us for some days, at least 10 days. After that, she will go."

**56** But the servant said to them, "Do not stop me. The LORD gave me success on my journey. Send me away so that I can go to my master."

**57** They said, "We will call the young woman. We will ask her what she wants."

**58** They called Rebekah and said to her, "Will you go with this man?" She said, "I will go."

**59** So they sent away their sister Rebekah and her nurse. They also sent away the servant of Abraham and his men.

**60** They gave a blessing to Rebekah. They said to her, "Our sister, become the mother of thousands of millions. Let your descendants take the cities of their enemies."

**61** Rebekah and her female servants got up. They got on the camels and went with the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.

**62** Isaac came from the road to the well of Lahai Roi. He lived in the land of the south (the Negev).

**63** In the evening, Isaac went out to the field to think and to pray. He looked up and saw camels. The camels came near.

**64** Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac. She got down from the camel.

**65** She said to the servant, "Who is that man? He walks in the field to meet us." The servant said, "He is my master." So Rebekah took her veil and covered her face.

**66** The servant told Isaac all the things that he did.

**67** Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent of his mother Sarah. Rebekah became his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac got comfort after the death of his mother.

## Chapter 25

**1** Abraham took another wife. Her name was Keturah.

**2** Keturah gave birth to these sons for Abraham: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

**3** Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan. The descendants of Dedan were the Asshurim, the Letushim, and the Leummim.

**4** The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these people were descendants of Keturah.

**5** Abraham gave all his property to Isaac.

**6** But Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines (secondary wives). While Abraham was alive, he sent these sons away from his son Isaac. He sent them to the east, to the country of the east.

**7** Abraham lived for 175 years.

**8** Abraham took his last breath and died at a good old age. He was old and satisfied with his life. He joined his ancestors in death.

**9** His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah. The cave is in the field of Ephron, the son of Zohar the Hittite. The field is near Mamre.

**10** Abraham bought that field from the sons of Heth. His sons buried Abraham there, with his wife Sarah.

**11** After the death of Abraham, God blessed his son Isaac. Isaac lived near the well of Lahai Roi.

**12** This is the list of the descendants of Ishmael, the son of Abraham. Hagar the Egyptian, the female servant of Sarah, gave birth to Ishmael for Abraham.

**13** These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, in the sequence of their births. Nebaioth was the first son of Ishmael. Then came Kedar, Adbeel, and Mibsam.

**14** After them came Mishma, Dumah, and Massa.

**15** After them came Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.

**16** These are the sons of Ishmael. These are their names, by their towns and by their camps. They were 12 princes of their tribes.

**17** Ishmael lived for 137 years. He took his last breath and died. He joined his ancestors in death.

**18** The descendants of Ishmael lived in the area from Havilah to Shur. Shur is east of Egypt, in the direction of Assyria. They lived in opposition to all their relatives.

**19** This is the list of the descendants of Isaac, the son of Abraham. Abraham became the father of Isaac.

**20** Isaac was 40 years old when he married Rebekah. Rebekah was the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan Aram. She was the sister of Laban the Aramean.

**21** Rebekah could not have children. So Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife. The LORD answered his prayer, and Rebekah became pregnant.

**22** The children pushed against each other inside her. She said, "Why does this occur to me?" So she went to ask the LORD.

**23** The LORD said to her, "2 nations are in your womb. 2 peoples will come from your body and separate. One people will be stronger than the other people. The older will serve the younger."

**24** The time for the birth came. There were twins in her womb.

**25** The first son came out red. His body was like a coat of hair. They gave him the name Esau.

**26** After that, his brother came out. The hand of his brother held the heel of Esau. So they gave him the name Jacob. Isaac was 60 years old when Rebekah gave birth to them.

**27** The boys grew. Esau became a skilled hunter, a man of the fields. Jacob was a quiet man. He lived in tents.

**28** Isaac loved Esau, because Isaac ate the meat of the animals that Esau hunted. But Rebekah loved Jacob.

**29** One day Jacob cooked a stew. Esau came in from the field, and he was very tired.

**30** Esau said to Jacob, "Please give me some of that red stew. I am very tired." That is why people called him Edom. The name Edom means "red."

**31** Jacob said, "First, sell me your birthright (the special rights of the first son)."

**32** Esau said, "Look, I am almost dead. My birthright has no use to me."

**33** Jacob said, "First, make a promise to me." So Esau made a promise to Jacob. He sold his birthright to Jacob.

**34** Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. Esau ate and drank. Then he got up and went away. So Esau showed that his birthright had no value to him.

## Chapter 26

**1** There was a famine (a time with no food) in the land. This famine was not the first famine, which occurred in the time of Abraham. Isaac went to Gerar, to Abimelech, the king of the Philistines.

**2** The LORD showed himself to Isaac. The LORD said, "Do not go down to Egypt. Live in the land that I will tell you about."

**3** "Live as a foreigner in this land. I will be with you, and I will bless you. I will give all these lands to you and to your descendants. I will do what I promised to your father Abraham."

**4** "I will make your descendants as many as the stars of the sky. I will give all these lands to your descendants. All the nations of the earth will get a blessing through your descendants."

**5** "I will do these things because Abraham obeyed my voice. He kept my orders, my commands, my rules, and my laws."

**6** So Isaac lived in Gerar.

**7** The men of that place asked Isaac about his wife. He said, "She is my sister." He was afraid to say, "She is my wife." He thought, "The men of this place will kill me to get Rebekah, because she is beautiful."

**8** Isaac lived there for a long time. One day Abimelech, the king of the Philistines, looked out of a window. He saw Isaac touch his wife Rebekah with love.

**9** Abimelech called Isaac. He said, "Surely she is your wife. Why did you say, 'She is my sister'?" Isaac said to him, "I thought, 'A man will kill me to get her.'"

**10** Abimelech said, "Why did you do this to us? A man of our people could easily sleep with your wife. Then we will be guilty because of you."

**11** So Abimelech gave an order to all the people. He said, "If a person touches this man or his wife, we will kill that person."

**12** Isaac planted seeds in that land. In that year he got 100 times more than he planted. The LORD blessed him.

**13** Isaac became rich. He continued to get more property until he became very rich.

**14** He had flocks of sheep, herds of cattle, and many servants. So the Philistines were jealous of him.

**15** In the time of Abraham, the servants of Abraham dug wells. The Philistines filled all these wells with earth.

**16** Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go away from us. You are much more powerful than we are."

**17** So Isaac went away from there. He put up his tents in the valley of Gerar and lived there.

**18** People dug wells of water in the time of his father Abraham. The Philistines filled these wells after the death of Abraham. Isaac dug these wells again. He gave the wells the same names that his father gave them.

**19** The servants of Isaac dug in the valley. They found a well of fresh water there.

**20** The shepherds of Gerar argued with the shepherds of Isaac. They said, "The water is ours." So Isaac gave the name Esek to the well, because they argued with him. The name Esek means "argument."

**21** Then the servants of Isaac dug another well. The shepherds of Gerar also argued about that well. So Isaac gave the well the name Sitnah. The name Sitnah means "opposition."

**22** Isaac went away from there and dug another well. The shepherds did not argue about that well. So Isaac gave the well the name Rehoboth. The name Rehoboth means "wide areas." He said, "Now the LORD gave us space. We will increase in this land."

**23** From there, Isaac went up to Beersheba.

**24** That night the LORD showed himself to Isaac. He said, "I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, because I am with you. I will bless you and make your descendants many. I will do this because of my servant Abraham."

**25** Isaac built an altar there and prayed to the LORD. He put up his tent there. The servants of Isaac dug a well there.

**26** Then Abimelech came to Isaac from Gerar. His friend Ahuzzath and Phicol, the commander of his army, came with him.

**27** Isaac said to them, "Why did you come to me? You hate me, and you sent me away from you."

**28** They said, "We saw clearly that the LORD is with you. So we said, 'Let there be a promise between us and you.' We want to make an agreement (covenant) with you."

**29** "Promise that you will not hurt us. We did not touch you. We did only good things to you, and we sent you away in peace. Now the LORD blesses you."

**30** Isaac made a feast for them. They ate and drank.

**31** Early in the morning, they got up and made promises to each other. Then Isaac sent them away, and they left him in peace.

**32** On that same day, the servants of Isaac came to him. They told him about a well that they dug. They said, "We found water."

**33** Isaac gave the well the name Shibah. So the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.

**34** When Esau was 40 years old, he married Judith, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite. He also married Basemath, the daughter of Elon the Hittite.

**35** These 2 wives caused much sadness to Isaac and Rebekah.

## Chapter 27

**1** Isaac became old, and his eyes became weak. He could not see. He called his older son Esau. He said to him, "My son." Esau said to him, "I am here."

**2** Isaac said, "Look, I am old. I do not know the day of my death."

**3** "So now, take your weapons, your arrows and your bow. Go out to the field and hunt an animal for me."

**4** "Make good food for me, the food that I like. Bring the food to me so that I can eat. Then I will give you my blessing before I die."

**5** Rebekah listened when Isaac spoke to his son Esau. Esau went to the field to hunt an animal and bring it back.

**6** Rebekah spoke to her son Jacob. She said, "I heard your father speak to your brother Esau."

**7** "Your father said to Esau, 'Bring me an animal and make good food for me. I will eat. Then I will bless you in front of the LORD before I die.'"

**8** "So now, my son, obey my voice. Do what I tell you."

**9** "Go to the flock and get 2 good young goats for me. I will make good food for your father with the goats. I will make the food that he likes."

**10** "Then take the food to your father so that he can eat. Then he will give you his blessing before he dies."

**11** Jacob said to his mother Rebekah, "My brother Esau has much hair on his body. But my skin is smooth."

**12** "Maybe my father will touch me. Then he will know that I deceive him. Then I will bring a curse on me, not a blessing."

**13** His mother said to him, "Let the curse come on me, my son. Only obey my voice. Go and get the goats for me."

**14** So Jacob went and got the goats. He brought them to his mother. His mother made good food, the food that his father liked.

**15** Then Rebekah took the best clothes of her older son Esau. These clothes were with her in the house. She put the clothes on her younger son Jacob.

**16** She put the skins of the young goats on his hands. She also put the skins on the smooth part of his neck.

**17** Then she gave the good food and the bread that she made to her son Jacob.

**18** Jacob went to his father and said, "My father." Isaac said, "I am here. Who are you, my son?"

**19** Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau, your first son. I did what you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my meat. Then give me your blessing."

**20** Isaac said to his son, "How did you find the animal so quickly, my son?" Jacob said, "The LORD your God gave me success."

**21** Isaac said to Jacob, "Please come near. I want to touch you, my son. Then I will know if you are my son Esau or not."

**22** Jacob went near to his father Isaac. Isaac touched him and said, "The voice is the voice of Jacob. But the hands are the hands of Esau."

**23** Isaac did not know that the man was Jacob. The hands of Jacob had hair, like the hands of his brother Esau. So Isaac blessed Jacob.

**24** Isaac said, "Are you really my son Esau?" Jacob said, "I am."

**25** Isaac said, "Bring the food to me. I will eat the meat of my son. Then I will give you my blessing." Jacob brought the food to him, and Isaac ate. Jacob also brought him wine, and Isaac drank.

**26** Then his father Isaac said to him, "Come near now and kiss me, my son."

**27** Jacob came near and kissed him. Isaac smelled the clothes of Jacob and blessed him. He said, "The smell of my son is like the smell of a field. The LORD blessed that field."

**28** "Let God give you the water of the sky and the good things of the earth. Let him give you much grain and new wine."

**29** "Let peoples serve you. Let nations bow down to you. Be the master of your brothers. Let the sons of your mother bow down to you. Each person who curses you will get a curse. Each person who blesses you will get a blessing."

**30** Isaac finished his blessing of Jacob. Jacob went away from his father Isaac. Then immediately his brother Esau came in from his hunt.

**31** Esau also made good food and brought the food to his father. He said to his father, "My father, sit up and eat the meat of your son. Then give me your blessing."

**32** His father Isaac said to him, "Who are you?" Esau said, "I am your son, your first son, Esau."

**33** Isaac shook very much. He said, "Then who hunted an animal and brought it to me? I ate all of the food before you came. I blessed that man. Yes, that man will keep the blessing."

**34** Esau heard the words of his father. He cried out with a loud and bitter cry. He said to his father, "Bless me also, my father."

**35** Isaac said, "Your brother came and deceived me. He took your blessing."

**36** Esau said, "The name Jacob is correct for him. He deceived me 2 times. He took my birthright. Now he took my blessing." Then Esau asked, "Did you not keep a blessing for me?"

**37** Isaac answered Esau, "Look, I made Jacob your master. I gave all his brothers to him as servants. I gave him grain and new wine. So what can I do for you, my son?"

**38** Esau said to his father, "Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me also, my father." Then Esau cried loudly.

**39** His father Isaac answered him. He said, "You will live far from the good things of the earth. You will live far from the water of the sky."

**40** "You will live by your sword. You will serve your brother. But when you become free, you will remove his control from your neck."

**41** Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing that his father gave to Jacob. Esau said in his heart, "My father will die soon. After the time of sadness for my father, I will kill my brother Jacob."

**42** A person told Rebekah the words of her older son Esau. So she sent for her younger son Jacob. She said to him, "Your brother Esau gets comfort from a plan. He plans to kill you."

**43** "So now, my son, obey my voice. Get up and go quickly to my brother Laban in Haran."

**44** "Stay with Laban for some days, until the anger of your brother stops."

**45** "Stay until your brother is not angry with you. Stay until he forgets what you did to him. Then I will send a message and bring you back from there. I do not want to lose both of you in one day."

**46** Then Rebekah said to Isaac, "I hate my life because of the Hittite women. Maybe Jacob will marry a Hittite woman like these women from this land. Then my life will have no value to me."

## Chapter 28

**1** Isaac called Jacob and blessed him. Isaac gave him an order. He said, "Do not marry a woman from the daughters of Canaan."

**2** "Get up and go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethuel, the father of your mother. Marry a daughter of Laban, the brother of your mother."

**3** "Let God Almighty bless you. Let him give you many children and make your descendants many. Then you will become a large group of peoples."

**4** "Let God give you and your descendants the blessing of Abraham. Then you will own the land where you now live as a foreigner. God gave that land to Abraham."

**5** So Isaac sent Jacob away. Jacob went to Paddan Aram, to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean. Laban was the brother of Rebekah. Rebekah was the mother of Jacob and Esau.

**6** Esau saw that Isaac blessed Jacob. He saw that Isaac sent Jacob to Paddan Aram to get a wife there. He saw that Isaac gave Jacob an order: "Do not marry a woman from the daughters of Canaan."

**7** Esau also saw that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother. Jacob went to Paddan Aram.

**8** Esau saw that his father Isaac did not like the daughters of Canaan.

**9** So Esau went to Ishmael. He married Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, the son of Abraham. Mahalath was the sister of Nebaioth. She became the wife of Esau, in addition to his other wives.

**10** Jacob left Beersheba and went in the direction of Haran.

**11** He came to a place and stayed there for the night, because the sun went down. He took one of the stones of that place and put the stone under his head. He lay down in that place to sleep.

**12** Jacob had a dream. He saw a ladder that stood on the earth. The top of the ladder touched heaven. The angels of God went up and came down on the ladder.

**13** The LORD stood above the ladder. He said, "I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you the land where you lie. I will give that land to you and to your descendants."

**14** "Your descendants will be as many as the dust of the earth. You will spread to the west, the east, the north, and the south. All the families of the earth will get a blessing through you and your descendants."

**15** "Look, I am with you. I will keep you safe in all places where you go. I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I do all that I promised to you."

**16** Jacob woke up from his sleep. He said, "Surely the LORD is in this place, and I did not know that."

**17** He was afraid and said, "This place causes fear! This place is the house of God. This place is the gate of heaven."

**18** Early in the morning, Jacob got up. He took the stone that he put under his head. He set up the stone as a memorial stone (pillar). He poured oil on top of the stone.

**19** He gave that place the name Bethel. The name Bethel means "house of God." Before that time, the name of the city was Luz.

**20** Then Jacob made a vow (a solemn promise). He said, "God, be with me. Keep me safe on this journey. Give me bread to eat and clothes to wear."

**21** "Bring me back to the house of my father in peace. If you do these things, then the LORD will be my God."

**22** "This stone that I set up as a memorial stone will be the house of God. I will give to you one tenth of all that you give me."

## Chapter 29

**1** Jacob continued his journey. He went to the land of the people of the east.

**2** He looked and saw a well in a field. 3 flocks of sheep lay near the well. The shepherds gave water to the flocks from that well. A large stone was on the mouth of the well.

**3** The shepherds gathered all the flocks there. Then they rolled the stone off the mouth of the well. They gave water to the sheep. Then they put the stone back in its place on the mouth of the well.

**4** Jacob said to the shepherds, "My brothers, where do you come from?" They said, "We come from Haran."

**5** He said to them, "Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?" They said, "We know him."

**6** He said to them, "Is Laban well?" They said, "He is well. Look, his daughter Rachel comes with the sheep."

**7** Jacob said, "Look, the sun is still high. It is not the time to gather the animals. Give water to the sheep. Then go and let them eat grass."

**8** They said, "We cannot do that until all the flocks come together. Then the shepherds roll the stone off the mouth of the well. Then we give water to the sheep."

**9** While Jacob spoke with them, Rachel came with the sheep of her father. She was a shepherd.

**10** Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Laban, the brother of his mother. He also saw the sheep of Laban. Jacob went near and rolled the stone off the mouth of the well. He gave water to the flock of Laban.

**11** Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and he cried loudly.

**12** Jacob told Rachel that he was a relative of her father. He told her that he was the son of Rebekah. Rachel ran and told her father.

**13** Laban heard the news about Jacob, the son of his sister. Laban ran to meet him. He held Jacob in his arms and kissed him. He brought Jacob to his house. Jacob told Laban about all these events.

**14** Laban said to him, "Surely you are my bone and my flesh." Jacob stayed with Laban for a month.

**15** Then Laban said to Jacob, "You are my relative. But you must not work for me for no pay. Tell me what your pay must be."

**16** Laban had 2 daughters. The name of the older daughter was Leah. The name of the younger daughter was Rachel.

**17** The eyes of Leah were weak. But Rachel had a beautiful body and a beautiful face.

**18** Jacob loved Rachel. He said, "I will work for you for 7 years to get your younger daughter Rachel."

**19** Laban said, "I prefer to give Rachel to you, not to another man. Stay with me."

**20** So Jacob worked for 7 years to get Rachel. The 7 years were like a few days to him, because he loved her.

**21** Then Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wife. My time of work is complete. I want to sleep with her."

**22** So Laban gathered all the men of that place and made a feast.

**23** In the evening, Laban took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob. Jacob slept with her.

**24** Laban gave his female servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her servant.

**25** In the morning, Jacob saw that the woman was Leah. He said to Laban, "What did you do to me? I worked for you to get Rachel. Why did you deceive me?"

**26** Laban said, "In our country, we do not give the younger daughter in marriage before the first daughter."

**27** "Complete the week of marriage with Leah. Then we will also give Rachel to you. In return, you will work for me for 7 more years."

**28** Jacob did that. He completed the week with Leah. Then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.

**29** Laban gave his female servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her servant.

**30** Jacob also slept with Rachel. He loved Rachel more than Leah. He worked for Laban for 7 more years.

**31** The LORD saw that Jacob did not love Leah. So the LORD made Leah able to have children. But Rachel could not have children.

**32** Leah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She gave him the name Reuben. She said, "The LORD saw my trouble. Now my husband will love me."

**33** Leah became pregnant again and gave birth to a son. She said, "The LORD heard that my husband does not love me. So he also gave me this son." She gave him the name Simeon.

**34** Leah became pregnant again and gave birth to a son. She said, "Now my husband will join himself to me, because I gave him 3 sons." So she gave him the name Levi.

**35** Leah became pregnant again and gave birth to a son. She said, "Now I will praise the LORD." So she gave him the name Judah. Then for some time she did not have more children.

## Chapter 30

**1** Rachel saw that she did not give children to Jacob. So she was jealous of her sister. She said to Jacob, "Give me children, or I will die."

**2** Jacob became angry with Rachel. He said, "I am not God. God did not let you have children."

**3** Rachel said, "Here is my female servant Bilhah. Sleep with her. She will give birth to children on my knees. Then I can also have children through her."

**4** So Rachel gave her female servant Bilhah to Jacob as a wife. Jacob slept with Bilhah.

**5** Bilhah became pregnant and gave birth to a son for Jacob.

**6** Rachel said, "God judged me. He also heard my voice and gave me a son." So she gave him the name Dan.

**7** Bilhah, the female servant of Rachel, became pregnant again. She gave birth to a second son for Jacob.

**8** Rachel said, "I fought a hard fight with my sister, and I won." So she gave him the name Naphtali.

**9** Leah saw that she did not have more children. So she took her female servant Zilpah. She gave Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.

**10** Zilpah, the female servant of Leah, gave birth to a son for Jacob.

**11** Leah said, "Good fortune came!" So she gave him the name Gad.

**12** Zilpah, the female servant of Leah, gave birth to a second son for Jacob.

**13** Leah said, "I am happy! The women will call me happy." So she gave him the name Asher.

**14** In the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben went into the fields. He found mandrakes (a plant). He brought the mandrakes to his mother Leah. Rachel said to Leah, "Please give me some of the mandrakes of your son."

**15** Leah said to her, "You took my husband from me. Is that a small thing? Now do you also want to take the mandrakes of my son?" Rachel said, "Then Jacob will sleep with you tonight. That is my payment for the mandrakes of your son."

**16** Jacob came from the field in the evening. Leah went out to meet him. She said, "You must sleep with me tonight. I paid for you with the mandrakes of my son." So Jacob slept with Leah that night.

**17** God listened to Leah. She became pregnant and gave birth to a fifth son for Jacob.

**18** Leah said, "God gave me my pay, because I gave my female servant to my husband." So she gave him the name Issachar.

**19** Leah became pregnant again. She gave birth to a sixth son for Jacob.

**20** Leah said, "God gave me a good gift. Now my husband will live with me, because I gave him 6 sons." So she gave him the name Zebulun.

**21** After that, Leah gave birth to a daughter. She gave her the name Dinah.

**22** Then God remembered Rachel. God listened to her and made her able to have children.

**23** Rachel became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She said, "God took away my shame."

**24** She gave him the name Joseph. She said, "Let the LORD give me another son."

**25** After Rachel gave birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Send me away. I want to go to my own place and to my own country."

**26** "Give me my wives and my children. I worked for you to get them. Then I will go. You know how much work I did for you."

**27** Laban said to him, "Please stay, if you are my friend. I learned from signs that the LORD blessed me because of you."

**28** Laban also said, "Tell me your pay, and I will give it to you."

**29** Jacob said to him, "You know how I worked for you. You know how your animals increased while I kept them."

**30** "You had a small number of animals before I came. Now you have a very large number. The LORD blessed you in all places where I went. But when will I get property for my own family?"

**31** Laban said, "What will I give you?" Jacob said, "Do not give me anything. But do one thing for me. Then I will again feed your flock and keep it safe."

**32** "Today I will go through all your flocks. I will remove each sheep with spots and each dark lamb. I will also remove each goat with spots. These animals will be my pay."

**33** "In the future, my honesty will show the truth. You will come to look at my pay. If you find with me a goat without spots, then I stole that goat. If you find a lamb that is not dark, then I stole that lamb."

**34** Laban said, "Good. I agree with your words."

**35** But on that day, Laban removed the male goats with stripes or spots. He removed all the female goats with spots, and each goat with white on it. He also removed each dark lamb. He gave these animals to his sons to keep.

**36** Laban put a distance of 3 days of travel between himself and Jacob. Jacob fed the rest of the flocks of Laban.

**37** Jacob took fresh sticks from poplar trees, almond trees, and plane trees. He cut white stripes in the sticks. He removed parts of the bark and showed the white wood under the bark.

**38** He put the sticks in front of the flocks, in the water containers. The flocks came to the water containers to drink. The animals mated when they came to drink.

**39** The flocks mated in front of the sticks. The flocks gave birth to young animals with stripes and spots.

**40** Jacob put the lambs away from the other animals. He turned the faces of the flocks of Laban toward the animals with stripes and the dark animals. He kept his own flocks away from the flocks of Laban.

**41** When the strong animals mated, Jacob put the sticks in the water containers in front of them. Then the animals mated near the sticks.

**42** But when the weak animals came, Jacob did not put the sticks there. So the weak animals became the property of Laban. The strong animals became the property of Jacob.

**43** So Jacob became very rich. He had large flocks, female servants, male servants, camels, and donkeys.

## Chapter 31

**1** Jacob heard the words of the sons of Laban. They said, "Jacob took all that our father had. He got all his wealth from the property of our father."

**2** Jacob saw the face of Laban. Laban was not friendly to him as before.

**3** The LORD said to Jacob, "Go back to the land of your fathers and to your family. I will be with you."

**4** Jacob sent a message to Rachel and Leah. He told them to come to the field where his flocks were.

**5** He said to them, "I see the face of your father. He is not friendly to me as before. But the God of my father was with me.

**6** You know that I worked for your father with all my strength.

**7** But your father lied to me. He changed my pay 10 times. But God did not let him hurt me.

**8** When he said, 'The animals with spots will be your pay,' then all the flocks gave birth to animals with spots. When he said, 'The animals with stripes will be your pay,' then all the flocks gave birth to animals with stripes.

**9** Thus God took the animals of your father and gave them to me.

**10** At the time when the flocks mated, I had a dream. In the dream I looked up. I saw that the male goats that mated with the flocks had stripes, spots, and marks.

**11** The angel of God spoke to me in the dream. He said, 'Jacob.' I said, 'I am here.'

**12** He said, 'Look up and see. All the male goats that mate with the flocks have stripes, spots, and marks. I saw all that Laban does to you.

**13** I am the God of Bethel. At Bethel you put oil on a stone pillar. There you made a promise (vow) to me. Now get up. Go out of this land. Go back to the land of your birth.'"

**14** Rachel and Leah answered him. They said, "We do not have a part or an inheritance in the house of our father now.

**15** He thinks that we are foreigners. He sold us. Then he used all the money that he got for us.

**16** God took all the wealth from our father. That wealth is ours and our children's. So do all that God told you."

**17** Then Jacob got up. He put his sons and his wives on camels.

**18** He took all his animals and all the property that he got in Paddan Aram. He started to go to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.

**19** Laban went away to cut the wool of his sheep. Then Rachel stole the household idols of her father.

**20** Jacob tricked Laban the Aramean. He did not tell Laban that he went away.

**21** Thus Jacob ran away with all that he had. He crossed the Euphrates River. He went in the direction of the hill country of Gilead.

**22** On the third day, a person told Laban that Jacob ran away.

**23** Laban took his relatives with him. He followed Jacob for 7 days. He came near to Jacob in the hill country of Gilead.

**24** In the night, God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream. God said to him, "Be careful. Do not say good or bad things to Jacob."

**25** Laban came to Jacob. Jacob put up his tent in the hill country. Laban and his relatives also put up their tents in the hill country of Gilead.

**26** Laban said to Jacob, "Why did you do this? You tricked me. You took my daughters away like prisoners of war.

**27** Why did you run away secretly? Why did you trick me? Why did you not tell me? I could send you away with joy, with songs, with drums, and with harps.

**28** You did not let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. You did a foolish thing.

**29** I have the power to hurt you. But last night the God of your father spoke to me. He said, 'Be careful. Do not say good or bad things to Jacob.'

**30** Now you go away because you want to go back to the house of your father. But why did you steal my gods?"

**31** Jacob answered Laban, "I was afraid. I thought that you will take your daughters from me by force.

**32** If you find your gods with a person, that person will die. In front of our relatives, look for your property among my things. Take what is yours." Jacob did not know that Rachel stole the idols.

**33** Laban went into the tent of Jacob, into the tent of Leah, and into the tent of the 2 female servants. He did not find the idols. Then he went out of the tent of Leah. He went into the tent of Rachel.

**34** Rachel took the idols and put them in the saddle of her camel. She sat on them. Laban looked through all the tent, but he did not find the idols.

**35** Rachel said to her father, "Do not be angry, my lord. I cannot stand up in front of you. I have my monthly period." Laban looked for the idols, but he did not find them.

**36** Then Jacob became angry. He argued with Laban. He said, "What did I do wrong? What is my sin? Why do you follow me so angrily?

**37** You looked through all my things. What did you find from your household? Put it here in front of my relatives and your relatives. Let them decide between the 2 of us.

**38** I was with you for 20 years. Your female sheep and your female goats did not lose their young. I did not eat the rams from your flocks.

**39** When wild animals killed one of your animals, I did not bring it to you. I paid for the loss myself. You made me pay for all the animals that thieves stole in the day or in the night.

**40** In the day, the heat hurt me. In the night, the cold hurt me. I could not sleep.

**41** I was in your house for 20 years. I worked 14 years for your 2 daughters. I worked 6 years for your flocks. You changed my pay 10 times.

**42** The God of my father was with me. He is the God of Abraham and the God whom Isaac fears. Without him, you will send me away with nothing now. But God saw my trouble and my hard work. So he told you that you were wrong last night."

**43** Laban answered Jacob, "These women are my daughters. These children are my children. These flocks are my flocks. All that you see is mine. But what can I do now about my daughters and their children?

**44** Come now. We will make an agreement (covenant), you and I. The agreement will be a witness between us."

**45** So Jacob took a stone. He put it up as a pillar.

**46** Jacob said to his relatives, "Collect stones." They collected stones and made a pile. They ate there, near the pile of stones.

**47** Laban gave the pile the name Jegar Sahadutha. Jacob gave the pile the name Galeed.

**48** Laban said, "This pile of stones is a witness between you and me today." That is why people call it Galeed.

**49** The pile also has the name Mizpah. Laban said, "The LORD will watch between you and me when we are apart.

**50** Do not hurt my daughters. Do not take other wives in addition to my daughters. No person is with us, but God is the witness between you and me."

**51** Laban said to Jacob, "Look at this pile of stones. Look at this pillar. I put them between you and me.

**52** This pile is a witness. This pillar is a witness. I will not go past this pile to hurt you. You will not go past this pile and this pillar to hurt me.

**53** The God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, will be the judge between us." Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the God whom his father Isaac feared.

**54** Jacob gave a sacrifice on the mountain. He told his relatives to come and eat food. They ate food and stayed all night on the mountain.

**55** Early in the morning, Laban got up. He kissed his grandchildren and his daughters. He gave them his blessing. Then Laban went back to his home.

## Chapter 32

**1** Jacob continued on his journey. The angels of God met him.

**2** When Jacob saw them, he said, "This is the army of God." So he gave that place the name Mahanaim.

**3** Jacob sent messengers in front of him to his brother Esau. Esau lived in the land of Seir, in the country of Edom.

**4** Jacob told the messengers, "Say this to my lord Esau: 'Your servant Jacob says this. I lived with Laban. I stayed there until now.

**5** I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male servants, and female servants. I send this message to my lord. I hope that you will be kind to me.'"

**6** The messengers came back to Jacob. They said, "We went to your brother Esau. Now he comes to meet you. 400 men are with him."

**7** Jacob was very afraid and troubled. He divided the people with him into 2 groups. He also divided the flocks, the cattle, and the camels into 2 groups.

**8** He thought, "Esau can come and attack one group. Then the other group can escape."

**9** Then Jacob said, "You are the God of my father Abraham and the God of my father Isaac. LORD, you told me, 'Go back to your country and to your family. I will do good to you.'

**10** I am not worthy of all your kindness and faithfulness to me, your servant. I crossed this Jordan River with only my stick. Now I have enough for 2 groups.

**11** Please save me from my brother Esau. I am afraid of him. He can come and attack me, the mothers, and the children.

**12** But you said, 'I will do good to you. I will make your descendants as many as the sand of the sea. No person can count them.'"

**13** Jacob stayed there that night. He took a gift for his brother Esau from his property.

**14** The gift was 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 female sheep, 20 rams,

**15** 30 female camels with their young, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys.

**16** He gave each herd to one of his servants. He said to his servants, "Go in front of me. Keep a space between the herds."

**17** He told the first servant, "My brother Esau will meet you. He will ask you, 'Who is your master? Where do you go? Who owns these animals in front of you?'

**18** Then say, 'They are the property of your servant Jacob. They are a gift for my lord Esau. Jacob comes behind us.'"

**19** He gave the same instructions to the second servant, the third servant, and to all the servants that followed the herds. He said, "Say these words to Esau when you meet him.

**20** Also say, 'Your servant Jacob comes behind us.'" Jacob thought, "I will make Esau calm with the gifts that go in front of me. Then I will see him. Maybe he will accept me."

**21** So the gifts went in front of Jacob. Jacob stayed that night in the camp.

**22** That night Jacob got up. He took his 2 wives, his 2 female servants, and his 11 sons. He crossed the shallow part of the Jabbok River.

**23** He sent them across the river. He also sent across all that he had.

**24** Then Jacob was alone. A man fought with him until the sun came up.

**25** The man saw that he could not defeat Jacob. So he touched the hip of Jacob. The hip of Jacob came out of its joint while they fought.

**26** The man said, "Let me go. The day starts." Jacob said, "I will not let you go. First give me your blessing."

**27** The man asked him, "What is your name?" He said, "Jacob."

**28** The man said, "Your name will not be Jacob any more. Your name will be Israel. You fought with God and with men, and you won."

**29** Jacob asked him, "Please tell me your name." The man said, "Why do you ask my name?" Then he gave Jacob a blessing there.

**30** Jacob gave the place the name Peniel. He said, "I saw God face to face, but I am still alive."

**31** The sun came up when Jacob went past Penuel. Jacob walked with a limp because of his hip.

**32** That is why the people of Israel do not eat the tendon at the hip joint. They do not eat it to this day. The man touched the hip joint of Jacob at that tendon.

## Chapter 33

**1** Jacob looked up and saw Esau. Esau came with 400 men. So Jacob divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the 2 female servants.

**2** He put the female servants and their children at the front. He put Leah and her children behind them. He put Rachel and Joseph at the back.

**3** Jacob went in front of them all. He bowed down to the ground 7 times. Then he came near to his brother.

**4** Esau ran to meet Jacob. He put his arms around Jacob and kissed him. They cried.

**5** Esau looked up and saw the women and the children. He asked, "Who are these people with you?" Jacob said, "They are the children that God kindly gave to me, your servant."

**6** Then the female servants and their children came near. They bowed down.

**7** Leah and her children also came near and bowed down. Then Joseph and Rachel came near and bowed down.

**8** Esau asked, "Why did you send all these herds that I met?" Jacob said, "I sent them because I want you to be kind to me, my lord."

**9** Esau said, "I have enough, my brother. Keep what you have."

**10** Jacob said, "No, please. If you are kind to me, accept my gift. I see your face, and it is like the face of God. You received me kindly.

**11** Please accept the gift that I brought to you. God was kind to me. I have all that I need." Jacob asked Esau again and again. So Esau accepted the gift.

**12** Esau said, "We will go now. I will go in front of you."

**13** Jacob said to him, "My lord knows that the children are weak. Also, I must take care of the sheep and cows that have young. If the men move the animals too fast for 1 day, all the flocks will die.

**14** Please, my lord, go in front of your servant. I will move slowly. I will move at the speed of the animals and the children. Then I will come to my lord in Seir."

**15** Esau said, "I will leave some of my men with you." Jacob said, "That is not necessary. I only want you to be kind to me, my lord."

**16** So that day Esau went back to Seir.

**17** Jacob went to Succoth. There he built a house for himself. He made shelters for his animals. That is why the name of the place is Succoth.

**18** Jacob came from Paddan Aram. He arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan. He put up his tents near the city.

**19** He bought the field where he put his tent. He bought it from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem. He paid 100 pieces of silver.

**20** He built an altar there. He gave the altar the name El Elohe Israel ("God is the God of Israel").

## Chapter 34

**1** Dinah was the daughter of Leah and Jacob. One day Dinah went out to visit the women of that land.

**2** Shechem was the son of Hamor the Hivite. Hamor was the ruler of that area. Shechem saw Dinah. He took her and forced her to have sex with him.

**3** Then Shechem loved Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, very much. He loved the young woman and spoke kindly to her.

**4** Shechem said to his father Hamor, "Get this young woman for me as my wife."

**5** Jacob heard that Shechem did a shameful thing to his daughter Dinah. His sons were in the field with his animals. So Jacob said nothing until they came home.

**6** Hamor, the father of Shechem, went out to talk with Jacob.

**7** The sons of Jacob heard the news. They came in from the field. They were very sad and very angry. Shechem did a shameful thing in Israel when he had sex with the daughter of Jacob. Such a thing must not occur.

**8** Hamor spoke with them. He said, "My son Shechem loves your daughter very much. Please give her to him as his wife.

**9** Let our families marry. Give your daughters to us. Take our daughters for yourselves.

**10** Live with us. The land is open to you. Live in the land and buy and sell in it. Get property in it."

**11** Then Shechem spoke to the father and the brothers of Dinah. He said, "Please be kind to me. I will give you what you ask.

**12** Ask me for a large bride price and gift. I will pay what you tell me. But give me the young woman as my wife."

**13** Shechem made Dinah, their sister, unclean. So the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and his father Hamor with lies.

**14** They said, "We cannot give our sister to a man who did not receive circumcision. That is a shame for us.

**15** We will agree with you on 1 condition. All the males among you must receive circumcision, as we did.

**16** Then we will give our daughters to you. We will take your daughters for ourselves. We will live with you, and we will become 1 people.

**17** But if you do not agree to receive circumcision, then we will take our sister and go away."

**18** Hamor and his son Shechem liked their words.

**19** The young man did the thing quickly, because he loved the daughter of Jacob very much. Shechem was the most respected person in the family of his father.

**20** Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city. They spoke to the men of their city.

**21** They said, "These men are friendly to us. Let them live in the land and buy and sell in it. The land is large enough for them. We can marry their daughters, and they can marry our daughters.

**22** But the men will agree to live with us and become 1 people on 1 condition. All our males must receive circumcision, as they did.

**23** Then their animals, their property, and all their livestock will become ours. So we will agree with them, and they will live with us."

**24** All the men who went out of the city gate agreed with Hamor and his son Shechem. All the males of the city received circumcision.

**25** On the third day, the men were still in pain. Then 2 of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, took their swords. They were brothers of Dinah. They attacked the city by surprise. They killed all the males.

**26** They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with the sword. They took Dinah from the house of Shechem and went away.

**27** The other sons of Jacob came to the dead bodies. They took all the property in the city, because the men of the city made their sister unclean.

**28** They took the sheep, the cattle, and the donkeys. They took the things in the city and in the fields.

**29** They took all the wealth of the people. They took all their children and wives as prisoners. They took all the things in the houses.

**30** Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You brought trouble on me. Now the people of this land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites, hate me. We are only a small number of people. They will join together and attack me. Then they will kill me and my family."

**31** But Simeon and Levi said, "We cannot let him treat our sister like a prostitute."

## Chapter 35

**1** God said to Jacob, "Go up to Bethel and live there. Make an altar there to God. God appeared to you when you ran away from your brother Esau."

**2** So Jacob said to his family and to all the people with him, "Throw away the foreign gods that you have. Make yourselves clean. Change your clothes.

**3** Then we will go up to Bethel. There I will make an altar to God. He answered me when I was in trouble. He was with me in all the places where I went."

**4** So they gave Jacob all their foreign gods and their earrings. Jacob buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.

**5** Then they started their journey. God made the people in the cities around them very afraid. So the people did not follow the sons of Jacob.

**6** Jacob and all the people with him came to Luz in the land of Canaan. Luz is Bethel.

**7** He built an altar there. He gave the place the name El Bethel. God appeared to Jacob there when he ran away from his brother.

**8** Deborah, the nurse of Rebekah, died. They buried her under the oak tree below Bethel. So they gave the tree the name Allon Bacuth ("oak of tears").

**9** Jacob came back from Paddan Aram. God appeared to him again and gave him a blessing.

**10** God said to him, "Your name is Jacob. But your name will not be Jacob any more. Your name will be Israel." So God gave him the name Israel.

**11** God said to him, "I am God Almighty. Have many children and become many. A nation and a group of nations will come from you. Kings will come from your descendants.

**12** I gave a land to Abraham and to Isaac. I will give that land to you. I will also give the land to your descendants after you."

**13** Then God went up from Jacob at the place where he spoke with him.

**14** Jacob put up a stone pillar at the place where God spoke with him. He poured a drink offering on the pillar. He also poured oil on the pillar.

**15** Jacob gave the place where God spoke with him the name Bethel.

**16** Then they went away from Bethel. They were still a short distance from Ephrath. Then Rachel started to give birth. She had much pain.

**17** The pain was very bad. The midwife said to Rachel, "Do not be afraid. You will have another son."

**18** Rachel was about to die. Before she died, she gave her son the name Ben-Oni ("son of my trouble"). But his father gave him the name Benjamin ("son of my right hand").

**19** So Rachel died. They buried her beside the road to Ephrath. Ephrath is Bethlehem.

**20** Jacob put a pillar on her grave. That pillar marks the grave of Rachel to this day.

**21** Israel continued his journey. He put up his tent on the other side of the tower of Eder.

**22** Israel lived in that land. During that time, Reuben had sex with Bilhah, a concubine of his father. Israel heard about it. Jacob had 12 sons.

**23** The sons of Leah were Reuben (the first son of Jacob), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.

**24** The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.

**25** The sons of Bilhah, the female servant of Rachel, were Dan and Naphtali.

**26** The sons of Zilpah, the female servant of Leah, were Gad and Asher. These were the sons of Jacob. Their mothers gave birth to them in Paddan Aram.

**27** Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath Arba. Kiriath Arba is Hebron. Abraham and Isaac lived there as foreigners.

**28** Isaac lived for 180 years.

**29** Then Isaac died. He was very old, and he had a full life. He joined his ancestors in death. His sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

## Chapter 36

**1** This is the list of the descendants of Esau. Esau is Edom.

**2** Esau married women from Canaan. He married Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite. He married Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah. Anah was the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite.

**3** He also married Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael. Basemath was the sister of Nebaioth.

**4** Adah gave birth to Eliphaz for Esau. Basemath gave birth to Reuel.

**5** Oholibamah gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These were the sons of Esau. Their mothers gave birth to them in the land of Canaan.

**6** Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the people of his family. He took his livestock, all his animals, and all the property that he got in Canaan. He went to a different land, away from his brother Jacob.

**7** Esau and Jacob had too much property. They could not live together. The land where they lived could not support both of them, because they had too many animals.

**8** So Esau lived in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom.

**9** This is the list of the descendants of Esau, the father of the Edomites, in the hill country of Seir.

**10** These are the names of the sons of Esau. Eliphaz was the son of Adah, the wife of Esau. Reuel was the son of Basemath, the wife of Esau.

**11** The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.

**12** Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz, the son of Esau. She gave birth to Amalek for Eliphaz. These were the grandsons of Adah, the wife of Esau.

**13** The sons of Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the grandsons of Basemath, the wife of Esau.

**14** Oholibamah was the daughter of Anah. Anah was the daughter of Zibeon. Oholibamah was the wife of Esau. She gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah for Esau.

**15** These were the chiefs among the descendants of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, the first son of Esau, were chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,

**16** chief Korah, chief Gatam, and chief Amalek. These were the chiefs from Eliphaz in the land of Edom. They were the grandsons of Adah.

**17** The sons of Reuel, the son of Esau, were chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, and chief Mizzah. These were the chiefs from Reuel in the land of Edom. They were the grandsons of Basemath, the wife of Esau.

**18** The sons of Oholibamah, the wife of Esau, were chief Jeush, chief Jalam, and chief Korah. These were the chiefs from Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the wife of Esau.

**19** These were the sons of Esau, and these were their chiefs. Esau is Edom.

**20** These were the sons of Seir the Horite. They lived in that land before Esau. They were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

**21** Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These were the chiefs of the Horites, the sons of Seir in the land of Edom.

**22** The sons of Lotan were Hori and Heman. The sister of Lotan was Timna.

**23** The sons of Shobal were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.

**24** The sons of Zibeon were Aiah and Anah. This Anah found the hot springs in the desert. He found them when he took care of the donkeys of his father Zibeon.

**25** The children of Anah were Dishon and Oholibamah. Oholibamah was the daughter of Anah.

**26** The sons of Dishon were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.

**27** The sons of Ezer were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

**28** The sons of Dishan were Uz and Aran.

**29** These were the chiefs of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,

**30** chief Dishon, chief Ezer, and chief Dishan. These were the chiefs of the Horites, by their clans, in the land of Seir.

**31** These were the kings who ruled in the land of Edom. They ruled before a king ruled over the people of Israel.

**32** Bela, the son of Beor, was king in Edom. The name of his city was Dinhabah.

**33** Bela died. Then Jobab, the son of Zerah from Bozrah, became king after him.

**34** Jobab died. Then Husham from the land of the Temanites became king after him.

**35** Husham died. Then Hadad, the son of Bedad, became king after him. Hadad defeated the Midianites in the country of Moab. The name of his city was Avith.

**36** Hadad died. Then Samlah from Masrekah became king after him.

**37** Samlah died. Then Shaul from Rehoboth on the river became king after him.

**38** Shaul died. Then Baal-Hanan, the son of Achbor, became king after him.

**39** Baal-Hanan, the son of Achbor, died. Then Hadar became king after him. The name of his city was Pau. The name of his wife was Mehetabel. She was the daughter of Matred, and Matred was the daughter of Me-Zahab.

**40** These are the names of the chiefs from Esau, by their clans, their places, and their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,

**41** chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

**42** chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

**43** chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom. Each chief had his area in the land that they owned. Esau was the father of the Edomites.

## Chapter 37

**1** Jacob lived in the land of Canaan. His father lived in that land as a foreigner.

**2** This is the history of the family of Jacob. Joseph was 17 years old. He took care of the flocks with his brothers. He worked with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, the wives of his father. Joseph told his father about the bad things that his brothers did.

**3** Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons. Joseph's mother gave birth to him when Israel was old. Israel made a special robe of many colors for Joseph.

**4** The brothers of Joseph saw that their father loved Joseph more than them. So they hated Joseph. They could not speak kindly to him.

**5** Joseph had a dream. He told the dream to his brothers. Then they hated him more.

**6** He said to them, "Please listen to my dream.

**7** In the dream, we tied bundles of grain in the field. My bundle stood up straight. Your bundles stood around my bundle. They bowed down to my bundle."

**8** His brothers said to him, "Do you think that you will be our king? Will you rule over us?" They hated him more because of his dreams and his words.

**9** Then Joseph had another dream. He told it to his brothers. He said, "Listen, I had another dream. The sun, the moon, and 11 stars bowed down to me."

**10** He told the dream to his father and to his brothers. His father said that Joseph was wrong. He said to Joseph, "What is this dream? Will I, your mother, and your brothers come and bow down to the ground in front of you?"

**11** The brothers of Joseph were jealous of him. But his father remembered the dream.

**12** The brothers of Joseph went to take care of the flocks of their father near Shechem.

**13** Israel said to Joseph, "Your brothers take care of the flocks near Shechem. Come, I will send you to them." Joseph said, "I am ready."

**14** Israel said to him, "Go and see if your brothers and the flocks are well. Then come back and tell me." So he sent Joseph from the valley of Hebron. Joseph came to Shechem.

**15** A man found Joseph in the fields. Joseph did not know where to go. The man asked him, "What do you look for?"

**16** Joseph said, "I look for my brothers. Please tell me where they take care of the flocks."

**17** The man said, "They went away from here. I heard them say, 'We will go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went after his brothers. He found them at Dothan.

**18** The brothers saw Joseph from far away. Before he came near to them, they made a plan to kill him.

**19** They said to each other, "Look, the dreamer comes.

**20** Come now. We will kill him and throw his body into one of the dry wells. We will say that a wild animal ate him. Then we will see what occurs to his dreams."

**21** Reuben heard their plan. He tried to save Joseph from them. He said, "We will not kill him."

**22** Reuben said to them, "Do not kill him. Throw him into this dry well here in the desert. But do not hurt him." Reuben said this because he wanted to save Joseph. He wanted to take Joseph back to their father.

**23** Joseph came to his brothers. They took his robe from him, the robe of many colors.

**24** They took him and threw him into the well. The well was empty. It had no water in it.

**25** Then they sat down to eat food. They looked up and saw a group of Ishmaelites. The Ishmaelites came from Gilead. Their camels carried spices, balm, and myrrh. They went down to Egypt with these goods.

**26** Judah said to his brothers, "We will get nothing if we kill our brother and hide his death.

**27** Come, we will sell him to the Ishmaelites. We will not hurt him, because he is our brother and our own family." His brothers agreed.

**28** Some Midianite traders came near. The brothers pulled Joseph up out of the well. They sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for 20 pieces of silver. The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt.

**29** Reuben went back to the well. He saw that Joseph was not in the well. He tore his clothes because he was very sad.

**30** He went back to his brothers. He said, "The boy is not there. What can I do now?"

**31** The brothers took the robe of Joseph. They killed a male goat. They put the robe in the blood of the goat.

**32** They took the robe of many colors to their father. They said, "We found this robe. Look at it. Is it the robe of your son or not?"

**33** Jacob looked at the robe. He said, "It is the robe of my son. A wild animal ate him. A wild animal tore Joseph into pieces."

**34** Jacob tore his clothes. He put rough cloth (sackcloth) around his waist. He cried for his son for a long time.

**35** All his sons and daughters came to him. They tried to make him feel better. But he did not let them. He said, "I will cry for my son until I die and go down to the grave." So his father cried for Joseph.

**36** The Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar. Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh. He was the captain of the guards.

## Chapter 38

**1** At that time, Judah went away from his brothers. He went to stay with a man from Adullam. The name of the man was Hirah.

**2** There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man. The name of the man was Shua. Judah married her and had sex with her.

**3** She became pregnant and gave birth to a son. Judah gave him the name Er.

**4** She became pregnant again and gave birth to a son. She gave him the name Onan.

**5** She had another son. She gave him the name Shelah. Judah was at Kezib when she gave birth to Shelah.

**6** Judah got a wife for Er, his first son. The name of the wife was Tamar.

**7** But Er, the first son of Judah, was evil in the sight of the LORD. So the LORD killed him.

**8** Then Judah said to Onan, "Have sex with the wife of your brother. Marry her as the brother of her husband. Then give a child to your brother."

**9** But Onan knew that the child will not be his. So when he had sex with the wife of his brother, he let his seed fall on the ground. He did not want to give a child to his brother.

**10** The LORD did not like what Onan did. So the LORD killed him also.

**11** Then Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, "Live as a widow in the house of your father. Wait until my son Shelah grows up." Judah was afraid that Shelah will also die, as his brothers did. So Tamar went to live in the house of her father.

**12** After a long time, the wife of Judah died. She was the daughter of Shua. When the time of sadness was at an end, Judah went up to Timnah. He went to the men who cut the wool of his sheep. His friend Hirah the Adullamite went with him.

**13** A person told Tamar, "Your father-in-law goes up to Timnah to cut the wool of his sheep."

**14** So Tamar took off the clothes of a widow. She covered herself with a veil. She sat at the entrance of Enaim, on the road to Timnah. She saw that Shelah was now a man. But Judah did not give her to Shelah as his wife.

**15** Judah saw her. He thought that she was a prostitute, because she covered her face.

**16** He went to her at the side of the road. He did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. He said, "Come, I want to have sex with you." She said, "What will you give me?"

**17** He said, "I will send you a young goat from my flock." She said, "Give me a guarantee until you send the goat."

**18** He said, "What guarantee will I give you?" She said, "Give me your seal, its cord, and the stick in your hand." He gave them to her and had sex with her. She became pregnant by him.

**19** Then she got up and went away. She took off her veil. She put on the clothes of a widow again.

**20** Judah sent the young goat with his friend, the Adullamite. He wanted to get back his guarantee from the woman. But his friend did not find her.

**21** His friend asked the men of that place, "Where is the prostitute who was at the side of the road at Enaim?" They said, "No prostitute was here."

**22** So he went back to Judah. He said, "I did not find her. Also, the men of the place said, 'No prostitute was here.'"

**23** Judah said, "Let her keep the things. If we look more, people will laugh at us. I sent the young goat, but you did not find her."

**24** About 3 months later, a person told Judah, "Your daughter-in-law Tamar acted like a prostitute. Now she is pregnant because of it." Judah said, "Bring her out. Burn her."

**25** The men brought her out. Then she sent a message to her father-in-law. She said, "The man who owns these things made me pregnant. Please look at them. Whose seal, cord, and stick are these?"

**26** Judah looked at the things. He said, "She is more righteous than I am. I did not give her to my son Shelah." Judah did not have sex with her again.

**27** The time came for Tamar to give birth. She had twins in her body.

**28** When she gave birth, one baby put out his hand. The midwife took a red thread. She tied the red thread on his hand. She said, "This baby came out first."

**29** But the baby pulled back his hand. Then his brother came out. The midwife said, "You broke out first!" So they gave him the name Perez ("break out").

**30** Then his brother came out with the red thread on his hand. They gave him the name Zerah.

## Chapter 39

**1** The Ishmaelites took Joseph down to Egypt. Potiphar, an Egyptian, bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites. Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh and the captain of the guards.

**2** The LORD was with Joseph. Joseph was successful. He lived in the house of his Egyptian master.

**3** His master saw that the LORD was with Joseph. The LORD made all the work of Joseph successful.

**4** Joseph pleased his master, and Joseph became his personal servant. Potiphar put Joseph in charge of his house. He gave Joseph control of all his property.

**5** From that time, the LORD gave his blessing to the house of the Egyptian because of Joseph. The blessing of the LORD was on all that Potiphar had, in the house and in the field.

**6** So Potiphar gave Joseph control of all his property. With Joseph in charge, Potiphar did not think about his property. He only thought about the food that he ate. Joseph was strong and handsome.

**7** After some time, the wife of his master looked at Joseph with desire. She said, "Have sex with me."

**8** But Joseph refused. He said to the wife of his master, "My master trusts me with all that is in his house. He does not think about his property. He gave me control of all that he has.

**9** No person in this house is more important than I am. My master kept nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. I cannot do this very bad thing. I cannot sin against God."

**10** She spoke to Joseph day after day. But Joseph did not agree to have sex with her or to be with her.

**11** One day Joseph went into the house to do his work. None of the men of the house were in the house.

**12** She took hold of his robe. She said, "Have sex with me." But Joseph left his robe in her hand. He ran out of the house.

**13** She saw that Joseph left his robe in her hand and ran outside.

**14** So she called the men of her house. She said to them, "Look, my husband brought a Hebrew into the house to insult us. He came to me and tried to have sex with me. But I shouted loudly.

**15** He heard me shout. Then he left his robe beside me and ran outside."

**16** She kept the robe of Joseph beside her until his master came home.

**17** Then she told her husband the same story. She said, "You brought a Hebrew servant to us. He came to me to insult me.

**18** But I shouted loudly. Then he left his robe beside me and ran outside."

**19** His master heard the story of his wife. She said, "Your servant did these things to me." Then his master became very angry.

**20** The master of Joseph took him and put him in the prison. The prisoners of the king were in that prison. Joseph stayed there in the prison.

**21** But the LORD was with Joseph. The LORD showed him kindness. The LORD caused the chief guard of the prison to like Joseph.

**22** So the chief guard put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners in the prison. Joseph controlled all the work there.

**23** The chief guard did not worry about the things in the control of Joseph. The LORD was with Joseph. The LORD made all the work of Joseph successful.

## Chapter 40

**1** After these things, 2 servants of the king of Egypt did wrong things to their master, the king. One servant was the cupbearer of the king. The other servant was the baker of the king.

**2** Pharaoh was angry with his 2 officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.

**3** He put them in prison in the house of the captain of the guards. Joseph was in that same prison.

**4** The captain of the guards told Joseph to serve them. Joseph took care of them. They stayed in the prison for some time.

**5** One night the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt each had a dream. They were in the prison. Each dream had a different meaning.

**6** In the morning, Joseph came to them. He saw that they were sad.

**7** He asked the officers of Pharaoh in the prison with him, "Why do you look sad today?"

**8** They said to him, "We each had a dream. But no person can tell us the meaning of the dreams." Joseph said to them, "God knows the meaning of dreams. Please tell me your dreams."

**9** So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream. He said, "In my dream, I saw a vine in front of me.

**10** The vine had 3 branches. The branches grew buds. The buds opened into flowers. Then the flowers became bunches of ripe grapes.

**11** The cup of Pharaoh was in my hand. I took the grapes. I pressed them into the cup of Pharaoh. I put the cup in the hand of Pharaoh."

**12** Joseph said to him, "This is the meaning of your dream. The 3 branches are 3 days.

**13** In 3 days, Pharaoh will take you out of the prison. He will give your job back to you. You will put the cup of Pharaoh in his hand again. You will do the same work as before.

**14** But please remember me when things are good for you. Please be kind to me. Tell Pharaoh about me. Help me to get out of this prison.

**15** Men took me by force from the land of the Hebrews. Here also I did nothing wrong. But they put me in this prison."

**16** The chief baker saw that the meaning of the dream was good. So he said to Joseph, "I also had a dream. In my dream, 3 baskets of white bread were on my head.

**17** The top basket had many types of baked food for Pharaoh. But the birds ate the food from the basket on my head."

**18** Joseph answered, "This is the meaning of your dream. The 3 baskets are 3 days.

**19** In 3 days, Pharaoh will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole. The birds will eat your flesh."

**20** On the third day it was the birthday of Pharaoh. He gave a feast for all his officers. He brought the chief cupbearer and the chief baker out of the prison. He brought them in front of his officers.

**21** Pharaoh gave the chief cupbearer his job again. The chief cupbearer put the cup in the hand of Pharaoh again.

**22** But Pharaoh hanged the chief baker. All occurred as Joseph said.

**23** But the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph. He forgot about him.

## Chapter 41

**1** After 2 full years, Pharaoh had a dream. In the dream, he stood by the Nile river.

**2** Seven cows came up out of the river. They were fat and good to look at. They ate the grass at the edge of the river.

**3** Then seven other cows came up out of the river after them. They were thin and ugly. They stood near the other cows at the edge of the river.

**4** The thin, ugly cows ate the seven fat, good cows. Then Pharaoh woke up.

**5** He slept again and had a second dream. Seven heads of grain grew on one stalk. The heads were full and good.

**6** Then seven other heads of grain grew after them. They were thin, and the east wind made them dry.

**7** The thin heads of grain ate the seven full heads. Then Pharaoh woke up. He knew that the dream was only a dream.

**8** In the morning, Pharaoh was very worried. He sent for all the magicians and all the wise men of Egypt. Pharaoh told them his dreams. But no person could tell Pharaoh the meaning of the dreams.

**9** Then the chief cupbearer (the man who served wine to Pharaoh) spoke to Pharaoh. He said, "Today I remember my faults."

**10** "Pharaoh was angry with his servants. You put me in the prison in the house of the captain of the guard. You also put the chief baker there."

**11** "We each had a dream in the same night. Each dream had a different meaning."

**12** "A young Hebrew man was there with us. He was a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams. He told each man the meaning of his dream."

**13** "The dreams occurred as he said. Pharaoh gave me my position again. Pharaoh hanged the other man."

**14** Then Pharaoh sent for Joseph. They quickly brought him out of the prison. Joseph shaved and changed his clothes. Then he came to Pharaoh.

**15** Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I had a dream. No person can tell the meaning of the dream. But I heard about you. People say that you can hear a dream and tell its meaning."

**16** Joseph answered Pharaoh, "I cannot do it. But God will give Pharaoh a good answer."

**17** Pharaoh said to Joseph, "In my dream, I stood on the bank of the Nile river."

**18** "Seven cows came up out of the river. They were fat and good to look at. They ate the grass at the edge of the river."

**19** "Then seven other cows came up after them. They were weak, very ugly, and thin. I did not see cows as ugly as those cows in all the land of Egypt."

**20** "The thin, ugly cows ate the first seven fat cows."

**21** "But after they ate the fat cows, no person could know that they ate them. The thin cows were as ugly as before. Then I woke up."

**22** "In my second dream, I saw seven heads of grain on one stalk. They were full and good."

**23** "Then seven other heads of grain grew after them. They were dry and thin. The east wind made them dry."

**24** "The thin heads of grain ate the seven good heads. I told the dreams to the magicians. But no magician could tell me the meaning."
