**25** Joseph said to Pharaoh, "The two dreams of Pharaoh are one dream. God shows Pharaoh what he will do."

**26** "The seven good cows are seven years. The seven good heads of grain are seven years. The two dreams are one dream."

**27** "The seven thin, ugly cows that came up after them are seven years. The seven empty heads of grain are also seven years. The east wind made them dry. They will be seven years of famine (a time with no food)."

**28** "The meaning is as I told Pharaoh. God shows Pharaoh what he will do."

**29** "Seven years of much food will come in all the land of Egypt."

**30** "After them, seven years of famine will come. The people will forget all the much food in the land of Egypt. The famine will destroy the land."

**31** "The people will not remember the much food in the land, because the famine will be very bad."

**32** "God gave the dream to Pharaoh two times. This shows that God decided the thing. God will make the thing occur soon."

**33** "Now Pharaoh must find a man with good sense and wisdom. Pharaoh must put him in control of the land of Egypt."

**34** "Pharaoh must also put officers over the land. They must take one fifth of the food of the land of Egypt in the seven years of much food."

**35** "They must collect all the food of the good years that will come. They must keep the grain under the control of Pharaoh. They must keep the food in the cities."

**36** "That food will be a supply for the land for the seven years of famine. Then the famine will not destroy the land."

**37** Pharaoh and all his servants thought that the plan was good.

**38** Pharaoh said to his servants, "We cannot find another man like this man. The Spirit of God is in him."

**39** Pharaoh said to Joseph, "God showed you all this. No other man has as much good sense and wisdom as you."

**40** "You will be in control of my house. All my people will obey your words. Only I, as king, will be greater than you."

**41** Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Look, I put you in control of all the land of Egypt."

**42** Pharaoh took his signet ring (a ring with the seal of the king) from his hand. He put the ring on the hand of Joseph. He put clothes of fine linen on Joseph. He put a gold chain around the neck of Joseph.

**43** Pharaoh made Joseph ride in his second chariot. Men went in front of Joseph. They shouted, "Bow the knee!" Thus Pharaoh put Joseph in control of all the land of Egypt.

**44** Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh. But without your permission, no man in all the land of Egypt will lift his hand or his foot."

**45** Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-Paneah. He gave Joseph a wife, Asenath. She was the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of On. Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.

**46** Joseph was 30 years old when he started to serve Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Joseph went out from Pharaoh. He went through all the land of Egypt.

**47** In the seven years of much food, the land made very large crops.

**48** Joseph collected all the food of the seven years in the land of Egypt. He put the food in the cities. In each city, he put the food from the fields around that city.

**49** Joseph collected very much grain. The grain was as much as the sand of the sea. Then he stopped the count, because the grain was too much to count.

**50** Before the years of famine came, Joseph had two sons. Asenath was their mother. She was the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of On.

**51** Joseph gave the name Manasseh to the first son. He said, "God made me forget all my trouble and all the house of my father."

**52** He gave the name Ephraim to the second son. He said, "God gave me children in the land where I had much pain."

**53** The seven years of much food in the land of Egypt came to an end.

**54** Then the seven years of famine started, as Joseph said. There was famine in all the lands. But in all the land of Egypt, there was bread.

**55** All the land of Egypt became hungry. The people cried to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, "Go to Joseph. Do what he tells you."

**56** The famine was over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the storehouses. He sold grain to the Egyptians. The famine was very bad in the land of Egypt.

**57** People from all countries came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph. The famine was very bad in all the earth.

## Chapter 42

**1** Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt. Jacob said to his sons, "Why do you look at each other?"

**2** He said, "I heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy grain for us. Then we will live and not die."

**3** Ten brothers of Joseph went down to buy grain from Egypt.

**4** But Jacob did not send Benjamin, the brother of Joseph, with his brothers. Jacob said, "Maybe something bad will occur to him."

**5** The sons of Israel came to buy grain with the other people who came. The famine was in the land of Canaan.

**6** Joseph was the governor over the land. He sold grain to all the people of the land. The brothers of Joseph came. They bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

**7** Joseph saw his brothers and he knew them. But he acted as a stranger to them and spoke strongly. He said to them, "Where do you come from?" They said, "We come from the land of Canaan to buy food."

**8** Joseph knew his brothers, but they did not know him.

**9** Joseph remembered the dreams that he had about them. He said to them, "You are spies. You came to see the weak parts of the land."

**10** They said to him, "No, my lord. Your servants came to buy food."

**11** "We are all sons of one man. We are honest men. Your servants are not spies."

**12** He said to them, "No. You came to see the weak parts of the land."

**13** They said, "Your servants are 12 brothers. We are the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest brother is with our father today. One brother is dead."

**14** Joseph said to them, "My words are correct. You are spies."

**15** "I will test you with this test. As Pharaoh lives, you will not go from here until your youngest brother comes here."

**16** "Send one of you to get your brother. The others will stay in prison. Then I will test your words. I will know if you tell the truth. If you do not tell the truth, then, as Pharaoh lives, you are spies."

**17** He put them all in prison for 3 days.

**18** On the third day, Joseph said to them, "Do this and you will live. I fear God."

**19** "If you are honest men, let one of your brothers stay in prison. The others will go and take grain for the hunger of your families."

**20** "Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that your words are true. And you will not die." They agreed.

**21** They said to each other, "We are guilty because of our brother. We saw the distress of his soul when he asked us for mercy. But we did not listen. Thus this distress comes to us."

**22** Reuben answered them, "I told you, 'Do not do wrong to the boy.' But you did not listen. Now God asks us to pay for his blood."

**23** They did not know that Joseph understood them. An interpreter (a man who changes words from one language to another) spoke between them.

**24** Joseph went away from them and cried. Then he came back to them and spoke to them. He took Simeon from them. He tied Simeon in front of their eyes.

**25** Then Joseph told his servants to fill the bags of the brothers with grain. He told them to put the money of each man back in his sack. He told them to give the brothers food for the travel. His servants did these things for them.

**26** The brothers put the grain on their donkeys. Then they went away from there.

**27** At the place where they stopped for the night, one brother opened his sack to give food to his donkey. He saw his money in the mouth of his sack.

**28** He said to his brothers, "Someone put my money back. The money is here in my sack." They became very afraid. They turned and looked at each other. They said, "What is this thing that God did to us?"

**29** They came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan. They told him all the things that occurred to them. They said,

**30** "The man who is the lord of the land spoke strongly to us. He thought that we were spies in the country."

**31** "We said to him, 'We are honest men. We are not spies.'"

**32** "'We are 12 brothers, the sons of our father. One brother is dead. The youngest brother is with our father in the land of Canaan today.'"

**33** "The man, the lord of the land, said to us, 'This test will show me if you are honest men. Leave one of your brothers with me. Take food for the hunger of your families, and go.'"

**34** "'Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies, but honest men. Then I will give your brother back to you. And you can trade in the land.'"

**35** They emptied their sacks. Each man found his bag of money in his sack. They and their father saw the bags of money, and they were afraid.

**36** Jacob their father said to them, "You took my children from me. Joseph is dead and Simeon is dead. Now you want to take Benjamin. All these things are against me."

**37** Reuben spoke to his father. He said, "If I do not bring Benjamin back to you, you can kill my two sons. Put him in my care. I will bring him back to you."

**38** Jacob said, "My son will not go down with you. His brother is dead, and he is the only son that stays. Something bad can occur to him on the travel. Then you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol (the place of the dead) with sorrow."

## Chapter 43

**1** The famine was very bad in the land.

**2** They ate all the grain that they brought from Egypt. Then their father said to them, "Go again. Buy a small quantity of food for us."

**3** Judah spoke to him. He said, "The man gave us a strong caution. He said, 'You will not see my face again if your brother is not with you.'"

**4** "If you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you."

**5** "But if you do not send him, we will not go down. The man said to us, 'You will not see my face if your brother is not with you.'"

**6** Israel said, "Why did you do this bad thing to me? Why did you tell the man that you have another brother?"

**7** They said, "The man asked about us and about our family. He asked, 'Is your father alive? Do you have another brother?' We answered his questions. We could not know that he will tell us to bring our brother down."

**8** Judah said to Israel his father, "Send the boy with me. We will start and go. Then we will live and not die. We, you, and our little children will live."

**9** "I will be the guarantee for him. You can make me responsible for him. I must bring him back to you and put him in front of you. If I do not, then let the blame be on me for all time."

**10** "We waited too long. If we did not wait, we can now go and come back two times."

**11** Israel their father said to them, "If you must go, then do this. Take some of the best products of the land in your bags. Take them down to the man as a gift. Take some balm, some honey, spices, myrrh, nuts, and almonds."

**12** "Take two times the money with you. Take back the money that you found in the mouth of your sacks. Possibly the money was a mistake."

**13** "Also take your brother. Start and go again to the man."

**14** "I pray that God Almighty will give you mercy in front of the man. Then the man will release your other brother and Benjamin. If I lose my children, I lose them."

**15** The men took the gift. They took two times the money in their hands. They took Benjamin. They started and went down to Egypt. They stood in front of Joseph.

**16** Joseph saw Benjamin with them. He said to the steward of his house, "Bring the men into the house. Kill an animal and prepare the meat. These men will eat with me at noon."

**17** The steward did as Joseph told him. He brought the men into the house of Joseph.

**18** The men were afraid because the steward brought them into the house of Joseph. They said, "He brings us in because of the money in our sacks the first time. He wants to attack us and take us as slaves. He wants to take our donkeys."

**19** They came near to the steward of the house of Joseph. They spoke to him at the door of the house.

**20** They said, "Sir, we came down the first time to buy food."

**21** "At the place where we stopped for the night, we opened our sacks. The money of each man was in the mouth of his sack. All of our money was there. We brought the money back with us."

**22** "We also brought other money to buy food. We do not know who put our money in our sacks."

**23** The steward said, "Peace be with you. Do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father put treasure in your sacks. I received your money." Then he brought Simeon out to them.

**24** The steward brought the men into the house of Joseph. He gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave food to their donkeys.

**25** They made the gift ready for the arrival of Joseph at noon. They heard that they will eat bread there.

**26** Joseph came home. They brought the gift into the house to him. They bowed down to the ground in front of him.

**27** He asked them about their health. He said, "Is your old father well? You spoke to me about him. Is he still alive?"

**28** They said, "Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive." They bowed their heads low to show respect.

**29** Joseph looked up and saw his brother Benjamin, the son of his mother. He said, "Is this your youngest brother? You spoke to me about him." Then Joseph said, "God give you grace, my son."

**30** Joseph quickly went away, because he had strong love for his brother. He wanted to cry. He went into his room and cried there.

**31** He washed his face and came out. He controlled himself. He said, "Put the food on the table."

**32** The servants put food for Joseph on one table. They put food for the brothers on another table. They put food for the Egyptians who ate with him on another table. The Egyptians did not eat with the Hebrews. That was a hateful thing to the Egyptians.

**33** The brothers sat in front of Joseph in the order of their ages, from the oldest to the youngest. The men looked at each other with surprise.

**34** Joseph sent portions of food from his table to them. The portion of Benjamin was five times larger than the portions of the others. They drank and were happy with Joseph.

## Chapter 44

**1** Joseph gave an order to the steward of his house. He said, "Fill the sacks of the men with food. Put as much food as they can carry. Put the money of each man in the mouth of his sack."

**2** "Put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest. Also put his money for the grain there." The steward did as Joseph told him.

**3** In the morning, at first light, the servants sent the men away with their donkeys.

**4** The men went out of the city, but they did not go far. Joseph said to his steward, "Start and follow the men. When you catch them, say to them, 'Why did you do evil in return for good?'"

**5** "'My lord drinks from that cup. He also uses that cup to know the future. You did evil.'"

**6** The steward caught them. He told them these words.

**7** They said to him, "Why does my lord say these words? Your servants will not do such a thing."

**8** "We found money in the mouth of our sacks. We brought that money back to you from the land of Canaan. Thus we will not steal silver or gold from the house of your lord."

**9** "If you find the cup with one of your servants, that man will die. And we will also be the slaves of my lord."

**10** The steward said, "It will be as you say. The man with the cup will be my slave. The others will be free of blame."

**11** Each man quickly put his sack down on the ground. Each man opened his sack.

**12** The steward searched the sacks. He started with the oldest and stopped with the youngest. He found the cup in the sack of Benjamin.

**13** The brothers tore their clothes. Each man put the load on his donkey. They went back to the city.

**14** Judah and his brothers came to the house of Joseph. Joseph was still there. They fell to the ground in front of him.

**15** Joseph said to them, "What did you do? Do you not know that a man such as I can know secret things?"

**16** Judah said, "What can we say to my lord? What can we speak? How can we show that we are honest? God found the sin of your servants. We are now the slaves of my lord. We and the man with the cup are your slaves."

**17** Joseph said, "I will not do such a thing. Only the man with the cup will be my slave. The others can go in peace to your father."

**18** Then Judah came near to Joseph. He said, "My lord, please let your servant speak a word to my lord. Do not be angry with your servant. You are as powerful as Pharaoh."

**19** "My lord asked his servants, 'Do you have a father or a brother?'"

**20** "We said to my lord, 'We have an old father. He has a young son. The mother of the son gave birth to him when our father was old. The brother of that son is dead. Only he stays from the sons of his mother. His father loves him.'"

**21** "You said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me. I want to see him.'"

**22** "We said to my lord, 'The boy cannot go away from his father. If he goes away from his father, his father will die.'"

**23** "You said to your servants, 'If your youngest brother does not come down with you, you will not see my face again.'"

**24** "We went up to your servant, my father. We told him the words of my lord."

**25** "Our father said, 'Go again and buy a small quantity of food for us.'"

**26** "We said, 'We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down. We cannot see the face of the man if our youngest brother is not with us.'"

**27** "Your servant, my father, said to us, 'You know that my wife gave me two sons.'"

**28** "'One son went away from me. I said, "A wild animal surely tore him to pieces." I did not see him after that time.'"

**29** "'You want to take this son from me also. Something bad can occur to him. Then you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol with sorrow.'"

**30** "Now I must go back to your servant, my father. If the boy is not with us, there will be a problem. The life of my father is tied to the life of the boy."

**31** "When my father sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. Your servants will bring the gray hair of our father down to Sheol with sorrow."

**32** "I, your servant, became the guarantee for the boy to my father. I said, 'If I do not bring him back to you, let the blame be on me for all time.'"

**33** "Now, please let me stay as the slave of my lord in place of the boy. Let the boy go back with his brothers."

**34** "How can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? I do not want to see the misery that will come to my father."

## Chapter 45

**1** Joseph could not control himself in front of all the persons who stood near him. He shouted, "Make all persons go out from me." No person stayed with Joseph when he told his brothers who he was.

**2** Joseph cried very loudly. The Egyptians heard him. The house of Pharaoh also heard about Joseph.

**3** Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?" His brothers could not answer him. They were very afraid in front of him.

**4** Joseph said to his brothers, "Please come near to me." They came near. He said, "I am Joseph your brother. You sold me into Egypt."

**5** "Now do not be sad. Do not be angry with yourselves because you sold me here. God sent me in front of you to keep people alive."

**6** "The famine was in the land for 2 years. For 5 more years, people will not plow and will not cut crops."

**7** "God sent me in front of you to keep your family alive on the earth. He sent me to save your lives with a great rescue."

**8** "Thus you did not send me here. God sent me here. He made me a father to Pharaoh. He made me lord of all the house of Pharaoh. He made me ruler over all the land of Egypt."

**9** "Go up quickly to my father. Say to him, 'Your son Joseph says this: God made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Do not wait.'"

**10** "'You will live in the land of Goshen. You will be near me. Your children, your grandchildren, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have will be near me.'"

**11** "'I will give you food there, because 5 more years of famine will come. If you do not come, you, your family, and all that you have will become poor.'"

**12** "Look. Your eyes and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see that I speak to you with my mouth."

**13** "Tell my father about all my glory in Egypt. Tell him about all that you saw. Quickly bring my father down here."

**14** Joseph put his arms around the neck of his brother Benjamin and cried. Benjamin cried on the neck of Joseph.

**15** Joseph kissed all his brothers and cried over them. After that, his brothers spoke with him.

**16** The house of Pharaoh heard the news. People said, "The brothers of Joseph came." Pharaoh and his servants were happy.

**17** Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers: 'Do this. Put loads on your animals. Go to the land of Canaan.'"

**18** "'Get your father and your families and come to me. I will give you the good things of the land of Egypt. You will eat the best food of the land.'"

**19** "You must also tell them: 'Do this. Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little children and your wives. Bring your father and come.'"

**20** "'Do not worry about your things. The good things of all the land of Egypt are yours.'"

**21** The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, as Pharaoh told him. He gave them food for the travel.

**22** He gave each of them a set of new clothes. But he gave Benjamin 300 pieces of silver and 5 sets of clothes.

**23** He sent these things to his father: 10 donkeys with loads of the good things of Egypt. He also sent 10 female donkeys with loads of grain, bread, and food for his father on the travel.

**24** Then he sent his brothers away, and they went. He said to them, "Do not argue on the travel."

**25** They went up out of Egypt. They came into the land of Canaan to Jacob their father.

**26** They told him, "Joseph is still alive. He is the ruler over all the land of Egypt." The heart of Jacob became numb. He did not believe them.

**27** They told him all the words that Joseph said to them. Jacob saw the wagons that Joseph sent to carry him. Then the spirit of Jacob their father became alive again.

**28** Israel said, "This is sufficient. My son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."

## Chapter 46

**1** Israel went with all that he had. He came to Beersheba. He offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.

**2** God spoke to Israel in visions in the night. He said, "Jacob, Jacob." Jacob said, "I am here."

**3** God said, "I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down into Egypt. I will make you into a great nation there."

**4** "I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph will close your eyes with his hand."

**5** Jacob went from Beersheba. The sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, their little children, and their wives in the wagons. Pharaoh sent the wagons to carry Jacob.

**6** They took their livestock and their goods. They got these things in the land of Canaan. They came into Egypt. Jacob and all his descendants came with him.

**7** He brought his sons and his grandsons with him. He brought his daughters and his granddaughters. He brought all his descendants into Egypt.

**8** These are the names of the children of Israel who came into Egypt: Jacob and his sons. Reuben was the first son of Jacob.

**9** The sons of Reuben were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

**10** The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul. Shaul was the son of a Canaanite woman.

**11** The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

**12** The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. But Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

**13** The sons of Issachar were Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.

**14** Zebulun had 3 sons: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.

**15** These were the sons of Leah. She gave birth to them for Jacob in Paddan Aram. She also gave birth to his daughter Dinah. All his sons and daughters from Leah were 33 persons.

**16** The sons of Gad were Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.

**17** The sons of Asher were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Serah was their sister. The sons of Beriah were Heber and Malchiel.

**18** These were the sons of Zilpah. Laban gave Zilpah to his daughter Leah. Zilpah gave birth to these children for Jacob. They were 16 persons.

**19** The sons of Rachel, the wife of Jacob, were Joseph and Benjamin.

**20** In the land of Egypt, Joseph became the father of Manasseh and Ephraim. Asenath gave birth to them. She was the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of On.

**21** The sons of Benjamin were Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.

**22** These were the sons of Rachel. She gave birth to them for Jacob. They were 14 persons in all.

**23** The son of Dan was Hushim.

**24** The sons of Naphtali were Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.

**25** These were the sons of Bilhah. Laban gave Bilhah to his daughter Rachel. Bilhah gave birth to these children for Jacob. They were 7 persons in all.

**26** All the persons who came with Jacob into Egypt were his descendants. The wives of the sons of Jacob are not in this count. They were 66 persons in all.

**27** Joseph had 2 sons in Egypt. All the persons of the house of Jacob who came into Egypt were 70.

**28** Jacob sent Judah in front of him to Joseph. Judah went to get directions to Goshen. Then they came into the land of Goshen.

**29** Joseph made his chariot ready. He went up to Goshen to meet his father Israel. Joseph came to his father and put his arms around his neck. He cried on the neck of his father for a long time.

**30** Israel said to Joseph, "Now I can die. I saw your face. You are still alive."

**31** Joseph said to his brothers and to the family of his father, "I will go up and speak to Pharaoh. I will say to him, 'My brothers and the family of my father came to me. They were in the land of Canaan.'"

**32** "'The men are shepherds. They keep livestock. They brought their flocks, their herds, and all that they have.'"

**33** "Pharaoh will call you. He will ask, 'What is your work?'"

**34** "You must say, 'Your servants kept livestock from our youth until now. We and our fathers did this work.' Then you can live in the land of Goshen. All shepherds are hateful to the Egyptians."

## Chapter 47

**1** Joseph went in and spoke to Pharaoh. He said, "My father and my brothers came from the land of Canaan. They brought their flocks, their herds, and all that they have. They are now in the land of Goshen."

**2** Joseph took 5 of his brothers with him. He brought them in front of Pharaoh.

**3** Pharaoh said to the brothers of Joseph, "What is your work?" They said to Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds. We and our fathers are shepherds."

**4** They also said to Pharaoh, "We came to live for a time in the land. There is no grass for the flocks of your servants. The famine is very bad in the land of Canaan. Please let your servants live in the land of Goshen."

**5** Pharaoh spoke to Joseph. He said, "Your father and your brothers came to you."

**6** "The land of Egypt is open to you. Let your father and your brothers live in the best part of the land. Let them live in the land of Goshen. If you know capable men among them, put them in control of my livestock."

**7** Joseph brought Jacob his father in front of Pharaoh. Jacob gave a blessing to Pharaoh.

**8** Pharaoh said to Jacob, "How old are you?"

**9** Jacob said to Pharaoh, "I travelled on the earth for 130 years. My years were few and bad. They are not as many as the years of my fathers on their travels."

**10** Jacob gave a blessing to Pharaoh. Then he went out from Pharaoh.

**11** Joseph gave a place to his father and his brothers. He gave them property in the land of Egypt, in the best part of the land. He gave them the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh told him.

**12** Joseph gave food to his father, his brothers, and all the family of his father. He gave food to each family for the number of its children.

**13** There was no bread in all the land. The famine was very bad. The land of Egypt and the land of Canaan became weak because of the famine.

**14** Joseph collected all the money in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan. The people gave the money for the grain that they bought. Joseph brought the money into the house of Pharaoh.

**15** The money in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan came to an end. All the Egyptians came to Joseph. They said, "Give us bread. Why must we die in front of you? We have no more money."

**16** Joseph said, "Give me your livestock. If you have no money, I will give you food for your livestock."

**17** They brought their livestock to Joseph. Joseph gave them bread for their horses, flocks, herds, and donkeys. He gave them bread for all their livestock for that year.

**18** That year came to an end. They came to him in the second year. They said to him, "We will not hide from my lord that all our money is gone. My lord has all our herds of animals. Nothing stays for my lord but our bodies and our land."

**19** "Why must we and our land die in front of your eyes? Buy us and our land for bread. We and our land will be slaves to Pharaoh. Give us seed so that we live and do not die. Then the land will not become empty."

**20** Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh. Each Egyptian sold his field, because the famine was very bad for them. Thus the land became the property of Pharaoh.

**21** Joseph moved the people into the cities, from one end of Egypt to the other end.

**22** But Joseph did not buy the land of the priests. The priests received food from Pharaoh. They ate the food that Pharaoh gave them. Thus they did not sell their land.

**23** Joseph said to the people, "Today I bought you and your land for Pharaoh. Here is seed for you. Plant the seed in the land."

**24** "At the harvest, you will give one fifth to Pharaoh. Four fifths will be yours. Use them as seed for the field. Use them as food for you, your families, and your little children."

**25** They said, "You saved our lives. Let us find grace in the eyes of my lord. We will be the slaves of Pharaoh."

**26** Joseph made a law about the land of Egypt. The law continues to this day. Pharaoh must get one fifth. Only the land of the priests did not become the property of Pharaoh.

**27** Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen. They got property there. They had many children and became very many.

**28** Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for 17 years. The full age of Jacob was 147 years.

**29** The time came near for Israel to die. He called his son Joseph. He said to him, "If you love me, put your hand under my thigh. Promise to be kind and faithful to me. Do not bury me in Egypt."

**30** "When I die and go to my fathers, carry me out of Egypt. Bury me in their grave." Joseph said, "I will do as you say."

**31** Israel said, "Make a vow to me." Joseph made a vow to him. Then Israel bowed down at the head of his bed.

## Chapter 48

**1** After these things, someone told Joseph, "Your father is sick." Joseph took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, with him.

**2** Someone told Jacob, "Your son Joseph comes to you." Israel used his strength and sat up on the bed.

**3** Jacob said to Joseph, "God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan. He gave me a blessing."

**4** "He said to me, 'I will make you fruitful, and I will make you many. I will make you a group of nations. I will give this land to your descendants after you. The land will be their property for all time.'"

**5** "Your two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, are now mine. You became their father in the land of Egypt before I came to you. They will be mine, as Reuben and Simeon are mine."

**6** "The children that you will have after them will be yours. They will receive their inheritance under the names of their brothers."

**7** "When I came from Paddan, Rachel died near me in the land of Canaan. She died on the road, a short distance from Ephrath. I buried her there on the road to Ephrath. Ephrath is Bethlehem."

**8** Israel saw the sons of Joseph. He said, "Who are these boys?"

**9** Joseph said to his father, "They are my sons. God gave them to me here." Israel said, "Please bring them to me. I will give them a blessing."

**10** The eyes of Israel were weak from old age. He could not see well. Joseph brought his sons near to him. Israel kissed them and put his arms around them.

**11** Israel said to Joseph, "I did not think that I will see your face again. But God also let me see your children."

**12** Joseph took the boys from between the knees of Israel. Then Joseph bowed down with his face to the earth.

**13** Joseph took his two sons. He put Ephraim at his right hand, at the left hand of Israel. He put Manasseh at his left hand, at the right hand of Israel. He brought them near to Israel.

**14** Israel put out his right hand and put it on the head of Ephraim. Ephraim was the younger son. Israel put his left hand on the head of Manasseh. Manasseh was the first son. Israel crossed his hands on purpose.

**15** Israel gave a blessing to Joseph. He said, "My fathers Abraham and Isaac walked in front of God. God was my shepherd all my life until today."

**16** "The angel saved me from all evil. Let the angel give a blessing to these boys. Let my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac continue in them. Let them become very many on the earth."

**17** Joseph saw that his father put his right hand on the head of Ephraim. Joseph did not like this. He held the hand of his father to move it from the head of Ephraim to the head of Manasseh.

**18** Joseph said to his father, "Not so, my father. This boy is the first son. Put your right hand on his head."

**19** His father did not agree. He said, "I know, my son, I know. He will also become a people. He will also become great. But his younger brother will be greater than he. The descendants of his younger brother will become many nations."

**20** Israel gave them a blessing that day. He said, "The people of Israel will use your names in blessings. They will say, 'God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh.'" Thus Israel put Ephraim before Manasseh.

**21** Israel said to Joseph, "I will die soon. But God will be with you. He will bring you back to the land of your fathers."

**22** "I give you one more portion of land than your brothers. I took that land from the Amorites with my sword and my bow."

## Chapter 49

**1** Jacob called his sons. He said, "Come together. I will tell you what will occur to you in the days that will come."

**2** "Come together and listen, you sons of Jacob. Listen to Israel your father."

**3** "Reuben, you are my first son. You are my strength and the start of my power. You are the first in honor and the first in power."

**4** "But you are as unstable as water. You will not be first. You went up onto the bed of your father. You made my bed unclean."

**5** "Simeon and Levi are brothers. Their swords are weapons of violence."

**6** "My soul will not go into their secret meetings. My honor will not join their group. In their anger, they killed men. In their bad will, they made oxen lame."

**7** "I curse their anger, because their anger is fierce. I curse their fury, because their fury is cruel. I will divide them in Jacob. I will scatter them in Israel."

**8** "Judah, your brothers will praise you. Your hand will be on the neck of your enemies. The sons of your father will bow down to you."

**9** "Judah is a young lion. My son, you go up from the prey. He lies down like a lion. He is like a female lion. Who will make him get up?"

**10** "The scepter (the rod of a king) will not go away from Judah. The staff of a ruler will not go from between his feet. This will continue until Shiloh comes. The peoples will obey him."

**11** "He ties his young donkey to the vine. He ties the young of his donkey to the best vine. He washes his clothes in wine. He washes his robes in the blood of grapes."

**12** "His eyes will be red with wine. His teeth will be white with milk."

**13** "Zebulun will live at the shore of the sea. He will be a harbor for ships. His border will be near Sidon."

**14** "Issachar is a strong donkey. He lies down between two loads."

**15** "He saw that a place of rest was good. He saw that the land was pleasant. He put his shoulder under the load. He became a slave who does forced work."

**16** "Dan will judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel."

**17** "Dan will be a snake on the road. He will be a viper on the path. He bites the heels of the horse. Then the rider falls backward."

**18** "LORD, I wait for your salvation."

**19** "A group of attackers will attack Gad. But Gad will attack their heels."

**20** "Asher will have rich food. He will give food that is good for kings."

**21** "Naphtali is a free female deer. He says beautiful words."

**22** "Joseph is a fruitful vine. He is a fruitful vine near a spring. His branches go over the wall."

**23** "The archers attacked him angrily. They shot at him and hated him."

**24** "But his bow stayed strong. His arms stayed strong because of the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob. The Shepherd, the Stone of Israel, comes from there."

**25** "The God of your father will help you. The Almighty will give you blessings. He will give you blessings of the sky above and of the deep water below. He will give you blessings of the breasts and of the womb."

**26** "The blessings of your father are greater than the blessings of my ancestors. They go to the edge of the old hills. Let them be on the head of Joseph. Let them be on the head of the prince among his brothers."

**27** "Benjamin is a hungry wolf. In the morning, he eats the prey. In the evening, he divides the things that he took from his enemies."

**28** All these are the 12 tribes of Israel. Their father said these words to them. He gave each son the correct blessing for that son.

**29** Jacob gave orders to his sons. He said, "I will soon die and go to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite."

**30** "The cave is in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre, in the land of Canaan. Abraham bought the cave with the field from Ephron the Hittite. He bought the cave as a burial place."

**31** "People buried Abraham and his wife Sarah there. People buried Isaac and his wife Rebekah there. I buried Leah there."

**32** "Abraham bought the field and the cave from the sons of Heth."

**33** Jacob completed his orders to his sons. He put his feet up into the bed. He breathed his last breath and died. He went to his people.

## Chapter 50

**1** Joseph fell on the face of his father. He cried over him and kissed him.

**2** Joseph told his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father (to prepare the body with spices to keep it). The physicians embalmed Israel.

**3** They used 40 days for this work, because that work takes 40 days. The Egyptians cried for Jacob for 70 days.

**4** The days of sorrow for Jacob came to an end. Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh. He said, "If I find grace in your eyes, please speak to Pharaoh for me. Tell him this:"

**5** "'My father made me make a vow. He said, "I will die soon. Bury me in the grave that I dug for me in the land of Canaan." Now please let me go up and bury my father. Then I will come back.'"

**6** Pharaoh said, "Go up and bury your father, as you made a vow to him."

**7** Joseph went up to bury his father. All the servants of Pharaoh went up with him. The elders of the house of Pharaoh and all the elders of the land of Egypt went with him.

**8** All the family of Joseph, his brothers, and the family of his father also went. They left only their little children, their flocks, and their herds in the land of Goshen.

**9** Chariots and horsemen also went up with him. The group was very large.

**10** They came to the floor of Atad, where people beat the grain, on the other side of the Jordan. There they cried very loudly and with much sorrow. Joseph mourned for his father for 7 days.

**11** The Canaanites who lived in the land saw the sorrow at the floor of Atad, where people beat the grain. They said, "The Egyptians have a time of very deep sorrow." Thus people gave the place the name Abel Mizraim. The place is on the other side of the Jordan.

**12** The sons of Jacob did for him as he told them.

**13** His sons carried him into the land of Canaan. They buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, near Mamre. Abraham bought the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place.

**14** After Joseph buried his father, he went back into Egypt. His brothers and all the persons who went up with him to bury his father also went back.

**15** The brothers of Joseph saw that their father was dead. They said, "Maybe Joseph will hate us. Maybe he will do to us all the evil that we did to him."

**16** They sent a message to Joseph. They said, "Your father gave this order before he died:"

**17** "'Tell Joseph: "Please forgive the sin of your brothers. They did evil to you. Please forgive them."' Now, please forgive the sin of the servants of the God of your father." Joseph cried when they spoke to him.

**18** His brothers also came and fell down in front of him. They said, "We are your slaves."

**19** Joseph said to them, "Do not be afraid. I am not in the place of God."

**20** "You wanted to do evil against me. But God used the evil for good. He did so to keep many people alive, as he does today."

**21** "Now do not be afraid. I will give food to you and your little children." He comforted them and spoke kindly to them.

**22** Joseph lived in Egypt with the family of his father. Joseph lived 110 years.

**23** Joseph saw the children of Ephraim to the third generation. He also took the children of Machir, the son of Manasseh, onto his knees at their birth.

**24** Joseph said to his brothers, "I will die soon. But God will surely help you. He will bring you up out of this land. He will bring you to the land that he promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."

**25** Joseph made the children of Israel make a vow. He said, "God will surely help you. When he helps you, carry my bones up from here."

**26** Joseph died. He was 110 years old. They embalmed him. They put his body in a coffin in Egypt.

# Exodus

## Chapter 1

**1** These are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt with Jacob. Each man came with his family.

**2** The sons were Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,

**3** Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,

**4** Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

**5** The descendants of Jacob were 70 persons in total. Joseph was already in Egypt.

**6** Then Joseph died. All his brothers and all the people of that generation also died.

**7** But the Israelites had many children. Their number became very large, and they became very strong. They filled the land.

**8** Then a new king started to rule over Egypt. This king did not know about Joseph.

**9** The king said to his people, "Look, the Israelites are more numerous and stronger than we are.

**10** We must be careful with them. If we do nothing, their number will increase more. If a war starts, they will join our enemies. They will fight against us and go out of the land."

**11** Thus the Egyptians put slave masters over the Israelites to make their work very hard. The Israelites built the storage cities Pithom and Raamses for Pharaoh.

**12** But when the Egyptians made the work harder, the number of the Israelites increased more. The Egyptians became afraid of the Israelites.

**13** The Egyptians made the Israelites work very hard as slaves.

**14** They made the lives of the Israelites bitter with hard work. The Israelites made mortar and bricks and did all types of work in the fields. The Egyptians were cruel to them in all this work.

**15** The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives. The name of one midwife was Shiphrah, and the name of the other was Puah.

**16** The king said, "When you help the Hebrew women give birth, look at the baby. If the baby is a son, kill him. If the baby is a daughter, let her live."

**17** But the midwives had respect for God. They did not do what the king of Egypt told them. They let the boys live.

**18** The king of Egypt called the midwives. He said to them, "Why did you do this? Why did you let the boys live?"

**19** The midwives said to Pharaoh, "The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women. The Hebrew women are strong. They give birth before the midwife comes to them."

**20** Thus God was good to the midwives. The number of the people increased, and they became very strong.

**21** Because the midwives had respect for God, God gave them families of their own.

**22** Then Pharaoh gave an order to all his people. He said, "Throw every newborn Hebrew son into the river Nile. But let every daughter live."

## Chapter 2

**1** A man from the tribe of Levi married a woman from the tribe of Levi.

**2** The woman became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She saw that he was a beautiful child. She hid him for 3 months.

**3** After that time, she could not hide him longer. She got a basket made of reeds. She covered the basket with tar and pitch to keep the water out. She put the child in the basket. Then she put the basket in the reeds at the edge of the river.

**4** The sister of the child stood at a distance. She wanted to know what will happen to him.

**5** The daughter of Pharaoh came down to the river to wash. Her female servants walked along the edge of the river. She saw the basket among the reeds. She sent her servant to get the basket.

**6** She opened the basket and saw the child. The baby cried. She felt pity for him. She said, "This is one of the Hebrew children."

**7** Then the sister of the baby spoke to the daughter of Pharaoh. She said, "Do you want me to find a Hebrew woman to feed the baby for you?"

**8** The daughter of Pharaoh said to her, "Go." The girl went and called the mother of the child.

**9** The daughter of Pharaoh said to the woman, "Take this child and feed him for me. I will pay you." The woman took the child and fed him.

**10** The child grew. Then the woman brought him to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he became her son. She gave him the name Moses. She said, "I pulled him out of the water."

**11** When Moses was a man, he went out to his own people, the Hebrews. He saw their hard work. He saw an Egyptian who hit a Hebrew, one of his own people.

**12** Moses looked around in all directions. He saw that no person was there. Then he killed the Egyptian and hid the body in the sand.

**13** On the next day, Moses went out again. He saw 2 Hebrew men who fought. He said to the man who was wrong, "Why do you hit your fellow Hebrew?"

**14** The man said, "Who made you a ruler and a judge over us? Do you plan to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" Then Moses was afraid. He said, "Surely other people know what I did."

**15** Pharaoh heard about this and tried to kill Moses. But Moses ran away from Pharaoh. He went to live in the land of Midian. He sat down near a well.

**16** The priest of Midian had 7 daughters. They came to the well and got water. They filled the troughs to give water to the flock of their father.

**17** Some shepherds came and pushed the daughters away. But Moses stood up and helped the daughters. He gave water to their flock.

**18** The daughters went back to Reuel, their father. He said, "Why did you come back so early today?"

**19** They said, "An Egyptian saved us from the shepherds. He also got water for us and gave water to the flock."

**20** Reuel said to his daughters, "Where is the man? Why did you leave him there? Invite him to eat with us."

**21** Moses agreed to live with Reuel. Reuel gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses as his wife.

**22** Zipporah gave birth to a son. Moses gave him the name Gershom. Moses said, "I am a foreigner in a foreign land."

**23** After a long time, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites were sad because of their hard work as slaves. They cried for help. Their cry went up to God.

**24** God heard their sad cries. God remembered his agreement (covenant) with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

**25** God saw the Israelites, and God knew about their trouble.

## Chapter 3

**1** Moses kept the flock of his father-in-law, Jethro, the priest of Midian. Moses took the flock to the far side of the desert. He came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

**2** There the angel of the LORD appeared to Moses in a flame of fire from the middle of a bush. Moses looked. The bush burned, but the fire did not destroy the bush.

**3** Moses said, "I will go near and look at this strange thing. I want to know why the bush does not burn up."

**4** The LORD saw that Moses came near to look. God called to him from the middle of the bush. God said, "Moses! Moses!" Moses said, "I am here."

**5** God said, "Do not come nearer. Take off your sandals. The place where you stand is holy ground."

**6** God also said, "I am the God of your father. I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." Moses hid his face, because he was afraid to look at God.

**7** The LORD said, "I saw the trouble of my people in Egypt. I heard their cries because of their slave masters. I know about their pain.

**8** I came down to save them from the Egyptians. I will bring them out of Egypt to a good, large land. That land has much milk and honey. It is the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.

**9** The cry of the Israelites came to me. I also saw how the Egyptians are cruel to them.

**10** Thus go now. I will send you to Pharaoh. You will bring my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt."

**11** Moses said to God, "I am not an important person. How can I go to Pharaoh? How can I bring the Israelites out of Egypt?"

**12** God said, "I will be with you. This will be the sign that I sent you: when you bring the people out of Egypt, you will all worship God on this mountain."

**13** Moses said to God, "I will go to the Israelites. I will tell them, 'The God of your ancestors sent me to you.' Then they will ask me, 'What is his name?' What must I tell them?"

**14** God said to Moses, "I AM WHO I AM." He said, "Tell the Israelites this: 'I AM sent me to you.'"

**15** God also said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites this: 'The LORD, the God of your ancestors, sent me to you. He is the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' This is my name for all time. All generations will remember me by this name.

**16** Go and gather the leaders of Israel. Tell them, 'The LORD, the God of your ancestors, appeared to me. He is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He said, "I watched you carefully. I saw what the Egyptians do to you.

**17** I promise that I will bring you out of your trouble in Egypt. I will bring you to the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. That land has much milk and honey."'

**18** The leaders will listen to you. Then you and the leaders of Israel must go to the king of Egypt. Tell him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, met with us. Please let us go on a journey of 3 days into the desert. There we will offer sacrifices to the LORD our God.'

**19** I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go. He will not let you go, even if a strong hand pushes him.

**20** Thus I will use my power and attack Egypt. I will do many miracles among the Egyptians. After that, the king will let you go.

**21** I will cause the Egyptians to be kind to my people. When you go, you will not go with nothing.

**22** Each woman will ask her neighbor and any woman who lives in her house for silver and gold jewelry and clothing. You will put these things on your sons and daughters. In this way you will take the riches of the Egyptians."

## Chapter 4

**1** Moses said, "But the Israelites will not believe me. They will not listen to me. They will say, 'The LORD did not appear to you.'"

**2** The LORD said to Moses, "What is that in your hand?" Moses said, "A staff."

**3** The LORD said, "Throw it on the ground." Moses threw it on the ground, and the staff became a snake. Moses ran away from the snake.

**4** The LORD said to Moses, "Put out your hand and take the snake by the tail." Moses put out his hand and took the snake. The snake became a staff in his hand again.

**5** The LORD said, "Do this, and the people will believe that the LORD appeared to you. I am the LORD, the God of their ancestors, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob."

**6** The LORD also said to Moses, "Put your hand inside your coat." Moses put his hand inside his coat. When he took it out, his hand had a skin disease. The hand was white like snow.

**7** God said, "Put your hand inside your coat again." Moses put his hand inside his coat again. When he took it out, the hand was healthy again, as the rest of his body.

**8** The LORD said, "The people possibly will not believe you or the first sign. Then they will believe the second sign.

**9** If they do not believe these 2 signs and do not listen to you, take some water from the river Nile. Pour the water on the dry ground. The water from the river will become blood on the dry ground."

**10** Moses said to the LORD, "Please, Lord, I am not a good speaker. I was not a good speaker in the past. I am not a good speaker now that you spoke to me. My speech is slow, and my tongue is slow."

**11** The LORD said to him, "Who made the mouth of man? Who makes a person unable to speak or unable to hear? Who gives sight or makes a person blind? I, the LORD, do these things.

**12** Thus go now. I will help you speak. I will teach you what to say."

**13** But Moses said, "Please, Lord, send a different person."

**14** Then the LORD became angry with Moses. He said, "Your brother Aaron the Levite can speak well. I know this. Aaron comes now to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad.

**15** Speak to Aaron and tell him what to say. I will help you and Aaron speak. I will teach you both what to do.

**16** Aaron will speak to the people for you. He will be your mouth, and you will be like God to him.

**17** Take this staff in your hand. You will do the signs with the staff."

**18** Moses went back to Jethro, his father-in-law. Moses said to him, "Please let me go back to my people in Egypt. I want to see if they are still alive." Jethro said to Moses, "Go in peace."

**19** The LORD said to Moses in Midian, "Go back to Egypt. All the men who wanted to kill you are dead."

**20** Moses put his wife and his sons on a donkey and went back to Egypt. Moses held the staff of God in his hand.

**21** The LORD said to Moses, "When you go back to Egypt, do all the miracles in front of Pharaoh. I gave you the power to do them. But I will make Pharaoh stubborn. He will not let the people go.

**22** Then tell Pharaoh, 'The LORD says this: Israel is my son, my firstborn son.

**23** I told you to let my son go so that he can worship me. But you refused to let him go. Thus I will kill your son, your firstborn son.'"

**24** On the journey, Moses stopped at a place for the night. There the LORD met Moses and tried to kill him.

**25** Then Zipporah took a sharp stone and cut off the foreskin of her son. She touched the feet of Moses with the foreskin. She said, "Surely you are a husband of blood to me."

**26** Then the LORD let Moses live. Zipporah said, "You are a husband of blood," because of the circumcision.

**27** The LORD said to Aaron, "Go into the desert to meet Moses." Aaron went and met Moses at the mountain of God. Aaron kissed Moses.

**28** Moses told Aaron all the words that the LORD sent him to speak. Moses also told Aaron about all the signs that the LORD told him to do.

**29** Moses and Aaron went and gathered all the leaders of the Israelites.

**30** Aaron told them all the words that the LORD spoke to Moses. Aaron also did the signs in front of the people.

**31** The people believed. They heard that the LORD came to help the Israelites. They heard that he saw their trouble. Then they bowed their heads and worshipped.

## Chapter 5

**1** After that, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh. They said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: 'Let my people go. Then they can hold a festival for me in the desert.'"

**2** Pharaoh said, "Who is the LORD? Why must I obey him and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD. I will not let Israel go."

**3** Moses and Aaron said, "The God of the Hebrews met with us. Please let us go on a journey of 3 days into the desert. There we will offer sacrifices to the LORD our God. If we do not do this, he will possibly attack us with disease or with the sword."

**4** But the king of Egypt said to them, "Moses and Aaron, why do you stop the people from their work? Go back to your work!"

**5** Pharaoh also said, "Look, the people of the land are now many. And you make them stop their work."

**6** On that same day, Pharaoh gave orders to the slave masters and the foremen of the people. He said,

**7** "Do not give the people straw to make bricks as before. Let them go and gather straw for themselves.

**8** But they must make the same number of bricks as before. Do not decrease the number. They are lazy. That is why they cry, 'Let us go and offer sacrifices to our God.'

**9** Give the men more work. Keep them busy, so that they do not listen to lies."

**10** The slave masters and the foremen of the people went out. They said to the people, "Pharaoh says this: 'I will not give you straw.

**11** Go and get straw where you can find it. But your work will not decrease.'"

**12** Thus the people went to all parts of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.

**13** The slave masters pushed them to work fast. They said, "Each day, finish all your work, as when you had straw."

**14** Pharaoh's slave masters put Israelite foremen over the people. The slave masters hit these foremen. They asked, "Why did you not make the usual number of bricks yesterday and today, as before?"

**15** Then the Israelite foremen went to Pharaoh and cried out to him. They said, "Why do you do this to your servants?

**16** Your officials give us no straw. But they tell us, 'Make bricks!' And they hit your servants. But the fault is with your own people."

**17** Pharaoh said, "You are lazy! You are lazy! That is why you say, 'Let us go and offer sacrifices to the LORD.'

**18** Go now and work. We will give you no straw. But you must make the full number of bricks."

**19** The Israelite foremen saw that they were in trouble. Pharaoh told them, "You must not decrease the number of bricks each day."

**20** The foremen came out from Pharaoh. They met Moses and Aaron, who waited for them.

**21** The foremen said to Moses and Aaron, "The LORD will look at what you did and judge you. You caused Pharaoh and his officials to hate us. You gave them a reason to kill us."

**22** Then Moses went back to the LORD. Moses said, "Lord, why did you cause trouble for this people? Why did you send me?

**23** I went to Pharaoh to speak in your name. Since that time, he did more evil to this people. And you did not save your people at all."

## Chapter 6

**1** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh. My strong power will cause him to let the people go. My strong power will cause him to push them out of his land."

**2** God also spoke to Moses. He said, "I am the LORD.

**3** I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty. But I did not let them know me by my name, the LORD.

**4** I also made my agreement (covenant) with them. I promised to give them the land of Canaan. They lived in that land as foreigners.

**5** Also, I heard the sad cries of the Israelites. The Egyptians keep them as slaves. I remembered my covenant.

**6** Thus tell the Israelites this: 'I am the LORD. I will bring you out from under the hard work of the Egyptians. I will make you free from slavery. I will use my great power to save you. I will punish the Egyptians severely.

**7** I will take you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God. I will bring you out from under the hard work of the Egyptians.

**8** I will bring you to the land that I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I made a solemn promise to give it to them. I will give that land to you as your property. I am the LORD.'"

**9** Moses told this to the Israelites. But they did not listen to Moses. Their spirits were weak because of their cruel slavery.

**10** Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**11** "Go and tell Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to let the Israelites go out of his land."

**12** But Moses said to the LORD, "The Israelites did not listen to me. Thus Pharaoh will not listen to me. I am not a good speaker."

**13** But the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He gave them orders for the Israelites and for Pharaoh, king of Egypt. He told them to bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.

**14** These are the heads of the families of Israel. The sons of Reuben, the firstborn son of Israel, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. These were the families of Reuben.

**15** The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul. The mother of Shaul was a Canaanite woman. These were the families of Simeon.

**16** These are the names of the sons of Levi, in the order of their birth: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.

**17** The sons of Gershon were Libni and Shimei, with their families.

**18** The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.

**19** The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These were the families of Levi, in the order of their birth.

**20** Amram married Jochebed, the sister of his father. She gave birth to Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.

**21** The sons of Izhar were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.

**22** The sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Zithri.

**23** Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon. She gave birth to Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

**24** The sons of Korah were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. These were the families of the Korahites.

**25** Eleazar, the son of Aaron, married one of the daughters of Putiel. She gave birth to Phinehas. These were the heads of the families of the Levites.

**26** These are the same Aaron and Moses to whom the LORD spoke. The LORD said, "Bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt, group by group, as an army."

**27** Moses and Aaron spoke to Pharaoh, king of Egypt. They told him to let the Israelites go out of Egypt.

**28** On a day in Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses.

**29** The LORD said to Moses, "I am the LORD. Tell Pharaoh, king of Egypt, all the things that I tell you."

**30** But Moses said to the LORD, "I am not a good speaker. Pharaoh will not listen to me."

## Chapter 7

**1** The LORD said to Moses, "Look, I make you like God to Pharaoh. Your brother Aaron will be your prophet.

**2** Speak all the things that I tell you. Then your brother Aaron must tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his land.

**3** But I will make Pharaoh stubborn. I will do many signs and miracles in the land of Egypt.

**4** Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will use my power against Egypt. I will punish Egypt severely. I will bring my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt group by group.

**5** I will use my power against Egypt and bring the Israelites out. Then the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD."

**6** Moses and Aaron did all the things that the LORD told them.

**7** Moses was 80 years old, and Aaron was 83 years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

**8** The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

**9** "Pharaoh will tell you, 'Show me a miracle.' Then tell Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down in front of Pharaoh.' The staff will become a snake."

**10** Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh. They did what the LORD told them. Aaron threw down his staff in front of Pharaoh and his officials. The staff became a snake.

**11** Then Pharaoh called his wise men and sorcerers. The magicians of Egypt used their secret arts and did the same thing.

**12** Each magician threw down his staff, and each staff became a snake. But the staff of Aaron swallowed their staffs.

**13** But Pharaoh became stubborn. He did not listen to Moses and Aaron, as the LORD said.

**14** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh is stubborn. He refuses to let the people go.

**15** Go to Pharaoh in the morning when he goes out to the water. Stand on the bank of the river Nile to meet him. Hold in your hand the staff that became a snake.

**16** Tell him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you. He told you, "Let my people go, so that they can worship me in the desert." But until now you did not listen.

**17** The LORD says this: "By this you will know that I am the LORD." Look, I will hit the water of the river Nile with the staff in my hand. The water will become blood.

**18** The fish in the river will die. The river will smell bad. The Egyptians will not be able to drink water from the river.'"

**19** The LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Take your staff. Hold your hand out over the waters of Egypt.' Hold it over their streams, canals, ponds, and all their pools. The water will become blood. There will be blood in all the land of Egypt. There will be blood even in containers of wood and stone."

**20** Moses and Aaron did what the LORD told them. Aaron lifted up the staff and hit the water of the river Nile. Pharaoh and his officials saw this. All the water in the river became blood.

**21** The fish in the river died. The river smelled bad. The Egyptians could not drink water from the river. There was blood in all the land of Egypt.

**22** But the magicians of Egypt did the same thing with their secret arts. Thus Pharaoh stayed stubborn. He did not listen to Moses and Aaron, as the LORD said.

**23** Pharaoh turned and went into his house. He did not think about this miracle.

**24** All the Egyptians dug along the river to find water to drink. They could not drink the water of the river.

**25** 7 days went by after the LORD hit the river.

## Chapter 8

**1** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and tell him, 'The LORD says this: Let my people go. Then they can worship me.

**2** If you refuse to let them go, I will send frogs on all your country.

**3** The river Nile will be full of frogs. The frogs will come into your palace, into your bedroom, and onto your bed. They will come into the houses of your officials and onto your people. They will come into your ovens and into your bowls for bread.

**4** The frogs will come up on you, on your people, and on all your officials.'"

**5** The LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Hold your staff out over the streams, the canals, and the ponds. Cause frogs to come up on the land of Egypt.'"

**6** Aaron held his hand out over the waters of Egypt. The frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.

**7** But the magicians did the same thing with their secret arts. They also caused frogs to come up on the land of Egypt.

**8** Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron. He said, "Pray to the LORD. Ask him to take the frogs away from me and from my people. Then I will let the people go to offer sacrifices to the LORD."

**9** Moses said to Pharaoh, "You can choose the time. Tell me when to pray for you, your officials, and your people. Then the frogs will go away from you and your houses. Frogs will stay only in the river Nile."

**10** Pharaoh said, "Tomorrow." Moses said, "It will be as you say. Then you will know that there is no god like the LORD our God.

**11** The frogs will go away from you, your houses, your officials, and your people. Frogs will stay only in the river Nile."

**12** Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh. Then Moses prayed to the LORD about the frogs that the LORD sent on Pharaoh.

**13** The LORD did what Moses asked. The frogs died in the houses, the yards, and the fields.

**14** The people put the dead frogs in piles. The land smelled bad.

**15** But Pharaoh saw that the trouble stopped. Then he became stubborn again. He did not listen to Moses and Aaron, as the LORD said.

**16** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Hold out your staff and hit the dust on the ground.' The dust will become gnats in all the land of Egypt."

**17** Moses and Aaron did this. Aaron held out his hand with the staff and hit the dust on the ground. Gnats came on the people and on the animals. All the dust in the land of Egypt became gnats.

**18** The magicians tried to make gnats with their secret arts, but they could not. The gnats stayed on the people and on the animals.

**19** The magicians said to Pharaoh, "God did this with his power." But Pharaoh stayed stubborn. He did not listen to Moses and Aaron, as the LORD said.

**20** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning. Stand in front of Pharaoh when he goes out to the water. Tell him, 'The LORD says this: Let my people go, so that they can worship me.

**21** If you do not let my people go, I will send swarms of flies on you, your officials, and your people. The flies will go into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be full of flies. The ground also will be full of flies.

**22** But on that day I will keep the land of Goshen separate, where my people live. No flies will be there. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am in this land.

**23** I will make a difference between my people and your people. This sign will occur tomorrow.'"

**24** The LORD did this. Large swarms of flies came into the palace of Pharaoh and into the houses of his officials. The flies went into all the land of Egypt. The flies destroyed the land.

**25** Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron. He said, "Go and offer sacrifices to your God here in this land."

**26** But Moses said, "That is not correct. The Egyptians hate the sacrifices that we give to the LORD our God. If we offer those sacrifices in front of the Egyptians, they will throw stones at us and kill us.

**27** We must go on a journey of 3 days into the desert. There we will offer sacrifices to the LORD our God, as he tells us."

**28** Pharaoh said, "I will let you go to offer sacrifices to the LORD your God in the desert. But do not go very far. Pray for me."

**29** Moses said, "I will go out from you and pray to the LORD. Tomorrow the flies will go away from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. But Pharaoh must not lie to us again. He must let the people go to offer sacrifices to the LORD."

**30** Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD.

**31** The LORD did what Moses asked. He took the flies away from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. Not 1 fly stayed.

**32** But Pharaoh became stubborn again. He did not let the people go.

## Chapter 9

**1** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and tell him this. 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says this: Let my people go. Then they can worship me.

**2** Possibly you will refuse to let them go and keep them.

**3** Then the LORD will use his power against your animals in the fields. He will send a very bad disease on your horses, donkeys, camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.

**4** But the LORD will make a difference between the animals of Israel and the animals of Egypt. No animal that belongs to the Israelites will die.'"

**5** The LORD set a time. He said, "Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land."

**6** On the next day, the LORD did this. All the animals of the Egyptians died. But not 1 animal of the Israelites died.

**7** Pharaoh sent men to look. Not 1 animal of the Israelites was dead. But Pharaoh stayed stubborn. He did not let the people go.

**8** Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Take handfuls of ashes from a furnace. Moses must throw the ashes into the air in front of Pharaoh.

**9** The ashes will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt. The dust will cause painful sores on the people and on the animals in all the land of Egypt."

**10** Moses and Aaron took ashes from a furnace and stood in front of Pharaoh. Moses threw the ashes into the air. Painful sores came on the people and on the animals.

**11** The magicians could not stand in front of Moses because of the sores. The sores were on the magicians and on all the Egyptians.

**12** But the LORD made Pharaoh stubborn. Pharaoh did not listen to Moses and Aaron, as the LORD told Moses.

**13** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning and stand in front of Pharaoh. Tell him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says this: Let my people go, so that they can worship me.

**14** This time I will send all my plagues against you, your officials, and your people. Then you will know that there is no god like me in all the earth.

**15** I could use my power now and attack you and your people with disease. Then you will be gone from the earth.

**16** But I let you live for this reason: to show you my power. I want all people on the earth to know my name.

**17** You still act proudly against my people. You do not let them go.

**18** Thus tomorrow at this time I will send very heavy hail. There was never hail like this in Egypt from the start of the nation until now.

**19** Thus send an order now. Bring your animals and all that you have in the fields into a shelter. The hail will fall on every person and animal that stays in the field. They will die.'"

**20** Some officials of Pharaoh had respect for the word of the LORD. They quickly brought their slaves and their animals into shelters.

**21** But other officials did not pay attention to the word of the LORD. They left their slaves and their animals in the fields.

**22** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Hold your hand up toward the sky. Then hail will fall on all the land of Egypt. It will fall on the people, on the animals, and on all the plants in the fields of Egypt."

**23** Moses held his staff up toward the sky. The LORD sent thunder and hail. Lightning hit the ground. The LORD caused hail to fall on the land of Egypt.

**24** The hail was very heavy, and lightning flashed among the hail. There was never a storm like this in all of Egypt since it became a nation.

**25** In all the land of Egypt, the hail hit all the people and animals in the fields. The hail destroyed all the plants in the fields. It broke all the trees.

**26** Only in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was there no hail.

**27** Then Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron. He said to them, "This time I sinned. The LORD is right, and I and my people are wrong.

**28** Pray to the LORD. We had enough of this thunder and hail. I will let you go. You do not have to stay here longer."

**29** Moses said to Pharaoh, "When I go out of the city, I will lift up my hands in prayer to the LORD. The thunder will stop, and there will be no more hail. Then you will know that the earth belongs to the LORD.

**30** But I know that you and your officials still do not have respect for the LORD God."

**31** The hail destroyed the flax and the barley. The barley had heads of grain, and the flax had flowers.

**32** But the hail did not destroy the wheat and the spelt, because they grow later.

**33** Moses left Pharaoh and went out of the city. He lifted up his hands to the LORD. The thunder and the hail stopped. No more rain fell on the land.

**34** Pharaoh saw that the rain, the hail, and the thunder stopped. Then he sinned again. Pharaoh and his officials became stubborn again.

**35** Pharaoh stayed stubborn. He did not let the Israelites go, as the LORD said through Moses.

## Chapter 10

**1** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh. I made Pharaoh and his officials stubborn. I did this so that I can show these miraculous signs among them.

**2** I also did this so that you can tell your children and your grandchildren about my actions in Egypt. Tell them about the signs that I did among the Egyptians. Then you will all know that I am the LORD."

**3** Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh. They said to him, "The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says this: 'How long will you refuse to be humble in front of me? Let my people go, so that they can worship me.

**4** If you refuse to let my people go, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your country.

**5** The locusts will cover the ground. No person will be able to see the ground. They will eat the few plants that the hail did not destroy. They will eat all the trees that grow in your fields.

**6** They will fill your houses, the houses of your officials, and the houses of all the Egyptians. Your fathers and your grandfathers never saw so many locusts. They did not see this from the time that they lived on the earth until today.'" Then Moses turned and went out from Pharaoh.

**7** The officials of Pharaoh said to him, "How long will this man be a danger to us? Let the men go. Then they can worship the LORD their God. Do you not know that Egypt is in ruins?"

**8** Then the officials brought Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh. Pharaoh said to them, "Go and worship the LORD your God. But tell me, who will go?"

**9** Moses said, "We will go with our young people and our old people. We will go with our sons and our daughters, and with our flocks and our herds. We must hold a festival for the LORD."

**10** Pharaoh said to them, "I will never let you go with your children. The LORD will need to be with you for that! Look, you plan to do evil.

**11** No! Only the men can go and worship the LORD. That is what you asked for." Then Pharaoh's officials pushed Moses and Aaron out from Pharaoh.

**12** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Hold your hand out over the land of Egypt. Then locusts will come on the land of Egypt. They will eat all the plants in the land that the hail did not destroy."

**13** Moses held his staff out over the land of Egypt. Then the LORD caused an east wind to blow over the land all that day and all that night. In the morning, the east wind brought the locusts.

**14** The locusts came on all the land of Egypt. They landed on all parts of Egypt. There were very many locusts. There were never so many locusts before, and there will never be so many again.

**15** The locusts covered the ground until the land was dark. They ate all the plants in the land and all the fruit on the trees that the hail did not destroy. No green thing stayed on the trees or on the plants in all the land of Egypt.

**16** Then Pharaoh quickly called Moses and Aaron. He said, "I sinned against the LORD your God and against you.

**17** Now please forgive my sin only this 1 time. Pray to the LORD your God. Ask him to take away this deadly plague from me."

**18** Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD.

**19** The LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind. The wind took away the locusts and blew them into the Red Sea. Not 1 locust stayed in all of Egypt.

**20** But the LORD made Pharaoh stubborn. Pharaoh did not let the Israelites go.
