**16** Take this atonement money from the Israelites. Use it for the work of the Tent of Meeting. It will remind the LORD of the Israelites. It will make atonement for your lives."

**17** Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**18** "Make a large bronze bowl with a bronze base. Use it to wash. Put it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar. Put water in it.

**19** Aaron and his sons must wash their hands and their feet with the water from the bowl.

**20** When they go into the Tent of Meeting, they must wash with water. Then they will not die. They must also wash when they come near the altar to burn an offering to the LORD.

**21** They must wash their hands and their feet so that they do not die. This is a permanent law for Aaron and his descendants in all future generations."

**22** Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**23** "Take the best spices. Take 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, 250 shekels of sweet cinnamon, and 250 shekels of sweet cane.

**24** Also take 500 shekels of cassia and 1 hin of olive oil. Use the shekel of the holy place to weigh them.

**25** Make a holy oil to anoint from these things. Mix them carefully, as a perfume maker does. This will be the holy oil to anoint.

**26** Use this oil to anoint the Tent of Meeting and the ark of the testimony.

**27** Also anoint the table and all its tools, the lampstand and its tools, and the altar of incense.

**28** Also anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its tools, and the large bowl and its base.

**29** Make these things holy. Then they will be most holy. Any thing that touches them will become holy.

**30** Anoint Aaron and his sons and make them holy. Then they can serve me as priests.

**31** Tell the Israelites, 'This will be my holy oil to anoint in all future generations.

**32** Do not pour it on the bodies of ordinary people. Do not make any other oil with the same mixture. It is holy, and you must treat it as holy.

**33** A person can make oil with the same mixture, or put it on a person who is not a priest. Remove that person from his people.'"

**34** Then the LORD said to Moses, "Take sweet spices: stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense. Use the same weight of each spice.

**35** Make incense from these spices. Mix them as a perfume maker does. Add salt to it. It must be pure and holy.

**36** Crush some of it into very fine powder. Put the powder in front of the tablets of the law in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you. This incense must be most holy to you.

**37** Do not make incense with the same mixture for yourselves. This incense is holy, and it belongs to the LORD.

**38** If a person makes incense like it to enjoy its smell, remove that person from his people."

## Chapter 31

**1** Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Look, I chose Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.

**3** I filled him with the Spirit of God. I gave him wisdom, good sense, knowledge, and skill in all types of work.

**4** He can make artistic designs. He can work with gold, silver, and bronze.

**5** He can cut stones and set them. He can carve wood. He can do all types of skilled work.

**6** I also chose Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to help Bezalel. I gave skill to all the skilled workers. They will make all the things that I told you to make.

**7** They will make the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the testimony with its cover, and all the other equipment of the tent.

**8** They will make the table and its tools, the pure gold lampstand and all its tools, and the altar of incense.

**9** They will make the altar of burnt offering and all its tools, and the large bowl and its base.

**10** They will make the woven clothes. They will make the holy clothes for Aaron the priest and the clothes for his sons when they serve as priests.

**11** They will make the holy oil to anoint and the sweet incense for the Holy Place. They must make all these things as I told you."

**12** Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**13** "Tell the Israelites, 'You must obey the rules of my Sabbath days. The Sabbath is a sign between me and you in all future generations. It shows that I, the LORD, make you holy.

**14** Keep the Sabbath, because it is holy for you. If a person does not treat the Sabbath as holy, you must kill that person. If a person does any work on the Sabbath, remove that person from his people.

**15** Do work for 6 days. But the seventh day is a Sabbath, a day of complete rest. It is holy to the LORD. If a person does any work on the Sabbath day, you must kill that person.

**16** The Israelites must keep the Sabbath. They must keep it in all future generations as a permanent covenant.

**17** The Sabbath is a permanent sign between me and the Israelites. In 6 days the LORD made the sky and the earth. On the seventh day he stopped his work and rested.'"

**18** The LORD finished his talk with Moses on Mount Sinai. Then he gave Moses the 2 tablets of the testimony. The tablets were stone. God wrote the words on them with his own finger.

## Chapter 32

**1** The people saw that Moses stayed on the mountain for a long time. They gathered around Aaron and said to him, "Come, make gods for us to lead us. Moses brought us out of Egypt, but we do not know what happened to him."

**2** Aaron said to them, "Take off the gold earrings from the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters. Bring them to me."

**3** Thus all the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.

**4** Aaron took the gold from them. He melted it and made a statue of a calf. He used a tool to give it shape. Then the people said, "Israel, these are your gods who brought you out of Egypt!"

**5** Aaron saw this and built an altar in front of the calf. Then Aaron said, "Tomorrow we will hold a festival to the LORD."

**6** On the next day, the people got up early. They offered burnt offerings and brought peace offerings. Then the people sat down to eat and drink. After that, they got up to celebrate wildly.

**7** The LORD said to Moses, "Go down, because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, became corrupt.

**8** They quickly stopped and did not obey my commands. They made a metal statue of a calf for themselves. They worshipped it and offered sacrifices to it. They said, 'Israel, these are your gods who brought you out of Egypt.'"

**9** The LORD also said to Moses, "I watched these people. They are very stubborn people.

**10** Now do not try to stop me. I am very angry with them. I will destroy them. Then I will make you into a great nation."

**11** But Moses asked the LORD his God for mercy. Moses said, "LORD, why are you so angry with your people? You brought them out of Egypt with great power and strength.

**12** Do not let the Egyptians say, 'God brought them out with an evil plan. He wanted to kill them in the mountains and remove them from the earth.' Stop your strong anger. Change your mind and do not do this evil thing to your people.

**13** Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. You made a solemn promise to them in your own name. You told them, 'I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky. I will give your descendants all this land that I promised. It will always be their land.'"

**14** Then the LORD changed his mind. He did not do the evil thing that he said he will do to his people.

**15** Moses turned and went down the mountain. He held the 2 tablets of the testimony in his hands. There were words on both sides of the tablets, on the front and on the back.

**16** God made the tablets. God also wrote the words that he cut into the tablets.

**17** Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted. He said to Moses, "There is a sound of war in the camp."

**18** Moses said, "It is not the sound of victory. It is not the sound of defeat. I hear the sound of people who sing."

**19** Moses came near the camp. He saw the calf and the people who danced. Then Moses became very angry. He threw the tablets down and broke them at the bottom of the mountain.

**20** He took the calf that the people made and burned it in the fire. Then he ground it into powder. He put the powder in the water and made the Israelites drink it.

**21** Moses said to Aaron, "What did these people do to you? Why did you cause them to commit such a great sin?"

**22** Aaron said, "My master, do not be angry. You know that these people always want to do evil.

**23** They said to me, 'Make gods for us to lead us. Moses brought us out of Egypt, but we do not know what happened to him.'

**24** I said to them, 'If you have gold, take it off.' They gave me the gold. I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out!"

**25** Moses saw that the people were out of control. Aaron let them get out of control. Thus their enemies laughed at them.

**26** Thus Moses stood at the entrance of the camp. He said, "All the people who are on the side of the LORD, come to me." All the Levites gathered around him.

**27** Moses said to them, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: 'Each man must take his sword. Go through the camp from 1 end to the other. Each man must kill his brother, his friend, and his neighbor.'"

**28** The Levites did what Moses told them. On that day about 3,000 of the people died.

**29** Moses said, "Today you set yourselves apart to serve the LORD. You did this at the cost of your sons and your brothers. Thus the LORD gave you a blessing today."

**30** On the next day, Moses said to the people, "You committed a very great sin. But now I will go up to the LORD. Possibly I can make atonement for your sin."

**31** Moses went back to the LORD. He said, "These people committed a very great sin. They made gods of gold for themselves.

**32** But now, please forgive their sin. If you do not forgive them, then remove my name from the book that you wrote."

**33** The LORD said to Moses, "I will remove from my book the name of each person who sinned against me.

**34** Now go and lead the people to the place that I told you about. My angel will go in front of you. But when the time comes to punish, I will punish them for their sin."

**35** Then the LORD sent a plague on the people, because they worshipped the calf that Aaron made.

## Chapter 33

**1** The LORD said to Moses, "Leave this place. Go with the people that you brought out of the land of Egypt. Go to the land that I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I said to them, 'I will give the land to your descendants.'

**2** I will send an angel in front of you. I will push out the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.

**3** Go to a land that has much milk and honey. But I will not go with you. You are a stubborn people. If I go with you, I can destroy you on the road."

**4** The people heard these bad words, and they were very sad. No person put on his jewelry.

**5** The LORD said to Moses, "Tell the people of Israel, 'You are a stubborn people. If I go with you for 1 moment, I can destroy you. Thus, remove your jewelry now. Then I will decide what to do with you.'"

**6** Thus, the people of Israel removed their jewelry at Mount Horeb.

**7** Moses took the tent and put it outside the camp, at a distance from the camp. He called it the Tent of Meeting. Each person who wanted to ask the LORD a question went out to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.

**8** When Moses went out to the tent, all the people stood up. Each man stood at the door of his tent. The people watched Moses until he went into the tent.

**9** When Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud came down. The pillar stood at the door of the tent, and the LORD spoke with Moses.

**10** All the people saw the pillar of cloud at the door of the tent. All the people stood up and worshipped. Each man worshipped at the door of his tent.

**11** The LORD spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Then Moses went back into the camp. But his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, did not leave the tent.

**12** Moses said to the LORD, "Look, you tell me, 'Lead these people.' But you did not tell me who you will send with me. You said, 'I know you by name, and I am happy with you.'

**13** If you are happy with me, show me your ways. Then I will know you, and you will continue to be happy with me. Remember that this nation is your people."

**14** The LORD said, "I will go with you. I will give you rest."

**15** Moses said to him, "If you do not go with us, do not send us from this place.

**16** If you do not go with us, how will people know that you are happy with me and with your people? Your presence makes us different. It makes me and your people different from all the other people on the earth."

**17** The LORD said to Moses, "I will also do this thing that you ask. I am happy with you, and I know you by name."

**18** Moses said, "Please show me your glory."

**19** The LORD said, "I will cause all my goodness to go in front of you. I will speak my name, 'the LORD,' in front of you. I will be kind to the person that I choose. I will show mercy to the person that I choose."

**20** He said, "But you cannot see my face. No person can see me and continue to live."

**21** The LORD said, "Look, there is a place near me. You will stand on a rock there.

**22** When my glory goes past, I will put you in a crack in the rock. I will cover you with my hand until I go past.

**23** Then I will remove my hand, and you will see my back. But you will not see my face."

## Chapter 34

**1** The LORD said to Moses, "Cut 2 flat stones (tablets) the same as the first tablets. I will write on these tablets the words that were on the first tablets. You broke those tablets.

**2** Be ready in the morning. In the morning, come up Mount Sinai. Stand in front of me there at the top of the mountain.

**3** No person must come up with you. No person must be on any part of the mountain. Do not let the sheep or the cattle eat grass in front of that mountain."

**4** Thus, Moses cut 2 stone tablets the same as the first tablets. He got up early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD told him. He carried the 2 stone tablets in his hand.

**5** The LORD came down in the cloud and stood there with Moses. The LORD spoke his name, "the LORD."

**6** The LORD went past in front of Moses and said, "The LORD, the LORD God, is merciful and kind. He is slow to become angry. He has much love and he is very faithful.

**7** He continues to show love to thousands of people. He forgives wrong actions, rebellion, and sin. But he will not let the guilty go without punishment. He punishes the children and the grandchildren for the sins of their fathers. He punishes them to the third and fourth generation."

**8** Moses quickly bowed his head to the ground and worshipped.

**9** He said, "Lord, if you are happy with me, please go with us. These people are stubborn. But forgive our wrong actions and our sin. Take us as your own people."

**10** The LORD said, "Look, I make an agreement (covenant). In front of all your people, I will do wonderful things. No person did such things on all the earth or in any nation before. All the people near you will see the work of the LORD. The thing that I will do for you will cause fear.

**11** Obey what I tell you today. I will push out the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites in front of you.

**12** Be careful. Do not make a covenant with the people who live in the land where you go. That covenant will be a trap among you.

**13** You must destroy their altars. Break their stone pillars. Cut down their poles for the goddess Asherah.

**14** Do not worship any other god. The LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

**15** Do not make a covenant with the people who live in the land. They are not faithful to me, and they worship their gods. They make sacrifices to their gods. Then a person will invite you, and you will eat from his sacrifice.

**16** Then you will take their daughters as wives for your sons. Their daughters will worship their gods. Then their daughters will cause your sons to worship their gods too.

**17** Do not make gods from melted metal.

**18** Keep the Festival of Bread Without Yeast. For 7 days, eat bread without yeast, as I told you. Do this at the correct time in the month of Abib. In the month of Abib, you came out of Egypt.

**19** Each first male child is mine. Each first male animal of your cattle and sheep is mine.

**20** Buy back the first male donkey with a lamb. If you do not buy it back, then break its neck. Buy back all your first sons. No person must come to me with empty hands.

**21** Work for 6 days, but rest on the seventh day. Rest also in the time to plow and in the time to harvest.

**22** Keep the Festival of Weeks with the first grain of the wheat harvest. Keep the Festival of Harvest at the end of the year.

**23** 3 times each year, all your men must come in front of the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.

**24** I will push out the nations in front of you, and I will make your land larger. No person will try to take your land when you go to the LORD your God 3 times each year.

**25** Do not give the blood of my sacrifice with bread that has yeast. Do not keep any of the Passover sacrifice until the morning.

**26** Bring the best of the first crops of your land to the house of the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in the milk of its mother."

**27** The LORD said to Moses, "Write these words. I make a covenant with you and with Israel by these words."

**28** Moses was there with the LORD for 40 days and 40 nights. He did not eat bread or drink water. The LORD wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the 10 commandments.

**29** Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the 2 tablets of the testimony in his hand. Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he spoke with the LORD.

**30** Aaron and all the people of Israel saw Moses. The skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to come near him.

**31** But Moses called to them. Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and Moses spoke with them.

**32** After that, all the people of Israel came near. Moses gave them all the commands that the LORD told him on Mount Sinai.

**33** When Moses stopped and did not speak with them more, he put a cloth (veil) on his face.

**34** When Moses went in to speak with the LORD, he removed the veil until he came out. Then he came out and told the people of Israel what the LORD commanded.

**35** The people of Israel saw that the skin of the face of Moses shone. Then Moses put the veil on his face again until he went in to speak with the LORD.

## Chapter 35

**1** Moses gathered all the community of the people of Israel. He said to them, "These are the things that the LORD commands you to do.

**2** Work for 6 days. But the seventh day must be a holy day for you, a Sabbath of rest to the LORD. Kill each person who does work on that day.

**3** Do not make a fire in any of your homes on the Sabbath day."

**4** Moses spoke to all the community of the people of Israel. He said, "This is what the LORD commands.

**5** Collect an offering for the LORD from among you. Each person who wants to give must bring an offering to the LORD. Bring gold, silver, and bronze.

**6** Bring blue, purple, and red yarn, fine linen, and goat hair.

**7** Bring ram skins that have a red color, fine leather, and acacia wood.

**8** Bring olive oil for the light. Bring spices for the holy oil to anoint and for the sweet incense.

**9** Bring onyx stones and other stones to put on the ephod and on the breastplate.

**10** Each skilled person among you must come. He must make all the things that the LORD commands.

**11** Make the tabernacle, its tent, and its cover. Make its hooks, frames, bars, posts, and bases.

**12** Make the ark and its poles, the mercy seat, and the curtain that hangs in front of the ark.

**13** Make the table, its poles, and all its equipment, and the holy bread.

**14** Make the lampstand for the light, its equipment, its lamps, and the oil for the light.

**15** Make the incense altar and its poles. Make the holy oil to anoint and the sweet incense. Make the curtain for the door at the entrance of the tabernacle.

**16** Make the altar of burnt offering, its bronze grate, its poles, and all its equipment. Make the basin and its base.

**17** Make the curtains of the courtyard, its posts, and their bases. Make the curtain for the gate of the courtyard.

**18** Make the tent pegs of the tabernacle and the courtyard, and their ropes.

**19** Make the woven clothes for the work in the holy place. Make the holy clothes for Aaron the priest and the clothes for his sons. They will wear these clothes when they do the work of priests."

**20** Then all the community of the people of Israel went away from Moses.

**21** Each person who wanted to give came. They brought the offering of the LORD for the work on the Tent of Meeting. They brought offerings for all its services and for the holy clothes.

**22** Men and women came. All the people who wanted to give brought gold jewelry. They brought pins, earrings, rings, and necklaces. Each person gave an offering of gold to the LORD.

**23** Each man who had blue, purple, or red yarn, fine linen, or goat hair brought it. Each man who had red ram skins or fine leather brought them.

**24** Each person who gave silver or bronze brought it as an offering to the LORD. Each man who had acacia wood for the work brought the wood.

**25** All the skilled women made yarn with their hands. They brought the blue, purple, and red yarn and the fine linen that they made.

**26** All the skilled women who wanted to help made yarn from goat hair.

**27** The leaders brought onyx stones and other stones to put on the ephod and on the breastplate.

**28** They brought spices and olive oil for the light, for the holy oil to anoint, and for the sweet incense.

**29** All the men and women of Israel who wanted to give brought gifts to the LORD. They brought these gifts for all the work that the LORD told Moses to do.

**30** Then Moses said to the people of Israel, "Look, the LORD chose Bezalel by name. Bezalel is the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.

**31** The LORD filled Bezalel with the Spirit of God. He gave him skill, good sense, and knowledge for all types of work.

**32** Bezalel can make good designs. He can work with gold, silver, and bronze.

**33** He can cut stones and put them in settings. He can cut wood. He can do all types of skilled work.

**34** The LORD gave him and Oholiab the ability to teach other people. Oholiab is the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

**35** The LORD filled them with skill to do all types of work. They can engrave, design, and sew with blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen. They can weave cloth. They can do all types of work and make good designs."

## Chapter 36

**1** Bezalel, Oholiab, and each skilled man worked. The LORD gave these men skill and good sense to do all the work for the holy place. They did all the work as the LORD commanded.

**2** Moses called Bezalel, Oholiab, and each skilled man. The LORD gave these men skill. Each of them wanted to come and do the work.

**3** They received from Moses all the offerings that the people of Israel brought for the work of the holy place. The people continued to bring free offerings to Moses each morning.

**4** Then all the skilled men who did the work of the holy place stopped their work. They came to Moses.

**5** They said to Moses, "The people bring much more than we need. We need less for the work that the LORD commanded."

**6** Moses gave a command, and the men sent a message through the camp. The message said, "Men and women, do not make more things for the offering of the holy place." Thus, the people stopped and did not bring more things.

**7** The people had more than enough material to do all the work.

**8** All the skilled men made the tabernacle with 10 curtains. They made the curtains of fine linen and blue, purple, and red yarn. Bezalel put designs of cherubim (winged beings) in the curtains.

**9** Each curtain was 28 cubits long and 4 cubits wide. All the curtains had the same size.

**10** He joined 5 curtains together. He joined the other 5 curtains together.

**11** He made loops of blue yarn on the edge of the last curtain in the first set. He did the same on the edge of the last curtain in the second set.

**12** He made 50 loops on the first curtain. He made 50 loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set. The loops were opposite each other.

**13** He made 50 gold hooks. He joined the curtains together with the hooks. Thus, the tabernacle was 1 unit.

**14** He made 11 curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle.

**15** Each curtain was 30 cubits long and 4 cubits wide. The 11 curtains had the same size.

**16** He joined 5 curtains together. He joined the other 6 curtains together.

**17** He made 50 loops on the edge of the last curtain in the first set. He made 50 loops on the edge of the last curtain in the second set.

**18** He made 50 bronze hooks to join the tent together. Thus, the tent was 1 unit.

**19** He made a cover for the tent from ram skins with a red color. Above that, he put a cover of fine leather.

**20** He made upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.

**21** Each frame was 10 cubits long and 1.5 cubits wide.

**22** Each frame had 2 pegs to join it to the next frame. He made all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.

**23** He made 20 frames for the south side of the tabernacle.

**24** He made 40 silver bases to put under the 20 frames. He put 2 bases under each frame, 1 for each peg.

**25** For the north side of the tabernacle, he made 20 frames.

**26** He made 40 silver bases for these frames, 2 bases under each frame.

**27** For the back of the tabernacle on the west side, he made 6 frames.

**28** He made 2 frames for the back corners of the tabernacle.

**29** These 2 frames were double from the bottom to the top. They joined at the top in 1 ring. He made the 2 corners in this way.

**30** Thus, there were 8 frames and 16 silver bases, 2 bases under each frame.

**31** He made bars of acacia wood. He made 5 bars for the frames on 1 side of the tabernacle.

**32** He made 5 bars for the frames on the other side. He made 5 bars for the frames on the west side, at the back.

**33** He made the middle bar go through the center of the frames from 1 end to the other end.

**34** He put a layer of gold on the frames. He made gold rings to hold the bars. He put a layer of gold on the bars.

**35** He made a curtain of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen. He put designs of cherubim in the curtain.

**36** He made 4 posts of acacia wood for the curtain and put a layer of gold on them. He made gold hooks for the posts. He made 4 silver bases for the posts from melted metal.

**37** He made a curtain for the entrance of the tent. He made it from blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen, with sewn designs.

**38** He made 5 posts with hooks for the curtain. He put a layer of gold on the tops of the posts and on their bands. But he made their 5 bases of bronze.

## Chapter 37

**1** Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. The ark was 2.5 cubits long, 1.5 cubits wide, and 1.5 cubits high.

**2** He put a layer of pure gold on the inside and the outside. He made a gold edge around the top.

**3** He made 4 gold rings from melted metal for the ark. He put them on the 4 feet of the ark, 2 rings on 1 side and 2 rings on the other side.

**4** He made poles of acacia wood and put a layer of gold on them.

**5** He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry the ark.

**6** He made the mercy seat (cover) of pure gold. The mercy seat was 2.5 cubits long and 1.5 cubits wide.

**7** He made 2 cherubim of hammered gold. He put them on the 2 ends of the mercy seat.

**8** He put 1 cherub on 1 end and the other cherub on the other end. He made the cherubim and the mercy seat as 1 piece.

**9** The cherubim spread their wings upward. Their wings covered the mercy seat. The cherubim faced each other, and they looked down at the mercy seat.

**10** He made the table of acacia wood. The table was 2 cubits long, 1 cubit wide, and 1.5 cubits high.

**11** He put a layer of pure gold on the table. He made a gold edge around the top.

**12** He made a frame around the table, as wide as the width of a hand. He made a gold edge around the frame.

**13** He made 4 gold rings from melted metal for the table. He put the rings on the 4 corners, at the 4 legs.

**14** The rings were near the frame. The rings held the poles to carry the table.

**15** He made the poles of acacia wood. He put a layer of gold on them to carry the table.

**16** He made the equipment for the table from pure gold. He made the plates, the dishes, the bowls, and the jars for the drink offerings.

**17** He made the lampstand of pure gold. He made it of hammered gold. Its base, its center stem, its cups, its buds, and its flowers were 1 piece.

**18** 6 branches came out from the sides of the lampstand. 3 branches came out from 1 side, and 3 branches came out from the other side.

**19** Each branch had 3 cups with the shape of almond flowers, each with a bud and a flower. All 6 branches of the lampstand were the same.

**20** On the center stem of the lampstand, there were 4 cups with the shape of almond flowers, with their buds and flowers.

**21** There was 1 bud under each pair of branches. There were 3 buds for the 6 branches that came out of the lampstand.

**22** The buds and the branches were 1 piece with the lampstand. He made all of it from 1 piece of hammered pure gold.

**23** He made its 7 lamps, its wick cutters, and its trays of pure gold.

**24** He used 1 talent of pure gold to make the lampstand and all its equipment.

**25** He made the incense altar of acacia wood. It was square, 1 cubit long and 1 cubit wide. It was 2 cubits high. Its horns were 1 piece with it.

**26** He put a layer of pure gold on its top, its sides, and its horns. He made a gold edge around it.

**27** He made 2 gold rings under the edge, on the 2 opposite sides. The rings held the poles to carry the altar.

**28** He made the poles of acacia wood and put a layer of gold on them.

**29** He made the holy oil to anoint and the pure, sweet incense. He made them as a skilled perfume maker does.

## Chapter 38

**1** He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood. It was square, 5 cubits long and 5 cubits wide. It was 3 cubits high.

**2** He made horns on its 4 corners. The horns were 1 piece with the altar. He put a layer of bronze on the altar.

**3** He made all the equipment for the altar from bronze. He made the pots, the shovels, the bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans.

**4** He made a bronze grate for the altar. He put it under the edge of the altar, halfway up the altar.

**5** He made 4 rings from melted metal for the 4 corners of the bronze grate. The rings held the poles.

**6** He made the poles of acacia wood and put a layer of bronze on them.

**7** He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar to carry it. He made the altar hollow, with sides of boards.

**8** He made the bronze basin and its bronze base. He used the bronze mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**9** Then he made the courtyard. On the south side, the curtains of the courtyard were of fine linen. They were 100 cubits long.

**10** There were 20 posts and 20 bronze bases. The hooks and the bands of the posts were silver.

**11** On the north side, the curtains were 100 cubits long. There were 20 posts and 20 bronze bases. The hooks and the bands of the posts were silver.

**12** On the west side, the curtains were 50 cubits long. There were 10 posts and 10 bases. The hooks and the bands of the posts were silver.

**13** The east side was 50 cubits wide.

**14** The curtains on 1 side of the gate were 15 cubits long. There were 3 posts and 3 bases.

**15** The curtains on the other side of the gate were 15 cubits long. There were 3 posts and 3 bases.

**16** All the curtains around the courtyard were of fine linen.

**17** The bases for the posts were bronze. The hooks and the bands of the posts were silver. The tops of the posts had a layer of silver. All the posts of the courtyard had silver bands.

**18** The curtain for the gate of the courtyard had sewn designs. He made it of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen. It was 20 cubits long and 5 cubits high, the same as the curtains of the courtyard.

**19** There were 4 posts and 4 bronze bases. Their hooks were silver. The tops of the posts and their bands had a layer of silver.

**20** All the tent pegs of the tabernacle and of the courtyard were bronze.

**21** This is the list of the materials for the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony. The Levites counted the materials as Moses commanded. Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest, controlled the work.

**22** Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all the things that the LORD commanded Moses.

**23** Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, helped him. Oholiab engraved, made designs, and sewed with blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen.

**24** The people gave gold as an offering for all the work on the holy place. The total weight was 29 talents and 730 shekels, by the shekel of the holy place.

**25** The men that Moses counted in the community gave silver. The total weight was 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, by the shekel of the holy place.

**26** Each man gave 1 beka, that is, half a shekel, by the shekel of the holy place. Each man 20 years old or older gave this. There were 603,550 men.

**27** He used the 100 talents of silver to make the bases of the holy place and the bases of the curtain. He made 100 bases from the 100 talents, 1 talent for each base.

**28** He used the 1,775 shekels of silver to make hooks for the posts. He also put a layer of silver on the tops of the posts and made bands for them.

**29** The people gave 70 talents and 2,400 shekels of bronze as an offering.

**30** He used the bronze to make the bases for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. He made the bronze altar, its bronze grate, and all the equipment of the altar.

**31** He also made the bases around the courtyard and the bases for the gate of the courtyard. He made all the tent pegs of the tabernacle and all the tent pegs around the courtyard.

## Chapter 39

**1** With the blue, purple, and red yarn, they made woven clothes for the work in the holy place. They made the holy clothes for Aaron, as the LORD commanded Moses.

**2** Bezalel made the ephod (a holy vest) of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen.

**3** They hammered the gold into thin sheets. They cut the sheets into threads. They wove the gold threads into the blue, purple, and red yarn and the fine linen. They made skilled designs.

**4** They made shoulder pieces for the ephod. They joined the shoulder pieces to the 2 top corners of the ephod.

**5** The belt of the ephod was 1 piece with the ephod. They made the belt in the same way, of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen. They did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**6** They put onyx stones in gold settings. They engraved the names of the sons of Israel on the stones, as a person engraves a seal.

**7** He put the stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod. The stones helped the LORD to remember the people of Israel. They did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**8** He made the breastplate with skilled designs, the same as the ephod. He made it of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen.

**9** The breastplate was square. They folded it to make it double. It was 1 span long and 1 span wide when they folded it.

**10** They put 4 rows of stones on it. The first row was a ruby, a topaz, and a beryl.

**11** The second row was a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald.

**12** The third row was a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.

**13** The fourth row was a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. They put the stones in gold settings.

**14** There were 12 stones, 1 for each name of the sons of Israel. They engraved each stone as a seal with 1 name. The 12 stones were for the 12 tribes.

**15** They made chains of pure gold for the breastplate. The chains had the shape of ropes.

**16** They made 2 gold settings and 2 gold rings. They put the 2 rings on the 2 top corners of the breastplate.

**17** They put the 2 gold chains through the 2 rings on the corners of the breastplate.

**18** They tied the other 2 ends of the chains to the 2 settings. They put the settings on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the front.

**19** They made 2 gold rings and put them on the 2 bottom corners of the breastplate. They put them on the inside edge, near the ephod.

**20** They made 2 more gold rings. They put them on the bottom of the 2 shoulder pieces, on the front of the ephod. They put the rings near the seam, above the belt of the ephod.

**21** They tied the rings of the breastplate to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord. Thus, the breastplate stayed above the belt and did not move from the ephod. They did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**22** He made the robe of the ephod. He wove the robe with only blue cloth.

**23** There was a hole for the head in the center of the robe. The hole had a woven edge, the same as a collar of armor. Thus, the hole did not tear.

**24** On the bottom edge of the robe, they made pomegranates (fruits) of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen.

**25** They made bells of pure gold. They put the bells between the pomegranates around the bottom edge of the robe.

**26** There was a bell and a pomegranate, then a bell and a pomegranate, around the bottom edge of the robe. Aaron wore the robe when he did his work. They did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**27** They wove coats of fine linen for Aaron and his sons.

**28** They made the turban of fine linen and the decorated caps of fine linen. They made the underwear of fine linen.

**29** They made the sash of fine linen and blue, purple, and red yarn, with sewn designs. They did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**30** They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold. They engraved words on the plate, as a person engraves a seal: "HOLY TO THE LORD."

**31** They tied a blue cord to the plate to attach it to the front of the turban. They did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**32** Thus, the people of Israel completed all the work on the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting. The people of Israel did all the things that the LORD commanded Moses.

**33** They brought the tabernacle to Moses. They brought the tent and all its equipment, its hooks, its frames, its bars, its posts, and its bases.

**34** They brought the cover of red ram skins, the cover of fine leather, and the curtain that hangs in front of the ark.

**35** They brought the ark of the testimony, its poles, and the mercy seat.

**36** They brought the table, all its equipment, and the holy bread.

**37** They brought the pure gold lampstand, its lamps in their positions, all its equipment, and the oil for the light.

**38** They brought the gold altar, the holy oil to anoint, the sweet incense, and the curtain for the entrance of the tent.

**39** They brought the bronze altar, its bronze grate, its poles, and all its equipment. They brought the basin and its base.

**40** They brought the curtains of the courtyard, its posts, and its bases. They brought the curtain for the gate of the courtyard, its ropes, and its tent pegs. They brought all the equipment for the work of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.

**41** They brought the woven clothes for the work in the holy place. They brought the holy clothes for Aaron the priest and the clothes for his sons. His sons wore these clothes when they did the work of priests.

**42** The people of Israel did all the work as the LORD commanded Moses.

**43** Moses examined all the work. The people did the work as the LORD commanded. Then Moses blessed them.

## Chapter 40

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "On the first day of the first month, set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.

**3** Put the ark of the testimony in the tabernacle. Hang the curtain in front of the ark.

**4** Bring in the table and put its items on it. Bring in the lampstand and light its lamps.

**5** Put the gold altar for incense in front of the ark of the testimony. Hang the curtain at the entrance of the tabernacle.

**6** Put the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.

**7** Put the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar. Put water in the basin.

**8** Set up the courtyard around the tabernacle. Hang the curtain at the gate of the courtyard.

**9** Take the holy oil to anoint. Pour it on the tabernacle and on all the things in it. Make the tabernacle and all its equipment holy. Then it will be holy.

**10** Pour the holy oil to anoint on the altar of burnt offering and on all its equipment. Make the altar holy. Then the altar will be most holy.

**11** Pour the holy oil to anoint on the basin and its base. Make them holy.

**12** Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Wash them with water.

**13** Put the holy clothes on Aaron. Pour the holy oil to anoint on him and make him holy. Then he will serve me as priest.

**14** Bring his sons and put coats on them.

**15** Pour the holy oil to anoint on them, as you did on their father. Then they will serve me as priests. Because of this oil, they and their descendants will be priests for all time."

**16** Moses did all the things that the LORD commanded him.

**17** On the first day of the first month of the second year, Moses set up the tabernacle.

**18** Moses set up the tabernacle. He put its bases in position and set up its frames. He put in its bars and set up its posts.

**19** He spread the tent over the tabernacle. He put the cover on top of the tent, as the LORD commanded Moses.

**20** He took the testimony (the stone tablets) and put it into the ark. He put the poles on the ark. He put the mercy seat on top of the ark.

**21** He brought the ark into the tabernacle. He hung the curtain to cover the ark of the testimony, as the LORD commanded Moses.

**22** He put the table in the Tent of Meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the curtain.

**23** He put the bread on the table in front of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.

**24** He put the lampstand in the Tent of Meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.

**25** He lit the lamps in front of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.

**26** He put the gold altar in the Tent of Meeting, in front of the curtain.

**27** He burned sweet incense on the gold altar, as the LORD commanded Moses.

**28** He hung the curtain at the entrance of the tabernacle.

**29** He put the altar of burnt offering near the entrance of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting. He offered the burnt offering and the grain offering on it, as the LORD commanded Moses.

**30** He put the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar. He put water in the basin to wash.

**31** Moses, Aaron, and the sons of Aaron washed their hands and their feet with the water.

**32** They washed when they went into the Tent of Meeting and when they went near the altar. They did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**33** Moses set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar. He hung the curtain at the gate of the courtyard. Thus, Moses completed the work.

**34** Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting. The glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

**35** Moses could not go into the Tent of Meeting. The cloud stayed on the tent, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

**36** When the cloud went up from the tabernacle, the people of Israel started to travel. They did this on all their journeys.

**37** But if the cloud did not go up, they did not travel. They waited until the day that the cloud went up.

**38** The cloud of the LORD was on the tabernacle during the day. Fire was in the cloud during the night. All the people of Israel saw it during all their journeys.

# Leviticus

## Chapter 1

**1** The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'When a person among you brings an offering to the LORD, bring an animal from the cattle or from the sheep and goats.

**3** If the offering is a burnt offering from the cattle, the person must offer a male with no defects. He must offer it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Then the LORD will accept him.

**4** He must put his hand on the head of the burnt offering. Then the LORD will accept the offering for him, to remove his sin (make atonement).

**5** He must kill the young bull in front of the LORD. The priests, the sons of Aaron, must bring the blood. They must sprinkle the blood on all sides of the altar at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**6** He must remove the skin from the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.

**7** The sons of Aaron the priest must put fire on the altar. They must put wood on the fire.

**8** The priests, the sons of Aaron, must put the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood. This wood is on the fire on the altar.

**9** The person must wash the inner organs and the legs with water. The priest must burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire. Its smell pleases the LORD.

**10** If the burnt offering is from the flock, from the sheep or the goats, the person must bring a male with no defects.

**11** He must kill it on the north side of the altar in front of the LORD. The priests, the sons of Aaron, must sprinkle its blood on all sides of the altar.

**12** He must cut it into pieces. The priest must put the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood. This wood is on the fire on the altar.

**13** The person must wash the inner organs and the legs with water. The priest must bring all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire. Its smell pleases the LORD.

**14** If the burnt offering to the LORD is a bird, the person must bring a dove or a young pigeon.

**15** The priest must bring the bird to the altar. He must twist off its head and burn the head on the altar. He must drain its blood on the side of the altar.

**16** He must remove the crop and its contents. He must throw them on the east side of the altar, at the place for the ashes.

**17** He must tear the bird open by its wings, but he must not divide it into 2 parts. The priest must burn it on the altar, on the wood on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire. Its smell pleases the LORD.'"

## Chapter 2

**1** "'When a person brings a grain offering to the LORD, the offering must be fine flour. He must pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.

**2** He must bring it to the priests, the sons of Aaron. The priest must take a handful of the flour and oil, with all the frankincense. The priest must burn this part on the altar as a memorial portion. It is an offering by fire, and its smell pleases the LORD.

**3** The rest of the grain offering is for Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy part of the offerings by fire to the LORD.

**4** If you bring a grain offering that you bake in an oven, it must be fine flour without yeast. Bring thick loaves mixed with oil, or thin wafers with oil on them.

**5** If your grain offering comes from a flat pan, it must be fine flour without yeast, mixed with oil.

**6** Break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.

**7** If you cook your grain offering in a pot, make it from fine flour and oil.

**8** Bring the grain offering that you make from these things to the LORD. Give it to the priest, and he must bring it to the altar.

**9** The priest must take the memorial portion from the grain offering. He must burn it on the altar. It is an offering by fire, and its smell pleases the LORD.

**10** The rest of the grain offering is for Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy part of the offerings by fire to the LORD.

**11** Do not make with yeast any grain offering that you bring to the LORD. Do not burn yeast or honey in any offering by fire to the LORD.

**12** You can offer yeast and honey to the LORD as an offering of the first crops. But do not burn them on the altar as an offering with a sweet smell.

**13** Put salt on each grain offering. Salt is a sign of the covenant with your God. Always put salt in your grain offerings. Offer salt with all your offerings.

**14** If you offer a grain offering of your first crops to the LORD, offer new grain. Roast the heads of grain in the fire and crush them.

**15** Put oil and frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.

**16** The priest must burn the memorial portion. He must burn some of the crushed grain and some of the oil, with all the frankincense. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.'"

## Chapter 3

**1** "'A person can offer a peace offering. If he offers an animal from the cattle, it can be a male or a female. He must offer an animal with no defects in front of the LORD.

**2** He must put his hand on the head of the animal. He must kill it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The priests, the sons of Aaron, must sprinkle the blood on all sides of the altar.

**3** From the peace offering, he must offer an offering by fire to the LORD. He must offer the fat that covers the inner organs and all the fat on them.

**4** He must also remove the 2 kidneys with their fat, near the lower back. He must remove the best part of the liver with the kidneys.

**5** The sons of Aaron must burn these parts on the altar, on top of the burnt offering. The burnt offering is on the wood on the fire. It is an offering by fire, and its smell pleases the LORD.

**6** If the peace offering to the LORD is from the flock, it can be a male or a female. He must offer an animal with no defects.

**7** If he offers a lamb, he must offer it in front of the LORD.

**8** He must put his hand on the head of the animal. He must kill it in front of the Tent of Meeting. The sons of Aaron must sprinkle its blood on all sides of the altar.

**9** From the peace offering, he must offer an offering by fire to the LORD. He must offer the fat and all of the fat tail. He must cut the tail off near the backbone. He must offer the fat that covers the inner organs and all the fat on them.

**10** He must also remove the 2 kidneys with their fat, near the lower back. He must remove the best part of the liver with the kidneys.

**11** The priest must burn these parts on the altar. It is food, an offering by fire to the LORD.

**12** If his offering is a goat, he must offer it in front of the LORD.

**13** He must put his hand on the head of the goat. He must kill it in front of the Tent of Meeting. The sons of Aaron must sprinkle its blood on all sides of the altar.

**14** From the goat, he must offer an offering by fire to the LORD. He must offer the fat that covers the inner organs and all the fat on them.

**15** He must also remove the 2 kidneys with their fat, near the lower back. He must remove the best part of the liver with the kidneys.

**16** The priest must burn these parts on the altar. It is food, an offering by fire, and its smell pleases the LORD. All the fat is for the LORD.

**17** This is a permanent law for all your descendants, in all the places where you live. Do not eat any fat or any blood.'"

## Chapter 4

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'A person can sin by accident. He can do a thing that one of the commands of the LORD does not permit.

**3** If the anointed priest sins, he causes guilt on the people. Then he must bring a young bull with no defects to the LORD. It is a sin offering for the sin that he did.

**4** He must bring the bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting in front of the LORD. He must put his hand on the head of the bull and kill the bull in front of the LORD.

**5** The anointed priest must take some of the blood of the bull. He must bring the blood into the Tent of Meeting.

**6** The priest must put his finger in the blood. He must sprinkle some of the blood 7 times in front of the LORD, in front of the curtain of the holy place.

**7** The priest must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of sweet incense in front of the LORD. This altar is in the Tent of Meeting. He must pour out all the rest of the blood of the bull at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering. This altar is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**8** He must remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering. He must remove the fat that covers the inner organs and all the fat on them.

**9** He must also remove the 2 kidneys with their fat, near the lower back. He must remove the best part of the liver with the kidneys.

**10** He must remove these parts in the same way as from the bull of the peace offering. The priest must burn them on the altar of burnt offering.

**11** But he must take the skin of the bull, all its meat, its head, its legs, its inner organs, and its dung.

**12** He must carry all of the bull outside the camp to a clean place. This is the place where the priests pour the ashes. He must burn the bull on a wood fire there.

**13** All the community of Israel can sin by accident. They can do a thing that one of the commands of the LORD does not permit. They are guilty, but the community does not know about the sin.

**14** When they learn about the sin, the community must offer a young bull as a sin offering. They must bring it in front of the Tent of Meeting.

**15** The elders of the community must put their hands on the head of the bull in front of the LORD. Then a person must kill the bull in front of the LORD.

**16** The anointed priest must bring some of the blood of the bull into the Tent of Meeting.

**17** The priest must put his finger in the blood. He must sprinkle the blood 7 times in front of the LORD, in front of the curtain.

**18** He must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar in front of the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. He must pour out all the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering. This altar is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**19** He must remove all the fat from the bull and burn it on the altar.

**20** He must do the same things with this bull as with the bull for the sin offering of the priest. The priest must make atonement for the people, and God will forgive them.

**21** He must carry the bull outside the camp. He must burn it in the same way as the first bull. It is the sin offering for the community.

**22** A leader can sin by accident. He can do a thing that one of the commands of the LORD his God does not permit. Then he is guilty.

**23** When a person tells him about his sin, he must bring a male goat with no defects as his offering.

**24** He must put his hand on the head of the goat. He must kill it in front of the LORD, in the place where they kill the burnt offering. It is a sin offering.

**25** The priest must put his finger in the blood of the sin offering. He must put some blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering.

**26** He must burn all the fat on the altar, the same as the fat of the peace offering. The priest must make atonement for the sin of the leader, and God will forgive him.

**27** A usual person of the community can sin by accident. He can do a thing that one of the commands of the LORD does not permit. Then he is guilty.

**28** When a person tells him about his sin, he must bring a female goat with no defects. It is his offering for the sin that he did.

**29** He must put his hand on the head of the sin offering. He must kill it in the place of the burnt offering.

**30** The priest must put his finger in some of the blood. He must put the blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out all the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.

**31** He must remove all the fat, as the priests remove the fat from the peace offering. The priest must burn it on the altar, and its smell will please the LORD. The priest must make atonement for him, and God will forgive him.

**32** If he brings a lamb as his sin offering, he must bring a female with no defects.

**33** He must put his hand on the head of the sin offering. He must kill it as a sin offering in the place where they kill the burnt offering.

**34** The priest must put his finger in some of the blood of the sin offering. He must put the blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out all the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.

**35** He must remove all the fat, as the priests remove the fat of the lamb from the peace offering. The priest must burn it on the altar with the offerings by fire to the LORD. The priest must make atonement for the sin of the person, and God will forgive him.'"

## Chapter 5

**1** "'A person can hear a public call to give evidence about a thing that he saw or knows. If he does not speak, he sins and he is responsible for his guilt.

**2** A person can touch an unclean thing without knowledge. It can be the dead body of an unclean wild animal, an unclean farm animal, or an unclean small animal. Then that person is unclean and guilty.

**3** A person can touch an unclean thing from a human without knowledge. It can be any type of uncleanness. When he knows about it, he is guilty.

**4** A person can make a careless promise to do bad or good. People can make many types of careless promises. When he knows about his promise, he is guilty.

**5** When a person is guilty of 1 of these things, he must say that he did the sin.

**6** He must bring a guilt offering to the LORD for his sin. He must bring a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering. The priest must make atonement for his sin.

**7** If he does not have sufficient money for a lamb, he must bring 2 doves or 2 young pigeons to the LORD for his sin. He must bring 1 bird for a sin offering and 1 bird for a burnt offering.

**8** He must bring them to the priest. The priest must offer the bird for the sin offering first. He must twist its head from its neck, but he must not remove the head.

**9** He must sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar. He must drain the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar. It is a sin offering.

**10** He must offer the second bird as a burnt offering, as the rules tell. The priest must make atonement for the sin of the person, and God will forgive him.

**11** If he does not have sufficient money for 2 doves or 2 young pigeons, he must bring fine flour as his sin offering. He must bring 1/10 of an ephah. He must not put oil or frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.

**12** He must bring it to the priest. The priest must take a handful of it as a memorial portion. He must burn it on the altar with the offerings by fire to the LORD. It is a sin offering.

**13** The priest must make atonement for the person for his sin, and God will forgive him. The rest of the flour is for the priest, the same as a grain offering.'"

**14** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**15** "A person can be unfaithful and sin by accident about the holy things of the LORD. Then he must bring a ram with no defects from the flock to the LORD. You must calculate its value in silver shekels, by the shekel of the holy place. It is a guilt offering.

**16** He must pay for the damage that he caused to the holy thing. He must add 1/5 of its value and give it to the priest. The priest must make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and God will forgive him.

**17** A person can sin and do a thing that the commands of the LORD do not permit. If he does not know about it, he is still guilty. He is responsible for his guilt.

**18** He must bring to the priest a ram with no defects from the flock, at your calculated value. It is a guilt offering. The priest must make atonement for the mistake that the person did without knowledge. Then God will forgive him.

**19** It is a guilt offering. He is guilty in front of the LORD."

## Chapter 6

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "A person can sin and be unfaithful to the LORD. He can lie to his neighbor about a thing that the neighbor gave him to keep. He can lie about a thing that the neighbor left with him. He can steal from his neighbor or cheat him.

**3** He can find a lost thing and lie about it. He can make a false promise. A person can sin in any of these ways.

**4** If he sins in this way and is guilty, he must give back the thing that he stole. He must give back the thing that he got by a trick. He must give back the thing that the neighbor gave him to keep, or the lost thing that he found.

**5** He must give back anything about which he made a false promise. He must pay the full value and add 1/5 to it. He must give it to the owner on the day that he brings his guilt offering.

**6** He must bring his guilt offering to the priest for the LORD. It must be a ram with no defects from the flock, at your calculated value.

**7** The priest must make atonement for him in front of the LORD. Then God will forgive him for any of the things that he did wrong."

**8** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**9** "Command Aaron and his sons. Tell them, 'This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering must stay on the altar all night until the morning. The fire on the altar must continue to burn.

**10** The priest must put on his linen clothes and his linen underwear. He must remove the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire burned on the altar. He must put the ashes next to the altar.

**11** Then he must remove his clothes and put on other clothes. He must carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

**12** The fire on the altar must continue to burn. Do not let it stop. Each morning the priest must put wood on the fire. He must put the burnt offering on the wood. He must burn the fat of the peace offerings on it.

**13** The fire must always burn on the altar. It must never stop.

**14** This is the law of the grain offering. The sons of Aaron must offer it in front of the LORD, in front of the altar.

**15** The priest must take a handful of the flour and oil of the grain offering, with all the frankincense on it. He must burn it on the altar as the memorial portion. Its smell pleases the LORD.

**16** Aaron and his sons must eat the rest of it. They must eat it without yeast in a holy place. They must eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

**17** Do not bake it with yeast. I give it to the priests as their part of my offerings by fire. It is most holy, the same as the sin offering and the guilt offering.

**18** All the males among the descendants of Aaron can eat it. This is a permanent law for all your descendants about the offerings by fire to the LORD. Each thing that touches these offerings will become holy.'"

**19** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**20** "This is the offering that Aaron and his sons must offer to the LORD on the day when Moses anoints a priest. They must offer 1/10 of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering. They must offer half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.

**21** Make it with oil on a flat pan. Mix it well and bring it in. Offer the grain offering in baked pieces. Its smell pleases the LORD.

**22** The son of Aaron who becomes the anointed priest after him must offer it. This is a permanent law. The priest must burn all of it for the LORD.

**23** The priest must burn all of each grain offering for a priest. No person must eat it."

**24** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**25** "Speak to Aaron and his sons. Tell them, 'This is the law of the sin offering. Kill the sin offering in front of the LORD, in the place where you kill the burnt offering. It is most holy.

**26** The priest who offers it for sin must eat it. He must eat it in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

**27** Each thing that touches its meat will become holy. If some of its blood falls on clothing, wash the clothing in a holy place.

**28** If you cook the meat in a clay pot, break the pot. If you cook the meat in a bronze pot, clean the pot fully and wash it with water.

**29** All the males among the priests can eat it. It is most holy.

**30** But a priest can bring some of the blood of a sin offering into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the holy place. Then no person must eat that offering. Burn it in the fire.'"

## Chapter 7

**1** "'This is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.

**2** Kill the guilt offering in the place where you kill the burnt offering. The priest must sprinkle its blood on all sides of the altar.

**3** He must offer all its fat. He must offer the fat tail and the fat that covers the inner organs.

**4** He must also remove the 2 kidneys with their fat, near the lower back. He must remove the best part of the liver with the kidneys.

**5** The priest must burn these parts on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.

**6** All the males among the priests can eat it. They must eat it in a holy place. It is most holy.

**7** The same law is for the sin offering and the guilt offering. The offering is for the priest who makes atonement with it.

**8** When a priest offers a burnt offering for a person, the skin of that animal is for the priest.

**9** Each grain offering that a person bakes in an oven is for the priest who offers it. Each grain offering that a person cooks in a pot or on a flat pan is also for that priest.

**10** Each grain offering, mixed with oil or dry, is for all the sons of Aaron. Each son must get an equal part.

**11** This is the law of the peace offering that a person offers to the LORD.

**12** If he offers it to say thanks, he must offer bread with the sacrifice. He must offer thick loaves without yeast, mixed with oil. He must offer thin wafers without yeast, with oil on them. He must offer loaves of fine flour, mixed well with oil.

**13** With his peace offering of thanks, he must also offer loaves of bread made with yeast.

**14** He must offer 1 loaf of each type as a gift to the LORD. This bread is for the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.

**15** The person must eat the meat of his peace offering of thanks on the day that he offers it. He must not keep any of it until the morning.

**16** But his sacrifice can be for a promise (vow), or it can be a free offering. Then he must eat it on the day that he offers it. He can eat the rest of it on the next day.

**17** But on the third day, he must burn the rest of the meat of the sacrifice.

**18** If a person eats any of the meat of his peace offering on the third day, the LORD will not accept the offering. The offering will not help the person who offered it. The meat will be detestable. The person who eats it will be responsible for his guilt.

**19** Do not eat meat that touches any unclean thing. Burn it. Any person who is clean can eat the other meat.

**20** If a person is unclean and eats the meat of a peace offering for the LORD, remove that person from his people.

**21** A person can touch an unclean thing. It can be an unclean thing from a human, an unclean animal, or any detestable unclean thing. If that person eats the meat of a peace offering for the LORD, remove that person from his people.'"

**22** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**23** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'Do not eat any fat from cattle, sheep, or goats.

**24** You can use the fat of an animal that dies naturally or that wild animals kill. You can use it for other work. But you must not eat it.

**25** People offer some animals as an offering by fire to the LORD. If a person eats the fat of such an animal, remove that person from his people.

**26** In all the places where you live, do not eat any blood. Do not eat the blood of birds or of animals.

**27** If a person eats any blood, remove that person from his people.'"

**28** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**29** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'A person who offers a peace offering to the LORD must bring a part of it as a gift to the LORD.

**30** He must bring the offering by fire to the LORD with his own hands. He must bring the fat with the breast. The priest must wave the breast in front of the LORD as a wave offering.

**31** The priest must burn the fat on the altar. But the breast is for Aaron and his sons.

**32** Give the right thigh from your peace offerings to the priest as a gift.

**33** The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the peace offering must get the right thigh as his part.

**34** I take the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the gift from the people of Israel. I take these parts from their peace offerings. I give them to Aaron the priest and to his sons. This is a permanent law for the people of Israel.'"

**35** This is the part of the offerings by fire to the LORD for Aaron and his sons. They got this part on the day when Moses brought them to serve the LORD as priests.

**36** On the day that the LORD anointed them, he commanded the people of Israel to give them this part. It is a permanent law for all their descendants.

**37** This is the law for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering. It is the law for the ordination offering and the peace offering.

**38** The LORD gave this law to Moses on Mount Sinai. He gave it on the day that he commanded the people of Israel to bring their offerings to the LORD in the desert of Sinai.

## Chapter 8

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Bring Aaron and his sons. Bring the clothes, the holy oil, the bull for the sin offering, the 2 rams, and the basket of bread without yeast.

**3** Gather all the community at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting."

**4** Moses did as the LORD commanded him. The community gathered at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**5** Moses said to the community, "This is what the LORD commands us to do."

**6** Moses brought Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.

**7** He put the coat on Aaron and tied the sash around him. He put the robe on him and put the ephod on him. He tied the woven belt of the ephod around him to attach the ephod.

**8** He put the breastplate on Aaron. He put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastplate.

**9** He put the turban on the head of Aaron. On the front of the turban, he put the gold plate, the holy crown. Moses did as the LORD commanded him.

**10** Moses took the holy oil. He poured it on the tabernacle and on all the things in it, and he made them holy.

**11** He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar 7 times. He poured oil on the altar and all its equipment, and on the basin and its base, to make them holy.

**12** He poured some of the holy oil on the head of Aaron. He anointed Aaron to make him holy.

**13** Moses brought the sons of Aaron. He put coats on them and tied sashes around them. He put caps on their heads. Moses did as the LORD commanded him.

**14** Moses brought the bull for the sin offering. Aaron and his sons put their hands on the head of the bull.

**15** Moses killed the bull. He took the blood and put it on all the horns of the altar with his finger. Thus, he made the altar pure. He poured out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar. He made the altar holy, to make atonement for it.

**16** Moses took all the fat on the inner organs, the best part of the liver, and the 2 kidneys with their fat. He burned them on the altar.

**17** But he burned the bull, its skin, its meat, and its dung outside the camp. Moses did as the LORD commanded him.

**18** Then Moses brought the ram for the burnt offering. Aaron and his sons put their hands on the head of the ram.

**19** Moses killed the ram. He sprinkled the blood on all sides of the altar.

**20** He cut the ram into pieces. Moses burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.

**21** He washed the inner organs and the legs with water. Moses burned all of the ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, an offering by fire to the LORD, and its smell pleased the LORD. Moses did as the LORD commanded him.

**22** Then Moses brought the other ram, the ram for the ordination. Aaron and his sons put their hands on the head of the ram.

**23** Moses killed the ram. He took some of its blood and put it on the bottom of the right ear of Aaron. He put blood on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.

**24** Moses brought the sons of Aaron. He put some of the blood on the bottom of their right ears. He put blood on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet. Moses sprinkled the rest of the blood on all sides of the altar.

**25** He took the fat, the fat tail, and all the fat on the inner organs. He took the best part of the liver, the 2 kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.

**26** From the basket of bread without yeast in front of the LORD, he took 1 thick loaf, 1 loaf with oil, and 1 thin wafer. He put them on the fat and on the right thigh.

**27** He put all these things in the hands of Aaron and his sons. They waved them in front of the LORD as a wave offering.

**28** Then Moses took these things from their hands. He burned them on the altar on top of the burnt offering. It was an ordination offering, and its smell pleased the LORD. It was an offering by fire to the LORD.

**29** Moses took the breast and waved it in front of the LORD as a wave offering. It was the part of the ram of ordination for Moses, as the LORD commanded him.

**30** Moses took some of the holy oil and some of the blood on the altar. He sprinkled it on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. Thus, he made Aaron, his sons, and their clothes holy.

**31** Moses said to Aaron and his sons, "Boil the meat at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Eat it there with the bread in the basket of the ordination offerings. I commanded, 'Aaron and his sons must eat it.'

**32** Burn the rest of the meat and bread.

**33** Do not go out of the entrance of the Tent of Meeting for 7 days, until the days of your ordination are complete. Your ordination will continue for 7 days.

**34** The LORD commanded us to do what we did today, to make atonement for you.

**35** Stay at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting day and night for 7 days. Obey the commands of the LORD. If you do not obey, you will die. The LORD commanded me to tell you this."

**36** Aaron and his sons did all the things that the LORD commanded through Moses.

## Chapter 9

**1** On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel.

**2** He said to Aaron, "Take a young calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. Both animals must have no defects. Offer them in front of the LORD.

**3** Then tell the people of Israel, 'Take a male goat for a sin offering. Take a calf and a lamb for a burnt offering. Both animals must be 1 year old with no defects.

**4** Take a bull and a ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice in front of the LORD. Take a grain offering mixed with oil. Today the LORD will appear to you.'"

**5** The people brought the things that Moses commanded to the front of the Tent of Meeting. All the community came near and stood in front of the LORD.

**6** Moses said, "The LORD commands you to do this. Then the glory of the LORD will appear to you."

**7** Moses said to Aaron, "Go to the altar. Offer your sin offering and your burnt offering. Make atonement for yourself and for the people. Offer the offering of the people and make atonement for them, as the LORD commanded."

**8** Thus, Aaron went to the altar. He killed the calf as the sin offering for himself.

**9** The sons of Aaron brought the blood to him. He put his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.

**10** He burned the fat, the kidneys, and the best part of the liver from the sin offering on the altar. He did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**11** He burned the meat and the skin outside the camp.

**12** Then he killed the burnt offering. The sons of Aaron gave him the blood, and he sprinkled it on all sides of the altar.

**13** They gave him the pieces of the burnt offering and the head. He burned them on the altar.

**14** He washed the inner organs and the legs. He burned them on top of the burnt offering on the altar.

**15** Then Aaron brought the offering of the people. He took the goat for the sin offering of the people. He killed it and offered it for sin, the same as the first animal.

**16** He brought the burnt offering and offered it as the rules tell.

**17** He brought the grain offering. He took a handful of it and burned it on the altar. He did this in addition to the burnt offering of the morning.

**18** He killed the bull and the ram as the peace offering for the people. The sons of Aaron gave him the blood, and he sprinkled it on all sides of the altar.

**19** They also gave him the fat of the bull and the ram. They gave him the fat tail, the fat that covers the inner organs, the kidneys, and the best part of the liver.

**20** They put the fat on the breasts. Aaron burned the fat on the altar.

**21** Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh in front of the LORD as a wave offering. He did as Moses commanded.

**22** Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them. Then he came down from the altar. He completed the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.

**23** Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of Meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.

**24** Fire came out from the LORD and burned the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. All the people saw the fire. They shouted and bowed down with their faces to the ground.

## Chapter 10

**1** Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, each took his incense pan. They put fire and incense in the pans. They offered fire in front of the LORD that the LORD did not permit. The LORD did not command them to do this.

**2** Fire came out from the LORD and burned them. They died in front of the LORD.

**3** Then Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD said: 'The people who come near me must respect me as holy. I will show my glory in front of all the people.'" Aaron did not speak.

**4** Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, the uncle of Aaron. He said to them, "Come here. Carry your relatives away from the front of the holy place. Take them outside the camp."

**5** Thus, they came and carried the dead men in their coats outside the camp, as Moses told them.

**6** Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not let your hair hang loose. Do not tear your clothes. If you do these things, you will die, and the LORD will be angry with all the community. But your relatives, all the people of Israel, can cry for the people that the LORD burned.

**7** Do not go out of the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. If you go out, you will die. The holy oil of the LORD is on you." Thus, they did what Moses said.

**8** The LORD spoke to Aaron. He said,
