**9** "You and your sons must not drink wine or other strong drinks when you go into the Tent of Meeting. If you drink, you will die. This is a permanent law for all your descendants.

**10** You must know the difference between holy things and common things. You must know the difference between unclean things and clean things.

**11** You must teach the people of Israel all the laws that the LORD gave them through Moses."

**12** Moses spoke to Aaron and to the 2 sons of Aaron who were still alive, Eleazar and Ithamar. He said, "Take the rest of the grain offering from the offerings by fire to the LORD. Eat it without yeast next to the altar, because it is most holy.

**13** Eat it in a holy place. It is your part and the part of your sons from the offerings by fire to the LORD. The LORD commanded me to tell you this.

**14** You, your sons, and your daughters must eat the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the gift. Eat them in a clean place. The people of Israel give these parts of their peace offerings to you and your sons.

**15** The people must bring the thigh and the breast with the fat for the offerings by fire. The priest must wave them in front of the LORD as a wave offering. These parts are for you and your sons. This is a permanent law, as the LORD commanded."

**16** Moses looked carefully for the goat of the sin offering. He found that the priests burned it. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who were still alive. He said,

**17** "Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy. God gave it to you to remove the guilt of the community. You must make atonement for them in front of the LORD.

**18** Look, you did not bring its blood into the holy place. Thus, you had to eat the meat in the holy place, as I commanded."

**19** Aaron said to Moses, "Today my sons offered their sin offering and their burnt offering in front of the LORD. But these bad things happened to me. If I ate the sin offering today, will the LORD accept it?"

**20** When Moses heard this, he was content.

## Chapter 11

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said to them,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'From all the animals on the land, you can eat these animals.

**3** You can eat each animal that has a split hoof and chews the cud.

**4** But some animals only chew the cud or only have a split hoof. Do not eat these animals. The camel chews the cud but does not have a split hoof. Thus, it is unclean for you.

**5** The rock badger chews the cud but does not have a split hoof. Thus, it is unclean for you.

**6** The rabbit chews the cud but does not have a split hoof. Thus, it is unclean for you.

**7** The pig has a split hoof, but it does not chew the cud. Thus, it is unclean for you.

**8** Do not eat their meat. Do not touch their dead bodies. They are unclean for you.

**9** From all the animals in the water, you can eat these animals. You can eat each animal in the seas and in the rivers that has fins and scales.

**10** But some animals in the seas and rivers do not have fins and scales. These include all the small animals and all the other animals in the water. These animals are detestable to you.

**11** They are detestable to you. Do not eat their meat. Think of their dead bodies as detestable.

**12** Each animal in the water that does not have fins and scales is detestable to you.

**13** These are the birds that you must think of as detestable. Do not eat them, because they are detestable. Do not eat the eagle, the vulture, or the black vulture.

**14** Do not eat the kite or any type of falcon.

**15** Do not eat any type of raven.

**16** Do not eat the ostrich, the night hawk, the seagull, or any type of hawk.

**17** Do not eat the little owl, the cormorant, or the great owl.

**18** Do not eat the white owl, the pelican, or the carrion vulture.

**19** Do not eat the stork, any type of heron, the hoopoe, or the bat.

**20** All insects with wings that walk on 4 legs are detestable to you.

**21** But you can eat some insects with wings that walk on 4 legs. You can eat the insects that have legs with joints to jump on the ground.

**22** You can eat any type of locust, bald locust, cricket, or grasshopper.

**23** But all other insects with wings and 4 legs are detestable to you.

**24** These animals will make you unclean. Each person who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until the evening.

**25** Each person who carries any part of their dead bodies must wash his clothes. He will be unclean until the evening.

**26** Some animals have a hoof that is not fully split, or they do not chew the cud. These animals are unclean for you. Each person who touches them will be unclean.

**27** All the animals that walk on paws on 4 legs are unclean for you. Each person who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until the evening.

**28** Each person who carries their dead bodies must wash his clothes. He will be unclean until the evening. These animals are unclean for you.

**29** These small animals that move on the ground are unclean for you: the weasel, the rat, and any type of large lizard.

**30** The gecko, the monitor lizard, the lizard, the skink, and the chameleon are also unclean.

**31** These small animals are unclean for you. Each person who touches them when they are dead will be unclean until the evening.

**32** One of these dead animals can fall on an item. Then that item will be unclean. The item can be wood, cloth, leather, or a bag. Put any such item that people use into water. It will be unclean until the evening. Then it will be clean.

**33** If one of these dead animals falls into a clay pot, all the things in the pot will be unclean. Break the pot.

**34** If water from that pot touches any food, the food will be unclean. Any drink in that pot will be unclean.

**35** If any part of a dead body of these animals falls on a thing, that thing will be unclean. Break an oven or a pot for food that becomes unclean. These things are unclean, and you must think of them as unclean.

**36** But a spring or a well with water will stay clean. But a person who touches the dead body will be unclean.

**37** If any part of a dead body falls on seeds that a person will plant, the seeds will stay clean.

**38** But if a person puts water on the seeds and a part of a dead body falls on them, they are unclean for you.

**39** An animal that you can eat can die naturally. Each person who touches its dead body will be unclean until the evening.

**40** A person who eats some of the dead body must wash his clothes. He will be unclean until the evening. A person who carries the dead body must wash his clothes. He will be unclean until the evening.

**41** Each small animal that moves on the ground is detestable. Do not eat it.

**42** Do not eat any small animal that moves on the ground. Do not eat an animal that moves on its stomach, on 4 legs, or on many legs. These animals are detestable.

**43** Do not make yourselves detestable with any small animal that moves on the ground. Do not make yourselves unclean with these animals.

**44** I am the LORD your God. Make yourselves holy and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean with any small animal that moves on the ground.

**45** I am the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. Thus, be holy, because I am holy.

**46** This is the law about the animals, the birds, each animal in the water, and each animal that moves on the ground.

**47** With this law, you must know the difference between unclean things and clean things. You must know the difference between the animals that you can eat and the animals that you must not eat.'"

## Chapter 12

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'A woman can become pregnant and give birth to a boy. Then she will be unclean for 7 days. She will be unclean, the same as during her monthly period.

**3** On the eighth day, circumcise the boy.

**4** Then the woman must wait 33 days to become pure from her flow of blood. She must not touch any holy thing. She must not go into the holy place until her time of purification is complete.

**5** If she gives birth to a girl, she will be unclean for 2 weeks, the same as during her monthly period. Then she must wait 66 days to become pure from her flow of blood.

**6** After the birth of a son or a daughter, her time of purification will be complete. Then she must bring a lamb 1 year old for a burnt offering. She must bring a young pigeon or a dove for a sin offering. She must bring them to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**7** The priest must offer them in front of the LORD and make atonement for her. Then she will be clean from her flow of blood. This is the law for a woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.

**8** If she does not have sufficient money for a lamb, she must bring 2 doves or 2 young pigeons. She must bring 1 bird for the burnt offering and 1 bird for a sin offering. The priest must make atonement for her, and she will be clean.'"

## Chapter 13

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**2** "A person can have a lump, a scab, or a bright spot on his skin. It can look like a serious skin disease (leprosy). Then bring the person to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

**3** The priest must examine the sore on the skin. If the hair in the sore is white and the sore goes deeper than the skin, it is leprosy. After the priest examines him, he must say that the person is unclean.

**4** The bright spot on the skin can be white, but not deeper than the skin. The hair in it can stay its usual color. Then the priest must isolate the person for 7 days.

**5** On the seventh day, the priest must examine him again. If the sore does not change and does not spread on the skin, the priest must isolate him for 7 more days.

**6** On the seventh day, the priest must examine him again. If the sore becomes less bright and does not spread, the priest must say that the person is clean. It is only a rash. The person must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.

**7** But after the priest examines him and says that he is clean, the rash can spread on the skin. Then the person must go to the priest again.

**8** The priest must examine him. If the rash spreads on the skin, the priest must say that the person is unclean. It is leprosy.

**9** When a person has leprosy, bring him to the priest.

**10** The priest must examine him. There can be a white lump on the skin that makes the hair white. There can be raw flesh in the lump.

**11** Then it is a chronic leprosy on his skin. The priest must say that the person is unclean. The priest must not isolate him, because he is already unclean.

**12** The leprosy can spread over all the skin of the person. It can cover him from his head to his feet, as far as the priest can see.

**13** Then the priest must examine him. If the leprosy covers all his body, the priest must say that the person is clean. All his skin is white, and he is clean.

**14** But when raw flesh appears on him, he will be unclean.

**15** The priest must examine the raw flesh and say that the person is unclean. The raw flesh is unclean. It is leprosy.

**16** But if the raw flesh changes and becomes white again, the person must go to the priest.

**17** The priest must examine him. If the sore becomes white, the priest must say that the person is clean. He is clean.

**18** A person can have a boil on his skin, and the boil can heal.

**19** In the place of the boil, a white lump or a bright, red-white spot can appear. Then the person must show it to the priest.

**20** The priest must examine it. If it is deeper than the skin and the hair in it is white, the priest must say that the person is unclean. It is leprosy that started in the boil.

**21** But the priest can examine it and see that there are no white hairs in it. It can be not deeper than the skin and less bright. Then the priest must isolate the person for 7 days.

**22** If it spreads on the skin, the priest must say that the person is unclean. It is a disease.

**23** But if the bright spot stays in its place and does not spread, it is only the scar of the boil. The priest must say that the person is clean.

**24** A person can have a burn on his skin. The raw flesh of the burn can become a bright, red-white or white spot.

**25** Then the priest must examine it. If the hair in the bright spot is white and the spot is deeper than the skin, it is leprosy that started in the burn. The priest must say that the person is unclean. It is leprosy.

**26** But the priest can examine it and see that there is no white hair in the bright spot. It can be not deeper than the skin and less bright. Then the priest must isolate the person for 7 days.

**27** On the seventh day, the priest must examine him. If it spreads on the skin, the priest must say that the person is unclean. It is leprosy.

**28** But if the bright spot stays in its place, does not spread, and is less bright, it is a lump from the burn. The priest must say that the person is clean, because it is only the scar of the burn.

**29** A man or a woman can have a sore on the head or on the chin.

**30** Then the priest must examine the sore. If it is deeper than the skin and has thin yellow hair in it, the priest must say that the person is unclean. It is an itch, a leprosy of the head or the chin.

**31** But the priest can examine the itch and see that it is not deeper than the skin. There can be no black hair in it. Then the priest must isolate the person for 7 days.

**32** On the seventh day, the priest must examine the sore. The itch can stay the same and have no yellow hair in it. It can stay not deeper than the skin.

**33** Then the person must shave his hair, but not the hair on the itch. The priest must isolate him for 7 more days.

**34** On the seventh day, the priest must examine the itch. If the itch does not spread on the skin and is not deeper than the skin, the priest must say that the person is clean. The person must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.

**35** But after the priest says that he is clean, the itch can spread on the skin.

**36** Then the priest must examine him. If the itch spreads on the skin, the priest does not need to look for yellow hair. The person is unclean.

**37** But if the itch stays the same and black hair grows in it, the itch is gone. The person is clean, and the priest must say that he is clean.

**38** A man or a woman can have bright spots on the skin, white bright spots.

**39** Then the priest must examine them. If the bright spots on the skin are a dull white, it is only a rash on the skin. The person is clean.

**40** A man can lose the hair on his head. He is bald, but he is clean.

**41** A man can lose the hair on the front of his head. He is bald on his forehead, but he is clean.

**42** But a red-white sore can appear on his bald head or on his bald forehead. Then it is leprosy that started there.

**43** The priest must examine him. The lump of the sore can be red-white on his bald head or forehead. It can look like leprosy on the skin.

**44** Then the man has leprosy, and he is unclean. The priest must say that he is unclean, because of the sore on his head.

**45** The person with leprosy must wear torn clothes and let the hair of his head hang loose. He must cover the lower part of his face. He must shout, 'Unclean! Unclean!'

**46** He will be unclean for all the time that he has the disease. He is unclean. He must live alone, outside the camp.

**47** A garment of wool or linen can have mold (leprosy) in it.

**48** The mold can be in the woven or knitted material of linen or wool. It can be in leather or in any item made of leather.

**49** If the mold in the garment, leather, or material is green or red, it is leprosy. Show it to the priest.

**50** The priest must examine the mold. He must isolate the item for 7 days.

**51** On the seventh day, he must examine the mold. If the mold spreads in the garment, material, or leather, it is a destructive mold. The item is unclean.

**52** He must burn the garment, the material of wool or linen, or the leather item that has the mold. It is a destructive mold. Burn the item in the fire.

**53** But if the priest examines it and the mold does not spread in the garment, material, or leather,

**54** then the priest must command the people to wash the item with the mold. He must isolate it for 7 more days.

**55** After someone washes the item, the priest must examine it. If the mold does not change its color, the item is unclean, even if the mold does not spread. Burn the item in the fire. The mold eats into the item, on the inside or the outside.

**56** But the priest can examine it after someone washes it, and the mold can be less bright. Then he must tear that part out of the garment, leather, or material.

**57** If the mold appears again in the garment, material, or leather, it spreads. Burn the item with the mold.

**58** But you can wash the garment, material, or leather item, and the mold can go away. Then wash it a second time, and it will be clean.

**59** This is the law about mold in a garment of wool or linen, in woven or knitted material, or in any leather item. With this law, the priest can say that an item is clean or unclean."

## Chapter 14

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "This is the law for a person with leprosy on the day that he becomes clean. Bring him to the priest.

**3** The priest must go outside the camp and examine the person. The leprosy of the person can be gone.

**4** Then the priest must command people to bring 2 clean, live birds for the person. They must also bring cedar wood, red yarn, and hyssop.

**5** The priest must command people to kill 1 of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot.

**6** Then he must take the live bird, the cedar wood, the red yarn, and the hyssop. He must put them and the live bird into the blood of the bird that they killed over the fresh water.

**7** He must sprinkle the blood 7 times on the person who becomes clean from the leprosy. Then he must say that the person is clean. He must release the live bird into the open field.

**8** The person who becomes clean must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and wash with water. Then he will be clean. After that, he can come into the camp. But he must stay outside his tent for 7 days.

**9** On the seventh day, he must shave all the hair off his head. He must shave his beard and his eyebrows and all his hair. He must wash his clothes and wash his body with water. Then he will be clean.

**10** On the eighth day, he must take 2 male lambs with no defects and 1 female lamb 1 year old with no defects. He must take 3/10 of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering. He must take 1 log of oil.

**11** The priest who makes him clean must bring the person and these items in front of the LORD. He must do this at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**12** The priest must take 1 male lamb and offer it as a guilt offering with the log of oil. He must wave them in front of the LORD as a wave offering.

**13** He must kill the lamb in the holy place, where they kill the sin offering and the burnt offering. The guilt offering is for the priest, the same as the sin offering. It is most holy.

**14** The priest must take some of the blood of the guilt offering. He must put it on the bottom of the right ear of the person who becomes clean. He must put it on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.

**15** The priest must take some of the log of oil and pour it into his own left hand.

**16** The priest must put his right finger into the oil in his left hand. He must sprinkle some of the oil with his finger 7 times in front of the LORD.

**17** The priest must take some of the rest of the oil in his hand. He must put it on the bottom of the right ear of the person who becomes clean. He must put it on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot. He must put the oil on top of the blood of the guilt offering.

**18** The priest must pour the rest of the oil in his hand on the head of the person who becomes clean. The priest must make atonement for him in front of the LORD.

**19** The priest must offer the sin offering and make atonement for the person who becomes clean from his uncleanness. After that, he must kill the burnt offering.

**20** The priest must offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. The priest must make atonement for him, and he will be clean.

**21** But the person can be poor and not have sufficient money. Then he must take 1 male lamb as a guilt offering to wave, to make atonement for him. He must take 1/10 of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering. He must take 1 log of oil.

**22** He must also take 2 doves or 2 young pigeons, as he can buy. 1 bird is for a sin offering, and 1 bird is for a burnt offering.

**23** On the eighth day, he must bring them to the priest to make himself clean. He must bring them to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, in front of the LORD.

**24** The priest must take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil. The priest must wave them in front of the LORD as a wave offering.

**25** He must kill the lamb of the guilt offering. The priest must take some of the blood of the guilt offering. He must put it on the bottom of the right ear of the person who becomes clean. He must put it on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.

**26** The priest must pour some of the oil into his own left hand.

**27** With his right finger, the priest must sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand 7 times in front of the LORD.

**28** The priest must put some of the oil in his hand on the bottom of the right ear of the person who becomes clean. He must put it on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot. He must put it on the same place as the blood of the guilt offering.

**29** The priest must put the rest of the oil in his hand on the head of the person who becomes clean. This makes atonement for him in front of the LORD.

**30** Then he must offer 1 of the doves or young pigeons, as the person can buy.

**31** He must offer 1 bird as a sin offering and 1 bird as a burnt offering, with the grain offering. The priest must make atonement in front of the LORD for the person who becomes clean.

**32** This is the law for a person who has leprosy and does not have sufficient money for the usual offerings to make himself clean."

**33** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**34** "You will go into the land of Canaan. I give that land to you as your property. I can put mold (leprosy) in a house in that land.

**35** Then the owner of the house must come and tell the priest, 'I think that there is a type of mold in my house.'

**36** Before the priest goes in to examine the mold, he must command people to empty the house. Then the things in the house will not become unclean. After that, the priest must go in to examine the house.

**37** He must examine the mold. The mold on the walls can be green or red, and the spots can go deeper than the surface of the wall.

**38** Then the priest must go out of the house to the door. He must close the house for 7 days.

**39** On the seventh day, the priest must come back and examine the house. The mold can spread on the walls of the house.

**40** Then the priest must command people to remove the stones with the mold. They must throw them into an unclean place outside the city.

**41** He must make people scrape all the inside walls of the house. They must throw the material that they scrape off into an unclean place outside the city.

**42** They must put other stones in the place of the old stones. They must put new plaster on the house.

**43** But after they remove the stones, scrape the house, and put new plaster on it, the mold can appear in the house again.

**44** Then the priest must come and examine the house. If the mold spreads in the house, it is a destructive mold. The house is unclean.

**45** People must break down the house, its stones, its wood, and all its plaster. They must carry these materials out of the city to an unclean place.

**46** Each person who goes into the house while the priest keeps it closed will be unclean until the evening.

**47** Each person who sleeps in the house must wash his clothes. Each person who eats in the house must wash his clothes.

**48** But the priest can come in and examine the house after the new plaster. If the mold does not spread in the house, the priest must say that the house is clean. The mold is gone.

**49** To make the house clean, he must take 2 birds, cedar wood, red yarn, and hyssop.

**50** He must kill 1 of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot.

**51** He must take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the red yarn, and the live bird. He must put them into the blood of the dead bird and into the fresh water. He must sprinkle the house 7 times.

**52** He must make the house clean with the blood of the bird and the fresh water. He must also use the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the red yarn.

**53** But he must release the live bird outside the city into the open fields. Thus, he makes atonement for the house, and it will be clean.

**54** This is the law for all types of leprosy and itch.

**55** It is the law for mold in a garment or in a house.

**56** It is the law for a lump, a rash, or a bright spot.

**57** This law shows when a thing is unclean and when a thing is clean. This is the law about leprosy."

## Chapter 15

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'If a man has a discharge from his body, the discharge makes him unclean.

**3** This is how his discharge makes him unclean. His body can continue to flow with the discharge, or the discharge can stop. In both conditions, he is unclean.

**4** Each bed where the man with the discharge lies is unclean. Each thing where he sits is unclean.

**5** Each person who touches his bed must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**6** Each person who sits on a thing where the man with the discharge sat must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**7** Each person who touches the body of the man with the discharge must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**8** If the man with the discharge spits on a clean person, that person must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**9** Each saddle where the man with the discharge rides will be unclean.

**10** Each person who touches any thing that was under him will be unclean until the evening. Each person who carries those things must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**11** The man with the discharge can touch a person, and not wash his hands with water first. Then that person must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**12** If the man with the discharge touches a clay pot, break the pot. If he touches a wood item, wash the item with water.

**13** When the discharge of the man stops, he must count 7 days to become clean. He must wash his clothes and wash his body in fresh water. Then he will be clean.

**14** On the eighth day, he must take 2 doves or 2 young pigeons. He must come in front of the LORD to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. He must give the birds to the priest.

**15** The priest must offer them. 1 bird is a sin offering, and 1 bird is a burnt offering. The priest must make atonement for the man in front of the LORD because of his discharge.

**16** If a man has an emission of semen, he must wash all his body with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**17** If semen falls on a garment or on leather, wash the item with water. The item will be unclean until the evening.

**18** If a man has sex with a woman and has an emission of semen, both of them must wash with water. They will be unclean until the evening.

**19** A woman has a discharge of blood from her body during her monthly period. She will be unclean for 7 days. Each person who touches her will be unclean until the evening.

**20** Each thing where she lies during her period will be unclean. Each thing where she sits will be unclean.

**21** Each person who touches her bed must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**22** Each person who touches any thing where she sat must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**23** If a person touches a thing on her bed or on the place where she sits, he will be unclean until the evening.

**24** If a man has sex with her and her blood touches him, he will be unclean for 7 days. Each bed where he lies will be unclean.

**25** A woman can have a discharge of blood for many days, at a time that is not her usual period. Or her discharge can continue after her usual period. During all the days of her discharge, she will be unclean, the same as during her period.

**26** Each bed where she lies during her discharge will be unclean, the same as her bed during her period. Each thing where she sits will be unclean, the same as during her period.

**27** Each person who touches those things will be unclean. He must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**28** When her discharge stops, she must count 7 days. After that, she will be clean.

**29** On the eighth day, she must take 2 doves or 2 young pigeons. She must bring them to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**30** The priest must offer 1 bird as a sin offering and 1 bird as a burnt offering. The priest must make atonement for her in front of the LORD because of the discharge that made her unclean.

**31** Thus, you must keep the people of Israel separate from things that make them unclean. If they make my tabernacle unclean, they will die. My tabernacle is among them.

**32** This is the law for a man with a discharge, and for a man who has an emission of semen that makes him unclean.

**33** It is the law for a woman during her monthly period, and for a man or a woman with a discharge. It is the law for a man who has sex with a woman who is unclean.'"

## Chapter 16

**1** The 2 sons of Aaron came near to the LORD with an offering, and they died. After their death, the LORD spoke to Moses.

**2** The LORD said to Moses, "Tell your brother Aaron that he must not come at any time into the most holy place behind the curtain. He must not come in front of the mercy seat on the ark when he wants. If he does, he will die. I will appear in the cloud above the mercy seat.

**3** Aaron must come into the holy place in this way. He must bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

**4** He must put on the holy linen coat and the linen underwear. He must tie the linen sash around him and put on the linen turban. These are holy clothes. Thus, he must wash his body with water before he puts them on.

**5** He must take 2 male goats for a sin offering and 1 ram for a burnt offering from the community of Israel.

**6** Aaron must offer the bull as the sin offering for himself. He must make atonement for himself and for his family.

**7** He must take the 2 goats and put them in front of the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**8** Aaron must throw lots (stones to decide) for the 2 goats. 1 lot is for the LORD, and 1 lot is for the scapegoat (Azazel).

**9** Aaron must bring the goat that the lot chooses for the LORD. He must offer it as a sin offering.

**10** But he must put the goat that the lot chooses as the scapegoat in front of the LORD alive. He must use it to make atonement. Then he must send it into the desert as the scapegoat.

**11** Aaron must bring the bull of the sin offering for himself. He must make atonement for himself and for his family. He must kill the bull as the sin offering for himself.

**12** He must take an incense pan full of hot coals from the altar in front of the LORD. He must take 2 handfuls of sweet incense, crushed fine. He must bring them behind the curtain.

**13** He must put the incense on the fire in front of the LORD. Then the smoke of the incense will cover the mercy seat above the testimony. If he does not do this, he will die.

**14** He must take some of the blood of the bull. He must sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the mercy seat, on the east side. He must sprinkle some of the blood with his finger 7 times in front of the mercy seat.

**15** Then he must kill the goat of the sin offering for the people. He must bring its blood behind the curtain. He must do the same with this blood as with the blood of the bull. He must sprinkle it on the mercy seat and in front of the mercy seat.

**16** Thus, he must make atonement for the most holy place. The people of Israel are unclean, and they rebel and sin. He must also do this for the Tent of Meeting, because the tent is among the unclean people.

**17** No person must be in the Tent of Meeting when Aaron goes in to make atonement in the most holy place. No person must be there until he comes out. He makes atonement for himself, for his family, and for all the community of Israel.

**18** Then he must go out to the altar in front of the LORD and make atonement for the altar. He must take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat. He must put the blood on all the horns of the altar.

**19** He must sprinkle some of the blood on the altar with his finger 7 times. Thus, he makes the altar clean and holy again from the uncleanness of the people of Israel.

**20** When he completes the atonement for the most holy place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he must bring the live goat.

**21** Aaron must put both his hands on the head of the live goat. He must confess over it all the sins, rebellion, and wrong actions of the people of Israel. Thus, he puts these sins on the head of the goat. Then he must send the goat into the desert with a man who is ready to take it.

**22** The goat will carry all their sins to a land where no people live. The man must release the goat in the desert.

**23** Then Aaron must go into the Tent of Meeting. He must remove the linen clothes that he wore when he went into the most holy place. He must leave them there.

**24** He must wash his body with water in a holy place and put on his usual clothes. Then he must come out and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people. He must make atonement for himself and for the people.

**25** He must burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.

**26** The man who releases the scapegoat must wash his clothes and wash his body with water. After that, he can come into the camp.

**27** The priest brings the blood of the bull and the goat of the sin offering into the most holy place to make atonement. Then a person must carry these animals outside the camp. People must burn their skins, their meat, and their dung in the fire.

**28** The person who burns them must wash his clothes and wash his body with water. After that, he can come into the camp.

**29** This is a permanent law for you. On the tenth day of the seventh month, you must make yourselves humble (fast). Do not do any work. This law is for the people of Israel and for the foreigners who live among you.

**30** On that day, the priest will make atonement for you to make you clean. Then you will be clean from all your sins in front of the LORD.

**31** It is a Sabbath of full rest for you. You must make yourselves humble. This is a permanent law.

**32** Someone will anoint a priest and ordain him to serve as priest after his father. That priest must make the atonement. He must put on the holy linen clothes.

**33** He must make atonement for the most holy place, for the Tent of Meeting, and for the altar. He must make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the community.

**34** This is a permanent law for you. The priest must make atonement 1 time each year for all the sins of the people of Israel." Aaron did as the LORD commanded Moses.

## Chapter 17

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel. Tell them, 'This is what the LORD commands.

**3** A man of Israel can kill a bull, a lamb, or a goat in the camp or outside the camp.

**4** If he does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting as an offering to the LORD, he is guilty of bloodshed. He is guilty because he killed an animal. Remove that man from his people.

**5** This law is for the people of Israel. They make sacrifices in the open field. But now they must bring them to the LORD. They must bring them to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. They must offer them as peace offerings to the LORD.

**6** The priest must sprinkle the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. He must burn the fat, and its smell will please the LORD.

**7** The people must not offer their sacrifices to goat idols (demons) again. They were not faithful to me because they worshipped these idols. This is a permanent law for them and for all their descendants.'

**8** Tell them, 'A man of Israel or a foreigner who lives among you can offer a burnt offering or a sacrifice.

**9** He can fail to bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to offer it to the LORD. Then remove that man from his people.

**10** A man of Israel or a foreigner who lives among you can eat blood. I will be against that person. I will remove him from his people.

**11** The life of a body is in the blood. I give the blood to you to put on the altar. Thus, you can make atonement for your lives. The blood makes atonement because it is the life.

**12** Thus, I tell the people of Israel, "No person among you must eat blood. No foreigner who lives among you must eat blood."

**13** A man of Israel or a foreigner who lives among you can hunt an animal or a bird that people can eat. He must pour out its blood and cover the blood with soil.

**14** The life of each animal is its blood. Thus, I tell the people of Israel, "Do not eat the blood of any animal, because the life of each animal is its blood. Remove each person who eats blood."

**15** A person can eat an animal that dies naturally or that wild animals kill. This person can be an Israelite or a foreigner. He must wash his clothes and wash with water. He will be unclean until the evening. Then he will be clean.

**16** But if he does not wash his clothes and his body, he will be responsible for his guilt.'"

## Chapter 18

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'I am the LORD your God.

**3** You lived in the land of Egypt. Do not do what the people there do. I bring you to the land of Canaan. Do not do what the people there do. Do not obey their customs.

**4** Obey my rules and keep my laws. Live by them. I am the LORD your God.

**5** Keep my laws and my rules. The person who obeys them will live by them. I am the LORD.

**6** Do not have sex with a close relative. I am the LORD.

**7** Do not dishonor your father by sex with your mother. She is your mother. Do not have sex with her.

**8** Do not have sex with the wife of your father. That dishonors your father.

**9** Do not have sex with your sister. She can be the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother. Her mother can give birth to her in your home or in another place.

**10** Do not have sex with the daughter of your son or the daughter of your daughter. That dishonors you.

**11** Do not have sex with the daughter of the wife of your father. Your father is her father, and she is your sister.

**12** Do not have sex with the sister of your father. She is a close relative of your father.

**13** Do not have sex with the sister of your mother. She is a close relative of your mother.

**14** Do not dishonor the brother of your father. Do not have sex with his wife. She is your aunt.

**15** Do not have sex with your daughter-in-law. She is the wife of your son. Do not have sex with her.

**16** Do not have sex with the wife of your brother. That dishonors your brother.

**17** Do not have sex with a woman and her daughter. Do not marry and have sex with the daughter of her son or the daughter of her daughter. They are her close relatives. This is evil.

**18** While your wife is alive, do not marry her sister as a second wife. Do not have sex with her sister. That will cause your wife to be a rival to her sister.

**19** Do not have sex with a woman during her monthly period, when she is unclean.

**20** Do not have sex with the wife of your neighbor. That makes you unclean.

**21** Do not give any of your children as a sacrifice to Molech by fire. Do not dishonor the name of your God. I am the LORD.

**22** A man must not have sex with a man as with a woman. That is detestable.

**23** A man must not have sex with any animal. That makes him unclean. A woman must not offer herself to an animal for sex. That is a perversion.

**24** Do not make yourselves unclean with any of these things. The nations that I push out in front of you made themselves unclean with all these things.

**25** Their land became unclean. Thus, I punish the land for its sin, and the land throws out its people.

**26** You must keep my laws and my rules. Do not do any of these detestable things. This law is for the people of Israel and for the foreigners who live among you.

**27** The people who lived in the land before you did all these detestable things. Thus, the land became unclean.

**28** If you make the land unclean, the land will throw you out. It will do the same as it did to the nations before you.

**29** Remove from their people all the persons who do any of these detestable things.

**30** Thus, obey my commands. Do not do any of the detestable customs that the people did before you. Do not make yourselves unclean with these customs. I am the LORD your God.'"

## Chapter 19

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to all the community of the people of Israel. Tell them, 'Be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.

**3** Each person must respect his mother and his father. Keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.

**4** Do not worship idols. Do not make gods from melted metal for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.

**5** When you offer a peace offering to the LORD, offer it in the correct way. Then the LORD will accept you.

**6** Eat it on the day that you offer it or on the next day. If some of it remains until the third day, burn it.

**7** If a person eats any of it on the third day, it is detestable. The LORD will not accept it.

**8** Each person who eats it will be responsible for his guilt. He dishonors a holy thing of the LORD. Remove that person from his people.

**9** When you harvest the crops of your land, do not harvest to the edges of your field. Do not collect the grain that falls on the ground.

**10** Do not go back over your vineyard a second time. Do not collect the grapes that fall on the ground. Leave them for the poor people and for the foreigners. I am the LORD your God.

**11** Do not steal. Do not cheat. Do not lie to each other.

**12** Do not use my name to make a false promise. Do not dishonor the name of your God. I am the LORD.

**13** Do not cheat your neighbor or rob him. Do not keep the pay of a worker until the next morning.

**14** Do not curse a deaf person. Do not put an obstacle in front of a blind person. Respect your God. I am the LORD.

**15** Do not make an unfair decision in court. Do not give special help to a poor person. Do not give special honor to an important person. Judge your neighbor fairly.

**16** Do not spread false stories about other people among your people. Do not do anything that puts the life of your neighbor in danger. I am the LORD.

**17** Do not hate your brother in your heart. Correct your neighbor when he does wrong. Then you will not share the guilt of his sin.

**18** Do not take revenge on your people. Do not continue to be angry with them. Love your neighbor as you love yourself. I am the LORD.

**19** Obey my laws. Do not let 2 different types of animals breed together. Do not plant 2 types of seed in your field. Do not wear clothes made of 2 types of material.

**20** A man can have sex with a female slave who has a promise of marriage to another man. Her owner did not set her free or pay to make her free. Then there must be a punishment. But do not kill them, because she was not free.

**21** The man must bring a ram as his guilt offering to the LORD. He must bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**22** The priest must make atonement for him in front of the LORD with the ram of the guilt offering. He makes atonement for the sin that the man did. Then God will forgive his sin.

**23** When you go into the land, you will plant all types of fruit trees. Think of their fruit as forbidden for 3 years. Do not eat it.

**24** In the fourth year, all their fruit will be holy. Offer it as praise to the LORD.

**25** In the fifth year, you can eat their fruit. Then the trees will give you more fruit. I am the LORD your God.

**26** Do not eat any meat with the blood in it. Do not use magic. Do not try to tell the future by signs.

**27** Do not cut the hair on the sides of your head. Do not cut the edges of your beard.

**28** Do not cut your bodies for the dead. Do not put tattoos on yourselves. I am the LORD.

**29** Do not dishonor your daughter. Do not make her a prostitute. If you do, the land will become full of prostitution and evil.

**30** Keep my Sabbaths. Respect my holy place. I am the LORD.

**31** Do not go to mediums who speak with the dead. Do not go to people who speak with spirits. They will make you unclean. I am the LORD your God.

**32** Stand up in front of old people. Show respect to old people. Respect your God. I am the LORD.

**33** When a foreigner lives with you in your land, do not treat him badly.

**34** Treat the foreigner who lives with you as a person from your own people. Love him as you love yourself. You were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

**35** Do not cheat when you measure length, weight, or quantity.

**36** Use honest scales and honest weights. Use an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God. I brought you out of the land of Egypt.

**37** Keep all my laws and all my rules. Obey them. I am the LORD.'"

## Chapter 20

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Tell the people of Israel, 'A person of Israel or a foreigner who lives in Israel can give 1 of his children to Molech. Kill that person. The people of the community must throw stones at him until he dies.

**3** I will be against that man, and I will remove him from his people. He gave 1 of his children to Molech. Thus, he made my holy place unclean and dishonored my holy name.

**4** The people of the community can ignore the man who gives 1 of his children to Molech. They can choose not to kill him.

**5** Then I will be against that man and against his family. I will remove him from his people. I will also remove all the people who follow him and worship Molech.

**6** A person can go to mediums and to people who speak with spirits. He is not faithful to me when he follows them. I will be against that person. I will remove him from his people.

**7** Make yourselves holy and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.

**8** Keep my laws and obey them. I am the LORD who makes you holy.

**9** Kill each person who curses his father or his mother. He cursed his father or his mother. He is responsible for his own death.

**10** A man can have sex with the wife of another man, the wife of his neighbor. Kill both the man and the woman.

**11** A man can have sex with the wife of his father. He dishonors his father. Kill both the man and the woman. They are responsible for their own deaths.

**12** A man can have sex with his daughter-in-law. Kill both of them. They did a perversion. They are responsible for their own deaths.

**13** A man can have sex with another man as with a woman. Both of them did a detestable thing. Kill both of them. They are responsible for their own deaths.

**14** A man can marry a woman and her mother. That is evil. Burn him and the 2 women with fire. Then there will be no evil among you.

**15** A man can have sex with an animal. Kill the man and kill the animal.

**16** A woman can offer herself to an animal for sex. Kill the woman and the animal. They are responsible for their own deaths.

**17** A man can marry his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother, and they can have sex. That is shameful. Remove them from their people in public. He dishonored his sister. He will be responsible for his guilt.

**18** A man can have sex with a woman during her monthly period. He exposes the flow of her blood, and she shows it. Remove both of them from their people.

**19** Do not have sex with the sister of your mother or the sister of your father. That dishonors a close relative. Both persons will be responsible for their guilt.

**20** A man can have sex with the wife of his uncle. He dishonors his uncle. They will be responsible for their sin. They will die without children.

**21** A man can marry the wife of his brother. That is unclean. He dishonors his brother. They will have no children.

**22** Keep all my laws and all my rules. Obey them. I bring you to a land to live in. If you obey, the land will not throw you out.

**23** Do not follow the customs of the nations that I push out in front of you. They did all these things, and I hated them.

**24** I told you, "You will receive their land. I will give it to you as your property. It is a land that has much milk and honey." I am the LORD your God. I made you separate from other people.

**25** Thus, you must know the difference between clean and unclean animals and between unclean and clean birds. Do not make yourselves detestable with any animal, bird, or small animal on the ground. I showed you that these animals are unclean.

**26** Be holy to me, because I, the LORD, am holy. I made you separate from other people. You are my people.

**27** A man or a woman who is a medium or who speaks with spirits must die. Throw stones at them until they die. They are responsible for their own deaths.'"

## Chapter 21

**1** The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron. Tell them, 'A priest must not make himself unclean for a dead person among his people.

**2** But he can do so for a close relative. He can do so for his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, or his brother.

**3** He can also make himself unclean for his sister who is a virgin. She is close to him, because she has no husband.

**4** He is a leader among his people. Thus, he must not make himself unclean and dishonor himself.

**5** Priests must not shave their heads. They must not cut the edges of their beards. They must not make cuts in their bodies.

**6** They must be holy to their God. They must not dishonor the name of their God. They offer the offerings by fire to the LORD, the food of their God. Thus, they must be holy.

**7** A priest must not marry a prostitute or a woman who is not pure. He must not marry a woman whose husband divorced her. The priest is holy to his God.

**8** Think of the priest as holy, because he offers the food of your God. He must be holy to you, because I, the LORD, am holy. I make you holy.

**9** If the daughter of a priest dishonors herself by prostitution, she dishonors her father. Burn her with fire.

**10** The high priest is the most important priest among his brothers. Moses poured the holy oil on his head. Moses ordained him to wear the holy clothes. He must not let the hair of his head hang loose. He must not tear his clothes.

**11** He must not go near a dead body. He must not make himself unclean, even for his father or his mother.

**12** He must not leave the holy place. He must not dishonor the holy place of his God. The holy oil of his God is on him as a crown. I am the LORD.

**13** The high priest must marry a virgin.

**14** He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, a woman who is not pure, or a prostitute. He must marry a virgin from his own people.

**15** Then he will not dishonor his children among his people. I am the LORD who makes him holy.'"

**16** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**17** "Speak to Aaron. Tell him, 'In all future generations, some of your descendants can have a physical defect. That person must not come near to offer the food of his God.

**18** No man with a defect must come near. A man who is blind or lame must not come near. A man with a damaged face or a deformed body must not come near.

**19** A man with a broken foot or a broken hand must not come near.

**20** A man who has a bent back or who is very short must not come near. A man with a defect in his eye, with a skin disease, or with damaged testicles must not come near.

**21** No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a defect must come near to offer the offerings by fire to the LORD. He has a defect. Thus, he must not come near to offer the food of his God.

**22** He can eat the food of his God, from the most holy and the holy offerings.

**23** But he must not go near the curtain or the altar, because he has a defect. If he does, he will dishonor my holy places. I am the LORD who makes them holy.'"

**24** Moses told these things to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the people of Israel.

## Chapter 22

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy things that the people of Israel give to me. Thus they will not make my holy name unclean. I am the LORD.

**3** Tell them, 'In all future generations, a descendant of yours can be unclean and come near the holy things. The people of Israel give these things to the LORD. I will remove that person from my presence. I am the LORD.

**4** A descendant of Aaron can have a skin disease (leprosy) or a fluid that comes from his body. He must not eat the holy things until he is clean. A man can touch a thing that a dead body made unclean. Or semen can come from his body.

**5** Or a man can touch a small animal that makes him unclean. Or he can touch a person who makes him unclean in any way.

**6** The person who touches such a thing will be unclean until the evening. He must not eat the holy things until he washes his body with water.

**7** When the sun goes down, he will be clean. Then he can eat the holy things, because they are his food.

**8** He must not eat an animal that died naturally or that wild animals killed. That food will make him unclean. I am the LORD.

**9** The priests must obey my rules. If they do not obey, they will be guilty and they will die. I am the LORD. I make them holy.

**10** A person who is not from the family of a priest must not eat the holy food. A guest of the priest or a hired worker must not eat the holy food.

**11** But a priest can buy a slave with his money. That slave can eat the holy food. Slaves that his slave women give birth to in his house can also eat his food.

**12** If the daughter of a priest marries a man who is not a priest, she must not eat the holy offerings.

**13** But the daughter of a priest can become a widow or she can divorce. If she has no child and she goes back to her father's house, she can eat her father's food again. But a person who is not from the family of a priest must not eat that food.

**14** A man can eat holy food by mistake. Then he must give the priest the same quantity of holy food and add 1/5 of its value.

**15** The priests must not make unclean the holy things that the people of Israel give to the LORD.

**16** If the people eat these holy things, the priests will cause the people to become guilty. I am the LORD. I make the people holy.'"

**17** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**18** "Speak to Aaron, to his sons and to all the people of Israel. Tell them, 'An Israelite or a foreigner in Israel can bring a burnt offering to the LORD. He can give it to complete a promise (vow) or as a gift that he wants to give (freewill offering).

**19** For the LORD to accept it, you must give a male animal with no defect. It must come from the cattle, the sheep or the goats.

**20** Do not offer an animal that has a defect. The LORD will not accept it from you.

**21** A person can bring a peace offering to the LORD to complete a vow or as a freewill offering. The animal can be from the cattle or the sheep. The animal must have no defect, or the LORD will not accept it.

**22** Do not offer to the LORD an animal that is blind, injured or maimed. Do not offer an animal that has a wart, sores or a skin disease. Do not put such an animal on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD.

**23** A bull or a lamb can have a body part that is too long or too short. You can give it as a freewill offering. But the LORD will not accept it for a vow.

**24** Do not offer to the LORD an animal with damaged, crushed, torn or cut testicles. Do not do this in your land.

**25** Do not accept such animals from a foreigner and offer them as food for your God. They have defects, so the LORD will not accept them from you.'"

**26** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**27** "When a cow, a sheep or a goat gives birth to its young, the young animal must stay with its mother for 7 days. From the 8th day, the LORD will accept it as an offering by fire.

**28** Do not kill a cow or a sheep and its young on the same day.

**29** When you give a sacrifice of thanks to the LORD, give it in a way that the LORD will accept.

**30** Eat all of it on the same day. Do not keep any of it until the next morning. I am the LORD.

**31** Keep my commands and obey them. I am the LORD.

**32** Do not make my holy name unclean. The people of Israel must honor me as holy. I am the LORD. I make you holy.

**33** I brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."

## Chapter 23

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'These are the festivals of the LORD. You must announce them as holy meetings. They are my festivals.

**3** You can work for 6 days. But the 7th day is a Sabbath of full rest. It is a holy assembly. Do not do any work on that day. It is a Sabbath to the LORD in all your homes.

**4** These are the festivals of the LORD. They are holy meetings. You must announce them at their correct times.

**5** The Passover of the LORD starts in the evening on the 14th day of the 1st month.

**6** On the 15th day of the same month, the Festival of Bread Without Yeast to the LORD starts. For 7 days you must eat bread without yeast.

**7** On the 1st day, you must have a holy assembly. Do not do your usual work on that day.

**8** For 7 days you must give an offering by fire to the LORD. On the 7th day, you must have a holy assembly. Do not do your usual work on that day.'"

**9** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**10** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'You will go into the land that I give you. When you cut the grain there, bring the first bundle of grain to the priest.

**11** The priest must lift up the bundle in front of the LORD. Then the LORD will accept it for you. The priest must do this on the day after the Sabbath.

**12** On the day that you lift up the bundle, offer a male lamb that is 1 year old. It must have no defect. It is a burnt offering to the LORD.

**13** With it, give a grain offering of 2/10 of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. It is an offering by fire to the LORD, and its smell pleases him. Also give a drink offering of 1/4 of a hin of wine.

**14** Do not eat bread, roasted grain or new grain until that day. First you must bring the offering to your God. This is a permanent rule for all your generations in all your homes.

**15** Count 7 full weeks from the day after the Sabbath. Start on the day that you bring the bundle of grain as a wave offering.

**16** Count 50 days to the day after the 7th Sabbath. Then give a new grain offering to the LORD.

**17** From your homes, bring 2 loaves of bread as a wave offering. Make each loaf from 2/10 of an ephah of fine flour. Bake them with yeast. They are the first part of the harvest for the LORD.

**18** With the bread, offer 7 lambs that are 1 year old with no defect. Also offer 1 young bull and 2 rams. They are a burnt offering to the LORD. Give them with their grain offering and their drink offerings. They are an offering by fire, and their smell pleases the LORD.

**19** Then sacrifice 1 male goat for a sin offering. Also sacrifice 2 lambs that are 1 year old for a peace offering.

**20** The priest must lift up the 2 lambs and the bread of the first part of the harvest. They are a wave offering in front of the LORD. They are holy to the LORD and they are for the priest.

**21** On that same day, announce a holy assembly. Do not do your usual work on that day. This is a permanent rule in all your homes for all your generations.

**22** When you cut the grain in your land, do not cut the grain at the edges of your field. Do not pick up the grain that falls. Leave it for the poor people and for the foreigners. I am the LORD your God.'"

**23** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**24** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'The 1st day of the 7th month is a day of rest for you. You must blow trumpets to remember it. It is a holy assembly.

**25** Do not do your usual work on that day. Give an offering by fire to the LORD.'"

**26** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**27** "The 10th day of this 7th month is the Day of Atonement. On that day the priest removes the guilt of your sins (atonement). It is a holy assembly for you. You must not eat food on that day, and you must offer an offering by fire to the LORD.

**28** Do not do any work on that day. It is the Day of Atonement. On that day the priest makes atonement for you in front of the LORD your God.

**29** Remove from his people a person who eats food on that day.

**30** If a person does any work on that day, I will destroy that person from among his people.

**31** Do not do any work. This is a permanent rule for all your generations in all your homes.

**32** It is a Sabbath of full rest for you. You must not eat food. Keep your Sabbath from the evening of the 9th day of the month until the next evening."

**33** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**34** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'On the 15th day of this 7th month, the Festival of Shelters starts. It continues for 7 days for the LORD.

**35** On the 1st day there is a holy assembly. Do not do your usual work on that day.

**36** For 7 days you must give an offering by fire to the LORD. On the 8th day you must have a holy assembly. Give an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a special assembly. Do not do your usual work on that day.

**37** These are the festivals of the LORD. You must announce them as holy meetings. At these festivals you must give offerings by fire to the LORD. Give burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings. Give each offering on its correct day.

**38** These offerings are in addition to the Sabbaths of the LORD. They are also in addition to your gifts, your vows and your freewill offerings to the LORD.

**39** On the 15th day of the 7th month, you will collect the crops of the land. Then keep the festival of the LORD for 7 days. The 1st day is a day of rest. The 8th day is also a day of rest.

**40** On the 1st day, take good fruit from the trees. Also take palm branches, branches from leafy trees and willows from the streams. Be happy in front of the LORD your God for 7 days.

**41** Keep this festival to the LORD for 7 days each year. This is a permanent rule for all your generations. Keep it in the 7th month.

**42** Live in shelters for 7 days. All the people who are Israelites by birth must live in shelters.

**43** Then your descendants will know that I made the people of Israel live in shelters. I did this when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.'"

**44** Thus Moses told the people of Israel about the festivals of the LORD.

## Chapter 24

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Tell the people of Israel to bring you pure olive oil from crushed olives. The oil is for the light, so that the lamps always burn.

**3** In the Tent of Meeting, outside the curtain in front of the box of the Testimony, Aaron must keep the lamps lit. They must burn in front of the LORD from evening until morning. This is a permanent rule for all your generations.

**4** Aaron must always keep the lamps on the pure gold lampstand in front of the LORD.

**5** Take fine flour and bake 12 loaves of bread. Use 2/10 of an ephah of flour for each loaf.

**6** Put them in 2 rows, with 6 loaves in each row. Put them on the pure gold table in front of the LORD.

**7** Put pure incense on each row. The incense is a reminder for the bread. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.

**8** On each Sabbath, Aaron must put the bread in rows in front of the LORD. The people of Israel must always give this bread. It is a permanent agreement (covenant).

**9** The bread is for Aaron and his sons. They must eat it in a holy place, because it is a most holy part of the offerings by fire to the LORD. This is a permanent rule."

**10** The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian man went out among the people of Israel. In the camp, he started to fight with an Israelite man.

**11** The son of the Israelite woman spoke against the name of the LORD and he cursed. Thus the people brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith. She was the daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.

**12** The people kept him under guard until the LORD told them what to do.

**13** Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**14** "Take the man who cursed outside the camp. All the people who heard him must put their hands on his head. Then all the people must throw stones at him until he dies.

**15** Tell the people of Israel, 'A person who curses his God will be guilty.

**16** A person who speaks against the name of the LORD must die. All the people must throw stones at him until he dies. The foreigner and the native Israelite must die if they speak against the name of the LORD.

**17** A person who kills a man must die.

**18** A person who kills an animal of another person must pay for it. He must give an animal for an animal.

**19** If a person injures another person, you must do the same thing to him.

**20** Give a broken bone for a broken bone, an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth. The person must get the same injury that he caused.

**21** A person who kills an animal must pay for it. But a person who kills a man must die.

**22** You must have the same law for the foreigner and for the native Israelite. I am the LORD your God.'"

**23** Then Moses spoke to the people of Israel. They took the man who cursed outside the camp. They threw stones at him until he died. The people of Israel did as the LORD commanded Moses.

## Chapter 25

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'You will go into the land that I give you. Then the land must have a Sabbath rest to the LORD.

**3** For 6 years you can plant your fields. For 6 years you can cut back your vines and collect their fruit.

**4** But the 7th year is a Sabbath of full rest for the land. It is a Sabbath for the LORD. Do not plant your fields and do not cut back your vines.

**5** Do not cut the crops that grow without your help. Do not collect the grapes from vines that you did not cut back. It is a year of rest for the land.

**6** The crops that grow during the Sabbath year will be food for all of you. They will be food for you, your male and female slaves, your hired worker and the foreigner who lives with you.

**7** The crops will also be food for your livestock and for the wild animals in your land.

**8** Count 7 Sabbaths of years, 7 times 7 years. The 7 Sabbaths of years are a total of 49 years.

**9** Then on the 10th day of the 7th month, blow the trumpet loudly. On the Day of Atonement, blow the trumpet in all your land.

**10** Make the 50th year holy. Announce freedom in all the land for all the people who live there. It is a Jubilee year for you. Each man must go back to his own land and to his own family.

**11** The 50th year is a Jubilee for you. Do not plant. Do not cut the crops that grow without your help. Do not collect grapes from vines that you did not cut back.

**12** It is the Jubilee, and it is holy for you. Eat only the crops that grow in the fields.

**13** In this year of Jubilee, each man must go back to his own land.

**14** When you sell land to your neighbor or buy land from your neighbor, do not cheat one another.

**15** When you buy from your neighbor, calculate the price from the number of years after the Jubilee. He must sell to you as a function of the number of harvests that remain.

**16** If there are many years, increase the price. If there are few years, decrease the price. He sells you only the number of harvests.

**17** Do not cheat one another. Respect your God. I am the LORD your God.

**18** Obey my rules and my laws. Then you will live safely in the land.

**19** The land will give its fruit. You will eat as much as you want, and you will live safely in the land.

**20** You can ask, "What will we eat in the 7th year? We will not plant and we will not collect our crops."

**21** I will send my blessing to you in the 6th year. The land will give sufficient crops for 3 years.

**22** When you plant in the 8th year, you will still eat the old crops. You will eat the old crops until the harvest of the 9th year.

**23** Do not sell the land permanently, because the land is mine. You are only foreigners and guests with me.

**24** In all the land that you own, you must let the seller buy back the land.

**25** Your fellow Israelite can become poor and sell some of his land. Then his nearest relative must come and buy back what his relative sold.

**26** A man can have no relative to buy back the land. But later he can become rich and have sufficient money to buy it back himself.

**27** Then he must count the years after the sale. He must pay the value of the rest of the years to the man who bought the land. Then he can go back to his land.

**28** If he does not have sufficient money to buy it back, the buyer keeps the land until the year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee the land goes back to the seller. Then the seller can go back to his land.

**29** A man can sell a house in a city with walls. He can buy it back for 1 full year after the sale.

**30** If he does not buy it back in 1 full year, the house becomes the permanent property of the buyer and his descendants. The house does not go back to the seller in the Jubilee.

**31** But houses in villages without walls are the same as fields. The seller can buy them back. They go back to the seller in the Jubilee.

**32** But the Levites can always buy back their houses in the cities that they own.

**33** A Levite can sell a house in a Levite city and not buy it back. That house will go back to him in the Jubilee. The houses in the cities of the Levites are their property among the people of Israel.

**34** No one must sell the fields around the Levite cities. They are the permanent property of the Levites.

**35** Your fellow Israelite can become poor and unable to support himself. Then you must help him. Help him as you help a foreigner or a guest, so that he can continue to live near you.

**36** Do not take interest or profit from him. Respect your God. Thus your fellow Israelite can continue to live near you.

**37** Do not lend him money for interest. Do not sell him food for profit.

**38** I am the LORD your God. I brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.

**39** Your fellow Israelite can become poor and sell himself to you. Do not make him work as a slave.

**40** Treat him as a hired worker or as a guest. He must work for you until the year of Jubilee.

**41** Then he and his children can leave you. He will go back to his family and to the land of his ancestors.

**42** The people of Israel are my servants. I brought them out of the land of Egypt. Thus no one must sell them as slaves.

**43** Do not be cruel to him. Respect your God.

**44** You can buy male and female slaves from the nations around you.

**45** You can also buy slaves from the foreigners who live among you. You can buy them from their families that they had in your land. They can become your property.

**46** You can give them to your children after you as permanent property. They can be your slaves permanently. But do not be cruel to your fellow Israelites.

**47** A foreigner or a guest among you can become rich. Your fellow Israelite can become poor and sell himself to that foreigner or to a member of the family of that foreigner.

**48** After he sells himself, one of his relatives can buy him back.

**49** His uncle, his cousin or any near relative from his family can buy him back. Or, if he gets sufficient money, he can buy himself back.

**50** He and the buyer must count the years from the sale to the year of Jubilee. The price for his freedom is a function of the number of years. Calculate his value as the pay of a hired worker for those years.

**51** If many years remain, he must pay back a larger part of his sale price.

**52** If only a few years remain until the Jubilee, he must count them. He must pay the price for his freedom from the number of years.

**53** He must be with the buyer as a worker whom the buyer pays each year. Make sure that the buyer is not cruel to him.

**54** If no one buys him back in these ways, he and his children will go free in the year of Jubilee.

**55** The people of Israel are my servants. I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.'"

## Chapter 26

**1** "Do not make idols for yourselves. Do not put up carved images or holy stone pillars. Do not put carved stones in your land to bow down to them. I am the LORD your God.

**2** Keep my Sabbaths and respect my holy place. I am the LORD.

**3** You must obey my rules and keep my commands.

**4** If you do, I will give you rain at the correct time. The land will give its crops, and the trees will give their fruit.

**5** You will have so much grain that you will continue to separate it until the grape harvest. The grape harvest will continue until the time to plant. You will eat all the food that you want, and you will live safely in your land.

**6** I will give peace in the land. You will lie down and no one will make you afraid. I will remove dangerous animals from the land. No army will attack your land.

**7** You will chase your enemies, and you will kill them with the sword.

**8** 5 of you will chase 100 enemies. 100 of you will chase 10,000 enemies. You will kill your enemies with the sword.

**9** I will be kind to you. I will give you many children and make you a large nation. I will keep my agreement (covenant) with you.

**10** You will still eat old crops when the new crops come. You will have to remove the old crops to make space for the new crops.

**11** I will put my tabernacle among you. I will not hate you.

**12** I will walk among you. I will be your God, and you will be my people.

**13** I am the LORD your God. I brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that you were not slaves of the Egyptians. I broke the heavy load on you and made you free.

**14** But you can refuse to listen to me and to obey all these commands.

**15** You can refuse my rules and hate my laws. You can disobey all my commands and break my covenant.

**16** If you do, I will do these things to you. I will send terror, disease and fever. These will make you blind and they will make you weak. You will plant your seed for no result, because your enemies will eat the crops.

**17** I will turn against you, and your enemies will defeat you. The people who hate you will rule you. You will run away when no one chases you.

**18** If you still do not listen to me after all this, I will punish you 7 times more for your sins.

**19** I will destroy your proud strength. I will make the sky above you as hard as iron. I will make the ground below you as hard as bronze.

**20** Your work will be for no result. Your land will not give its crops, and the trees will not give their fruit.

**21** If you continue to act against me and refuse to listen to me, I will punish you 7 times more for your sins.

**22** I will send wild animals among you. They will kill your children and destroy your cattle. You will become few, and your roads will be empty.

**23** If these things do not correct you and you continue to act against me,

**24** then I will act against you. I will punish you 7 times more for your sins.

**25** I will bring war against you to punish you because you broke my covenant. You will go into your cities for safety, but I will send disease among you. Then your enemies will defeat you.

**26** I will stop your supply of food. 10 women will bake all your bread in 1 oven. They will measure your bread by weight. You will eat, but you will still be hungry.

**27** If you still do not listen to me after all this, and you continue to act against me,

**28** then I will act against you in anger. I myself will punish you 7 times more for your sins.

**29** You will be so hungry that you will eat the bodies of your sons and your daughters.

**30** I will destroy your high places of worship. I will cut down your incense altars. I will throw your dead bodies on the remains of your idols. I will hate you.

**31** I will make your cities into ruins. I will destroy your holy places. I will not accept the pleasant smell of your offerings.

**32** I will destroy the land. Your enemies who come to live there will feel great surprise at it.

**33** I will send you away among the nations. I will pull out my sword and chase you. Your land will be empty and your cities will be ruins.

**34** Then the land will have its Sabbath years. The land will rest while it is empty and you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and have its Sabbaths.

**35** While the land is empty, it will rest. It did not rest during your Sabbaths when you lived on it.

**36** I will make the survivors very afraid in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a leaf in the wind will make them run away. They will run as if from a sword. They will fall when no one chases them.

**37** They will fall over one another, as if they run from a sword. But no one will chase them. You will not have the strength to fight your enemies.

**38** You will die among the nations. The land of your enemies will destroy you.

**39** The survivors will become weak in the lands of their enemies because of their sins. They will also become weak because of the sins of their ancestors.

**40** But the survivors can confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors. They can confess that they were not loyal to me and that they acted against me.
