**41** They can know that I acted against them and brought them into the land of their enemies. Their stubborn hearts can become humble, and they can accept the punishment for their sins.

**42** Then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac and my covenant with Abraham. I will also remember the land.

**43** The people will leave the land empty, and the land will have its Sabbaths while it is empty. The people will accept the punishment for their sins. They will get this punishment because they refused my laws and hated my rules.

**44** But when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not refuse them. I will not hate them so much that I destroy them all. I will not break my covenant with them. I am the LORD their God.

**45** For them I will remember the covenant with their ancestors. I brought those ancestors out of the land of Egypt while the nations watched. I did this to be their God. I am the LORD."

**46** These are the rules, the decisions and the laws that the LORD gave on Mount Sinai. He gave them through Moses to the people of Israel.

## Chapter 27

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'A man can make a special promise (vow) to give a person to the LORD. He can pay money for the value of that person.

**3** The value of a male from 20 to 60 years old is 50 shekels of silver. Use the standard shekel of the holy place.

**4** The value of a female of that age is 30 shekels.

**5** The value of a male from 5 to 20 years old is 20 shekels. The value of a female of that age is 10 shekels.

**6** The value of a male from 1 month to 5 years old is 5 shekels of silver. The value of a female of that age is 3 shekels of silver.

**7** The value of a male who is 60 years old or more is 15 shekels. The value of a female of that age is 10 shekels.

**8** But the man who makes the vow can be too poor to pay the value. Then he must bring the person to the priest. The priest will set a value that the man can pay.

**9** A man can promise to give an animal that the LORD accepts as an offering. All such animals that a man gives to the LORD become holy.

**10** He must not change the animal for a different animal. He must not change a good animal for a bad animal, or a bad animal for a good animal. If he changes one animal for a different animal, both animals become holy.

**11** A man can promise to give an unclean animal that the LORD does not accept as an offering. Then he must bring the animal to the priest.

**12** The priest will set its value as good or bad. The value that the priest sets is the value.

**13** If the man wants to buy back the animal, he must pay its value and add 1/5.

**14** A man can give his house as a holy gift to the LORD. Then the priest will set its value as good or bad. The value that the priest sets is the value.

**15** If the man who gave the house wants to buy it back, he must pay its value and add 1/5. Then the house will be his again.

**16** A man can give to the LORD a part of the land of his family. Then calculate its value from the quantity of seed that is necessary to plant it. The value is 50 shekels of silver for each homer of barley seed.

**17** If he gives his field during the year of Jubilee, it keeps the full value.

**18** But if he gives his field after the Jubilee, the priest will calculate its value from the years that remain until the next Jubilee. The priest will decrease the full value.

**19** If the man who gave the field wants to buy it back, he must pay its value and add 1/5. Then the field will be his again.

**20** But he can fail to buy back the field, or he can sell the field to a different man. Then he cannot buy it back again.

**21** When the field becomes free in the Jubilee, it will be holy to the LORD. It will be a field that a man gives permanently to the LORD. It will become the property of the priests.

**22** A man can give to the LORD a field that he bought, which is not part of the land of his family.

**23** Then the priest will calculate its value until the year of Jubilee. The man must pay that value on the same day. The money is holy to the LORD.

**24** In the year of Jubilee, the field will go back to the man who sold it. It will go back to the person who owned the land.

**25** Calculate all values with the standard shekel of the holy place. 1 shekel is 20 gerahs.

**26** But no man can give the firstborn of an animal to the LORD, because the firstborn is already the property of the LORD. A firstborn bull or sheep is the LORD's.

**27** If the firstborn is from an unclean animal, the man can buy it back. He must pay its value and add 1/5. If he does not buy it back, the priest must sell it for its value.

**28** But a man can give a thing permanently to the LORD. It can be a person, an animal or a field from his family land. No one can sell it or buy it back. All things that people give permanently are most holy to the LORD.

**29** No one must buy back a person that people give permanently for destruction. That person must die.

**30** 1/10 (the tithe) of all the crops of the land is the LORD's. This includes the grain of the fields and the fruit of the trees. It is holy to the LORD.

**31** If a man wants to buy back a part of his tithe, he must pay its value and add 1/5.

**32** Every 10th animal from the herds and flocks is holy to the LORD. The shepherd counts the animals as they go under his stick.

**33** The owner must not choose between good and bad animals. He must not change one animal for a different animal. If he changes one, both animals become holy. He cannot buy them back.'"

**34** These are the commands that the LORD gave to Moses on Mount Sinai for the people of Israel.

# Numbers

## Chapter 1

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the desert of Sinai. This was on the 1st day of the 2nd month, in the 2nd year after the people of Israel came out of Egypt. The LORD said,

**2** "Count all the people of Israel. Count them by their clans and by their families. Write the name of each male.

**3** You and Aaron must count all the men in Israel who are 20 years old or more and who can fight in the army. Count them by their divisions.

**4** 1 man from each tribe must help you. Each man must be the leader of his family.

**5** These are the names of the men who will help you. From the tribe of Reuben, Elizur the son of Shedeur.

**6** From Simeon, Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.

**7** From Judah, Nahshon the son of Amminadab.

**8** From Issachar, Nethanel the son of Zuar.

**9** From Zebulun, Eliab the son of Helon.

**10** From the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama the son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.

**11** From Benjamin, Abidan the son of Gideoni.

**12** From Dan, Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.

**13** From Asher, Pagiel the son of Ocran.

**14** From Gad, Eliasaph the son of Deuel.

**15** From Naphtali, Ahira the son of Enan."

**16** These were the men that the people chose. They were the leaders of the tribes of their ancestors. They were the heads of the clans of Israel.

**17** Moses and Aaron took these men whose names the LORD gave.

**18** On the 1st day of the 2nd month, they called all the people together. The people recorded their ancestry by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more.

**19** Moses counted them in the desert of Sinai, as the LORD commanded him.

**20** They counted the descendants of Reuben, the firstborn son of Israel. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**21** The total from the tribe of Reuben was 46,500.

**22** They counted the descendants of Simeon. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**23** The total from the tribe of Simeon was 59,300.

**24** They counted the descendants of Gad. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**25** The total from the tribe of Gad was 45,650.

**26** They counted the descendants of Judah. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**27** The total from the tribe of Judah was 74,600.

**28** They counted the descendants of Issachar. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**29** The total from the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.

**30** They counted the descendants of Zebulun. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**31** The total from the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.

**32** They counted the descendants of Joseph. From Ephraim, they recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**33** The total from the tribe of Ephraim was 40,500.

**34** They counted the descendants of Manasseh. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**35** The total from the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.

**36** They counted the descendants of Benjamin. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**37** The total from the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.

**38** They counted the descendants of Dan. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**39** The total from the tribe of Dan was 62,700.

**40** They counted the descendants of Asher. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**41** The total from the tribe of Asher was 41,500.

**42** They counted the descendants of Naphtali. They recorded them by clans and by families. They wrote the name of each male who was 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army.

**43** The total from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.

**44** Moses, Aaron and the 12 leaders of Israel counted these men. Each leader represented his family.

**45** They counted all the men of Israel who were 20 years old or more and who could fight in the army. They counted them by families.

**46** The total was 603,550.

**47** But they did not count the Levites with the other tribes.

**48** The LORD told Moses,

**49** "Do not count the tribe of Levi. Do not include them with the other people of Israel.

**50** Make the Levites responsible for the tabernacle of the Testimony, for all its equipment and for all the things that belong to it. They must carry the tabernacle and all its equipment. They must do the work of the tabernacle. They must put their tents around it.

**51** When the tabernacle moves, the Levites must take it down. When the people stop to camp, the Levites must put it up. Kill any other person who comes near it.

**52** The people of Israel must put up their tents in their divisions. Each man must camp in his own camp, near the flag of his group.

**53** But the Levites must put up their tents around the tabernacle of the Testimony. Thus the anger of the LORD will not come on the people of Israel. The Levites must guard the tabernacle of the Testimony."

**54** The people of Israel did all that the LORD commanded Moses.

## Chapter 2

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**2** "Each man of Israel must camp near his flag, with the signs of his family. They must camp around the Tent of Meeting, at a distance from it.

**3** The divisions of the camp of Judah must camp on the east side, toward the sunrise. They must camp near their flag. Nahshon the son of Amminadab is the leader of the people of Judah.

**4** His division has 74,600 men.

**5** The tribe of Issachar must camp next to Judah. Nethanel the son of Zuar is the leader of the people of Issachar.

**6** His division has 54,400 men.

**7** Then the tribe of Zebulun must camp there. Eliab the son of Helon is the leader of the people of Zebulun.

**8** His division has 57,400 men.

**9** The total of the men in the camp of Judah is 186,400. They will move out first.

**10** The divisions of the camp of Reuben must camp on the south side near their flag. Elizur the son of Shedeur is the leader of the people of Reuben.

**11** His division has 46,500 men.

**12** The tribe of Simeon must camp next to Reuben. Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai is the leader of the people of Simeon.

**13** His division has 59,300 men.

**14** Then the tribe of Gad must camp there. Eliasaph the son of Reuel is the leader of the people of Gad.

**15** His division has 45,650 men.

**16** The total of the men in the camp of Reuben is 151,450. They will move out second.

**17** Then the Tent of Meeting and the camp of the Levites will move out in the middle of the camps. The tribes must move out in the same order as they camp. Each man must stay in his position near his flag.

**18** The divisions of the camp of Ephraim must camp on the west side near their flag. Elishama the son of Ammihud is the leader of the people of Ephraim.

**19** His division has 40,500 men.

**20** The tribe of Manasseh must camp next to Ephraim. Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur is the leader of the people of Manasseh.

**21** His division has 32,200 men.

**22** Then the tribe of Benjamin must camp there. Abidan the son of Gideoni is the leader of the people of Benjamin.

**23** His division has 35,400 men.

**24** The total of the men in the camp of Ephraim is 108,100. They will move out third.

**25** The divisions of the camp of Dan must camp on the north side near their flag. Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai is the leader of the people of Dan.

**26** His division has 62,700 men.

**27** The tribe of Asher must camp next to Dan. Pagiel the son of Ocran is the leader of the people of Asher.

**28** His division has 41,500 men.

**29** Then the tribe of Naphtali must camp there. Ahira the son of Enan is the leader of the people of Naphtali.

**30** His division has 53,400 men.

**31** The total of the men in the camp of Dan is 157,600. They will move out last, with their flags."

**32** These are the men of Israel that Moses and Aaron counted by families. The total of all the men in the camps was 603,550.

**33** But they did not count the Levites with the other people of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses.

**34** The people of Israel did all that the LORD commanded Moses. They camped near their flags, and they moved out in that order. Each man stayed with his clan and his family.

## Chapter 3

**1** These are the descendants of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.

**2** The names of the sons of Aaron were Nadab, the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

**3** These were the sons of Aaron, who were priests. Moses poured oil on them (anointed them) and made them holy to serve as priests.

**4** But Nadab and Abihu died in front of the LORD in the desert of Sinai. They died because they offered fire that the LORD did not permit. They had no sons. Thus Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests while their father Aaron was alive.

**5** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**6** "Bring the tribe of Levi to Aaron the priest. They must help him.

**7** They must do work for Aaron and for all the people at the Tent of Meeting. They must do the work of the tabernacle.

**8** They must take care of all the equipment of the Tent of Meeting. They must do the work of the tabernacle for the people of Israel.

**9** Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. From all the people of Israel, I give the Levites completely to Aaron.

**10** Make Aaron and his sons responsible for the work of the priests. Kill any other person who comes near the holy place."

**11** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**12** "I take the Levites from among the people of Israel. I take them in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel. Thus the Levites are mine.

**13** All the firstborn are mine. I killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. On that day I made holy for myself all the firstborn in Israel, both men and animals. They are mine. I am the LORD."

**14** The LORD spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai. He said,

**15** "Count the Levites by their families and by their clans. Count each male who is 1 month old or more."

**16** Thus Moses counted them, as the LORD commanded him.

**17** These were the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

**18** The sons of Gershon were Libni and Shimei. They were the heads of clans.

**19** The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel. They were the heads of clans.

**20** The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. They were the heads of clans. These were the clans of the Levites by their families.

**21** The clans of the Libnites and the Shimeites came from Gershon. These were the clans of the Gershonites.

**22** The total of all the males who were 1 month old or more was 7,500.

**23** The clans of the Gershonites camped behind the tabernacle, on the west side.

**24** The leader of the families of the Gershonites was Eliasaph the son of Lael.

**25** At the Tent of Meeting, the Gershonites were responsible for the tabernacle, the tent and its coverings. They were also responsible for the curtain at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**26** They were also responsible for the curtains of the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard. The courtyard is around the tabernacle and the altar. They were also responsible for the ropes and for all the work on these things.

**27** The clans of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites and the Uzzielites came from Kohath. These were the clans of the Kohathites.

**28** The total of all the males who were 1 month old or more was 8,600. They were responsible for the holy place.

**29** The clans of the Kohathites camped on the south side of the tabernacle.

**30** The leader of the families of the Kohathites was Elizaphan the son of Uzziel.

**31** They were responsible for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars and the equipment that the priests used in the holy place. They were also responsible for the curtain and for all the work on these things.

**32** Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, was the chief leader of the Levites. He supervised the men who were responsible for the holy place.

**33** The clans of the Mahlites and the Mushites came from Merari. These were the clans of Merari.

**34** The total of all the males who were 1 month old or more was 6,200.

**35** The leader of the families of Merari was Zuriel the son of Abihail. They camped on the north side of the tabernacle.

**36** The Merarites were responsible for the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, its posts and its bases. They were also responsible for all its equipment and all the work on these things.

**37** They were also responsible for the posts around the courtyard, with their bases, pegs and ropes.

**38** Moses, Aaron and the sons of Aaron camped on the east side of the tabernacle, in front of the Tent of Meeting. They were responsible for the holy place for the people of Israel. The people had to kill any other person who came near the holy place.

**39** Moses and Aaron counted the Levites by their clans, as the LORD commanded. The total of all the males who were 1 month old or more was 22,000.

**40** The LORD told Moses, "Count all the firstborn males of Israel who are 1 month old or more. Write their names.

**41** Take the Levites for me in place of all the firstborn of the people of Israel. I am the LORD. Also take the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the people of Israel."

**42** Thus Moses counted all the firstborn of the people of Israel, as the LORD commanded him.

**43** The total of all the firstborn males who were 1 month old or more was 22,273.

**44** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**45** "Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the people of Israel. Take the livestock of the Levites in place of the livestock of the people. The Levites will be mine. I am the LORD.

**46** There are 273 more firstborn sons of Israel than Levites. You must pay a price to buy back these 273 sons.

**47** Take 5 shekels for each of them. Use the standard shekel of the holy place. 1 shekel is 20 gerahs.

**48** Give this money to Aaron and his sons. It is the price for the firstborn sons that are more than the Levites."

**49** Thus Moses took the money for the firstborn sons that were more than the Levites.

**50** He took the money from the firstborn of the people of Israel. The total was 1,365 shekels, with the standard shekel of the holy place.

**51** Moses gave this money to Aaron and his sons, as the LORD commanded him.

## Chapter 4

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**2** "Count the Kohathites, who are a part of the Levites. Count them by their clans and by their families.

**3** Count all the men from 30 to 50 years old who can do the work in the Tent of Meeting.

**4** This is the work of the Kohathites in the Tent of Meeting. They are responsible for the most holy things.

**5** When the camp moves out, Aaron and his sons must go into the tent. They must take down the curtain that is in front of the ark. They must put it over the ark of the Testimony.

**6** Then they must put a cover of fine leather on the ark. They must put a blue cloth over it. Then they must put the poles in their positions.

**7** They must put a blue cloth on the table for the holy bread. They must put the plates, the dishes, the bowls and the jars for drink offerings on the cloth. The bread that is always there must also stay on it.

**8** They must put a red cloth over these things, and a cover of fine leather over the red cloth. Then they must put the poles of the table in their positions.

**9** They must take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand. They must also cover its lamps, its tools, its trays and all the jars for the oil.

**10** They must put the lampstand and all its equipment in a cover of fine leather. Then they must put it on a frame to carry it.

**11** They must put a blue cloth on the gold altar. They must cover it with fine leather. Then they must put its poles in their positions.

**12** They must take all the equipment that the priests use in the holy place. They must put it in a blue cloth and cover it with fine leather. Then they must put it on a frame to carry it.

**13** They must remove the ashes from the bronze altar. Then they must put a purple cloth on the altar.

**14** They must put on it all the equipment of the altar. This includes the fire pans, the meat forks, the shovels and the bowls. They must put a cover of fine leather on it. Then they must put its poles in their positions.

**15** Aaron and his sons must cover the holy place and all its holy equipment. When they finish, the camp can move out. Then the Kohathites must come and carry these things. But the Kohathites must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things in the Tent of Meeting that the Kohathites must carry.

**16** Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, is responsible for the oil for the light and for the sweet incense. He is also responsible for the daily grain offering and for the oil that the priests use to anoint. He must supervise all the tabernacle, all the holy things and all its equipment."

**17** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**18** "Do not let the clans of the Kohathites disappear from among the Levites.

**19** Do this for them, so that they live and do not die when they come near the most holy things. Aaron and his sons must go in. They must give each Kohathite his work and the things that he must carry.

**20** But the Kohathites must not go in and look at the holy things, not even for a moment. If they do, they will die."

**21** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**22** "Count the Gershonites also, by their families and by their clans.

**23** Count all the men from 30 to 50 years old who can do the work in the Tent of Meeting.

**24** This is the work of the clans of the Gershonites. They must do work and carry loads.

**25** They must carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the Tent of Meeting. They must carry its cover and the outer cover of fine leather. They must carry the curtain at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**26** They must carry the curtains of the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar. They must carry the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard, the ropes and all the equipment for this work. They must do all the work with these things.

**27** Aaron and his sons must supervise all the work of the Gershonites. They must supervise all that the Gershonites carry and do. Tell the Gershonites all the things that they must carry.

**28** This is the work of the clans of the Gershonites at the Tent of Meeting. Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest, must supervise their work.

**29** Count the Merarites by their clans and by their families.

**30** Count all the men from 30 to 50 years old who can do the work in the Tent of Meeting.

**31** These are the things that they must carry for their work at the Tent of Meeting. They must carry the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, its posts and its bases.

**32** They must also carry the posts around the courtyard, with their bases, pegs and ropes. They must carry all the equipment for this work. Give each man a list of the things that he must carry.

**33** This is the work of the clans of the Merarites at the Tent of Meeting. Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest, must supervise their work."

**34** Moses, Aaron and the leaders of the people counted the Kohathites by their clans and by their families.

**35** They counted all the men from 30 to 50 years old who could do the work in the Tent of Meeting.

**36** The total by clans was 2,750.

**37** This was the total of the clans of the Kohathites who could do the work at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them, as the LORD commanded through Moses.

**38** They counted the Gershonites by their clans and by their families.

**39** They counted all the men from 30 to 50 years old who could do the work in the Tent of Meeting.

**40** The total by clans and by families was 2,630.

**41** This was the total of the clans of the Gershonites who could do the work at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them, as the LORD commanded.

**42** They counted the clans of the Merarites by their clans and by their families.

**43** They counted all the men from 30 to 50 years old who could do the work in the Tent of Meeting.

**44** The total by clans was 3,200.

**45** This was the total of the clans of the Merarites. Moses and Aaron counted them, as the LORD commanded through Moses.

**46** Moses, Aaron and the leaders of Israel counted all the Levites by their clans and by their families.

**47** They counted all the men from 30 to 50 years old who could do the work and carry the loads at the Tent of Meeting.

**48** The total was 8,580.

**49** Moses counted them as the LORD commanded. He gave each man his work and the things that he had to carry. He did as the LORD commanded Moses.

## Chapter 5

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Tell the people of Israel to send out of the camp all persons with a skin disease (leprosy). Also send out all persons who have a fluid that comes from their body. Send out all persons who are unclean because they touched a dead body.

**3** Send out the men and the women. Send them outside the camp. Thus they will not make the camp unclean, because I live among the people."

**4** The people of Israel did this. They sent these persons outside the camp. The people of Israel did as the LORD told Moses.

**5** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**6** "Tell the people of Israel, 'A man or a woman can do a wrong thing to another person. That person is not loyal to the LORD and is guilty.

**7** He must confess the sin that he did. He must pay the full value for the wrong and add 1/5. He must give it to the person that he did wrong to.

**8** But that person can have no near relative to receive the payment. Then the payment is for the LORD and it goes to the priest. The guilty person must also give a ram to the priest. With that ram, the priest makes atonement for him.

**9** All the holy gifts that the people of Israel bring to the priest are for that priest.

**10** Each man keeps his holy gifts. But the things that he gives to the priest are for the priest.'"

**11** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**12** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'A man's wife can be unfaithful to him.

**13** She can have sex with a different man, and her husband does not know about it. She becomes unclean, but no one sees it and there is no witness.

**14** Her husband can become jealous and think that his wife is unclean. Or her husband can become jealous when his wife is not unclean.

**15** Then the man must bring his wife to the priest. He must bring an offering for her of 1/10 of an ephah of barley flour. He must not pour oil on it or put incense on it. It is a grain offering for jealousy. It is a grain offering to make people remember a sin.

**16** The priest must bring the woman near. He must put her in front of the LORD.

**17** The priest must put holy water in a clay jar. He must take some dust from the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.

**18** The priest must put the woman in front of the LORD and let her hair go loose. He must put the grain offering for jealousy in her hands. The priest must hold the bitter water that brings a curse.

**19** Then the priest must make the woman make a solemn promise (oath). He must say to the woman, "No other man had sex with you. You were not unfaithful to your husband and you did not become unclean. If this is true, then this bitter water that brings a curse will not hurt you.

**20** But you were possibly unfaithful to your husband and became unclean. A man who is not your husband possibly had sex with you."

**21** Then the priest must make the woman take an oath with a curse. The priest must say to the woman, "If you are guilty, the LORD will make your people curse you. He will make your thigh waste away and your belly swell.

**22** This water that brings a curse will go into your body. It will make your belly swell and your thigh waste away." Then the woman must say, "Amen. Amen."

**23** The priest must write these curses on a scroll. He must wash the words off into the bitter water.

**24** He must make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse. If she is guilty, the water will go into her and cause bitter pain.

**25** The priest must take the grain offering for jealousy from the hands of the woman. He must lift it up in front of the LORD and bring it to the altar.

**26** The priest must take a handful of the grain offering as a reminder. He must burn it on the altar. Then he must make the woman drink the water.

**27** If she is unclean and unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings a curse will go into her. It will cause bitter pain. Her belly will swell and her thigh will waste away. Her people will use her name as a curse.

**28** But if the woman is not unclean, she is clean. Then she will not be hurt, and she will be able to have children.

**29** This is the law about jealousy. It is for a wife who is unfaithful to her husband and becomes unclean.

**30** It is also for a husband who becomes jealous and thinks that his wife is unclean. He must put the woman in front of the LORD. The priest must do all this law to her.

**31** The husband will not be guilty of sin. But if the woman is guilty, she will get the punishment for her sin.'"

## Chapter 6

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'A man or a woman can make a special promise to become a Nazirite. A Nazirite is a person who promises to separate himself to the LORD.

**3** He must not drink wine or other alcohol. He must not drink vinegar that people make from wine or from other alcohol. He must not drink grape juice. He must not eat fresh grapes or dried grapes.

**4** While he is a Nazirite, he must not eat anything from the grapevine. He must not eat the seeds or the skins.

**5** While he is a Nazirite, he must not cut the hair on his head. He is holy until the end of the time that he promised to the LORD. He must let the hair on his head grow long.

**6** While he keeps himself separate for the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.

**7** He must not make himself unclean, even if his father, mother, brother or sister dies. His long hair shows that he gave himself to his God.

**8** While he is a Nazirite, he is holy to the LORD.

**9** A person can die suddenly near the Nazirite. That makes his hair unclean. Thus he must shave his head on the 7th day, when he becomes clean.

**10** On the 8th day, he must bring 2 doves or 2 young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**11** The priest must offer 1 bird as a sin offering and 1 bird as a burnt offering. Thus the priest makes atonement for him, because he became unclean near the dead body. On that same day, the Nazirite must make his head holy again.

**12** He must give himself to the LORD again for the full time of his promise. He must bring a male lamb that is 1 year old as a guilt offering. The days before do not count, because he became unclean during his time as a Nazirite.

**13** This is the law for the Nazirite when his time as a Nazirite is complete. He must go to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**14** He must bring his offerings to the LORD. He must bring 1 male lamb that is 1 year old with no defect for a burnt offering. He must bring 1 female lamb that is 1 year old with no defect for a sin offering. He must bring 1 ram with no defect for a peace offering.

**15** He must also bring a basket of bread without yeast. The basket must contain loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and thin bread with oil on it. He must also bring their grain offerings and drink offerings.

**16** The priest must bring these things to the LORD. He must offer the sin offering and the burnt offering.

**17** He must offer the ram as a peace offering to the LORD, with the basket of bread without yeast. The priest must also offer the grain offering and the drink offering.

**18** At the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the Nazirite must shave off his long hair. He must put the hair in the fire under the peace offering.

**19** After the Nazirite shaves his hair, the priest must take the boiled shoulder of the ram. He must also take 1 loaf and 1 thin piece of bread without yeast from the basket. He must put them in the hands of the Nazirite.

**20** Then the priest must lift them up as a wave offering in front of the LORD. They are holy and they are for the priest. The breast and the thigh of the ram are also for the priest. After this, the Nazirite can drink wine.

**21** This is the law for the Nazirite who makes a promise. He must give these offerings to the LORD as a Nazirite. He can also give more if he can. He must do all that he promised, as the law of the Nazirite tells him.'"

**22** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**23** "Tell Aaron and his sons, 'Bless the people of Israel with these words:

**24** "May the LORD bless you and keep you safe.

**25** May the LORD look at you with kindness and be good to you.

**26** May the LORD look at you with favor and give you peace."'

**27** Thus the priests will put my name on the people of Israel, and I will bless them."

**3** They brought their offerings to the LORD in front of the tabernacle. They brought 6 covered carts and 12 oxen. Each 2 leaders gave 1 cart, and each leader gave 1 ox.

**89** Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD. There he heard the voice of the LORD. The voice spoke to him from above the cover of the ark of the Testimony. The voice came from between the 2 cherubim. Thus the LORD spoke to Moses.


## Chapter 8

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to Aaron. Tell him, 'When you light the 7 lamps, they must give light to the area in front of the lampstand.'"

**3** Aaron did this. He put the lamps so that they gave light to the area in front of the lampstand, as the LORD commanded Moses.

**4** The lampstand was of hammered gold, from its base to its flowers. Moses made the lampstand from the design that the LORD showed him.

**5** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**6** "Take the Levites from among the people of Israel and make them clean.

**7** Do this to make them clean. Put water for purification on them. Tell them to shave all their bodies and wash their clothes. Thus they will make themselves clean.

**8** Then they must take a young bull and its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil. You must take a second young bull for a sin offering.

**9** Bring the Levites in front of the Tent of Meeting. Bring all the people of Israel together.

**10** Bring the Levites in front of the LORD. The people of Israel must put their hands on the Levites.

**11** Aaron must give the Levites to the LORD as a wave offering from the people of Israel. Thus the Levites will be ready to do the work of the LORD.

**12** The Levites must put their hands on the heads of the bulls. Offer 1 bull as a sin offering and 1 bull as a burnt offering to the LORD. This makes atonement for the Levites.

**13** Put the Levites in front of Aaron and his sons. Give the Levites to the LORD as a wave offering.

**14** Thus you will separate the Levites from the other people of Israel. The Levites will be mine.

**15** After this, the Levites can go in and do the work at the Tent of Meeting. You must make them clean and give them as a wave offering.

**16** The people of Israel give the Levites completely to me. I take the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel.

**17** All the firstborn in Israel are mine, both men and animals. I killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. On that day I made the firstborn of Israel holy for myself.

**18** I take the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel.

**19** I give the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons. The Levites will do the work for the people of Israel at the Tent of Meeting. They will make atonement for the people of Israel. Thus no disease will hit the people of Israel when they come near the holy place."

**20** Moses, Aaron and all the people of Israel did to the Levites all that the LORD commanded Moses about them.

**21** The Levites made themselves clean and washed their clothes. Aaron gave them as a wave offering in front of the LORD. Aaron made atonement for them to make them clean.

**22** After this, the Levites went in to do their work at the Tent of Meeting. Aaron and his sons supervised them. The people did to the Levites as the LORD commanded Moses.

**23** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**24** "This is the rule for the Levites. Men who are 25 years old or more must start to do the work at the Tent of Meeting.

**25** At the age of 50 years, they must stop their usual work. They must not work any more.

**26** But they can help their fellow Levites to guard the Tent of Meeting. They must not do the usual work. This is how you must give the Levites their work."

## Chapter 9

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai. This was in the 1st month of the 2nd year after the people came out of Egypt. The LORD said,

**2** "The people of Israel must keep the Passover at the correct time.

**3** Keep it at the correct time, in the evening of the 14th day of this month. Obey all its rules and its ceremonies."

**4** Thus Moses told the people of Israel to keep the Passover.

**5** They kept the Passover in the desert of Sinai, in the evening of the 14th day of the 1st month. The people of Israel did all that the LORD commanded Moses.

**6** But some men were unclean because they touched a dead body. Thus they could not keep the Passover on that day. On that day they came to Moses and Aaron.

**7** The men said to Moses, "We are unclean because we touched a dead body. But why must we not give our offering to the LORD at the correct time with the other people of Israel?"

**8** Moses said to them, "Wait. I will find out what the LORD commands about you."

**9** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**10** "Tell the people of Israel, 'You or your descendants can be unclean because of a dead body. Or you can be on a long journey. But you can still keep the Passover to the LORD.

**11** Keep it in the evening of the 14th day of the 2nd month. Eat the lamb with bread without yeast and with bitter herbs.

**12** Do not keep any of it until the morning. Do not break any of its bones. Obey all the rules of the Passover.

**13** But a man can be clean and not on a journey, and he does not keep the Passover. You must remove that person from his people. He did not give the offering to the LORD at the correct time. Thus he will be guilty of his sin.

**14** A foreigner who lives among you can keep the Passover to the LORD. He must obey the rules and the ceremonies of the Passover. Use the same rules for the foreigner and for the native Israelite.'"

**15** On the day that Moses put up the tabernacle, the cloud covered it. This was the tent of the Testimony. From the evening until the morning, the cloud above the tabernacle looked like fire.

**16** It was always like this. The cloud covered the tabernacle during the day, and it looked like fire during the night.

**17** When the cloud moved up from the tent, the people of Israel moved out. Where the cloud stopped, the people of Israel camped.

**18** The people of Israel moved out when the LORD commanded. They camped when the LORD commanded. While the cloud stayed above the tabernacle, they stayed in their camp.

**19** Sometimes the cloud stayed above the tabernacle for many days. Then the people of Israel obeyed the LORD and did not move out.

**20** Sometimes the cloud stayed above the tabernacle only for a few days. The people stayed in their camp when the LORD commanded. They moved out when the LORD commanded.

**21** Sometimes the cloud stayed only from the evening until the morning. When the cloud moved up in the morning, they moved out. During the day or the night, when the cloud moved up, they moved out.

**22** The cloud could stay above the tabernacle for 2 days, 1 month or 1 year. While it stayed, the people of Israel stayed in their camp and did not move out. But when the cloud moved up, they moved out.

**23** They camped when the LORD commanded, and they moved out when the LORD commanded. They obeyed the LORD as he commanded through Moses.

## Chapter 10

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Make 2 trumpets of hammered silver. Use them to call the people together and to tell the camps to move out.

**3** When the priests blow both trumpets, all the people must come to you at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

**4** If the priests blow only 1 trumpet, the leaders must come to you. They are the heads of the clans of Israel.

**5** When you blow a loud signal, the camps on the east side must move out.

**6** When you blow a loud signal the 2nd time, the camps on the south side must move out. The loud signal tells the camps to move out.

**7** To call the people together, blow the trumpets, but do not blow a loud signal.

**8** The priests, who are the sons of Aaron, must blow the trumpets. This is a permanent rule for you and for all your generations.

**9** You will go to war in your land against an enemy who attacks you. Then blow a loud signal with the trumpets. The LORD your God will remember you, and he will save you from your enemies.

**10** Also blow the trumpets at your happy times, at your festivals and at the start of each month. Blow them over your burnt offerings and your peace offerings. They will be a reminder of you in front of your God. I am the LORD your God."

**11** On the 20th day of the 2nd month of the 2nd year, the cloud moved up from the tabernacle of the Testimony.

**12** Then the people of Israel moved out from the desert of Sinai. They went from place to place until the cloud stopped in the desert of Paran.

**13** This was the first time that they moved out as the LORD commanded through Moses.

**14** The divisions of the camp of Judah went first, with their flag. Nahshon the son of Amminadab was the leader of the army of Judah.

**15** Nethanel the son of Zuar was the leader of the tribe of Issachar.

**16** Eliab the son of Helon was the leader of the tribe of Zebulun.

**17** Then the Levites took down the tabernacle. The Gershonites and the Merarites carried it and moved out.

**18** Next, the divisions of the camp of Reuben moved out, with their flag. Elizur the son of Shedeur was the leader of the army of Reuben.

**19** Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Simeon.

**20** Eliasaph the son of Deuel was the leader of the tribe of Gad.

**21** Then the Kohathites moved out. They carried the holy things. The other Levites put up the tabernacle before the Kohathites arrived.

**22** Next, the divisions of the camp of Ephraim moved out, with their flag. Elishama the son of Ammihud was the leader of the army of Ephraim.

**23** Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur was the leader of the tribe of Manasseh.

**24** Abidan the son of Gideoni was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin.

**25** Last, the divisions of the camp of Dan moved out, with their flag. They guarded the rear of all the camps. Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the army of Dan.

**26** Pagiel the son of Ocran was the leader of the tribe of Asher.

**27** Ahira the son of Enan was the leader of the tribe of Naphtali.

**28** This was the order in which the divisions of the people of Israel moved out.

**29** Hobab was the son of Reuel the Midianite. Reuel was the father-in-law of Moses. Moses said to Hobab, "We are on our journey to the place that the LORD promised to give us. Come with us, and we will be good to you. The LORD promised good things to Israel."

**30** But Hobab said to Moses, "I will not go. I will go back to my own land and to my own family."

**31** Moses said, "Please do not leave us. You know where we can camp in the desert. You can be our guide.

**32** If you come with us, we will share with you all the good things that the LORD gives us."

**33** Thus they moved out from the mountain of the LORD and went for 3 days. The ark of the covenant of the LORD went in front of them during the 3 days. It went to find a place for them to rest.

**34** During the day, the cloud of the LORD was above them when they moved out from the camp.

**35** When the ark moved out, Moses said, "Rise up, LORD. Make your enemies run in all directions. Make the people who hate you run away from you."

**36** When the ark stopped, Moses said, "LORD, come back to the many thousands of people of Israel."

## Chapter 11

**1** The people complained about their problems, and the LORD heard them. The LORD became angry. The fire of the LORD burned among them and destroyed some areas at the edge of the camp.

**2** The people called to Moses for help. Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire stopped.

**3** Thus Moses called the name of that place Taberah, because the fire of the LORD burned among them.

**4** Some foreigners among the people of Israel started to want other food very much. The people of Israel also started to cry again. They said, "We want meat to eat.

**5** We remember the fish that we ate in Egypt at no cost. We also remember the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions and the garlic.

**6** But now we have no strength. We see nothing except this manna."

**7** The manna was like coriander seed. Its color was like the color of resin.

**8** The people went out and collected it. They crushed it with stones or they pounded it in a bowl. They cooked it in pots and made it into flat bread. It tasted like bread that people cook with olive oil.

**9** At night the dew came down on the camp. The manna also came down with the dew.

**10** Moses heard the people of all the families cry at the entrances of their tents. The LORD became very angry, and Moses was also unhappy.

**11** Moses said to the LORD, "Why do you cause problems for your servant? Why are you not pleased with me? Why do you put the load of all these people on me?

**12** I did not give birth to all these people. I am not their father. But you tell me to carry them as a nurse carries a baby. You tell me to carry them to the land that you promised to their ancestors.

**13** Where can I get meat for all these people? They cry to me and say, 'Give us meat to eat.'

**14** I cannot carry all these people alone. The load is too heavy for me.

**15** If you treat me like this, please kill me now. If you are happy with me, do not let me see more of my trouble."

**16** The LORD said to Moses, "Bring me 70 of the elders of Israel. They must be men that you know as leaders and officers of the people. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting. Tell them to stand there with you.

**17** I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put the Spirit on them. They will help you carry the load of the people. Then you will not carry it alone.

**18** Tell the people, 'Make yourselves holy for tomorrow. Then you will eat meat. The LORD heard you cry. You said, "We want meat to eat. Our life in Egypt was good." Thus the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat it.

**19** You will eat it for more than 1 day, 2 days, 5 days, 10 days or 20 days.

**20** You will eat it for a full month. You will eat it until it comes out of your nose and you hate it. This will occur because you refused the LORD, who is among you. You cried in front of him and said, "Why did we leave Egypt?"'"

**21** But Moses said, "There are 600,000 men on foot among these people. But you say, 'I will give them meat to eat for a full month.'

**22** If we kill all the flocks and herds, that will not be sufficient for them. If we catch all the fish in the sea, that will not be sufficient for them."

**23** The LORD said to Moses, "My power is not too small. Now you will see if my words come true or not."

**24** Thus Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD. He brought together 70 of the elders of the people. He put them around the tent.

**25** Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to Moses. He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put the Spirit on the 70 elders. When the Spirit came on them, they spoke as prophets. But they did not do this again.

**26** But 2 of the men stayed in the camp. Their names were Eldad and Medad. Their names were on the list of elders, but they did not go out to the tent. The Spirit came on them also, and they spoke as prophets in the camp.

**27** A young man ran and told Moses. He said, "Eldad and Medad speak as prophets in the camp."

**28** Joshua the son of Nun was the helper of Moses since his youth. Joshua said, "Moses, my lord, stop them."

**29** But Moses said to him, "Are you jealous for me? I want all the people of the LORD to be prophets. I want the LORD to put his Spirit on all of them."

**30** Then Moses and the elders of Israel went back to the camp.

**31** Then the LORD sent a wind. The wind brought quail from the sea. The quail came down all around the camp. They covered the ground for the distance of 1 day of travel on each side. They were approximately 2 cubits deep on the ground.

**32** All that day, all that night and all the next day, the people collected the quail. No person collected less than 10 homers. The people put the quail all around the camp to dry them.

**33** But while the people still had the meat in their mouths, the LORD became angry with them. Before they finished the meat, the LORD hit the people with a very bad disease.

**34** Thus the people called that place Kibroth Hattaavah. They called it this name because they buried there the people who wanted meat too much.

**35** From Kibroth Hattaavah the people went to Hazeroth, and they stayed at Hazeroth.

## Chapter 12

**1** Miriam and Aaron started to speak against Moses because of his wife. She was from Cush, and Moses married her.

**2** They said, "The LORD does not speak only through Moses. He speaks through us also." The LORD heard what they said.

**3** Moses was a very humble man. He was more humble than all the other men on earth.

**4** Immediately the LORD spoke to Moses, Aaron and Miriam. He said, "All 3 of you, come out to the Tent of Meeting." Thus the 3 of them went out.

**5** The LORD came down in a column of cloud. He stood at the entrance of the tent and called Aaron and Miriam. Both of them came forward.

**6** The LORD said, "Listen to my words. When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, show myself to him in visions. I speak to him in dreams.

**7** But I do not do this with my servant Moses. He is loyal in all my house.

**8** I speak with Moses face to face. I speak clearly, and not in riddles. He sees the form of the LORD. Thus you must be afraid to speak against my servant Moses."

**9** The LORD was angry with them, and he left.

**10** When the cloud moved away from the tent, Miriam had a skin disease (leprosy). Her skin was as white as snow. Aaron looked at Miriam and saw that she had the disease.

**11** Aaron said to Moses, "My lord, please do not punish us for this sin. We were foolish, and we sinned.

**12** Do not let her be like a baby that is dead at birth, with half of its body destroyed."

**13** Moses called to the LORD. He said, "God, please make her well."

**14** The LORD said to Moses, "If her father spit in her face, she must feel shame for 7 days. Thus send her outside the camp for 7 days. After that, she can come back."

**15** Thus the people sent Miriam outside the camp for 7 days. The people did not move out until Miriam came back.

**16** After this, the people moved out from Hazeroth. They camped in the desert of Paran.

## Chapter 13

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Send men to explore the land of Canaan. I give this land to the people of Israel. Send 1 man from each tribe of their ancestors. Each man must be a leader of his tribe."

**3** Thus Moses sent them from the desert of Paran, as the LORD commanded. All these men were leaders of the people of Israel.

**4** These were their names. From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur.

**5** From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori.

**6** From the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.

**7** From the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph.

**8** From the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Nun.

**9** From the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu.

**10** From the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi.

**11** From the tribe of Joseph, which is the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi.

**12** From the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.

**13** From the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael.

**14** From the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi.

**15** From the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi.

**16** These are the names of the men that Moses sent to explore the land. Moses gave Hoshea the son of Nun the name Joshua.

**17** Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan. He said to them, "Go up through the Negev. Then go up into the hills.

**18** Look at the land and find out what it is like. Find out if the people who live there are strong or weak. Find out if they are few or many.

**19** Find out if the land where they live is good or bad. Find out if their towns are camps or cities with walls.

**20** Find out if the soil is rich or poor. Find out if there are trees in the land. Be brave, and bring back some of the fruit of the land." It was the time of the first ripe grapes.

**21** Thus the men went up and explored the land. They went from the desert of Zin to Rehob, near Lebo Hamath.

**22** They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai lived there. They were descendants of Anak. People built Hebron 7 years before they built Zoan in Egypt.

**23** The men came to the Valley of Eshcol. There they cut off a branch with 1 bunch of grapes. 2 men carried it on a pole between them. They also brought some pomegranates and figs.

**24** The people called that place the Valley of Eshcol. They called it this name because of the bunch of grapes that the men of Israel cut there.

**25** After 40 days, the men came back from the land.

**26** They came back to Moses, to Aaron and to all the people of Israel at Kadesh in the desert of Paran. They told them what they found. They showed them the fruit of the land.

**27** They told Moses, "We went into the land where you sent us. It is a very rich land, full of milk and honey. This is its fruit.

**28** But the people who live there are strong. The cities have walls and they are very large. We also saw the descendants of Anak there.

**29** The Amalekites live in the Negev. The Hittites, the Jebusites and the Amorites live in the hills. The Canaanites live near the sea and along the Jordan River."

**30** Then Caleb told the people near Moses to be quiet. He said, "We must go up now and take the land. We can certainly defeat them."

**31** But the men who went with him said, "We cannot attack those people. They are stronger than we are."

**32** These men gave the people of Israel a bad report about the land that they explored. They said, "The land that we explored destroys the people who live there. All the people that we saw there are very tall.

**33** We saw the giants (Nephilim) there. The descendants of Anak come from the giants. We felt as small as grasshoppers, and the giants thought the same about us."

## Chapter 14

**1** That night all the people of Israel shouted and cried loudly.

**2** All the people of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron. All the people said to them, "We want to be dead in the land of Egypt. Or we want to be dead in this desert.

**3** Why does the LORD bring us to this land? Our enemies will kill us with the sword. They will take our wives and our children. It is better for us to go back to Egypt."

**4** They said to one another, "We must choose a leader and go back to Egypt."

**5** Then Moses and Aaron bowed down with their faces to the ground in front of all the people of Israel.

**6** Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh tore their clothes. They were 2 of the men who explored the land.

**7** They said to all the people of Israel, "The land that we went through and explored is a very good land.

**8** If the LORD is happy with us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us. It is a very rich land, full of milk and honey.

**9** Do not rebel against the LORD. Do not be afraid of the people of the land. We will defeat them easily. Nothing protects them, but the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them."

**10** But all the people said, "Throw stones at them until they die." Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the Tent of Meeting to all the people of Israel.

**11** The LORD said to Moses, "How long will these people refuse to respect me? I did many miracles among them. How long will they refuse to believe me?

**12** I will hit them with disease and destroy them. Then I will make you into a nation that is larger and stronger than they are."

**13** But Moses said to the LORD, "The Egyptians will hear about it. With your power you brought these people out from among them.

**14** The Egyptians will tell the people who live in this land. Those people already heard that you, LORD, are with these people. They know that the people see you face to face. They know that your cloud stays above them. They know that you go in front of them in a column of cloud during the day and in a column of fire at night.

**15** If you kill all these people at one time, the nations will hear about it. They will say,

**16** 'The LORD was not able to bring these people into the land that he promised them. Thus he killed them in the desert.'

**17** Now please show your great power, Lord. Do what you said.

**18** You said, 'The LORD is slow to become angry. He has much love and he forgives sin and rebellion. But he does not let the guilty go without punishment. He punishes the children for the sin of the parents, to the 3rd and 4th generation.'

**19** Your love is very great. Please forgive the sin of these people, as you forgave them from the time when they left Egypt until now."

**20** The LORD said, "I forgive them, as you asked.

**21** But as I live, and as the glory of the LORD will fill all the earth, I tell you this.

**22** All these men saw my glory and the miracles that I did in Egypt and in the desert. But they tested me 10 times and they did not obey me.

**23** Thus they will not see the land that I promised to their ancestors. None of the people who refused to respect me will see it.

**24** But my servant Caleb has a different spirit, and he obeys me completely. Thus I will bring him into the land that he explored. His descendants will own it.

**25** The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valleys. Tomorrow, turn around and go into the desert, along the road to the Red Sea."

**26** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**27** "How long will these evil people complain against me? I hear the complaints of the people of Israel against me.

**28** Tell them, 'As I live, the LORD says, I will do to you the things that you said.

**29** You will die in this desert. Moses counted all of you who are 20 years old or more. All of you who complained against me will die.

**30** Thus none of you will go into the land that I promised to give you as your home. Only Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun will go into it.

**31** You said that your enemies will take your children. But I will bring your children into the land. They will enjoy the land that you refused.

**32** But you will die in this desert.

**33** Your children will be shepherds in this desert for 40 years. They will suffer because you were not loyal to me. They will suffer until the last of you dies in the desert.

**34** You explored the land for 40 days. Thus you will suffer for your sins for 40 years, 1 year for each day. Then you will know what it is like when I am against you.'

**35** I, the LORD, said this. I will certainly do these things to all these evil people who came together against me. They will all die in this desert."

**36** Moses sent some men to explore the land. They came back and made all the people complain against Moses, because they gave a bad report about the land.

**37** Those men who gave the bad report about the land died from a disease in front of the LORD.

**38** But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh did not die. They were 2 of the men who went to explore the land.

**39** Moses told these words to all the people of Israel. The people were very sad.

**40** Early the next morning, they went up to the top of the hill country. They said, "We sinned. Now we are ready to go up to the place that the LORD promised."

**41** But Moses said, "Why do you disobey the command of the LORD? You will not be successful.

**42** Do not go up, because the LORD is not with you. Your enemies will defeat you.

**43** The Amalekites and the Canaanites will fight you there, and they will kill you with the sword. You turned away from the LORD, thus the LORD will not be with you."

**44** But they went up to the top of the hill country without permission. But Moses and the ark of the covenant of the LORD did not leave the camp.

**45** Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down. They attacked the people of Israel and defeated them. They chased them as far as Hormah.

## Chapter 15

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'Soon you will come into the land that I give to you. You will live there.

**3** You will make offerings by fire to the LORD from the cattle or from the flock. These can be burnt offerings or sacrifices for a promise (vow). They can be free offerings or offerings at your festivals. They make a pleasant smell for the LORD.

**4** The person who brings his offering to the LORD must also bring a grain offering. The grain offering is 1/10 of an ephah of fine flour. Mix the flour with 1/4 of a hin of oil.

**5** For each lamb, prepare 1/4 of a hin of wine as a drink offering. Give the wine with the burnt offering or the sacrifice.

**6** For a ram, prepare a grain offering of 2/10 of an ephah of fine flour. Mix the flour with 1/3 of a hin of oil.

**7** For the drink offering, offer 1/3 of a hin of wine. This makes a pleasant smell for the LORD.

**8** Sometimes you will prepare a young bull as a burnt offering, as a sacrifice for a vow, or as a peace offering to the LORD.

**9** Then bring a grain offering with the bull. The grain offering is 3/10 of an ephah of fine flour mixed with 1/2 of a hin of oil.

**10** Also bring 1/2 of a hin of wine as a drink offering. This is an offering by fire. It makes a pleasant smell for the LORD.

**11** Do these things for each bull, each ram, each lamb, or each young goat.

**12** Prepare a set of these offerings for each animal that you offer.

**13** Each person whose mother gave birth to him as an Israelite must do these things in this way. He must do them when he makes an offering by fire with a pleasant smell for the LORD.

**14** A foreigner can live with you, or another person can live among you in the future. If he makes an offering by fire with a pleasant smell for the LORD, he must do the same as you.

**15** The community must have 1 rule for you and for the foreigner who lives with you. This rule continues for all time in all your generations. The foreigner is the same as you in front of the LORD.

**16** You and the foreigner who lives with you must have 1 law and 1 rule.'"

**17** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**18** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'Soon you will come into the land where I take you.

**19** When you eat the food of that land, you must give a special offering (a heave offering) to the LORD.

**20** Give a loaf from the first of your dough as a heave offering. Give it in the same way as the heave offering from the floor where you separate the grain.

**21** In all your generations, give to the LORD a heave offering from the first of your dough.

**22** Sometimes you will make a mistake. You will not obey all these commands that the LORD gave to Moses.

**23** You will not obey all that the LORD commanded you through Moses. These commands start on the day that the LORD gave them, and they continue for all your generations.

**24** If the community makes this mistake and does not know about it, then all the community must make an offering. They must offer 1 young bull as a burnt offering with a pleasant smell for the LORD. They must also give the correct grain offering and drink offering. And they must offer 1 male goat as a sin offering.

**25** The priest must make a payment for sin (atonement) for all the community of Israel. Then the LORD will forgive them, because it was a mistake. They must bring their offering by fire to the LORD. They must also bring their sin offering to the LORD for their mistake.

**26** The LORD will forgive all the community of Israel. He will also forgive the foreigners who live among them. All the people made the mistake together.

**27** If 1 person sins by mistake, then he must bring a female goat that is 1 year old as a sin offering.

**28** The priest must make atonement in front of the LORD for the person who sins by mistake. Then the LORD will forgive that person.

**29** You must have 1 law for each person who sins by mistake. This law is for the Israelite and for the foreigner who lives among the Israelites.

**30** But a person can sin on purpose. This person can be an Israelite or a foreigner. This person insults the LORD. You must remove this person from among his people.

**31** He hated the word of the LORD, and he did not obey the command of the LORD. You must remove this person completely. He is responsible for his sin.'"

**32** While the people of Israel were in the desert, they found a man who picked up wood on the Sabbath day.

**33** The people who found him took him to Moses, Aaron, and all the community.

**34** They kept the man as a prisoner, because they did not know what to do with him.

**35** Then the LORD said to Moses, "You must kill the man. All the community must throw stones at him outside the camp."

**36** So all the community took the man outside the camp. They threw stones at him until he died. They did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**37** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**38** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them to make tassels on the corners of their clothes in all their generations. They must put a blue cord on each tassel.

**39** When you look at the tassels, you will remember all the commands of the LORD. Then you will obey the commands. Do not follow the desires of your heart and of your eyes. These desires cause you to be not loyal to the LORD.

**40** Thus you will remember all my commands and obey them. You will be holy to your God.

**41** I am the LORD your God. I brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God."

## Chapter 16

**1** Korah was the son of Izhar. Izhar was the son of Kohath, and Kohath was the son of Levi. Korah took some men with him. Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, were with him. These 3 men were from the tribe of Reuben.

**2** These men stood up against Moses. 250 men of Israel were with them. These men were leaders of the community. They were famous men in the assembly.

**3** They came together against Moses and Aaron. They said to them, "You take too much power. All the community is holy, and the LORD is among the people. Why do you put yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?"

**4** When Moses heard this, he bowed down with his face to the ground.

**5** Then he spoke to Korah and to all his group. He said, "Tomorrow morning the LORD will show who is his. He will show who is holy. He will let that person come near to him. The LORD will let the person whom he chooses come near to him.

**6** Korah, you and all your group must do this. Take incense pans (censers).

**7** Tomorrow put fire and incense in the censers in front of the LORD. The man whom the LORD chooses is the holy man. You sons of Levi take too much power!"

**8** Moses also said to Korah, "Listen, you sons of Levi!

**9** The God of Israel separated you from the community of Israel. He brought you near to himself. You do the work at the tabernacle of the LORD. You stand in front of the community and serve them. Is this not sufficient for you?

**10** God brought you and all your brothers, the sons of Levi, near to him. Now do you also try to get the work of the priests?

**11** Thus you and all your group come together against the LORD. Aaron is not important. Why do you complain against him?"

**12** Then Moses sent a message to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. But they said, "We will not come!

**13** You brought us out of Egypt, a land that has much milk and honey. You brought us here to kill us in the desert. Is that not sufficient? Now you also try to rule us!

**14** You did not bring us into a land that has much milk and honey. You did not give us fields and vineyards. Do you think that you can trick these men? We will not come!"

**15** Moses became very angry. He said to the LORD, "Do not accept their offering. I did not take 1 donkey from them. I did not hurt any of them."

**16** Moses said to Korah, "Tomorrow you and all your group must come in front of the LORD. You, your men, and Aaron must come.

**17** Each man must take his censer and put incense in it. Each man must bring his censer in front of the LORD. There will be 250 censers. You and Aaron must also bring your censers."

**18** So each man took his censer. They put fire and incense in the censers. They stood at the entrance of the tabernacle with Moses and Aaron.

**19** Korah brought all the community together against Moses and Aaron at the entrance of the tabernacle. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the community.

**20** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**21** "Move away from this community. I will destroy them immediately."

**22** But Moses and Aaron bowed down with their faces to the ground. They said, "O God, you are the God who gives life to all people. Only 1 man sins. Will you be angry with all the community?"

**23** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**24** "Tell the community, 'Move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.'"

**25** Moses stood up and went to Dathan and Abiram. The leaders (elders) of Israel followed him.

**26** Moses said to the community, "Please move away from the tents of these bad men! Do not touch anything that is theirs. If you touch their things, God will destroy you because of their sins."

**27** So the people moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents. Their wives, their sons, and their small children stood with them.

**28** Moses said, "Now you will know that the LORD sent me to do all these things. I did not do them from my own ideas.

**29** These men can die in the usual way that all people die. If this occurs, then the LORD did not send me.

**30** But the LORD can do a new thing. The ground can open and swallow these men and all their things. They can go down alive into the grave. If this occurs, then you will know that these men insulted the LORD."

**31** Moses stopped and said no more words. Then the ground under these men split open.

**32** The ground opened and swallowed them and their families. It swallowed all the men of Korah and all their things.

**33** They and all their things went down alive into the grave. The ground closed over them. They died, and they were no longer in the community.

**34** All the people of Israel who were near them heard their cries. These people ran away. They said, "The ground will swallow us too!"

**35** Then fire came out from the LORD. The fire destroyed the 250 men who offered the incense.

**36** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**37** "Tell Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, to take the censers out of the fire. Tell him to throw the hot coals far away. The censers are holy.

**38** These men sinned and lost their lives. Make the censers of these men into thin metal sheets. Use the sheets as a cover for the altar. The men offered the censers in front of the LORD, thus the censers are holy. They will be a sign to the people of Israel."

**39** So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers. The men whom the fire burned used these censers to offer incense. The workers made the censers into thin sheets to cover the altar.

**40** The sheets are a reminder to the people of Israel. Only the descendants of Aaron can come near to offer incense in front of the LORD. Other persons must not do this. If they do, they will become the same as Korah and his group. Eleazar did as the LORD told him through Moses.

**41** But on the next day, all the community of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron. They said, "You killed the people of the LORD!"

**42** The community came together against Moses and Aaron. Then the people looked at the tabernacle. The cloud covered the tabernacle, and the glory of the LORD appeared.

**43** Moses and Aaron went to the front of the tabernacle.

**44** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**45** "Move away from this community. I will destroy them immediately." Moses and Aaron bowed down with their faces to the ground.

**46** Moses said to Aaron, "Take your censer. Put fire from the altar in it, and put incense on it. Go quickly to the community and make atonement for them. The LORD is angry. The disease (plague) started."

**47** Aaron did as Moses told him. He ran into the middle of the community. The plague already started among the people. Aaron put on the incense and made atonement for the people.

**48** He stood between the dead people and the people who were alive. Then the plague stopped.

**49** 14,700 people died in the plague. This number does not include the people who died because of Korah.

**50** Then Aaron went back to Moses at the entrance of the tabernacle. The plague stopped.

## Chapter 17

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Speak to the people of Israel. Get 12 sticks (rods) from them. Get 1 rod from the leader of each tribe. Write the name of each leader on his rod.

**3** Write the name of Aaron on the rod of Levi. There must be 1 rod for the leader of each tribe.

**4** Put the rods in the tabernacle in front of the box of the law (the testimony). I meet with you at that place.

**5** The rod of the man whom I choose will grow flowers. Thus I will stop the complaints of the people of Israel against you."

**6** So Moses spoke to the people of Israel. Each of their leaders gave him a rod. Each tribe gave 1 rod, thus there were 12 rods. The rod of Aaron was among the rods.

**7** Moses put the rods in front of the LORD in the tabernacle of the testimony.

**8** On the next day, Moses went into the tabernacle. The rod of Aaron for the tribe of Levi had buds on it. The rod grew buds and flowers, and it made almonds.

**9** Moses brought out all the rods from in front of the LORD. He showed them to all the people of Israel. The leaders looked at the rods, and each man took his rod.

**10** The LORD said to Moses, "Put the rod of Aaron back in front of the testimony. Keep it there as a sign for the people who do not obey. Thus you will stop their complaints against me, and they will not die."

**11** Moses did as the LORD commanded him.

**12** The people of Israel said to Moses, "We will die! We will all die!

**13** Each person who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD will die. Will all of us die?"

## Chapter 18

**1** The LORD said to Aaron, "You, your sons, and your family are responsible for sins against the holy place (sanctuary). You and your sons are responsible for sins against your work as priests.

**2** Bring with you your relatives from the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father. They will join you and help you. But you and your sons must serve in front of the tabernacle of the testimony.

**3** The Levites must obey your orders and do the work of the tabernacle. But they must not go near the holy equipment of the sanctuary or near the altar. If they do, they and you will die.

**4** The Levites must join you. They must do all the work of the tabernacle. No other person can come near you.

**5** You must do the work of the sanctuary and of the altar. Then I will not be angry with the people of Israel again.

**6** I took your relatives, the Levites, from among the people of Israel. I give them to you as a gift. They are for the LORD. They do the work of the tabernacle.
