**7** But only you and your sons can do the work of the priests. Only you can do the work at the altar and behind the curtain. I give you the work of the priests as a gift. You must kill any other person who comes near."

**8** Then the LORD said to Aaron, "I give you the responsibility for my heave offerings. I give you all the holy gifts of the people of Israel. I give them to you and to your sons as your part. This rule continues for all time.

**9** You will get part of the most holy offerings that the priests do not burn. You will get their grain offerings, their sin offerings, and their guilt offerings. These offerings that they give to me are most holy. They are for you and for your sons.

**10** Eat them as most holy things. Each male can eat them. They are holy to you.

**11** These things are also yours: the heave offerings and all the wave offerings of the people of Israel. I give them to you, to your sons, and to your daughters. This rule continues for all time. Each person in your family who is clean can eat them.

**12** I give you all the best oil, the best new wine, and the best grain. These are the first part of the harvest (firstfruits) that the people give to the LORD.

**13** All the first fruit that grows in the land and that they bring to the LORD will be yours. Each person in your family who is clean can eat it.

**14** All the things in Israel that the people give completely to the LORD will be yours.

**15** The first male child of each mother, human or animal, that the people bring to the LORD is yours. But you must buy back (redeem) each firstborn son. You must also redeem each firstborn male of an unclean animal.

**16** Redeem them when they are 1 month old. The price is 5 shekels of silver. Use the shekel of the sanctuary, which weighs 20 gerahs.

**17** But do not redeem a firstborn cow, a firstborn sheep, or a firstborn goat. They are holy. Put their blood on the altar. Burn their fat as an offering by fire. This makes a pleasant smell for the LORD.

**18** Their meat is yours. It is the same as the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh. These are yours.

**19** I give you all the heave offerings of the holy things that the people of Israel give to the LORD. I give them to you, to your sons, and to your daughters. This rule continues for all time. It is a permanent covenant (a covenant of salt) in front of the LORD. It is for you and for your descendants."

**20** The LORD said to Aaron, "You will not own land in Israel. You will not have a part of the land among the people. I am your part. I am what you get among the people of Israel.

**21** I give the Levites 1/10 (the tithe) of all things in Israel. This is their payment for the work that they do at the tabernacle.

**22** From now on, the other people of Israel must not go near the tabernacle. If they do, they will be guilty of sin and they will die.

**23** Only the Levites must do the work of the tabernacle. They are responsible for sins against it. This rule continues for all time in all your generations. The Levites will not own land among the people of Israel.

**24** The people of Israel give the tithe as a heave offering to the LORD. I give this tithe to the Levites as their part. Thus I tell the Levites, 'You will not own land among the people of Israel.'"

**25** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**26** "Speak to the Levites. Tell them, 'You will get the tithe from the people of Israel. I give it to you as your part. Then you must give 1/10 of that tithe as a heave offering to the LORD.

**27** The LORD will accept your heave offering as your offering. It is the same as grain from the floor where you separate the grain, or wine from the winepress.

**28** Thus you also must give a heave offering to the LORD from all the tithes that you get from the people of Israel. Give this part of the LORD to Aaron the priest.

**29** From all the gifts that you get, you must give a heave offering to the LORD. Give the best and the holiest part.'

**30** Tell the Levites, 'When you give the best part, the LORD will accept the other part for you. It is the same as grain from the floor where you separate the grain, and wine from the winepress.

**31** You and your families can eat the rest in any place. It is your payment for your work at the tabernacle.

**32** If you give the best part to the LORD, you will not be guilty of sin because of this food. But do not make the holy gifts of the people of Israel unclean. If you do, you will die.'"

## Chapter 19

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**2** "This is a rule of the law that the LORD commands. Tell the people of Israel to bring you a red cow (heifer). The heifer must have no defect. It must never carry a yoke.

**3** Give the heifer to Eleazar the priest. He must take it outside the camp. A man must kill it in front of Eleazar.

**4** Eleazar the priest must put some of the blood on his finger. He must sprinkle the blood 7 times toward the front of the tabernacle.

**5** Then a man must burn the heifer while Eleazar watches. He must burn its skin, its meat, its blood, and its dung.

**6** The priest must take cedar wood, hyssop, and red cloth. He must throw these things into the fire that burns the heifer.

**7** Then the priest must wash his clothes and his body in water. After this, he can come into the camp. But he will be unclean until the evening.

**8** The man who burns the heifer must also wash his clothes and his body in water. He will be unclean until the evening.

**9** A man who is clean must collect the ashes of the heifer. He must put them in a clean place outside the camp. The community of Israel must keep the ashes. They will use the ashes to make the water for purification. This water removes sin.

**10** The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes. He will be unclean until the evening. This rule continues for all time. It is for the people of Israel and for the foreigners who live among them.

**11** A person who touches a dead human body will be unclean for 7 days.

**12** He must make himself clean with the water on the 3rd day and on the 7th day. Then he will be clean. If he does not make himself clean on the 3rd day and on the 7th day, he will not be clean.

**13** A person who touches a dead body and does not make himself clean makes the tabernacle of the LORD unclean. You must remove that person from Israel. Nobody sprinkled the water for purification on him, thus he is unclean. He continues to be unclean.

**14** This is the law when a person dies in a tent. Each person who goes into the tent will be unclean for 7 days. Each person who is in the tent will also be unclean for 7 days.

**15** Each open container that has no cover on it is unclean.

**16** A person can be in the open fields and touch a person whom a sword killed. Or he can touch a dead body, a human bone, or a grave. Then he will be unclean for 7 days.

**17** For the unclean person, take some ashes from the burnt heifer of the sin offering. Put them in a container and add fresh water.

**18** A clean person must take hyssop and put it in the water. He must sprinkle the water on the tent, on all the containers, and on the people who were in the tent. He must also sprinkle it on the person who touched a bone, a person that someone killed, a dead body, or a grave.

**19** The clean person must sprinkle the water on the unclean person on the 3rd day and on the 7th day. On the 7th day, the unclean person must make himself clean. He must wash his clothes and his body in water. In the evening he will be clean.

**20** But an unclean person who does not make himself clean must leave the community. You must send him away. He made the sanctuary of the LORD unclean. Nobody sprinkled the water for purification on him. He is unclean.

**21** This rule continues for all time. The person who sprinkles the water for purification must wash his clothes. The person who touches the water for purification will be unclean until the evening.

**22** All that an unclean person touches will become unclean. Each person who touches that thing will be unclean until the evening."

## Chapter 20

**1** In the 1st month, all the community of Israel came into the desert of Zin. The people stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there, and the people buried her there.

**2** The community had no water. Thus the people came together against Moses and Aaron.

**3** The people argued with Moses. They said, "We wish that we died when our brothers died in front of the LORD!

**4** Why did you bring the assembly of the LORD into this desert? Do you want us and our animals to die here?

**5** Why did you bring us out of Egypt into this bad place? We cannot grow grain, figs, grapes, or pomegranates here. There is also no water to drink!"

**6** Moses and Aaron went away from the assembly to the entrance of the tabernacle. They bowed down with their faces to the ground. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to them.

**7** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**8** "Take the rod. You and your brother Aaron must bring the community together. Speak to the rock while the people watch. Then the rock will give its water. Thus you will bring water out of the rock for the community and their animals."

**9** So Moses took the rod from in front of the LORD, as the LORD commanded him.

**10** Moses and Aaron brought the community together in front of the rock. Moses said to them, "Listen, you people who do not obey! Must we bring water out of this rock for you?"

**11** Then Moses lifted his hand. He hit the rock 2 times with his rod. Much water came out. The community and their animals drank.

**12** But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "You did not trust me. You did not show my holiness to the people of Israel. Thus you will not bring this community into the land that I give them."

**13** These were the waters of Meribah. At this place the people of Israel argued with the LORD, and he showed his holiness among them.

**14** Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom. They said, "Your brother Israel says this: 'You know all the troubles that we had.

**15** Our ancestors went down into Egypt. We lived in Egypt for a long time. The Egyptians were cruel to us and to our ancestors.

**16** We called to the LORD, and he heard us. He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are at Kadesh. Kadesh is a city at the edge of your land.

**17** Please let us go through your country. We will not go through your fields or your vineyards. We will not drink water from your wells. We will stay on the King's Road. We will not turn to the right or to the left until we go through your land.'"

**18** But the king of Edom said, "You cannot go through my land. If you try, I will attack you with my army."

**19** The people of Israel said, "We will stay on the main road. If we or our animals drink your water, we will pay for it. We only want to walk through. We will do nothing more."

**20** But the king of Edom said, "You cannot go through." Then Edom came out against Israel with a large and strong army.

**21** Thus Edom did not let Israel go through its land. So Israel turned away from Edom.

**22** All the community of Israel went from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.

**23** At Mount Hor, near the border of Edom, the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

**24** "Aaron will die and go to his ancestors. He will not go into the land that I give to the people of Israel. You two did not obey my command at the waters of Meribah.

**25** Take Aaron and his son Eleazar up on Mount Hor.

**26** Remove the special clothes of Aaron and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will die there and go to his ancestors."

**27** Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up on Mount Hor while all the community watched.

**28** Moses removed the clothes of Aaron and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.

**29** All the community saw that Aaron was dead. All the people of Israel cried for Aaron for 30 days.

## Chapter 21

**1** The Canaanite king of Arad lived in the Negev, in the south. He heard that Israel came on the road to Atharim. So he fought against Israel and took some of the Israelites as prisoners.

**2** Then Israel made a promise (vow) to the LORD. The people said, "If you give these people to us, then we will completely destroy their cities."

**3** The LORD heard Israel and gave the Canaanites to them. The Israelites completely destroyed the Canaanites and their cities. Thus the people called the place Hormah.

**4** The people went from Mount Hor on the road to the Red Sea. They went around the land of Edom. On the trip, the people became impatient.

**5** The people spoke against God and against Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us out of Egypt to die in the desert? We have no bread and no water. We hate this bad food!"

**6** So the LORD sent poisonous snakes among the people. The snakes bit the people, and many Israelites died.

**7** The people came to Moses. They said, "We sinned, because we spoke against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD. Ask him to take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.

**8** The LORD said to Moses, "Make a model of a poisonous snake. Put it on a pole. Each person whom a snake bites can look at it, and he will live."

**9** So Moses made a bronze snake and put it on a pole. When a snake bit a person, that person looked at the bronze snake. Then the person lived.

**10** The people of Israel continued their trip and made their camp at Oboth.

**11** They went from Oboth and made their camp at Iye Abarim. This place is in the desert east of Moab.

**12** From there they went and made their camp in the valley of Zered.

**13** From there they went and made their camp on the other side of the Arnon River. This place is in the desert that goes into the land of the Amorites. The Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.

**14** Thus the Book of the Wars of the LORD says, "Waheb in Suphah and the valleys of the Arnon,

**15** and the slopes of the valleys that go down to the town of Ar and are next to the border of Moab."

**16** From there they went to Beer. At this well the LORD said to Moses, "Bring the people together, and I will give them water."

**17** Then Israel sang this song: "Give water, O well! Sing to the well!

**18** The leaders dug the well. The important men of the people dug it with their rods and sticks." Then the people went from the desert to Mattanah.

**19** They went from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.

**20** From Bamoth they went to the valley in the country of Moab. This valley is near the top of Mount Pisgah. From Pisgah a person can see the desert (Jeshimon).

**21** Israel sent messengers to Sihon, the king of the Amorites. They said,

**22** "Let us go through your land. We will not go into your fields or your vineyards. We will not drink water from your wells. We will stay on the King's Road until we go through your land."

**23** But Sihon did not let Israel go through his land. Sihon brought all his army together and went out into the desert against Israel. He came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.

**24** But Israel killed him with the sword. Israel took his land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River. Israel took the land as far as the land of the Ammonites. The border of the Ammonites had strong defenses.

**25** Israel took all these cities of the Amorites and lived in them. Israel lived in Heshbon and in all the villages near it.

**26** Heshbon was the city of Sihon, the king of the Amorites. Sihon fought against the previous king of Moab. Sihon took all his land as far as the Arnon River.

**27** Thus the poets say, "Come to Heshbon. Build it again. Make the city of Sihon strong again.

**28** Fire came out of Heshbon. Flames came from the city of Sihon. The fire destroyed Ar in Moab and the rulers of the hills of the Arnon.

**29** Moab, you will have much trouble! People of Chemosh, your enemies destroy you! Your god Chemosh let his sons run away. He let his daughters become prisoners of Sihon, the king of the Amorites.

**30** But we defeated the Amorites. We destroyed Heshbon as far as Dibon. We destroyed their land as far as Nophah, near Medeba."

**31** Thus Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.

**32** Moses sent men to look at the town of Jazer. The Israelites took the villages near Jazer. They forced out the Amorites who lived there.

**33** Then the Israelites turned and went up on the road to Bashan. Og, the king of Bashan, and all his army came out to fight against them at Edrei.

**34** The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of Og. I will give him, all his army, and his land to you. Do to him as you did to Sihon, the king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon."

**35** So the Israelites killed Og, his sons, and all his army. Nobody stayed alive. Then the Israelites took his land.

## Chapter 22

**1** The people of Israel continued their trip and made their camp in the plains of Moab. This place is east of the Jordan River, across from Jericho.

**2** Balak, the son of Zippor, saw all that Israel did to the Amorites.

**3** The people of Moab were very afraid of the Israelites, because there were many Israelites. The Moabites were full of fear because of the people of Israel.

**4** The Moabites said to the elders of Midian, "This large group of people will destroy all the land around us. They will be the same as a bull that eats all the grass in a field." At that time Balak, the son of Zippor, was the king of Moab.

**5** Balak sent messengers to Balaam, the son of Beor. Balaam lived at Pethor, near the Euphrates River, in the land of his people. Balak said, "A nation came out of Egypt. They cover the land, and they live near me.

**6** Please come now and curse these people for me. They are too strong for me. Then maybe I can defeat them and force them out of the land. I know that the person whom you bless gets good things. I know that the person whom you curse gets bad things."

**7** The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went to Balaam. They had money with them to pay him for magic. They told Balaam what Balak said.

**8** Balaam said to them, "Stay here tonight. I will tell you the answer that the LORD gives me." So the leaders of Moab stayed with Balaam.

**9** God came to Balaam and said, "Who are these men with you?"

**10** Balaam said to God, "Balak, the son of Zippor, the king of Moab, sent them to me. He said,

**11** 'A nation came out of Egypt. They cover the land. Come now and curse them for me. Then maybe I can fight them and force them out.'"

**12** But God said to Balaam, "Do not go with them. Do not curse these people, because I blessed them."

**13** In the morning, Balaam got up. He said to the leaders of Balak, "Go back to your country. The LORD does not let me go with you."

**14** So the leaders of Moab went back to Balak. They said, "Balaam does not agree to come with us."

**15** Then Balak sent more leaders. These leaders were more in number and more important than the first leaders.

**16** They came to Balaam and said to him, "Balak, the son of Zippor, says this: 'Please do not let anything stop you. Come to me.

**17** I will give you very great honor. I will do all that you tell me. Please come and curse these people for me.'"

**18** But Balaam said to the servants of Balak, "Balak can give me his palace full of silver and gold. But I cannot disobey the command of the LORD my God. I cannot do anything, small or large, that the LORD does not tell me.

**19** Please stay here tonight too. Then I will know what more the LORD will tell me."

**20** That night God came to Balaam. He said, "These men came to call you. Get up and go with them. But you must do only what I tell you."

**21** In the morning, Balaam got up and put a saddle on his female donkey. He went with the leaders of Moab.

**22** But God was angry because Balaam went. The angel of the LORD stood in the road to stop him. Balaam rode on his donkey, and his 2 servants were with him.

**23** The donkey saw the angel of the LORD in the road with a sword in his hand. So the donkey went off the road into a field. Balaam hit the donkey to make her go back to the road.

**24** Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between 2 vineyards. There was a wall on each side of the path.

**25** The donkey saw the angel of the LORD. She moved against the wall and pushed the foot of Balaam against the wall. So Balaam hit her again.

**26** Then the angel of the LORD went farther ahead. He stood in a narrow place. There was no space to turn to the right or to the left.

**27** The donkey saw the angel of the LORD, and she lay down under Balaam. Balaam became angry, and he hit the donkey with his stick.

**28** Then the LORD let the donkey speak. She said to Balaam, "What did I do to you? Why did you hit me these 3 times?"

**29** Balaam said to the donkey, "You made me look foolish! I wish that I had a sword in my hand. If I had a sword, I will kill you now."

**30** The donkey said to Balaam, "I am your donkey. You rode on me all your life until today. Did I ever do this to you before?" Balaam said, "No."

**31** Then the LORD let Balaam see the angel of the LORD. The angel stood in the road with a sword in his hand. Balaam bowed down with his face to the ground.

**32** The angel of the LORD said to him, "Why did you hit your donkey these 3 times? I came to stop you, because your trip is wrong in my sight.

**33** The donkey saw me and turned away from me 3 times. If she did not turn away from me, I will kill you now. But I will let the donkey live."

**34** Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I sinned. I did not know that you stood in the road against me. If you think that my trip is wrong, I will go back home."

**35** The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men. But say only what I tell you." So Balaam went with the leaders of Balak.

**36** Balak heard that Balaam came. So Balak went out to meet him at a city of Moab. This city is on the Arnon River, at the edge of the land of Moab.

**37** Balak said to Balaam, "I sent a strong request for you to come. Why did you not come to me? I can give you great honor!"

**38** Balaam said to Balak, "Now I am here. But I do not have the power to say anything that I want. I must say only the words that God puts in my mouth."

**39** Then Balaam went with Balak to Kiriath Huzoth.

**40** Balak killed cattle and sheep as sacrifices. He sent some of the meat to Balaam and to the leaders with him.

**41** In the morning, Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth Baal. From there Balaam could see a part of the people of Israel.

## Chapter 23

**1** Balaam said to Balak, "Build 7 altars for me here. Prepare 7 bulls and 7 rams for me here."

**2** Balak did as Balaam said. Balak and Balaam offered 1 bull and 1 ram on each altar.

**3** Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stay next to your burnt offering. I will go away. Maybe the LORD will come to meet me. I will tell you all that he shows me." Then Balaam went to a high place with no trees.

**4** God met Balaam. Balaam said to him, "I prepared 7 altars. I offered 1 bull and 1 ram on each altar."

**5** The LORD gave Balaam a message. He said, "Go back to Balak and give him this message."

**6** So Balaam went back to Balak. Balak stood next to his burnt offering with all the leaders of Moab.

**7** Then Balaam spoke this message: "Balak, the king of Moab, brought me from Aram, from the mountains in the east. He said, 'Come, curse Jacob for me. Come, speak against Israel.'

**8** But God did not curse these people. How can I curse them? The LORD did not speak against them. How can I speak against them?

**9** I see them from the top of the rocks. I look at them from the hills. They are a people who live separately. They do not think that they are one of the nations.

**10** The descendants of Jacob are as many as the dust. Nobody can count them. Nobody can count even 1/4 of Israel. I wish that I could die as these good people die. I wish that my end is the same as theirs!"

**11** Balak said to Balaam, "What did you do to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies. But you only blessed them!"

**12** Balaam said, "I must say only what the LORD tells me to say."

**13** Then Balak said to him, "Please come with me to a different place. From there you will see only a part of the people. You will not see all of them. Curse them for me from there."

**14** So Balak took Balaam to the field of Zophim, on the top of Mount Pisgah. There Balak built 7 altars. He offered 1 bull and 1 ram on each altar.

**15** Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here next to your burnt offering. I will go over there to meet the LORD."

**16** The LORD met Balaam and gave him a message. He said, "Go back to Balak and give him this message."

**17** So Balaam went to Balak. Balak stood next to his burnt offering with the leaders of Moab. Balak asked him, "What did the LORD say?"

**18** Then Balaam spoke this message: "Balak, stand up and listen. Son of Zippor, hear me.

**19** God is not a man. He does not lie. God is not a human. He does not change his mind. When he makes a promise, he does what he says. When he speaks, he does what he promises.

**20** God told me to bless these people. God blessed them, and I cannot change it.

**21** God sees no wrong in the descendants of Jacob. He sees no trouble in Israel. The LORD their God is with them. The people shout because God is their king.

**22** God brought them out of Egypt. He is as strong as a wild bull for them.

**23** No magic can work against Jacob. No sorcery can work against Israel. Now people will say about Jacob and Israel, 'Look at the great things that God did!'

**24** The people will be as strong as a lion. They will stand up as a lion stands up. A lion does not lie down until it eats its prey and drinks the blood of the animals that it kills."

**25** Then Balak said to Balaam, "Do not curse them at all. But also do not bless them at all!"

**26** Balaam said to Balak, "I told you that I must do all that the LORD tells me."

**27** Then Balak said to Balaam, "Please come. I will take you to a different place. Maybe God will let you curse them for me from there."

**28** So Balak took Balaam to the top of Mount Peor. From there a person can see the desert (Jeshimon).

**29** Balaam said to Balak, "Build 7 altars for me here. Prepare 7 bulls and 7 rams for me here."

**30** Balak did as Balaam said. He offered 1 bull and 1 ram on each altar.

## Chapter 24

**1** Balaam saw that the LORD wanted to bless Israel. Thus Balaam did not go to look for magic signs, as he did at other times. Instead, he turned and looked toward the desert.

**2** Balaam saw the people of Israel in their camp. Each tribe was in its own area. Then the Spirit of God came on Balaam.

**3** Balaam spoke this message: "This is the message of Balaam, the son of Beor. This is the message of the man who sees clearly.

**4** This is the message of the man who hears the words of God. He sees a vision from God All-Powerful. He bows down, and his eyes are open.

**5** Your tents are very beautiful, people of Jacob! Your homes are very beautiful, people of Israel!

**6** They spread out as valleys. They are the same as gardens next to a river. They are the same as aloe trees that the LORD planted. They are the same as cedar trees next to the water.

**7** Water will flow from their buckets. Their seeds will have much water. Their king will be greater than Agag. Their kingdom will be very great.

**8** God brought them out of Egypt. He is as strong as a wild bull for them. They will destroy the nations that are their enemies. They will break the bones of their enemies. They will kill their enemies with arrows.

**9** Israel lies down as a lion. Israel is the same as a strong lion. Nobody will try to wake it. God will bless each person who blesses you. God will curse each person who curses you."

**10** Balak became very angry with Balaam. He hit his hands together. He said to Balaam, "I called you to curse my enemies. But you blessed them these 3 times!

**11** Now go home! I wanted to give you great honor. But the LORD stopped you. He did not let you get honor."

**12** Balaam said to Balak, "You sent messengers to me. I told them,

**13** 'Balak can give me his palace full of silver and gold. But I cannot disobey the command of the LORD. I cannot do anything good or bad from my own ideas. I must say what the LORD tells me.'

**14** Now I go back to my people. But first I will tell you what these people will do to your people in the future."

**15** Then Balaam spoke this message: "This is the message of Balaam, the son of Beor. This is the message of the man who sees clearly.

**16** This is the message of the man who hears the words of God. He knows the knowledge of the Most High God. He sees a vision from God All-Powerful. He bows down, and his eyes are open.

**17** I see a person in the future, but not now. I look at him, but he is not near. A star will come from Jacob. A king will come from Israel. He will break the heads of the leaders of Moab. He will destroy all the people of Sheth.

**18** Israel will take the land of Edom. Israel will take Seir, the land of its enemy. Israel will become very strong.

**19** A ruler will come from the descendants of Jacob. He will destroy the people who stay alive in the city."

**20** Then Balaam looked at the people of Amalek. He spoke this message: "Amalek was the first of the nations. But at the end, Amalek will die for all time."

**21** Then Balaam looked at the Kenites. He spoke this message: "Your home is strong. It is the same as a nest high in a rock.

**22** But the Kenites will become a ruin. Assyria will take you away as prisoners."

**23** Then Balaam spoke this message: "When God does this, nobody will stay alive!

**24** Ships will come from the coast of Cyprus (Kittim). They will attack Assyria and Eber. But they will also die for all time."

**25** Then Balaam got up and went back home. Balak also went away.

## Chapter 25

**1** Israel stayed at Shittim. There the men started to have sex with the women of Moab.

**2** The women of Moab asked the people to come to the sacrifices for their gods. The people ate the food and bowed down to the gods of Moab.

**3** Thus Israel started to worship the god Baal of Peor. The LORD became angry with Israel.

**4** The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of these people. Kill them and show their bodies in the daylight in front of the LORD. Then the strong anger of the LORD will go away from Israel."

**5** So Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you must kill the men in your group who worship Baal of Peor."

**6** Then a man of Israel brought a Midianite woman to his family. Moses and all the community of Israel saw him. The people cried at the entrance of the tabernacle.

**7** Phinehas was the son of Eleazar, and Eleazar was the son of Aaron the priest. Phinehas saw this. He stood up and left the community. He took a spear in his hand.

**8** He followed the man of Israel into the tent. He pushed the spear through the man and through the stomach of the woman. Then the disease (plague) among the people of Israel stopped.

**9** 24,000 people died in the plague.

**10** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**11** "Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, turned my anger away from the people of Israel. He was as eager as I am to protect my honor among them. Thus I did not destroy the people of Israel in my anger.

**12** Thus tell him that I make my covenant of peace with him.

**13** This covenant is for him and for his descendants. They will be priests for all time. Phinehas was eager for the honor of his God. He made a payment for sin (atonement) for the people of Israel."

**14** The man of Israel whom Phinehas killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri, the son of Salu. Zimri was the leader of a family in the tribe of Simeon.

**15** The name of the Midianite woman whom Phinehas killed was Cozbi. She was the daughter of Zur. Zur was the leader of a family group in Midian.

**16** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**17** "Attack the Midianites and kill them.

**18** They are your enemies. They tricked you about Baal of Peor. They also tricked you with Cozbi, the daughter of a leader of Midian. Phinehas killed Cozbi on the day of the plague, which came because of Peor."

## Chapter 26

**1** After the plague, the LORD spoke to Moses and to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest. He said,

**2** "Count all the community of Israel by their families. Count all the men who are 20 years old or older and who can fight in the army of Israel."

**3** So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke to the people in the plains of Moab. This place was next to the Jordan River, across from Jericho. They said,

**4** "Count the men who are 20 years old or older, as the LORD commanded Moses." These are the people of Israel who came out of the land of Egypt:

**5** Reuben was the oldest son of Israel. These are the descendants of Reuben: The Hanochites came from Hanoch. The Palluites came from Pallu.

**6** The Hezronites came from Hezron. The Carmites came from Carmi.

**7** These were the families of Reuben. The total number of men was 43,730.

**8** The son of Pallu was Eliab.

**9** The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram were the leaders of the community who fought against Moses and Aaron. They were in the group of Korah when that group fought against the LORD.

**10** The ground opened and swallowed them with Korah. Their group died when the fire destroyed 250 men. The death of these men became a sign to the people.

**11** But the sons of Korah did not die.

**12** These are the descendants of Simeon by their families: The Nemuelites came from Nemuel. The Jaminites came from Jamin. The Jachinites came from Jachin.

**13** The Zerahites came from Zerah. The Shaulites came from Shaul.

**14** These were the families of Simeon. The total number of men was 22,200.

**15** These are the descendants of Gad by their families: The Zephonites came from Zephon. The Haggites came from Haggi. The Shunites came from Shuni.

**16** The Oznites came from Ozni. The Erites came from Eri.

**17** The Arodites came from Arod. The Arelites came from Areli.

**18** These were the families of Gad. The total number of men was 40,500.

**19** Judah had 2 sons, Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.

**20** These are the descendants of Judah by their families: The Shelanites came from Shelah. The Perezites came from Perez. The Zerahites came from Zerah.

**21** These are the descendants of Perez: The Hezronites came from Hezron. The Hamulites came from Hamul.

**22** These were the families of Judah. The total number of men was 76,500.

**23** These are the descendants of Issachar by their families: The Tolaites came from Tola. The Punites came from Puah.

**24** The Jashubites came from Jashub. The Shimronites came from Shimron.

**25** These were the families of Issachar. The total number of men was 64,300.

**26** These are the descendants of Zebulun by their families: The Seredites came from Sered. The Elonites came from Elon. The Jahleelites came from Jahleel.

**27** These were the families of Zebulun. The total number of men was 60,500.

**28** The descendants of Joseph by their families came from Manasseh and Ephraim.

**29** These are the descendants of Manasseh: The Machirites came from Machir. Machir was the father of Gilead. The Gileadites came from Gilead.

**30** These are the descendants of Gilead: The Iezerites came from Iezer. The Helekites came from Helek.

**31** The Asrielites came from Asriel. The Shechemites came from Shechem.

**32** The Shemidaites came from Shemida. The Hepherites came from Hepher.

**33** Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, had no sons. He had only daughters. The names of his daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

**34** These were the families of Manasseh. The total number of men was 52,700.

**35** These are the descendants of Ephraim by their families: The Shuthelahites came from Shuthelah. The Becherites came from Becher. The Tahanites came from Tahan.

**36** These are the descendants of Shuthelah: The Eranites came from Eran.

**37** These were the families of Ephraim. The total number of men was 32,500. These were the descendants of Joseph by their families.

**38** These are the descendants of Benjamin by their families: The Belaites came from Bela. The Ashbelites came from Ashbel. The Ahiramites came from Ahiram.

**39** The Shuphamites came from Shupham. The Huphamites came from Hupham.

**40** The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman. The Ardites came from Ard. The Naamites came from Naaman.

**41** These were the families of Benjamin. The total number of men was 45,600.

**42** These are the descendants of Dan by their families: The Shuhamites came from Shuham. These were the families of Dan.

**43** All the families of the Shuhamites had a total of 64,400 men.

**44** These are the descendants of Asher by their families: The Imnites came from Imnah. The Ishvites came from Ishvi. The Beriites came from Beriah.

**45** These are the descendants of Beriah: The Heberites came from Heber. The Malchielites came from Malchiel.

**46** Asher had a daughter. Her name was Serah.

**47** These were the families of Asher. The total number of men was 53,400.

**48** These are the descendants of Naphtali by their families: The Jahzeelites came from Jahzeel. The Gunites came from Guni.

**49** The Jezerites came from Jezer. The Shillemites came from Shillem.

**50** These were the families of Naphtali. The total number of men was 45,400.

**51** The total number of the men of Israel was 601,730.

**52** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**53** "Divide the land among these tribes. Give each tribe its part by the number of names.

**54** Give a large part of land to a large tribe. Give a small part of land to a small tribe. Give each tribe its land by the number of its men.

**55** But use lots to divide the land. Each tribe will get its land by the name of its ancestor.

**56** Use lots to divide the land between the large tribes and the small tribes."

**57** These are the Levites whom Moses and Eleazar counted by their families: The Gershonites came from Gershon. The Kohathites came from Kohath. The Merarites came from Merari.

**58** These were also families of the Levites: the Libnites, the Hebronites, the Mahlites, the Mushites, and the Korahites. Kohath was the father of Amram.

**59** The wife of Amram had the name Jochebed. She was a descendant of Levi. Her mother gave birth to her in Egypt. She and Amram had 3 children: Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.

**60** Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

**61** But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered fire that the LORD did not approve.

**62** The total number of the Levite males who were 1 month old or older was 23,000. Moses did not count them with the other people of Israel. The Levites did not get land among the people of Israel.

**63** Moses and Eleazar the priest counted all these people. They counted the people of Israel in the plains of Moab, next to the Jordan River, across from Jericho.

**64** Moses and Aaron the priest counted the people of Israel before, in the desert of Sinai. But none of the men in that count were in this new count.

**65** The LORD told the men of the first count that they will die in the desert. Only Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua, the son of Nun, stayed alive.

## Chapter 27

**1** Zelophehad was the son of Hepher. Hepher was the son of Gilead, Gilead was the son of Machir, and Machir was the son of Manasseh. Zelophehad was from the families of Manasseh, the son of Joseph. The names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. These daughters came to Moses.

**2** They went to the entrance of the tabernacle. They stood in front of Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and all the community. They said,

**3** "Our father died in the desert. He was not in the group of Korah, who came together against the LORD. Our father died because of his own sin. He had no sons.

**4** Our father had no son. But his name must not disappear from his family. Thus give us land among the relatives of our father."

**5** So Moses took their request to the LORD.

**6** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**7** "The daughters of Zelophehad are correct. You must give them land among the relatives of their father. Give them the land of their father.

**8** Tell the people of Israel, 'If a man dies and has no son, give his land to his daughter.

**9** If he has no daughter, give his land to his brothers.

**10** If he has no brothers, give his land to the brothers of his father.

**11** If his father has no brothers, give his land to his nearest relative in his family. That relative will own the land.' This will be a law for the people of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses."

**12** The LORD said to Moses, "Go up this mountain in the Abarim mountains. Look at the land that I give to the people of Israel.

**13** After you see the land, you will die and go to your ancestors, as your brother Aaron did.

**14** In the desert of Zin, the community argued with me. At that time, you two did not obey my command. You did not show my holiness to the people at the water." This was the water of Meribah at Kadesh in the desert of Zin.

**15** Moses spoke to the LORD. He said,

**16** "LORD, you are the God who gives life to all people. Please choose a man to lead the community.

**17** He must lead them in war and bring them home. He must lead them out and bring them in. Then the community of the LORD will not be the same as sheep without a shepherd."

**18** The LORD said to Moses, "Take Joshua, the son of Nun. My Spirit is in him. Put your hand on him.

**19** Put him in front of Eleazar the priest and in front of all the community. Give him his orders while the people watch.

**20** Give him some of your authority. Then all the community of Israel will obey him.

**21** Joshua will stand in front of Eleazar the priest. Eleazar will use the Urim to ask the LORD what Joshua must do. Joshua and all the community of Israel will go out and come in when the LORD tells them."

**22** Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua and put him in front of Eleazar the priest and all the community.

**23** Moses put his hands on Joshua and gave him his orders. He did as the LORD told him.

## Chapter 28

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Give this command to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'You must bring my offerings to me at the correct times. These offerings are my food. They are offerings by fire that make a pleasant smell for me.'

**3** Tell them, 'This is the offering by fire that you must give to the LORD. Each day, offer 2 male lambs that are 1 year old and have no defect. They are a daily burnt offering.

**4** Offer 1 lamb in the morning. Offer the other lamb in the evening.

**5** With each lamb, give a grain offering of 1/10 of an ephah of fine flour. Mix the flour with 1/4 of a hin of pressed olive oil.

**6** This is the daily burnt offering that the LORD gave at Mount Sinai. It is an offering by fire that makes a pleasant smell for the LORD.

**7** With each lamb, give a drink offering of 1/4 of a hin of wine. Pour the strong wine to the LORD in the holy place.

**8** Offer the other lamb in the evening. Give the same grain offering and drink offering that you give in the morning. This is an offering by fire that makes a pleasant smell for the LORD.

**9** On the Sabbath day, offer 2 male lambs that are 1 year old and have no defect. Also give a grain offering of 2/10 of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. Give its drink offering too.

**10** This is the burnt offering for each Sabbath. Give it together with the daily burnt offering and its drink offering.

**11** On the 1st day of each month, give a burnt offering to the LORD. Offer 2 young bulls, 1 ram, and 7 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**12** With each bull, give a grain offering of 3/10 of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. With the ram, give a grain offering of 2/10 of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil.

**13** With each lamb, give a grain offering of 1/10 of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. This is a burnt offering that makes a pleasant smell. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.

**14** The drink offerings are 1/2 of a hin of wine with each bull and 1/3 of a hin with the ram. Give 1/4 of a hin with each lamb. This is the burnt offering for each month of the year.

**15** Also offer 1 male goat to the LORD as a sin offering. Give it together with the daily burnt offering and its drink offering.

**16** On the 14th day of the 1st month, keep the Passover of the LORD.

**17** On the 15th day of that month, there will be a festival. For 7 days, eat bread that has no yeast.

**18** On the 1st day of the festival, have a holy assembly. Do not do your usual work.

**19** Give an offering by fire to the LORD as a burnt offering. Offer 2 young bulls, 1 ram, and 7 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**20** Give grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil. Give 3/10 of an ephah with each bull and 2/10 of an ephah with the ram.

**21** Give 1/10 of an ephah with each of the 7 lambs.

**22** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.

**23** Give these offerings together with the daily burnt offering in the morning.

**24** In this way, give these offerings each day for 7 days. This is food for the offering by fire that makes a pleasant smell for the LORD. Give it together with the daily burnt offering and its drink offering.

**25** On the 7th day, have a holy assembly. Do not do your usual work.

**26** On the day of the firstfruits, you will give a new grain offering to the LORD at your Festival of Weeks. On that day, have a holy assembly. Do not do your usual work.

**27** Give a burnt offering that makes a pleasant smell for the LORD. Offer 2 young bulls, 1 ram, and 7 male lambs that are 1 year old.

**28** Give grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil. Give 3/10 of an ephah with each bull and 2/10 of an ephah with the ram.

**29** Give 1/10 of an ephah with each of the 7 lambs.

**30** Also offer 1 male goat to make atonement for you.

**31** Give these offerings and their drink offerings together with the daily burnt offering and its grain offering. All the animals must have no defect.'"

## Chapter 29

**1** "'On the 1st day of the 7th month, have a holy assembly. Do not do your usual work. On that day you will blow the trumpets.

**2** Give a burnt offering that makes a pleasant smell for the LORD. Offer 1 young bull, 1 ram, and 7 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**3** Give grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil. Give 3/10 of an ephah with the bull and 2/10 of an ephah with the ram.

**4** Give 1/10 of an ephah with each of the 7 lambs.

**5** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.

**6** Give these offerings together with the burnt offering of the month and its grain offering. Also give them together with the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and their drink offerings. Do these things by the rules. They are offerings by fire that make a pleasant smell for the LORD.

**7** On the 10th day of the 7th month, have a holy assembly. On that day you must not eat, and you must humble yourselves. Do not do any work.

**8** Give a burnt offering that makes a pleasant smell for the LORD. Offer 1 young bull, 1 ram, and 7 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**9** Give grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil. Give 3/10 of an ephah with the bull and 2/10 of an ephah with the ram.

**10** Give 1/10 of an ephah with each of the 7 lambs.

**11** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering. Give it together with the sin offering for atonement, the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and their drink offerings.

**12** On the 15th day of the 7th month, have a holy assembly. Do not do your usual work. Keep a festival to the LORD for 7 days.

**13** Give a burnt offering by fire that makes a pleasant smell for the LORD. Offer 13 young bulls, 2 rams, and 14 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**14** Give grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil. Give 3/10 of an ephah with each of the 13 bulls. Give 2/10 of an ephah with each of the 2 rams.

**15** Give 1/10 of an ephah with each of the 14 lambs.

**16** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering. Give these offerings together with the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

**17** On the 2nd day, offer 12 young bulls, 2 rams, and 14 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**18** Give the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs. Give them by the number of animals and by the rules.

**19** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering. Give it together with the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and their drink offerings.

**20** On the 3rd day, offer 11 bulls, 2 rams, and 14 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**21** Give the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs. Give them by the number of animals and by the rules.

**22** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering. Give it together with the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

**23** On the 4th day, offer 10 bulls, 2 rams, and 14 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**24** Give the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs. Give them by the number of animals and by the rules.

**25** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering. Give it together with the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

**26** On the 5th day, offer 9 bulls, 2 rams, and 14 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**27** Give the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs. Give them by the number of animals and by the rules.

**28** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering. Give it together with the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

**29** On the 6th day, offer 8 bulls, 2 rams, and 14 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**30** Give the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs. Give them by the number of animals and by the rules.

**31** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering. Give it together with the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

**32** On the 7th day, offer 7 bulls, 2 rams, and 14 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**33** Give the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs. Give them by the number of animals and by the rules.

**34** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering. Give it together with the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

**35** On the 8th day, have a special assembly. Do not do your usual work.

**36** Give a burnt offering by fire that makes a pleasant smell for the LORD. Offer 1 bull, 1 ram, and 7 male lambs that are 1 year old. All the animals must have no defect.

**37** Give the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bull, the ram, and the lambs. Give them by the number of animals and by the rules.

**38** Also offer 1 male goat as a sin offering. Give it together with the daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

**39** Give these offerings to the LORD at your festivals. Give them together with the offerings for your vows and your free offerings. These include your burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings.'"

**40** Moses told the people of Israel all that the LORD commanded him.

## Chapter 30

**1** Moses spoke to the leaders of the tribes of Israel. He said, "This is what the LORD commands.

**2** A man can make a promise (vow) to the LORD. Or he can make an oath that he will do or not do a thing. He must not break his word. He must do all that he said.

**3** A young woman who lives in the house of her father can make a vow to the LORD. Or she can promise that she will do or not do a thing.

**4** Her father can hear about her vow or her promise and say nothing to her. Then she must do all her vows and all her promises.

**5** But her father can hear about them and refuse them on that same day. Then her vows and her promises have no force. The LORD will forgive her, because her father refused them.

**6** A woman can make a vow or a careless promise, and then she can get married.

**7** Her husband can hear about it and say nothing to her on that day. Then she must do her vows and her promises.

**8** But her husband can hear about it and refuse it on that same day. Then he cancels her vow and her careless promise. The LORD will forgive her.

**9** A widow or a divorced woman must do all her vows and all her promises.

**10** A married woman who lives in the house of her husband can make a vow. Or she can make an oath that she will do or not do a thing.

**11** Her husband can hear about it and say nothing to her. If he does not refuse it, then she must do all her vows and all her promises.

**12** But her husband can cancel them on the day that he hears about them. Then her vows and her promises have no force. Her husband cancelled them, and the LORD will forgive her.

**13** Her husband can accept or cancel each vow and each oath that she makes to deny herself.

**14** If her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he accepts all her vows and her promises. He accepts them because he said nothing to her on the day that he heard about them.

**15** But he can cancel them some time after he hears about them. Then he is responsible for her guilt."

**16** These are the laws that the LORD gave to Moses. They are about a man and his wife. They are also about a father and his young daughter who lives in his house.

## Chapter 31

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Punish the Midianites for what they did to the people of Israel. After this, you will die and go to your ancestors."

**3** So Moses said to the people, "Prepare some of your men for war. They must go against the Midianites and do the punishment of the LORD on Midian.

**4** Send 1,000 men from each tribe of Israel to the war."

**5** So the people chose 1,000 men from each tribe of Israel. There were 12,000 men ready for war.

**6** Moses sent them to the war, 1,000 men from each tribe. Phinehas, the son of Eleazar the priest, went with them. He took the holy equipment and the trumpets to blow.

**7** They fought against the Midianites, as the LORD commanded Moses. They killed all the men.

**8** They also killed the 5 kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. They also killed Balaam, the son of Beor, with the sword.

**9** The people of Israel took the women of Midian and their children as prisoners. They took all their cattle, their flocks, and their possessions.

**10** They burned all the cities where the Midianites lived. They also burned all their camps.

**11** They took all the people and all the animals as plunder.

**12** They brought the prisoners, the animals, and the plunder to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the community of Israel. They brought them to the camp in the plains of Moab, next to the Jordan River, across from Jericho.

**13** Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the community went out of the camp to meet them.

**14** Moses was angry with the officers of the army. These were the commanders of 1,000 men and the commanders of 100 men. They came back from the battle.

**15** Moses said to them, "Why did you let all the women live?

**16** These women followed the advice of Balaam. They caused the people of Israel to sin against the LORD at Peor. Then a plague came on the community of the LORD.

**17** Now kill each boy among the children. Kill each woman who had sex with a man.

**18** But let all the girls who did not have sex with a man live. Keep them for yourselves.

**19** Each man who killed a person or touched a dead body must stay outside the camp for 7 days. On the 3rd day and on the 7th day, you and your prisoners must make yourselves clean.

**20** Make all your clothes clean. Also make clean all things that people make of leather, of goat hair, or of wood."

**21** Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who went to the battle, "This is the rule of the law that the LORD commanded Moses.

**22** Gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead are metals that fire does not destroy.

**23** Put these metals and all other things that fire does not destroy through the fire. Then they will be clean. But you must also make them clean with the water for purification. Put all the things that fire destroys through the water.

**24** On the 7th day, wash your clothes. Then you will be clean. After this, you can come into the camp."

**25** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**26** "You, Eleazar the priest, and the family leaders of the community must count the people and the animals that the army took.

**27** Divide the plunder into 2 equal parts. Give 1 part to the soldiers who went to the battle. Give the other part to all the community.

**28** From the part of the soldiers, take a tax for the LORD. Take 1 of each 500 persons, cattle, donkeys, and sheep.

**29** Take this tax from their half. Give it to Eleazar the priest as a heave offering of the LORD.

**30** From the half of the people of Israel, take 1 of each 50 persons, cattle, donkeys, sheep, and other animals. Give them to the Levites, who do the work of the tabernacle of the LORD."

**31** So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**32** The plunder that the soldiers took was 675,000 sheep,

**33** 72,000 cattle,

**34** 61,000 donkeys,

**35** and 32,000 girls who did not have sex with a man.

**36** The half for the soldiers was 337,500 sheep.

**37** From these sheep, the tax for the LORD was 675.

**38** There were 36,000 cattle. From these cattle, the tax for the LORD was 72.

**39** There were 30,500 donkeys. From these donkeys, the tax for the LORD was 61.

**40** There were 16,000 persons. From these persons, the tax for the LORD was 32.

**41** Moses gave the tax to Eleazar the priest as the heave offering of the LORD. He did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**42** Moses separated the half for the people of Israel from the half for the soldiers.

**43** The half for the community was 337,500 sheep,

**44** 36,000 cattle,

**45** 30,500 donkeys,

**46** and 16,000 persons.

**47** From the half for the people of Israel, Moses took 1 of each 50 persons and animals. He gave them to the Levites, who did the work of the tabernacle of the LORD. He did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**48** Then the officers of the army came to Moses. These were the commanders of 1,000 men and the commanders of 100 men.

**49** They said to Moses, "We, your servants, counted the soldiers under our command. All the men are there. Not 1 man is absent.

**50** Thus we bring an offering to the LORD. Each man brings the gold things that he found: bracelets, chains, rings, earrings, and necklaces. We give them to make atonement for ourselves in front of the LORD."

**51** Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them. All the gold things were well made.

**52** The commanders of 1,000 men and the commanders of 100 men gave this gold to the LORD. All the gold weighed 16,750 shekels.

**53** Each soldier kept the plunder that he took for himself.

**54** Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders. They brought it into the tabernacle. It is a reminder for the people of Israel in front of the LORD.

## Chapter 32

**1** The tribes of Reuben and Gad had very large herds of animals. They saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were good places for animals.

**2** So the people of Gad and Reuben came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the community. They said,

**3** "Look at the towns of Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon.

**4** The LORD defeated the people of this land for the community of Israel. It is a good land for animals, and we, your servants, have animals."

**5** They said, "Please be kind to us. Give this land to us, your servants, as our property. Do not make us go across the Jordan River."



**6** Moses said to the people of Gad and Reuben, "Will your brothers go to war while you stay here?

**7** Why do you make the people of Israel afraid to go across into the land that the LORD gives them?

**8** Your fathers did the same thing. I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to look at the land.

**9** They went up to the valley of Eshcol and saw the land. Then they made the people of Israel afraid to go into the land that the LORD gave them.

**10** On that day the LORD became angry. He made a solemn promise (oath). He said,

**11** 'The men who came out of Egypt and who are 20 years old or older will not see the land. I promised that land to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. But these men did not follow me completely.

**12** Only Caleb, the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and Joshua, the son of Nun, will see the land. They followed the LORD completely.'

**13** The LORD was angry with Israel. He made them go from place to place in the desert for 40 years. Then all the people of that generation who did evil in the sight of the LORD were dead.

**14** Now you take the place of your fathers. You are a new group of sinful men. You make the LORD more angry with Israel.

**15** If you turn away from the LORD, he will again leave the people in the desert. Then you will cause the destruction of all these people."

**16** Then the men of Gad and Reuben came near to Moses. They said, "We will build pens for our animals and cities for our children here.

**17** But we will prepare for war and go in front of the people of Israel. We will go until we bring them to their land. Our children will live in cities with walls. The walls will protect them from the people of this land.

**18** We will not go back to our homes until each Israelite gets his land.

**19** We will not take land with them on the other side of the Jordan River. We received our land on the east side of the Jordan River."

**20** Moses said to them, "You must do this. You must prepare for war in front of the LORD.

**21** All your soldiers must go across the Jordan River in front of the LORD. You must go until the LORD forces out his enemies.

**22** When the LORD defeats the people of the land, you can come back. Then you will not be guilty in front of the LORD and in front of Israel. This land will be your property in front of the LORD.

**23** But if you do not do this, you will sin against the LORD. You can be sure that your sin will find you. God will punish you for it.

**24** Build cities for your children and pens for your sheep. But do what you promised."

**25** The people of Gad and Reuben said to Moses, "We, your servants, will do what you, our master, command.

**26** Our children, our wives, our flocks, and all our animals will stay here in the cities of Gilead.

**27** But each of your servants will prepare for war. We will go across the Jordan River to fight in front of the LORD, as you, our master, say."

**28** So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest and to Joshua, the son of Nun. He also gave orders to the family leaders of the tribes of Israel.

**29** Moses said to them, "The people of Gad and Reuben must go with you across the Jordan River. Each man must prepare for battle in front of the LORD. If they do this and you defeat the land, then give them the land of Gilead as their property.

**30** But if they do not go across with you for war, they must take land among you in Canaan."

**31** The people of Gad and Reuben said, "We, your servants, will do what the LORD said.

**32** We will prepare for war and go across in front of the LORD into the land of Canaan. But our land will be on this side of the Jordan River."

**33** So Moses gave land to the people of Gad and to the people of Reuben. He also gave land to half of the tribe of Manasseh, the son of Joseph. He gave them the kingdom of Sihon, the king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og, the king of Bashan. He gave them all the land with its cities and the areas around the cities.

**34** The people of Gad built again the cities of Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,

**35** Atroth Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,

**36** Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran. These cities had walls. They also built pens for their sheep.

**37** The people of Reuben built again the cities of Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,

**38** Nebo, Baal Meon, and Sibmah. They changed the names of Nebo and Baal Meon. They gave new names to the cities that they built.

**39** The descendants of Machir, the son of Manasseh, went to Gilead and took it. They forced out the Amorites who lived there.

**40** So Moses gave Gilead to the descendants of Machir, the son of Manasseh. They lived there.

**41** Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, went and took the villages of Gilead. He called them Havvoth Jair.

**42** Nobah went and took Kenath and the villages near it. He called the town Nobah, by his own name.

## Chapter 33

**1** These are the trips of the people of Israel after they came out of Egypt. They went in their army groups under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.

**2** The LORD commanded Moses to write down the places where they went. These are the stages of their trip, from each place to the next place.

**3** The people of Israel went from Rameses on the 15th day of the 1st month. This was the day after the Passover. They went out boldly while all the Egyptians watched.

**4** At that time the Egyptians buried their firstborn sons, whom the LORD killed. The LORD also punished their gods.

**5** The people of Israel went from Rameses and made their camp at Succoth.

**6** They went from Succoth and made their camp at Etham, at the edge of the desert.

**7** They went from Etham and turned back to Pi Hahiroth, east of Baal Zephon. They made their camp near Migdol.

**8** They went from Pi Hahiroth and went through the middle of the sea into the desert. They traveled for 3 days in the desert of Etham and made their camp at Marah.

**9** They went from Marah and came to Elim. At Elim there were 12 springs of water and 70 palm trees. They made their camp there.

**10** They went from Elim and made their camp next to the Red Sea.

**11** They went from the Red Sea and made their camp in the desert of Sin.

**12** They went from the desert of Sin and made their camp at Dophkah.

**13** They went from Dophkah and made their camp at Alush.

**14** They went from Alush and made their camp at Rephidim. At Rephidim there was no water for the people to drink.

**15** They went from Rephidim and made their camp in the desert of Sinai.

**16** They went from the desert of Sinai and made their camp at Kibroth Hattaavah.

**17** They went from Kibroth Hattaavah and made their camp at Hazeroth.

**18** They went from Hazeroth and made their camp at Rithmah.

**19** They went from Rithmah and made their camp at Rimmon Perez.

**20** They went from Rimmon Perez and made their camp at Libnah.

**21** They went from Libnah and made their camp at Rissah.

**22** They went from Rissah and made their camp at Kehelathah.

**23** They went from Kehelathah and made their camp at Mount Shepher.

**24** They went from Mount Shepher and made their camp at Haradah.

**25** They went from Haradah and made their camp at Makheloth.

**26** They went from Makheloth and made their camp at Tahath.

**27** They went from Tahath and made their camp at Terah.

**28** They went from Terah and made their camp at Mithkah.

**29** They went from Mithkah and made their camp at Hashmonah.

**30** They went from Hashmonah and made their camp at Moseroth.

**31** They went from Moseroth and made their camp at Bene Jaakan.

**32** They went from Bene Jaakan and made their camp at Hor Haggidgad.

**33** They went from Hor Haggidgad and made their camp at Jotbathah.

**34** They went from Jotbathah and made their camp at Abronah.

**35** They went from Abronah and made their camp at Ezion Geber.

**36** They went from Ezion Geber and made their camp in the desert of Zin, at Kadesh.

**37** They went from Kadesh and made their camp at Mount Hor, at the edge of the land of Edom.

**38** The LORD commanded Aaron the priest to go up on Mount Hor. Aaron went up, and he died there. He died on the 1st day of the 5th month, in the 40th year after the people of Israel came out of Egypt.

**39** Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.

**40** The Canaanite king of Arad lived in the Negev, in the south of the land of Canaan. He heard that the people of Israel came.

**41** The people went from Mount Hor and made their camp at Zalmonah.

**42** They went from Zalmonah and made their camp at Punon.

**43** They went from Punon and made their camp at Oboth.

**44** They went from Oboth and made their camp at Iye Abarim, at the border of Moab.

**45** They went from Iyim and made their camp at Dibon Gad.

**46** They went from Dibon Gad and made their camp at Almon Diblathaim.

**47** They went from Almon Diblathaim and made their camp in the Abarim mountains, near Nebo.

**48** They went from the Abarim mountains and made their camp in the plains of Moab. This place was next to the Jordan River, across from Jericho.

**49** In the plains of Moab, their camp went along the Jordan River from Beth Jeshimoth to Abel Shittim.

**50** In the plains of Moab, next to the Jordan River, across from Jericho, the LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**51** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'Soon you will go across the Jordan River into the land of Canaan.

**52** Then you must force out all the people who live in the land. Destroy all their carved stones and all their metal idols. Destroy all their high places of worship.

**53** Take the land and live in it. I give you the land as your property.

**54** Use lots to divide the land among your families. Give a large part of land to a large group. Give a small part of land to a small group. Each family will get the land where its lot falls. Divide the land among the tribes of your ancestors.

**55** But if you do not force out the people of the land, they will cause you much trouble. They will be the same as sharp sticks in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will be your enemies in the land where you live.

**56** Then I will do to you what I planned to do to them.'"

## Chapter 34

**1** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Give this command to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'Soon you will go into the land of Canaan. This is the land that you will get as your property. These are the borders of the land of Canaan:

**3** Your south side will go from the desert of Zin along the border of Edom. On the east, your south border will start at the end of the Dead Sea.

**4** The border will turn south of the Scorpion Pass and go on to Zin. It will go south of Kadesh Barnea. Then it will go to Hazar Addar and on to Azmon.

**5** From Azmon the border will turn and go to the stream of Egypt. It will end at the Mediterranean Sea.

**6** Your west border will be the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. This will be your west border.

**7** This will be your north border: Make a line from the Mediterranean Sea to Mount Hor.

**8** From Mount Hor make a line to Lebo Hamath. Then the border will go to Zedad.

**9** The border will go on to Ziphron and end at Hazar Enan. This will be your north border.

**10** For your east border, make a line from Hazar Enan to Shepham.

**11** The border will go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain. Then the border will go along the hills to the east of the Sea of Galilee (Chinnereth).

**12** Then the border will go down along the Jordan River and end at the Dead Sea. These will be the borders around your land.'"

**13** Moses gave this command to the people of Israel: "This is the land that you will get by lots. The LORD commanded that we give this land to the 9 tribes and to half of the tribe of Manasseh.

**14** The families of the tribe of Reuben, the families of the tribe of Gad, and half of the tribe of Manasseh already received their land.

**15** These 2 tribes and the half tribe received their land on the east side of the Jordan River, across from Jericho."

**16** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**17** "These are the names of the men who will divide the land for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua, the son of Nun.

**18** Also choose 1 leader from each tribe to help divide the land.

**19** These are the names of the men: From the tribe of Judah, Caleb, the son of Jephunneh.

**20** From the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel, the son of Ammihud.

**21** From the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad, the son of Kislon.

**22** From the tribe of Dan, the leader Bukki, the son of Jogli.

**23** From the descendants of Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh, the leader Hanniel, the son of Ephod.

**24** From the tribe of Ephraim, the leader Kemuel, the son of Shiphtan.

**25** From the tribe of Zebulun, the leader Elizaphan, the son of Parnach.

**26** From the tribe of Issachar, the leader Paltiel, the son of Azzan.

**27** From the tribe of Asher, the leader Ahihud, the son of Shelomi.

**28** From the tribe of Naphtali, the leader Pedahel, the son of Ammihud."

**29** The LORD commanded these men to divide the land of Canaan among the people of Israel.

## Chapter 35

**1** In the plains of Moab, next to the Jordan River, across from Jericho, the LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**2** "Command the people of Israel to give some cities to the Levites from the land that they get. The Levites will live in these cities. Also give the Levites the pastures around the cities.

**3** The Levites will live in the cities. The pastures will be for their cattle, their flocks, and all their other animals.

**4** The pastures around the cities that you give to the Levites will go out 1,000 cubits from the city wall on all sides.

**5** Measure 2,000 cubits outside the city on the east side, on the south side, on the west side, and on the north side. The city will be in the middle. This area will be the pastures for their cities.

**6** Give 6 of the cities to the Levites as cities of safety (refuge). A person who kills another person can run to a city of refuge. Also give the Levites 42 other cities.

**7** Thus you will give the Levites a total of 48 cities with their pastures.

**8** The cities that you give to the Levites must come from the land of the people of Israel. A tribe that has much land must give many cities. A tribe that has little land must give few cities. Each tribe must give cities to the Levites by the size of its land."

**9** The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

**10** "Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'Soon you will go across the Jordan River into the land of Canaan.

**11** Then choose some cities to be your cities of refuge. A person who kills another person by accident can run to these cities.

**12** These cities will be a safe place from the relative who wants revenge. The person who killed must not die before the community judges him.

**13** You will choose 6 cities of refuge.

**14** Choose 3 cities on the east side of the Jordan River. Choose 3 cities in the land of Canaan. These will be the cities of refuge.

**15** These 6 cities will be a safe place for the people of Israel and for the foreigners who live among them. Each person who kills another person by accident can run there.

**16** But a person can hit another person with an iron object and kill him. Then the person who killed is a murderer. You must kill the murderer.

**17** A person can hit another person with a stone that can kill, and the other person dies. Then the person who killed is a murderer. You must kill the murderer.

**18** A person can hit another person with a wooden object that can kill, and the other person dies. Then the person who killed is a murderer. You must kill the murderer.

**19** The relative who must get revenge for the dead person will kill the murderer. When he finds the murderer, he will kill him.

**20** A person can hate another person and push him. Or he can wait to attack him and throw something at him. If the other person dies, the attacker is a murderer.

**21** Or a person can hit another person with his hand because of hate, and that person dies. You must kill the attacker, because he is a murderer. The relative who must get revenge will kill the murderer when he finds him.

**22** But a person can push another person suddenly without hate. Or he can throw something at him without the intention to hurt him.

**23** Or he can drop a stone that can kill on a person, but he does not see the person. The person dies, but the attacker was not his enemy. He did not want to hurt him.

**24** Then the community must judge between the person who killed and the relative who wants revenge. They must use these rules.

**25** The community must protect the person who killed from the relative who wants revenge. The community must send him back to the city of refuge where he ran. He must stay there until the high priest dies. The high priest is the priest who received the holy oil.

**26** But the person who killed can go outside the border of his city of refuge.

**27** Then the relative who wants revenge can find him outside the city of refuge and kill him. The relative will not be guilty of murder.

**28** The person who killed must stay in his city of refuge until the high priest dies. After the high priest dies, the person who killed can go back to his own land.

**29** These rules are laws for you in all your generations and in all the places where you live.

**30** If a person kills another person, you must kill the murderer only when there are witnesses. You must not kill a person on the word of only 1 witness.

**31** Do not accept money for the life of a murderer who must die. You must kill him.

**32** Do not accept money from a person who ran to a city of refuge. He must not go back to live on his land before the high priest dies.

**33** Do not make the land where you live unclean. Murder makes the land unclean. Only the blood of the murderer can make the land clean after a murder.

**34** Do not make the land where you live unclean. I live in this land. I, the LORD, live among the people of Israel.'"

## Chapter 36

**1** The family leaders of the clan of Gilead came to Moses. Gilead was the son of Machir, and Machir was the son of Manasseh. These family leaders were from the descendants of Joseph. They spoke to Moses and to the leaders, the family leaders of Israel.

**2** They said, "The LORD commanded you, our master, to give the land to the people of Israel by lots. The LORD also commanded you to give the land of our relative Zelophehad to his daughters.

**3** But the daughters can marry men from other tribes of Israel. Then their land will go away from the land of our ancestors. It will go to the tribe of their husbands. Thus our tribe will lose a part of our land.
