**5** "Then the officers must speak to the army. They must say, 'Did any man build a new house but not yet dedicate it? He must go back to his house. If he does not, he can die in the battle, and another man will dedicate the house.

**6** Did any man plant a vineyard but not yet eat its grapes? He must go back to his house. If he does not, he can die in the battle, and another man will eat the grapes.

**7** Is any man engaged to a woman but not yet married to her? He must go back to his house. If he does not, he can die in the battle, and another man will marry her.'

**8** The officers must also say, 'Is any man afraid or without courage? He must go back to his house. If he does not, he will cause his brothers to lose courage too.'

**9** When the officers stop their words to the army, they must appoint commanders to lead the army.

**10** "When you come near a city to attack it, first offer peace to its people.

**11** The people of the city can accept peace and open their gates to you. If so, all the people in the city will work for you and serve you.

**12** But the city can refuse peace and fight against you. If so, put your army around the city to attack it.

**13** The LORD your God will give the city to you. Then kill all the men in it with the sword.

**14** But you can take for yourselves the women, the children, the animals and all the valuable things in the city. You can use the valuable things of your enemies that the LORD your God gives you.

**15** Do this to all the cities that are far away from you. These cities are not the cities of the nations near you.

**16** But do not let anyone stay alive in the cities of the nations that the LORD your God gives you as your property.

**17** Destroy them completely: the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites. The LORD your God commanded you to do this.

**18** If you do not destroy them, they will teach you to do all the hated things that they do for their gods. Then you will sin against the LORD your God.

**19** "You can attack a city for a long time to capture it. Do not cut down its fruit trees with an axe. You can eat their fruit. Do not cut them down. The trees are not your enemies. Do not attack them as you attack the city.

**20** But you can cut down trees that you know do not give fruit. Use them to build attack structures against the city that fights you. Use them until you defeat the city.

## Chapter 21

**1** "Someone can find a dead person in a field in the land that the LORD your God gives you as your property. No one knows who killed that person.

**2** Then your elders and your judges must go out. They must measure the distance from the body to the cities around it.

**3** The elders of the city that is nearest to the body must take a young cow. Nobody used the cow for work. It did not pull a yoke.

**4** The elders of that city must take the young cow down to a valley with a stream. Nobody plowed or planted the valley. There in the valley they must break the neck of the young cow.

**5** Then the priests, the sons of Levi, must come forward. The LORD your God chose them to serve him and to bless the people in the name of the LORD. They decide each dispute and each case of an attack.

**6** All the elders of the city nearest to the body must wash their hands over the young cow whose neck they broke in the valley.

**7** They must say, 'We did not kill this person. We did not see who did it.

**8** LORD, forgive your people Israel, whom you made free. Do not make your people Israel guilty of the death of an innocent person.' Then the LORD will forgive them for the death.

**9** Thus remove from among you the guilt of the death of an innocent person. You will do what is right in the sight of the LORD.

**10** "You can go out to fight a war against your enemies. The LORD your God can give them to you, and you can take prisoners.

**11** You can see a beautiful woman among the prisoners. You can want her as your wife.

**12** Then bring her to your house. She must shave her head and cut her nails.

**13** She must remove the clothes that she wore when you captured her. She must stay in your house and cry for her father and her mother for 1 full month. After that, you can go to her and be her husband, and she will be your wife.

**14** But if you are not happy with her, let her go where she wants. Do not sell her for money. Do not treat her as a slave, because you dishonored her.

**15** "A man can have 2 wives. He can love one wife and not love the other. Both wives can have sons for him. The firstborn son can be the son of the wife that he does not love.

**16** When the man gives his property to his sons, he must not treat the son of the wife that he loves as the firstborn. He must not do this in place of the real firstborn, the son of the other wife.

**17** He must accept the son of the wife that he does not love as the firstborn. He must give that son 2 parts of all his property. That son is the first sign of his strength. The right of the firstborn belongs to that son.

**18** "A man can have a stubborn son who does not obey. The son does not obey his father or his mother. They correct him, but he does not listen to them.

**19** Then his father and his mother must take him to the elders at the gate of his town.

**20** They must say to the elders of the town, 'This son of ours is stubborn and he does not obey. He does not listen to us. He eats too much and he drinks too much.'

**21** Then all the men of his town must throw stones at him until he dies. Thus remove the evil from among you. All Israel will hear about it and be afraid.

**22** "A man can do a sin that deserves death. You can kill him and hang his body on a tree.

**23** Do not let his body stay on the tree during the night. Bury him on the same day. God curses each person who hangs on a tree. Do not make unclean the land that the LORD your God gives you as your property.

## Chapter 22

**1** "You can see the ox or the sheep of your brother go away from its place. Do not ignore it. Take it back to your brother.

**2** Your brother can live far from you, or you can not know who owns it. Then take it to your house. Keep it until your brother looks for it. Then give it back to him.

**3** Do the same with his donkey, with his clothes and with any thing that your brother lost and you find. Do not ignore it.

**4** You can see the donkey or the ox of your brother fall down on the road. Do not ignore it. Help him to lift it up.

**5** "A woman must not wear the clothes of a man. A man must not wear the clothes of a woman. The LORD your God hates the people who do this.

**6** "You can find a bird nest in a tree or on the ground near the road. The mother bird can sit on the young birds or on the eggs. Do not take the mother with the young birds.

**7** Let the mother go. You can take the young birds for yourself. Then all will be well for you, and you will live a long time.

**8** "When you build a new house, put a low wall around the edge of the roof. Then if a person falls from the roof, you will not be guilty of his death.

**9** "Do not plant 2 types of seed in your vineyard. If you do, you must give all the crops to the holy place, both the seed and the grapes.

**10** Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together.

**11** Do not wear clothes made of wool and linen together.

**12** Put tassels on the 4 corners of the coat that you wear.

**13** "A man can marry a woman and sleep with her. Then he can start to hate her.

**14** He can accuse her of shameful things and give her a bad reputation. He can say, 'I married this woman. But when I slept with her, I did not find proof that she was a virgin.'

**15** Then the father and the mother of the young woman must bring the proof that she was a virgin. They must bring it to the elders of the town at the gate.

**16** The father of the young woman must say to the elders, 'I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, but he hates her.

**17** He accuses her of shameful things. He says, "I did not find that your daughter was a virgin." But here is the proof that my daughter was a virgin.' Then her parents must spread the cloth in front of the elders of the town.

**18** Then the elders of that town must take the man and punish him.

**19** They must make him pay 100 shekels of silver to the father of the young woman. They do this because he gave a bad reputation to a virgin of Israel. She will stay his wife. He must not divorce her for all his life.

**20** "But the accusation can be true. There can be no proof that the young woman was a virgin.

**21** If so, the men of her town must bring her out to the door of the house of her father. They must throw stones at her until she dies. She did a shameful thing in Israel. She had sex with a man while she lived in the house of her father. Thus remove the evil from among you.

**22** "A man can have sex with the wife of another man. If someone finds them, both of them must die. The man and the woman must die. Thus remove the evil from Israel.

**23** "A young woman who is a virgin can have a promise of marriage to a man. Another man can meet her in a town and have sex with her.

**24** Then take both of them to the gate of that town. Throw stones at them until they die. The young woman must die because she did not shout for help in the town. The man must die because he dishonored the wife of his neighbor. Thus remove the evil from among you.

**25** "But a man can meet an engaged young woman in a field. He can use force and have sex with her. Then only the man who had sex with her must die.

**26** Do nothing to the young woman. She did no sin that deserves death. This case is like the case of a man who attacks his neighbor and kills him.

**27** The man met her in the field. The engaged young woman shouted for help, but no one was there to save her.

**28** "A man can meet a young woman who is a virgin and who has no promise of marriage to a man. He can take her and have sex with her. Then someone can find them.

**29** If so, the man must pay 50 shekels of silver to the father of the young woman. She must become his wife, because he dishonored her. He must not divorce her for all his life.

**30** "A man must not marry the wife of his father. He must not dishonor his father.

## Chapter 23

**1** "A man whose sexual organs have damage or whose sexual organs someone cut off must not come into the assembly of the LORD.

**2** A person born from a forbidden marriage must not come into the assembly of the LORD. His descendants must not come into the assembly of the LORD, even to the 10th generation.

**3** No Ammonite or Moabite must come into the assembly of the LORD. Their descendants must not come into the assembly of the LORD, even to the 10th generation, for all time.

**4** The Ammonites and the Moabites did not give you bread and water on the road when you came out of Egypt. They also paid Balaam the son of Beor from Pethor in Mesopotamia to curse you.

**5** But the LORD your God did not listen to Balaam. The LORD your God changed the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loved you.

**6** Never make a peace agreement with them or help them to become rich, for all your life.

**7** "Do not hate an Edomite, because he is your brother. Do not hate an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.

**8** The third generation of their children can come into the assembly of the LORD.

**9** "When your army goes out to fight against your enemies, keep away from all evil things.

**10** A man can become unclean because of an emission of semen at night. If so, he must go out of the camp. He must not come into the camp.

**11** In the evening he must wash himself with water. When the sun goes down, he can come back into the camp.

**12** "Have a place outside the camp where you can go to be a toilet.

**13** Have a tool for holes with your equipment. When you go outside the camp to empty your body, dig a hole with the tool. Then cover your waste.

**14** The LORD your God walks in your camp to protect you and to defeat your enemies in front of you. Thus your camp must be holy. The LORD must not see anything unclean among you. If he does, he will turn away from you.

**15** "A slave can run away from his master and come to you. Do not send him back to his master.

**16** Let him live among you in any town that he chooses. Let him live where he wants. Do not treat him badly.

**17** "No Israelite woman or man must become a temple prostitute.

**18** Do not bring the money from a female or male prostitute into the house of the LORD your God to pay a vow. The LORD your God hates both of these things.

**19** "Do not charge interest when you lend to your brother. Do not charge interest on money, food or any thing that you lend.

**20** You can charge interest to a foreigner. But do not charge interest to your brother. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all that you do in the land that you go into to take.

**21** "When you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not wait to do what you promised. The LORD your God will surely demand it from you. If you do not do it, you will be guilty of sin.

**22** But if you do not make a vow, you are not guilty of sin.

**23** Be careful to do what you say. Do what you promised freely to the LORD your God with your mouth.

**24** "When you go into the vineyard of your neighbor, you can eat as many grapes as you want. But do not put any grapes in your basket.

**25** When you go into the grain field of your neighbor, you can pull off the heads of grain with your hand. But do not cut the grain of your neighbor with a sickle.

## Chapter 24

**1** "A man can marry a woman, and then he is not happy with her because he finds something shameful in her. Then he must write a document of divorce. He must give it to her and send her away from his house.

**2** After she goes away from his house, she can marry another man.

**3** The second husband can also hate her. He can write a document of divorce, give it to her and send her away from his house. Or the second husband can die.

**4** Then her first husband, who sent her away, must not marry her again. She is now unclean to him. The LORD hates this. Do not bring sin on the land that the LORD your God gives you as your property.

**5** "When a man marries a new wife, he must not go to war. Do not give him any other duty. He must be free to stay at home for 1 year and make his wife happy.

**6** "Do not take a millstone, either the lower or the upper stone, as a guarantee for a debt. If you do, you take the thing that a man needs to live.

**7** "A man can kidnap one of his brothers, a person of Israel. He can treat him as a slave or sell him. Then that kidnapper must die. Thus remove the evil from among you.

**8** "When there is a skin disease (leprosy), be careful to obey all that the Levitical priests teach you. Be careful to do as I commanded them.

**9** Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the road after you came out of Egypt.

**10** "When you lend any thing to your neighbor, do not go into his house to get the thing that he gives as a guarantee.

**11** Stay outside. Then the man who borrows from you will bring the guarantee outside to you.

**12** If the man is poor, do not keep his guarantee during the night.

**13** Give it back to him when the sun goes down. Then he can sleep in his coat, and he will bless you. The LORD your God will see that you did a righteous thing.

**14** "Do not treat badly a hired worker who is poor and needy. Do this for your brothers and for the foreigners who live in your towns.

**15** Pay him his wages each day before the sun goes down. He is poor and he needs the money. If you do not pay him, he will cry to the LORD against you. Then you will be guilty of sin.

**16** "Do not kill fathers for the sins of their children. Do not kill children for the sins of their fathers. Each person must die for his own sin.

**17** "Do not take away the rights of a foreigner or an orphan. Do not take the coat of a widow as a guarantee for a debt.

**18** Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. The LORD your God made you free from there. Thus I command you to do this.

**19** "When you cut the grain in your field, you can forget a bundle of grain. Do not go back to get it. Leave it for the foreigner, the orphan and the widow. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all your work.

**20** When you hit your olive trees to get the olives, do not go over the branches a second time. Leave the other olives for the foreigner, the orphan and the widow.

**21** When you gather the grapes in your vineyard, do not go over the vines a second time. Leave the other grapes for the foreigner, the orphan and the widow.

**22** Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. Thus I command you to do this.

## Chapter 25

**1** "Men can have a dispute and go to court. The judges will decide the case. They must say that the innocent man is not guilty. They must say that the guilty man is guilty.

**2** The guilty man can deserve punishment with a whip. If so, the judge must make him lie down. Then someone must hit him in front of the judge. The number of hits must agree with his crime.

**3** The judge can give him a maximum of 40 hits. He must not give more hits. If someone hits your brother more, your brother will have shame in front of you.

**4** "Do not put a cover on the mouth of an ox while it walks on the grain to separate it.

**5** "Brothers can live together, and one of them can die with no son. Then his widow must not marry a man from outside the family. The brother of her husband must marry her. He must do the duty of a brother-in-law to her.

**6** Her first son will have the name of the dead brother. Then the name of the dead brother will not disappear from Israel.

**7** But the man can refuse to marry the widow of his brother. Then she must go to the elders at the town gate. She must say, 'The brother of my husband refuses to keep the name of his brother in Israel. He refuses to do the duty of a brother-in-law to me.'

**8** Then the elders of his town must call him and speak to him. He can still refuse and say, 'I do not want to marry her.'

**9** Then the widow of his brother must go to him in front of the elders. She must pull his sandal off his foot and spit in his face. She must say, 'This is what we do to a man who refuses to give his brother a family.'

**10** In Israel people will call his family 'The family of the man who lost his sandal.'

**11** "2 men can fight together. The wife of one man can come near to save her husband from the man who attacks him. She can put out her hand and take hold of the sexual organs of the other man.

**12** If so, cut off her hand. Do not feel pity for her.

**13** "Do not have 2 different weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.

**14** Do not have 2 different measures in your house, one large and one small.

**15** Have correct and honest weights and measures. Then you will live a long time in the land that the LORD your God gives you.

**16** The LORD your God hates all people who do such things, all people who are not honest.

**17** "Remember what the Amalekites did to you on the road when you came out of Egypt.

**18** They met you on the road when you were weak and had no strength. They attacked all the weak people at the rear of your group. They did not fear God.

**19** The LORD your God will give you rest from all your enemies around you in the land that he gives you as your property. Then destroy the Amalekites completely, so that no one on earth remembers them. Do not forget!

## Chapter 26

**1** "You will come into the land that the LORD your God gives you as your property. You will take it and live in it.

**2** Then take some of the first crops that you grow in the land that the LORD your God gives you. Put them in a basket. Go to the place that the LORD your God will choose for his name.

**3** Go to the priest who serves at that time. Say to him, 'Today I tell the LORD your God that I came into the land. The LORD promised this land to our fathers to give to us.'

**4** Then the priest must take the basket from you. He must put it down in front of the altar of the LORD your God.

**5** Then say in front of the LORD your God, 'My father was an Aramean who went from place to place. He went down into Egypt with a few people and lived there as a foreigner. There his family became a large, strong nation with many people.

**6** But the Egyptians treated us badly and caused us to suffer. They made us work hard as slaves.

**7** Then we cried to the LORD, the God of our fathers. The LORD heard us. He saw our pain, our hard work and our trouble.

**8** The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and a powerful arm. He did great and terrible things. He used signs and wonders.

**9** He brought us into this place and gave us this land. It is a land that has much milk and honey.

**10** Now I bring the first crops of the land that you, LORD, gave me.' Then put the basket in front of the LORD your God and bow down to him.

**11** Be happy about all the good things that the LORD your God gave to you and your family. You, the Levites and the foreigners among you must be happy.

**12** "In the 3rd year, the year of the tithe, give the tithe of all your crops. Give it to the Levites, the foreigners, the orphans and the widows. Then they can eat in your towns until they are full.

**13** Then say in front of the LORD your God, 'I removed the holy part from my house. I gave it to the Levites, the foreigners, the orphans and the widows, as you commanded me. I did not disobey your commands or forget them.

**14** I did not eat any of the tithe while I mourned. I did not remove any of it while I was unclean. I did not give any of it to the dead. I obeyed the LORD my God. I did all that you commanded me.

**15** Look down from your holy home in heaven. Bless your people Israel. Bless the land that you gave us, as you promised to our fathers. It is a land that has much milk and honey.'

**16** "Today the LORD your God commands you to obey these laws and rules. Be careful to obey them with all your heart and with all your soul.

**17** Today you said that the LORD is your God. You said that you will live in his ways and obey his laws, his commands and his rules. You said that you will obey him.

**18** Today the LORD said that you are his special people, as he promised you. He said that you must obey all his commands.

**19** He will make you greater than all the nations that he made. You will have praise, fame and honor. You will be a holy people to the LORD your God, as he promised."

## Chapter 27

**1** Moses and the elders of Israel gave a command to the people. They said, "Obey all the commands that I give you today.

**2** On the day that you go across the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God gives you, put up some large stones. Cover them with plaster.

**3** Write on them all the words of this law after you go across. Then you will go into the land that the LORD your God gives you. It is a land that has much milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, promised you.

**4** After you go across the Jordan, put up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I command you today. Cover them with plaster.

**5** Build an altar of stones there to the LORD your God. Do not use any iron tool on the stones.

**6** Build the altar of the LORD your God with whole stones. Do not cut them with a tool. Offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.

**7** Offer peace offerings and eat them there. Be happy in front of the LORD your God.

**8** Write all the words of this law very clearly on the stones."

**9** Then Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel. They said, "Be quiet and listen, Israel. Today you became the people of the LORD your God.

**10** So obey the LORD your God. Obey his commands and his laws that I give you today."

**11** On the same day Moses gave this command to the people:

**12** "After you go across the Jordan, these tribes must stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.

**13** These tribes must stand on Mount Ebal to announce the curses: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.

**14** The Levites must speak to all the men of Israel with a loud voice. They must say,

**15** 'God curses the man who makes an idol of carved wood or of metal and hides it. The LORD hates idols that a skilled worker makes.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**16** 'God curses the person who does not honor his father or his mother.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**17** 'God curses the person who moves the boundary stone of his neighbor.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**18** 'God curses the person who causes a blind person to go the wrong way on the road.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**19** 'God curses the person who takes away the rights of the foreigner, the orphan or the widow.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**20** 'God curses the man who has sex with the wife of his father, because he dishonors his father.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**21** 'God curses the person who has sex with any animal.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**22** 'God curses the man who has sex with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**23** 'God curses the man who has sex with his mother-in-law.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**24** 'God curses the person who secretly kills his neighbor.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**25** 'God curses the person who takes money to kill an innocent person.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

**26** 'God curses the person who does not obey all the words of this law.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

## Chapter 28

**1** "Carefully obey the LORD your God and all his commands that I give you today. If you do this, the LORD your God will make you greater than all the nations on the earth.

**2** If you obey the LORD your God, then all these blessings will come to you:

**3** The LORD will bless you in the city. He will bless you in the field.

**4** He will bless your children, your crops and the young of your cattle and your sheep.

**5** He will bless your basket and your bowl for bread.

**6** He will bless you when you come in. He will bless you when you go out.

**7** "The LORD will defeat the enemies who attack you. They will come against you from 1 direction, but they will run away from you in 7 directions.

**8** The LORD will bless your storehouses and all that you do. He will bless you in the land that the LORD your God gives you.

**9** The LORD will make you his holy people, as he promised you. He will do this if you obey the commands of the LORD your God and live in his ways.

**10** Then all the peoples of the earth will see that you belong to the LORD. They will be afraid of you.

**11** The LORD will give you much wealth. He will give you many children, many young animals and many crops. He will do this in the land that he promised to your fathers to give you.

**12** The LORD will open the sky, his storehouse of good things. He will send rain on your land at the correct time. He will bless all your work. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.

**13** The LORD will make you the leader, not the follower. You will always be at the top, never at the bottom. This will occur if you carefully obey the commands of the LORD your God that I give you today.

**14** Do not turn away from any of the commands that I give you today, to the right or to the left. Do not worship and serve other gods.

**15** "But you can disobey the LORD your God. You can fail to obey all his commands and laws that I give you today. If so, all these curses will come to you:

**16** The LORD will curse you in the city. He will curse you in the field.

**17** He will curse your basket and your bowl for bread.

**18** He will curse your children, your crops and the young of your cattle and your sheep.

**19** He will curse you when you come in. He will curse you when you go out.

**20** "The LORD will send on you curses, confusion and trouble in all that you do. He will do this until he destroys you and you die quickly. This will occur because you did evil things and left him.

**21** The LORD will make you sick with terrible diseases until he removes you from the land that you go into to take.

**22** The LORD will attack you with sickness, fever and pain. He will attack you with very hot heat, with war, with hot winds and with disease in your plants. These things will chase you until you die.

**23** The sky above you will be hard like bronze. The ground below you will be hard like iron.

**24** The LORD will change the rain of your land into dust. Dust will come down on you from the sky until it destroys you.

**25** "The LORD will let your enemies defeat you. You will go against them from 1 direction, but you will run away from them in 7 directions. All the kingdoms of the earth will have fear when they see you.

**26** Your dead bodies will be food for all the birds and the wild animals. No one will chase them away.

**27** The LORD will attack you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, with sores and with itch. No one will be able to cure you.

**28** The LORD will attack you with madness, blindness and confusion of mind.

**29** At noon you will feel your way as a blind person does in the dark. You will not be successful in anything that you do. People will always treat you badly and steal from you. No one will save you.

**30** You will become engaged to a woman, but another man will have sex with her. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not eat its grapes.

**31** Your enemies will kill your ox in front of you, but you will not eat its meat. They will take your donkey from you, and they will not give it back. They will take your sheep, and no one will help you.

**32** Another people will take your sons and your daughters. Each day you will look for your children, but you will not see them. You will be powerless.

**33** A nation that you do not know will eat your crops and all that you worked for. People will always treat you badly and crush you.

**34** The things that you see will make you mad.

**35** The LORD will attack your knees and your legs with painful boils that no one can cure. The boils will cover you from your feet to the top of your head.

**36** "The LORD will send you and the king that you choose to a nation that you and your fathers did not know. There you will serve other gods, gods of wood and stone.

**37** In all the nations where the LORD sends you, the people will have shock when they see you. They will laugh at you and make jokes about you.

**38** You will plant much seed in the field, but you will gather only a little crop. Locusts will eat it.

**39** You will plant vineyards and work in them. But you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them.

**40** You will have olive trees in all your land, but you will not have olive oil for your body. The olives will fall off the trees.

**41** You will have sons and daughters, but they will not stay with you. Enemies will take them as prisoners.

**42** Locusts will eat all your trees and the crops of your land.

**43** The foreigners who live among you will become more and more powerful. You will become weaker and weaker.

**44** They will lend to you, but you will not lend to them. They will be the leaders, and you will be the followers.

**45** "All these curses will come to you. They will chase you and catch you until they destroy you. This will occur because you did not obey the LORD your God. You did not keep his commands and laws that he gave you.

**46** These curses will be a sign and a wonder against you and your descendants for all time.

**47** You did not serve the LORD your God with joy and a happy heart when you had all things.

**48** Thus you will serve the enemies that the LORD sends against you. You will be hungry, thirsty and naked. You will need all things. The LORD will put an iron yoke on your neck until he destroys you.

**49** "The LORD will bring a nation against you from far away, from the end of the earth. It will attack you as fast as an eagle. You will not understand its language.

**50** The people of that nation will look cruel. They will not respect old people or show mercy to young people.

**51** They will eat the young of your animals and the crops of your land until they destroy you. They will not leave you any grain, new wine or olive oil. They will not leave you any young cattle or sheep. They will do this until they destroy you.

**52** They will attack all the towns in your land. They will attack until your high, strong walls fall down. You trusted these walls. They will attack all the towns in the land that the LORD your God gave you.

**53** "Your enemies will put their army around your towns, and you will suffer greatly. Then you will eat your own children. You will eat the bodies of the sons and daughters that the LORD your God gave you.

**54** Even the most gentle and kind man among you will become selfish. He will refuse to share food with his brother, his loved wife and the children that he still has.

**55** He will not give them any of the meat of his children that he eats. He will have nothing else to eat, because of the pain that your enemies cause in all your towns.

**56** Even the most gentle and kind woman among you will become selfish. Before, she was too gentle to put her foot on the ground. But she will refuse to share food with her loved husband, her son and her daughter.

**57** She will secretly eat the baby that she gives birth to. She will eat her children because she has nothing else to eat. This will occur because of the pain that your enemies cause in your towns.

**58** "Be careful to obey all the words of this law that Moses wrote in this book. Fear this glorious and terrible name, the LORD your God.

**59** If you do not, the LORD will send terrible disasters on you and your descendants. He will send great disasters that continue for a long time. He will send bad sicknesses that continue for a long time.

**60** He will send on you all the diseases of Egypt that you were afraid of. These diseases will stay with you.

**61** The LORD will also send each sickness and each disaster that this book of the law does not name. He will send them until he destroys you.

**62** You were as many as the stars in the sky. But only a few of you will stay alive, because you did not obey the LORD your God.

**63** Before, the LORD was happy to do good things for you and to make you many. In the same way, the LORD will be happy to destroy you. He will remove you from the land that you go into to take.

**64** "The LORD will send you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end. There you will serve other gods of wood and stone. You and your fathers did not know these gods.

**65** Among those nations you will have no peace. You will not find a place to rest. The LORD will make your heart afraid, your eyes tired and your soul sad.

**66** You will always be in danger of death. You will be afraid day and night. You will never be sure of your life.

**67** In the morning you will say, 'I wish that it was evening!' In the evening you will say, 'I wish that it was morning!' You will say these things because of the fear in your heart and the things that you see.

**68** The LORD will send you back to Egypt in ships. He will send you on the journey that I told you that you will never make again. There you will try to sell yourselves as slaves to your enemies. But no one will buy you."

## Chapter 29

**1** These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the people of Israel in the land of Moab. This covenant is in addition to the covenant that the LORD made with them at Horeb.

**2** Moses called all Israel together. He said to them, "You saw all that the LORD did in the land of Egypt. You saw what he did to Pharaoh, to all his officials and to all his land.

**3** You saw the great tests, the signs and the great wonders.

**4** But to this day the LORD did not give you a heart that understands. He did not give you eyes that see or ears that hear.

**5** For 40 years I led you in the wilderness. During that time your clothes did not wear out, and your sandals did not wear out on your feet.

**6** You did not eat bread or drink wine or strong drink. The LORD did this so that you will know that he is the LORD your God.

**7** When you came to this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon and Og the king of Bashan came out to fight against us. But we defeated them.

**8** We took their land. We gave it as property to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh.

**9** So carefully obey the words of this covenant. Then you will be successful in all that you do.

**10** "Today all of you stand in front of the LORD your God. Your leaders, your tribes, your elders, your officers and all the men of Israel are here.

**11** Your children, your wives and the foreigners in your camp are also here. The people who cut your wood and the people who carry your water are here.

**12** You stand here to make a covenant with the LORD your God. Today the LORD your God makes this covenant with you, with a solemn promise.

**13** Today he makes you his people, and he will be your God. He told you this, and he promised this to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

**14** I do not make this covenant and this promise only with you.

**15** I make it with all who stand here with us today in front of the LORD our God. I also make it with the people who are not here with us today.

**16** "You know how we lived in the land of Egypt. You know how we went through the nations on our journey.

**17** You saw their hated things and their idols of wood, stone, silver and gold.

**18** Be sure that no man, woman, family or tribe among you turns away from the LORD our God today. Do not let anyone go and worship the gods of those nations. Such a person is like a root that grows a poisonous and bitter plant.

**19** That person can hear the words of this curse but think that he is safe. He can say, 'All will be well for me, even if I do what I want.' This person will cause destruction to the good and the bad alike.

**20** The LORD will not forgive that person. The anger and the jealousy of the LORD will burn against him. All the curses in this book will come to him. The LORD will remove his name from the earth.

**21** The LORD will choose him from all the tribes of Israel for disaster. He will do to him all the curses of the covenant in this book of the law.

**22** "Your children in future generations will see the disasters and the sicknesses that the LORD sends on that land. Foreigners from far away will also see them.

**23** They will see that all the land is a burned waste of sulfur and salt. No one plants in it, nothing grows in it and no grass comes up. It will be like the destruction of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim. The LORD destroyed those cities in his anger.

**24** All the nations will ask, 'Why did the LORD do this to this land? Why is his anger so great?'

**25** Then people will say, 'The people of this land left the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers. He made this covenant with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.

**26** They went and served and worshipped other gods. They did not know these gods, and the LORD did not give these gods to them.

**27** So the LORD became angry with this land. He brought on it all the curses in this book.

**28** The LORD was very angry, and he removed them from their land. He sent them into another land, as it is today.'

**29** "The secret things belong to the LORD our God. But the things that he showed us belong to us and to our children for all time. Then we can obey all the words of this law.

## Chapter 30

**1** "All these things will occur to you, the blessings and the curses that I put in front of you. Then you will remember them among all the nations where the LORD your God sends you.

**2** You and your children will come back to the LORD your God. You will obey him with all your heart and with all your soul. You will do all that I command you today.

**3** Then the LORD your God will make you successful again and show you mercy. He will gather you again from all the nations where the LORD your God sent you.

**4** Some of your people can be in the farthest parts of the earth. But the LORD your God will gather you from there and bring you back.

**5** The LORD your God will bring you into the land that your fathers had, and you will take it. He will make you more successful and more numerous than your fathers.

**6** The LORD your God will make your hearts and the hearts of your descendants obedient, as a circumcision of the heart. Then you will love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, and you will live.

**7** The LORD your God will put all these curses on your enemies. He will put them on the people who hate you and who caused you to suffer.

**8** You will again obey the LORD. You will do all his commands that I give you today.

**9** The LORD your God will make you very successful in all your work. He will give you many children, many young animals and many crops. The LORD will again be happy to do good things for you, as he was happy with your fathers.

**10** He will do this if you obey the LORD your God. Keep his commands and his laws in this book of the law. Come back to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

**11** "The command that I give you today is not too difficult for you. It is not too far away from you.

**12** It is not in heaven. So you do not need to ask, 'Who will go up to heaven to get it for us? Who will tell it to us so that we can obey it?'

**13** It is not on the other side of the sea. So you do not need to ask, 'Who will go across the sea to get it for us? Who will tell it to us so that we can obey it?'

**14** No, the word is very near to you. It is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can obey it.

**15** "Look, today I give you a choice between life and good, and death and evil.

**16** Today I command you to love the LORD your God. Live in his ways and obey his commands, his laws and his rules. Then you will live and become many. The LORD your God will bless you in the land that you go into to take.

**17** But your heart can turn away, and you can refuse to obey. Something can tempt you to bow down to other gods and worship them.

**18** If so, I tell you today that you will surely die. You will not live for a long time in the land that you go across the Jordan to take.

**19** Today I tell heaven and earth to be witnesses against you. I give you a choice between life and death, between blessings and curses. Choose life, so that you and your descendants will live.

**20** Love the LORD your God, obey him and stay loyal to him. He is your life. He will let you live for a long time in the land that the LORD promised to give to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob."

## Chapter 31

**1** Then Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.

**2** He said to them, "Today I am 120 years old. I cannot lead you any more. Also, the LORD told me, 'You will not go across this Jordan.'

**3** The LORD your God will go across in front of you. He will destroy these nations in front of you, and you will take their land. Joshua will also go across in front of you, as the LORD said.

**4** The LORD will destroy these nations, as he destroyed Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and their land.

**5** The LORD will give the nations to you. Do to them all that I commanded you.

**6** Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid of them, and do not shake with fear. The LORD your God goes with you. He will not fail you or leave you."

**7** Then Moses called Joshua. In front of all Israel he said to Joshua, "Be strong and brave. You will go with this people into the land that the LORD promised to their fathers to give them. You will help them take the land as their property.

**8** The LORD himself goes in front of you. He will be with you. He will not fail you or leave you. Do not be afraid, and do not lose courage."

**9** Then Moses wrote this law. He gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD. He also gave it to all the elders of Israel.

**10** Then Moses gave them this command: "At the end of each 7 years, in the year to cancel debts, at the Festival of Shelters,

**11** all Israel will come to the LORD your God at the place that he will choose. Then read this law to all Israel so that they can hear it.

**12** Gather the people together: the men, the women, the children and the foreigners who live in your towns. Then they will hear and learn to fear the LORD your God. They will be careful to obey all the words of this law.

**13** Their children, who do not know this law, will hear it. They will learn to fear the LORD your God for all the time that you live in the land. This is the land that you go across the Jordan to take."

**14** Then the LORD said to Moses, "The day of your death is near. Call Joshua. Come to the tabernacle (Tent of Meeting) together. There I will give him my orders." So Moses and Joshua went to the tabernacle.

**15** Then the LORD appeared at the tabernacle in a column of cloud. The column of cloud stood over the door of the tabernacle.

**16** The LORD said to Moses, "Soon you will die, as your fathers did. Then these people will be unfaithful to me. They will worship the foreign gods of the land that they go into. They will leave me and break the covenant that I made with them.

**17** On that day I will become angry with them. I will leave them and hide my face from them. Their enemies will destroy them. Many disasters and troubles will come to them. On that day they will say, 'These disasters came to us because our God is not with us.'

**18** On that day I will surely hide my face from them. I will do this because of all the evil things that they did when they turned to other gods.

**19** "So write this song for yourselves. Teach it to the people of Israel and help them sing it. Then this song will be my witness against the people of Israel.

**20** I will bring them into the land that I promised to their fathers. It is a land that has much milk and honey. They will eat until they are full and fat. Then they will turn to other gods and worship them. They will reject me and break my covenant.

**21** Then many disasters and troubles will come to them. This song will be a witness against them, because their descendants will not forget it. I know what they plan to do now, before I bring them into the land that I promised."

**22** So on that day Moses wrote this song and taught it to the people of Israel.

**23** Then the LORD gave Joshua the son of Nun his orders. He said, "Be strong and brave. You will bring the people of Israel into the land that I promised them. I will be with you."

**24** Moses wrote all the words of this law in a book until he completed it.

**25** Then Moses gave a command to the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD. He said,

**26** "Take this book of the law and put it next to the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God. It will stay there as a witness against you.

**27** I know that you are stubborn and that you disobey. You disobeyed the LORD while I was alive with you. You will disobey him more after my death.

**28** Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your officers. I will speak these words to them. I will tell heaven and earth to be witnesses against them.

**29** I know that after my death you will become completely evil. You will turn away from the way that I commanded you. In the future, disaster will come to you, because you will do evil in the sight of the LORD. You will make him angry with the idols that you make."

**30** Then Moses spoke all the words of this song to all the assembly of Israel, from the start to the end.

## Chapter 32

**1** "Heavens, listen, and I will speak. Earth, hear the words of my mouth.

**2** My words will fall like rain. My message will come down like dew. It will be like light rain on new grass and like showers on plants.

**3** I will announce the name of the LORD. Praise the greatness of our God!

**4** He is the Rock. His work is perfect, and all his ways are fair. He is a faithful God who does no wrong. He is honest and right.

**5** But his people did evil things against him. They are not his children, because of their sin. They are an evil and dishonest generation.

**6** Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish people with no wisdom? He is your father, who made you his own. He made you and gave you strength.

**7** Remember the past. Think about the years of many generations. Ask your father, and he will tell you. Ask your elders, and they will explain to you.

**8** The Most High gave the nations their land. He divided all humans into nations. He set the borders of the peoples by the number of the sons of Israel.

**9** The people of the LORD are his own part. Jacob is his own property.

**10** The LORD found Jacob in a desert land, in an empty wilderness where the wind blew. He protected him and took care of him. He guarded him as a man guards his own eye.

**11** An eagle shakes her nest and flies over her young birds. She spreads her wings to catch them and carries them on her wings.

**12** In the same way, the LORD alone led Jacob. No foreign god was with him.

**13** The LORD let Jacob live on the high land and eat the crops of the fields. He gave him honey from the rocks and olive oil from the hard rock.

**14** He gave him butter from the cattle and milk from the sheep. He gave him the best lambs, rams and goats from Bashan, and the best wheat. You drank the red wine of the grape.

**15** But Jeshurun (Israel) became fat and kicked against God. You became fat, heavy and full. Then Israel left God, who made him. He rejected the Rock who saved him.

**16** The people made God jealous with foreign gods. They made him angry with hated idols.

**17** They made sacrifices to demons, which are not God. They worshipped gods that they did not know. These were new gods that their fathers did not fear.

**18** You forgot the Rock who gave you life. You forgot God who made you.

**19** The LORD saw this and rejected them. His sons and his daughters made him angry.

**20** He said, 'I will hide my face from them. I will see what their end will be. They are an evil generation, children who are not faithful.

**21** They made me jealous with things that are not gods. They made me angry with their worthless idols. So I will make them jealous with people who are not a nation. I will make them angry with a foolish nation.

**22** My anger burns like a fire. It burns down to the deepest place of the dead. It burns the earth and its crops. It burns the bottom of the mountains.

**23** I will send many disasters on them. I will shoot all my arrows at them.

**24** They will become weak from hunger. Fever and terrible disease will destroy them. I will send wild animals to bite them. I will send poisonous snakes that move in the dust.

**25** Outside, the sword will kill them. Inside, terror will kill them. It will kill young men and young women. It will kill babies and old men.

**26** I said that I will send them far away. I will cause all people to forget them.

**27** But I did not want their enemies to say proud things. I did not want their enemies to misunderstand and say, "We won with our own power. The LORD did not do all this."'

**28** Israel is a nation without good sense. They do not understand.

**29** I wish that they were wise and understood this. I wish that they thought about their future!

**30** How can 1 enemy chase 1,000 of them? How can 2 enemies cause 10,000 to run away? Only if their Rock sold them. Only if the LORD gave them to their enemies.

**31** The rock of our enemies is not like our Rock. Even our enemies know this.

**32** The people of our enemies are like the grapevines of Sodom and the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are poisonous, and their bunches of grapes are bitter.

**33** Their wine is like the poison of snakes, the deadly poison of cobras.

**34** 'I keep this in mind. I keep it locked in my storehouse.

**35** I will punish them and pay them back. At the correct time, their feet will slip. The day of their disaster is near. Their destruction will come quickly.'

**36** The LORD will judge his people and show mercy to his servants. He will see that their strength is gone. He will see that no one remains, slave or free.

**37** Then he will say, 'Where are their gods now? Where is the rock that they trusted?

**38** Their gods ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings. Let those gods get up and help you! Let them protect you!

**39** Now see that I alone am God. There is no other god but me. I kill, and I give life. I wound, and I heal. No one can save anyone from my power.

**40** I lift up my hand to heaven and make a solemn promise. As surely as I live for all time,

**41** I will sharpen my bright sword. I will take hold of it to judge. I will punish my enemies. I will pay back the people who hate me.

**42** Their blood will cover my arrows. My sword will kill many people. I will kill the wounded and the prisoners. I will kill the leaders of the enemy.'

**43** Nations, be happy with his people. He will punish the people who kill his servants. He will punish his enemies. He will make his land and his people clean from sin."

**44** Moses came with Joshua the son of Nun. They spoke all the words of this song to the people.

**45** Moses completed all these words to all Israel.

**46** Then he said to them, "Think carefully about all the words that I tell you today to warn you. Command your children to carefully obey all the words of this law.

**47** These words are not useless for you. They are your life. If you obey them, you will live for a long time in the land that you go across the Jordan to take."

**48** On that same day the LORD said to Moses,

**49** "Go up into the Abarim Mountains, to Mount Nebo in the land of Moab, opposite Jericho. Look at the land of Canaan, which I give to the people of Israel as their property.

**50** You will die on the mountain that you go up. You will join your people who died before you. This is as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and joined his people.

**51** Both of you were not faithful to me among the people of Israel. This occurred at the waters of Meribah-kadesh in the wilderness of Zin. You did not show the people of Israel that I am holy.

**52** You will see the land from far away. But you will not go into the land that I give to the people of Israel."

## Chapter 33

**1** This is the blessing that Moses, the man of God, gave to the people of Israel before his death.

**2** He said, "The LORD came from Sinai. He came to his people like the sunrise from Seir. He shone from Mount Paran. He came with 10,000 holy angels. A fiery law was in his right hand for them.

**3** The LORD loves his people. All his holy people are in his hand. They sit at his feet, and each one gets his words.

**4** Moses gave us a law. This law is the property of the people of Jacob.

**5** The LORD was king over Jeshurun (Israel). He was king when the leaders of the people and the tribes of Israel gathered together.

**6** "Let Reuben live and not die. But let his men be few."

**7** This is what Moses said about Judah: "LORD, hear the cry of Judah. Bring him back to his people. Fight for him with your power. Help him against his enemies."

**8** About Levi he said, "LORD, your Thummim and your Urim belong to your loyal servant. You tested him at Massah. You argued with him at the waters of Meribah.

**9** He said about his father and his mother, 'I do not have regard for them.' He did not accept his brothers or know his own children. The Levites obeyed your word and kept your covenant.

**10** They will teach your rules to Jacob and your law to Israel. They will put incense in front of you and burnt offerings on your altar.

**11** LORD, bless his work and accept all that he does. Crush his enemies and the people who hate him, so that they do not get up again."

**12** About Benjamin he said, "The LORD loves Benjamin. Let him live in safety near the LORD. The LORD protects him all day long. Benjamin lives between his shoulders."

**13** About Joseph he said, "Let the LORD bless his land with the best gifts from heaven. Let him bless it with dew and with the deep water below.

**14** Let him bless it with the best crops that the sun makes grow. Let him bless it with the best crops of each month.

**15** Let him bless it with the best things of the old mountains and the hills that last for all time.

**16** Let him bless it with the best gifts of the earth and all that it contains. Let him bless it with the kindness of the LORD, who lived in the bush that burned. Let these blessings come on the head of Joseph. He was the prince among his brothers.

**17** He is strong like a firstborn bull. His horns are like the horns of a wild ox. With them he will push back the nations, all the way to the ends of the earth. These horns are the 10,000s of Ephraim and the 1,000s of Manasseh."

**18** About Zebulun he said, "Zebulun, be happy when you go out. Issachar, be happy in your tents.

**19** They will call the peoples to the mountain. There they will offer correct sacrifices. They will get wealth from the seas and from treasures hidden in the sand."

**20** About Gad he said, "Praise the LORD, who makes the land of Gad larger. Gad lives there like a lion. He tears off the arm and the head of his enemies.

**21** He chose the best land for himself. He received the part of a leader. He came with the leaders of the people. He did what the LORD said was right. He obeyed the rules of the LORD with Israel."

**22** About Dan he said, "Dan is a young lion. He jumps out from Bashan."

**23** About Naphtali he said, "Naphtali has many good things from the LORD. He is full of the blessing of the LORD. He will take the land to the west and the south."

**24** About Asher he said, "Asher has the most blessings of all the sons. Let his brothers like him. Let him have very much olive oil.

**25** Your town gates will have bars of iron and bronze. Your strength will continue for all your life.

**26** "No one is like the God of Jeshurun (Israel). He rides across the sky to help you. He rides on the clouds in his majesty.

**27** The eternal God is your place of safety. His arms always hold you up. He will push your enemies away from you. He will say, 'Destroy them!'

**28** So Israel will live in safety. The descendants of Jacob will live alone in a land of grain and new wine. Dew will fall from the sky on that land.

**29** Israel, you are blessed! No other people is like you. The LORD saved you. He is your shield that protects you and your sword that wins for you. Your enemies will bow down to you. You will walk on their high places."

## Chapter 34

**1** Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, opposite Jericho. There the LORD showed him all the land. He showed him Gilead as far as Dan,

**2** all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the Mediterranean Sea.

**3** He showed him the Negev and the plain of the Valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.

**4** Then the LORD said to Moses, "This is the land that I promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.' I let you see it with your eyes, but you will not go across into it."

**5** So Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in the land of Moab, as the LORD said.

**6** The LORD buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor. But to this day no one knows where his grave is.

**7** Moses was 120 years old when he died. His eyes were still good, and he was still strong.

**8** The people of Israel cried for Moses in the plains of Moab for 30 days. Then the time when they mourned for Moses ended.

**9** Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, because Moses put his hands on him. So the people of Israel obeyed Joshua. They did as the LORD commanded Moses.

**10** Since that time, no prophet in Israel was like Moses. The LORD knew Moses face to face.

**11** The LORD sent Moses to do all the signs and the wonders in the land of Egypt. Moses did them against Pharaoh, all his officials and all his land.

**12** No other prophet showed such great power. No other prophet did such terrible things in front of all Israel as Moses did.

---

# Joshua

## Chapter 1

**1** Moses, the servant of the LORD, died. After his death, the LORD spoke to Joshua the son of Nun. Joshua was the helper of Moses. The LORD said,

**2** "My servant Moses is dead. Thus, get up now and go across the Jordan River. You and all these people must go into the land. I give this land to the people of Israel.

**3** I give you each place where you put your foot. I made this promise to Moses.

**4** Your borders will go from the desert and Lebanon to the big river, the Euphrates River. All the land of the Hittites will be yours. Your border will go west to the Great Sea.

**5** No person will be able to stop you during all your life. I was with Moses, and I will be with you in the same way. I will not fail you. I will not leave you.

**6** Be strong and brave. You will divide the land among these people as their property. I made a promise to their fathers to give them this land.

**7** Be strong and very brave. Obey all the law that my servant Moses gave you. Do not turn away from the law to the right or to the left. Then you will have success in all the places that you go.

**8** Always speak the words of this book of the law. Think about the law during the day and during the night. Then you will obey all the things that it tells you to do. Then you will have success, and your work will go well.

**9** I gave you a command. Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid. Do not lose your courage. The LORD your God is with you in all the places that you go."

**10** Then Joshua gave a command to the officers of the people. He said,

**11** "Go through the camp and tell the people this: 'Prepare food for yourselves. In 3 days you will go across the Jordan River. You will go in and take the land. The LORD your God gives you this land as your property.'"

**12** Joshua also spoke to the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh. He said,

**13** "Remember the command that Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you. He said, 'The LORD your God gives you rest. He gives you this land.'

**14** Your wives, your small children, and your animals will stay in the land on the east side of the Jordan River. Moses gave you that land. But all your strong soldiers must go across in front of your brothers. Take your weapons and help them.

**15** Help them until the LORD gives your brothers rest, as he gave rest to you. Help them until they also take the land that the LORD your God gives them. Then you can go back to your own land and live in it. Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you that land on the east side of the Jordan River."

**16** The men answered Joshua, "We will do all the things that you tell us to do. We will go to each place where you send us.

**17** We obeyed Moses in all things. We will obey you in the same way. We pray that the LORD your God will be with you, as he was with Moses.

**18** If a person does not obey your command and does not obey your words, we will kill that person. Only be strong and brave."

## Chapter 2

**1** Joshua the son of Nun secretly sent 2 men from Shittim to spy. He told them, "Go and look at the land, and look at Jericho." The 2 men went. They came to the house of a prostitute with the name Rahab, and they stayed there that night.

**2** A person told the king of Jericho, "Look, some men from the people of Israel came here tonight. They came to search the country."

**3** The king of Jericho sent a message to Rahab. He said, "Bring out the men who came to you into your house. They came to search all the country."

**4** But the woman took the 2 men and hid them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me. But I did not know where they came from.

**5** When it was dark, at the time to close the city gate, the men went out. I do not know where they went. Go after them quickly. You can catch them."

**6** But Rahab took the men up to the roof of the house. She hid them below the stems of flax plants. She put these stems in lines on the roof.

**7** The king's men went after the 2 men on the road to the places where people cross the Jordan River. The people of Jericho closed the gate after the king's men went out.

**8** The 2 men did not go to sleep yet. Rahab went up to the roof to them.

**9** She said to the men, "I know that the LORD gives you this land. We are very afraid of you. All the people who live in this land have no courage because of you.

**10** We heard how the LORD made the water of the Red Sea dry for you when you came out of Egypt. We also heard what you did to Sihon and Og. They were the 2 kings of the Amorites on the east side of the Jordan River. You destroyed them completely.

**11** When we heard these things, we became very afraid. Nobody has courage now because of you. The LORD your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.

**12** Now please make a promise to me by the LORD. I was kind to you. Thus, promise that you will also be kind to my family. Give me a sign that I can trust.

**13** Promise that you will keep my father, my mother, my brothers, my sisters, and all their families alive. Save us from death."

**14** The men answered her, "We will give our lives for your lives. But you must not tell anybody about our work. When the LORD gives us the land, we will be kind and honest with you."

**15** Then Rahab used a rope to let the men down through the window. Her house was part of the city wall, and she lived on the wall.

**16** She told them, "Go to the hills. Then the men who search for you will not find you. Hide there for 3 days until those men come back. After that, you can go on your way."

**17** The men said to her, "We will keep the promise that you caused us to make. But you must do these things.

**18** When we come into the land, tie this red rope in the window. You used this window to let us down. Bring your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your family into your house.

**19** If a person goes out of the doors of your house into the street, that person will be responsible for his own death. We will not be guilty. But if a person in the house with you gets hurt, we will be responsible for that person's death.

**20** But if you tell anybody about our work, then we will not have to keep the promise that you caused us to make."

**21** Rahab said, "I agree with your words." Then she sent them away, and they went. She tied the red rope in the window.

**22** The 2 men went into the hills and stayed there for 3 days. They stayed until the men who searched for them went back. The king's men searched along all the road, but they did not find the 2 men.

**23** Then the 2 men came down from the hills and went back across the river. They came to Joshua the son of Nun. They told him all the things that occurred.

**24** They said to Joshua, "Truly, the LORD gave all the land to us. All the people who live in the country have no courage because of us."

## Chapter 3

**1** Joshua got up early in the morning. He and all the people of Israel left Shittim and came to the Jordan River. They stayed there before they went across.

**2** After 3 days, the officers went through the camp.

**3** They gave a command to the people. They said, "You will see the ark of the covenant (the holy box of the agreement) of the LORD your God. The priests, who are Levites, will carry it. When you see the ark, leave your place and follow it.

**4** But keep a distance of approximately 2,000 cubits (900 meters) between you and the ark. Do not go near it. Then you will know which way to go, because you did not go on this road before."

**5** Joshua said to the people, "Make yourselves holy. Tomorrow the LORD will do wonderful things among you."

**6** Joshua said to the priests, "Lift the ark of the covenant and go across in front of the people." Thus, the priests lifted the ark of the covenant and went in front of the people.

**7** The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will start to make you great in the eyes of all Israel. Then the people will know that I am with you, as I was with Moses.

**8** Give a command to the priests who carry the ark of the covenant. Tell them, 'When you come to the edge of the water of the Jordan, stop and stand in the river.'"

**9** Joshua said to the people of Israel, "Come here. Listen to the words of the LORD your God."

**10** Joshua said, "This is how you will know that the God who lives is among you. He will surely push out the people in front of you. He will push out the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites.

**11** Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth will go in front of you into the Jordan River.

**12** Now choose 12 men from the tribes of Israel, 1 man from each tribe.

**13** The priests carry the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth. When their feet go into the water of the Jordan, the water will stop. The water that comes down from upstream will stop and stand up as a wall."

**14** The people left their tents to go across the Jordan River. The priests carried the ark of the covenant in front of the people.

**15** It was the time of harvest, and the Jordan River was full above all its banks. The priests who carried the ark came to the Jordan. Their feet touched the edge of the water.

**16** Then the water that came down from upstream stopped. The water stood up as a wall a long distance away, at the city of Adam near Zarethan. The water that flowed down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, stopped completely. The people went across near Jericho.

**17** The priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firmly on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. All the people of Israel went across on dry ground. The priests stood there until all the people were across the Jordan.

## Chapter 4

**1** All the people went across the Jordan River. Then the LORD spoke to Joshua. He said,

**2** "Choose 12 men from the people, 1 man from each tribe.

**3** Give them this command: 'Take 12 stones from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests stood. Carry the stones with you. Put them down in the place where you will stay tonight.'"

**4** Then Joshua called the 12 men that he chose from the people of Israel, 1 man from each tribe.

**5** Joshua said to them, "Go in front of the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan. Each man must lift a stone onto his shoulder. There must be 1 stone for each tribe of the people of Israel.

**6** These stones will be a sign among you. In the future, your children will ask, 'What do these stones mean?'

**7** Then tell them, 'The water of the Jordan stopped in front of the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When the ark went across the Jordan, the water stopped.' These stones will help the people of Israel to remember this event for all time."

**8** The people of Israel did as Joshua told them. They took 12 stones from the middle of the Jordan, as the LORD told Joshua. There was 1 stone for each tribe of the people of Israel. They carried the stones to the place where they stayed. They put the stones down there.

**9** Joshua also put 12 stones in the middle of the Jordan, at the place where the priests with the ark of the covenant stood. These stones are there today.

**10** The priests who carried the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan. They stood there until the people did all the things that the LORD told Joshua. Moses also gave Joshua these commands. The people went across quickly.

**11** When all the people were across, the ark of the LORD and the priests went across in front of the people.

**12** The men of Reuben, the men of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh went across in front of the people of Israel. They carried their weapons, as Moses told them.

**13** Approximately 40,000 soldiers, ready for war, went across in front of the LORD to the plains of Jericho.

**14** On that day, the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel. The people respected Joshua all his life, as they respected Moses.

**15** The LORD said to Joshua,

**16** "Tell the priests who carry the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan."

**17** Thus, Joshua gave a command to the priests. He said, "Come up out of the Jordan."

**18** The priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up out of the middle of the Jordan. When their feet touched the dry land, the water of the Jordan went back to its place. The water flowed above all its banks again, as before.

**19** The people came up out of the Jordan on the 10th day of the 1st month. They made their camp at Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho.

**20** Joshua put up the 12 stones at Gilgal. The people took these stones from the Jordan.

**21** He said to the people of Israel, "In the future, your children will ask their fathers, 'What do these stones mean?'

**22** Then tell your children, 'Israel went across this Jordan River on dry land.'

**23** The LORD your God made the water of the Jordan dry in front of you until you were across. He did the same thing at the Red Sea. He made the Red Sea dry in front of us until we were across.

**24** He did this so that all the people of the earth will know that the hand of the LORD is strong. He did this so that you will respect the LORD your God for all time."

## Chapter 5

**1** All the kings of the Amorites on the west side of the Jordan heard about these things. All the kings of the Canaanites near the sea also heard. They heard that the LORD made the water of the Jordan dry until the people of Israel were across. Then the kings became very afraid. They had no courage because of the people of Israel.

**2** At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make knives from sharp stones. Circumcise the men of Israel again."

**3** Thus, Joshua made knives from sharp stones. He circumcised the men of Israel at Gibeath Haaraloth (the hill of foreskins).

**4** This is why Joshua circumcised them. All the males who came out of Egypt, all the soldiers, died in the desert on the journey after they left Egypt.

**5** All the men who came out of Egypt received circumcision. But nobody circumcised the boys born in the desert on the journey from Egypt.

**6** The people of Israel walked in the desert for 40 years. During that time, all the soldiers who came out of Egypt died, because they did not obey the LORD. So the LORD made this promise to them: 'You will not see the land.' He promised to give this land to our fathers. It is a land with much milk and honey.

**7** Joshua circumcised the sons of those soldiers. God made these sons the new people of Israel. Nobody circumcised them on the journey. Thus, they did not have circumcision.

**8** After Joshua circumcised all the men, they stayed in their places in the camp. They stayed there until their bodies healed.

**9** Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I removed from you the shame of Egypt." Thus, the name of that place is Gilgal today.

**10** The people of Israel made their camp at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho. They kept the Passover on the evening of the 14th day of the month.

**11** On the day after the Passover, they ate some of the food that grew in the land. On that same day they ate bread without yeast and cooked grain.

**12** On the day after they ate the food of the land, the manna stopped. The people of Israel did not have manna again. That year they ate the food that grew in the land of Canaan.

**13** Joshua was near Jericho. He looked up and saw a man in front of him. The man held a sword in his hand. Joshua went to him and said, "Are you on our side or on the side of our enemies?"

**14** The man said, "Neither. I am the commander of the army of the LORD, and I come now." Then Joshua bowed down with his face to the ground and worshiped. He said, "My lord, what do you tell me, your servant?"

**15** The commander of the army of the LORD said to Joshua, "Remove your shoes from your feet. The place where you stand is holy." Joshua did this.

## Chapter 6

**1** The people of Jericho closed the gates of the city tightly because of the people of Israel. Nobody went out and nobody came in.

**2** The LORD said to Joshua, "Look, I give Jericho, its king, and its strong soldiers to you.

**3** All your soldiers must march around the city 1 time each day. Do this for 6 days.

**4** 7 priests must carry 7 trumpets made from the horns of male sheep. They must go in front of the ark. On the 7th day, march around the city 7 times. The priests must blow the trumpets.

**5** The priests will make a long sound with the horns. When you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people must shout loudly. Then the wall of the city will fall down. All the people will go up into the city. Each man will go straight in."

**6** Joshua the son of Nun called the priests. He said to them, "Lift the ark of the covenant. 7 priests must carry 7 trumpets of horns in front of the ark of the LORD."

**7** He said to the people, "Go forward and march around the city. The soldiers with weapons must go in front of the ark of the LORD."

**8** After Joshua spoke to the people, the 7 priests with the 7 trumpets went forward in front of the LORD. They blew the trumpets. The ark of the covenant of the LORD followed them.

**9** The soldiers with weapons went in front of the priests who blew the trumpets. Other soldiers came behind the ark. The priests continued to blow the trumpets.

**10** Joshua gave a command to the people. He said, "Do not shout. Do not make a noise with your voice. Do not say a word until the day that I tell you to shout. Then shout."

**11** Thus, the people carried the ark of the LORD around the city 1 time. Then they went back into the camp and stayed there that night.

**12** Joshua got up early in the morning. The priests lifted the ark of the LORD.

**13** The 7 priests with the 7 trumpets went in front of the ark of the LORD. They continued to walk and blow the trumpets. The soldiers with weapons went in front of them. Other soldiers came behind the ark of the LORD. The priests continued to blow the trumpets.

**14** On the 2nd day, they marched around the city 1 time. Then they went back to the camp. They did this for 6 days.

**15** On the 7th day, they got up early at dawn. They marched around the city in the same way, but 7 times. Only on that day did they march around the city 7 times.

**16** The 7th time, the priests blew the trumpets. Joshua said to the people, "Shout! The LORD gives you the city.
