**17** The city and all the things in it belong to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute will live. She and all the people with her in her house will live, because she hid the men that we sent.

**18** Do not take any of the things that are for destruction. If you take them, you will also be for destruction. You will cause the camp of Israel to be for destruction, and you will bring trouble on it.

**19** All the silver and gold and all the containers of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD. They must go into the treasury of the LORD."

**20** The priests blew the trumpets, and the people shouted. When the people heard the sound of the trumpet, they shouted loudly. Then the wall fell down. The people went up into the city. Each man went straight in, and they took the city.

**21** They destroyed all the people and animals in the city with the sword. They killed men and women, young and old people. They killed the cattle, the sheep, and the donkeys.

**22** Joshua spoke to the 2 men who spied on the country. He said, "Go into the house of the prostitute. Bring out the woman and all her family, as you promised her."

**23** Thus, the young men who were spies went in. They brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers, and all the people who were with her. They brought out all her family. They put them in a place outside the camp of Israel.

**24** Then the people burned the city and all the things in it. But they put the silver, the gold, and the containers of bronze and iron into the treasury of the house of the LORD.

**25** But Joshua kept Rahab the prostitute alive. He also kept her family and all her people alive. She lives in Israel today. Joshua saved her because she hid the men that he sent to spy on Jericho.

**26** At that time Joshua made a serious promise in front of the people. He said, "The LORD will curse the man who builds this city Jericho again. When he builds the base of the city, his oldest son will die. When he puts up its gates, his youngest son will die."

**27** Thus, the LORD was with Joshua. People in all the country heard about him.

## Chapter 7

**1** But the people of Israel did not obey the command about the things for destruction. Achan took some of these things. Achan was the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah. Thus, the LORD became very angry with the people of Israel.

**2** Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai. Ai is near Beth Aven, on the east side of Bethel. He told them, "Go up and look at the country." The men went up and looked at Ai.

**3** They came back to Joshua and said to him, "Do not send all the people. Send approximately 2,000 or 3,000 men to attack Ai. Do not cause all the people to go there, because the people of Ai are few."

**4** Thus, approximately 3,000 men went up there. But they ran away from the men of Ai.

**5** The men of Ai killed approximately 36 of them. The men of Ai chased them from the city gate to Shebarim. They killed them on the hillside. Then the people of Israel lost their courage completely.

**6** Joshua tore his clothes. He bowed down with his face to the ground in front of the ark of the LORD until evening. The leaders of Israel did the same thing. They put dust on their heads.

**7** Joshua said, "Oh, Lord GOD, why did you bring these people across the Jordan River? Did you bring us here to give us to the Amorites to destroy us? We wish that we stayed on the other side of the Jordan!

**8** Oh, Lord, what can I say now? Israel ran away from its enemies!

**9** The Canaanites and all the people of the land will hear about this. They will come around us and kill us all. Then nobody on the earth will remember our name. What will you do for your great name?"

**10** The LORD said to Joshua, "Get up! Why do you lie with your face on the ground?

**11** Israel sinned. The people did not obey my covenant that I gave them. They took some of the things that were for destruction. They stole and they lied. They put those things among their own possessions.

**12** That is why the people of Israel cannot stand against their enemies. They run away from their enemies, because they are now for destruction. I will not be with you again until you destroy the things for destruction that are among you.

**13** Get up! Make the people holy. Tell them, 'Make yourselves holy for tomorrow. The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: "Israel, there are things for destruction among you. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove these things."'

**14** In the morning, come forward tribe by tribe. The LORD will choose 1 tribe. That tribe must come forward family by family. The LORD will choose 1 family. That family must come forward household by household. The LORD will choose 1 household. That household must come forward man by man.

**15** The LORD will choose the man who has the things for destruction. You must burn that man and all his possessions with fire. He did not obey the covenant of the LORD. He did a shameful thing in Israel."

**16** Joshua got up early in the morning. He caused Israel to come forward tribe by tribe. The LORD chose the tribe of Judah.

**17** Joshua caused the families of Judah to come forward. The LORD chose the family of Zerah. Joshua caused the family of Zerah to come forward man by man. The LORD chose Zabdi.

**18** Joshua caused the household of Zabdi to come forward man by man. The LORD chose Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah.

**19** Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel. Tell him your sin. Tell me now what you did. Do not hide it from me."

**20** Achan answered Joshua, "It is true. I sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did.

**21** Among the things that we took from the city, I saw a beautiful coat from Babylonia. I also saw 200 shekels (2.3 kilograms) of silver and a bar of gold with a weight of 50 shekels (570 grams). I wanted them, and I took them. They are in the ground below my tent. The silver is below the other things."

**22** Thus, Joshua sent men, and they ran to the tent. The things were in the ground below the tent, and the silver was below them.

**23** The men took the things from the tent. They brought them to Joshua and to all the people of Israel. They put them on the ground in front of the LORD.

**24** Then Joshua and all Israel took Achan the son of Zerah. They also took the silver, the coat, and the bar of gold. They took his sons and his daughters, his cattle, his donkeys, and his sheep. They took his tent and all his possessions. They brought them to the Valley of Achor.

**25** Joshua said, "Why did you bring this trouble on us? Today the LORD will bring trouble on you." Then all Israel threw stones at Achan and killed him. They threw stones at his family and killed them. Then they burned them with fire.

**26** They put a large pile of stones over Achan. This pile is there today. Then the LORD stopped his strong anger. Thus, the name of that place is the Valley of Achor (Valley of Trouble) today.

## Chapter 8

**1** The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid. Do not lose your courage. Take all your soldiers with you and go up to Ai. Look, I give you the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.

**2** Do to Ai and its king the same things that you did to Jericho and its king. But this time you can keep the possessions and the animals for yourselves. Put some soldiers in a hidden position behind the city."

**3** Thus, Joshua and all his soldiers got ready to go up to Ai. Joshua chose 30,000 strong and brave soldiers. He sent them out during the night.

**4** He gave them this command: "Hide behind the city and wait. Do not go very far from the city. All of you must be ready.

**5** I and all the people with me will go near the city. The men of the city will come out to attack us, as they did before. Then we will run away from them.

**6** They will chase us until we pull them away from the city. They will say, 'The Israelites run away from us as they did before.' Thus, we will run away from them.

**7** Then come out of your hidden position and take the city. The LORD your God will give the city to you.

**8** When you take the city, set it on fire. Do as the LORD tells you. Look, I give you this command."

**9** Thus, Joshua sent them out. They went to their hidden position and waited between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai. But Joshua stayed with the people that night.

**10** Joshua got up early in the morning and prepared his soldiers. He and the leaders of Israel went in front of the soldiers to Ai.

**11** All the soldiers with Joshua went up and came near the city. They made their camp on the north side of Ai. There was a valley between them and Ai.

**12** Joshua took approximately 5,000 men. He put them in a hidden position between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city.

**13** Thus, the soldiers were in their positions. The main army was on the north side of the city. The hidden soldiers were on the west side of the city. That night Joshua went into the middle of the valley.

**14** The king of Ai saw the Israelites. Then he and all the men of the city got up early and quickly went out to fight against Israel. They went to a place in front of the plain. But the king did not know that soldiers waited in a hidden position behind the city.

**15** Joshua and all Israel acted as if the men of Ai defeated them. They ran away toward the desert.

**16** All the men in Ai got a command to chase the Israelites. They chased Joshua and went far from the city.

**17** All the men in Ai and Bethel went out after Israel. Nobody stayed in the cities. They left the city open and chased Israel.

**18** Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Hold out the spear in your hand toward Ai. I will give the city to you." Thus, Joshua held out the spear in his hand toward the city.

**19** When Joshua held out his hand, the hidden soldiers quickly got up from their position. They ran into the city and took it. They quickly set the city on fire.

**20** The men of Ai looked back and saw the smoke of their city. The smoke went up into the sky. The men of Ai could not escape in any direction. Then the Israelites who ran toward the desert turned back against the men who chased them.

**21** Joshua and all Israel saw that the hidden soldiers took the city. They saw the smoke that went up from the city. Then they turned back and killed the men of Ai.

**22** The other Israelites came out of the city to fight against the men of Ai. Thus, the men of Ai were in the middle, with Israelites on the 2 sides. The Israelites killed all of them. Nobody stayed alive or escaped.

**23** But the Israelites caught the king of Ai alive. They brought him to Joshua.

**24** The Israelites killed all the men of Ai in the fields and in the desert, where they chased them. All of them died by the sword. Then all the Israelites went back to Ai and killed the people in the city with the sword.

**25** On that day 12,000 men and women died. These were all the people of Ai.

**26** Joshua did not lower the hand that held out the spear until the Israelites destroyed all the people of Ai.

**27** But the Israelites kept the animals and the possessions of that city for themselves. The LORD gave this command to Joshua.

**28** Joshua burned Ai. He made it a pile of ruins for all time. It is empty today.

**29** Joshua hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset, Joshua told the people to take the body down from the tree. They threw the body down at the city gate. They put a large pile of stones on it. That pile is there today.

**30** Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal.

**31** Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave this command to the people of Israel. The command is in the book of the law of Moses. Joshua made the altar of whole stones. Nobody cut these stones with iron tools. On the altar the people offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to the LORD.

**32** There, Joshua wrote a copy of the law of Moses on the stones. He wrote it in front of the people of Israel.

**33** All Israel stood on the 2 sides of the ark, in front of the priests. The priests were Levites, and they carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD. The leaders, officers, and judges were there. The foreigners and the people of Israel were there. Half of the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim. Half of the people stood in front of Mount Ebal. Moses, the servant of the LORD, told them to do this when they blessed the people of Israel.

**34** After that, Joshua read all the words of the law. He read the blessings and the curses. He read all the things in the book of the law.

**35** Joshua read each word of all the commands of Moses. He read them in front of all the people of Israel. The women, the small children, and the foreigners who lived among them were also there.

## Chapter 9

**1** Many kings lived on the west side of the Jordan River. They lived in the hills, in the low hills, and along all the coast of the Great Sea to Lebanon. They were the kings of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. These kings heard about the things that Israel did.

**2** Thus, they came together as 1 army to fight against Joshua and Israel.

**3** The people who lived in Gibeon heard what Joshua did to Jericho and Ai.

**4** Thus, they made a plan to trick Israel. They acted as if they were messengers from a far country. They put old bags on their donkeys. They took old wine containers. The containers had tears, and someone repaired them.

**5** They wore old shoes that had repairs on them. They wore old clothes. All the bread that they took for food was dry and in pieces.

**6** They went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal. They said to him and to the men of Israel, "We came from a far country. Thus, make a treaty with us now."

**7** The men of Israel said to the Hivites, "Possibly you live near us. If you live near us, we cannot make a treaty with you."

**8** The men said to Joshua, "We are your servants." Joshua said to them, "Who are you? Where do you come from?"

**9** They said to him, "We, your servants, came from a very far country because of the name of the LORD your God. We heard about him and about all the things that he did in Egypt.

**10** We also heard about all the things that he did to the 2 kings of the Amorites on the east side of the Jordan. He defeated Sihon, the king of Heshbon, and Og, the king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.

**11** Thus, our leaders and all the people of our country spoke to us. They said, 'Take food with you for the journey. Go and meet the Israelites. Tell them, "We are your servants. Make a treaty with us now."'

**12** Look at our bread. It was hot when we took it from our houses on the day that we left to come to you. But now it is dry and in pieces.

**13** When we filled these wine containers, they were new. But look, now they have holes in them. Our clothes and our shoes are old because the journey was very long."

**14** The men of Israel examined some of their food. But they did not ask the LORD what to do.

**15** Joshua made peace with them. He made a treaty with them to let them live. The leaders of the people of Israel made a promise to them.

**16** 3 days after the Israelites made the treaty, they heard that these people were their neighbors. They lived near Israel.

**17** Thus, the people of Israel went out. On the 3rd day they came to the cities of these people. These cities were Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim.

**18** But the people of Israel did not attack them. The leaders of the people made a promise to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. All the people of Israel complained against the leaders.

**19** But all the leaders said to all the people, "We made a promise to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. Thus, we cannot hurt them now.

**20** This is what we will do to them. We will let them live. If we do not keep our promise, God will be angry with us."

**21** The leaders said, "Let them live. But they must cut wood and carry water for all the people." Thus, the leaders kept their promise to them.

**22** Joshua called the Gibeonites. He said to them, "Why did you trick us? You said, 'We live very far from you.' But you live near us.

**23** Thus, now a curse is on you. You will always be slaves. You will cut wood and carry water for the house of my God."

**24** They answered Joshua, "We, your servants, heard clearly about the command of the LORD your God to his servant Moses. The LORD told Moses to give you all the land. He told Moses to destroy all the people of the land in front of you. Thus, we were very afraid for our lives because of you. That is why we did this.

**25** Now we are in your control. Do to us the thing that you think is good and right."

**26** Thus, Joshua did that to them. He saved them from the people of Israel, and the Israelites did not kill them.

**27** On that day Joshua made the Gibeonites cut wood and carry water for the people and for the altar of the LORD. They do this work today at the place that the LORD chooses.

## Chapter 10

**1** Adoni-Zedek was the king of Jerusalem. He heard that Joshua took Ai and destroyed it completely. Joshua did to Ai and its king the same things that he did to Jericho and its king. Adoni-Zedek also heard that the people of Gibeon made peace with Israel and lived among them.

**2** Thus, Adoni-Zedek and his people were very afraid. Gibeon was a large city, as large as a city with a king. It was larger than Ai, and all its men were strong soldiers.

**3** Thus, Adoni-Zedek, the king of Jerusalem, sent a message to 4 kings. He sent it to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon. He said,

**4** "Come up to me and help me. We must attack Gibeon, because the Gibeonites made peace with Joshua and the people of Israel."

**5** Thus, the 5 kings of the Amorites came together. They were the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon. They and all their armies went up. They made their camp near Gibeon and attacked it.

**6** The men of Gibeon sent a message to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal. They said, "Do not leave us, your servants. Come up to us quickly. Save us and help us. All the kings of the Amorites who live in the hills came together against us."

**7** Thus, Joshua went up from Gilgal with all his army and all his strong soldiers.

**8** The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. I give them to you. Not 1 of them will be able to stand against you."

**9** Joshua and his army marched all night from Gilgal. They attacked the Amorites by surprise.

**10** The LORD caused the Amorites to panic in front of Israel. Israel killed very many of them at Gibeon. Israel chased them along the road up to Beth Horon. Israel killed them all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.

**11** The Amorites ran away from Israel down the hill from Beth Horon. Then the LORD threw large hailstones on them from the sky all the way to Azekah. More of them died from the hailstones than from the swords of the Israelites.

**12** On the day that the LORD gave the Amorites to Israel, Joshua spoke to the LORD. In front of Israel he said, "Sun, stop over Gibeon. Moon, stop over the Valley of Aijalon."

**13** Thus, the sun stopped and the moon stopped until the people defeated their enemies. The Book of Jashar tells about this. The sun stopped in the middle of the sky. It did not go down for approximately 1 full day.

**14** There was no day like that day before it or after it. On that day the LORD obeyed the voice of a man. The LORD fought for Israel.

**15** Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.

**16** The 5 kings ran away and hid in a cave at Makkedah.

**17** A person told Joshua, "Somebody found the 5 kings. They hide in a cave at Makkedah."

**18** Joshua said, "Roll large stones over the mouth of the cave. Put men there to guard the kings.

**19** But do not stay there yourselves. Chase your enemies. Attack them from behind. Do not let them go into their cities. The LORD your God gives them to you."

**20** Joshua and the people of Israel killed very many of the enemy soldiers. They almost destroyed them all. Only a few of them escaped into cities with walls.

**21** Then all the people came back safely to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah. Nobody said a word against the people of Israel.

**22** Then Joshua said, "Open the cave. Bring the 5 kings out to me."

**23** Thus, the men brought the 5 kings out of the cave to Joshua. They were the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.

**24** The men brought these kings to Joshua. Then Joshua called all the men of Israel. He said to the commanders of the soldiers who went with him, "Come here. Put your feet on the necks of these kings." Thus, they came and put their feet on the necks of the kings.

**25** Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid. Do not lose your courage. Be strong and brave. The LORD will do this to all the enemies that you fight."

**26** Then Joshua killed the kings. He hanged them on 5 trees. The bodies stayed on the trees until evening.

**27** At sunset, Joshua gave a command. His men took the bodies down from the trees. They threw them into the cave where the kings hid. They put large stones over the mouth of the cave. These stones are there today.

**28** On that day Joshua took Makkedah. He killed the king and all the people in the city with the sword. He destroyed them completely. Nobody stayed alive. He did to the king of Makkedah the same thing that he did to the king of Jericho.

**29** Then Joshua and all Israel went from Makkedah to Libnah. They attacked Libnah.

**30** The LORD also gave Libnah and its king to Israel. Joshua killed all the people in the city with the sword. Nobody stayed alive. He did to the king of Libnah the same thing that he did to the king of Jericho.

**31** Then Joshua and all Israel went from Libnah to Lachish. They made their camp near Lachish and attacked it.

**32** The LORD gave Lachish to Israel. On the 2nd day Israel took the city. They killed all the people in the city with the sword, as they did at Libnah.

**33** Then Horam, the king of Gezer, came up to help Lachish. But Joshua defeated him and his army. Nobody stayed alive.

**34** Then Joshua and all Israel went from Lachish to Eglon. They made their camp near Eglon and attacked it.

**35** They took the city on that same day. They killed all the people in the city with the sword. Joshua destroyed them completely, as he did at Lachish.

**36** Then Joshua and all Israel went up from Eglon to Hebron. They attacked Hebron.

**37** They took the city. They killed its king and all the people in the city and in its villages with the sword. Nobody stayed alive. Joshua destroyed the city and all its people completely, as he did at Eglon.

**38** Then Joshua and all Israel turned back to Debir. They attacked Debir.

**39** Joshua took Debir, its king, and its villages. The Israelites killed all the people with the sword. They destroyed them completely. Nobody stayed alive. Joshua did to Debir and its king the same thing that he did to Hebron, and to Libnah and its king.

**40** Thus, Joshua defeated all the land. He defeated the hills, the Negev (the south), the low hills, and the hillsides. He defeated all their kings. Nobody stayed alive. He destroyed all people who breathed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, told him.

**41** Joshua defeated them from Kadesh Barnea to Gaza. He also defeated all the area of Goshen as far as Gibeon.

**42** Joshua took all these kings and their land in 1 military campaign. He did this because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.

**43** Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.

## Chapter 11

**1** Jabin, the king of Hazor, heard about these things. Thus, he sent a message to Jobab, the king of Madon. He also sent it to the king of Shimron and the king of Akshaph.

**2** He sent it to the kings in the north, in the hills. He sent it to the kings in the Arabah south of Kinnereth, in the low hills, and in the hills of Dor on the west.

**3** He sent it to the Canaanites in the east and in the west. He sent it to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Jebusites in the hills. He also sent it to the Hivites below Mount Hermon in the area of Mizpah.

**4** These kings came out with all their armies. There were very many soldiers, as many as the grains of sand on the beach. They had very many horses and chariots.

**5** All these kings met together. They made their camp together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.

**6** The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. Tomorrow at this time I will give all of them to Israel, and they will be dead. Cut the leg muscles of their horses. Burn their chariots with fire."

**7** Thus, Joshua and all his soldiers came against them at the waters of Merom. They attacked them by surprise.

**8** The LORD gave the enemies to Israel. The Israelites defeated them and chased them to Greater Sidon and to Misrephoth Maim. They chased them east to the Valley of Mizpah. They killed them until nobody stayed alive.

**9** Joshua did to them as the LORD told him. He cut the leg muscles of their horses and burned their chariots with fire.

**10** At that time Joshua turned back and took Hazor. He killed its king with the sword. Before that time, Hazor was the most important of all those kingdoms.

**11** The Israelites killed all the people in Hazor with the sword. They destroyed them completely. Nobody stayed alive. Then Joshua burned Hazor with fire.

**12** Joshua took all the cities of those kings. He also caught all their kings. He killed them with the sword. He destroyed them completely, as Moses, the servant of the LORD, told him.

**13** But Israel did not burn the cities that stood on their hills. Joshua burned only Hazor.

**14** The people of Israel took all the possessions and the animals of these cities for themselves. But they killed all the people with the sword until they destroyed them. Nobody stayed alive.

**15** The LORD gave commands to his servant Moses. Moses gave the same commands to Joshua, and Joshua obeyed them. Joshua did all the things that the LORD told Moses.

**16** Thus, Joshua took all that land. He took the hills, all the Negev, and all the area of Goshen. He also took the low hills, the Arabah, and the hills of Israel with their low hills.

**17** He took the land from Mount Halak, near Seir, to Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. He caught all their kings and killed them.

**18** Joshua fought against all those kings for a long time.

**19** Only 1 city made peace with the people of Israel. That was the city of the Hivites who lived in Gibeon. Israel took all the other cities in battle.

**20** The LORD made these people stubborn. Thus, they fought against Israel. Then Israel destroyed them completely without mercy. The LORD gave this command to Moses.

**21** At that time Joshua went and destroyed the Anakites. He destroyed them in the hills, in Hebron, Debir, and Anab. He destroyed them in all the hills of Judah and all the hills of Israel. Joshua destroyed them and their cities completely.

**22** No Anakites stayed alive in the land of Israel. Only a few of them stayed in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.

**23** Thus, Joshua took all the land, as the LORD told Moses. Joshua gave the land to Israel as their property. He divided it among the tribes. Then there was peace in the land.

## Chapter 12

**1** These are the kings that the people of Israel defeated on the east side of the Jordan. Israel took the land of these kings. It went from the Arnon River to Mount Hermon. It included all the east side of the Arabah.

**2** Sihon was the king of the Amorites. He lived in Heshbon. He ruled from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon River, and from the middle of the valley. He ruled half of Gilead, as far as the Jabbok River. The Jabbok River is the border of the Ammonites.

**3** He also ruled the east side of the Arabah, from the Sea of Kinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea. His land went toward Beth Jeshimoth. In the south it went to the bottom of the hills of Pisgah.

**4** Og was the king of Bashan. He was one of the last of the Rephaites (the giants). He lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.

**5** He ruled Mount Hermon, Salekah, and all of Bashan, to the border of the Geshurites and the Maakathites. He also ruled half of Gilead, to the border of Sihon, the king of Heshbon.

**6** Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the people of Israel defeated these 2 kings. Moses gave their land to the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh as their property.

**7** These are the kings that Joshua and the people of Israel defeated on the west side of the Jordan. Their land went from Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, near Seir. Joshua gave this land to the tribes of Israel as their property. He divided it among them.

**8** The land included the hills, the low hills, the Arabah, the hillsides, the desert, and the Negev. It was the land of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. These are the kings:

**9** The king of Jericho, 1. The king of Ai, near Bethel, 1.

**10** The king of Jerusalem, 1. The king of Hebron, 1.

**11** The king of Jarmuth, 1. The king of Lachish, 1.

**12** The king of Eglon, 1. The king of Gezer, 1.

**13** The king of Debir, 1. The king of Geder, 1.

**14** The king of Hormah, 1. The king of Arad, 1.

**15** The king of Libnah, 1. The king of Adullam, 1.

**16** The king of Makkedah, 1. The king of Bethel, 1.

**17** The king of Tappuah, 1. The king of Hepher, 1.

**18** The king of Aphek, 1. The king of Lasharon, 1.

**19** The king of Madon, 1. The king of Hazor, 1.

**20** The king of Shimron Meron, 1. The king of Akshaph, 1.

**21** The king of Taanach, 1. The king of Megiddo, 1.

**22** The king of Kedesh, 1. The king of Jokneam in Carmel, 1.

**23** The king of Dor, in the hills of Dor, 1. The king of Goyim in Gilgal, 1.

**24** The king of Tirzah, 1. There was a total of 31 kings.

## Chapter 13

**1** Joshua was very old. The LORD said to him, "You are very old. But there is still very much land that Israel must take.

**2** This is the land that Israel must still take. It includes all the areas of the Philistines and of the Geshurites.

**3** It goes from the Shihor River, on the east border of Egypt, north to the border of Ekron. People think of this land as land of the Canaanites. It includes the land of the 5 rulers of the Philistines in Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron. It also includes the land of the Avites.

**4** In the south, it includes all the land of the Canaanites. It goes from Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, to Aphek, at the border of the Amorites.

**5** It includes the land of the Gebalites and all Lebanon to the east. It goes from Baal Gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo Hamath.

**6** It includes all the people who live in the hills from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim, and all the Sidonians. I will push them out in front of the people of Israel. You must divide this land among the Israelites by lot as their property, as I told you.

**7** Now divide this land among the 9 tribes and half the tribe of Manasseh as their property."

**8** The other half of the tribe of Manasseh, the tribe of Reuben, and the tribe of Gad received their land from Moses. Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave them land on the east side of the Jordan.

**9** Their land went from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon River, and from the city in the middle of the valley. It included all the plain of Medeba as far as Dibon.

**10** It included all the cities of Sihon, the king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. It went to the border of the Ammonites.

**11** It also included Gilead and the areas of the Geshurites and the Maakathites. It included all Mount Hermon and all Bashan as far as Salekah.

**12** It included all the kingdom of Og in Bashan. Og ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was one of the last of the Rephaites (the giants). Moses defeated these people and pushed them out.

**13** But the people of Israel did not push out the Geshurites and the Maakathites. The Geshurites and the Maakathites live among the Israelites today.

**14** Moses did not give land to the tribe of Levi. The offerings that the people burn for the LORD, the God of Israel, are the property of the Levites. The LORD told them this.

**15** Moses gave land to the tribe of Reuben, family by family.

**16** Their land went from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon River, and from the city in the middle of the valley. It included all the plain near Medeba.

**17** It included Heshbon and all its cities on the plain: Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon,

**18** Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,

**19** Kiriathaim, Sibmah, and Zereth Shahar on the hill in the valley.

**20** It included Beth Peor, the hillsides of Pisgah, and Beth Jeshimoth.

**21** It included all the cities of the plain and all the kingdom of Sihon, the king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. Moses defeated Sihon and the leaders of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. These leaders were the allies of Sihon and lived in that country.

**22** The people of Israel also killed Balaam, the son of Beor, with the sword. Balaam used magic to tell the future. They killed him with the other people that they killed.

**23** The border of the tribe of Reuben was the Jordan River. These cities and their villages were the property of the tribe of Reuben, family by family.

**24** Moses gave land to the tribe of Gad, family by family.

**25** Their land included Jazer and all the cities of Gilead. It included half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, near Rabbah.

**26** It went from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpah and Betonim. It went from Mahanaim to the border of Debir.

**27** In the valley it included Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Sukkoth, and Zaphon. These were the other parts of the kingdom of Sihon, the king of Heshbon. The land went along the east side of the Jordan to the end of the Sea of Kinnereth.

**28** These cities and their villages were the property of the tribe of Gad, family by family.

**29** Moses gave land to half the tribe of Manasseh. This was the property of half the tribe of Manasseh, family by family.

**30** Their land went from Mahanaim and included all Bashan. It included all the kingdom of Og, the king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair in Bashan. There were 60 cities.

**31** It also included half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of Og in Bashan. This land was for the descendants of Machir, the son of Manasseh. It was for half of the descendants of Machir, family by family.

**32** Moses gave these areas to the tribes as their property when he was on the plains of Moab. These plains were on the east side of the Jordan, across from Jericho.

**33** But Moses did not give land to the tribe of Levi. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their property, as he told them.

## Chapter 14

**1** These are the areas that the people of Israel received as their property in the land of Canaan. Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the leaders of the tribes of Israel divided the land among them.

**2** They divided the land among the 9 and a half tribes by lot. The LORD gave this command through Moses.

**3** Moses gave land to 2 and a half tribes on the east side of the Jordan. But he did not give land to the Levites among the other tribes.

**4** The descendants of Joseph became 2 tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites did not get a part of the land. They got only cities to live in, with fields around them for their animals and their possessions.

**5** Thus, the people of Israel divided the land, as the LORD told Moses.

**6** The men of the tribe of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb the son of Jephunneh, the Kenizzite, spoke to Joshua. He said, "You know what the LORD said to Moses, the man of God, about you and me at Kadesh Barnea.

**7** I was 40 years old when Moses, the servant of the LORD, sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy on the land. I came back and told him the truth as I thought it.

**8** But the other men who went with me made the people afraid. But I followed the LORD my God completely.

**9** On that day Moses made a promise to me. He said, 'The land where your feet walked will be the property of you and your children for all time. You followed the LORD my God completely.'

**10** Now look, the LORD kept me alive for 45 years, as he promised. That was the time when the LORD said this to Moses. During that time, Israel moved from place to place in the desert. Now I am 85 years old.

**11** Today I am as strong as I was on the day that Moses sent me. I am as strong now as I was then. I can fight in a war, and I can go out and come in.

**12** Thus, now give me this hill country. The LORD promised it to me on that day. On that day you heard that the Anakites live there. Their cities are large and have strong walls. But possibly the LORD will be with me. Then I will push them out, as the LORD said."

**13** Joshua blessed Caleb the son of Jephunneh. He gave him Hebron as his property.

**14** Thus, Hebron is the property of Caleb the son of Jephunneh, the Kenizzite, today. This is because Caleb followed the LORD, the God of Israel, completely.

**15** Before that time, the name of Hebron was Kiriath Arba. Arba was the greatest man among the Anakites. Then there was peace in the land.

## Chapter 15

**1** This is the land that the tribe of Judah received by lot, family by family. It went south to the border of Edom, to the Desert of Zin at the farthest south point.

**2** Their south border started at the south end of the Salt Sea, at the bay that points south.

**3** It went south of the Akrabbim Pass, continued to Zin, and went up south of Kadesh Barnea. Then it continued past Hezron, went up to Addar, and turned toward Karka.

**4** From there it continued to Azmon and went to the Brook of Egypt. It ended at the sea. This was their south border.

**5** The east border was the Salt Sea, to the mouth of the Jordan River. The north border started at the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan.

**6** The border went up to Beth Hoglah and continued north of Beth Arabah. It went up to the Stone of Bohan, the son of Reuben.

**7** Then the border went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor. It turned north toward Gilgal. Gilgal is across from the Adummim Pass, on the south side of the valley. The border continued to the waters of En Shemesh and ended at En Rogel.

**8** Then the border went up the Valley of Ben Hinnom along the south side of the city of the Jebusites. That city is Jerusalem. The border went up to the top of the hill west of the Valley of Hinnom. This hill is at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim.

**9** From the top of the hill, the border went to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah. It went to the cities of Mount Ephron. Then it went to Baalah, which is Kiriath Jearim.

**10** From Baalah, the border turned west to Mount Seir. It continued along the north side of Mount Jearim, which is Kesalon. It went down to Beth Shemesh and continued to Timnah.

**11** The border went to the north side of Ekron. It turned toward Shikkeron and continued to Mount Baalah. It went to Jabneel and ended at the sea.

**12** The west border was the coast of the Great Sea. These were the borders around the land of the tribe of Judah, family by family.

**13** Joshua gave Caleb the son of Jephunneh a part of the land of Judah, as the LORD told him. He gave him Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron. Arba was the father of Anak.

**14** Caleb pushed out the 3 sons of Anak from Hebron. Their names were Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. They were descendants of Anak.

**15** From there Caleb went to attack the people who lived in Debir. Before that time, the name of Debir was Kiriath Sepher.

**16** Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Aksah as a wife to the man who attacks Kiriath Sepher and takes it."

**17** Othniel took the city. He was the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb. Thus, Caleb gave his daughter Aksah to Othniel as his wife.

**18** When Aksah came to Othniel, she told him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey. Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"

**19** She answered, "Please give me a special gift. You gave me land in the Negev (the dry south). Also give me springs of water." Thus, Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

**20** This is the property of the tribe of Judah, family by family.

**21** These are the cities of the tribe of Judah in the farthest south, near the border of Edom: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,

**22** Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,

**23** Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,

**24** Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,

**25** Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (which is Hazor),

**26** Amam, Shema, Moladah,

**27** Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet,

**28** Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah,

**29** Baalah, Iim, Ezem,

**30** Eltolad, Kesil, Hormah,

**31** Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,

**32** Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon. There was a total of 29 cities with their villages.

**33** In the low hills there were these cities: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,

**34** Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam,

**35** Jarmuth, Adullam, Sokoh, Azekah,

**36** Shaaraim, Adithaim, and Gederah (or Gederothaim). There were 14 cities with their villages.

**37** There were also Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad,

**38** Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel,

**39** Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,

**40** Kabbon, Lahmas, Kitlish,

**41** Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah. There were 16 cities with their villages.

**42** There were also Libnah, Ether, Ashan,

**43** Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,

**44** Keilah, Akzib, and Mareshah. There were 9 cities with their villages.

**45** There was Ekron, with its towns and villages.

**46** There were all the cities near Ashdod, from Ekron to the sea, with their villages.

**47** There was Ashdod with its towns and villages. There was Gaza with its towns and villages, as far as the Brook of Egypt and the coast of the Great Sea.

**48** In the hills there were these cities: Shamir, Jattir, Sokoh,

**49** Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (which is Debir),

**50** Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,

**51** Goshen, Holon, and Giloh. There were 11 cities with their villages.

**52** There were also Arab, Dumah, Eshan,

**53** Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah,

**54** Humtah, Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron), and Zior. There were 9 cities with their villages.

**55** There were also Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,

**56** Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,

**57** Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah. There were 10 cities with their villages.

**58** There were also Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor,

**59** Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon. There were 6 cities with their villages.

**60** There were also Kiriath Baal (which is Kiriath Jearim) and Rabbah. There were 2 cities with their villages.

**61** In the desert there were these cities: Beth Arabah, Middin, Sekakah,

**62** Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi. There were 6 cities with their villages.

**63** But the people of Judah could not push out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem. The Jebusites live with the people of Judah in Jerusalem today.

## Chapter 16

**1** The land that the descendants of Joseph received by lot started at the Jordan River near Jericho. It started east of the springs of Jericho. The border went from Jericho up through the desert into the hills of Bethel.

**2** It went from Bethel (which is Luz) and continued to Ataroth, in the area of the Arkites.

**3** It went down west to the area of the Japhletites, as far as Lower Beth Horon and Gezer. It ended at the sea.

**4** Thus, the descendants of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their property.

**5** This was the land of the tribe of Ephraim, family by family. The border of their property went east from Ataroth Addar to Upper Beth Horon.

**6** It continued to the sea. Michmethath was on the north side. Then the border turned east to Taanath Shiloh. It went past Taanath Shiloh on the east to Janoah.

**7** Then it went down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah. It touched Jericho and ended at the Jordan.

**8** From Tappuah the border went west to the Kanah Valley and ended at the sea. This was the property of the tribe of Ephraim, family by family.

**9** The tribe of Ephraim also received some cities with their villages in the land of the tribe of Manasseh.

**10** But the people of Ephraim did not push out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer. The Canaanites live among the people of Ephraim today. But the Canaanites must do hard work for them as slaves.

## Chapter 17

**1** The tribe of Manasseh also received land by lot. Manasseh was the oldest son of Joseph. Machir was the oldest son of Manasseh and the father of Gilead. Machir was a good soldier. Thus, his descendants received Gilead and Bashan.

**2** The other families of Manasseh also received land. These were the families of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. They were the male descendants of Manasseh, the son of Joseph, family by family.

**3** Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh. Zelophehad had no sons. He had only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milkah, and Tirzah.

**4** These daughters went to Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the leaders. They said, "The LORD told Moses to give us property among our male relatives." Thus, Joshua gave them property among the brothers of their father, as the LORD told him.

**5** Thus, Manasseh received 10 parts of land west of the Jordan. This was in addition to Gilead and Bashan on the east side of the Jordan.

**6** The daughters of Manasseh received property among the sons. The other descendants of Manasseh received the land of Gilead.

**7** The land of Manasseh went from Asher to Michmethath, near Shechem. The border went south to the people who lived in En Tappuah.

**8** The land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh. But the city of Tappuah, on the border of Manasseh, belonged to the tribe of Ephraim.

**9** The border went down to the Kanah Valley. Some cities south of the valley belonged to Ephraim, but they were among the cities of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh was on the north side of the valley and ended at the sea.

**10** The land south of the valley belonged to Ephraim. The land north of the valley belonged to Manasseh. The sea was the west border of Manasseh. The land of Manasseh touched Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

**11** In Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also had these cities with their towns: Beth Shan, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo. These cities were in 3 areas of hills.

**12** But the people of Manasseh could not push out the people of those cities. The Canaanites continued to live in that land.

**13** Later, the people of Israel became stronger. Then they made the Canaanites do hard work as slaves. But they did not push them out completely.

**14** The descendants of Joseph said to Joshua, "Why did you give us only 1 part of the land as our property? We are a large people. The LORD blessed us very much."

**15** Joshua answered them, "If you are a large people, go up into the forest. Cut down the trees and make space for yourselves there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaites. Do this if the hills of Ephraim are too small for you."

**16** The descendants of Joseph said, "The hills are not sufficient for us. And all the Canaanites who live in the valleys have chariots of iron. The Canaanites in Beth Shan and its towns have them. The Canaanites in the Valley of Jezreel also have them."

**17** Then Joshua spoke to the descendants of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh. He said, "You are a large people, and you are very strong. You will not have only 1 part.

**18** The hills will also be yours. They are a forest, but you will cut down the trees. All the land to its farthest borders will be yours. You will push out the Canaanites, but they have chariots of iron and they are strong."

## Chapter 18

**1** All the people of Israel came together at Shiloh. They put up the tent of the assembly (the tabernacle) there. Israel now controlled the land.

**2** But there were still 7 tribes of Israel that did not receive their property.

**3** Joshua said to the people of Israel, "Why do you wait so long to take the land? The LORD, the God of your fathers, gave it to you.

**4** Choose 3 men from each tribe. I will send them out. They will go through the land and write a description of it, for the division of the property. Then they will come back to me.

**5** They will divide the land into 7 parts. The tribe of Judah will stay in its land in the south. The descendants of Joseph will stay in their land in the north.

**6** Write a description of the 7 parts of the land and bring it here to me. Then I will throw lots for you here in front of the LORD our God.

**7** The Levites will not get a part of the land among you. Their work as priests of the LORD is their property. Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh received their property on the east side of the Jordan. Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave it to them."

**8** The men got ready to go. Joshua gave them this command: "Go and walk through the land. Write a description of it. Then come back to me. I will throw lots for you here at Shiloh in front of the LORD."

**9** Thus, the men went through the land. They wrote a description of it in a book. They divided it into 7 parts by its cities. Then they came back to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.

**10** Joshua threw lots for them at Shiloh in front of the LORD. There he divided the land among the tribes of Israel.

**11** The first lot was for the tribe of Benjamin, family by family. Their land was between the land of Judah and the land of Joseph.

**12** Their north border started at the Jordan. It went up along the north side of Jericho. Then it went west into the hills and ended at the desert of Beth Aven.

**13** From there the border went south to Luz (which is Bethel). Then it went down to Ataroth Addar, near the hill south of Lower Beth Horon.

**14** From the hill south of Beth Horon, the border turned south along the west side. It ended at Kiriath Baal (which is Kiriath Jearim), a city of Judah. This was the west border.

**15** The south border started at the edge of Kiriath Jearim on the west. It went to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

**16** Then it went down to the bottom of the hill near the Valley of Ben Hinnom, at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim. It went down the Valley of Hinnom along the south side of the city of the Jebusites. Then it went down to En Rogel.

**17** Then it turned north and went to En Shemesh. It continued to Geliloth, across from the Adummim Pass. It went down to the Stone of Bohan, the son of Reuben.

**18** It continued to the north side of Beth Arabah and went down into the Arabah.

**19** Then it went to the north side of Beth Hoglah. It ended at the north bay of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Jordan. This was the south border.

**20** The Jordan was the east border. These were the borders around the property of the tribe of Benjamin, family by family.

**21** These were the cities of the tribe of Benjamin, family by family: Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz,

**22** Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,

**23** Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,

**24** Kephar Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba. There were 12 cities with their villages.

**25** There were also Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,

**26** Mizpah, Kephirah, Mozah,

**27** Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,

**28** Zelah, Haeleph, the Jebusite city (which is Jerusalem), Gibeah, and Kiriath. There were 14 cities with their villages. This was the property of the tribe of Benjamin, family by family.

## Chapter 19

**1** The 2nd lot was for the tribe of Simeon, family by family. Their property was inside the land of the tribe of Judah.

**2** Their property included Beersheba (or Sheba), Moladah,

**3** Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem,

**4** Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,

**5** Ziklag, Beth Markaboth, Hazar Susah,

**6** Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen. There were 13 cities with their villages.

**7** There were also Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan. There were 4 cities with their villages.

**8** Their property also included all the villages around these cities as far as Baalath Beer (Ramah in the Negev). This was the property of the tribe of Simeon, family by family.

**9** The property of Simeon came from the part of Judah. The part of Judah was too large for them. Thus, the tribe of Simeon received their property inside the land of Judah.

**10** The 3rd lot was for the tribe of Zebulun, family by family. The border of their property went as far as Sarid.

**11** It went west to Maralah and touched Dabbesheth. It continued to the valley near Jokneam.

**12** From Sarid it turned east to the border of Kisloth Tabor. It went on to Daberath and up to Japhia.

**13** From there it continued east to Gath Hepher and Eth Kazin. It went on to Rimmon and turned toward Neah.

**14** On the north side the border went around to Hannathon. It ended at the Valley of Iphtah El.

**15** The land included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem. There were 12 cities with their villages.

**16** These cities with their villages were the property of the tribe of Zebulun, family by family.

**17** The 4th lot was for the tribe of Issachar, family by family.

**18** Their land included Jezreel, Kesulloth, Shunem,

**19** Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,

**20** Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,

**21** Remeth, En Gannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez.

**22** The border touched Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth Shemesh. It ended at the Jordan. There were 16 cities with their villages.

**23** These cities with their villages were the property of the tribe of Issachar, family by family.

**24** The 5th lot was for the tribe of Asher, family by family.

**25** Their land included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Akshaph,

**26** Allammelek, Amad, and Mishal. On the west the border touched Carmel and Shihor Libnath.

**27** Then it turned east toward Beth Dagon. It touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah El. It went north to Beth Emek and Neiel. It continued north to Kabul.

**28** It went to Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.

**29** Then the border turned toward Ramah and the city of Tyre, which had strong walls. It turned toward Hosah and ended at the sea in the area of Akzib.

**30** The land also included Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob. There were 22 cities with their villages.

**31** These cities with their villages were the property of the tribe of Asher, family by family.

**32** The 6th lot was for the tribe of Naphtali, family by family.

**33** Their border went from Heleph and the large tree in Zaanannim. It went past Adami Nekeb and Jabneel to Lakkum. It ended at the Jordan.

**34** Then the border turned west to Aznoth Tabor and went on to Hukkok. It touched Zebulun on the south and Asher on the west. On the east it touched Judah at the Jordan.

**35** The cities with strong walls were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Kinnereth,

**36** Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,

**37** Kedesh, Edrei, En Hazor,

**38** Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh. There were 19 cities with their villages.

**39** These cities with their villages were the property of the tribe of Naphtali, family by family.

**40** The 7th lot was for the tribe of Dan, family by family.

**41** Their property included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir Shemesh,

**42** Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,

**43** Elon, Timnah, Ekron,

**44** Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,

**45** Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon,

**46** Me Jarkon, and Rakkon, with the area across from Joppa.

**47** But the tribe of Dan lost their land. Thus, the people of Dan went up and attacked Leshem. They took the city and killed its people with the sword. They took the land and lived there. They changed the name of Leshem to Dan, the name of their ancestor.

**48** These cities with their villages were the property of the tribe of Dan, family by family.

**49** The people of Israel completed the division of the land into its parts. Then they gave some property among them to Joshua the son of Nun.

**50** They gave him the city that he asked for, as the LORD told them. It was Timnath Serah in the hills of Ephraim. Joshua built the city again and lived there.

**51** Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the leaders of the tribes of Israel divided these areas by lot. They did this at Shiloh in front of the LORD, at the entrance to the tent of the assembly. Thus, they completed the division of the land.

## Chapter 20

**1** The LORD spoke to Joshua. He said,

**2** "Tell the people of Israel this: 'Choose the cities of refuge (cities of safety). I told you about them through Moses.

**3** If a person kills somebody by accident and without the intention to kill, that person can run to one of these cities. These cities will give him protection from the relative who wants to kill him for revenge.

**4** He must run to one of these cities and stand at the entrance of the city gate. He must tell his story to the leaders of that city. Then the leaders must take him into the city. They must give him a place to live among them.

**5** The relative who wants revenge can chase him. But the leaders must not give the person to the relative. That person killed his neighbor by accident. He did not hate his neighbor before.

**6** The person must stay in that city until he stands in front of the people for judgment. He must stay there until the death of the high priest who serves at that time. Then he can go back to his own city and his own house. He can go back to the city that he ran away from.'"

**7** Thus, the Israelites chose these cities. They chose Kedesh in Galilee in the hills of Naphtali and Shechem in the hills of Ephraim. They also chose Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron) in the hills of Judah.

**8** On the east side of the Jordan, across from Jericho, they chose these cities. From the tribe of Reuben, they chose Bezer in the desert on the plain. From the tribe of Gad, they chose Ramoth in Gilead. From the tribe of Manasseh, they chose Golan in Bashan.

**9** These were the cities for all the people of Israel and for the foreigners who lived among them. If a person killed somebody by accident, he could run to one of these cities. Then the relative who wanted revenge could not kill him before he stood in front of the people for judgment.

## Chapter 21

**1** The leaders of the families of the Levites went to Eleazar the priest and to Joshua the son of Nun. They also went to the leaders of the tribes of Israel.

**2** They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan. They said, "The LORD told Moses to give us cities to live in. He also told Moses to give us the fields around these cities for our animals."

**3** Thus, the people of Israel gave these cities and their fields to the Levites from their own property, as the LORD told them.

**4** The first lot was for the families of Kohath. The Levites who were descendants of Aaron the priest received 13 cities by lot. These cities came from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.

**5** The other descendants of Kohath received 10 cities by lot. These cities came from the tribes of Ephraim and Dan and from half the tribe of Manasseh.

**6** The descendants of Gershon received 13 cities by lot. These cities came from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali and from half the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.

**7** The descendants of Merari, family by family, received 12 cities. These cities came from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

**8** Thus, the people of Israel gave these cities and their fields to the Levites by lot. The LORD gave this command through Moses.

**9** From the tribes of Judah and Simeon, they gave these cities. Here are their names.

**10** These cities were for the descendants of Aaron, from the families of Kohath, who were Levites. They received the first lot.

**11** The Israelites gave them Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron) in the hills of Judah, with the fields around it. Arba was the father of Anak.

**12** But they gave the fields farther from the city and its villages to Caleb the son of Jephunneh as his property.

**13** Thus, the Israelites gave these cities with their fields to the descendants of Aaron the priest. They gave Hebron, a city of refuge for a person who killed somebody by accident. They also gave Libnah,

**14** Jattir, Eshtemoa,

**15** Holon, Debir,

**16** Ain, Juttah, and Beth Shemesh. There were 9 cities from these 2 tribes.

**17** From the tribe of Benjamin they gave these cities with their fields: Gibeon, Geba,

**18** Anathoth, and Almon. There were 4 cities.

**19** There was a total of 13 cities with their fields for the priests, the descendants of Aaron.

**20** The other families of Kohath, who were Levites, received cities by lot from the tribe of Ephraim.

**21** The Israelites gave them these cities with their fields. They gave Shechem in the hills of Ephraim, a city of refuge for a person who killed somebody by accident. They also gave Gezer,

**22** Kibzaim, and Beth Horon. There were 4 cities.

**23** From the tribe of Dan they gave these cities with their fields: Eltekeh, Gibbethon,

**24** Aijalon, and Gath Rimmon. There were 4 cities.

**25** From half the tribe of Manasseh they gave these cities with their fields: Taanach and Gath Rimmon. There were 2 cities.

**26** There was a total of 10 cities with their fields for the other families of Kohath.

**27** The families of Gershon were also Levites. The Israelites gave them these cities with their fields from the other half of the tribe of Manasseh. They gave Golan in Bashan, a city of refuge for a person who killed somebody by accident. They also gave Be Eshterah. There were 2 cities.

**28** From the tribe of Issachar they gave these cities with their fields: Kishion, Daberath,

**29** Jarmuth, and En Gannim. There were 4 cities.

**30** From the tribe of Asher they gave these cities with their fields: Mishal, Abdon,

**31** Helkath, and Rehob. There were 4 cities.

**32** From the tribe of Naphtali they gave these cities with their fields. They gave Kedesh in Galilee, a city of refuge for a person who killed somebody by accident. They also gave Hammoth Dor and Kartan. There were 3 cities.

**33** There was a total of 13 cities with their fields for the families of Gershon.

**34** The families of Merari were the other Levites. From the tribe of Zebulun, the Israelites gave them these cities with their fields: Jokneam, Kartah,

**35** Dimnah, and Nahalal. There were 4 cities.

**36** From the tribe of Reuben they gave these cities with their fields: Bezer, Jahaz,

**37** Kedemoth, and Mephaath. There were 4 cities.

**38** From the tribe of Gad they gave these cities with their fields. They gave Ramoth in Gilead, a city of refuge for a person who killed somebody by accident. They also gave Mahanaim,

**39** Heshbon, and Jazer. There was a total of 4 cities.

**40** Thus, the families of Merari, the other Levites, received a total of 12 cities by lot.

**41** The Levites received a total of 48 cities with their fields inside the land of Israel.

**42** Each of these cities had fields around it. All the cities were the same in this.

**43** Thus, the LORD gave Israel all the land that he promised to give to their fathers. The Israelites took the land and lived in it.

**44** The LORD gave them peace on all sides, as he promised their fathers. None of their enemies could stand against them. The LORD gave all their enemies to them.

**45** The LORD made many good promises to the people of Israel. He kept each of these promises. All of them came true.

## Chapter 22

**1** Then Joshua called the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

**2** He said to them, "You did all the things that Moses, the servant of the LORD, told you to do. You also obeyed me in all the things that I told you to do.

**3** For a long time, until today, you did not leave your brothers. You carefully obeyed the commands of the LORD your God.

**4** Now the LORD your God gave peace to your brothers, as he promised them. Thus, now go back to your homes. Go back to your land on the east side of the Jordan. Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you that land.

**5** But be very careful to obey the commands and the law that Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you. Love the LORD your God. Live as he tells you. Obey his commands. Stay close to him. Serve him with all your heart and with all your soul."

**6** Then Joshua blessed them and sent them away. They went to their homes.

**7** Moses gave land in Bashan to half the tribe of Manasseh. Joshua gave land to the other half of the tribe on the west side of the Jordan, among their brothers. When Joshua sent them to their homes, he blessed them.

**8** He said to them, "Go back to your homes with much wealth. Take very many animals, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and very many clothes. Share with your brothers the possessions that you took from your enemies."

**9** Thus, the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh left the people of Israel. They left Shiloh in the land of Canaan. They went back to Gilead, their own land. They received that land as the LORD told Moses.

**10** They came to the area near the Jordan in the land of Canaan. There they built a very large altar near the Jordan.

**11** The people of Israel heard about this. Somebody said, "Look, the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh built an altar. They built it at the border of the land of Canaan, near the Jordan, on the Israelite side."

**12** When the people of Israel heard this, all of them came together at Shiloh. They got ready to go and fight against these tribes.

**13** The people of Israel sent Phinehas, the son of Eleazar the priest, to the land of Gilead. He went to the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

**14** 10 leaders went with Phinehas, 1 from each tribe of Israel. Each one was the head of a family among the clans of Israel.

**15** They came to the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead. They said to them,

**16** "All the people of the LORD say this: 'Why did you do this bad thing against the God of Israel? Why do you turn away from the LORD today? You built an altar for yourselves. Today you rebel against the LORD.

**17** Remember our sin at Peor. Because of that sin, a disease came on the people of the LORD. Even today we are not clean from that sin. That sin is sufficient!

**18** Now you turn away from the LORD today. If you rebel against the LORD today, then tomorrow he will be angry with all the people of Israel.

**19** If you think that your land is unclean, come over into the land of the LORD. The tabernacle of the LORD is there. Take some land among us. But do not rebel against the LORD or against us. Do not build an altar other than the altar of the LORD our God.

**20** Remember Achan the son of Zerah. He did not obey the command about the things for destruction. Then God was angry with all the people of Israel. Achan was not the only person who died because of his sin.'"

**21** Then the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of the clans of Israel. They said,

**22** "The LORD is the Mighty One, God! The LORD is the Mighty One, God! He knows, and Israel must also know! If we rebelled against the LORD or did not obey him, then do not save us today.

**23** If we built an altar to turn away from the LORD, then let the LORD punish us. If we built it for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or peace offerings, then let the LORD punish us.

**24** No! We did this because we were afraid. We thought that in the future your children will say to our children, 'You have no part in the LORD, the God of Israel.

**25** The LORD made the Jordan a border between us and you, you people of Reuben and Gad. You have no part in the LORD.' Then your children will cause our children to stop their worship of the LORD.

**26** Thus, we said, 'We will build an altar. It is not for burnt offerings or for sacrifices.

**27** It is a witness between us and you, and between our descendants and your descendants. It shows that we will worship the LORD at his tabernacle with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings. Then in the future your children cannot say to our children, "You have no part in the LORD."'

**28** We said, 'In the future they possibly will say this to us or to our descendants. Then we will answer, "Look at this copy of the altar of the LORD. Our fathers made it. It is not for burnt offerings or for sacrifices. It is a witness between us and you."'

**29** We will never rebel against the LORD. We will not turn away from him today. We will not build an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices other than the altar of the LORD our God. His altar is in front of his tabernacle."

**30** Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the clans of Israel heard the words of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh. They were happy with these words.

**31** Phinehas, the son of Eleazar the priest, said to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, "Today we know that the LORD is among us. You did not do this bad thing against the LORD. Thus, you saved the people of Israel from the punishment of the LORD."

**32** Then Phinehas, the son of Eleazar the priest, and the leaders left the tribes of Reuben and Gad in the land of Gilead. They went back to the people of Israel in the land of Canaan. They told them what occurred.

**33** The people of Israel were happy with the report, and they praised God. They did not talk again about a war against the tribes of Reuben and Gad. They did not want to destroy the land where these tribes lived.

**34** The tribes of Reuben and Gad gave the altar the name Ed (witness). They said, "This altar is a witness between us that the LORD is God."

## Chapter 23

**1** Many years after that, the LORD gave Israel peace from all their enemies around them. Joshua was very old at that time.

**2** Joshua called all Israel together. He called their elders, their leaders, their judges, and their officers. He said to them, "I am very old.

**3** You saw all the things that the LORD your God did to all these nations because of you. The LORD your God fought for you.

**4** Look, I gave your tribes the land of the nations that remain, as your property. I divided this land among you by lot. It includes the land of all the nations that I destroyed. It goes from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west.

**5** The LORD your God will push these nations out in front of you. He will remove them. Then you will take their land, as the LORD your God promised you.

**6** Thus, be very strong. Obey all the words in the book of the law of Moses. Do not turn away from the law to the right or to the left.

**7** Do not mix with these nations that remain among you. Do not speak the names of their gods. Do not make promises by the names of their gods. Do not serve these gods or bow down to them.

**8** Stay close to the LORD your God, as you did until today.

**9** The LORD pushed out large and strong nations in front of you. Until today, nobody was able to stand against you.

**10** 1 man of you can chase 1,000 men. The LORD your God fights for you, as he promised you.

**11** Thus, be very careful to love the LORD your God.

**12** But you possibly will turn away from the LORD. You possibly will join with the nations that remain among you. You possibly will marry their people and mix with them.

**13** If you do this, then know this: the LORD your God will not push out these nations in front of you again. These nations will be a trap for you. They will hurt you as a whip on your back and as thorns in your eyes. This will continue until you die and leave this good land. The LORD your God gave you this land.

**14** Now I will die soon, as all people on the earth die. You know with all your heart and with all your soul that the LORD your God kept all his good promises to you. All of them came true. Not 1 of them failed.

**15** The LORD your God kept all his good promises to you. In the same way, he will also bring all the bad things on you that he warned you about. He will do this until he removes you from this good land. The LORD your God gave you this land.

**16** If you do not obey the covenant of the LORD your God, then he will be angry. If you serve other gods and bow down to them, then the LORD will be very angry with you. Then you will die quickly and leave the good land that he gave you."

## Chapter 24

**1** Joshua called all the tribes of Israel together at Shechem. He called the elders, the leaders, the judges, and the officers of Israel. They came and stood in front of God.

**2** Joshua said to all the people, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says this. 'A long time ago, your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River. Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor, lived there. They served other gods.

**3** But I took your father Abraham from the other side of the river. I led him through all the land of Canaan. I gave him many descendants. I gave him a son, Isaac.

**4** I gave Isaac 2 sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hills of Seir as his property. But Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

**5** Then I sent Moses and Aaron. I sent disasters on Egypt by the things that I did there. After that, I brought you out.

**6** I brought your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians chased your fathers with chariots and soldiers on horses to the Red Sea.

**7** Your fathers called to the LORD for help. Then he put darkness between you and the Egyptians. He brought the sea over the Egyptians and covered them. You saw with your own eyes what I did in Egypt. Then you lived in the desert for a long time.

**8** I brought you into the land of the Amorites, who lived on the east side of the Jordan. They fought against you, but I gave them to you. I destroyed them in front of you, and you took their land.

**9** Then Balak the son of Zippor, the king of Moab, got ready to fight against Israel. He sent a message to Balaam the son of Beor. He asked Balaam to curse you.

**10** But I did not listen to Balaam. Thus, Balaam blessed you again and again. I saved you from Balak.

**11** Then you went across the Jordan and came to Jericho. The men of Jericho fought against you. The Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites also fought against you. But I gave them to you.

**12** I sent the hornet (an insect that stings) in front of you. The hornet pushed out the 2 kings of the Amorites in front of you. You did not do this with your sword or your bow.

**13** I gave you a land that you did not work for. I gave you cities that you did not build, and you live in them. You eat fruit from vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant.'

**14** Thus, now respect the LORD. Serve him honestly and faithfully. Throw away the gods that your ancestors served on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt. Serve the LORD.

**15** Possibly you do not want to serve the LORD. Then choose today whom you will serve. You can serve the gods of your ancestors on the other side of the river. Or you can serve the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you live. But my family and I will serve the LORD."

**16** The people answered, "We will never leave the LORD to serve other gods!

**17** The LORD our God brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, where we were slaves. He did those great miracles in front of us. He kept us safe on all our journey and among all the nations that we went through.

**18** The LORD pushed out all the nations in front of us. He pushed out the Amorites who lived in the land. Thus, we will also serve the LORD, because he is our God."

**19** Joshua said to the people, "You cannot serve the LORD. He is a holy God. He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your rebellion or your sins.

**20** If you leave the LORD and serve foreign gods, then he will turn against you. He was good to you before. But then he will bring disaster on you and destroy you."

**21** The people said to Joshua, "No! We will serve the LORD."

**22** Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves. You chose to serve the LORD." The people said, "Yes, we are witnesses."

**23** Joshua said, "Then throw away the foreign gods that are among you. Give your hearts completely to the LORD, the God of Israel."

**24** The people said to Joshua, "We will serve the LORD our God. We will obey him."

**25** Thus, on that day at Shechem, Joshua made a covenant with the people. He gave them laws and rules.

**26** Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God. Then he took a large stone. He put the stone up there below the oak tree near the holy place of the LORD.

**27** Joshua said to all the people, "Look, this stone will be a witness against us. It heard all the words that the LORD spoke to us. Thus, it will be a witness against you if you are not faithful to your God."

**28** Then Joshua sent the people away. Each person went to his own property.

**29** After these things, Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died. He was 110 years old.

**30** The people buried him on his own land at Timnath Serah, in the hills of Ephraim. This place is north of Mount Gaash.

**31** Israel served the LORD during all the life of Joshua. Israel also served the LORD during the lives of the elders who lived after Joshua. These elders knew all the things that the LORD did for Israel.

**32** The people of Israel brought the bones of Joseph up from Egypt. They buried the bones at Shechem, in the field that Jacob bought. Jacob bought the field from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem. He paid 100 pieces of silver for it. This field became the property of the descendants of Joseph.

**33** Eleazar the son of Aaron also died. The people buried him at Gibeah in the hills of Ephraim. The people gave this place to his son Phinehas.

# Judges

## Chapter 1

**1** After Joshua died, the people of Israel asked the LORD a question. They said, "Which tribe will go first to fight against the Canaanites for us?"

**2** The LORD said, "Judah will go. I give the land into the control of Judah."

**3** The men of Judah spoke to the men of Simeon, their brothers. They said, "Come with us into the land that we got by lot. Then we will fight the Canaanites together. Then we will go with you into your land." So the men of Simeon went with them.

**4** The men of Judah attacked. The LORD gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their control. They killed 10,000 men at Bezek.

**5** At Bezek they found Adoni-bezek and fought against him. They defeated the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

**6** But Adoni-bezek ran away. They chased him and caught him. They cut off his thumbs and his big toes.

**7** Adoni-bezek said, "70 kings with no thumbs and no big toes got their food from below my table. Now God paid me back for what I did to them." They took him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
