**12** Abner sent messengers to David for him. Abner said, "Who controls the land? Make an agreement with me. Then I will help you. I will bring all Israel to you."

**13** David said, "Good. I will make an agreement with you. But I tell you to do 1 thing. When you come to see me, bring Michal, the daughter of Saul. If you do not bring her, do not come to see me."

**14** David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul. David said, "Give me my wife Michal. I paid 100 foreskins of the Philistines to marry her."

**15** So Ish-bosheth sent men. They took Michal from her husband Paltiel, the son of Laish.

**16** Her husband went with her and cried behind her all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go back home." So he went back.

**17** Abner spoke with the leaders (elders) of Israel. He said, "In the past you wanted David as your king.

**18** Now do it! The LORD spoke about David. The LORD said, 'I will use my servant David to save my people Israel from the Philistines and from all their enemies.'"

**19** Abner also spoke to the people of Benjamin. Then Abner went to Hebron to speak to David. He told David all that Israel and all the people of Benjamin wanted to do.

**20** Abner came to David at Hebron with 20 men. David made a feast for Abner and his men.

**21** Abner said to David, "I will go now and bring all Israel to you, my lord the king. They will make an agreement with you. Then you will rule over all that you want." So David sent Abner away, and Abner went in peace.

**22** Then the men of David and Joab came back from an attack. They brought many valuable things with them. Abner was not with David in Hebron, because David sent him away in peace.

**23** Joab and all his army arrived. The people told Joab, "Abner, the son of Ner, came to the king. The king sent him away, and Abner went in peace."

**24** Then Joab went to the king and said, "What did you do? Abner came to you. Why did you let him go?

**25** You know Abner, the son of Ner! He came to trick you. He came to learn about all your movements and all that you do."

**26** Joab left David and sent messengers after Abner. They brought Abner back from the well of Sirah. But David did not know about it.

**27** Abner came back to Hebron. Joab took him to the side of the gate to speak with him quietly. There Joab pushed a knife into the stomach of Abner, and Abner died. Joab did this because Abner killed his brother Asahel.

**28** Later, David heard about it. He said, "I and my kingdom are not guilty of the blood of Abner, the son of Ner. The LORD knows this forever.

**29** Let the guilt fall on Joab and on all his family. Let the family of Joab always have a man with a sore, or a man with a skin disease. Let it always have a man who needs a stick to walk. Let it have a man who dies by the sword, or a man who has no food."

**30** Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because Abner killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.

**31** David said to Joab and to all the people with him, "Tear your clothes. Put on rough cloth (sackcloth). Mourn for Abner." King David walked behind the body of Abner.

**32** They buried Abner in Hebron. The king cried loudly at the grave of Abner, and all the people cried.

**33** The king sang this sad song about Abner: "Must Abner die like a fool dies?

**34** No one tied your hands. No one put chains on your feet. You fell as a man falls in front of evil men." And all the people cried again for Abner.

**35** All the people came to David to make him eat food during the day. But David made a promise. He said, "May God punish me very severely if I eat bread or other food before the sun goes down."

**36** All the people saw this, and they were happy. All that the king did made the people happy.

**37** That day all the people and all Israel knew that the king did not cause the death of Abner, the son of Ner.

**38** The king said to his officers, "You know that a great leader died today in Israel.

**39** Today I am weak, although I am the anointed king. These sons of Zeruiah are too strong for me. May the LORD punish the evil man as his evil deserves."

## Chapter 4

**1** Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul, heard that Abner died in Hebron. Then he lost his courage, and all the people of Israel became afraid.

**2** The son of Saul had 2 men who were captains of raid groups. Their names were Baanah and Rechab. They were the sons of Rimmon from Beeroth, of the tribe of Benjamin. The people thought that Beeroth was a part of Benjamin.

**3** The people of Beeroth ran away to Gittaim. They still live there as foreigners today.

**4** Jonathan, the son of Saul, had a son who could not walk well. The news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel when the boy was 5 years old. His nurse picked him up and ran away. She ran quickly, and the boy fell. After that, he could not walk well. His name was Mephibosheth.

**5** Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon from Beeroth, went to the house of Ish-bosheth. They arrived in the hottest part of the day. Ish-bosheth was on his bed at noon.

**6** They went into the house as if they wanted to get wheat. They pushed a knife into the stomach of Ish-bosheth. Then Rechab and his brother Baanah escaped.

**7** When they went into the house, Ish-bosheth was on his bed in his bedroom. They hit him and killed him. They cut off his head and took it with them. They traveled all night on the road through the Jordan Valley.

**8** They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron. They said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul. He was your enemy, and he tried to kill you. Today the LORD punished Saul and his family for you, my lord the king."

**9** David spoke to Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon from Beeroth. He said, "The LORD saved me from all trouble. As surely as the LORD lives, I tell you this:

**10** A man told me, 'Saul is dead.' He thought that his news was good. But I took hold of him and killed him in Ziklag. That was the reward that I gave him for his news.

**11** You are evil men. You killed a good man in his own house on his bed! Thus I will punish you more severely. I will make you pay for his death. I will remove you from the earth!"

**12** David gave an order to his young men, and they killed Rechab and Baanah. They cut off their hands and their feet. They hung the bodies near the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in the tomb of Abner in Hebron.

## Chapter 5

**1** Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron. They said, "We are your own family.

**2** In the past, Saul was our king. But you led the army of Israel in battle and brought it back. The LORD said to you, 'You will take care of my people Israel like a shepherd. You will be the leader of Israel.'"

**3** So all the leaders (elders) of Israel came to King David at Hebron. The king made an agreement with them in Hebron in front of the LORD. They anointed David as king over Israel.

**4** David was 30 years old when he became king. He ruled for 40 years.

**5** In Hebron he ruled over Judah for 7 years and 6 months. In Jerusalem he ruled over all Israel and Judah for 33 years.

**6** The king and his men went to Jerusalem to attack the Jebusites who lived there. The Jebusites said to David, "You will not come in here. Even the blind men and the lame men can stop you." They thought, "David cannot come in here."

**7** But David captured the fortress of Zion. It is now the City of David.

**8** On that day David said, "To attack the Jebusites, go up through the water tunnel. Attack those 'lame and blind' enemies that I hate." Thus the people say, "The blind and the lame will not come into the house."

**9** David lived in the fortress and called it the City of David. David built walls around the city, from the Millo inward.

**10** David became more and more powerful, because the LORD God of armies was with him.

**11** Hiram, the king of Tyre, sent messengers to David. He also sent cedar trees, carpenters, and stone workers. They built a palace for David.

**12** Then David knew that the LORD made him king over Israel. He knew that the LORD made his kingdom great for the people of Israel.

**13** After David came from Hebron, he took more concubines and wives in Jerusalem. He had more sons and daughters.

**14** These are the names of the sons born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

**15** Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,

**16** Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.

**17** The Philistines heard that the people anointed David as king over Israel. So all the Philistines went to find David. David heard about it and went down to the fortress.

**18** The Philistines came and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

**19** David asked the LORD, "Must I attack the Philistines? Will you give them to me?" The LORD said to David, "Attack them. I will surely give the Philistines to you."

**20** So David went to Baal Perazim, and he defeated the Philistines there. He said, "The LORD broke through my enemies in front of me as a flood of water breaks through." Thus he called that place Baal Perazim.

**21** The Philistines left their idols there. David and his men burned the idols.

**22** The Philistines came again. They spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

**23** David asked the LORD again. The LORD said, "Do not attack them from the front. Go around behind them. Attack them in front of the balsam trees.

**24** You will hear a sound like soldiers that march in the tops of the balsam trees. Then attack quickly. At that time the LORD will go in front of you to defeat the army of the Philistines."

**25** David did as the LORD told him. He defeated the Philistines from Geba to Gezer.

## Chapter 6

**1** Again David brought together all the best men of Israel. There were 30,000 men.

**2** David and all his men went to Baalah in Judah. They went to bring the ark of God from there to Jerusalem. The ark (the sacred box) has the name of the LORD of armies on it. The LORD sits on his throne between the cherubim on the ark.

**3** They put the ark of God on a new cart. They took it from the house of Abinadab on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.

**4** They brought the ark of God from the house of Abinadab on the hill. Ahio walked in front of the ark.

**5** David and all the people of Israel celebrated in front of the LORD. They played all types of instruments made of pine wood. They played lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.

**6** They came to the floor of Nacon where people beat grain. There the oxen stumbled. So Uzzah put out his hand and took hold of the ark of God.

**7** The LORD became angry with Uzzah. God killed him there because of his mistake. Uzzah died there near the ark of God.

**8** David was angry because the LORD killed Uzzah suddenly. David called that place Perez Uzzah. It has that name today.

**9** That day David was afraid of the LORD. He said, "How can the ark of the LORD come to me?"

**10** So David did not take the ark of the LORD into the City of David. He took it to the house of Obed-Edom from Gath.

**11** The ark of the LORD stayed in the house of Obed-Edom from Gath for 3 months. The LORD blessed Obed-Edom and all his family.

**12** People told King David, "The LORD blessed the family of Obed-Edom and all that he has because of the ark of God." So David went and brought the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the City of David. He was very happy.

**13** The men who carried the ark of the LORD walked 6 steps. Then David sacrificed a bull and a fat calf.

**14** David danced in front of the LORD with all his strength. He wore a linen apron (ephod).

**15** David and all the people of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD. They shouted and blew trumpets.

**16** The ark of the LORD came into the City of David. Michal, the daughter of Saul, looked through a window. She saw King David as he jumped and danced in front of the LORD. Then she hated him in her heart.

**17** They brought in the ark of the LORD. They put it in its place in the tent that David put up for it. David gave burnt offerings and peace offerings in front of the LORD.

**18** David finished the burnt offerings and the peace offerings. Then he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of armies.

**19** He gave food to all the people of Israel, to the men and to the women. He gave each person a loaf of bread, a good piece of meat, and a container of wine. Then all the people went back to their homes.

**20** David went home to bless his family. Michal, the daughter of Saul, came out to meet him. She said, "Today the king of Israel did not act with honor! Today he took off his clothes in front of the slave girls of his officers. He acted like a foolish man with no shame!"

**21** David said to Michal, "I did it in front of the LORD. The LORD chose me instead of your father and all his family. He made me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel. Thus I will celebrate in front of the LORD.

**22** I will make myself even less important than this. I will be humble in my own eyes. But the slave girls that you spoke about will give me honor."

**23** Michal, the daughter of Saul, had no children all her life.

## Chapter 7

**1** King David lived in his palace. The LORD gave him peace from all the enemies around him.

**2** Then the king said to Nathan the prophet, "Look! I live in a palace of cedar wood. But the ark of God stays in a tent."

**3** Nathan said to the king, "Go and do all that you want to do. The LORD is with you."

**4** But that night the LORD spoke to Nathan. He said,

**5** "Go and tell my servant David, 'The LORD says this: You will not build a house for me to live in.

**6** I did not live in a house from the day that I brought the people of Israel out of Egypt until today. I moved from place to place in a tent (tabernacle).

**7** I moved with all the people of Israel to many places. I told leaders of the tribes to take care of my people Israel like shepherds. I did not ask one of them, "Why did you not build a house of cedar for me?"'

**8** Now tell my servant David, 'The LORD of armies says this: I took you from the field where you took care of the sheep. I made you the leader of my people Israel.

**9** I was with you in all the places where you went. I destroyed all your enemies in front of you. I will make your name great, as the names of the great men on the earth.

**10** I will make a place for my people Israel. I will put them there like a tree in the ground. They will live in their own place, and they will not move again. Evil people will not hurt them again as before.

**11** In the past I put judges over my people Israel. But I will give you peace from all your enemies. The LORD tells you that he will make a family of kings from you.

**12** Your life will end, and you will die. People will bury you with your ancestors. Then I will make one of your own sons king after you. I will make his kingdom strong.

**13** He will build a house for my name. I will make the throne of his kingdom strong forever.

**14** I will be his father, and he will be my son. If he does wrong, I will punish him as a father punishes his son.

**15** But I will not stop my love for him. I took my love from Saul, and I removed Saul from your path. But I will not do that to your son.

**16** Your family and your kingdom will continue forever in front of me. Your throne will continue forever.'"

**17** Nathan told David all these words and all that God showed him.

**18** Then King David went in and sat in front of the LORD. He said, "Lord GOD, who am I? My family is not important. But you brought me to this place.

**19** Lord GOD, you think that this is a small thing. So you also spoke about the future of my family for a long time to come. Lord GOD, this is not usual for a man!

**20** What more can I, David, say to you? Lord GOD, you know me, your servant.

**21** You did all these great things because of your word and because you wanted to do them. You told me, your servant, about them.

**22** Lord GOD, you are great! No one is like you. There is no God but you. We heard all this with our own ears.

**23** No other nation on earth is like your people Israel. God went to free them, and he made them his own people. He made his name famous. He did great and wonderful things for them. He made other nations and their gods go out in front of your people. You freed your people from Egypt for yourself.

**24** You made your people Israel your own people forever. And you, LORD, became their God.

**25** Now, LORD God, keep your promise about me, your servant, and about my family forever. Do as you said.

**26** Then your name will be great forever. People will say, 'The LORD of armies is God over Israel!' Then the family of your servant David will continue strong in front of you.

**27** LORD of armies, God of Israel, you showed this to me, your servant. You said, 'I will build a family of kings from you.' Thus I, your servant, have the courage to pray this prayer to you.

**28** Lord GOD, you are God! Your words are true. You promised these good things to me, your servant.

**29** Now please bless the family of your servant. Let it continue forever in front of you. Lord GOD, you spoke these words. With your blessing, the family of your servant will have blessing forever."

## Chapter 8

**1** After this, David defeated the Philistines and made them weak. He took control of Metheg Ammah from the Philistines.

**2** David also defeated the people of Moab. He made the men lie down on the ground in rows. He measured them with a rope. He killed the men in 2 lengths of rope. He let the men in 1 length of rope live. So the people of Moab became servants of David and paid money (tribute) to him.

**3** David also defeated Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, the king of Zobah. Hadadezer went to take back control of the land near the Euphrates River.

**4** David captured 1,000 chariots, 700 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. David cut the leg tendons of all the chariot horses. But he kept enough horses for 100 chariots.

**5** The Syrians from Damascus came to help Hadadezer, the king of Zobah. But David killed 22,000 of the Syrians.

**6** Then David put groups of soldiers in Syria near Damascus. The Syrians became servants of David and paid money (tribute) to him. The LORD gave David victory in all the places where he went.

**7** David took the gold shields of the officers of Hadadezer. He brought them to Jerusalem.

**8** King David also took very much bronze from Betah and Berothai. These were cities of Hadadezer.

**9** Toi, the king of Hamath, heard that David defeated all the army of Hadadezer.

**10** So Toi sent his son Joram to King David. Joram greeted David and congratulated him because David fought against Hadadezer and defeated him. Hadadezer was often at war with Toi. Joram brought with him objects of silver, gold, and bronze.

**11** King David gave these objects to the LORD. He also gave to the LORD the silver and gold from all the nations that he defeated.

**12** He took these from Syria, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek. He also took valuable things from Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, the king of Zobah.

**13** David became famous when he came back. He killed 18,000 Syrians in the Valley of Salt.

**14** He put groups of soldiers in all of Edom. All the people of Edom became servants of David. The LORD gave David victory in all the places where he went.

**15** David ruled over all Israel. He did what was right and fair for all his people.

**16** Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was the commander of the army. Jehoshaphat, the son of Ahilud, wrote the records of the kingdom.

**17** Zadok, the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech, the son of Abiathar, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.

**18** Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, was the commander of the Kerethites and the Pelethites. The sons of David were chief officials.

## Chapter 9

**1** David asked, "Is someone from the family of Saul still alive? I want to be kind to him because of Jonathan."

**2** A servant of the family of Saul had the name Ziba. The people called him to David. The king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" He said, "Yes, I am your servant."

**3** The king asked, "Is someone from the family of Saul still alive? I want to show the kindness of God to him." Ziba said to the king, "Jonathan has a son who is still alive. He cannot walk well."

**4** The king asked Ziba, "Where is he?" Ziba said to the king, "He is in the house of Makir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar."

**5** So King David sent men to bring him from the house of Makir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar.

**6** Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan and the grandson of Saul. He came to David and bowed down to the ground to show respect. David said, "Mephibosheth!" He said, "I am your servant."

**7** David said to him, "Do not be afraid. I will surely be kind to you because of your father Jonathan. I will give back to you all the land of your grandfather Saul. You will always eat at my table."

**8** Mephibosheth bowed down and said, "I am your servant, but I am not important. I am like a dead dog. Why do you show kindness to me?"

**9** Then the king called Ziba, the servant of Saul. He said to him, "I gave to the grandson of your master all that was Saul's and his family's.

**10** You, your sons, and your servants must work the land for him. You must bring in the crops. Then the grandson of your master will have food to eat. But Mephibosheth, the grandson of your master, will always eat at my table." Ziba had 15 sons and 20 servants.

**11** Then Ziba said to the king, "I, your servant, will do all that my lord the king tells me." So Mephibosheth ate at the table of David like one of the sons of the king.

**12** Mephibosheth had a young son. His name was Mica. All the people in the house of Ziba became servants of Mephibosheth.

**13** Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the table of the king. He was lame in both feet.

## Chapter 10

**1** After this, the king of the Ammonites died. His son Hanun became king after him.

**2** David said, "I will be kind to Hanun, the son of Nahash, because his father was kind to me." So David sent some of his officers to comfort Hanun about the death of his father. The officers of David came into the land of the Ammonites.

**3** But the leaders of the Ammonites said to their lord Hanun, "Do you think that David honors your father? Do you think that this is why he sent men to comfort you? No! David sent his officers to look at the city. They will spy on it and then destroy it."

**4** So Hanun took the officers of David. He shaved off half of the beard of each man. He cut off their clothes in the middle, at the hips. Then he sent them away.

**5** People told David about this. He sent messengers to meet the men, because the men were very ashamed. The king said, "Stay at Jericho until your beards grow again. Then come back."

**6** The Ammonites knew that David hated them now. So the Ammonites hired 20,000 foot soldiers from the Syrians of Beth Rehob and Zobah. They also hired 1,000 men from the king of Maacah and 12,000 men from Tob.

**7** David heard about it. He sent Joab with all the army of strong soldiers.

**8** The Ammonites came out and got ready for battle at the entrance of the city gate. The Syrians of Zobah and Rehob, and the men of Tob and Maacah, stayed by themselves in the open field.

**9** Joab saw that the enemy was in front of him and behind him. So he chose some of the best soldiers of Israel. He put them in position against the Syrians.

**10** He gave the other men to his brother Abishai. Abishai put them in position against the Ammonites.

**11** Joab said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you must help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come and help you.

**12** Be strong! Let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. The LORD will do what he thinks is good."

**13** Joab and his men went near to attack the Syrians. The Syrians ran away from him.

**14** The Ammonites saw that the Syrians ran away. So they also ran away from Abishai and went into the city. Then Joab stopped the attack on the Ammonites and went back to Jerusalem.

**15** The Syrians saw that Israel defeated them. So they came together again.

**16** Hadadezer sent messengers and brought the Syrians from the other side of the Euphrates River. They came to Helam. Shobach, the commander of the army of Hadadezer, led them.

**17** People told David about this. He brought all Israel together, went across the Jordan River, and came to Helam. The Syrians got ready for battle against David and fought with him.

**18** But the Syrians ran away from Israel. David killed the men of 700 Syrian chariots and 40,000 horsemen. He also attacked Shobach, the commander of their army, and Shobach died there.

**19** All the kings who served Hadadezer saw that Israel defeated them. So they made peace with Israel and became servants of Israel. After that, the Syrians were afraid to help the Ammonites again.

## Chapter 11

**1** In the spring, kings usually go out to battle. At that time David sent out Joab, his officers, and all the army of Israel. They destroyed the Ammonites and attacked the city of Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem.

**2** One evening David got up from his bed. He walked on the roof of the palace. From the roof he saw a woman who washed herself. The woman was very beautiful.

**3** David sent someone to find out about the woman. The man said, "She is Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam. She is the wife of Uriah the Hittite."

**4** David sent messengers to get her. She came to him, and he had sex with her. She was clean again after her monthly period. Then she went back to her house.

**5** The woman became pregnant. She sent a message to David. She said, "I am pregnant."

**6** David sent a message to Joab. He said, "Send me Uriah the Hittite." So Joab sent Uriah to David.

**7** Uriah came to David. David asked him about Joab, about the soldiers, and about the war.

**8** Then David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." Uriah left the palace. The king sent a gift of food after him.

**9** But Uriah did not go down to his house. He slept at the door of the palace with all the officers of his master.

**10** People told David, "Uriah did not go down to his house." So David said to Uriah, "You came from a long trip. Why did you not go down to your house?"

**11** Uriah said to David, "The ark, Israel, and Judah stay in tents. My master Joab and his officers are in camp in the open fields. Thus I cannot go to my house to eat, drink, and have sex with my wife. As surely as you live, I will not do this!"

**12** Then David said to Uriah, "Stay here today too. Tomorrow I will send you back." So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next day.

**13** David invited Uriah, and Uriah ate and drank with him. David made him drunk. But in the evening, Uriah went out to sleep on his mat with the officers of his master. He did not go down to his house.

**14** In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab. He sent it with Uriah.

**15** In the letter David wrote, "Put Uriah at the front, where the fight is the worst. Then move back from him. Then the enemy will kill him."

**16** Joab watched the city carefully. He put Uriah at a place where he knew the strongest enemy soldiers were.

**17** The men of the city came out and fought against Joab. Some of the officers of David died. Uriah the Hittite also died.

**18** Then Joab sent David a full report about the battle.

**19** Joab told the messenger, "Tell the king all the news about the battle.

**20** Then the king will possibly become angry. He will possibly ask you, 'Why did you go so near to the city to fight? You knew that the enemy will shoot arrows from the wall.

**21** Who killed Abimelech, the son of Jerub-Besheth? A woman threw a millstone on him from the wall, and he died in Thebez. Why did you go so near to the wall?' If the king asks this, tell him, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead too.'"

**22** The messenger went to David. He told David all that Joab sent him to say.

**23** The messenger said to David, "The enemy was stronger than us. They came out to attack us in the field. But we pushed them back to the entrance of the city gate.

**24** Then the archers shot arrows at your officers from the wall. Some of the officers of the king died. Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead too."

**25** David said to the messenger, "Tell Joab this: 'Do not let this trouble you. The sword kills one man and then another man. Make your attack on the city stronger and destroy it.' Thus give courage to Joab."

**26** The wife of Uriah heard that her husband Uriah was dead. She mourned for him.

**27** After the time of grief ended, David sent men to bring her to his house. She became his wife and had a son by him. But the LORD was not happy with what David did.

## Chapter 12

**1** The LORD sent Nathan to David. Nathan came to David and said, "There were 2 men in a city. One man was rich, and the other man was poor.

**2** The rich man had very many sheep and cattle.

**3** But the poor man had nothing, only 1 small female lamb. He bought it and took care of it. It grew up with him and his children. It ate from his food and drank from his cup. It slept in his arms. It was like a daughter to him.

**4** A traveler came to the rich man. The rich man did not want to take one of his own sheep or cattle to make a meal for the traveler. So he took the lamb of the poor man. He cooked it for his guest."

**5** David became very angry with the rich man. He said to Nathan, "As surely as the LORD lives, the man who did this must die!

**6** He must pay back 4 lambs for that lamb, because he did this and had no pity."

**7** Nathan said to David, "You are that man! The LORD God of Israel says this: 'I anointed you king over Israel. I saved you from Saul.

**8** I gave you the house of your master and the wives of your master. I gave you the people of Israel and Judah. If that was not enough, I was ready to give you much more.

**9** Why did you show no respect for the command of the LORD? Why did you do this evil thing in front of him? You killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword. You took his wife as your wife. You used the sword of the Ammonites to kill him.

**10** Thus the sword will never go away from your family. You showed no respect for me. You took the wife of Uriah the Hittite as your wife.'

**11** The LORD says this: 'I will cause trouble against you from your own family. In front of your eyes, I will take your wives and give them to another man. He will have sex with your wives in the daylight.

**12** You did your sin secretly. But I will do this in front of all Israel, in the daylight.'"

**13** David said to Nathan, "I sinned against the LORD." Nathan said to David, "The LORD forgives your sin. You will not die.

**14** But you did this, and thus you caused the enemies of the LORD to insult him. So the son that your wife gave birth to will surely die."

**15** Then Nathan went home. The LORD caused the child that the wife of Uriah had by David to become very sick.

**16** David prayed to God for the child. He did not eat. He went into his room and lay on the ground all night.

**17** The leaders of his household came to him. They tried to lift him up from the ground. But he did not agree, and he did not eat food with them.

**18** On the seventh day, the child died. The officers of David were afraid to tell him that the child was dead. They said, "When the child was still alive, we spoke to David. But he did not listen to us. If we tell him that the child is dead, he will possibly hurt himself."

**19** But David saw that his officers whispered to each other. So he knew that the child was dead. David asked his officers, "Is the child dead?" They said, "Yes, he is dead."

**20** Then David got up from the ground. He washed, put on oil, and changed his clothes. He went into the house of the LORD and worshipped. Then he went to his own house. He asked for food, and they gave him food. He ate.

**21** His officers said to him, "Why do you do this? When the child was alive, you did not eat and you cried. But now the child is dead, and you get up and eat food!"

**22** David said, "When the child was still alive, I did not eat and I cried. I thought, 'Possibly the LORD will be kind to me and let the child live.'

**23** But now the child is dead. Why must I continue to fast? I cannot bring him back. I will go to him, but he will not come back to me."

**24** Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba. He went to her and had sex with her. She had a son, and David gave him the name Solomon. The LORD loved the child.

**25** The LORD sent a message through Nathan the prophet. Nathan gave the child the name Jedidiah, because the LORD loved him.

**26** Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites. He captured the royal fortress.

**27** Joab sent messengers to David. He said, "I fought against Rabbah. I captured the water supply of the city.

**28** Now bring together the rest of the army. Attack the city and capture it. If you do not, I will capture the city. Then people will call the city by my name."

**29** So David brought together all the army and went to Rabbah. He fought against the city and captured it.

**30** David took the crown from the head of their king. The crown was of gold and had valuable stones on it. It weighed about 34 kilograms. The people put the crown on the head of David. David also took very many valuable things from the city.

**31** David brought out the people of the city. He made them work with saws, iron picks, and iron axes. He made them work at the brick ovens. David did the same to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then David and all the army went back to Jerusalem.

## Chapter 13

**1** After this, Amnon, the son of David, loved Tamar. Tamar was the beautiful sister of Absalom, another son of David.

**2** Amnon wanted Tamar so much that he became sick. She was a virgin. Amnon thought that he could not do anything to her.

**3** Amnon had a friend with the name Jonadab. Jonadab was the son of Shimeah, the brother of David. Jonadab was a very clever man.

**4** Jonadab said to Amnon, "You are the son of the king. Why do you become thinner each day? Tell me." Amnon said to him, "I love Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom."

**5** Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and act as if you are sick. Your father will come to see you. Then say to him, 'Please let my sister Tamar come and give me food. Let her make the food in front of me. Then I can see it and eat it from her hand.'"

**6** So Amnon lay down and acted as if he was sick. The king came to see him. Amnon said to the king, "Please let my sister Tamar come. Let her make 2 cakes in front of me. Then I can eat from her hand."

**7** David sent a message to Tamar at the palace. He said, "Go to the house of your brother Amnon and make food for him."

**8** So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon. He was in bed. She took flour and mixed it. She made cakes in front of him and cooked them.

**9** She took the pan and put the cakes in front of him. But he did not eat. Amnon said, "Send all the people out of here." So all the people went out.

**10** Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the bedroom. Then I can eat from your hand." Tamar took the cakes that she made. She brought them into the bedroom to her brother Amnon.

**11** She brought the cakes to him to eat. But he took hold of her and said, "My sister, come and have sex with me."

**12** She said to him, "No, my brother! Do not force me! People must not do this in Israel. Do not do this foolish act!

**13** Where can I go with my shame? And you will be like one of the foolish men in Israel. Please speak to the king. He will let you marry me."

**14** But Amnon did not listen to her. He was stronger than she was. He forced her and raped her.

**15** Then Amnon hated her very much. His hate for her was greater than his love for her before. Amnon said to her, "Get up and go away!"

**16** She said to him, "No! If you send me away, that is a worse wrong than the wrong that you did to me." But he did not listen to her.

**17** He called his young servant and said, "Put this woman out of my room. Lock the door behind her."

**18** Tamar wore a long robe with sleeves. The virgin daughters of the king wore robes of this type. The servant put her out and locked the door behind her.

**19** Tamar put ashes on her head. She tore the long robe that she wore. She put her hand on her head and went away. She cried loudly as she went.

**20** Her brother Absalom said to her, "Did your brother Amnon do this to you? Now be quiet, my sister. He is your brother. Do not let this trouble you." So Tamar lived in the house of her brother Absalom. She was alone and very sad.

**21** King David heard about all these things. He became very angry.

**22** Absalom did not speak to his brother Amnon, good or bad. Absalom hated Amnon because Amnon raped his sister Tamar.

**23** After 2 full years, Absalom had men who cut the wool from his sheep in Baal Hazor, near Ephraim. Absalom invited all the sons of the king.

**24** Absalom went to the king and said, "Your servant has men who cut the wool from the sheep. Please let the king and his officers come with me."

**25** The king said to Absalom, "No, my son. We will not all go. We will be too much trouble for you." Absalom asked him again and again. But the king did not go. He blessed Absalom.

**26** Then Absalom said, "If you do not go, please let my brother Amnon go with us." The king said to him, "Why must he go with you?"

**27** But Absalom asked again and again. So the king let Amnon and all the sons of the king go with Absalom.

**28** Absalom gave an order to his servants. He said, "Watch Amnon. When he is happy from the wine, I will say to you, 'Attack Amnon!' Then kill him. Do not be afraid. I gave you the order. Be strong and brave."

**29** So the servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom told them. Then all the other sons of the king got up. Each man got on his mule and ran away.

**30** While they were on the road, news came to David. The news was, "Absalom killed all the sons of the king. Not one of them is alive."

**31** The king got up and tore his clothes. He lay on the ground. All his officers stood near him with their clothes torn.

**32** But Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, the brother of David, spoke. He said, "My lord, do not think that they killed all the young men, the sons of the king. Only Amnon is dead. Absalom made this plan on the day that Amnon raped his sister Tamar.

**33** My lord the king, do not believe the news that all the sons of the king are dead. Only Amnon is dead."

**34** But Absalom ran away. The young man who was the guard looked up. He saw many people who came on the road from the west, along the side of the hill.

**35** Jonadab said to the king, "Look, the sons of the king come! It is as I, your servant, said."

**36** When he finished his words, the sons of the king arrived. They cried loudly. The king and all his officers also cried very much.

**37** But Absalom ran away. He went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. David mourned for his son every day.

**38** Absalom ran away to Geshur. He stayed there for 3 years.

**39** Then King David wanted very much to go to Absalom. He stopped his sadness about the death of Amnon.

## Chapter 14

**1** Joab, the son of Zeruiah, knew that the king thought about Absalom very much.

**2** So Joab sent a man to Tekoa to bring a wise woman. Joab said to her, "Please act as if you are sad for a dead person. Put on clothes for grief. Do not put oil on yourself. Act like a woman who was sad for the dead for a long time.

**3** Then go to the king and say these words to him." Joab told her the words that she must say.

**4** The woman from Tekoa went to the king. She bowed down to the ground to show respect. She said, "King, help me!"

**5** The king said to her, "What is your problem?" She said, "I am a widow. My husband is dead.

**6** I, your servant, had 2 sons. They fought each other in the field. No one was there to separate them. One son hit the other son and killed him.

**7** Now all the family is against me, your servant. They say, 'Give us the man who killed his brother. We will kill him because he killed his brother. We will also kill the only son who can receive the property of the family.' If they do this, they will take the last hope that I have. My husband will have no name and no family on the earth."

**8** The king said to the woman, "Go home. I will give an order about your problem."

**9** The woman from Tekoa said to the king, "My lord the king, let the guilt be on me and on the family of my father. The king and his throne are not guilty."

**10** The king said, "If a person says something against you, bring him to me. He will not trouble you again."

**11** She said, "Please, king, pray to the LORD your God. Do not let the relative who wants revenge kill again. Do not let him kill my son." The king said, "As surely as the LORD lives, no one will hurt your son. Not one hair of his head will fall to the ground."

**12** Then the woman said, "Please let me, your servant, say 1 more thing to my lord the king." He said, "Speak."

**13** The woman said, "Why did you think a thing like this against the people of God? When you say this, you show that you are guilty. You do not bring back your own son who had to go away.

**14** All of us must die. We are like water on the ground. No one can pick up the water again. But God does not take life away. He makes plans to bring back a person who had to go away.

**15** I came to speak to my lord the king about this because the people made me afraid. I, your servant, thought, 'I will speak to the king. Possibly the king will do what I ask.

**16** The king will listen and save me, his servant, from the man who wants to kill me and my son. That man wants to remove us from the land that God gave to us.'

**17** I, your servant, thought, 'The words of my lord the king will give me peace.' My lord the king is like an angel of God. He knows the difference between good and bad. May the LORD your God be with you!"

**18** Then the king said to the woman, "Do not hide from me the answer to the question that I will ask you." The woman said, "My lord the king, please speak."

**19** The king said, "Did Joab tell you to do all this?" The woman said, "As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can avoid the question of my lord the king. Yes, your servant Joab told me to do this. He put all these words in my mouth.

**20** Your servant Joab did this to change the situation. But my lord is wise, like an angel of God. He knows all things on the earth."

**21** Then the king said to Joab, "Good. I will do this. Go and bring back the young man Absalom."

**22** Joab bowed down to the ground to show respect. He thanked the king and blessed him. Joab said, "Today I, your servant, know that you are happy with me, my lord the king. The king did what I asked."

**23** Then Joab got up and went to Geshur. He brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.

**24** But the king said, "Absalom must go to his own house. He must not see my face." So Absalom went to his own house. He did not see the face of the king.

**25** In all Israel no man received as much praise for his beauty as Absalom. He had no problem with his body from his feet to the top of his head.

**26** At the end of each year, Absalom cut the hair of his head. He cut it because it became too heavy for him. He weighed the hair, and it weighed 200 shekels by the royal standard. That is about 2.3 kilograms.

**27** Absalom had 3 sons and 1 daughter. The name of his daughter was Tamar. She was a beautiful woman.

**28** Absalom lived in Jerusalem for 2 full years, but he did not see the face of the king.

**29** Then Absalom sent a message to Joab. He wanted to send Joab to the king. But Joab did not come to him. Absalom sent a message a second time, but Joab did not come.

**30** So Absalom said to his servants, "The field of Joab is near my field. He has barley in it. Go and set it on fire." So the servants of Absalom set the field on fire.

**31** Then Joab went to the house of Absalom. Joab said to him, "Why did your servants set my field on fire?"

**32** Absalom said to Joab, "I sent a message to you. I said, 'Come here. I want to send you to the king with a question. Why did I come back from Geshur? It was better for me to stay there.' Now let me see the face of the king. If I am guilty of a wrong, let him kill me."

**33** So Joab went to the king and told him this. The king called Absalom. Absalom came to the king. He bowed down to the ground in front of the king. Then the king kissed Absalom.

## Chapter 15

**1** After this, Absalom got a chariot and horses for himself. He also got 50 men to run in front of him.

**2** Absalom got up early each day. He stood beside the road to the city gate. Sometimes a man had a problem and came to the king for a decision. Then Absalom called to him and asked, "Which city do you come from?" The man said, "I, your servant, come from one of the tribes of Israel."

**3** Then Absalom said to him, "Your claims are good and right. But the king has no man to listen to you."

**4** Absalom also said, "I want someone to make me judge in the land! Then each man with a problem can come to me. I will give him justice."

**5** Sometimes a man came near to bow down to Absalom. Then Absalom put out his hand, took hold of the man, and kissed him.

**6** Absalom did this to all the people of Israel who came to the king for a decision. Thus Absalom won the loyalty of the men of Israel.

**7** After 40 years, Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go to Hebron. I want to do what I promised the LORD.

**8** When I, your servant, lived at Geshur in Syria, I made a promise. I said, 'If the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.'"

**9** The king said to him, "Go in peace." So Absalom went to Hebron.

**10** But Absalom sent secret messengers to all the tribes of Israel. They said, "When you hear the sound of the trumpet, then say, 'Absalom is king in Hebron!'"

**11** 200 men from Jerusalem went with Absalom. He invited them to go. They went with honest hearts. They did not know about the plan.

**12** While Absalom gave sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel from Giloh. Ahithophel was an adviser of David. He came from his city, Giloh. The plot against David became strong. The number of people who followed Absalom increased.

**13** A messenger came to David and said, "The men of Israel now follow Absalom."

**14** David said to all his officers with him in Jerusalem, "Get up! We must run away. If we do not, we will not escape from Absalom. Leave quickly! If he catches us, he will destroy us. He will kill the people of the city with the sword."

**15** The officers of the king said to him, "We, your servants, are ready to do all that our lord the king decides."

**16** The king left, and all his family followed him. But the king left 10 concubines to take care of the palace.

**17** The king left with all the people behind him. They stopped at the last house of the city.

**18** All his officers walked past him. All the Kerethites and all the Pelethites walked past the king. The 600 men from Gath who followed him also walked past the king.

**19** Then the king said to Ittai from Gath, "Why do you also go with us? Go back and stay with the new king. You are a foreigner, and you are far from your home.

**20** You came only yesterday. I must not make you travel with us today. I do not know where I go. Go back, and take your brothers with you. May the LORD show you kindness and truth."

**21** But Ittai spoke to the king. He said, "The LORD lives, and my lord the king lives. As surely as this is true, I will be where my lord the king is. If you die, I will die. If you live, I will live."

**22** David said to Ittai, "Then go across." So Ittai from Gath went across with all his men and all the children who were with him.

**23** All the people in the country cried loudly as the people went across. The king also went across the Kidron Valley. All the people went toward the desert.

**24** Zadok was there too. All the Levites were with him. They carried the ark of the covenant (the agreement) of God. They put down the ark of God. Abiathar gave offerings until all the people left the city.

**25** Then the king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back into the city. If the LORD is happy with me, he will bring me back. He will let me see the ark and the place where it stays again.

**26** But if he says, 'I am not happy with you,' then I am ready. Let him do to me what he thinks is good."

**27** The king also said to Zadok the priest, "You are a seer. Go back to the city in peace. Take your son Ahimaaz and Jonathan, the son of Abiathar, with you.

**28** I will wait at the places where people go across the river near the desert. I will wait until I get a message from you."

**29** So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem. They stayed there.

**30** David went up the Mount of Olives. He cried as he went. He covered his head, and he did not wear shoes. All the people with him covered their heads too. They cried as they went up.

**31** Someone told David, "Ahithophel is with Absalom in the plot." So David prayed, "LORD, please make the advice of Ahithophel foolish."

**32** David came to the top of the mountain, where people worshipped God. There Hushai the Arkite came to meet him. Hushai had tears in his coat, and he had dirt on his head.

**33** David said to him, "If you go with me, you will be a problem for me.

**34** But go back to the city. Say to Absalom, 'King, I will be your servant. In the past I was the servant of your father. Now I will be your servant.' Then you can help me. You can cause the advice of Ahithophel to fail.

**35** The priests Zadok and Abiathar will be there with you. Tell them all that you hear in the palace.

**36** Their 2 sons are there with them, Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar. Send them to me with all the news that you hear."

**37** So Hushai, the friend of David, came into the city. At the same time Absalom came into Jerusalem.

## Chapter 16

**1** David went a short distance past the top of the hill. There Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, met him. Ziba had 2 donkeys with saddles. On the donkeys were 200 loaves of bread, 100 bunches of raisins, 100 summer fruits, and a container of wine.

**2** The king said to Ziba, "Why did you bring these?" Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the family of the king to ride. The bread and the summer fruit are for the young men to eat. The wine is for the people who become weak in the desert."

**3** The king asked, "Where is Mephibosheth, the grandson of your master?" Ziba said to the king, "He stays in Jerusalem. He says, 'Today the people of Israel will give me back the kingdom of my grandfather.'"

**4** Then the king said to Ziba, "All that was Mephibosheth's is now yours." Ziba said, "I bow down to you. Please always be kind to me, my lord the king."

**5** King David came to Bahurim. A man from the family of Saul came out from there. His name was Shimei, the son of Gera. As he came out, he cursed David again and again.

**6** He threw stones at David and at all the officers of King David. All the people and all the strong soldiers were on the right and on the left of David.

**7** Shimei cursed and said, "Go away! Go away, you murderer! You worthless man!

**8** The LORD punishes you for all the blood of the family of Saul. You took his place as king. Now the LORD gave the kingdom to your son Absalom. Now you have trouble because you are a murderer!"

**9** Then Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, said to the king, "This man is like a dead dog. Why do you let him curse my lord the king? Please let me go across and cut off his head."

**10** But the king said, "Sons of Zeruiah, this is not your problem. If he curses because the LORD told him, 'Curse David,' then no one can ask him, 'Why do you do this?'"

**11** David also said to Abishai and to all his officers, "My own son tries to kill me. Thus this man from Benjamin has more cause to do it! Leave him alone. Let him curse, because the LORD told him to do it.

**12** Possibly the LORD will see my trouble. Possibly the LORD will give me good things instead of the curses that I hear today."

**13** So David and his men continued on the road. Shimei walked along the side of the hill near him. He cursed as he went. He threw stones and dirt at David.

**14** The king and all the people with him were weary when they arrived. There they rested.

**15** Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem. Ahithophel was with him.

**16** Hushai the Arkite, the friend of David, came to Absalom. Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"

**17** Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this how you show loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"

**18** Hushai said to Absalom, "No! I will serve the man that the LORD, these people, and all the men of Israel choose. I will stay with him.

**19** Also, whom must I serve? Must I not serve his son? I served your father. In the same way I will serve you."

**20** Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give us your advice. What must we do?"

**21** Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Have sex with the concubines of your father. He left them to take care of the palace. Then all Israel will hear that your father hates you. Then all the people who are with you will be stronger."

**22** So they put up a tent for Absalom on the roof of the palace. Absalom had sex with the concubines of his father in front of all Israel.

**23** At that time, people thought that the advice of Ahithophel was like a word from God. David and Absalom both thought this about all the advice of Ahithophel.

## Chapter 17

**1** Ahithophel also said to Absalom, "Let me choose 12,000 men. Tonight I will go and follow David.

**2** I will attack him while he is weary and weak. I will make him afraid. Then all the people who are with him will run away. I will kill only the king.

**3** Then I will bring all the people back to you. When the man that you want is dead, all the people will come back. All the people will be in peace."

**4** This plan pleased Absalom and all the leaders (elders) of Israel.

**5** But Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Arkite too. Let us also hear what he says."

**6** Hushai came to Absalom. Absalom said to him, "Ahithophel gave us this advice. Must we do what he says? If not, tell us your advice."

**7** Hushai said to Absalom, "This time the advice of Ahithophel is not good."

**8** Hushai also said, "You know your father and his men. They are strong soldiers. They are very angry, like a wild bear when someone takes her young bears. Also, your father is an experienced soldier. He will not sleep the night with the people.

**9** Now he hides in a hole or in some other place. Possibly some of your men will die at the start of the battle. Then the people who hear about it will say, 'Many people who follow Absalom are dead.'

**10** Then even the bravest soldier with a heart like a lion will become very afraid. All Israel knows that your father is a strong soldier. They know that his men are brave.

**11** Thus I give you this advice. Bring together all the men of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba. They will be as many as the grains of sand on the seashore. You must lead them into battle yourself.

**12** Then we will attack David in the place where we find him. We will cover him as the dew covers the ground. Not one of his men will stay alive. David will not stay alive.

**13** If David goes into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city. We will pull the city down into the valley. Not even 1 small stone will stay there."

**14** Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The advice of Hushai the Arkite is better than the advice of Ahithophel." The LORD decided to stop the good advice of Ahithophel. The LORD wanted to bring disaster on Absalom.

**15** Then Hushai told the priests Zadok and Abiathar, "Ahithophel gave this advice to Absalom and the leaders of Israel. But I gave different advice.

**16** Now quickly send a message to David. Tell him, 'Do not stay tonight at the places near the desert where people go across the river. Go across the river quickly. If you do not, the enemy will destroy the king and all the people with him.'"

**17** Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed at En Rogel. They could not let people see them go into the city. A female servant went and told them the message. Then they went to tell King David.

**18** But a boy saw them and told Absalom. So the 2 men left quickly. They went to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his yard. Jonathan and Ahimaaz went down into the well.

**19** The wife of the man put a cover over the mouth of the well. She put grain on the cover. No one knew about the men.

**20** The officers of Absalom came to the woman at the house. They asked, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman said to them, "They went across the stream." The officers looked for them but did not find them. So the officers went back to Jerusalem.

**21** After the officers left, the 2 men came up out of the well. They went and told King David. They said to him, "Go quickly across the river. Ahithophel made a plan against you."

**22** So David and all the people with him got up. They went across the Jordan River. By sunrise, all the people were on the other side of the Jordan.

**23** Ahithophel saw that the people did not obey his advice. So he put a saddle on his donkey and went home to his city. He gave orders to his family about his property. Then he hanged himself and died. The people buried him in the tomb of his father.

**24** David came to Mahanaim. Absalom and all the men of Israel went across the Jordan River.

**25** Absalom made Amasa commander of the army instead of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man with the name Ithra, an Israelite. Ithra married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash. Abigail was the sister of Zeruiah, the mother of Joab.

**26** The army of Israel and Absalom made their camp in the land of Gilead.

**27** David came to Mahanaim. There 3 men met him. The first was Shobi, the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites. The second was Makir, the son of Ammiel from Lo Debar. The third was Barzillai from Rogelim in Gilead.

**28** They brought beds, bowls, and clay pots. They also brought wheat, barley, flour, cooked grain, beans, and lentils.

**29** They brought honey, butter, sheep, and cheese from cows. They gave this food to David and the people with him. They said, "The people are hungry, tired, and thirsty in the desert."

## Chapter 18

**1** David counted the men who were with him. He put commanders over groups of 1,000 men and over groups of 100 men.

**2** David sent out the army in 3 groups. Joab led 1 group. Abishai, the son of Zeruiah and the brother of Joab, led 1 group. Ittai from Gath led 1 group. The king said to the army, "I will surely go out with you too."

**3** But the men said, "You must not go out. If we run away, the enemy will not care about us. If half of us die, they will not care. But you are as valuable as 10,000 of us. Thus it is better for you to stay in the city and send us help."

**4** The king said to them, "I will do what you think is best." So the king stood beside the gate. All the army went out in groups of 100 and 1,000.

**5** The king gave an order to Joab, Abishai, and Ittai. He said, "For me, be gentle with the young man Absalom." All the army heard the order of the king to all the commanders about Absalom.

**6** The army of David went out into the field to fight against Israel. The battle was in the forest of Ephraim.

**7** There the men of David defeated the army of Israel. Many men died that day. 20,000 men died.

**8** The battle spread over all the country. The forest killed more men that day than the sword killed.

**9** Absalom met some of the men of David. Absalom rode on a mule. The mule went under the thick branches of a large oak tree. The head of Absalom caught in the tree. He hung in the air, and the mule continued without him.

**10** A man saw this. He told Joab, "I saw Absalom. He hangs in an oak tree."

**11** Joab said to the man, "You saw him! Why did you not kill him there? I was ready to give you 10 pieces of silver and a belt."

**12** The man said to Joab, "If I had 1,000 pieces of silver in my hand, I still will not attack the son of the king. We heard the king give an order to you, Abishai, and Ittai. He said, 'Be careful. No one must hurt the young man Absalom.'

**13** If I killed him, the king will know. No one can hide anything from the king. And you will not help me."

**14** Joab said, "I will not wait here with you." He took 3 spears in his hand. He pushed them into the chest of Absalom. Absalom was still alive in the oak tree.

**15** 10 young men who carried the weapons of Joab came around Absalom. They attacked him and killed him.

**16** Then Joab blew the trumpet. The army stopped the attack on Israel, because Joab stopped them.

**17** They took the body of Absalom and threw it into a large hole in the forest. They put a very large pile of stones on it. All the men of Israel ran away to their homes.

**18** When Absalom was alive, he made a stone pillar for himself in the King's Valley. He said, "I have no son to keep my name alive." He gave his own name to the pillar. Today people still call it the Monument of Absalom.

**19** Then Ahimaaz, the son of Zadok, said, "Let me run and take the news to the king. I will tell him that the LORD saved him from his enemies."

**20** Joab said to him, "You will not take the news today. You can take news on another day. But today you must not take the news, because the son of the king is dead."

**21** Then Joab said to a man from Cush, "Go and tell the king what you saw." The man from Cush bowed down to Joab and ran.

**22** Ahimaaz, the son of Zadok, spoke to Joab again. He said, "I do not care what occurs. Please let me also run after the man from Cush." Joab said, "My son, why do you want to run? You will get no reward for this news."

**23** Ahimaaz said, "I do not care. I want to run." So Joab said to him, "Run." Then Ahimaaz ran on the road through the Jordan Valley. He ran past the man from Cush.

**24** David sat between the 2 gates of the city. The guard went up to the roof over the gate, on the wall. He looked and saw a man who ran alone.

**25** The guard shouted and told the king. The king said, "If he is alone, he brings news." The man came nearer and nearer.

**26** Then the guard saw another man who ran. The guard called to the gatekeeper, "Look! Another man runs alone." The king said, "He also brings news."

**27** The guard said, "I think that the first man runs like Ahimaaz, the son of Zadok." The king said, "He is a good man. He brings good news."

**28** Ahimaaz called to the king, "All is well!" He bowed down to the ground in front of the king. He said, "Praise the LORD your God! He gave you victory over the men who fought against my lord the king."

**29** The king asked, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" Ahimaaz said, "When Joab sent me, your servant, I saw a large crowd with much noise. But I do not know what occurred."

**30** The king said, "Move to the side and stand here." So Ahimaaz moved to the side and stood there.

**31** Then the man from Cush arrived. He said, "My lord the king, I have good news! Today the LORD saved you from all the people who fought against you."

**32** The king asked the man from Cush, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" The man from Cush said, "May all the enemies of my lord the king become like that young man. May all who attack you become like him."

**33** The king was very sad. He went up to the room over the gate and cried. As he went, he said, "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish that I died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!"

## Chapter 19

**1** People told Joab, "The king cries and mourns for Absalom."

**2** That day the victory became a time of grief for all the army. The army heard that day that the king was very sad for his son.

**3** That day the soldiers went into the city quietly. They acted like soldiers who feel shame because they ran away from a battle.

**4** The king covered his face. He cried loudly, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"

**5** Then Joab went into the house to the king. He said, "Today you make all your officers ashamed. Today they saved your life. They saved the lives of your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your concubines.

**6** You love the people who hate you, and you hate the people who love you. Today you showed that your commanders and officers are not important to you. I see now that you want Absalom alive and all of us dead. That will make you happy.

**7** Now get up! Go out and say kind words to your officers. I make a promise by the LORD: if you do not go out, not one man will stay with you tonight. That will be worse for you than all the trouble that you had from your youth until now."

**8** So the king got up and sat in the gate. People told all the army, "The king sits in the gate." Then all the army came to the king. But the men of Israel ran away to their homes.

**9** All the people in all the tribes of Israel argued with each other. They said, "The king saved us from our enemies. He saved us from the Philistines. But now he ran away from the country because of Absalom.

**10** We anointed Absalom to rule over us, but he died in the battle. Thus why do you say nothing about the return of the king?"

**11** King David sent a message to the priests Zadok and Abiathar. He said, "Speak to the leaders (elders) of Judah. Ask them, 'Why are you the last to bring the king back to his palace? All Israel speaks about the return of the king.'

**12** You are my relatives, my own family. Why are you the last to bring back the king?'

**13** And say to Amasa, 'You are my own relative. You will be the commander of my army instead of Joab from now on. If I do not do this, I ask God to punish me very severely.'"

**14** Thus David made all the men of Judah agree, as if they were 1 man. They sent a message to the king. The message was, "Come back, you and all your officers."

**15** So the king came back to the Jordan River. The men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king. They came to help the king go across the Jordan.

**16** Shimei, the son of Gera, from the tribe of Benjamin, was from Bahurim. He came down quickly with the men of Judah to meet King David.

**17** 1,000 men from Benjamin were with him. Ziba, the servant of the family of Saul, was also with him. Ziba had his 15 sons and his 20 servants with him. They went quickly into the Jordan River in front of the king.

**18** They went across the river to bring the family of the king across. They wanted to do what the king wanted. When the king came across the Jordan, Shimei, the son of Gera, bowed down in front of him.

**19** Shimei said to the king, "My lord, please do not think that I am guilty. Do not remember the wrong thing that I, your servant, did on the day that my lord the king left Jerusalem. Please forget it.

**20** I, your servant, know that I sinned. Thus I came today. I am the first of all the family of Joseph to come down and meet my lord the king."

**21** But Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, said, "Shimei must die for this! He cursed the king that the LORD chose (anointed)."

**22** David said, "Sons of Zeruiah, this is not your problem! Today you act like my enemies. No man in Israel will die today. Today I know that I am king over Israel."

**23** Then the king said to Shimei, "You will not die." The king made a promise to him.

**24** Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came down to meet the king. He did not take care of his feet, cut his beard, or wash his clothes from the day the king left. He waited until the day the king came back safely.

**25** Mephibosheth came from Jerusalem to meet the king. The king said to him, "Mephibosheth, why did you not go with me?"

**26** He said, "My lord the king, my servant tricked me. I said, 'I will put a saddle on my donkey. Then I can ride with the king.' I needed the donkey because I, your servant, am lame.

**27** But Ziba told lies about me to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God. So do what you think is good.

**28** All the family of my grandfather deserved death from my lord the king. But you let me, your servant, eat at your own table. Thus I have no right to ask the king for more."

**29** The king said to him, "You do not need to say more. I decide this: you and Ziba will divide the land."

**30** Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let Ziba take all of it. It is enough for me that my lord the king came home safely."

**31** Barzillai from Gilead came down from Rogelim. He went with the king to the Jordan River to help him go across.

**32** Barzillai was a very old man. He was 80 years old. He gave food to the king while the king stayed at Mahanaim, because he was a very rich man.

**33** The king said to Barzillai, "Come with me to Jerusalem. I will take care of you there."

**34** But Barzillai said to the king, "I will not live much longer. Why must I go up with the king to Jerusalem?

**35** I am 80 years old now. I cannot know the difference between good and bad. I, your servant, cannot taste what I eat or drink. I cannot hear the voices of men and women who sing. Why must I, your servant, be more trouble for my lord the king?

**36** I, your servant, will go only a short distance across the Jordan with the king. Why must the king give me a reward like this?

**37** Please let me, your servant, go back home. Let me die in my own city near the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Kimham. Let him go across with my lord the king. Do for him what you think is good."

**38** The king said, "Kimham will go across with me. I will do for him what you think is good. I will do for you all that you ask."

**39** All the people went across the Jordan River. Then the king went across. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him. Then Barzillai went back to his home.

**40** The king went to Gilgal, and Kimham went with him. All the army of Judah and half of the army of Israel went with the king.

**41** Then all the men of Israel came to the king. They said to him, "Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you secretly? Why did they bring the king, his family, and all his men across the Jordan?"

**42** All the men of Judah said to the men of Israel, "We did it because the king is our close relative. Why are you angry about this? We did not eat food at the cost of the king. He did not give us gifts."

**43** The men of Israel said to the men of Judah, "We have 10 parts in the king. Thus we have more right to David than you. Why did you have no respect for us? We were the first to speak about the return of our king!" But the words of the men of Judah were stronger than the words of the men of Israel.

## Chapter 20

**1** A worthless man was there. His name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, from the tribe of Benjamin. He blew a trumpet and said, "We have no part in David! We have no share in the son of Jesse! Men of Israel, all of you go home!"

**2** So all the men of Israel left David and followed Sheba, the son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed with their king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

**3** David came to his palace in Jerusalem. He took the 10 concubines that he left to take care of the palace. He put them in a house with a guard. He gave them food, but he did not have sex with them. They stayed in that house until they died. They lived as widows.

**4** Then the king said to Amasa, "Bring the men of Judah to me in 3 days. You must also be here."

**5** So Amasa went to bring together the men of Judah. But he stayed longer than the time that the king gave him.

**6** David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba, the son of Bichri, will do more harm to us than Absalom. Take my officers and follow him. If you do not, he will possibly find cities with walls and escape from us."

**7** So the men of Joab, the Kerethites, the Pelethites, and all the strong soldiers went out with Abishai. They left Jerusalem to follow Sheba, the son of Bichri.

**8** They came to the large rock in Gibeon. There Amasa came to meet them. Joab wore his military clothes. Over his clothes he wore a belt with a sword in its sheath. As Joab went forward, the sword fell out.

**9** Joab said to Amasa, "Are you well, my brother?" Joab took hold of the beard of Amasa with his right hand to kiss him.

**10** Amasa did not see the sword in the left hand of Joab. Joab pushed the sword into the stomach of Amasa. His insides fell out on the ground. Joab did not need to hit him again, and Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai followed Sheba, the son of Bichri.

**11** One of the young men of Joab stood near the body of Amasa. He said, "All men who support Joab and David, follow Joab!"

**12** Amasa lay in his blood in the middle of the road. The man saw that all the army stopped there. So he moved Amasa from the road into the field. He saw that all the people stopped when they came to the body. So he put a cloth over it.

**13** After he moved the body from the road, all the men continued with Joab. They followed Sheba, the son of Bichri.

**14** Sheba went through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth Maacah. All the Berites came together and followed him.

**15** The army of Joab came and attacked Sheba in Abel of Beth Maacah. They made a hill of dirt against the wall of the city. All the soldiers with Joab hit the wall to make it fall.

**16** Then a wise woman shouted from the city, "Listen! Listen! Please tell Joab to come here. I want to speak with him."

**17** Joab came near to her. The woman said, "Are you Joab?" He said, "I am." She said to him, "Listen to the words of your servant." He said, "I listen."

**18** She said, "In the past, people said, 'Ask for advice at Abel.' Thus they solved their problems.

**19** We are peaceful and loyal people in Israel. But you try to destroy an important city in Israel. Why do you want to destroy what belongs to the LORD?"

**20** Joab said, "No! I do not want to destroy or ruin your city!

**21** That is not true. A man from the hill country of Ephraim fought against King David. His name is Sheba, the son of Bichri. Give me only this man, and I will leave the city." The woman said to Joab, "We will throw his head to you over the wall."

**22** Then the woman went to all the people of the city with her wise advice. They cut off the head of Sheba, the son of Bichri. They threw it out to Joab. Joab blew a trumpet, and his men left the city and went home. Joab went back to the king in Jerusalem.

**23** Joab was the commander of all the army of Israel. Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, was the commander of the Kerethites and the Pelethites.

**24** Adoram was in charge of the forced workers. Jehoshaphat, the son of Ahilud, wrote the records of the kingdom.

**25** Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.

**26** Ira from Jair was a chief official of David.

## Chapter 21

**1** During the rule of David, there was a famine for 3 years, one year after another. David asked the LORD about it. The LORD said, "The famine is because of Saul and his family of murderers. Saul killed the Gibeonites."

**2** The Gibeonites were not Israelites. They were the last of the Amorites. The Israelites made a promise to protect them. But Saul tried to kill them because he was too eager to help Israel and Judah. So King David called the Gibeonites and spoke to them.

**3** David said to the Gibeonites, "What can I do for you? How can I make payment (atonement) for the wrong? I want you to bless the people of the LORD."

**4** The Gibeonites said to him, "We do not want silver or gold from Saul or his family. And we do not want to kill a man in Israel." David said, "I will do for you what you ask."

**5** They said to the king, "Saul tried to destroy us. He made plans to kill all of us, so that we cannot live in any part of Israel.

**6** Give us 7 of his male descendants. We will hang them in front of the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the king that the LORD chose." The king said, "I will give them to you."

**7** But the king protected Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul. David did this because of the promise in the name of the LORD between David and Jonathan, the son of Saul.

**8** The king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the 2 sons of Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. Rizpah had them by Saul. The king also took the 5 sons of Michal, the daughter of Saul. Michal brought them up for Adriel, the son of Barzillai from Meholah.

**9** David gave them to the Gibeonites. The Gibeonites hanged them on the hill in front of the LORD. All 7 of them died together. They died at the start of the barley harvest.

**10** Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah, took a rough cloth (sackcloth) and put it on the rock for herself. She stayed there from the start of the harvest until the rain fell on the bodies. She did not let the birds land on them during the day. She did not let the wild animals come near at night.

**11** People told David what Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah and the concubine of Saul, did.

**12** Then David went to the men of Jabesh Gilead. He took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from them. The men of Jabesh Gilead took the bones secretly from the public square of Beth Shan. The Philistines hung the bodies there after they killed Saul on Gilboa.

**13** David brought the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from there. The people also collected the bones of the 7 men that the Gibeonites hanged.

**14** They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the tomb of Kish, the father of Saul. The tomb is in Zela, in the land of Benjamin. They did all that the king told them. After that, God answered their prayers for the land.

**15** There was war again between the Philistines and Israel. David and his officers went down and fought against the Philistines. David became very tired.

**16** Ishbi-Benob was one of the descendants of the giants. His bronze spear weighed 300 shekels, about 3.5 kilograms. He also had a new sword. He thought that he could kill David.

**17** But Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, helped David. He attacked the Philistine and killed him. Then the men of David made a promise. They said to him, "You will not go out to battle with us again. If you die, the light of Israel will go out."

**18** After this, there was another battle with the Philistines at Gob. There Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph. Saph was one of the descendants of the giants.

**19** There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob. There Elhanan, the son of Jaare-Oregim from Bethlehem, killed the brother of Goliath from Gath. The shaft of the spear of Goliath was as thick as the beam of a weaver.

**20** There was another battle at Gath. A very tall man was there. He had 6 fingers on each hand and 6 toes on each foot. He had 24 fingers and toes in total. He was also a descendant of the giants.
