**16** All the people of Israel saw that the king did not listen to them. So they answered the king, "We have no share in David! We have no part in the son of Jesse! People of Israel, go home! David, take care of your own family!" So the people of Israel went to their homes.

**17** But Rehoboam still ruled over the people of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah.

**18** Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram, the chief of the forced workers. But all the people of Israel threw stones at Adoram until he died. King Rehoboam quickly got into his chariot and ran away to Jerusalem.

**19** So Israel rebelled against the family of David. They are still separate today.

**20** All the people of Israel heard that Jeroboam came back. They sent for him and called him to their assembly. They made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah stayed with the family of David.

**21** Rehoboam came to Jerusalem. He collected all the men of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin. There were 180,000 chosen soldiers. They prepared to fight against Israel and get the kingdom back for Rehoboam the son of Solomon.

**22** But the word of God came to Shemaiah, the man of God. God said,

**23** "Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah. Speak to all the people of Judah and Benjamin, and to all the other people. Tell them,

**24** 'The LORD says this: Do not go up and fight against your brothers, the people of Israel. Each man must go home. I caused this to occur.'" So the people obeyed the word of the LORD. They went home, as the LORD told them.

**25** Then Jeroboam built the city of Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. Then he went out from there and built Penuel.

**26** Jeroboam thought, "Now the kingdom can go back to the family of David.

**27** These people will go to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to give sacrifices. Then they will again give their hearts to their master, Rehoboam, the king of Judah. They will kill me and go back to King Rehoboam."

**28** So the king asked for advice. Then he made 2 calves of gold. He said to the people, "It is too difficult for you to go up to Jerusalem. People of Israel, here are your gods. These gods brought you out of Egypt."

**29** He put 1 calf in Bethel and the other calf in Dan.

**30** This caused the people to sin. The people went as far as Dan to worship the calf there.

**31** Jeroboam also built shrines on the high places. He chose priests from all kinds of people. These priests were not from the tribe of Levi.

**32** Jeroboam started a feast on the 15th day of the 8th month. It was like the feast in Judah. He gave sacrifices on the altar. He did this in Bethel and made sacrifices to the calves that he made. He put the priests of the high places that he made in Bethel.

**33** On the 15th day of the 8th month, he gave sacrifices on the altar that he made in Bethel. He chose this month himself. He started a feast for the people of Israel. He went up to the altar to burn incense.

## Chapter 13

**1** A man of God came from Judah to Bethel because of a command from the LORD. Jeroboam stood next to the altar to burn incense.

**2** The man of God spoke loudly against the altar, as the LORD told him. He said, "Altar, altar! The LORD says this: 'A woman in the family of David will give birth to a son with the name Josiah. On you, Josiah will kill the priests of the high places who now burn incense on you. Josiah will burn human bones on you.'"

**3** That same day the man of God gave a sign. He said, "This is the sign that the LORD gives: The altar will break apart. The ashes on it will fall out."

**4** King Jeroboam heard what the man of God said against the altar in Bethel. He pointed his hand at the man from the altar and said, "Catch him!" But the hand of the king became paralyzed. He could not move his hand back.

**5** The altar also broke apart, and the ashes fell out of the altar. This was the sign that the man of God gave as the LORD told him.

**6** Then the king said to the man of God, "Please pray to the LORD your God for me. Ask him to heal my hand." So the man of God prayed to the LORD, and the LORD healed the hand of the king. His hand became as it was before.

**7** The king said to the man of God, "Come home with me and eat. I will give you a gift."

**8** But the man of God answered the king. He said, "Even if you give me half of all that you have, I will not go with you. I will not eat food or drink water in this place.

**9** The LORD gave me a command. He said, 'Do not eat food or drink water. Do not go back on the same road that you came on.'"

**10** So he went home on a different road. He did not go back on the road that he came on to Bethel.

**11** An old prophet lived in Bethel. His sons came and told him all that the man of God did that day in Bethel. They also told their father the words that the man of God said to the king.

**12** Their father asked them, "Which road did he go on?" His sons saw which road the man of God from Judah went on.

**13** So he said to his sons, "Put a saddle on the donkey for me." They put a saddle on the donkey for him, and he rode on it.

**14** He went after the man of God and found him. The man of God sat under an oak tree. The old prophet asked him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" He said, "Yes, I am."

**15** Then the old prophet said to him, "Come home with me and eat some food."

**16** The man of God said, "I cannot go back with you or go into your home. I will not eat food or drink water with you in this place.

**17** The LORD gave me a command. He said, 'Do not eat food or drink water there. Do not go back on the road that you came on.'"

**18** The old prophet said to him, "I am also a prophet, as you are. An angel spoke to me with a command from the LORD. The angel said, 'Bring the man of God back to your house to eat food and drink water.'" But the old prophet lied to him.

**19** So the man of God went back with him. He ate food and drank water at his house.

**20** While they sat at the table, the word of the LORD came to the old prophet who brought him back.

**21** The old prophet shouted to the man of God who came from Judah, "The LORD says this: 'You disobeyed the word of the LORD. You did not obey the command that the LORD your God gave you.

**22** You came back and ate food and drank water in the place where the LORD told you not to eat or drink. Thus no one will put your body in the tomb of your ancestors.'"

**23** The man of God finished his food and drink. Then the old prophet put a saddle on the donkey for the prophet that he brought back.

**24** The man of God went away. On the road a lion attacked him and killed him. His body lay on the road. The donkey and the lion stood next to the body.

**25** Some men went past and saw the body on the road and the lion next to the body. They went to the city where the old prophet lived and told the people there.

**26** The old prophet who brought the man back heard about this. He said, "That is the man of God who disobeyed the word of the LORD. Thus the LORD gave him to the lion. The lion attacked him and killed him, as the LORD told him."

**27** Then the old prophet said to his sons, "Put a saddle on the donkey for me." So they did.

**28** He went and found the body on the road. The donkey and the lion stood next to the body. The lion did not eat the body. The lion did not attack the donkey.

**29** The old prophet lifted up the body of the man of God. He put it on the donkey and brought it back to his own city. He wanted to mourn for him and bury him.

**30** He put the body in his own tomb. The people mourned for the man of God. They said, "Oh, my brother!"

**31** After the old prophet buried him, he spoke to his sons. He said, "When I die, bury me in the tomb where I buried the man of God. Put my bones next to his bones.

**32** The LORD told him to speak against the altar in Bethel and against all the shrines on the high places in the cities of Samaria. What he said will surely come true."

**33** After this, Jeroboam still did not stop his evil actions. He again chose priests for the high places from all kinds of people. He made any man who wanted it a priest of the high places.

**34** This sin of the family of Jeroboam caused the destruction of his family. It caused his family to be completely removed from the earth.

## Chapter 14

**1** At that time Abijah, the son of Jeroboam, became sick.

**2** Jeroboam said to his wife, "Get up and change your appearance. Then no one will know that you are the wife of Jeroboam. Go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there. He told me that I will be king over these people.

**3** Take 10 loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey with you. Go to Ahijah. He will tell you what will occur to the boy."

**4** The wife of Jeroboam did this. She went to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah. Ahijah could not see, because he was very old and blind.

**5** But the LORD said to Ahijah, "The wife of Jeroboam comes to ask you about her son, because he is sick. She will act as if she is a different woman. When she comes, tell her what I tell you."

**6** Ahijah heard the sound of her feet at the door. He said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why do you act as if you are a different woman? I must give you bad news.

**7** Go and tell Jeroboam this: 'The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: I chose you from among the people. I made you the leader of my people Israel.

**8** I took the kingdom away from the family of David and gave it to you. But you are not like my servant David. He obeyed my commands and followed me with all his heart. He did only what was right in my sight.

**9** You did more evil than all the kings before you. You made other gods and metal idols for yourself. You made me angry. You turned your back on me.

**10** Thus I will bring disaster on the family of Jeroboam. I will kill every male in the family of Jeroboam in Israel, slave or free. I will remove the family of Jeroboam completely, as a man burns waste until all of it is gone.

**11** Dogs will eat the people of the family of Jeroboam who die in the city. Birds will eat the people who die in the fields. The LORD said this.'

**12** Now get up and go to your home. When you go into the city, the boy will die.

**13** All the people of Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He is the only person in the family of Jeroboam who will go into a grave. He is the only person in the family of Jeroboam in whom the LORD, the God of Israel, found something good.

**14** The LORD will choose another king over Israel. That king will destroy the family of Jeroboam. This will start now.

**15** The LORD will hit Israel, and Israel will shake like a reed in the water. The LORD will pull Israel out of this good land that he gave to their ancestors. He will send them to the other side of the Euphrates River. He will do this because they made Asherah poles and made the LORD angry.

**16** The LORD will leave Israel because of the sins of Jeroboam. Jeroboam sinned and caused Israel to sin."

**17** Then the wife of Jeroboam got up and went to Tirzah. When she came to the entrance of her house, the boy died.

**18** The people of Israel buried him and mourned for him. This was what the LORD said through his servant Ahijah the prophet.

**19** The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel tells the other events of the life of Jeroboam. It tells about his wars and how he ruled.

**20** Jeroboam ruled for 22 years. Then he died, and his son Nadab became king in his place.

**21** Rehoboam the son of Solomon ruled in Judah. He was 41 years old when he became king. He ruled for 17 years in Jerusalem. The LORD chose Jerusalem from all the tribes of Israel as the city for his name. The name of the mother of Rehoboam was Naamah. She was an Ammonite.

**22** The people of Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD. Their sins made the LORD angry. They sinned more than their ancestors.

**23** They also built high places, stone pillars, and Asherah poles for themselves. They put them on each high hill and under each green tree.

**24** There were also male prostitutes at the shrines in the land. The people did all the terrible things of the nations that the LORD removed in front of the people of Israel.

**25** In the 5th year of King Rehoboam, Shishak, the king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem.

**26** He took the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the palace of the king. He took everything. He also took all the gold shields that Solomon made.

**27** King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place. He gave them to the commanders of the guards who protected the entrance of the palace.

**28** Each time that the king went into the house of the LORD, the guards carried the shields. Then they brought the shields back to the room of the guards.

**29** The Book of the History of the Kings of Judah tells the other events of the life of Rehoboam and all that he did.

**30** There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam during all their lives.

**31** Rehoboam died and they buried him with his ancestors in the City of David. The name of his mother was Naamah. She was an Ammonite. His son Abijam became king in his place.

## Chapter 15

**1** Abijam became king over Judah in the 18th year that Jeroboam the son of Nebat was king.

**2** Abijam ruled in Jerusalem for 3 years. The name of his mother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.

**3** Abijam did all the sins that his father did before him. His heart was not fully faithful to the LORD his God, as the heart of his ancestor David was.

**4** But the LORD his God gave Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem because of David. The LORD gave him a son to be king after him, and he kept Jerusalem strong.

**5** The LORD did this because David did what was right in the sight of the LORD. David obeyed all the commands of the LORD during all his life. He disobeyed only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

**6** There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam during all the life of Abijam.

**7** The Book of the History of the Kings of Judah tells the other events of the life of Abijam and all that he did. There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

**8** Abijam died and they buried him in the City of David. His son Asa became king in his place.

**9** Asa became king over Judah in the 20th year that Jeroboam was king of Israel.

**10** Asa ruled in Jerusalem for 41 years. The name of his grandmother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.

**11** Asa did what was right in the sight of the LORD, as his ancestor David did.

**12** He removed the male prostitutes of the shrines from the land. He removed all the idols that his ancestors made.

**13** He also removed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother. He did this because she made a terrible idol for Asherah. Asa cut down her idol and burned it at the Kidron Valley.

**14** But Asa did not remove the high places. But his heart was fully faithful to the LORD during all his life.

**15** He brought into the house of the LORD the silver, the gold, and the items that he and his father gave to the LORD.

**16** There was war between Asa and Baasha, the king of Israel, during all their lives.

**17** Baasha, the king of Israel, attacked Judah. He built the city of Ramah with strong walls. He did this to stop people who wanted to go to Asa, the king of Judah, or come from him.

**18** Then Asa took all the silver and gold that were still in the treasuries of the house of the LORD. He also took the silver and gold from the palace of the king. He gave them to his officials. King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad, king of Syria, who lived in Damascus. Ben-hadad was the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion. Asa told them to say,

**19** "There is a treaty between you and me, as there was between my father and your father. I send you a gift of silver and gold. Stop your treaty with Baasha, king of Israel. Then he will go away from me."

**20** Ben-hadad agreed with King Asa. He sent the commanders of his armies to attack the cities of Israel. They attacked Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, all Chinneroth, and all the land of Naphtali.

**21** Baasha heard about this. He stopped the work on Ramah and went to live in Tirzah.

**22** Then King Asa gave a command to all the people of Judah. Every person had to obey. They took away the stones and the wood that Baasha used to build Ramah. King Asa used these to build Geba in Benjamin and Mizpah.

**23** The Book of the History of the Kings of Judah tells the other events of the life of Asa. It tells about all his power, all that he did, and the cities that he built. But when he was old, he had a disease in his feet.

**24** Asa died and they buried him with his ancestors in the City of David, his ancestor. His son Jehoshaphat became king in his place.

**25** Nadab the son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the 2nd year that Asa was king of Judah. Nadab ruled over Israel for 2 years.

**26** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He lived as his father did. He did the same sin that his father caused Israel to do.

**27** Baasha the son of Ahijah, from the tribe of Issachar, made a secret plan against Nadab. Nadab and all the army of Israel attacked Gibbethon, a town of the Philistines. There Baasha killed Nadab.

**28** Baasha killed Nadab in the 3rd year that Asa was king of Judah. Then Baasha became king in his place.

**29** When Baasha became king, he killed all the family of Jeroboam. He did not let any person of the family of Jeroboam stay alive. He destroyed them all, as the LORD said through his servant Ahijah from Shiloh.

**30** This occurred because of the sins of Jeroboam. Jeroboam sinned and caused Israel to sin. He made the LORD, the God of Israel, very angry.

**31** The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel tells the other events of the life of Nadab and all that he did.

**32** There was war between Asa and Baasha, the king of Israel, during all their lives.

**33** Baasha the son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in the 3rd year that Asa was king of Judah. Baasha ruled in Tirzah for 24 years.

**34** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He lived as Jeroboam did. He did the same sin that Jeroboam caused Israel to do.

## Chapter 16

**1** Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha. The LORD said,

**2** "You were not important, and I made you important. I made you the leader of my people Israel. But you lived as Jeroboam did. You caused my people Israel to sin. Their sins made me angry.

**3** So I will destroy Baasha and his family. I will make your family like the family of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

**4** Dogs will eat the people of the family of Baasha who die in the city. Birds will eat the people of his family who die in the fields."

**5** The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel tells the other events of the life of Baasha. It tells about all that he did and about his power.

**6** Baasha died and they buried him in Tirzah. His son Elah became king in his place.

**7** The word of the LORD came through the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha and his family. This was because of all the evil that Baasha did in the sight of the LORD. His actions made the LORD angry. Baasha was like the family of Jeroboam. Also, Baasha killed the family of Jeroboam.

**8** Elah the son of Baasha became king over Israel in the 26th year that Asa was king of Judah. Elah ruled in Tirzah for 2 years.

**9** Zimri, an official of Elah, made a secret plan against him. Zimri was the commander of half of the chariots of Elah. Elah was in Tirzah at the house of Arza, the chief of the palace. Elah drank wine there and became drunk.

**10** Zimri went in and attacked Elah and killed him. This was in the 27th year that Asa was king of Judah. Then Zimri became king in the place of Elah.

**11** When Zimri started to rule and sat on the throne, he killed all the family of Baasha. He did not let any male stay alive, from the relatives or the friends of Baasha.

**12** So Zimri destroyed all the family of Baasha. This was what the LORD said against Baasha through Jehu the prophet.

**13** This occurred because of all the sins of Baasha and his son Elah. They sinned and caused Israel to sin. Their worthless idols made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry.

**14** The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel tells the other events of the life of Elah and all that he did.

**15** Zimri ruled in Tirzah for 7 days, in the 27th year that Asa was king of Judah. At that time the army of Israel had its camp near Gibbethon, a town of the Philistines.

**16** The soldiers in the camp heard that Zimri made a secret plan and killed the king. So that day, in the camp, all the soldiers of Israel made Omri king over Israel. Omri was the commander of the army.

**17** Then Omri and all the army of Israel went up from Gibbethon. They surrounded Tirzah and attacked it.

**18** Zimri saw that the army captured the city. So he went into the strong tower of the palace. He set fire to the palace with himself inside, and he died.

**19** He died because of his sins. He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He lived as Jeroboam did. He did the same sin that Jeroboam caused Israel to do.

**20** The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel tells the other events of the life of Zimri and his secret plan.

**21** Then the people of Israel separated into 2 groups. Half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath and wanted to make him king. The other half followed Omri.

**22** But the followers of Omri were stronger than the followers of Tibni the son of Ginath. So Tibni died, and Omri became king.

**23** Omri became king over Israel in the 31st year that Asa was king of Judah. Omri ruled for 12 years. He ruled for 6 of these years in Tirzah.

**24** Omri bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for 2 talents of silver. He built a city on the hill. He gave the city the name Samaria, from the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill.

**25** But Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did more evil than all the kings before him.

**26** He lived as Jeroboam the son of Nebat did. He did the same sin that Jeroboam caused Israel to do. Their worthless idols made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry.

**27** The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel tells the other events of the life of Omri. It tells about all that he did and the power that he showed.

**28** Omri died and they buried him in Samaria. His son Ahab became king in his place.

**29** Ahab the son of Omri became king over Israel in the 38th year that Asa was king of Judah. Ahab ruled over Israel in Samaria for 22 years.

**30** Ahab the son of Omri did more evil in the sight of the LORD than all the kings before him.

**31** For Ahab, the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat were not sufficient. He also married Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. Then Ahab started to serve and worship Baal.

**32** He built an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he built in Samaria.

**33** Ahab also made an Asherah pole. Ahab made the LORD, the God of Israel, more angry than all the kings of Israel before him.

**34** During the rule of Ahab, Hiel from Bethel built the city of Jericho again. When he made the foundation, his oldest son Abiram died. When he put up the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This was what the LORD said through Joshua the son of Nun.

## Chapter 17

**1** Elijah from Tishbe in Gilead said to Ahab, "I serve the LORD, the God of Israel. As surely as the LORD lives, there will be no dew or rain during the next years. There will be rain only when I say so."

**2** Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah. The LORD said,

**3** "Go away from here. Go east and hide near the Brook Cherith, east of the Jordan River.

**4** You will drink water from the brook. I commanded the ravens to bring you food there."

**5** So Elijah did as the LORD told him. He went and lived near the Brook Cherith, east of the Jordan River.

**6** The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and in the evening. He drank water from the brook.

**7** After some time the brook became dry, because there was no rain in the land.

**8** Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah. The LORD said,

**9** "Go to Zarephath, a town near Sidon, and live there. I commanded a widow there to give you food."

**10** So Elijah went to Zarephath. At the gate of the town, he saw a widow who collected sticks. He called to her, "Please bring me a little water in a cup. I want to drink."

**11** She went to get the water. Then he called to her, "Please also bring me a piece of bread."

**12** She said, "As surely as the LORD your God lives, I have no bread. I have only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jar. Now I collect some sticks. Then I will go home and make the last meal for my son and me. We will eat it, and then we will die."

**13** Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid. Go and do what you said. But first make a small loaf of bread for me and bring it to me. Then make food for yourself and your son.

**14** The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: 'The jar of flour will not become empty. The jar of oil will not become empty. This will continue until the day that the LORD sends rain on the land.'"

**15** So she went and did as Elijah told her. She, Elijah, and her family ate for many days.

**16** The jar of flour did not become empty. The jar of oil did not become empty. This was what the LORD said through Elijah.

**17** After this, the son of the woman became sick. She was the owner of the house. His sickness became worse and worse until he had no breath in him.

**18** She said to Elijah, "Man of God, what do you have against me? Did you come to remind God of my sin and to kill my son?"

**19** Elijah said to her, "Give me your son." He took the boy from her arms. He carried him up to the upper room where Elijah stayed. He put the boy on his own bed.

**20** Then he called to the LORD. He said, "O LORD my God, I stay with this widow. Did you also bring trouble on her? Did you kill her son?"

**21** Then Elijah lay on the boy 3 times. He called to the LORD, "O LORD my God, please let the life of this boy come back into him."

**22** The LORD heard the voice of Elijah. The life of the boy came back into him, and he lived.

**23** Elijah took the boy down from the upper room into the house. He gave the boy to his mother. Elijah said, "Look, your son is alive."

**24** The woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God. I know that the word of the LORD from your mouth is true."

## Chapter 18

**1** After a long time, in the 3rd year, the word of the LORD came to Elijah. The LORD said, "Go and show yourself to Ahab. I will send rain on the land."

**2** So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. At that time, the famine in Samaria was very bad.

**3** Ahab called Obadiah, the chief of his palace. Obadiah respected the LORD very much.

**4** Before this, Jezebel killed the prophets of the LORD. Then Obadiah took 100 prophets and hid them in 2 caves, 50 in each cave. He gave them bread and water.

**5** Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs and all the valleys. Maybe we can find grass to keep the horses and mules alive. Then we will not lose all our animals."

**6** So they divided the land between them to look through all of it. Ahab went in one direction alone. Obadiah went in a different direction alone.

**7** While Obadiah went on the road, Elijah met him. Obadiah knew who Elijah was. He bowed down with his face to the ground and said, "Is it you, my lord Elijah?"

**8** Elijah answered him, "Yes, it is I. Go and tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"

**9** Obadiah said, "What did I do wrong? Why do you give me, your servant, to Ahab to kill me?

**10** As surely as the LORD your God lives, my master sent men to look for you in all nations and kingdoms. When a nation said, 'Elijah is not here,' Ahab made that nation promise that they did not find you.

**11** And now you tell me, 'Go and tell your master that Elijah is here.'

**12** When I leave you, the Spirit of the LORD will take you to a place that I do not know. Then I will go and tell Ahab, and he will not find you. Then he will kill me. But I, your servant, respected the LORD since I was young.

**13** My lord, did no one tell you what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of the LORD? I hid 100 prophets of the LORD in 2 caves, 50 in each cave. I gave them bread and water.

**14** And now you tell me, 'Go and tell your master that Elijah is here.' He will kill me!"

**15** Elijah said, "I serve the LORD of armies. As surely as the LORD of armies lives, I will show myself to Ahab today."

**16** So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him. Then Ahab went to meet Elijah.

**17** Ahab saw Elijah and said to him, "Is it you, the man who causes trouble for Israel?"

**18** Elijah answered, "I do not cause trouble for Israel. You and the family of your father cause the trouble. You disobeyed the commands of the LORD and followed the Baals.

**19** Now send a message to all the people of Israel. Tell them to meet me at Mount Carmel. Also bring the 450 prophets of Baal and the 400 prophets of Asherah, who eat at the table of Jezebel."

**20** So Ahab sent a message to all the people of Israel. He brought the prophets together at Mount Carmel.

**21** Elijah went in front of all the people and said, "How long will you be unable to decide between 2 choices? If the LORD is God, follow him. But if Baal is God, follow Baal." But the people said nothing.

**22** Then Elijah said to the people, "I am the only prophet of the LORD who is still alive. But Baal has 450 prophets.

**23** Bring us 2 bulls. Let the prophets of Baal choose 1 bull for themselves. Let them cut it into pieces and put it on the wood. But they must not light a fire. I will prepare the other bull and put it on the wood. I also will not light a fire.

**24** Then you will call to your god, and I will call to the LORD. The God who answers with fire is the true God." Then all the people said, "That is a good plan."

**25** Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose 1 bull for yourselves and prepare it first, because there are many of you. Call to your god. But do not light a fire."

**26** So they took the bull that they received, and they prepared it. They called to Baal from the morning until noon. They shouted, "Baal, answer us!" But there was no voice. No one answered. They danced around the altar that they made.

**27** At noon, Elijah laughed at them. He said, "Shout louder! Surely he is a god! Maybe he thinks deeply, or he is busy, or he is on a trip. Maybe he sleeps and you must wake him up!"

**28** So they shouted louder. They cut themselves with swords and spears until blood flowed. This was their custom.

**29** Noon went past, and they continued to shout like prophets until the time of the evening sacrifice. But there was no voice. No one answered. No one paid attention.

**30** Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come near to me." All the people came near to him. Elijah repaired the altar of the LORD, which someone broke down.

**31** Elijah took 12 stones, 1 stone for each tribe of the sons of Jacob. The LORD spoke to Jacob and said, "Your name will be Israel."

**32** With the stones, Elijah built an altar in the name of the LORD. Around the altar he dug a ditch. The ditch was large enough to hold 2 measures of seed.

**33** He put the wood on the altar. He cut the bull into pieces and put the pieces on the wood. Then he said, "Fill 4 large jars with water. Pour the water on the sacrifice and on the wood."

**34** Then he said, "Do it again." So they did it again. Then he said, "Do it a 3rd time." So they did it a 3rd time.

**35** The water flowed around the altar. Elijah also filled the ditch with water.

**36** At the time of the evening sacrifice, Elijah the prophet came near the altar. He said, "LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, show today that you are God in Israel. Show that I am your servant. Show that I did all these things because you commanded me.

**37** Answer me, O LORD, answer me. Then these people will know that you, LORD, are God. They will know that you turn their hearts back to you."

**38** Then the fire of the LORD fell. It burned the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dirt. It also dried up the water in the ditch.

**39** All the people saw this. They bowed down with their faces to the ground. They said, "The LORD is God! The LORD is God!"

**40** Elijah said to them, "Catch the prophets of Baal. Do not let any of them escape." The people caught them. Elijah took them down to the Brook Kishon and killed them there.

**41** Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink. I hear the sound of a heavy rain."

**42** So Ahab went up to eat and drink. But Elijah went up to the top of Mount Carmel. He bowed down to the ground and put his face between his knees.

**43** He said to his servant, "Go up and look toward the sea." The servant went up and looked. He said, "There is nothing." Elijah said, "Go again." He told him to do this 7 times.

**44** The 7th time, the servant said, "A small cloud comes up from the sea. It is as small as the hand of a man." Elijah said, "Go and tell Ahab, 'Prepare your chariot and go down now. If you do not, the rain will stop you.'"

**45** Soon the sky became black with clouds and wind. There was a heavy rain. Ahab rode in his chariot and went to Jezreel.

**46** The power of the LORD was on Elijah. He tied his clothes around his waist. He ran in front of Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

## Chapter 19

**1** Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah did. He told her that Elijah killed all the prophets of Baal with the sword.

**2** So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah. The messenger said, "Jezebel says, 'Let the gods punish me very much if I do not kill you by this time tomorrow. I will kill you as you killed the prophets.'"

**3** Elijah was afraid. He got up and ran away to save his life. He went to Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there.

**4** Then Elijah went 1 day into the wilderness. He sat down under a broom tree. He asked God to let him die. He said, "I cannot continue, LORD. Take my life. I am not better than my ancestors."

**5** He lay down under the broom tree and slept. Then an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."

**6** Elijah looked around. Near his head there was bread that someone baked on hot stones, and a jar of water. He ate and drank, and then he lay down again.

**7** The angel of the LORD came again a 2nd time. He touched Elijah and said, "Get up and eat. If you do not eat, the trip will be too long for you."

**8** So Elijah got up and ate and drank. The food gave him strength. He walked for 40 days and 40 nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.

**9** There he went into a cave and stayed the night. Then the word of the LORD came to him. The LORD said, "Elijah, what do you do here?"

**10** Elijah said, "I worked very hard for the LORD, the God of armies. The people of Israel broke your covenant. They destroyed your altars. They killed your prophets with the sword. I am the only prophet who is still alive. Now they try to kill me too."

**11** The LORD said, "Go out and stand on the mountain in front of the LORD." Then the LORD went past. A very strong wind broke the mountains and the rocks into pieces in front of the LORD. But the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake. But the LORD was not in the earthquake.

**12** After the earthquake there was a fire. But the LORD was not in the fire. After the fire there was a quiet, soft voice.

**13** Elijah heard the voice. He covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. Then a voice said to him, "Elijah, what do you do here?"

**14** Elijah said, "I worked very hard for the LORD, the God of armies. The people of Israel broke your covenant. They destroyed your altars. They killed your prophets with the sword. I am the only prophet who is still alive. Now they try to kill me too."

**15** The LORD said to him, "Go back the way that you came, to the wilderness of Damascus. When you arrive, anoint Hazael as king over Syria.

**16** Also anoint Jehu the son of Nimshi as king over Israel. Anoint Elisha the son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah as prophet in your place.

**17** Jehu will kill the people who escape from the sword of Hazael. Elisha will kill the people who escape from the sword of Jehu.

**18** But I will keep 7,000 people in Israel alive. These are all the people who did not bow down to Baal and did not kiss his idol."

**19** So Elijah left there and found Elisha the son of Shaphat. Elisha plowed a field with 12 pairs of oxen. Elisha drove the 12th pair. Elijah went to him and put his coat on Elisha.

**20** Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah. He said, "Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye. Then I will follow you." Elijah said to him, "Go back. I did nothing to stop you."

**21** So Elisha went back. He took his pair of oxen and killed them. He burned the wood of the plow to cook the meat. He gave the meat to the people, and they ate. Then Elisha got up and followed Elijah. He became the servant of Elijah.

## Chapter 20

**1** Ben-hadad, the king of Syria, collected all his army. 32 kings were with him, with horses and chariots. He went up and surrounded Samaria and attacked it.

**2** He sent messengers into the city to Ahab, the king of Israel. They said to him, "Ben-hadad says this:

**3** 'Your silver and your gold are mine. Your most beautiful wives and children are also mine.'"

**4** The king of Israel answered, "My lord the king, I agree with what you say. I am yours, and all that I have is yours."

**5** The messengers came back again. They said, "Ben-hadad says this: 'I sent a message to you. I said, "Give me your silver, your gold, your wives, and your children."

**6** But tomorrow at this time I will send my officials to you. They will search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take away all that you value.'"

**7** Then the king of Israel called all the elders of the land. He said, "Look, this man wants to cause trouble. He sent a message to me for my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold. I did not refuse him."

**8** All the elders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen to him. Do not agree."

**9** So Ahab said to the messengers of Ben-hadad, "Tell my lord the king this: 'I will do all that you asked at first. But I cannot do this new thing.'" The messengers went away and took this answer back to Ben-hadad.

**10** Then Ben-hadad sent another message to Ahab. He said, "Let the gods punish me very much if I do not destroy Samaria. There will not be sufficient dust in Samaria to give a handful to each of my soldiers."

**11** The king of Israel answered, "Tell him this: 'A soldier who puts on his armor must not boast.' Only a soldier who takes off his armor after the battle can boast."

**12** Ben-hadad and the kings drank in their tents when Ben-hadad heard this message. He said to his men, "Prepare to attack!" So they prepared to attack the city.

**13** Then a prophet came to Ahab, the king of Israel. He said, "The LORD says this: 'Do you see this large army? Today I will give it to you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"

**14** Ahab asked, "Who will do this?" The prophet said, "The LORD says this: 'The young soldiers of the district governors will do it.'" Then Ahab asked, "Who will start the battle?" The prophet answered, "You."

**15** So Ahab counted the young soldiers of the district governors. There were 232 men. After this, he counted all the people of Israel. There were 7,000 men.

**16** They went out at noon. At that time, Ben-hadad and the 32 kings who helped him were in their tents. They drank wine and became drunk.

**17** The young soldiers of the district governors went out first. Ben-hadad sent men to look, and they told him, "Men come out of Samaria."

**18** Ben-hadad said, "If they come out for peace, catch them alive. If they come out for war, catch them alive."

**19** The young soldiers of the district governors went out of the city, and the army followed them.

**20** Each soldier of Israel killed an enemy soldier. The Syrians ran away, and the army of Israel chased them. But Ben-hadad, the king of Syria, escaped on a horse with some horsemen.

**21** The king of Israel went out and attacked the horses and the chariots. He killed very many Syrians.

**22** Then the prophet came to the king of Israel. He said to him, "Go and make your army strong. Think carefully about what you must do. In the spring, the king of Syria will attack you again."

**23** The officials of the king of Syria said to him, "The gods of Israel are gods of the hills. Thus the army of Israel was stronger than we were. But we must fight against them on the flat land. Then surely we will be stronger than they are.

**24** Do this: Remove the 32 kings from their positions. Put commanders in their places.

**25** Then collect an army like the army that you lost. Get horse for horse and chariot for chariot. We will fight against Israel on the flat land. Surely we will be stronger than they are." Ben-hadad agreed with their advice and did this.

**26** In the spring, Ben-hadad collected the Syrians. He went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.

**27** The people of Israel also collected their army and got supplies. They went out to fight against the Syrians. The army of Israel camped in front of the Syrians. The army of Israel was like 2 small groups of goats. But the Syrians filled all the land.

**28** A man of God came to the king of Israel. He said, "The LORD says this: 'The Syrians said this. "The LORD is a god of the hills, but he is not a god of the valleys." So I will give all this large army to you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"

**29** The 2 armies camped across from each other for 7 days. On the 7th day the battle started. In 1 day the army of Israel killed 100,000 soldiers of the Syrians.

**30** The other Syrians ran away into the city of Aphek. There a wall fell on 27,000 of those men. Ben-hadad also ran into the city and hid in an inner room.

**31** The officials of Ben-hadad said to him, "We heard that the kings of Israel are merciful. Let us put sackcloth around our waists and ropes on our heads. Then let us go out to the king of Israel. Maybe he will let you live."

**32** So they put sackcloth around their waists and ropes on their heads. They went to the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-hadad says, 'Please let me live.'" Ahab said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."

**33** The men looked for a good sign from Ahab. They quickly agreed with his words and said, "Yes, Ben-hadad is your brother!" Ahab said, "Go and bring him." Then Ben-hadad came out to Ahab. Ahab made him come up into his chariot.

**34** Ben-hadad said to him, "I will give back the cities that my father took from your father. You can make markets for yourself in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria." Ahab said, "With this treaty I will let you go." So Ahab made a treaty with him and let him go.

**35** A man from the group of prophets spoke to another prophet because the LORD told him. He said, "Please hit me." But the other man refused to hit him.

**36** So the prophet said to him, "You did not obey the voice of the LORD. Thus when you leave me, a lion will kill you." When the man left him, a lion found him and killed him.

**37** Then the prophet found another man. He said, "Please hit me." So the man hit him and wounded him.

**38** Then the prophet went and waited for the king next to the road. He put a cloth over his eyes so that no one knew who he was.

**39** The king went past, and the prophet shouted to him, "I, your servant, went into the battle. A soldier came to me with a prisoner. He said, 'Guard this man. If he escapes, then you will die in his place. Or you must pay a talent of silver.'

**40** But I, your servant, was busy with other things, and the prisoner escaped." The king of Israel said to him, "You decided your own punishment. You must accept it."

**41** Then the prophet quickly took the cloth away from his eyes. The king of Israel saw that he was one of the prophets.

**42** The prophet said to the king, "The LORD says this: 'I decided that Ben-hadad must die. But you let him go. Thus you will die in his place. Your people will die in the place of his people.'"

**43** The king of Israel went to his palace in Samaria. He was angry and sad.

## Chapter 21

**1** After these events, there was a vineyard that belonged to Naboth from Jezreel. The vineyard was in Jezreel, next to the palace of Ahab, the king of Samaria.

**2** Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your vineyard. It is near my palace and I want to use it as a vegetable garden. In return I will give you a better vineyard. Or, if you prefer, I will pay you its value in money."

**3** But Naboth said to Ahab, "The LORD does not let me give you the land of my ancestors."

**4** So Ahab went home angry and sad because of what Naboth from Jezreel said to him. Naboth said, "I will not give you the land of my ancestors." Ahab lay on his bed and turned his face away. He did not eat.

**5** His wife Jezebel came to him. She asked him, "Why are you so sad? Why do you not eat?"

**6** He said to her, "I spoke to Naboth from Jezreel. I said to him, 'Sell me your vineyard. Or, if you prefer, I will give you another vineyard in its place.' But he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"

**7** His wife Jezebel said to him, "Are you not the king of Israel? Get up and eat. Be happy. I will get the vineyard of Naboth from Jezreel for you."

**8** So Jezebel wrote letters with the name of Ahab. She put his seal on them. She sent the letters to the elders and the leaders who lived in the city of Naboth.

**9** She wrote in the letters, "Tell the people to fast. Give Naboth a seat of honor among the people.

**10** Put 2 worthless men across from him. Let them say that Naboth spoke against God and the king. Then take Naboth out of the city and throw stones at him until he dies."

**11** The elders and the leaders who lived in the city of Naboth did as Jezebel told them. They did as she wrote in the letters that she sent.

**12** They told the people to fast. They gave Naboth a seat of honor among the people.

**13** Then the 2 worthless men came and sat across from Naboth. They spoke against Naboth in front of the people. They said, "Naboth spoke against God and the king." So the people took Naboth out of the city. They threw stones at him until he died.

**14** Then the elders sent a message to Jezebel. They said, "Naboth is dead. The people killed him with stones."

**15** Jezebel heard that the people killed Naboth with stones. She said to Ahab, "Get up and take the vineyard of Naboth from Jezreel. Naboth refused to sell it to you. But now he is not alive. He is dead."

**16** Ahab heard that Naboth was dead. Then he got up and went down to the vineyard of Naboth from Jezreel to take it.

**17** Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah from Tishbe. The LORD said,

**18** "Go down to meet Ahab, the king of Israel, who lives in Samaria. He is now in the vineyard of Naboth. He went there to take it.

**19** Tell him, 'The LORD says this: You killed a man, and now you take his property!' Also tell him, 'The LORD says this: In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, dogs will lick your blood too.'"

**20** Ahab said to Elijah, "So, my enemy, you found me!" Elijah answered, "Yes, I found you. You decided to do evil in the sight of the LORD.

**21** The LORD says this: 'I will bring disaster on you. I will completely destroy your descendants. I will kill every male in the family of Ahab in Israel, slave or free.

**22** I will make your family like the family of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and like the family of Baasha the son of Ahijah. I will do this because you made me angry and caused Israel to sin.'

**23** The LORD also said about Jezebel, 'Dogs will eat Jezebel next to the wall of Jezreel.'

**24** Dogs will eat the people of the family of Ahab who die in the city. Birds will eat the people who die in the fields."

**25** There was no other person like Ahab. He decided to do evil in the sight of the LORD. His wife Jezebel encouraged him to do evil.

**26** He did very terrible things. He worshipped idols, as the Amorites did. The LORD removed the Amorites in front of the people of Israel.

**27** Ahab heard these words. Then he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth. He did not eat. He slept in sackcloth and walked quietly and sadly.

**28** Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah from Tishbe. The LORD said,

**29** "Do you see that Ahab made himself humble in front of me? Because he made himself humble, I will not bring the disaster during his life. I will bring the disaster on his family during the life of his son."

## Chapter 22

**1** For 3 years there was no war between Syria and Israel.

**2** In the 3rd year, Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, went down to visit the king of Israel.

**3** The king of Israel said to his officials, "You know that Ramoth-gilead belongs to us. But we do nothing to take it back from the king of Syria."

**4** He said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me to fight against Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "I will help you. My soldiers are your soldiers. My horses are your horses."

**5** Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, "But first ask the LORD what to do."

**6** So the king of Israel collected the prophets, about 400 men. He asked them, "Must I attack Ramoth-gilead or not?" They said, "Attack it. The Lord will give it to the king."

**7** But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not another prophet of the LORD here? We can ask him."

**8** The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is 1 other man. We can ask the LORD through him. His name is Micaiah the son of Imlah. But I hate him. He never says good things about me. He always says bad things." Jehoshaphat said, "The king must not say that."

**9** So the king of Israel called an official. He said, "Bring Micaiah the son of Imlah quickly."

**10** The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, wore their royal clothes. They sat on their thrones at the floor for grain near the entrance of the gate of Samaria. All the prophets spoke as prophets in front of them.

**11** Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made horns of iron for himself. He said, "The LORD says this: 'With these horns you will attack the Syrians until you destroy them.'"

**12** All the prophets said the same thing. They said, "Attack Ramoth-gilead and win. The LORD will give it to the king."

**13** The messenger who went to call Micaiah said to him, "All the prophets say that the king will win. Please agree with them and say something good."

**14** But Micaiah said, "As surely as the LORD lives, I will say only what the LORD tells me."

**15** Micaiah came to the king. The king asked him, "Micaiah, must we attack Ramoth-gilead or not?" Micaiah answered, "Attack and win. The LORD will give it to the king."

**16** But the king spoke to him again. He said, "How many times must I tell you to speak only the truth to me in the name of the LORD?"

**17** So Micaiah said, "I saw all the army of Israel on the hills. They were like sheep with no shepherd. The LORD said, 'These people have no leader. Let each man go home in peace.'"

**18** The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I told you that he never says good things about me. He says only bad things."

**19** Micaiah said, "So hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD as he sat on his throne. All the army of heaven stood around him, on his right side and on his left side.

**20** The LORD said, 'Who will trick Ahab, so that he will attack Ramoth-gilead and die there?' One angel said one thing, and another angel said a different thing.

**21** Then a spirit came and stood in front of the LORD. The spirit said, 'I will trick Ahab.'

**22** The LORD asked him, 'How?' The spirit said, 'I will go out and make all his prophets tell lies.' The LORD said, 'You will trick him and you will succeed. Go and do it.'

**23** So now, the LORD made all these prophets of yours tell lies. The LORD decided to bring disaster on you."

**24** Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah went to Micaiah and hit him on the face. Zedekiah said, "How did the Spirit of the LORD leave me to speak to you?"

**25** Micaiah said, "You will find out on the day that you go into an inner room to hide."

**26** Then the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah. Bring him back to Amon, the governor of the city, and to Joash, the son of the king.

**27** Tell them, 'The king says this: Put this man in prison. Give him only a little bread and water until I come back safely.'"

**28** Micaiah said, "If you come back safely, then the LORD did not speak through me." He also said, "Remember my words, all you people!"

**29** So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, attacked Ramoth-gilead.

**30** The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will change my appearance and go into the battle. But you will wear your royal clothes." So the king of Israel changed his appearance and went into the battle.

**31** The king of Syria gave a command to his 32 chariot commanders. He said, "Do not fight with any other soldier, small or great. Fight only with the king of Israel."

**32** The chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat and thought, "Surely that is the king of Israel." So they turned to attack him. But Jehoshaphat shouted.

**33** The chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel. So they stopped and did not chase him.

**34** But a soldier shot an arrow without a specific target. The arrow hit the king of Israel between the plates of his armor. The king said to the driver of his chariot, "Turn around and take me out of the battle. I have a wound."

**35** The battle was very fierce that day. Soldiers held the king up in his chariot, with his face toward the Syrians. In the evening he died. The blood from his wound flowed into the bottom of the chariot.

**36** At sunset a shout went through the army. The shout said, "Each man must go back to his city and his country!"

**37** So the king died. They brought him to Samaria and buried him there.

**38** They washed the chariot at the pool of Samaria, where the prostitutes washed. Dogs licked up his blood. This was what the LORD said.

**39** The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel tells the other events of the life of Ahab. It tells about all that he did and the palace that he decorated with ivory. It also tells about all the cities that he built.

**40** Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah became king in his place.

**41** Jehoshaphat the son of Asa became king over Judah in the 4th year that Ahab was king of Israel.

**42** Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 25 years. The name of his mother was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.

**43** He lived as his father Asa did. He did not stop. He did what was right in the sight of the LORD. But he did not remove the high places. The people still made sacrifices and burned incense at the high places.

**44** Jehoshaphat also made peace with the king of Israel.

**45** The Book of the History of the Kings of Judah tells the other events of the life of Jehoshaphat. It tells about the power that he showed and about his wars.

**46** He removed from the land the male prostitutes of the shrines who stayed after the time of his father Asa.

**47** At that time there was no king in Edom. A governor ruled Edom.

**48** Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold. But the ships did not go, because they broke at Ezion-geber.

**49** Then Ahaziah the son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my sailors go with your sailors in the ships." But Jehoshaphat refused.

**50** Jehoshaphat died, and they buried him with his ancestors in the City of David, his ancestor. His son Jehoram became king in his place.

**51** Ahaziah the son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the 17th year that Jehoshaphat was king of Judah. Ahaziah ruled over Israel for 2 years.

**52** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He lived as his father and his mother did. He lived as Jeroboam the son of Nebat did, who caused Israel to sin.

**53** Ahaziah served and worshipped Baal. He made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry, as his father did.

---

# 2 Kings

## Chapter 1

**1** After Ahab died, Moab started a rebellion against Israel.

**2** Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria, and he became sick. He sent messengers and told them, "Go and ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, if I will become well again from this sickness."

**3** But the angel of the LORD spoke to Elijah the Tishbite. The angel said, "Go up and meet the messengers of the king of Samaria. Ask them, 'Is there no God in Israel? Is that why you go to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?'

**4** Thus the LORD says, 'You will not come down from the bed that you are on. You will surely die.'" Then Elijah went away.

**5** The messengers went back to the king. He asked them, "Why did you come back?"

**6** They told him, "A man came up to meet us. He said, 'Go back to the king who sent you. Tell him that the LORD says this: Is there no God in Israel? Is that why you send men to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Thus you will not come down from the bed that you are on. You will surely die.'"

**7** The king asked them, "What type of man came up to meet you and told you these words?"

**8** They answered, "He was a man with much hair. He wore a leather belt around his waist." The king said, "That man is Elijah the Tishbite."

**9** Then the king sent a captain with his 50 men to Elijah. The captain went up to Elijah, who sat on the top of a hill. The captain said, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down.'"

**10** Elijah answered the captain, "If I am a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven. Let the fire burn you and your 50 men." Then fire came down from heaven and burned the captain and his 50 men.

**11** The king sent another captain with his 50 men to Elijah. This captain said, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down quickly.'"

**12** Elijah answered, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven. Let the fire burn you and your 50 men." Then the fire of God came down from heaven and burned the captain and his 50 men.

**13** The king sent a third captain with his 50 men. The third captain went up and fell on his knees in front of Elijah. He begged Elijah, "Man of God, please let my life and the lives of these 50 servants be valuable to you.

**14** Fire came down from heaven and burned the first 2 captains and their men. But please let my life now be valuable to you."

**15** The angel of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him. Do not be afraid of him." So Elijah got up and went down with the captain to the king.

**16** Elijah told the king, "The LORD says this: 'You sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron. Is there no God in Israel to ask? Thus you will not come down from the bed that you are on. You will surely die.'"

**17** So Ahaziah died, as the LORD said through Elijah. Ahaziah had no son. Thus Jehoram became king after him. This occurred in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah.

**18** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Ahaziah did.

## Chapter 2

**1** The LORD was about to take Elijah up into heaven in a whirlwind. At that time, Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.

**2** Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, because the LORD sent me to Bethel." But Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.

**3** The sons of the prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha. They asked him, "Do you know that the LORD will take your master away from you today?" Elisha said, "Yes, I know. Be quiet."

**4** Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, because the LORD sent me to Jericho." Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.

**5** The sons of the prophets at Jericho came to Elisha. They asked him, "Do you know that the LORD will take your master away from you today?" Elisha answered, "Yes, I know. Be quiet."

**6** Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, because the LORD sent me to the Jordan River." Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So the 2 men went on together.

**7** 50 men of the sons of the prophets went and stood at a distance to watch. Elijah and Elisha stood by the Jordan.

**8** Elijah took his cloak and rolled it up. He hit the water with it. The water divided to the left and to the right. Then the 2 men went across on dry ground.

**9** After they went across, Elijah said to Elisha, "Tell me what I can do for you before God takes me away from you." Elisha said, "Please let me get a double part of your spirit."

**10** Elijah said, "You ask for a difficult thing. If you see me when God takes me from you, then you will get it. If you do not see me, you will not get it."

**11** They continued to walk and talk. Then a chariot of fire and horses of fire suddenly came between the 2 men. Elijah went up into heaven in a whirlwind.

**12** Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father, my father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!" Elisha did not see Elijah again. Then Elisha took his own clothes and tore them into 2 pieces.

**13** Elisha picked up the cloak that fell from Elijah. He went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

**14** He hit the water with the cloak of Elijah. He said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" When he hit the water, the water divided to the left and to the right. Then Elisha went across.

**15** The sons of the prophets from Jericho watched him. They said, "The spirit of Elijah is on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed down to the ground in front of him.

**16** They said to him, "Look, we, your servants, have 50 strong men. Please let them go and look for your master. Maybe the Spirit of the LORD took him up and put him on a mountain or in a valley." Elisha said, "Do not send them."

**17** But they continued to ask him until he felt ashamed. Then he said, "Send them." So they sent 50 men. The men looked for Elijah for 3 days, but they did not find him.

**18** The men came back to Elisha, who stayed at Jericho. He said to them, "I told you not to go."

**19** The men of the city said to Elisha, "Please look. The position of this city is good, as you can see, my lord. But the water is bad, and the land produces no crops."

**20** Elisha said, "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.

**21** Elisha went out to the spring of water and threw the salt into it. He said, "The LORD says this: 'I make this water good. It will not cause death or bad land again.'"

**22** So the water became good, and it is good to this day. It occurred as Elisha said.

**23** Elisha went up from there to Bethel. As he went up on the road, some young boys came out of the city. They laughed at him and said, "Go up, you bald man! Go up, you bald man!"

**24** Elisha turned around and looked at them. He cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then 2 female bears came out of the forest and attacked 42 of the boys.

**25** Elisha went from there to Mount Carmel. Then he went back to Samaria.

## Chapter 3

**1** Jehoram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Samaria in the 18th year of Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah. Jehoram ruled for 12 years.

**2** Jehoram did evil in the sight of the LORD. But he was not as bad as his father and mother. He removed the sacred stone of Baal that his father made.

**3** But Jehoram continued in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin. Jehoram did not stop these sins.

**4** Mesha the king of Moab kept sheep. He gave the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and the wool of 100,000 rams each year.

**5** But after Ahab died, the king of Moab started a rebellion against the king of Israel.

**6** At that time King Jehoram went out of Samaria. He gathered all the men of Israel for war.

**7** He sent a message to Jehoshaphat the king of Judah. He said, "The king of Moab started a rebellion against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?" Jehoshaphat said, "I will go. I am as you are. My people are as your people. My horses are as your horses."

**8** Jehoshaphat asked, "Which road will we use?" Jehoram answered, "The road through the desert of Edom."

**9** So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went. They went around for 7 days. Then there was no water for the army or for the animals with them.

**10** The king of Israel said, "Oh no! The LORD called us 3 kings together to give us to Moab!"

**11** But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here? We can ask the LORD through him." One of the officers of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was the servant of Elijah."

**12** Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the LORD is with Elisha." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went down to Elisha.

**13** Elisha said to the king of Israel, "I have nothing to do with you. Go to the prophets of your father and of your mother." The king of Israel said, "No. The LORD called us 3 kings together to give us to Moab."

**14** Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD of armies lives, whom I serve, I respect Jehoshaphat the king of Judah. If he is not here, I will not look at you or see you.

**15** But now bring me a man who plays the harp." While the man played, the power of the LORD came on Elisha.

**16** Elisha said, "The LORD says this: 'Dig many ditches in this valley.'

**17** The LORD says, 'You will not see wind or rain. But this valley will become full of water. You, your cattle, and your other animals will drink.'

**18** This is an easy thing for the LORD. He will also give Moab to you.

**19** You will attack every city with walls and every important city. You will cut down every good tree. You will block all the springs of water. You will put stones on every good field and make it bad."

**20** In the morning, at the time of the grain offering, water came from the direction of Edom. The land became full of water.

**21** All the Moabites heard that the kings came to fight against them. So they gathered all the men who could fight, young and old. They stood at the border.

**22** They got up early in the morning. The sun shone on the water. To the Moabites, the water across from them looked as red as blood.

**23** They said, "That is blood! The kings fought and killed each other. Now, Moab, let us take their possessions!"

**24** But when the Moabites came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites got up and attacked them. The Moabites ran away from them. The Israelites went into the land of Moab and continued to kill the Moabites.

**25** They destroyed the cities. Each man threw a stone on every good field until the fields were full of stones. They blocked all the springs of water. They cut down all the good trees. Only the city of Kir-haraseth stayed with its stone walls. But the men with slings surrounded it and attacked it.

**26** The king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him. So he took 700 men with swords. They tried to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.

**27** Then the king of Moab took his oldest son, who was to become king after him. He sacrificed his son as a burnt offering on the city wall. Then there was great anger against Israel. So the Israelites went away from the king of Moab and went back to their land.

## Chapter 4

**1** The wife of one of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha. She said, "My husband, your servant, is dead. You know that he respected the LORD. But a man to whom he owed money came. That man wants to take my 2 sons as his slaves."

**2** Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in your house?" She said, "I, your servant, have nothing in the house but a small jar of oil."

**3** Elisha said, "Go out and borrow empty jars from all your neighbors. Get many jars.

**4** Then go into your house. Close the door behind you and your sons. Pour the oil into all those jars. Put each full jar to the side."

**5** So she went away from him. She closed the door behind her and her sons. Her sons brought the jars to her, and she poured the oil.

**6** When the jars were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another jar." He said to her, "There are no more jars." Then the oil stopped.

**7** She went and told the man of God. He said, "Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt. You and your sons can live on the money that remains."

**8** One day Elisha went to Shunem. An important woman lived there. She asked him strongly to eat a meal. After that, each time he went by, he stopped there to eat.

**9** The woman said to her husband, "I know that this man who often comes by is a holy man of God.

**10** Please let us make a small room on the roof. Let us put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp in it for him. Then he can stay there when he comes to us."

**11** One day Elisha came there. He went into the room and lay down.

**12** He said to Gehazi, his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman." Gehazi called her, and she stood in front of Elisha.

**13** Elisha said to Gehazi, "Tell her this: 'You did much work to help us. What can we do for you? Can we speak for you to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She answered, "I live safely among my own people."

**14** Elisha asked, "Then what can we do for her?" Gehazi answered, "She has no son, and her husband is old."

**15** Elisha said, "Call her." Gehazi called her, and she stood in the doorway.

**16** Elisha said, "At this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms." She said, "No, my lord, man of God. Do not lie to me, your servant."

**17** But the woman became pregnant. At that time the next year, she gave birth to a son, as Elisha told her.

**18** The child grew. One day he went out to his father, who was with the men who cut the grain.

**19** The boy said to his father, "My head! My head!" His father said to a servant, "Carry him to his mother."

**20** The servant took him and brought him to his mother. The boy sat on her lap until noon. Then he died.

**21** She went up and put him on the bed of the man of God. She closed the door and went out.

**22** She called her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys. I will go quickly to the man of God and come back."

**23** Her husband asked, "Why do you go to him today? It is not the new moon or the Sabbath." She said, "All is well."

**24** She put a saddle on a donkey. She said to her servant, "Go fast. Do not go slowly for me unless I tell you."

**25** So she went to the man of God at Mount Carmel. The man of God saw her at a distance. He said to Gehazi, his servant, "Look, there is the Shunammite woman.

**26** Please run now to meet her. Ask her, 'Are you well? Is your husband well? Is your child well?'" She answered, "All is well."

**27** She came to the man of God on the hill and held his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away. But the man of God said, "Let her be. She is very sad. The LORD did not show me the cause. He did not tell me."

**28** She said, "My lord, did I ask you for a son? Did I not tell you, 'Do not give me false hope'?"

**29** Elisha said to Gehazi, "Prepare to go. Take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet a man, do not stop to speak to him. If a man speaks to you, do not answer. Put my staff on the face of the child."

**30** But the mother of the child said, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So Elisha got up and followed her.

**31** Gehazi went ahead of them. He put the staff on the face of the child. But there was no sound and no response. So Gehazi went back to meet Elisha. He told him, "The child did not wake up."

**32** Elisha came into the house. The child lay dead on his bed.

**33** Elisha went in and closed the door behind the 2 of them. Then he prayed to the LORD.

**34** He went up on the bed and lay on the child. He put his mouth on the mouth of the child and his eyes on the eyes of the child. He put his hands on the hands of the child. He stretched out on the child, and the body of the child became warm.

**35** Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the house. Then he went up and stretched out on the child again. The child sneezed 7 times and opened his eyes.

**36** Elisha called Gehazi and said, "Call the Shunammite woman." So Gehazi called her. When she came in, Elisha said, "Pick up your son."

**37** She came in and fell at his feet. She bowed down to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.

**38** Elisha went back to Gilgal. At that time there was a famine in the land. The sons of the prophets sat in front of him. He said to his servant, "Put the large pot on the fire. Cook a stew for the sons of the prophets."

**39** One of them went out into the field to gather plants. He found a wild vine. He picked wild gourds from it until his cloak was full. He came back and cut them into the pot of stew. They did not know what the gourds were.

**40** They poured out the stew for the men to eat. But when the men ate the stew, they cried out, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" They could not eat it.

**41** Elisha said, "Bring some flour." He threw the flour into the pot. He said, "Pour out the stew for the people to eat." Then the stew in the pot was not dangerous.

**42** A man came from Baal-shalishah. He brought the man of God 20 loaves of barley bread from the first crop. He also brought some fresh grain in a bag. Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat."

**43** His servant said, "How can I put this in front of 100 men?" Elisha said again, "Give it to the people to eat. The LORD says this: 'They will eat, and some food will remain.'"

**44** So the servant put it in front of them. They ate, and some food remained, as the LORD said.

## Chapter 5

**1** Naaman was the commander of the army of the king of Syria. His master thought that he was a great and important man. Through Naaman, the LORD gave victory to Syria. Naaman was a strong soldier, but he had leprosy, a skin disease.

**2** Groups of Syrian soldiers went out and attacked Israel. They took a young girl from the land of Israel as a prisoner. She became the servant of the wife of Naaman.

**3** The girl said to her mistress, "I wish that my master was with the prophet who is in Samaria! That prophet can cure him of his leprosy."

**4** Naaman went in and told his master, "The girl from the land of Israel said these things."

**5** The king of Syria said, "Go now. I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So Naaman went. He took with him 10 talents of silver, 6,000 pieces of gold, and 10 sets of clothes.

**6** He brought the letter to the king of Israel. The letter said, "With this letter I send my servant Naaman to you. Cure him of his leprosy."

**7** The king of Israel read the letter. Then he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God? Can I kill and make alive? Why does this man send a man to me to cure him of leprosy? Look, the king of Syria tries to start a fight with me."

**8** Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel tore his clothes. So he sent this message to the king: "Why did you tear your clothes? Let the man come to me. Then he will know that there is a prophet in Israel."

**9** So Naaman came with his horses and his chariot. He stopped at the door of the house of Elisha.

**10** Elisha sent a messenger to him. The messenger said, "Go and wash in the Jordan River 7 times. Then your skin will become healthy again, and you will be clean."

**11** But Naaman became angry and went away. He said, "I thought that he will surely come out to me. I thought that he will stand and call on the name of the LORD his God. I thought that he will move his hand over the area and cure the leprosy.

**12** The Abana and the Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, are better than all the water in Israel. Can I not wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and went away very angry.

**13** His servants came near and spoke to him. They said, "My father, if the prophet told you to do a difficult thing, you were ready to do it. He only told you, 'Wash and be clean.' Thus you must surely obey him."

**14** So Naaman went down and went under the water of the Jordan 7 times, as the man of God told him. His skin became healthy again, as the skin of a little child. He was clean.

**15** Naaman and all his men went back to the man of God. Naaman stood in front of him and said, "Now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but only in Israel. Please accept a gift from me, your servant."

**16** But Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives, whom I serve, I will not accept a gift." Naaman asked him strongly to take it, but Elisha did not accept.

**17** Naaman said, "If you do not accept, then please give me, your servant, as much earth as 2 mules can carry. From now on I will not give burnt offerings or sacrifices to other gods. I will give them only to the LORD.

**18** But I ask the LORD to forgive me for one thing. My master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship there. He leans on my arm, and I must bow down in the temple of Rimmon. When I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, I ask the LORD to forgive me for this thing."

**19** Elisha said to him, "Go in peace." So Naaman went a short distance away from him.

**20** Gehazi was the servant of Elisha the man of God. He said to himself, "My master let this Syrian Naaman go. He did not accept the gifts that Naaman brought. As surely as the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something from him."

**21** So Gehazi followed Naaman. Naaman saw him run after him. So he got down from the chariot to meet him. He asked, "Is all well?"

**22** Gehazi said, "All is well. My master sent me. He said, 'Now 2 young men of the sons of the prophets came to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and 2 sets of clothes.'"

**23** Naaman said, "Please take 2 talents." He asked Gehazi strongly to accept. He tied 2 talents of silver in 2 bags with 2 sets of clothes. He gave them to 2 of his servants. The servants carried the bags in front of Gehazi.

**24** When Gehazi came to the hill, he took the bags from the servants. He put them in the house. Then he sent the men away, and they left.

**25** Gehazi went in and stood in front of his master. Elisha asked him, "Gehazi, where did you go?" Gehazi said, "I, your servant, did not go to a place."

**26** Elisha said to him, "My spirit was with you when the man got down from his chariot to meet you. This is not the time to accept money and clothes. It is not the time to get olive groves, vineyards, sheep, cattle, and servants.

**27** Thus the leprosy of Naaman will be on you and on your descendants for all time." Gehazi went out from Elisha with leprosy. His skin was as white as snow.

## Chapter 6

**1** The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we live with you is too small for us.

**2** Please let us go to the Jordan. Each of us will get a log there. Then we will make a place to live there." Elisha said, "Go."

**3** One of them said, "Please come with your servants." Elisha answered, "I will come."
