**4** So he went with them. They came to the Jordan and started to cut down trees.

**5** While one man cut down a tree, the iron head of his axe fell into the water. He cried out, "Oh no, my master! I borrowed that axe!"

**6** The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" The man showed him the place. Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water there. Then the iron came up and floated.

**7** Elisha said, "Take it out." So the man put out his hand and took it.

**8** The king of Syria was at war with Israel. He spoke with his officers. He said, "I will put my camp at this place."

**9** But the man of God sent a message to the king of Israel. He said, "Be careful. Do not go by that place, because the Syrians go down there."

**10** So the king of Israel sent men to the place that the man of God told him about. The man of God warned the king many times, and the king was careful there.

**11** This made the king of Syria very angry. He called his officers and said to them, "Tell me! Which of us helps the king of Israel?"

**12** One of his officers said, "None of us, my lord the king. But Elisha, the prophet in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom."

**13** The king said, "Go and find where Elisha is. Then I can send men to catch him." Men told the king, "Elisha is in Dothan."

**14** So the king sent horses, chariots, and a large army there. They came at night and surrounded the city.

**15** The servant of the man of God got up early in the morning and went out. He saw an army with horses and chariots around the city. The servant said, "Oh no, my master! What will we do?"

**16** Elisha answered, "Do not be afraid. The army with us is larger than the army with them."

**17** Then Elisha prayed, "LORD, please open his eyes so that he can see." The LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw. The hills around Elisha were full of horses and chariots of fire.

**18** The Syrians came down toward Elisha. Then Elisha prayed to the LORD, "Please make these people blind." So the LORD made them blind, as Elisha asked.

**19** Elisha said to them, "This is not the road, and this is not the city. Follow me. I will bring you to the man that you look for." But he took them to Samaria.

**20** When they came into Samaria, Elisha said, "LORD, open the eyes of these men so that they can see." The LORD opened their eyes, and they saw. They were in the center of Samaria.

**21** When the king of Israel saw them, he asked Elisha, "My father, must I kill them? Must I kill them?"

**22** Elisha answered, "Do not kill them. You do not kill men that you capture with your sword and bow. Give them food and water. Let them eat and drink. Then let them go back to their master."

**23** So the king prepared a large meal for them. After they ate and drank, he sent them away. They went back to their master. After that, the groups of Syrian soldiers did not attack the land of Israel again.

**24** Some time later, Ben-hadad the king of Syria gathered all his army. He went up and surrounded Samaria to attack it.

**25** Thus there was a very bad famine in Samaria. The Syrians surrounded the city for a long time. At last, the head of a donkey cost 80 pieces of silver. A quarter of a cab of dove dung cost 5 pieces of silver.

**26** The king of Israel walked on the wall of the city. A woman cried out to him, "Help me, my lord the king!"

**27** The king said, "If the LORD does not help you, how can I help you? I have no grain from the grain floor. I have no wine from the winepress."

**28** Then the king asked her, "What is your problem?" She answered, "This woman said to me, 'Give me your son. We will eat him today. Tomorrow we will eat my son.'

**29** So we cooked my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, 'Give me your son. We will eat him.' But she hid her son."

**30** The king heard the words of the woman. He tore his clothes. While he walked on the wall, the people looked at him. They saw that he wore sackcloth under his clothes, against his skin.

**31** The king said, "Let God punish me very much if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat stays on his body today!"

**32** Elisha sat in his house, and the elders sat with him. The king sent a messenger ahead of him. But before the messenger came, Elisha said to the elders, "This son of a murderer sent a man to cut off my head. Look, when the messenger comes, close the door. Hold the door shut against him. The sound of the feet of his master comes after him."

**33** While Elisha still spoke with them, the messenger came down to him. The king said, "The LORD caused this trouble. Why must I wait for the LORD more?"

## Chapter 7

**1** Elisha said, "Hear the word of the LORD. The LORD says this: 'Tomorrow at about this time, a measure of fine flour will cost 1 shekel. 2 measures of barley will cost 1 shekel. People will sell them at the gate of Samaria.'"

**2** The king leaned on the arm of an officer. That officer answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD makes windows in heaven, this cannot occur." Elisha said, "You will see it with your eyes. But you will not eat any of it."

**3** There were 4 men with leprosy at the entrance of the city gate. They said to each other, "Why do we sit here until we die?

**4** If we go into the city, we will die there, because there is famine in the city. If we stay here, we will also die. So let us go to the camp of the Syrians. If they let us live, we will live. If they kill us, we will only die."

**5** At sunset they got up and went to the camp of the Syrians. They came to the edge of the camp. But there were no men there.

**6** The Lord caused the Syrian army to hear the sound of chariots and horses, as the sound of a large army. The Syrians said to each other, "The king of Israel paid the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to attack us!"

**7** So the Syrians got up and ran away at sunset. They left their tents, their horses, and their donkeys. They left the camp as it was and ran to save their lives.

**8** The men with leprosy came to the edge of the camp. They went into a tent. They ate and drank. They took silver, gold, and clothes from it. Then they went and hid these things. They came back and went into another tent. They took things from it too and hid them.

**9** Then they said to each other, "We do wrong. This is a day of good news, but we are silent. If we wait until morning, we will get punishment. Now come, let us go and tell the household of the king."

**10** So they went and called to the gatekeepers of the city. They told them, "We went to the camp of the Syrians. There was no man there, and we heard no voice of a man. There were only horses and donkeys that were tied, and the tents as the Syrians left them."

**11** The gatekeepers shouted the news. People told it to the household of the king inside.

**12** The king got up in the night. He said to his officers, "I will tell you what the Syrians did to us. They know that we are hungry. Thus they left the camp to hide in the field. They think, 'When the Israelites come out of the city, we will capture them alive. Then we will go into the city.'"

**13** One of his officers answered, "Please let some men take 5 of the horses that remain in the city. If they die, it is no worse than for all the people of Israel who remain here. All of us will die. Let us send the men to see."

**14** So they took 2 chariots with horses. The king sent them after the Syrian army. He said, "Go and see."

**15** The men followed the Syrians as far as the Jordan. All the road was full of clothes and equipment. The Syrians threw them away when they ran quickly. The messengers came back and told the king.

**16** Then the people went out and took the possessions from the camp of the Syrians. So a measure of fine flour cost 1 shekel, and 2 measures of barley cost 1 shekel. This occurred as the LORD said.

**17** The king made the officer on whose arm he leaned responsible for the gate. The people walked over that officer in the gate, and he died. This occurred as the man of God said when the king came down to him.

**18** The man of God told the king, "Tomorrow at about this time, 2 measures of barley will cost 1 shekel. A measure of fine flour will cost 1 shekel at the gate of Samaria."

**19** The officer answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD makes windows in heaven, this cannot occur." The man of God said, "You will see it with your eyes. But you will not eat any of it."

**20** That is what occurred to him. The people walked over him in the gate, and he died.

## Chapter 8

**1** Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he made alive again. He said, "Get up and go away with your household. Live as a foreigner in a place where you can live. The LORD will send a famine. It will be on the land for 7 years."

**2** So the woman got up and did as the man of God told her. She went with her household and lived in the land of the Philistines for 7 years.

**3** At the end of the 7 years, the woman came back from the land of the Philistines. She went to the king to ask for her house and her land.

**4** At that time the king spoke with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God. The king said, "Please tell me all the great things that Elisha did."

**5** Gehazi told the king how Elisha made a dead person alive again. At that time the woman whose son Elisha made alive came to the king. She asked the king for her house and her land. Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman. This is her son whom Elisha made alive again."

**6** The king asked the woman, and she told him the story. So the king gave her an officer. He told the officer, "Give back to her all that was hers. Also give her all the income from her fields from the day that she left the land until now."

**7** Elisha went to Damascus. Ben-hadad the king of Syria was sick. People told the king, "The man of God came here."

**8** The king said to Hazael, "Take a gift with you and go meet the man of God. Ask the LORD through him, 'Will I become well again from this sickness?'"

**9** So Hazael went to meet Elisha. He took a gift with him of all the good things of Damascus. 40 camels carried the gift. Hazael came and stood in front of Elisha. He said, "Your son Ben-hadad, the king of Syria, sent me to you. He asks, 'Will I become well again from this sickness?'"

**10** Elisha said to him, "Go and tell him, 'You will surely become well.' But the LORD showed me that he will surely die."

**11** Elisha looked at Hazael with a fixed face until Hazael felt ashamed. Then the man of God cried.

**12** Hazael asked, "Why does my lord cry?" Elisha answered, "I know the evil that you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn their strong cities. You will kill their young men with the sword. You will kill their small children. You will cut open their pregnant women."

**13** Hazael said, "I, your servant, am only a dog. How can I do such a great thing?" Elisha answered, "The LORD showed me that you will become king of Syria."

**14** Then Hazael left Elisha and went back to his master. Ben-hadad asked him, "What did Elisha tell you?" Hazael answered, "He told me that you will surely become well."

**15** But the next day Hazael took a thick cloth and put it in water. He spread it over the face of the king, and the king died. Then Hazael became king after him.

**16** Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in the 5th year of Joram son of Ahab, the king of Israel. At that time Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.

**17** Jehoram was 32 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 8 years.

**18** He lived as the kings of Israel lived, as the family of Ahab did, because he married the daughter of Ahab. He did evil in the sight of the LORD.

**19** But the LORD did not want to destroy Judah, because of his servant David. The LORD promised to give a lamp to David and his descendants for all time.

**20** During the rule of Jehoram, Edom started a rebellion against Judah. The Edomites made a king for themselves.

**21** So Jehoram went to Zair with all his chariots. The Edomites surrounded him. But he got up at night and attacked the Edomites and the commanders of their chariots. Then his army ran away to their homes.

**22** So Edom continued in rebellion against Judah to this day. At the same time, the city of Libnah also started a rebellion.

**23** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Jehoram did.

**24** Jehoram died, and the people buried him with his ancestors in the City of David. Then his son Ahaziah became king after him.

**25** Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the 12th year of Joram son of Ahab, the king of Israel.

**26** Ahaziah was 22 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 1 year. His mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of Omri the king of Israel.

**27** Ahaziah lived as the family of Ahab lived. He did evil in the sight of the LORD, as the family of Ahab did. He was a relative of the family of Ahab through marriage.

**28** Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab to fight against Hazael the king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead. The Syrians wounded Joram.

**29** So King Joram went back to Jezreel to become well from the wounds. The Syrians gave him these wounds at Ramah when he fought against Hazael the king of Syria. Ahaziah son of Jehoram, the king of Judah, went down to Jezreel. He went to visit Joram son of Ahab, because Joram had wounds.

## Chapter 9

**1** Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets. He told him, "Prepare to go. Take this bottle of oil in your hand and go to Ramoth-gilead.

**2** When you come there, find Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Go in and take him away from his companions. Bring him into a room inside.

**3** Then take the bottle of oil and pour it on his head. Say, 'The LORD says this: I anoint you as king of Israel.' Then open the door and run away. Do not wait."

**4** So the young prophet went to Ramoth-gilead.

**5** When he came, the commanders of the army sat together. He said, "Commander, I have a message for you." Jehu asked, "For which of us?" The young man said, "For you, commander."

**6** Jehu got up and went into the house. The young man poured the oil on his head. He told Jehu, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: 'I anoint you as king of the people of the LORD, of Israel.

**7** You must kill the family of Ahab, your master. Thus I will punish Jezebel for the deaths of my servants the prophets. I will punish her for the deaths of all the servants of the LORD.

**8** All the family of Ahab will die. I will kill every male in the family of Ahab in Israel, slave or free.

**9** I will make the family of Ahab as the family of Jeroboam son of Nebat. I will make it as the family of Baasha son of Ahijah.

**10** Dogs will eat Jezebel in the field at Jezreel. No person will bury her.'" Then the young man opened the door and ran away.

**11** Jehu went out to the officers of his master. One of them asked him, "Is all well? Why did this crazy man come to you?" Jehu said to them, "You know the man and the type of thing that he says."

**12** They said, "That is not true. Tell us." Jehu said, "He told me this: 'The LORD says this: I anoint you as king of Israel.'"

**13** Then each of them quickly took his cloak. They put the cloaks under Jehu on the top of the steps. They blew trumpets and shouted, "Jehu is king!"

**14** So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, made a secret plan against Joram. Joram and all Israel guarded Ramoth-gilead against Hazael the king of Syria.

**15** But King Joram went back to Jezreel to become well from the wounds. The Syrians gave him these wounds when he fought against Hazael the king of Syria. Jehu said, "If you agree with me, let no person leave the city. Let no person go to tell the news in Jezreel."

**16** Then Jehu got into his chariot and went to Jezreel, because Joram lay there. Ahaziah the king of Judah went down there to visit Joram.

**17** A watchman stood on the tower in Jezreel. He saw the troops of Jehu come. He said, "I see some troops." Joram said, "Get a horseman. Send him to meet them. Let him ask, 'Do you come in peace?'"

**18** So a horseman went to meet Jehu. He said, "The king asks, 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu said, "Peace is not your business. Turn and follow me." The watchman told the king, "The messenger came to them, but he does not come back."

**19** Then the king sent a second horseman. He came to them and said, "The king asks, 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu answered, "Peace is not your business. Turn and follow me."

**20** The watchman told the king, "He came to them, but he does not come back. The man drives his chariot as Jehu son of Nimshi drives. He drives very fast, as a crazy man."

**21** Joram said, "Prepare my chariot." So the men prepared his chariot. Joram the king of Israel and Ahaziah the king of Judah went out, each in his chariot. They went out to meet Jehu. They met him in the field of Naboth from Jezreel.

**22** When Joram saw Jehu, he asked, "Do you come in peace, Jehu?" Jehu answered, "There can be no peace while your mother Jezebel continues to worship idols and use witchcraft."

**23** Joram turned his chariot and ran away. He shouted to Ahaziah, "Ahaziah, this is a trap!"

**24** Jehu pulled his bow with all his strength. He shot Joram between his shoulders. The arrow went through his heart, and he fell down in his chariot.

**25** Jehu said to Bidkar, his officer, "Pick him up and throw him into the field of Naboth from Jezreel. Remember the time when you and I rode together behind Ahab his father. Then the LORD said this prophecy against Ahab:

**26** 'Yesterday I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons,' says the LORD. 'I will surely punish you in this field,' says the LORD. Thus pick him up and throw him into the field, as the LORD said."

**27** Ahaziah the king of Judah saw this. He ran away on the road to Beth-haggan. Jehu followed him and shouted, "Kill him too!" They wounded him in his chariot on the road up to Gur, near Ibleam. But Ahaziah ran away to Megiddo and died there.

**28** His servants carried his body in a chariot to Jerusalem. They buried him in his tomb with his ancestors in the City of David.

**29** Ahaziah became king of Judah in the 11th year of Joram son of Ahab.

**30** Then Jehu came to Jezreel. Jezebel heard about it. She painted her eyes and arranged her hair. Then she looked out of a window.

**31** Jehu came in through the gate. She said, "Do you come in peace, you Zimri? You killed your master."

**32** Jehu looked up at the window and said, "Who is on my side? Who?" 2 or 3 palace officials looked down at him.

**33** Jehu said, "Throw her down!" So they threw her down. Some of her blood went on the wall and on the horses. Then the horses walked on her.

**34** Jehu went in and ate and drank. Then he said, "Go and get this cursed woman. Bury her, because she is the daughter of a king."

**35** They went to bury her. But they found only her skull, her feet, and the palms of her hands.

**36** They came back and told Jehu. He said, "This is the word of the LORD. He spoke it through his servant Elijah the Tishbite. He said, 'Dogs will eat the body of Jezebel in the field at Jezreel.

**37** The body of Jezebel will be as manure on the field at Jezreel. No person will be able to say, This is Jezebel.'"

## Chapter 10

**1** Ahab had 70 sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria. He sent them to the rulers of Jezreel, to the elders, and to the guardians of the sons of Ahab. The letters said,

**2** "The sons of your master are with you. You also have chariots, horses, a city with walls, and weapons. When this letter comes to you,

**3** choose the best and most qualified of the sons of your master. Put him on the throne of his father. Then fight for the family of your master."

**4** But they were very afraid. They said, "2 kings could not fight against Jehu. How can we fight against him?"

**5** So the manager of the palace, the governor of the city, the elders, and the guardians sent a message to Jehu. They said, "We are your servants. We will do all that you tell us. We will not make a person king. Do what you think is good."

**6** Then Jehu wrote a second letter to them. He said, "If you are on my side, obey me. Cut off the heads of the sons of your master. Bring the heads to me at Jezreel at this time tomorrow." The 70 sons of the king were with the important men of the city, who took care of them.

**7** When the letter came to them, they took the 70 sons of the king and killed them. They put the heads in baskets and sent them to Jehu at Jezreel.

**8** A messenger came and told Jehu, "They brought the heads of the sons of the king." Jehu said, "Put the heads in 2 piles at the entrance of the city gate until the morning."

**9** In the morning Jehu went out and stood in front of all the people. He said, "You are not guilty. I made a plan against my master and killed him. But who killed all these men?

**10** Know that all the words of the LORD against the family of Ahab will occur. The LORD did what he said through his servant Elijah."

**11** So Jehu killed all the people of the family of Ahab who remained in Jezreel. He also killed all the important officials, close friends, and priests of Ahab. No person of the family of Ahab remained.

**12** Then Jehu got up and went to Samaria. On the road he came to Beth-eked of the shepherds.

**13** There Jehu met the relatives of Ahaziah the king of Judah. He asked, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are the relatives of Ahaziah. We go down to visit the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."

**14** Jehu said, "Capture them alive." So his men captured them alive. Then the men killed them at the well of Beth-eked. They killed 42 men, and none of them remained.

**15** Jehu went from there. He met Jehonadab son of Rechab, who came to meet him. Jehu greeted him and asked, "Are you loyal to me, as I am loyal to you?" Jehonadab answered, "I am." Jehu said, "If you are, give me your hand." So Jehonadab gave him his hand. Jehu helped him up into the chariot.

**16** Jehu said, "Come with me. See how much I want to serve the LORD." So Jehonadab rode with him in his chariot.

**17** Jehu came to Samaria. He killed all the people of the family of Ahab who remained in Samaria. He destroyed them all, as the LORD told Elijah.

**18** Then Jehu gathered all the people together. He told them, "Ahab served Baal a little. Jehu will serve Baal much.

**19** Now call all the prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests to me. Do not let one of them stay away. I will make a large sacrifice to Baal. Any person who does not come will die." But Jehu tricked them. He wanted to destroy the worshippers of Baal.

**20** Jehu said, "Announce a holy assembly for Baal." So they announced it.

**21** Jehu sent messages through all Israel. All the worshippers of Baal came. Not one man stayed away. They went into the temple of Baal. The temple was full from one end to the other.

**22** Jehu said to the man in charge of the special clothes, "Bring out robes for all the worshippers of Baal." So the man brought out robes for them.

**23** Then Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab went into the temple of Baal. Jehu said to the worshippers of Baal, "Look around. Make sure that no servants of the LORD are here with you. Only the worshippers of Baal must be here."

**24** The worshippers went in to make sacrifices and burnt offerings. Jehu put 80 men outside. He told them, "I give these people to you. If a man lets one of them escape, that man will die in his place."

**25** When Jehu finished the burnt offering, he told the guards and the officers, "Go in and kill them. Do not let one person come out." So they killed the worshippers with their swords. The guards and the officers threw the bodies out. Then they went into the inner room of the temple of Baal.

**26** They brought the sacred stones out of the temple of Baal and burned them.

**27** They broke the sacred stone of Baal. They also destroyed the temple of Baal. They made the temple into a toilet, and it is a toilet to this day.

**28** Thus Jehu removed the worship of Baal from Israel.

**29** But Jehu did not stop the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin. He did not remove the gold calves at Bethel and at Dan.

**30** The LORD said to Jehu, "You did well. You did what is right in my sight. You did to the family of Ahab all that I wanted. Thus your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel for 4 generations."

**31** But Jehu was not careful to obey the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not stop the sins of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin.

**32** At that time the LORD started to make Israel smaller. Hazael defeated the Israelites in all the areas of Israel.

**33** He took the land east of the Jordan. He took all the land of Gilead, the land of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh. He took the land from Aroer by the Arnon River, through Gilead and Bashan.

**34** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Jehu did, and all his power.

**35** Jehu died, and the people buried him in Samaria. Then his son Jehoahaz became king after him.

**36** Jehu ruled over Israel in Samaria for 28 years.

## Chapter 11

**1** Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead. So she got up and killed all the royal family.

**2** But Jehosheba was the daughter of King Joram and the sister of Ahaziah. She took Joash son of Ahaziah away from the sons of the king who were about to die. She hid Joash and his nurse in a bedroom. Thus Athaliah did not find him, and he did not die.

**3** Joash stayed hidden with Jehosheba in the temple of the LORD for 6 years. During that time Athaliah ruled the land.

**4** In the 7th year, Jehoiada sent for the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, and the guards. He brought them to himself in the temple of the LORD. He made an agreement (covenant) with them. He made them make a promise in the temple of the LORD. Then he showed them the son of the king.

**5** Jehoiada told them, "This is what you must do. 1/3 of you who come on duty on the Sabbath will guard the palace of the king.

**6** 1/3 of you will be at the Sur Gate. 1/3 of you will be at the gate behind the guards. Thus you will guard the palace.

**7** The 2 groups of you who go off duty on the Sabbath will guard the temple of the LORD for the king.

**8** Stand all around the king. Each man must hold his weapons in his hand. Kill any person who comes near your lines. Stay with the king when he goes out and when he comes in."

**9** The commanders of hundreds did all that Jehoiada the priest told them. Each commander took his men who came on duty on the Sabbath and the men who went off duty on the Sabbath. They came to Jehoiada the priest.

**10** The priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and shields that were King David's. These weapons were in the temple of the LORD.

**11** The guards stood around the king, each man with his weapons in his hand. They stood from the south side of the temple to the north side of the temple, near the altar and the temple.

**12** Then Jehoiada brought out the son of the king. He put the crown on him and gave him a copy of the law. They made him king and anointed him. The people clapped their hands and shouted, "Long live the king!"

**13** Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people. She came to the people at the temple of the LORD.

**14** She looked and saw the king. He stood by the pillar, as was the custom. The commanders and the trumpeters stood by the king. All the people of the land were happy and blew trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and shouted, "Treason! Treason!"

**15** Jehoiada the priest gave orders to the commanders of hundreds, who were in charge of the army. He told them, "Take her out between your lines. Kill with the sword any person who follows her." The priest said this because he did not want them to kill her in the temple of the LORD.

**16** So they took hold of her. They took her through the horse entrance to the palace of the king. There they killed her.

**17** Then Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people. They agreed to be the people of the LORD. He also made an agreement between the king and the people.

**18** All the people of the land went to the temple of Baal and destroyed it. They broke the altars and the idols into pieces. They killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, in front of the altars. Then Jehoiada the priest put guards at the temple of the LORD.

**19** He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land. They brought the king down from the temple of the LORD. They went through the gate of the guards to the palace of the king. Then the king sat on the royal throne.

**20** All the people of the land were happy. The city was quiet, because they killed Athaliah with the sword at the palace of the king.

**21** Joash was 7 years old when he became king.

## Chapter 12

**1** Jehoash became king in the 7th year of Jehu. He ruled in Jerusalem for 40 years. His mother was Zibiah from Beersheba.

**2** Jehoash did what was right in the sight of the LORD during all the years that Jehoiada the priest taught him.

**3** But the people did not remove the high places of worship. The people continued to make sacrifices and burn incense at the high places.

**4** Jehoash said to the priests, "Collect all the money that people bring as holy gifts to the temple of the LORD. Collect the money from the census tax. Collect the money that people must pay for their vows. Collect the money that people give freely to the temple of the LORD.

**5** Let each priest take the money from the people that he knows. Then let the priests use the money to repair the temple where it has damage."

**6** But by the 23rd year of King Jehoash, the priests did not repair the temple.

**7** So King Jehoash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests. He asked them, "Why do you not repair the temple? From now on, do not take more money from the people that you know. Give the money to repair the temple."

**8** The priests agreed not to take more money from the people. They also agreed not to repair the temple themselves.

**9** Then Jehoiada the priest took a box and made a hole in its lid. He put it next to the altar, on the right side of the entrance of the temple of the LORD. The priests who guarded the door put into the box all the money that people brought to the temple of the LORD.

**10** When they saw that there was much money in the box, the secretary of the king and the high priest came. They counted the money that was in the temple of the LORD and put it in bags.

**11** Then they gave the counted money to the men who supervised the work on the temple of the LORD. These men paid the carpenters and the builders who worked on the temple of the LORD.

**12** They also paid the stone workers and the stone cutters. They bought wood and cut stone to repair the temple of the LORD. They paid for all the other costs of the repairs.

**13** But they did not use the money to make silver bowls, wick cutters, basins, or trumpets for the temple of the LORD. They did not make other objects of gold or silver with it.

**14** They gave the money to the workers, who used it to repair the temple of the LORD.

**15** They did not ask the supervisors to show how they used the money, because the supervisors were honest.

**16** The money from the guilt offerings and the sin offerings did not go to the temple of the LORD. That money was for the priests.

**17** At that time Hazael the king of Syria attacked Gath and captured it. Then Hazael decided to attack Jerusalem.

**18** Jehoash the king of Judah took all the holy objects that his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, the kings of Judah, gave to the LORD. He took his own holy objects too. He also took all the gold in the treasuries of the temple of the LORD and of the palace. He sent all of it to Hazael the king of Syria. Then Hazael went away from Jerusalem.

**19** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Joash did.

**20** His officers made a secret plan against him. They killed Joash at Beth-millo, on the road that goes down to Silla.

**21** His officers Jozachar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer attacked him, and he died. The people buried him with his ancestors in the City of David. Then his son Amaziah became king after him.

## Chapter 13

**1** Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel in Samaria in the 23rd year of Joash son of Ahaziah, the king of Judah. Jehoahaz ruled for 17 years.

**2** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He continued in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin. He did not stop these sins.

**3** So the LORD became angry with Israel. He gave the Israelites to Hazael the king of Syria and to Ben-hadad son of Hazael for a long time.

**4** Then Jehoahaz prayed to the LORD, and the LORD heard him. The LORD saw how the king of Syria made Israel suffer.

**5** So the LORD gave Israel a man who saved them. The Israelites became free from the power of the Syrians. They lived in their homes again, as before.

**6** But they did not stop the sins of the family of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin. They continued in these sins. The Asherah pole also stayed in Samaria.

**7** The army of Jehoahaz had only 50 horsemen, 10 chariots, and 10,000 foot soldiers. The king of Syria destroyed the others. He made them as dust that people beat on the grain floor.

**8** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Jehoahaz did, and his power.

**9** Jehoahaz died, and the people buried him in Samaria. Then his son Joash became king after him.

**10** Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king of Israel in Samaria in the 37th year of Joash, the king of Judah. Jehoash ruled for 16 years.

**11** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did not stop all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin. He continued in them.

**12** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Joash did. It tells about his power in the war against Amaziah the king of Judah.

**13** Joash died, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. The people buried Joash in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

**14** Elisha became sick with the sickness that caused his death. Joash the king of Israel went down to visit him. The king cried over him and said, "My father, my father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!"

**15** Elisha said to him, "Get a bow and some arrows." So the king got a bow and some arrows.

**16** Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow." So the king put his hand on the bow. Then Elisha put his hands on the hands of the king.

**17** Elisha said, "Open the east window." So the king opened it. Elisha said, "Shoot!" So the king shot. Elisha said, "That is the arrow of victory of the LORD. It is the arrow of victory over Syria. You will defeat the Syrians at Aphek completely."

**18** Elisha said, "Take the arrows." So the king took them. Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Hit the ground with them." The king hit the ground 3 times and stopped.

**19** The man of God was angry with him. He said, "You must hit the ground 5 or 6 times. Then you will defeat Syria completely. But now you will defeat Syria only 3 times."

**20** Elisha died, and the people buried him. Groups of Moabite soldiers attacked the land each spring.

**21** One time some men buried a man. Suddenly they saw a group of soldiers. So they threw the dead man into the tomb of Elisha. The body touched the bones of Elisha. Then the man became alive and stood up on his feet.

**22** Hazael the king of Syria made Israel suffer during all the rule of Jehoahaz.

**23** But the LORD was kind to the Israelites and had pity on them. He cared about them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He did not want to destroy them. He did not send them away from him at that time.

**24** Hazael the king of Syria died. Then his son Ben-hadad became king after him.

**25** Hazael took some cities from Jehoahaz in war. Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took these cities back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael. Jehoash defeated Ben-hadad 3 times. Thus he got back the cities of Israel.

## Chapter 14

**1** Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah in the 2nd year of Joash son of Jehoahaz, the king of Israel.

**2** Amaziah was 25 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 29 years. His mother was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.

**3** Amaziah did what was right in the sight of the LORD. But he was not as his ancestor David. He did all the things that his father Joash did.

**4** But the people did not remove the high places of worship. The people continued to make sacrifices and burn incense at the high places.

**5** When Amaziah had firm control of the kingdom, he killed the officers who killed his father the king.

**6** But he did not kill the sons of the murderers. He obeyed the book of the law of Moses. There the LORD commanded, "Do not kill fathers for the sins of their children. Do not kill children for the sins of their fathers. Each person must die for his own sin."

**7** Amaziah killed 10,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He captured the city of Sela in war. He gave it the name Joktheel, and it has that name to this day.

**8** Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, the king of Israel. He said, "Come, let us meet face to face in battle."

**9** But Jehoash the king of Israel sent this answer to Amaziah the king of Judah. He said, "A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon. It said, 'Give your daughter to my son as his wife.' Then a wild animal in Lebanon went by and walked on the thistle.

**10** You defeated Edom, and now you are proud. Be happy with your victory, but stay at home. Why do you cause trouble for yourself? You and Judah will both fall."

**11** But Amaziah did not listen. So Jehoash the king of Israel attacked. He and Amaziah the king of Judah met face to face in battle at Beth-shemesh in Judah.

**12** Israel defeated Judah. Each man of Judah ran away to his home.

**13** Jehoash the king of Israel captured Amaziah the king of Judah, son of Jehoash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. Then Jehoash went to Jerusalem. He broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate. That part of the wall was 400 cubits long.

**14** He took all the gold, the silver, and all the objects in the temple of the LORD and in the treasuries of the palace. He also took prisoners. Then he went back to Samaria.

**15** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Jehoash did, and his power. It tells about his war against Amaziah the king of Judah.

**16** Jehoash died, and the people buried him in Samaria with the kings of Israel. Then his son Jeroboam became king after him.

**17** Amaziah son of Joash, the king of Judah, lived 15 years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the king of Israel.

**18** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Amaziah did.

**19** Some people in Jerusalem made a secret plan against Amaziah. He ran away to Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish, and these men killed him there.

**20** They brought his body back on horses. The people buried him in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the City of David.

**21** Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was 16 years old. They made him king after his father Amaziah.

**22** After Amaziah died, Azariah built the town of Elath again. He gave it back to Judah.

**23** Jeroboam son of Joash became king of Israel in Samaria in the 15th year of Amaziah son of Joash, the king of Judah. Jeroboam ruled for 41 years.

**24** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did not stop all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

**25** Jeroboam took back the land of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Dead Sea. The LORD, the God of Israel, said that this will occur. He said it through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.

**26** The LORD saw that the Israelites suffered very much. There was no person to help Israel, slave or free.

**27** The LORD did not say that he will remove the name of Israel from the earth. So he saved them through Jeroboam son of Joash.

**28** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Jeroboam did, and his power. The book tells how he fought. It tells how he got back Damascus and Hamath for Israel. These cities were part of Judah before.

**29** Jeroboam died, and the people buried him with the kings of Israel. Then his son Zechariah became king after him.

## Chapter 15

**1** Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah in the 27th year of Jeroboam, the king of Israel.

**2** Azariah was 16 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 52 years. His mother was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.

**3** He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, as his father Amaziah did.

**4** But the people did not remove the high places of worship. The people continued to make sacrifices and burn incense at the high places.

**5** The LORD gave the king leprosy, and he had it until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house. Jotham, the son of the king, was in charge of the palace. Jotham governed the people of the land.

**6** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Azariah did.

**7** Azariah died, and the people buried him with his ancestors in the City of David. Then his son Jotham became king after him.

**8** Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Samaria in the 38th year of Azariah, the king of Judah. Zechariah ruled for 6 months.

**9** He did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his ancestors did. He did not stop the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

**10** Shallum son of Jabesh made a secret plan against Zechariah. He attacked him in front of the people and killed him. Then Shallum became king after him.

**11** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Zechariah did.

**12** Thus the word of the LORD to Jehu came true. The LORD told him, "Your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel for 4 generations." And that occurred.

**13** Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the 39th year of Uzziah, the king of Judah. Shallum ruled in Samaria for 1 month.

**14** Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah to Samaria. He attacked Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him. Then Menahem became king after him.

**15** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Shallum did, and his secret plan.

**16** At that time Menahem attacked Tiphsah and all the people in it. He also attacked the area around it, from Tirzah. He attacked the city because the people did not open the gates to him. He cut open all the pregnant women there.

**17** Menahem son of Gadi became king of Israel in the 39th year of Azariah, the king of Judah. Menahem ruled in Samaria for 10 years.

**18** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. During all his rule, he did not stop the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

**19** Pul the king of Assyria attacked the land. Menahem gave Pul 1,000 talents of silver. Menahem wanted Pul to help him keep firm control of the kingdom.

**20** Menahem got this money from Israel. He made each rich man pay 50 shekels of silver. He gave the money to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria went back and did not stay in the land.

**21** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Menahem did.

**22** Menahem died. Then his son Pekahiah became king after him.

**23** Pekahiah son of Menahem became king of Israel in Samaria in the 50th year of Azariah, the king of Judah. Pekahiah ruled for 2 years.

**24** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did not stop the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

**25** Pekah son of Remaliah, one of his officers, made a secret plan against him. Pekah took 50 men from Gilead with him. He attacked Pekahiah in the strong part of the palace in Samaria. He also killed Argob and Arieh. Thus Pekah killed Pekahiah and became king after him.

**26** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Pekahiah did.

**27** Pekah son of Remaliah became king of Israel in Samaria in the 52nd year of Azariah, the king of Judah. Pekah ruled for 20 years.

**28** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did not stop the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

**29** During the rule of Pekah the king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser the king of Assyria came. He captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee. He captured all the land of Naphtali. He took the people as prisoners to Assyria.

**30** Then Hoshea son of Elah made a secret plan against Pekah son of Remaliah. He attacked and killed Pekah. Then Hoshea became king after him. This occurred in the 20th year of Jotham son of Uzziah.

**31** The book of the history of the kings of Israel tells the other things that Pekah did.

**32** Jotham son of Uzziah became king of Judah in the 2nd year of Pekah son of Remaliah, the king of Israel.

**33** Jotham was 25 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 16 years. His mother was Jerusha, the daughter of Zadok.

**34** He did what was right in the sight of the LORD. He did all the things that his father Uzziah did.

**35** But the people did not remove the high places of worship. The people continued to make sacrifices and burn incense at the high places. Jotham built the Upper Gate of the temple of the LORD.

**36** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Jotham did.

**37** At that time the LORD started to send Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.

**38** Jotham died, and the people buried him with his ancestors in the City of David, his ancestor. Then his son Ahaz became king after him.

## Chapter 16

**1** Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the 17th year of Pekah son of Remaliah.

**2** Ahaz was 20 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 16 years. He did not do what was right in the sight of the LORD his God, as his ancestor David did.

**3** He lived as the kings of Israel lived. He even sacrificed his son in the fire. He did the terrible things of the nations that the LORD sent away from the Israelites.

**4** He made sacrifices and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.

**5** Then Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah, the king of Israel, came to attack Jerusalem. They surrounded Ahaz, but they could not defeat him.

**6** At that time Rezin the king of Syria got back Elath for Syria. He forced the people of Judah out of Elath. The Syrians came to Elath, and they live there to this day.

**7** Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser the king of Assyria. He said, "I am your servant and your son. Come and save me from the king of Syria and the king of Israel. They attack me."

**8** Ahaz took the silver and gold in the temple of the LORD and in the treasuries of the palace. He sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria.

**9** The king of Assyria agreed. He attacked Damascus and captured it. He took the people of Damascus as prisoners to Kir. He killed Rezin.

**10** King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser the king of Assyria. He saw an altar at Damascus. King Ahaz sent a plan of the altar to Urijah the priest. The plan showed all the details of how to make the altar.

**11** Urijah the priest built an altar as King Ahaz told him in the message from Damascus. Urijah finished it before King Ahaz came back from Damascus.

**12** The king came back from Damascus and saw the altar. He went near the altar and made offerings on it.

**13** He burned his burnt offering and his grain offering on the altar. He poured out his drink offering. He threw the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.

**14** The bronze altar of the LORD was in front of the temple, between the new altar and the temple of the LORD. Ahaz moved the bronze altar to the north side of the new altar.

**15** King Ahaz gave orders to Urijah the priest. He said, "On the large new altar, burn the morning burnt offering and the evening grain offering. Burn the burnt offering and grain offering of the king. Burn the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings of all the people of the land. Throw on it all the blood of the burnt offerings and of the sacrifices. But I will use the bronze altar to ask for guidance from God."

**16** Urijah the priest did all that King Ahaz told him.

**17** King Ahaz cut off the side panels of the stands. He removed the basins from them. He took down the large bronze water tank, called the Sea, from the bronze bulls under it. He put it on a stone base.

**18** He removed the covered area for the Sabbath that the people built at the temple. He also removed the outside entrance of the king from the temple of the LORD. He did these things to please the king of Assyria.

**19** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Ahaz did.

**20** Ahaz died, and the people buried him with his ancestors in the City of David. Then his son Hezekiah became king after him.

## Chapter 17

**1** Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in Samaria in the 12th year of Ahaz, the king of Judah. Hoshea ruled for 9 years.

**2** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. But he was not as bad as the kings of Israel before him.

**3** Shalmaneser the king of Assyria attacked Hoshea. Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.

**4** But the king of Assyria found that Hoshea made a secret plan against him. Hoshea sent messengers to So the king of Egypt. Hoshea also stopped the yearly payment to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria captured Hoshea and put him in prison.

**5** Then the king of Assyria attacked all the land. He went to Samaria and surrounded it for 3 years.

**6** In the 9th year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria. He took the Israelites as prisoners to Assyria. He put them in Halah, in Gozan on the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.

**7** This occurred because the Israelites sinned against the LORD their God. The LORD brought them out of the land of Egypt. He made them free from the power of Pharaoh the king of Egypt. But they worshipped other gods.

**8** They followed the customs of the nations that the LORD sent away from the Israelites. They also followed the customs that the kings of Israel started.

**9** The Israelites secretly did things that were wrong against the LORD their God. They built high places of worship in all their towns, from watchtowers to cities with walls.

**10** They put up sacred stones and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

**11** They burned incense at all the high places, as the nations did. The LORD sent those nations away from the Israelites. The Israelites did evil things and made the LORD angry.

**12** They worshipped idols. But the LORD told them, "Do not do this."

**13** The LORD warned Israel and Judah through all the prophets and seers. He said, "Turn away from your evil ways. Obey my commands and my laws. Obey all the law that I gave to your ancestors. I sent this law to you through my servants the prophets."

**14** But they did not listen. They were stubborn, as their ancestors were. Their ancestors did not trust the LORD their God.

**15** They rejected the laws of the LORD. They rejected the covenant that he made with their ancestors. They rejected his warnings. They worshipped idols that have no value, and they became people with no value. They followed the nations around them. But the LORD told them not to do as these nations did.

**16** They did not obey all the commands of the LORD their God. They made 2 metal idols in the shape of calves. They made an Asherah pole. They worshipped all the stars of the sky. They served Baal.

**17** They sacrificed their sons and daughters in the fire. They used magic and tried to know the future. They gave themselves completely to evil in the sight of the LORD. Thus they made the LORD angry.

**18** So the LORD was very angry with Israel. He removed them from his presence. Only the tribe of Judah remained.

**19** But Judah also did not obey the commands of the LORD their God. The people of Judah followed the customs that Israel started.

**20** So the LORD rejected all the descendants of Israel. He punished them. He gave them to enemies who took their possessions. At last he sent them away from his presence.

**21** The LORD took Israel away from the family of David. The Israelites made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. Jeroboam caused Israel to stop. They did not follow the LORD. He caused them to do a great sin.

**22** The Israelites continued in all the sins of Jeroboam. They did not stop these sins.

**23** At last the LORD removed Israel from his presence. He told all his servants the prophets that he will do this. So the Assyrians took the Israelites from their land to Assyria. They are there to this day.

**24** The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim. He put them in the cities of Samaria in place of the Israelites. These people took control of Samaria and lived in its cities.

**25** When they started to live there, they did not worship the LORD. So the LORD sent lions among them. The lions killed some of the people.

**26** Some men told the king of Assyria, "You took nations from their lands and put them in the cities of Samaria. These people do not know the laws of the god of that land. Thus the god sent lions among them. The lions kill the people, because the people do not know the laws of the god of the land."

**27** Then the king of Assyria gave this order: "Send back one of the priests that you took from Samaria. Let him go and live there. Let him teach the people the laws of the god of the land."

**28** So one of the priests whom they took from Samaria came and lived in Bethel. He taught the people how to worship the LORD.

**29** But each nation made its own gods. They put these gods in the temples on the high places that the people of Samaria made. Each nation did this in the cities where they lived.

**30** The men from Babylon made Succoth-benoth. The men from Cuth made Nergal. The men from Hamath made Ashima.

**31** The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak. The Sepharvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.

**32** These people worshipped the LORD. But they also chose all types of people from among themselves as priests of the high places. These priests made sacrifices for them in the temples on the high places.

**33** They worshipped the LORD, but they also served their own gods. They followed the customs of the nations from which the Assyrians took them.

**34** To this day they follow their old customs. They do not truly worship the LORD. They do not obey the laws, the rules, and the commands that the LORD gave to the descendants of Jacob. The LORD gave Jacob the name Israel.

**35** The LORD made a covenant with the Israelites. He commanded them, "Do not worship other gods. Do not bow down to them, serve them, or make sacrifices to them.

**36** Worship only the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt with great power and a strong arm. Bow down to him. Make sacrifices to him.

**37** Always obey the laws, the rules, and the commands that he wrote for you. Do not worship other gods.

**38** Do not forget the covenant that I made with you. Do not worship other gods.

**39** Worship the LORD your God. He will save you from all your enemies."

**40** But the people did not listen. They continued to follow their old customs.

**41** So these nations worshipped the LORD, but they also served their idols. Their children and their grandchildren continue to do as their ancestors did, to this day.

## Chapter 18

**1** Hezekiah son of Ahaz became king of Judah in the 3rd year of Hoshea son of Elah, the king of Israel.

**2** Hezekiah was 25 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 29 years. His mother was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.

**3** He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, as his ancestor David did.

**4** He removed the high places of worship. He broke the sacred stones and cut down the Asherah poles. He broke into pieces the bronze snake that Moses made. Until that time the Israelites burned incense to it. People called it Nehushtan.

**5** Hezekiah trusted the LORD, the God of Israel. There was no king of Judah as Hezekiah, before him or after him.

**6** He stayed loyal to the LORD. He did not stop. He continued to follow him. He obeyed the commands that the LORD gave to Moses.

**7** The LORD was with Hezekiah. Hezekiah was successful in all that he did. He started a rebellion against the king of Assyria and did not serve him.

**8** He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its area. He defeated them from the watchtowers to the cities with walls.

**9** In the 4th year of King Hezekiah, Shalmaneser the king of Assyria attacked Samaria and surrounded it. That was the 7th year of Hoshea son of Elah, the king of Israel.

**10** At the end of 3 years, the Assyrians captured Samaria. That was the 6th year of Hezekiah and the 9th year of Hoshea, the king of Israel.

**11** The king of Assyria took the Israelites as prisoners to Assyria. He put them in Halah, in Gozan on the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.

**12** This occurred because the Israelites did not obey the LORD their God. They broke his covenant. They did not obey all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded. They did not listen, and they did not obey.

**13** In the 14th year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib the king of Assyria attacked all the cities of Judah with walls. He captured them.

**14** Hezekiah the king of Judah sent a message to the king of Assyria at Lachish. He said, "I did wrong. Go away from me. I will pay all that you tell me to pay." The king of Assyria told Hezekiah the king of Judah to pay 300 talents of silver and 30 talents of gold.

**15** So Hezekiah gave him all the silver in the temple of the LORD and in the treasuries of the palace.

**16** At that time Hezekiah removed the gold from the doors and doorposts of the temple of the LORD. Hezekiah the king of Judah himself put that gold on them. He gave the gold to the king of Assyria.

**17** The king of Assyria sent Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rab-shakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah. They came to Jerusalem with a large army. They stopped at the water channel of the upper pool, on the road to the field where people wash clothes.

**18** They called for the king. Then 3 men came out to them. These men were Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the manager of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder.

**19** Rab-shakeh said to them, "Tell Hezekiah this: 'The great king, the king of Assyria, says this: Why do you feel so safe?

**20** You say that you have good plans and power for war. But your words are empty. On whom do you depend? Who gives you the courage to start a rebellion against me?

**21** Look, you depend on Egypt. Egypt is as a broken reed. If a man leans on it as a stick, it will cut his hand. Pharaoh the king of Egypt is as that reed to all who depend on him.

**22** Maybe you will tell me, "We depend on the LORD our God." But Hezekiah removed the high places and altars of the LORD. Hezekiah told Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship at this altar in Jerusalem."'

**23** Now make an agreement with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you 2,000 horses, if you can find riders for them.

**24** You cannot defeat even one officer, the smallest of the officers of my master. Why do you depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

**25** Also, I did not come to attack and destroy this place without the LORD. The LORD told me, 'Attack this land and destroy it.'"

**26** Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to Rab-shakeh, "Please speak to us, your servants, in the Aramaic language, because we understand it. Do not speak to us in the Hebrew language. The people on the wall can hear."

**27** But Rab-shakeh said to them, "My master did not send me to say these words only to your master and to you. He also sent me to the men who sit on the wall. They, as you, will eat their own dung and drink their own urine."

**28** Then Rab-shakeh stood and shouted in the Hebrew language, "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!

**29** The king says this: 'Do not let Hezekiah trick you. He cannot save you from my power.

**30** Do not let Hezekiah make you trust the LORD. He says, "The LORD will surely save us. The king of Assyria will not capture this city."

**31** Do not listen to Hezekiah.' The king of Assyria says this: 'Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree. Each of you will drink water from his own well.

**32** Then I will come and take you away to a land as your land. It is a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards. It is a land of olive oil and honey. Thus you will live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah. He tries to trick you when he says, "The LORD will save us."

**33** The gods of the other nations did not save their lands from the king of Assyria.

**34** Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Did they save Samaria from me?

**35** Not one of the gods of these countries saved its country from me. So how can the LORD save Jerusalem from me?'"

**36** But the people were silent. They did not answer him with one word, because the king commanded, "Do not answer him."

**37** Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the manager of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went to Hezekiah. Their clothes had tears in them. They told him the words of Rab-shakeh.

## Chapter 19

**1** King Hezekiah heard their report. He tore his clothes and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the LORD.

**2** He sent Eliakim the manager of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests to Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz. All these men wore sackcloth.

**3** They said to Isaiah, "Hezekiah says this: 'Today is a day of trouble, of punishment, and of shame. We are as a woman who is ready to give birth, but she does not have the strength to give birth.

**4** Possibly the LORD your God will hear all the words of Rab-shakeh. His master the king of Assyria sent him to insult the God who lives. Possibly the LORD your God will punish him for the words that the LORD heard. Thus pray for the people who remain alive.'"

**5** So the officers of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

**6** Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master this: 'The LORD says this: Do not be afraid of the words that you heard. The officers of the king of Assyria insulted me with these words.

**7** Listen. I will put a spirit in him. He will hear a report and go back to his own land. There I will make him die by the sword.'"

**8** Rab-shakeh went back. He heard that the king of Assyria left Lachish. He found the king at war against Libnah.

**9** Then the king of Assyria heard news about Tirhakah the king of Ethiopia. The news was, "He comes to fight against you." So the king of Assyria sent messengers again to Hezekiah. He told them,

**10** "Tell Hezekiah the king of Judah this: 'You trust your God. Do not let him trick you when he says, "The king of Assyria will not capture Jerusalem."

**11** You heard what the kings of Assyria did to all the other lands. They destroyed them completely. Do you think that you will escape?

**12** My ancestors destroyed Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar. Did the gods of those nations save them?

**13** Where is the king of Hamath? Where is the king of Arpad? Where are the kings of the cities of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?'"

**14** Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the temple of the LORD. He spread the letter open in front of the LORD.

**15** Hezekiah prayed to the LORD. He said, "LORD, God of Israel, you sit on your throne above the cherubim. You alone are God of all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.

**16** LORD, listen and hear. LORD, open your eyes and see. Hear the words that Sennacherib sent to insult the God who lives.

**17** LORD, it is true that the kings of Assyria destroyed the nations and their lands.

**18** They threw the gods of these nations into the fire. But they were not gods. They were only wood and stone that men made with their hands. Thus the Assyrians destroyed them.

**19** Now, LORD our God, please save us from his power. Then all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you alone, LORD, are God."

**20** Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah. He said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: 'I heard your prayer about Sennacherib the king of Assyria.'

**21** This is the word that the LORD says against Sennacherib: 'The young woman, the city of Zion, hates you and laughs at you. The city of Jerusalem shakes her head at you as you run away.

**22** Whom did you insult? Against whom did you speak bad words? Against whom did you shout and look up proudly? You did these things against the Holy One of Israel!

**23** You used your messengers to insult the Lord. You said, "With my many chariots I went up to the tops of the mountains, to the highest parts of Lebanon. I cut down its tall cedar trees and its best pine trees. I went into its farthest places and its best forests.

**24** I dug wells in foreign lands and drank their water. I walked through the rivers of the cities that I attacked, and the rivers became dry."

**25** Did you not hear? Long ago I decided this. In ancient times I planned it. Now I make it occur. I let you change cities with walls into piles of broken stones.

**26** Thus the people of those cities had no power. They were afraid and ashamed. They were as grass and green plants in the field. They were as grass on the roof that dries up before it grows.

**27** But I know where you stay, and when you go out and come in. I know how angry you are against me.

**28** You are angry against me, and I heard your proud words. Thus I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth. I will make you go back on the road by which you came.'

**29** Hezekiah, this will be a sign for you. This year you will eat the grain that grows by itself. Next year you will eat what grows from that grain. But in the 3rd year, plant seeds and cut the crops. Plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

**30** The people of Judah who escape and remain will grow strong again. They will be as a plant that puts its roots down and produces fruit above.

**31** Some people will remain in Jerusalem. Some people will escape from Mount Zion. The strong love of the LORD of armies will do this.

**32** Thus the LORD says this about the king of Assyria: 'He will not come into this city. He will not shoot an arrow here. He will not come near it with a shield. He will not build a ramp of earth against its walls.

**33** He will go back on the road by which he came. He will not come into this city,' says the LORD.

**34** 'I will protect this city and save it. I will do this for myself and for my servant David.'"

**35** That night the angel of the LORD went out and killed 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up early in the morning, they saw all the dead bodies.

**36** So Sennacherib the king of Assyria left. He went back home and stayed in Nineveh.

**37** One day he worshipped in the temple of his god Nisroch. His sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword. Then they escaped to the land of Armenia. His son Esarhaddon became king after him.

## Chapter 20

**1** At that time Hezekiah became sick and was about to die. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him. Isaiah said, "The LORD says this: 'Put your household in order, because you will die. You will not become well.'"

**2** Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD. He said,

**3** "LORD, please remember how I served you faithfully with all my heart. I did what is good in your sight." Then Hezekiah cried loudly.

**4** Isaiah left. But before he went out of the middle courtyard, the LORD spoke to him. The LORD said,

**5** "Go back and tell Hezekiah, the ruler of my people, this: 'The LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says this: I heard your prayer. I saw your tears. I will make you well. On the 3rd day you will go up to the temple of the LORD.

**6** I will add 15 years to your life. I will save you and this city from the king of Assyria. I will protect this city for myself and for my servant David.'"

**7** Isaiah said, "Get a mass of pressed figs." They got it and put it on the boil. Then Hezekiah became well.

**8** Hezekiah asked Isaiah, "What will be the sign that the LORD will make me well? What will show that I will go up to the temple of the LORD on the 3rd day?"

**9** Isaiah said, "This is the sign from the LORD. It will show that the LORD will do what he said. Do you want the shadow to go forward 10 steps or back 10 steps?"

**10** Hezekiah answered, "It is easy for the shadow to go forward 10 steps. No, let the shadow go back 10 steps."

**11** Isaiah the prophet called to the LORD. Then the LORD made the shadow go back 10 steps on the stairway of Ahaz.

**12** At that time Berodach-baladan son of Baladan, the king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah. He heard that Hezekiah was sick.

**13** Hezekiah welcomed the messengers. He showed them all his storehouse of valuable things. He showed them the silver, the gold, the spices, and the expensive oil. He showed them his armory and all that was in his treasuries. Hezekiah showed them all the things in his palace and in all his kingdom.

**14** Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah. He asked him, "What did these men say? Where did they come from?" Hezekiah said, "They came from a far country, from Babylon."

**15** Isaiah asked, "What did they see in your palace?" Hezekiah answered, "They saw all the things in my palace. I showed them all my treasures."

**16** Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD.

**17** 'A time will come when people will take all the things in your palace to Babylon. They will also take all the things that your ancestors stored until this day. Nothing will remain,' says the LORD.

**18** 'They will take away some of your own descendants. These men will become palace officials in the palace of the king of Babylon.'"

**19** Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you spoke is good." He thought, "Peace and safety will continue during my life. So that is good."

**20** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Hezekiah did, and all his power. The book tells how he made the pool and the tunnel that brought water into the city.

**21** Hezekiah died. Then his son Manasseh became king after him.

## Chapter 21

**1** Manasseh was 12 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 55 years. His mother was Hephzibah.

**2** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did the terrible things of the nations that the LORD sent away from the Israelites.

**3** He built again the high places of worship that his father Hezekiah destroyed. He built altars for Baal and made an Asherah pole, as Ahab the king of Israel did. He bowed down to all the stars of the sky and served them.

**4** He built altars in the temple of the LORD. About this temple the LORD said, "I will put my name in Jerusalem."

**5** In the 2 courtyards of the temple of the LORD, he built altars for all the stars of the sky.

**6** He sacrificed his son in the fire. He tried to know the future and used magic. He asked mediums and spiritists for advice. He did much evil in the sight of the LORD and made him angry.

**7** Manasseh made a carved Asherah pole and put it in the temple. About this temple the LORD said to David and to his son Solomon, "I chose Jerusalem from all the tribes of Israel. I will put my name in this temple and in Jerusalem for all time.

**8** I will not make the Israelites leave the land that I gave to their ancestors again. But they must be careful to do all that I commanded them. They must obey all the law that my servant Moses gave them."

**9** But the people did not listen. Manasseh caused them to do more evil than the nations did. The LORD destroyed those nations in front of the Israelites.

**10** The LORD spoke through his servants the prophets. He said,

**11** "Manasseh the king of Judah did these terrible things. He did more evil than the Amorites who lived here before him. He also caused Judah to sin with his idols.

**12** Thus the LORD, the God of Israel, says this: 'I will bring such disaster on Jerusalem and Judah. The ears of all who hear about it will ring.

**13** I will measure Jerusalem with the line that I used for Samaria. I will use the plumb line that I used for the family of Ahab. I will clean Jerusalem as a man cleans a dish. He cleans it and turns it upside down.

**14** I will leave the people of mine who remain. I will give them to their enemies. All their enemies will take them and their possessions.

**15** I will do this because they did evil in my sight. They made me angry from the day that their ancestors came out of Egypt until this day.'"

**16** Manasseh also killed very many innocent people. Their blood filled Jerusalem from one end to the other. He did this in addition to the sin that he caused Judah to do. He caused them to do evil in the sight of the LORD.

**17** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Manasseh did, and the sin that he did.

**18** Manasseh died, and the people buried him in the garden of his palace, the garden of Uzza. Then his son Amon became king after him.

**19** Amon was 22 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 2 years. His mother was Meshullemeth, the daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.

**20** Amon did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh did.

**21** He lived as his father lived. He served the idols that his father served, and he bowed down to them.

**22** He left the LORD, the God of his ancestors. He did not follow the way of the LORD.

**23** The officers of Amon made a secret plan against him. They killed the king in his palace.

**24** Then the people of the land killed all the men who made the plan against King Amon. The people of the land made his son Josiah king after him.

**25** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Amon did.

**26** The people buried Amon in his tomb in the garden of Uzza. Then his son Josiah became king after him.

## Chapter 22

**1** Josiah was 8 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 31 years. His mother was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath.

**2** He did what was right in the sight of the LORD. He lived as his ancestor David lived. He did not turn away from the right way.

**3** In the 18th year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan the secretary to the temple of the LORD. Shaphan was the son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam. The king said,

**4** "Go to Hilkiah the high priest. Tell him to count the money that people brought to the temple of the LORD. The gatekeepers collected this money from the people.

**5** Let the priests give the money to the men who supervise the work on the temple of the LORD. Let these men pay the workers who repair the temple of the LORD.

**6** Let them pay the carpenters, the builders, and the stone workers. Let them also buy wood and cut stone to repair the temple."

**7** But they did not ask the supervisors to show how they used the money, because the supervisors were honest.

**8** Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the secretary, "I found the book of the law in the temple of the LORD." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and Shaphan read it.

**9** Then Shaphan the secretary went to the king and gave him this report: "Your officers took the money that was in the temple. They gave it to the men who supervise the work on the temple of the LORD."

**10** Shaphan the secretary also told the king, "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." Then Shaphan read it to the king.

**11** The king heard the words of the book of the law. Then he tore his clothes.

**12** The king gave orders to Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Achbor son of Micaiah. He also gave orders to Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah, the servant of the king. He said,

**13** "Go and ask the LORD for me, for the people, and for all Judah. Ask about the words of this book that we found. The LORD is very angry with us. Our ancestors did not obey the words of this book. They did not do all that this book tells us to do."

**14** So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess. She was the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas. Shallum was in charge of the clothes. Huldah lived in the Second District of Jerusalem. The men spoke with her.

**15** She said to them, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: 'Tell the man who sent you to me,

**16** The LORD says this: I will bring disaster on this place and on its people. I will do all the things that the book says. The king of Judah read that book.

**17** The people left me. They burned incense to other gods. They made me angry with all the idols that they made. Thus my anger will burn against this place, and it will not stop.'

**18** The king of Judah sent you to ask the LORD. Tell him this: 'The LORD, the God of Israel, says this about the words that you heard:

**19** I said that this place and its people will become empty and cursed. When you heard this, your heart was sad, and you made yourself humble in front of the LORD. You tore your clothes and cried in front of me. Thus I heard you, says the LORD.

**20** So I will let you die and go to your ancestors. You will go to your grave in peace. Your eyes will not see all the disaster that I will bring on this place.'" Then the men took her answer back to the king.

## Chapter 23

**1** The king sent messengers, and they gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem to him.

**2** The king went up to the temple of the LORD. All the men of Judah and all the people of Jerusalem went with him. The priests, the prophets, and all the people, unimportant and important, went with him. He read to them all the words of the book of the covenant. The priest found this book in the temple of the LORD.

**3** The king stood by the pillar. He made a covenant in front of the LORD. He promised to follow the LORD and to obey his commands, his rules, and his laws with all his heart and soul. He promised to do the words of the covenant that this book contains. All the people agreed to the covenant.

**4** The king gave orders to Hilkiah the high priest, the priests of the second rank, and the gatekeepers. He told them to remove all the objects for Baal, for Asherah, and for all the stars of the sky. They removed these objects from the temple of the LORD.
