He burned these objects outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron Valley. He took their ashes to Bethel.

**5** The kings of Judah chose pagan priests to burn incense at the high places in the towns of Judah and around Jerusalem. Josiah removed these priests. He also removed the priests who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, and to the moon. They also burned incense to the planets and to all the stars of the sky.

**6** He took the Asherah pole from the temple of the LORD to the Kidron Valley outside Jerusalem. He burned it there and crushed it into powder. He threw the powder on the graves of the common people.

**7** He destroyed the rooms of the male temple prostitutes. These rooms were at the temple of the LORD. In these rooms women made woven cloth for Asherah.

**8** Josiah brought all the priests from the towns of Judah. He made the high places unclean where the priests burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba. He destroyed the high places at the gates. One was at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the governor of the city. It was on the left side of the city gate.

**9** The priests of the high places did not serve at the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem. But they ate bread without yeast with the other priests.

**10** Josiah made Topheth in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom unclean. He did this so that no person could sacrifice his son or daughter in the fire to Molech.

**11** He removed the horses that the kings of Judah gave to the sun. These horses were at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, near the room of Nathan-melech the official. This room was in the courtyard. Josiah burned the chariots of the sun.

**12** The kings of Judah made altars on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz. Manasseh made altars in the 2 courtyards of the temple of the LORD. The king broke all these altars. He removed them and threw their dust into the Kidron Valley.

**13** Solomon the king of Israel built high places east of Jerusalem, on the south side of the Hill of Corruption. He built them for Ashtoreth, the hateful goddess of the Sidonians. He built them for Chemosh, the hateful god of the Moabites, and for Milcom, the hateful god of the Ammonites. King Josiah made these high places unclean.

**14** He broke the sacred stones into pieces and cut down the Asherah poles. He filled their places with human bones.

**15** Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, made the altar and the high place at Bethel. Josiah broke down that altar and that high place. He burned the high place and crushed it into powder. He also burned the Asherah pole.

**16** Then Josiah turned around and saw the tombs on the hill. He sent men to take the bones out of the tombs. He burned the bones on the altar to make it unclean. This occurred as the LORD said. The man of God announced these things long before.

**17** Josiah asked, "What is that monument that I see?" The men of the city told him, "That is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah. He announced these things that you did against the altar of Bethel."

**18** Josiah said, "Let it be. Do not let a person move his bones." So they did not move his bones or the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.

**19** The kings of Israel built temples on the high places in the towns of Samaria. These temples made the LORD angry. Josiah removed all of them. He did to them all the things that he did at Bethel.

**20** He killed all the priests of the high places on the altars there. He burned human bones on the altars. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

**21** The king gave an order to all the people. He said, "Celebrate the Passover to the LORD your God, as this book of the covenant tells you."

**22** The people did not celebrate a Passover as this one since the time of the judges who led Israel. They did not celebrate one as this during all the time of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.

**23** In the 18th year of King Josiah, the people celebrated this Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem.

**24** Josiah also removed the mediums, the spiritists, the household gods, the idols, and all the other terrible things in Judah and Jerusalem. He did this to obey the words of the law. These words were in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the temple of the LORD.

**25** There was no king before Josiah who turned to the LORD as he did. He turned to the LORD with all his heart, all his soul, and all his strength. He obeyed all the law of Moses. After him, there was no king as Josiah.

**26** But the LORD did not stop his great anger against Judah. He was angry because of all the things that Manasseh did to make him angry.

**27** The LORD said, "I will remove Judah from my presence, as I removed Israel. I will reject this city Jerusalem, which I chose. I will reject the temple about which I said, 'My name will be there.'"

**28** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Josiah did.

**29** During the rule of Josiah, Pharaoh Neco the king of Egypt went to the Euphrates River to meet the king of Assyria. King Josiah went to fight against Neco. When Neco saw Josiah at Megiddo, Neco killed him.

**30** The officers of Josiah carried his body in a chariot from Megiddo to Jerusalem. They buried him in his own tomb. Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah. They anointed him and made him king after his father.

**31** Jehoahaz was 23 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 3 months. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

**32** He did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his ancestors did.

**33** Pharaoh Neco put him in chains at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Jehoahaz could not rule in Jerusalem. Neco made Judah pay a tax of 100 talents of silver and 1 talent of gold.

**34** Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king after his father Josiah. Neco changed the name of Eliakim to Jehoiakim. Neco took Jehoahaz to Egypt, and Jehoahaz died there.

**35** Jehoiakim paid the silver and the gold to Pharaoh. But he taxed the land to get the money that Pharaoh demanded. He made each person pay silver and gold as he decided. He gave it to Pharaoh Neco.

**36** Jehoiakim was 25 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 11 years. His mother was Zebidah, the daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.

**37** He did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his ancestors did.

## Chapter 24

**1** During the rule of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon attacked Judah. Jehoiakim became his servant for 3 years. Then Jehoiakim changed his mind and started a rebellion against him.

**2** The LORD sent groups of soldiers against Jehoiakim. These groups came from the Chaldeans, the Syrians, the Moabites, and the Ammonites. The LORD sent them to destroy Judah. This occurred as the LORD said through his servants the prophets.

**3** These things occurred to Judah because the LORD commanded them. He wanted to remove the people of Judah from his presence because of the sins of Manasseh. He punished them for all that Manasseh did.

**4** The LORD also punished them for the innocent blood that Manasseh shed. Manasseh filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. The LORD did not want to forgive this.

**5** The book of the history of the kings of Judah tells the other things that Jehoiakim did.

**6** Jehoiakim died. Then his son Jehoiachin became king after him.

**7** The king of Egypt did not go out from his land again. The king of Babylon took all the land of the king of Egypt, from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River.

**8** Jehoiachin was 18 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 3 months. His mother was Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.

**9** He did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father did.

**10** At that time the officers of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon attacked Jerusalem. They surrounded the city.

**11** Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon came to the city while his officers surrounded it.

**12** Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon. His mother, his servants, his commanders, and his officials went with him. The king of Babylon captured Jehoiachin. This occurred in the 8th year of the rule of the king of Babylon.

**13** Nebuchadnezzar took all the treasures from the temple of the LORD and from the palace. He cut into pieces all the gold objects that Solomon the king of Israel made for the temple of the LORD. This occurred as the LORD said.

**14** He took all the people of Jerusalem as prisoners. He took all the commanders and all the strong soldiers, 10,000 prisoners in total. He also took all the skilled workers and metal workers. Only the poorest people of the land remained.

**15** He took Jehoiachin as a prisoner to Babylon. He also took the mother of the king, the wives of the king, his officials, and the important men of the land. He took them all from Jerusalem to Babylon.

**16** The king of Babylon also took to Babylon all 7,000 strong soldiers and 1,000 skilled workers and metal workers. All of them were strong and could fight in war.

**17** The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, the uncle of Jehoiachin, king in his place. He changed the name of Mattaniah to Zedekiah.

**18** Zedekiah was 21 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 11 years. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

**19** He did evil in the sight of the LORD, as Jehoiakim did.

**20** These things occurred in Jerusalem and Judah because the LORD was angry with the people. At last he sent them away from his presence. Then Zedekiah started a rebellion against the king of Babylon.

## Chapter 25

**1** In the 9th year of the rule of Zedekiah, on the 10th day of the 10th month, Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon attacked Jerusalem. He came with all his army and made a camp near the city. They built siege walls all around it.

**2** The army surrounded the city until the 11th year of King Zedekiah.

**3** By the 9th day of the 4th month, the famine in the city was very bad. The people of the land had no food.

**4** Then the enemy broke through the city wall. All the soldiers ran away at night. They went through the gate between the 2 walls near the garden of the king. The Chaldeans were all around the city. The king went toward the Jordan Valley.

**5** But the army of the Chaldeans followed the king. They caught him in the plains of Jericho. All his army went away from him in different directions.

**6** The Chaldeans captured the king. They brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah. There the king of Babylon decided his punishment.

**7** They killed the sons of Zedekiah while Zedekiah watched. Then they made Zedekiah blind. They tied him with bronze chains and took him to Babylon.

**8** On the 7th day of the 5th month, Nebuzaradan came to Jerusalem. That was the 19th year of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon. Nebuzaradan was the commander of the guard and an officer of the king of Babylon.

**9** He burned the temple of the LORD, the palace of the king, and all the houses of Jerusalem. He burned every important building.

**10** All the army of the Chaldeans with the commander of the guard broke down the walls around Jerusalem.

**11** Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard took the people who remained in the city as prisoners. He also took the people who went over to the side of the king of Babylon. He took the rest of the people too.

**12** But the commander of the guard let some of the poorest people of the land stay. He made them work in the vineyards and the fields.

**13** The Chaldeans broke into pieces the bronze pillars of the temple of the LORD. They also broke the stands and the large bronze water tank, called the Sea, in the temple of the LORD. They took the bronze to Babylon.

**14** They also took the pots, the shovels, the wick cutters, the spoons, and all the bronze objects that the priests used in the temple.

**15** The commander of the guard took the fire pans and the bowls. He took all the objects made of pure gold or pure silver.

**16** Solomon made the 2 pillars, the Sea, and the stands for the temple of the LORD. The bronze of all these objects was too heavy to weigh.

**17** Each pillar was 18 cubits high. The bronze top on each pillar was 3 cubits high. A network of bronze chains and bronze pomegranates went around each top. The second pillar was the same as the first, with its network.

**18** The commander of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the 3 gatekeepers as prisoners.

**19** From the city he took the officer in charge of the soldiers and 5 advisers of the king. He also took the secretary of the army commander, who gathered the people of the land for the army. He took 60 men of the people of the land who were in the city.

**20** Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard took all these men. He brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

**21** The king of Babylon killed them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus the Babylonians took the people of Judah away from their land as prisoners.

**22** Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon let some people stay in the land of Judah. He made Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, the governor over them.

**23** All the army commanders and their men heard that the king of Babylon made Gedaliah governor. So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. These men were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite. Their men came with them.

**24** Gedaliah made a promise to them and their men. He told them, "Do not be afraid of the officials of the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon. Then things will go well for you."

**25** But in the 7th month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, came with 10 men. Ishmael was from the royal family. They attacked and killed Gedaliah. They also killed the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

**26** Then all the people, unimportant and important, and the army commanders got up and went to Egypt. They were afraid of the Chaldeans.

**27** In the 37th year after the Babylonians took Jehoiachin the king of Judah as a prisoner, Evil-merodach became king of Babylon. On the 27th day of the 12th month of that year, he let Jehoiachin the king of Judah out of prison.

**28** He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin. He gave him a seat of more honor than the seats of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

**29** So Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes. For the rest of his life, he ate regularly at the table of the king.

**30** Each day the king gave Jehoiachin the things that he needed, for the rest of his life.

# 1 Chronicles

## Chapter 1

**1** Adam, Sheth, Enosh,

**2** Kenan, Mahalaleel, Jered,

**3** Henoch, Methuselah, Lamech,

**4** Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

**5** The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

**6** The sons of Gomer were Ashchenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

**7** The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

**8** The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

**9** The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabtecha. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.

**10** Cush became the father of Nimrod. Nimrod became a strong man on the earth.

**11** Mizraim became the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,

**12** Pathrusim, Casluhim, and Caphthorim. The Philistines came from Casluhim.

**13** Canaan became the father of Zidon, his first son, and of Heth.

**14** He was also the father of the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,

**15** the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,

**16** the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.

**17** The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.

**18** Arphaxad became the father of Shelah. Shelah became the father of Eber.

**19** Eber had 2 sons. The name of one son was Peleg, because in his time the people of the earth became divided. The name of his brother was Joktan.

**20** Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

**21** Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

**22** Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,

**23** Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these men were the sons of Joktan.

**24** Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,

**25** Eber, Peleg, Reu,

**26** Serug, Nahor, Terah,

**27** and Abram. Abram is Abraham.

**28** The sons of Abraham were Isaac and Ishmael.

**29** These are their descendants. The first son of Ishmael was Nebaioth. Then came Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

**30** Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,

**31** Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were the sons of Ishmael.

**32** Keturah was a secondary wife (concubine) of Abraham. Her sons were Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan were Sheba and Dedan.

**33** The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Henoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the descendants of Keturah.

**34** Abraham became the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac were Esau and Israel.

**35** The sons of Esau were Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jaalam, and Korah.

**36** The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.

**37** The sons of Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

**38** The sons of Seir were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.

**39** The sons of Lotan were Hori and Homam. Timna was the sister of Lotan.

**40** The sons of Shobal were Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Zibeon were Aiah and Anah.

**41** The son of Anah was Dishon. The sons of Dishon were Amram, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.

**42** The sons of Ezer were Bilhan, Zavan, and Jakan. The sons of Dishan were Uz and Aran.

**43** These are the kings who ruled in the land of Edom before a king ruled over the people of Israel. Bela the son of Beor was king. The name of his city was Dinhabah.

**44** When Bela died, Jobab the son of Zerah from Bozrah became king after him.

**45** When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites became king after him.

**46** When Husham died, Hadad the son of Bedad became king after him. Hadad defeated Midian in the country of Moab. The name of his city was Avith.

**47** When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah became king after him.

**48** When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth by the river became king after him.

**49** When Shaul died, Baal-hanan the son of Achbor became king after him.

**50** When Baal-hanan died, Hadad became king after him. The name of his city was Pai. The name of his wife was Mehetabel. She was the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.

**51** Then Hadad died. The chiefs of Edom were chief Timnah, chief Aliah, chief Jetheth,

**52** chief Aholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

**53** chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

**54** chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.

## Chapter 2

**1** These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,

**2** Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

**3** The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, and Shelah. The mother of these 3 sons was the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite woman. Er, the first son of Judah, was evil in the sight of the LORD. Thus the LORD killed him.

**4** Tamar, the daughter-in-law of Judah, gave birth to Pharez and Zerah for him. Judah had 5 sons in total.

**5** The sons of Pharez were Hezron and Hamul.

**6** The sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara. They were 5 in total.

**7** The son of Carmi was Achar. Achar brought trouble on Israel because he took things that God told the people to destroy.

**8** The son of Ethan was Azariah.

**9** The sons of Hezron were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.

**10** Ram became the father of Amminadab. Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, the leader of the people of Judah.

**11** Nahshon became the father of Salma. Salma became the father of Boaz.

**12** Boaz became the father of Obed. Obed became the father of Jesse.

**13** Jesse became the father of Eliab, his first son. His second son was Abinadab, and his third son was Shimma.

**14** His fourth son was Nethaneel, and his fifth son was Raddai.

**15** His sixth son was Ozem, and his seventh son was David.

**16** Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The 3 sons of Zeruiah were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.

**17** Abigail gave birth to Amasa. The father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmeelite.

**18** Caleb the son of Hezron had children by Azubah his wife and by Jerioth. The sons of Azubah were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.

**19** When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath. She gave birth to Hur for him.

**20** Hur became the father of Uri. Uri became the father of Bezaleel.

**21** Later, Hezron married the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead. Hezron was 60 years old when he married her. She gave birth to Segub for him.

**22** Segub became the father of Jair. Jair had 23 cities in the land of Gilead.

**23** But Geshur and Aram took the towns of Jair from them. They also took Kenath and its towns, a total of 60 cities. All these cities belonged to the descendants of Machir, the father of Gilead.

**24** Hezron died in Caleb-ephratah. After his death, Abiah the wife of Hezron gave birth to Ashur for him. Ashur was the father of Tekoa.

**25** The sons of Jerahmeel, the first son of Hezron, were Ram, his first son, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.

**26** Jerahmeel also had another wife. Her name was Atarah. She was the mother of Onam.

**27** The sons of Ram, the first son of Jerahmeel, were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.

**28** The sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai were Nadab and Abishur.

**29** The name of the wife of Abishur was Abihail. She gave birth to Ahban and Molid for him.

**30** Nadab had 2 sons, Seled and Appaim. Seled died and had no children.

**31** The son of Appaim was Ishi. The son of Ishi was Sheshan. The son of Sheshan was Ahlai.

**32** The sons of Jada, the brother of Shammai, were Jether and Jonathan. Jether died and had no children.

**33** The sons of Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza. These were the descendants of Jerahmeel.

**34** Sheshan had no sons. He had only daughters. Sheshan had an Egyptian servant. The name of the servant was Jarha.

**35** Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant as a wife. She gave birth to Attai for him.

**36** Attai became the father of Nathan. Nathan became the father of Zabad.

**37** Zabad became the father of Ephlal. Ephlal became the father of Obed.

**38** Obed became the father of Jehu. Jehu became the father of Azariah.

**39** Azariah became the father of Helez. Helez became the father of Eleasah.

**40** Eleasah became the father of Sisamai. Sisamai became the father of Shallum.

**41** Shallum became the father of Jekamiah. Jekamiah became the father of Elishama.

**42** The sons of Caleb, the brother of Jerahmeel, included Mesha, his first son. Mesha was the father of Ziph. The sons of Caleb also included the sons of Mareshah, the father of Hebron.

**43** The sons of Hebron were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.

**44** Shema became the father of Raham, the father of Jorkoam. Rekem became the father of Shammai.

**45** The son of Shammai was Maon. Maon was the father of Beth-zur.

**46** Ephah, a concubine of Caleb, gave birth to Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran became the father of Gazez.

**47** The sons of Jahdai were Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.

**48** Maachah, a concubine of Caleb, gave birth to Sheber and Tirhanah.

**49** She also gave birth to Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea. The daughter of Caleb was Achsah.

**50** These were the descendants of Caleb. The sons of Hur, the first son of Ephratah, were Shobal the father of Kirjath-jearim,

**51** Salma the father of Beth-lehem, and Hareph the father of Beth-gader.

**52** Shobal the father of Kirjath-jearim had sons. They were Haroeh and half of the Manahethites.

**53** The families of Kirjath-jearim were the Ithrites, the Puhites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The Zareathites and the Eshtaulites came from these families.

**54** The descendants of Salma were Beth-lehem, the Netophathites, Ataroth of the family of Joab, half of the Manahethites, and the Zorites.

**55** The families of the scribes who lived at Jabez were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Suchathites. These were the Kenites who came from Hemath, the father of the family of Rechab.

## Chapter 3

**1** These were the sons of David that his wives gave birth to in Hebron. The first son was Amnon. His mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel. The second son was Daniel. His mother was Abigail from Carmel.

**2** The third son was Absalom. His mother was Maachah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur. The fourth son was Adonijah. His mother was Haggith.

**3** The fifth son was Shephatiah. His mother was Abital. The sixth son was Ithream. His mother was Eglah, the wife of David.

**4** David had these 6 sons in Hebron. David ruled there for 7 years and 6 months. He ruled in Jerusalem for 33 years.

**5** David had these sons in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon. These 4 sons were the sons of Bath-shua the daughter of Ammiel.

**6** There were also Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,

**7** Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,

**8** Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. These were 9 sons.

**9** All these were the sons of David. David also had sons from his concubines. Tamar was the sister of these sons.

**10** The son of Solomon was Rehoboam. The son of Rehoboam was Abia. The son of Abia was Asa. The son of Asa was Jehoshaphat.

**11** The son of Jehoshaphat was Joram. The son of Joram was Ahaziah. The son of Ahaziah was Joash.

**12** The son of Joash was Amaziah. The son of Amaziah was Azariah. The son of Azariah was Jotham.

**13** The son of Jotham was Ahaz. The son of Ahaz was Hezekiah. The son of Hezekiah was Manasseh.

**14** The son of Manasseh was Amon. The son of Amon was Josiah.

**15** The sons of Josiah were Johanan, the first son, Jehoiakim, the second son, Zedekiah, the third son, and Shallum, the fourth son.

**16** The sons of Jehoiakim were Jeconiah and Zedekiah.

**17** The sons of Jeconiah, the prisoner, were Salathiel,

**18** Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.

**19** The sons of Pedaiah were Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel were Meshullam and Hananiah. Shelomith was their sister.

**20** There were also 5 other sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed.

**21** The sons of Hananiah were Pelatiah and Jesaiah. Also listed are the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, and the sons of Shechaniah.

**22** The son of Shechaniah was Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah were Hattush, Igeal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat. They were 6 in total.

**23** The 3 sons of Neariah were Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam.

**24** The 7 sons of Elioenai were Hodaiah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Dalaiah, and Anani.

## Chapter 4

**1** The descendants of Judah were Pharez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.

**2** Reaiah the son of Shobal became the father of Jahath. Jahath became the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These were the families of the Zorathites.

**3** These were the sons of the father of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. The name of their sister was Hazelelponi.

**4** Penuel was the father of Gedor. Ezer was the father of Hushah. These were the descendants of Hur, the first son of Ephratah and the father of Beth-lehem.

**5** Ashur the father of Tekoa had 2 wives, Helah and Naarah.

**6** Naarah gave birth to Ahuzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari for him. These were the sons of Naarah.

**7** The sons of Helah were Zereth, Jezoar, and Ethnan.

**8** Coz became the father of Anub and Zobebah. He was also the ancestor of the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.

**9** Jabez had more honor than his brothers. His mother gave him the name Jabez. She said, "I gave birth to him with much pain."

**10** Jabez prayed to the God of Israel. He said, "Please bless me and make my land larger. Let your hand be with me. Keep me from harm, so that I do not have pain." God gave Jabez what he asked for.

**11** Chelub the brother of Shuah became the father of Mehir. Mehir was the father of Eshton.

**12** Eshton became the father of Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. Tehinnah was the father of Ir-nahash. These were the men of Rechah.

**13** The sons of Kenaz were Othniel and Seraiah. The son of Othniel was Hathath.

**14** Meonothai became the father of Ophrah. Seraiah became the father of Joab. Joab was the father of the people in the Valley of Charashim. They had this name because they were good craftsmen.

**15** The sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh were Iru, Elah, and Naam. The son of Elah was Kenaz.

**16** The sons of Jehaleleel were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asareel.

**17** The sons of Ezra were Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. A wife of Mered gave birth to Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah. Ishbah was the father of Eshtemoa.

**18** His wife from Judah gave birth to Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Socho, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. These were the sons of Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh. Mered married Bithiah.

**19** His wife Hodiah was the sister of Naham. Her sons were the father of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maachathite.

**20** The sons of Shimon were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Ishi were Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.

**21** The sons of Shelah the son of Judah were Er the father of Lecah, and Laadah the father of Mareshah. Shelah was also the ancestor of the families of linen workers at Beth-ashbea.

**22** He was also the ancestor of Jokim, the men of Chozeba, Joash, and Saraph. Joash and Saraph ruled in Moab and returned to Lehem. These records are very old.

**23** These men made clay pots. They lived at Netaim and Gederah. They lived there and did work for the king.

**24** The sons of Simeon were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.

**25** The son of Shaul was Shallum. The son of Shallum was Mibsam. The son of Mibsam was Mishma.

**26** The descendants of Mishma were Hamuel his son, Zacchur his son, and Shimei his son.

**27** Shimei had 16 sons and 6 daughters. But his brothers did not have many children. Their families did not become as large as the families of Judah.

**28** They lived at Beer-sheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual,

**29** Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,

**30** Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,

**31** Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-birei, and Shaaraim. These were their cities until David became king.

**32** Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan. These were 5 cities.

**33** They also had all the villages around these cities, as far as Baal. These were the places where they lived. They kept a record of their families.

**34** Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah the son of Amaziah,

**35** Joel, Jehu the son of Josibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,

**36** Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,

**37** and Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah.

**38** These men, whose names are in this list, were leaders of their families. Their families became very large.

**39** They went to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley. They looked for grass for their flocks.

**40** They found rich, good grass. The land was wide, quiet, and peaceful. Some descendants of Ham lived there before them.

**41** These men, whose names are in this list, came in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah. They attacked the tents of the people there and the Meunites who lived there. They destroyed these people completely, and the people are not there today. Then these men lived in their place, because there was grass there for their flocks.

**42** 500 men of the descendants of Simeon went to Mount Seir. Their leaders were Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.

**43** They killed the rest of the Amalekites who escaped. They live there today.

## Chapter 5

**1** These are the sons of Reuben, the first son of Israel. Reuben was the first son. But he slept with a wife of his father and made his father's bed unclean. Thus the rights of the first son went to the sons of Joseph the son of Israel. Because of this, the family records do not list Reuben as the first son.

**2** Judah became stronger than his brothers, and a ruler came from Judah. But the rights of the first son went to Joseph.

**3** The sons of Reuben, the first son of Israel, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

**4** The descendants of Joel were Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,

**5** Micah his son, Reaia his son, Baal his son,

**6** and Beerah his son. Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria took Beerah away as a prisoner. Beerah was a leader of the Reubenites.

**7** The family records list his relatives by their families. The chief was Jeiel, then Zechariah,

**8** and Bela the son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel. Bela lived in Aroer, as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.

**9** To the east, he lived as far as the edge of the desert near the Euphrates River. He lived there because their cattle became very many in the land of Gilead.

**10** In the time of Saul, they fought a war against the Hagarites and defeated them. Then they lived in the tents of the Hagarites in all the land east of Gilead.

**11** The descendants of Gad lived near them in the land of Bashan, as far as Salchah.

**12** Joel was the chief, and Shapham was the second. Jaanai and Shaphat were also leaders in Bashan.

**13** Their relatives by their families were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Heber. They were 7 in total.

**14** These were the sons of Abihail the son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead. Gilead was the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz.

**15** Ahi the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, was chief of their family.

**16** They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in all the fields of Sharon, as far as their borders.

**17** All these names went into the family records in the time of Jotham king of Judah and in the time of Jeroboam king of Israel.

**18** The tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 brave soldiers. These men could carry shields and swords and use bows. They had much skill in war.

**19** They fought a war against the Hagarites, Jetur, Nephish, and Nodab.

**20** God helped them in the fight. He gave the Hagarites and all their allies into their hands. God did this because they called to him in the battle. He answered them because they trusted him.

**21** They took the animals of the Hagarites: 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, and 2,000 donkeys. They also took 100,000 people.

**22** Many enemy soldiers died, because the war came from God. Then they lived in that land until the time of the exile.

**23** The people of the half tribe of Manasseh lived in the land. They became many. They lived from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.

**24** These were the leaders of their families: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were strong, brave, and famous men. They were leaders of their families.

**25** But these people did not obey the God of their fathers. They were not faithful to him. They worshipped the gods of the people of the land. God destroyed those people before them.

**26** Thus the God of Israel caused Pul king of Assyria to attack. Pul is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria. He took away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh. He took them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan. They are there today.

## Chapter 6

**1** The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

**2** The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

**3** The children of Amram were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

**4** Eleazar became the father of Phinehas. Phinehas became the father of Abishua.

**5** Abishua became the father of Bukki. Bukki became the father of Uzzi.

**6** Uzzi became the father of Zerahiah. Zerahiah became the father of Meraioth.

**7** Meraioth became the father of Amariah. Amariah became the father of Ahitub.

**8** Ahitub became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Ahimaaz.

**9** Ahimaaz became the father of Azariah. Azariah became the father of Johanan.

**10** Johanan became the father of Azariah. This Azariah served as priest in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem.

**11** Azariah became the father of Amariah. Amariah became the father of Ahitub.

**12** Ahitub became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Shallum.

**13** Shallum became the father of Hilkiah. Hilkiah became the father of Azariah.

**14** Azariah became the father of Seraiah. Seraiah became the father of Jehozadak.

**15** Jehozadak went away as a prisoner when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile. The LORD used Nebuchadnezzar to do this.

**16** The sons of Levi were Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.

**17** These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.

**18** The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

**19** The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites, listed by their fathers.

**20** The descendants of Gershom were Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,

**21** Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, and Jeaterai his son.

**22** The descendants of Kohath were Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,

**23** Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son, Assir his son,

**24** Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son.

**25** The sons of Elkanah were Amasai and Ahimoth.

**26** The descendants of Elkanah were Zophai his son, Nahath his son,

**27** Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, and Elkanah his son.

**28** The sons of Samuel were Vashni, the first son, and Abiah.

**29** The descendants of Merari were Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzza his son,

**30** Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, and Asaiah his son.

**31** David put these men in charge of the music in the house of the LORD. He did this after the ark (the holy box of the agreement) came to rest there.

**32** They served with music in front of the tabernacle (the holy tent) of assembly. They did this until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. They did their work in the order that David gave them.

**33** These are the men who served, with their sons. From the Kohathites there was Heman the singer. He was the son of Joel, the son of Shemuel,

**34** the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,

**35** the son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,

**36** the son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah,

**37** the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,

**38** the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.

**39** Heman's relative Asaph stood at his right side. Asaph was the son of Berachiah, the son of Shimea,

**40** the son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchiah,

**41** the son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah,

**42** the son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei,

**43** the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.

**44** Their relatives, the descendants of Merari, stood at the left side. Ethan was there. He was the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,

**45** the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,

**46** the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shamer,

**47** the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.

**48** Their relatives, the other Levites, received all the other work of the tabernacle, the house of God.

**49** But Aaron and his sons made the offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense. They did all the work in the Most Holy Place. They made atonement (removal of sin) for Israel. They did all that Moses the servant of God told them to do.

**50** These are the descendants of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,

**51** Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,

**52** Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,

**53** Zadok his son, and Ahimaaz his son.

**54** These are the places where the descendants of Aaron lived, in their areas. The first lot went to the families of the Kohathites.

**55** The people gave them Hebron in the land of Judah, with its fields around it.

**56** But they gave the fields of the city and its villages to Caleb the son of Jephunneh.

**57** To the descendants of Aaron they gave these cities of Judah: Hebron, a city of refuge, Libnah, Jattir, and Eshtemoa, with their fields.

**58** They also gave Hilen and Debir, with their fields,

**59** and Ashan and Beth-shemesh, with their fields.

**60** From the tribe of Benjamin they gave Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth, with their fields. Their families received 13 cities in total.

**61** The other families of Kohath received 10 cities by lot from the half tribe of Manasseh.

**62** The families of Gershom received 13 cities from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali, and from the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.

**63** The families of Merari received 12 cities by lot from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

**64** Thus the people of Israel gave these cities and their fields to the Levites.

**65** They gave by lot the cities from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. The list above gives the names of these cities.

**66** Some families of Kohath received cities from the tribe of Ephraim.

**67** They received these cities of refuge: Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer, with their fields,

**68** Jokmeam and Beth-horon, with their fields,

**69** and Aijalon and Gath-rimmon, with their fields.

**70** From the half tribe of Manasseh, the other families of Kohath received Aner and Bileam, with their fields.

**71** The families of Gershom received Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth, with their fields, from the half tribe of Manasseh.

**72** From the tribe of Issachar they received Kedesh and Daberath, with their fields,

**73** and Ramoth and Anem, with their fields.

**74** From the tribe of Asher they received Mashal and Abdon, with their fields,

**75** and Hukok and Rehob, with their fields.

**76** From the tribe of Naphtali they received Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kirjathaim, with their fields.

**77** The other families of Merari received Rimmon and Tabor, with their fields, from the tribe of Zebulun.

**78** The tribe of Reuben was on the east side of the Jordan River near Jericho. From that tribe they received Bezer in the desert and Jahzah, with their fields,

**79** and Kedemoth and Mephaath, with their fields.

**80** From the tribe of Gad they received Ramoth in Gilead and Mahanaim, with their fields,

**81** and Heshbon and Jazer, with their fields.

## Chapter 7

**1** The 4 sons of Issachar were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.

**2** The sons of Tola were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Jibsam, and Shemuel. They were leaders of the family of Tola. They were brave soldiers. In the time of David, their descendants were 22,600 men.

**3** The son of Uzzi was Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Ishiah. All 5 of them were chiefs.

**4** By their family records, they had 36,000 soldiers ready for war, because they had many wives and sons.

**5** Their relatives in all the families of Issachar were brave soldiers. The family records list 87,000 of these men in total.

**6** The 3 sons of Benjamin were Bela, Becher, and Jediael.

**7** The 5 sons of Bela were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were leaders of their families and brave soldiers. The family records list 22,034 of their descendants.

**8** The sons of Becher were Zemira, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jerimoth, Abiah, Anathoth, and Alameth. All these were the sons of Becher.

**9** The family records list 20,200 brave soldiers and family leaders from them.

**10** The son of Jediael was Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tharshish, and Ahishahar.

**11** All these descendants of Jediael were leaders of their families and brave soldiers. They had 17,200 soldiers ready to go to war.

**12** Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir. Hushim was the son of Aher.

**13** The sons of Naphtali were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They were the descendants of Bilhah.

**14** The descendants of Manasseh were Ashriel, whom his Aramean concubine gave birth to. She also gave birth to Machir the father of Gilead.

**15** Machir took a wife from the family of Huppim and Shuppim. The name of his sister was Maachah. The name of another descendant was Zelophehad. Zelophehad had only daughters.

**16** Maachah the wife of Machir gave birth to a son. She gave him the name Peresh. The name of his brother was Sheresh. The sons of Sheresh were Ulam and Rakem.

**17** The son of Ulam was Bedan. These were the descendants of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.

**18** His sister Hammoleketh gave birth to Ishod, Abiezer, and Mahalah.

**19** The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.

**20** The descendants of Ephraim were Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eladah his son, Tahath his son,

**21** Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son. Ezer and Elead also were sons of Ephraim. The men of Gath, who were natives of that land, killed Ezer and Elead. They killed them because Ezer and Elead went down to take the cattle of the men of Gath.

**22** Ephraim their father mourned for them for many days. His relatives came to comfort him.

**23** Then Ephraim slept with his wife. She became pregnant and gave birth to a son. Ephraim gave him the name Beriah, because trouble came on his family.

**24** His daughter was Sherah. She built Lower Beth-horon, Upper Beth-horon, and Uzzen-sherah.

**25** Rephah was his son, and Resheph. Telah was his son, and Tahan was his son.

**26** Laadan was his son, Ammihud was his son, and Elishama was his son.

**27** Non was his son, and Jehoshua was his son.

**28** Their land and towns were Beth-el and its towns, Naaran to the east, and Gezer and its towns to the west. They also had Shechem and its towns, as far as Gaza and its towns.

**29** Along the borders of Manasseh were Beth-shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, with their towns. The descendants of Joseph the son of Israel lived in these towns.

**30** The sons of Asher were Imnah, Isuah, Ishuai, and Beriah. Serah was their sister.

**31** The sons of Beriah were Heber and Malchiel. Malchiel was the father of Birzavith.

**32** Heber became the father of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham. Shua was their sister.

**33** The sons of Japhlet were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were the children of Japhlet.

**34** The sons of Shamer were Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.

**35** The sons of his brother Helem were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.

**36** The sons of Zophah were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,

**37** Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.

**38** The sons of Jether were Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.

**39** The sons of Ulla were Arah, Haniel, and Rezia.

**40** All these were descendants of Asher. They were leaders of their families. They were the best and bravest soldiers and chief leaders. The family records list 26,000 men ready for war.

## Chapter 8

**1** Benjamin became the father of Bela, his first son, Ashbel, the second son, Aharah, the third son,

**2** Nohah, the fourth son, and Rapha, the fifth son.

**3** The sons of Bela were Addar, Gera, Abihud,

**4** Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,

**5** Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.

**6** These are the descendants of Ehud. They were leaders of the families who lived in Geba. Their enemies forced them to move to Manahath.

**7** Naaman, Ahiah, and Gera led them when they moved. Gera became the father of Uzza and Ahihud.

**8** Shaharaim sent away his wives Hushim and Baara. After this, he had children in the country of Moab.

**9** By his wife Hodesh he became the father of Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcham,

**10** Jeuz, Shachia, and Mirma. These were his sons. They were leaders of their families.

**11** By Hushim he became the father of Abitub and Elpaal.

**12** The sons of Elpaal were Eber, Misham, and Shamed. Shamed built Ono and Lod with their towns.

**13** Beriah and Shema were leaders of the families who lived in Aijalon. They forced the people of Gath to go away.

**14** Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,

**15** Zebadiah, Arad, Ader,

**16** Michael, Ispah, and Joha were the sons of Beriah.

**17** Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hezeki, Heber,

**18** Ishmerai, Jezliah, and Jobab were the sons of Elpaal.

**19** Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,

**20** Elienai, Zilthai, Eliel,

**21** Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were the sons of Shimhi.

**22** Ishpan, Heber, Eliel,

**23** Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,

**24** Hananiah, Elam, Antothijah,

**25** Iphedeiah, and Penuel were the sons of Shashak.

**26** Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,

**27** Jaresiah, Eliah, and Zichri were the sons of Jeroham.

**28** These men were leaders of their families, as their family records show. They were chiefs. They lived in Jerusalem.

**29** Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. The name of his wife was Maachah.

**30** His first son was Abdon. His other sons were Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,

**31** Gedor, Ahio, and Zacher.

**32** Mikloth became the father of Shimeah. These families also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.

**33** Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.

**34** The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal. Merib-baal became the father of Micah.

**35** The sons of Micah were Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.

**36** Ahaz became the father of Jehoadah. Jehoadah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri became the father of Moza.

**37** Moza became the father of Binea. Rapha was his son, Eleasah was his son, and Azel was his son.

**38** Azel had 6 sons. Their names were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel.

**39** The sons of his brother Eshek were Ulam, his first son, Jehush, the second son, and Eliphelet, the third son.

**40** The sons of Ulam were brave soldiers who could use the bow. They had many sons and grandsons, 150 in total. All these were descendants of Benjamin.

## Chapter 9

**1** The family records list all the people of Israel. These records are in the book of the kings of Israel. The people of Judah went into exile in Babylon because they were not faithful to God.

**2** The first people who lived again in their own cities were some Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants (Nethinims).

**3** Some people from the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem.

**4** From the descendants of Pharez the son of Judah there was Uthai. He was the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani.

**5** From the Shilonites there was Asaiah, the first son, and his sons.

**6** From the descendants of Zerah there was Jeuel. He and his relatives were 690 people.

**7** From the descendants of Benjamin there was Sallu. He was the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hasenuah.

**8** There was also Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri. There was also Meshullam the son of Shephathiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah.

**9** Their relatives, as the family records show, were 956 people. All these men were leaders of their families.

**10** From the priests there were Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.

**11** There was also Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub. Azariah was the official in charge of the house of God.

**12** There was also Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchijah. There was also Maasiai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer.

**13** Their relatives were leaders of their families. They were 1,760 men. They were very able men for the work in the house of God.

**14** From the Levites there was Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah. Hashabiah was a descendant of Merari.

**15** There were also Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah. Mattaniah was the son of Micah, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph.

**16** There was also Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun. There was also Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah. Berechiah lived in the villages of the Netophathites.

**17** The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives. Shallum was their chief.

**18** Until now, they guarded the King's Gate on the east side. They were the gatekeepers for the camps of the Levites.

**19** Shallum was the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah. Shallum and his relatives from his family, the Korahites, were in charge of the work. They guarded the gates of the tabernacle (the holy tent). Their fathers were in charge of the camp of the LORD and guarded the entrance.

**20** In the past, Phinehas the son of Eleazar was the leader of the gatekeepers. The LORD was with him.

**21** Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the door of the tent of assembly.

**22** In total, David and Samuel chose 212 men as gatekeepers. The family records list them by their villages. David and Samuel the seer gave these men their positions because the men were faithful.

**23** Thus the gatekeepers and their sons guarded the gates of the house of the LORD, which was the tent. They worked in groups.

**24** The gatekeepers were on the 4 sides: east, west, north, and south.

**25** Their relatives lived in their villages. From time to time, these relatives came for 7 days to help them.

**26** The 4 chief gatekeepers were Levites. They had a position of trust. They were in charge of the rooms and the treasuries in the house of God.

**27** They stayed all night around the house of God because they had to guard it. Each morning they opened it.

**28** Some of them were in charge of the containers for the service. They counted the containers when they took them in and when they took them out.

**29** Other Levites were in charge of the furniture and all the holy containers. They also took care of the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the incense, and the spices.

**30** Some of the sons of the priests mixed the spices.

**31** Mattithiah, a Levite, was the first son of Shallum the Korahite. He had the position of trust to make the bread that they baked in pans.

**32** Some of their relatives, the Kohathites, were in charge of the holy bread. They prepared the holy bread for each Sabbath.

**33** These are the singers. They were leaders of the families of the Levites. They lived in the rooms of the temple and did no other work. They did their work day and night.

**34** These men were leaders of the families of the Levites, as their family records show. They lived in Jerusalem.

**35** Jehiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. The name of his wife was Maachah.

**36** His first son was Abdon. Then came Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,

**37** Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.

**38** Mikloth became the father of Shimeam. These families also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.

**39** Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.

**40** The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal. Merib-baal became the father of Micah.

**41** The sons of Micah were Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.

**42** Ahaz became the father of Jarah. Jarah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri became the father of Moza.

**43** Moza became the father of Binea. Rephaiah was his son, Eleasah was his son, and Azel was his son.

**44** Azel had 6 sons. Their names were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

## Chapter 10

**1** The Philistines fought against Israel. The men of Israel ran away from the Philistines. Many men of Israel died on Mount Gilboa.

**2** The Philistines chased Saul and his sons. The Philistines killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.

**3** The battle became very bad for Saul. The archers found him and hit him with arrows. Saul had bad wounds.

**4** Saul said to the man who carried his weapons, "Take out your sword and kill me with it. If you do not, these uncircumcised men will come and hurt me." But the man did not obey, because he was very afraid. Thus Saul took his own sword and fell on it.

**5** The man who carried his weapons saw that Saul was dead. Then he also fell on his sword and died.

**6** Thus Saul and his 3 sons died. All his family died together.

**7** All the men of Israel in the valley saw that the army ran away. They saw that Saul and his sons were dead. Thus they left their cities and ran away. Then the Philistines came and lived in those cities.

**8** On the next day, the Philistines came to take things from the dead soldiers. They found Saul and his sons dead on Mount Gilboa.

**9** They took the clothes and armor from Saul. They cut off his head and took his armor. They sent messengers through all the land of the Philistines. The messengers told the news to their idols and to the people.

**10** They put his armor in the temple of their gods. They put his head on the wall in the temple of Dagon.

**11** All the people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines did to Saul.

**12** Then all their brave men went and took the bodies of Saul and his sons. They brought the bodies to Jabesh. They buried the bones under the oak tree in Jabesh. Then they fasted for 7 days.

**13** Saul died because he was not faithful to the LORD. He did not obey the word of the LORD. He also asked a medium for advice. The medium spoke with the spirits of the dead.

**14** Saul did not ask the LORD for advice. Thus the LORD killed him. Then the LORD gave the kingdom to David the son of Jesse.

## Chapter 11

**1** Then all the people of Israel came to David at Hebron. They said, "We are your own family.

**2** In the past, when Saul was king, you led Israel in war. The LORD your God said to you, 'You will be the shepherd of my people Israel. You will be the ruler over my people Israel.'"

**3** All the leaders of Israel came to the king at Hebron. David made an agreement (covenant) with them in Hebron before the LORD. They anointed David king over Israel. This agreed with the word of the LORD through Samuel.

**4** David and all Israel went to Jerusalem. At that time, the name of Jerusalem was Jebus. The Jebusites lived in that land.

**5** The people of Jebus said to David, "You will not come in here." But David captured the fortress of Zion. Zion became the city of David.

**6** David said, "The man who attacks the Jebusites first will become the chief commander." Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first. Thus Joab became the chief.

**7** David lived in the fortress. Thus the people called it the city of David.

**8** David built the city around it, from the Millo to the area around it. Joab repaired the rest of the city.

**9** David became more and more powerful, because the LORD of armies was with him.

**10** These were the chiefs of the strong soldiers of David. They and all Israel gave David strong support in his kingdom. They made David king, as the LORD promised about Israel.

**11** This is the list of the strong soldiers of David. Jashobeam the Hachmonite was the chief of the commanders. He used his spear against 300 men and killed them at one time.

**12** Next was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. He was one of the 3 strongest soldiers.

**13** He was with David at Pas-dammim. The Philistines came together there for battle. There was a field full of barley. The army of Israel ran away from the Philistines.

**14** But Eleazar and David stood in the middle of the field and defended it. They killed the Philistines. The LORD saved them and gave them a great victory.

**15** 3 of the 30 chiefs went down to the rock, to David at the cave of Adullam. The army of the Philistines had its camp in the valley of Rephaim.

**16** At that time David was in the fortress. A group of Philistine soldiers was at Beth-lehem.

**17** David had a strong wish. He said, "I want someone to give me water from the well of Beth-lehem, near the gate!"

**18** The 3 men went through the camp of the Philistines. They took water from the well of Beth-lehem, near the gate. They brought the water to David. But David did not drink it. He poured the water out as an offering to the LORD.

**19** David said, "My God, I will not do this. These men put their lives in danger to get this water. If I drink it, it is like I drink their blood." Thus David did not drink the water. The 3 strongest soldiers did these things.

**20** Abishai, the brother of Joab, was the chief of the 3. He used his spear against 300 men and killed them. He became famous like the 3.

**21** He had more honor than the other 2 men in the group of 3. He became their commander. But he was not one of the first 3.

**22** Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel. He did many great things. He killed 2 of the best soldiers of Moab. On a day with snow, he also went down into a pit and killed a lion.

**23** He killed a very tall Egyptian. The Egyptian was 5 cubits (2.3 meters) tall. The Egyptian had a spear as large as the beam of a loom. Benaiah went against him with a stick. He pulled the spear out of the hand of the Egyptian. Then he killed the Egyptian with his own spear.

**24** Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did these things. He became famous like the 3 strongest soldiers.

**25** He had more honor than the 30, but he was not one of the first 3. David put him in charge of his guards.

**26** The brave soldiers of the army were Asahel the brother of Joab, and Elhanan the son of Dodo from Beth-lehem,

**27** Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,

**28** Ira the son of Ikkesh from Tekoa, Abi-ezer from Anathoth,

**29** Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,

**30** Maharai from Netophah, Heled the son of Baanah from Netophah,

**31** Ithai the son of Ribai from Gibeah of the tribe of Benjamin, Benaiah from Pirathon,

**32** Hurai from the valleys of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,

**33** Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,

**34** the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan the son of Shage the Hararite,

**35** Ahiam the son of Sacar the Hararite, Eliphal the son of Ur,

**36** Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,

**37** Hezro from Carmel, Naarai the son of Ezbai,

**38** Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Haggeri,

**39** Zelek the Ammonite, and Naharai the Berothite. Naharai carried the weapons of Joab the son of Zeruiah.

**40** There were also Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

**41** Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai,

**42** and Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite. Adina was a leader of the Reubenites, and 30 men were with him.

**43** There were also Hanan the son of Maachah, Joshaphat the Mithnite,

**44** Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jehiel the sons of Hothan from Aroer,

**45** Jediael the son of Shimri, and his brother Joha the Tizite,

**46** Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, Ithmah the Moabite,

**47** Eliel, Obed, and Jasiel the Mesobaite.

## Chapter 12

**1** These are the men who came to David at Ziklag. At that time David hid from Saul the son of Kish. These men were among the strong soldiers who helped David in war.

**2** They carried bows. They could throw stones and shoot arrows with the right hand and with the left hand. They were relatives of Saul from the tribe of Benjamin.

**3** The chief was Ahiezer. Next was Joash. They were the sons of Shemaah from Gibeah. There were also Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth. There were also Berachah and Jehu from Anathoth.

**4** There was Ismaiah from Gibeon. He was a strong soldier among the 30 and a leader of the 30. There were also Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Josabad from Gederah.

**5** There were Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite.

**6** There were Elkanah, Jesiah, Azareel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korhites.

**7** There were also Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

**8** Some men from the tribe of Gad left their tribe and went to David. They came to his fortress in the desert. They were strong soldiers, trained for battle. They could use the shield and the spear. Their faces were like the faces of lions. They could run as fast as deer on the mountains.

**9** Ezer was the first, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,

**10** Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,

**11** Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,

**12** Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,

**13** Jeremiah the tenth, and Machbanai the eleventh.

**14** These men from the tribe of Gad were commanders of the army. The least of them was in command of 100 men. The greatest was in command of 1,000 men.

**15** They went across the Jordan River in the first month. At that time the river flowed over all its banks. They forced all the people in the valleys to run away, to the east and to the west.

**16** Some men from the tribes of Benjamin and Judah also came to David at the fortress.

**17** David went out to meet them. He said to them, "If you come in peace to help me, then I will join with you. But maybe you come to give me to my enemies. I did no wrong to anyone. If you do this, then let the God of our fathers see it and punish you."

**18** Then the Spirit came on Amasai, the chief of the 30. Amasai said, "David, we are yours! Son of Jesse, we are with you! Peace to you, and peace to your helpers! Your God helps you." Then David accepted them. He made them commanders of his groups of soldiers.

**19** Some men from the tribe of Manasseh also joined David. This occurred when David went with the Philistines to fight against Saul. But David and his men did not help the Philistines. The rulers of the Philistines talked about it and sent David away. They said, "David will go back to his master Saul. Then we will lose our heads."

**20** David went to Ziklag. These men from Manasseh joined him there: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zilthai. They were commanders of 1,000 men in the tribe of Manasseh.

**21** They helped David fight against groups of raiders. All of them were brave soldiers and commanders in the army.

**22** Each day more men came to help David. Soon David had a large army, like the army of God.

**23** This is the number of the soldiers ready for war who came to David at Hebron. They came to give the kingdom of Saul to David, as the LORD said.

**24** From the tribe of Judah there were 6,800 men with shields and spears, ready for war.

**25** From the tribe of Simeon there were 7,100 brave soldiers, ready for war.

**26** From the tribe of Levi there were 4,600 men.

**27** Jehoiada was the leader of the descendants of Aaron. 3,700 men were with him.

**28** Zadok was a brave young soldier. He came with 22 commanders from his family.

**29** From the tribe of Benjamin, the relatives of Saul, there were 3,000 men. Until that time, most of them stayed loyal to the family of Saul.

**30** From the tribe of Ephraim there were 20,800 brave soldiers. They were famous men in their families.

**31** From the half tribe of Manasseh there were 18,000 men. Their tribe chose them by name to come and make David king.

**32** From the tribe of Issachar there were 200 leaders. These men understood the times. They knew what Israel must do. All their relatives obeyed their orders.

**33** From the tribe of Zebulun there were 50,000 skilled soldiers, ready for battle. They had all types of weapons. They were completely loyal to David.

**34** From the tribe of Naphtali there were 1,000 commanders. 37,000 men with shields and spears were with them.

**35** From the tribe of Dan there were 28,600 men, ready for war.

**36** From the tribe of Asher there were 40,000 skilled soldiers, ready for battle.

**37** From the east side of the Jordan River, from the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh, there were 120,000 men. They had all types of weapons for battle.

**38** All these soldiers came to Hebron ready for battle. They had one purpose: to make David king over all Israel. All the other people of Israel also agreed to make David king.

**39** The men stayed there with David for 3 days. They ate and drank, because their relatives prepared food for them.

**40** People from near and far, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, also brought food. They brought it on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. They brought flour, cakes of figs, raisins, wine, and oil. They also brought many oxen and sheep. There was great joy in Israel.

## Chapter 13

**1** David talked with the commanders of 1,000 men and the commanders of 100 men. He talked with each leader.

**2** Then David spoke to all the people of Israel who were there. He said, "If you think that this is good, and if the LORD our God agrees, we will send messengers. We will send them to all our relatives in the land of Israel. We will also send messengers to the priests and the Levites in their cities. We will tell them all to come to us.

**3** Then we will bring the ark (the holy box) of our God back to us. In the time of Saul, we did not ask God for help through the ark."

**4** All the people agreed to do this, because they all thought that it was the right thing to do.

**5** Thus David brought all the people of Israel together, from the Shihor River in Egypt to Lebo-hamath. They came to bring the ark of God from Kirjath-jearim.

**6** David and all Israel went up to Baalah, which is Kirjath-jearim in Judah. They went to bring up the ark of God, the LORD, from there. The LORD sits on his throne between the cherubim (the winged figures). The ark has his name.

**7** They put the ark of God on a new cart and took it from the house of Abinadab. Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.

**8** David and all Israel celebrated before God with all their strength. They sang and played harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.

**9** They came to the grain floor of Chidon. There the oxen stumbled. Uzza put out his hand to hold the ark.

**10** The LORD became angry with Uzza. The LORD killed him because Uzza put his hand on the ark. Thus Uzza died there before God.

**11** David became angry because the LORD struck Uzza in anger. Thus that place has the name Perez-uzza today.

**12** That day David was afraid of God. He said, "How can I bring the ark of God to my home?"

**13** Thus David did not take the ark to the city of David. Instead, he took it to the house of Obed-edom from Gath.

**14** The ark of God stayed with the family of Obed-edom in his house for 3 months. The LORD blessed the family of Obed-edom and all that he had.

## Chapter 14

**1** Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David. He also sent cedar wood, stone workers, and carpenters to build a house for David.

**2** Then David knew that the LORD made him king over Israel with a strong kingdom. He knew that the LORD made his kingdom great for the sake of the people of Israel.

**3** David married more wives in Jerusalem. He became the father of more sons and daughters.

**4** These are the names of the children that David had in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

**5** Ibhar, Elishua, Elpalet,

**6** Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,

**7** Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphalet.

**8** The Philistines heard that the people anointed David king over all Israel. Thus all the Philistines went up to find and attack David. David heard about it and went out to fight against them.

**9** The Philistines came and attacked the valley of Rephaim.

**10** David asked God, "Must I attack the Philistines? Will you give them into my hands?" The LORD said to him, "Attack. I will give them into your hands."

**11** Thus David and his army went up to Baal-perazim. David defeated the Philistines there. David said, "God broke through my enemies with my hand, as water breaks through a wall." Thus the people gave that place the name Baal-perazim.

**12** The Philistines left their gods there. David gave an order, and his men burned the gods with fire.

**13** The Philistines attacked the valley again.

**14** Thus David asked God again. God said to him, "Do not go up directly after them. Go around them. Attack them in front of the balsam trees.

**15** You will hear a sound of soldiers who march in the tops of the balsam trees. Then go out to the battle, because God will go in front of you to defeat the army of the Philistines."

**16** David did as God told him. His army defeated the army of the Philistines from Gibeon to Gazer.

**17** David became famous in all lands. The LORD caused all nations to fear David.

## Chapter 15

**1** David built houses for himself in the city of David. He prepared a place for the ark of God. He put up a tent for the ark.

**2** Then David said, "Only the Levites can carry the ark of God. The LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to serve him always."

**3** David brought all Israel together in Jerusalem. He wanted them to bring up the ark of the LORD to the place that he prepared for it.

**4** David called together the descendants of Aaron and the Levites.

**5** From the descendants of Kohath there were Uriel, the chief, and 120 of his relatives.

**6** From the descendants of Merari there were Asaiah, the chief, and 220 of his relatives.

**7** From the descendants of Gershom there were Joel, the chief, and 130 of his relatives.

**8** From the descendants of Elizaphan there were Shemaiah, the chief, and 200 of his relatives.

**9** From the descendants of Hebron there were Eliel, the chief, and 80 of his relatives.

**10** From the descendants of Uzziel there were Amminadab, the chief, and 112 of his relatives.

**11** David called Zadok and Abiathar, the priests. He also called the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.

**12** David said to them, "You are the leaders of the families of the Levites. You and your relatives must make yourselves holy. Then bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place that I prepared for it.

**13** The first time, you did not carry the ark. Thus the LORD our God became angry and struck us. This occurred because we did not ask him how to do it correctly."

**14** Thus the priests and the Levites made themselves holy to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**15** The Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with poles. They did this as Moses told them, as the LORD said.

**16** David told the leaders of the Levites to choose some of their relatives as singers. The singers were to play music on lyres, harps, and cymbals. They were to sing loudly with joy.

**17** Thus the Levites chose Heman the son of Joel. From his relatives they chose Asaph the son of Berechiah. From their relatives, the descendants of Merari, they chose Ethan the son of Kushaiah.

**18** With them were their relatives of the second rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Elipheleh, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel. These men were the gatekeepers.

**19** The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan had the work to play cymbals of bronze.

**20** Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played lyres in the high range (Alamoth).

**21** Mattithiah, Elipheleh, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah played harps in the low range (Sheminith). They led the music.

**22** Chenaniah, the leader of the Levites, was in charge of the songs. He taught the songs because he had much skill.

**23** Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.

**24** The priests Shebaniah, Jehoshaphat, Nethaneel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer blew the trumpets in front of the ark of God. Obed-edom and Jehiah were also gatekeepers for the ark.

**25** Thus David, the leaders of Israel, and the commanders of 1,000 men went with joy. They went to bring up the ark of the covenant (the agreement) of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom.

**26** God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD. Thus they sacrificed 7 bulls and 7 rams.

**27** David wore a robe of fine linen. All the Levites who carried the ark wore robes of fine linen. The singers and Chenaniah, the leader of the music, also wore these robes. David also wore a linen ephod (a priest's vest).

**28** Thus all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD. They shouted and blew horns and trumpets. They played cymbals, lyres, and harps loudly.

**29** The ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the city of David. Michal the daughter of Saul looked out of a window. She saw King David. He danced and celebrated. Michal hated him in her heart.

## Chapter 16

**1** They brought the ark of God and put it in the tent that David put up for it. Then they made burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.

**2** David finished the burnt offerings and the peace offerings. Then he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.

**3** He gave food to each person in Israel, to each man and each woman. He gave each person a loaf of bread, a piece of meat, and a cake of raisins.

**4** David chose some of the Levites to serve in front of the ark of the LORD. They were to celebrate, thank, and praise the LORD, the God of Israel.

**5** Asaph was the chief, and Zechariah was second to him. Then there were Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel. They played lyres and harps. Asaph played the cymbals loudly.

**6** The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel always blew trumpets in front of the ark of the covenant of God.

**7** On that day, David first gave this song of thanks to the LORD to Asaph and his relatives:

**8** Give thanks to the LORD. Call on his name. Tell the nations what he did.

**9** Sing to him. Sing praises to him. Tell about all his wonderful acts.

**10** Be proud of his holy name. Let the hearts of the people who look for the LORD be glad.

**11** Look to the LORD and his strength. Always look for him.

**12** Remember the wonderful things that he did. Remember his miracles and the judgments that he spoke.

**13** Remember these things, you descendants of Israel his servant. Remember them, you children of Jacob, his chosen people.

**14** He is the LORD our God. His judgments are in all the earth.

**15** Always remember his covenant. Remember his promise to 1,000 generations.

**16** He made this covenant with Abraham. He made a promise to Isaac with an oath.

**17** He made the covenant firm with Jacob as a law. He made it with Israel as a covenant that will never end.

**18** He said, "I will give you the land of Canaan. It will be your property."

**19** At that time you were few people. You were foreigners in that land.

**20** They went from nation to nation. They went from one kingdom to another.

**21** He did not let anyone hurt them. He spoke strongly against kings to protect them.

**22** He said, "Do not touch my anointed people. Do not hurt my prophets."

**23** Sing to the LORD, all the earth. Each day, tell about how he saves.
