**24** Tell the nations about his glory. Tell all peoples about his wonderful acts.

**25** The LORD is great. He is worthy of much praise. People must fear him more than all gods.

**26** All the gods of the nations are only idols. But the LORD made the heavens.

**27** Glory and honor are with him. Strength and joy are in his place.

**28** Families of the nations, give praise to the LORD. Tell of the glory and the strength of the LORD.

**29** Give the LORD the glory that his name deserves. Bring an offering and come before him. Worship the LORD in the beauty of his holiness.

**30** All the earth, shake with fear before him. The world is firm. It will not move.

**31** Let the heavens be glad. Let the earth be happy. Let people say among the nations, "The LORD is King."

**32** Let the sea and all that is in it make a loud noise. Let the fields and all that is in them be happy.

**33** Then the trees of the forest will sing with joy before the LORD. They will sing because he comes to judge the earth.

**34** Give thanks to the LORD, because he is good. His love will continue always.

**35** Say, "God, you save us. Save us now. Bring us together and rescue us from the nations. Then we will give thanks to your holy name. We will be proud to praise you."

**36** Bless the LORD, the God of Israel, always and forever. Then all the people said, "Amen," and praised the LORD.

**37** David left Asaph and his relatives in front of the ark of the covenant of the LORD. They were to serve in front of the ark always, as the work of each day needed.

**38** He also left Obed-edom and his 68 relatives. Obed-edom the son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers.

**39** David left Zadok the priest and his relatives the priests in front of the tabernacle of the LORD. The tabernacle was at the place of worship on the hill at Gibeon.

**40** They were to make burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering. They did this each morning and each evening. They did all that the law of the LORD tells. The LORD gave this law to Israel.

**41** Heman, Jeduthun, and the other chosen men were with them. Their names are on the list. They were to give thanks to the LORD, because his love continues always.

**42** Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments for the songs of God. The sons of Jeduthun were gatekeepers.

**43** Then all the people went back to their homes. David went back to bless his family.

## Chapter 17

**1** David lived in his house. He said to Nathan the prophet, "Look, I live in a house of cedar wood. But the ark of the covenant of the LORD is in a tent."

**2** Nathan said to David, "Do all that you want to do, because God is with you."

**3** But that night the word of God came to Nathan. God said,

**4** "Go and tell David my servant, 'The LORD says this: You will not build a house for me to live in.

**5** I did not live in a house from the day that I brought Israel out of Egypt until today. I moved from tent to tent and from one place to another.

**6** I went with all the people of Israel to many places. I never spoke to any of the judges of Israel about a house. I told those judges to be the shepherds of my people. I did not say to them, "Why do you not build a house of cedar wood for me?"'

**7** Now tell this to my servant David: 'The LORD of armies says this: I took you from the fields, where you followed the sheep. I made you the ruler of my people Israel.

**8** I was with you in all places where you went. I destroyed all your enemies in front of you. I will make your name great, like the names of the great men on the earth.

**9** I will make a place for my people Israel. I will put them in that place like a tree. They will live in their own place, and no one will trouble them again. Evil people will not hurt them again, as they did at the start.

**10** They hurt my people at the time when I put judges over my people Israel. I will defeat all your enemies. I also tell you that the LORD will build a house for you. This house will be a family of kings.

**11** Your life will end and you will go to be with your ancestors. Then I will make one of your descendants king after you. He will be one of your sons. I will make his kingdom strong.

**12** He will build a house for me. I will make his throne strong forever.

**13** I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will not take my love away from him. I took it away from Saul, who ruled before you.

**14** I will put him in charge of my house and my kingdom forever. His throne will continue forever.'"

**15** Nathan told David all these words and all this vision.

**16** Then King David went in and sat before the LORD. David said, "LORD God, I am not important. My family is not important. But you brought me to this place.

**17** God, you think that this is a small thing. Now you also speak about the future of the family of your servant. LORD God, you treat me like an important man.

**18** I cannot say more to you about the honor that you give to me, your servant. You know your servant.

**19** LORD, you did all these great things because of your servant and because of your own wish. You made known all these great things.

**20** LORD, no one is like you. There is no God but you. All that we heard tells us this.

**21** No other nation on earth is like your people Israel. God went to free them to be his own people. You made your name great with great and terrible acts. You forced nations to leave before your people. You freed your people from Egypt.

**22** You made your people Israel your own people forever. LORD, you became their God.

**23** Now, LORD, keep your promise about your servant and his family forever. Do what you said.

**24** Let your promise be firm. Then people will make your name great forever. They will say, 'The LORD of armies is the God of Israel.' Let the family of your servant David continue before you.

**25** My God, you told your servant that you will build a family of kings for him. Thus I, your servant, have the courage to pray this prayer to you.

**26** LORD, you are God. You promised these good things to your servant.

**27** Now please bless the family of your servant. Let my family continue before you forever. LORD, you blessed it, and it will be blessed forever."

## Chapter 18

**1** After this, David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. He took Gath and its towns from the control of the Philistines.

**2** David also defeated Moab. The Moabites became servants of David and paid tax to him.

**3** David also defeated Hadarezer king of Zobah, near Hamath. Hadarezer went to make his control strong at the Euphrates River.

**4** David took from him 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers. David cut the leg muscles of all the chariot horses. But he kept enough horses for 100 chariots.

**5** The Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadarezer king of Zobah. David killed 22,000 of the Syrians.

**6** Then David put groups of soldiers in Syria near Damascus. The Syrians became servants of David and paid tax to him. The LORD gave David victory in all places where he went.

**7** David took the gold shields that the officers of Hadarezer carried. He brought the shields to Jerusalem.

**8** David also took very much bronze from Tibhath and Chun, cities of Hadarezer. Later, Solomon used this bronze to make the large bronze water tank (the sea), the pillars, and the bronze containers.

**9** Tou king of Hamath heard that David defeated all the army of Hadarezer king of Zobah.

**10** Thus Tou sent his son Hadoram to King David. Hadoram greeted David and congratulated him because David fought against Hadarezer and defeated him. Hadarezer often fought wars with Tou. Hadoram brought all types of things made of gold, silver, and bronze.

**11** King David gave these things to the LORD. He also gave the silver and the gold that he took from all these nations. He took it from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.

**12** Abishai the son of Zeruiah killed 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

**13** He put groups of soldiers in Edom. All the Edomites became servants of David. The LORD gave David victory in all places where he went.

**14** Thus David ruled over all Israel. He did what was fair and right for all his people.

**15** Joab the son of Zeruiah was in command of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the records.

**16** Zadok the son of Ahitub and Abimelech the son of Abiathar were the priests. Shavsha was the secretary.

**17** Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of the Cherethites and the Pelethites. The sons of David were the chief officials next to the king.

## Chapter 19

**1** After this, Nahash the king of the Ammonites died. His son became king after him.

**2** David said, "I will be kind to Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father was kind to me." Thus David sent messengers to comfort Hanun about the death of his father. The officials of David came to Hanun in the land of the Ammonites to comfort him.

**3** But the leaders of the Ammonites said to Hanun, "Do you think that David honors your father? Do you think that he sent these men to comfort you? No! His officials came to look at the land. They came to spy, and then to destroy it."

**4** Thus Hanun took the officials of David and shaved them. He cut off their clothes in the middle, at the hips. Then he sent them away.

**5** Some people went and told David what occurred to the men. David sent messengers to meet them, because the men were very ashamed. The king said, "Stay at Jericho until your beards grow again. Then come back."

**6** The Ammonites saw that David now hated them. Thus Hanun and the Ammonites sent 1,000 talents of silver to pay for chariots and horsemen. They paid men from Mesopotamia, Syria-maachah, and Zobah.

**7** They paid for 32,000 chariots. They also paid the king of Maachah and his army. These men came and made their camp near Medeba. The Ammonites came together from their cities and came to the battle.

**8** David heard about this. He sent Joab and all the army of strong soldiers.

**9** The Ammonites came out and got ready for battle at the gate of their city. The kings who came to help them stayed in the open field.

**10** Joab saw that the enemy was in front of him and behind him. Thus he chose some of the best soldiers of Israel. He put them in position against the Syrians.

**11** He put the rest of the army under the command of his brother Abishai. They got into position against the Ammonites.

**12** Joab said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you must help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will help you.

**13** Be strong. We must fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. The LORD will do what he thinks is good."

**14** Joab and his soldiers went forward to fight against the Syrians. The Syrians ran away from him.

**15** The Ammonites saw that the Syrians ran away. Thus they also ran away from Abishai, the brother of Joab. They went into their city. Then Joab went back to Jerusalem.

**16** The Syrians saw that Israel defeated them. Thus they sent messengers and brought the Syrians from the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of the army of Hadarezer, led them.

**17** Someone told David about this. David brought all Israel together. He went across the Jordan River and came to the Syrians. He put his army in position against them. Then the Syrians fought against David.

**18** But the Syrians ran away from Israel. David killed 7,000 Syrian chariot soldiers and 40,000 foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach, the commander of the army.

**19** The officials of Hadarezer saw that Israel defeated them. Thus they made peace with David and became his servants. After this, the Syrians did not help the Ammonites again.

## Chapter 20

**1** In the spring, when kings usually go to war, Joab led the army out. He destroyed the land of the Ammonites. He came to Rabbah and put an army around the city. But David stayed in Jerusalem. Joab attacked Rabbah and destroyed it.

**2** David took the crown from the head of their king. The crown weighed 1 talent of gold, and it had valuable stones in it. The people put the crown on the head of David. David also took very many valuable things from the city.

**3** He brought out the people of the city. He made them do hard work with saws, iron picks, and axes. David did this to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then David and all the army went back to Jerusalem.

**4** After this, a war started with the Philistines at Gezer. At that time Sibbechai the Hushathite killed Sippai. Sippai was a descendant of the giants. Thus Israel defeated the Philistines.

**5** There was war again with the Philistines. Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath from Gath. The handle of the spear of Lahmi was as large as the beam of a loom.

**6** There was war again at Gath. There was a very tall man there. He had 24 fingers and toes, 6 on each hand and 6 on each foot. He also was a descendant of the giants.

**7** This man insulted Israel. Then Jonathan the son of Shimea, the brother of David, killed him.

**8** These men were descendants of the giants in Gath. David and his soldiers killed them.

## Chapter 21

**1** Satan went against Israel. He caused David to count the people of Israel.

**2** David said to Joab and the leaders of the people, "Go and count the people of Israel from Beer-sheba to Dan. Then bring the number to me. I want to know it."

**3** Joab said, "I want the LORD to make his people 100 times more than they are now. But my lord the king, all these people are your servants. Why do you want to do this? Why will you cause Israel to sin?"

**4** But the king did not change his order to Joab. Thus Joab left and went through all Israel. Then he came back to Jerusalem.

**5** Joab gave David the number of the people. In all Israel there were 1,100,000 men who could fight with the sword. In Judah there were 470,000 men who could fight with the sword.

**6** But Joab did not count the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he hated the order of the king.

**7** God was not happy with this act. Thus he punished Israel.

**8** David said to God, "I did a very bad sin because I did this. Now please take away the guilt of your servant. I did a very foolish thing."

**9** The LORD spoke to Gad, the seer of David. He said,

**10** "Go and tell David, 'The LORD says this: I give you 3 choices. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"

**11** Thus Gad came to David. He said to David, "The LORD says this: 'Choose one of these.

**12** You can have 3 years of famine. Or your enemies can defeat you for 3 months, and their swords will catch you. Or the LORD can send a disease on the land for 3 days. Then the angel of the LORD will destroy people in all the land of Israel.' Now decide what answer I must give to the LORD, who sent me."

**13** David said to Gad, "I am in great trouble. Let me fall into the hand of the LORD, because his mercy is very great. But do not let me fall into the hands of men."

**14** Thus the LORD sent a disease on Israel. 70,000 men of Israel died.

**15** God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. The angel started to destroy the city. Then the LORD looked and felt sorry about the disaster. He said to the angel who destroyed the people, "That is enough! Stop now." At that time, the angel of the LORD stood by the grain floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

**16** David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD. The angel stood between the earth and the sky. He had a sword in his hand. He held the sword out over Jerusalem. David and the leaders of Israel wore rough cloth (sackcloth) to show their sorrow. They bowed with their faces to the ground.

**17** David said to God, "I gave the order to count the people. I am the person who sinned and did this evil. These people are like sheep. They did nothing wrong. LORD my God, please punish me and my family. But do not send the disease on your people."

**18** Then the angel of the LORD told Gad to speak to David. Gad told David to go up and build an altar to the LORD at the grain floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

**19** David went up, because Gad told him to go in the name of the LORD.

**20** Ornan threshed wheat at that time. He turned and saw the angel. His 4 sons who were with him hid.

**21** David came to Ornan. Ornan looked and saw David. He went out of the grain floor. He bowed down to David with his face to the ground.

**22** David said to Ornan, "Sell me the place of this grain floor. I want to build an altar to the LORD on it. Sell it to me for the full price. Then the disease will stop among the people."

**23** Ornan said to David, "Take it. My lord the king can do what he thinks is good. Look, I will also give you the oxen for the burnt offerings. I will give you the tools that beat the grain for wood. I will give you the wheat for the grain offering. I give it all to you."

**24** But King David said to Ornan, "No. I will pay the full price for it. I will not take what is yours and give it to the LORD. I will not make burnt offerings that cost me nothing."

**25** Thus David paid Ornan 600 shekels (6.8 kilograms) of gold for the place.

**26** David built an altar to the LORD there. He made burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called to the LORD. The LORD answered him. He sent fire from heaven onto the altar of burnt offering.

**27** Then the LORD gave an order to the angel. The angel put his sword back in its cover.

**28** At that time, David saw that the LORD answered him at the grain floor of Ornan the Jebusite. Thus David made sacrifices there.

**29** At that time, the tabernacle of the LORD was at the place of worship on the hill at Gibeon. Moses made this tabernacle in the desert. The altar of burnt offering was also there.

**30** But David could not go there to ask God for help. He was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD.

## Chapter 22

**1** Then David said, "The house of the LORD God will be here. The altar of burnt offering for Israel will be here."

**2** David gave an order to bring together the foreigners who lived in the land of Israel. He chose stone workers from them to cut stones for the house of God.

**3** David prepared much iron to make nails and hinges for the doors of the gates. He also prepared more bronze than anyone could weigh.

**4** He also prepared more cedar logs than anyone could count. The people of Zidon and Tyre brought much cedar wood to David.

**5** David said, "My son Solomon is young and has no experience. The house for the LORD must be very great. It must be famous and beautiful in all countries. Thus I will prepare for it now." So David prepared many materials before his death.

**6** Then David called his son Solomon. He told Solomon to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.

**7** David said to Solomon, "My son, I wanted to build a house for the name of the LORD my God.

**8** But the LORD spoke to me. He said, 'You killed many people and fought many wars. You will not build a house for my name, because you killed many people on the earth in my sight.

**9** But you will have a son. He will be a man of peace. I will give him peace from all his enemies around him. His name will be Solomon. I will give peace and quiet to Israel during his life.

**10** He will build a house for my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. I will make the throne of his kingdom over Israel strong forever.'

**11** Now, my son, I pray that the LORD will be with you. Then you will be successful. Build the house of the LORD your God, as he said that you will do.

**12** I pray that the LORD will give you wisdom and the ability to understand. He will put you in charge of Israel. Then obey the law of the LORD your God.

**13** You will be successful if you carefully obey the laws and rules that the LORD gave to Moses for Israel. Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid. Do not lose courage.

**14** Look, I worked hard to prepare for the house of the LORD. I prepared 100,000 talents of gold and 1,000,000 talents of silver. I prepared more bronze and iron than anyone can weigh. I also prepared wood and stone. You can add more to these.

**15** You have many workers. There are stone cutters, stone workers, and carpenters. There are men with skill for all types of work.

**16** They can work with gold, silver, bronze, and iron. There is too much of it to count. Now start the work. I pray that the LORD will be with you."

**17** David also told all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon.

**18** David said, "The LORD your God is with you. He gave you peace on all sides. He gave the people of the land into my hands. The land is now under the control of the LORD and his people.

**19** Now give your hearts and souls to the LORD your God. Obey him. Start to build the holy place of the LORD God. Then bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy things of God into the house. You will build this house for the name of the LORD."

## Chapter 23

**1** David became old. He lived a long life. Then he made his son Solomon king over Israel.

**2** David brought together all the leaders of Israel, the priests, and the Levites.

**3** The officials counted the Levites who were 30 years old and older. There were 38,000 men in total.

**4** David said, "24,000 of them will be in charge of the work of the house of the LORD. 6,000 will be officials and judges.

**5** 4,000 will be gatekeepers. 4,000 will praise the LORD with the instruments that I made for praise."

**6** David divided the Levites into groups by the sons of Levi. The sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

**7** The descendants of Gershon were Laadan and Shimei.

**8** The 3 sons of Laadan were Jehiel, the chief, Zetham, and Joel.

**9** The 3 sons of Shimei were Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran. These were the leaders of the families of Laadan.

**10** The 4 sons of Shimei were Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah.

**11** Jahath was the chief, and Zizah was the second. But Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons. Thus the records list them as one family.

**12** The 4 sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

**13** The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. God chose Aaron and his sons for a special work forever. They were to make the most holy things holy. They were to burn incense before the LORD and serve him. They were to bless the people in his name forever.

**14** The sons of Moses, the man of God, were part of the tribe of Levi.

**15** The sons of Moses were Gershom and Eliezer.

**16** Shebuel was the chief of the sons of Gershom.

**17** Rehabiah was the chief of the descendants of Eliezer. Eliezer had no other sons. But Rehabiah had very many sons.

**18** Shelomith was the chief of the sons of Izhar.

**19** The sons of Hebron were Jeriah, the first, Amariah, the second, Jahaziel, the third, and Jekameam, the fourth.

**20** The sons of Uzziel were Michah, the first, and Jesiah, the second.

**21** The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish.

**22** Eleazar died and had no sons. He had only daughters. Their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them.

**23** The 3 sons of Mushi were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.

**24** These were the descendants of Levi by their families. They were the leaders of the families. The officials wrote the name of each man on the list. They did the work in the house of the LORD. They were 20 years old and older.

**25** David said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, gave peace to his people. He will live in Jerusalem forever.

**26** Thus the Levites do not have to carry the tabernacle again. They do not have to carry its containers for the service."

**27** By the last orders of David, the officials counted the Levites from 20 years old and older.

**28** Their work was to help the descendants of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD. They worked in the courtyards and in the rooms. They made all the holy things clean. They did other work in the house of God.

**29** They were in charge of the holy bread and the fine flour for the grain offerings. They were in charge of the bread without yeast and the bread baked in pans or mixed with oil. They were in charge of all the measures of quantity and size.

**30** They were to stand each morning to thank and praise the LORD. They did the same each evening.

**31** They helped when people made burnt offerings to the LORD on the Sabbaths, on the new moon festivals, and on the other festivals. They always served before the LORD in the number that the law told them.

**32** Thus the Levites took care of the tent of assembly and the holy place. They helped their relatives, the descendants of Aaron, in the service of the house of the LORD.

## Chapter 24

**1** These are the groups of the descendants of Aaron. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

**2** But Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no children. Thus Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.

**3** With the help of Zadok and Ahimelech, David divided the priests into groups for their work. Zadok was a descendant of Eleazar. Ahimelech was a descendant of Ithamar.

**4** There were more leaders among the descendants of Eleazar than among the descendants of Ithamar. Thus the descendants of Eleazar had 16 leaders of families. The descendants of Ithamar had 8 leaders of families.

**5** They divided both groups by lot, in the same way. There were officials of the holy place and officials of God from the descendants of Eleazar and of Ithamar.

**6** Shemaiah the son of Nethaneel was the secretary. He was a Levite. He wrote the names of the priests in front of the king and the leaders. Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the leaders of the families of the priests and Levites were also there. They chose one family from Eleazar, and then one family from Ithamar.

**7** The first lot went to Jehoiarib. The second went to Jedaiah.

**8** The third went to Harim. The fourth went to Seorim.

**9** The fifth went to Malchijah. The sixth went to Mijamin.

**10** The seventh went to Hakkoz. The eighth went to Abijah.

**11** The ninth went to Jeshua. The tenth went to Shecaniah.

**12** The eleventh went to Eliashib. The twelfth went to Jakim.

**13** The thirteenth went to Huppah. The fourteenth went to Jeshebeab.

**14** The fifteenth went to Bilgah. The sixteenth went to Immer.

**15** The seventeenth went to Hezir. The eighteenth went to Aphses.

**16** The nineteenth went to Pethahiah. The twentieth went to Jehezekel.

**17** The twenty-first went to Jachin. The twenty-second went to Gamul.

**18** The twenty-third went to Delaiah. The twenty-fourth went to Maaziah.

**19** This was the order of their service when they came into the house of the LORD. They obeyed the rules that their ancestor Aaron gave them. The LORD, the God of Israel, gave these rules to Aaron.

**20** These were the other descendants of Levi. From the sons of Amram there was Shubael. From the sons of Shubael there was Jehdeiah.

**21** From the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah was the first.

**22** From the Izharites there was Shelomoth. From the sons of Shelomoth there was Jahath.

**23** The sons of Hebron were Jeriah, the first, Amariah, the second, Jahaziel, the third, and Jekameam, the fourth.

**24** From the sons of Uzziel there was Michah. From the sons of Michah there was Shamir.

**25** The brother of Michah was Isshiah. From the sons of Isshiah there was Zechariah.

**26** The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. The son of Jaaziah was Beno.

**27** The descendants of Merari through Jaaziah were Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.

**28** From Mahli there was Eleazar, who had no sons.

**29** From Kish there was Jerahmeel, the son of Kish.

**30** The sons of Mushi were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the Levites by their families.

**31** These Levites also chose their work by lot, as their relatives, the descendants of Aaron, did. They did this in front of King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the leaders of the families of the priests and Levites. The families of the oldest brother and of the youngest brother got the same treatment.

## Chapter 25

**1** David and the commanders of the army chose some of the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun for special service. These men were to prophesy with harps, lyres, and cymbals. This is the list of the men who did this work:

**2** From the sons of Asaph there were Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah. Asaph led them. He prophesied under the orders of the king.

**3** From Jeduthun there were 6 sons: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah. Their father Jeduthun led them. He prophesied with the harp to thank and praise the LORD.

**4** From Heman there were his sons Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.

**5** All these were the sons of Heman, the seer of the king. God promised to make Heman strong. God gave Heman 14 sons and 3 daughters.

**6** Their fathers led all these men in the music of the house of the LORD. They played cymbals, lyres, and harps for the service of the house of God. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman worked under the orders of the king.

**7** They and their relatives learned the songs for the LORD. All of them had much skill. They were 288 men in total.

**8** They chose their work by lot. The young and the old, the teacher and the student, all did the same.

**9** The first lot went to Joseph, from the family of Asaph. The second went to Gedaliah. He, his relatives, and his sons were 12 men.

**10** The third went to Zaccur. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**11** The fourth went to Izri. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**12** The fifth went to Nethaniah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**13** The sixth went to Bukkiah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**14** The seventh went to Jesharelah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**15** The eighth went to Jeshaiah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**16** The ninth went to Mattaniah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**17** The tenth went to Shimei. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**18** The eleventh went to Azareel. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**19** The twelfth went to Hashabiah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**20** The thirteenth went to Shubael. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**21** The fourteenth went to Mattithiah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**22** The fifteenth went to Jeremoth. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**23** The sixteenth went to Hananiah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**24** The seventeenth went to Joshbekashah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**25** The eighteenth went to Hanani. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**26** The nineteenth went to Mallothi. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**27** The twentieth went to Eliathah. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**28** The twenty-first went to Hothir. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**29** The twenty-second went to Giddalti. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**30** The twenty-third went to Mahazioth. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

**31** The twenty-fourth went to Romamti-ezer. He, his sons, and his relatives were 12 men.

## Chapter 26

**1** These are the groups of the gatekeepers. From the Korhites there was Meshelemiah the son of Kore, from the descendants of Asaph.

**2** The sons of Meshelemiah were Zechariah, the first son, Jediael, the second, Zebadiah, the third, Jathniel, the fourth,

**3** Elam, the fifth, Jehohanan, the sixth, and Elioenai, the seventh.

**4** The sons of Obed-edom were Shemaiah, the first son, Jehozabad, the second, Joah, the third, Sacar, the fourth, Nethaneel, the fifth,

**5** Ammiel, the sixth, Issachar, the seventh, and Peulthai, the eighth. God blessed Obed-edom.

**6** His son Shemaiah also had sons. They were leaders in their family, because they were brave and strong men.

**7** The sons of Shemaiah were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad. Their relatives Elihu and Semachiah were also strong men.

**8** All these were descendants of Obed-edom. They, their sons, and their relatives were able and strong men for the work. There were 62 descendants of Obed-edom.

**9** Meshelemiah had 18 sons and relatives. They were strong men.

**10** Hosah, from the descendants of Merari, had sons. Simri was the chief. He was not the first son, but his father made him the chief.

**11** Hilkiah was the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth. Hosah had 13 sons and relatives in total.

**12** These groups of gatekeepers had their leaders. Like their relatives, they had work to serve in the house of the LORD.

**13** They chose each gate by lot, family by family. The young and the old did the same.

**14** The lot for the East Gate went to Shelemiah. Then they chose by lot for his son Zechariah, a wise adviser. The lot for the North Gate went to Zechariah.

**15** The lot for the South Gate went to Obed-edom. The lot for the storehouses went to his sons.

**16** The lots for the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road went to Shuppim and Hosah. The guards stood next to each other.

**17** Each day there were 6 Levites on the east side, 4 on the north side, and 4 on the south side. There were 2 at each storehouse.

**18** At the court on the west side, there were 4 guards at the road and 2 at the court.

**19** These were the groups of the gatekeepers from the descendants of Kore and Merari.

**20** From the Levites, Ahijah was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God. He was also in charge of the treasuries of the holy gifts.

**21** The descendants of Laadan were from the family of Gershon. Jehieli was a leader of the families of Laadan the Gershonite.

**22** The sons of Jehieli were Zetham and his brother Joel. They were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.

**23** There were also leaders from the families of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

**24** Shebuel was the son of Gershom, the son of Moses. Shebuel was the chief official over the treasuries.

**25** His relatives through Eliezer were Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.

**26** Shelomith and his relatives were in charge of all the treasuries of the holy gifts. King David and the leaders of the families gave these gifts to God. The commanders of 1,000 men, of 100 men, and of the army also gave these gifts.

**27** They gave some of the things that they took in battles. They gave these things to repair the house of the LORD.

**28** Samuel the seer, Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah also gave gifts to God. Shelomith and his relatives were in charge of all these holy gifts.

**29** From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons worked outside the temple. They were officials and judges over Israel.

**30** From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives were 1,700 able men. They were in charge of Israel on the west side of the Jordan River. They did all the work of the LORD and the service of the king.

**31** Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites, as their family records show. In the 40th year that David was king, people searched the records. They found brave men from the Hebronites at Jazer in Gilead.

**32** Jerijah had 2,700 relatives. They were able men and leaders of families. King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh. They did all the work for God and for the king.

## Chapter 27

**1** This is the list of the people of Israel who served the king. It lists the leaders of families, the commanders of 1,000 men and of 100 men, and their officials. They served the king in groups. Each group served for 1 month each year. Each group had 24,000 men.

**2** Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel was in command of the first group, for the first month. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**3** He was a descendant of Perez. He was the chief of all the commanders of the army for the first month.

**4** Dodai the Ahohite was in command of the group for the second month. Mikloth was the leader in his group. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**5** The third commander, for the third month, was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada the priest. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**6** This Benaiah was a strong soldier among the 30, and he was in command of the 30. His son Ammizabad was in charge of his group.

**7** The fourth commander, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab. His son Zebadiah was commander after him. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**8** The fifth commander, for the fifth month, was Shamhuth the Izrahite. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**9** The sixth commander, for the sixth month, was Ira the son of Ikkesh from Tekoa. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**10** The seventh commander, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, from the tribe of Ephraim. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**11** The eighth commander, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, from the family of Zerah. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**12** The ninth commander, for the ninth month, was Abi-ezer from Anathoth, from the tribe of Benjamin. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**13** The tenth commander, for the tenth month, was Maharai from Netophah, from the family of Zerah. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**14** The eleventh commander, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah from Pirathon, from the tribe of Ephraim. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**15** The twelfth commander, for the twelfth month, was Heldai from Netophah, from the family of Othniel. There were 24,000 men in his group.

**16** These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel. Eliezer the son of Zichri was the leader of the Reubenites. Shephatiah the son of Maachah was the leader of the Simeonites.

**17** Hashabiah the son of Kemuel was the leader of the Levites. Zadok was the leader of the descendants of Aaron.

**18** Elihu, a brother of David, was the leader of Judah. Omri the son of Michael was the leader of Issachar.

**19** Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah was the leader of Zebulun. Jerimoth the son of Azriel was the leader of Naphtali.

**20** Hoshea the son of Azaziah was the leader of Ephraim. Joel the son of Pedaiah was the leader of the half tribe of Manasseh.

**21** Iddo the son of Zechariah was the leader of the half tribe of Manasseh in Gilead. Jaasiel the son of Abner was the leader of Benjamin.

**22** Azareel the son of Jeroham was the leader of Dan. These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.

**23** David did not count the men who were 20 years old or younger. He did not count them because the LORD promised to make Israel as many as the stars in the sky.

**24** Joab the son of Zeruiah started to count the people, but he did not finish. God became angry with Israel because of the count. Thus the number did not go into the records of King David.

**25** Azmaveth the son of Adiel was in charge of the treasuries of the king. Jehonathan the son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses in the fields, the cities, the villages, and the towers.

**26** Ezri the son of Chelub was in charge of the workers who farmed the land.

**27** Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards. Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the wine from the vineyards and the wine storage.

**28** Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive trees and the sycamore trees in the low hills. Joash was in charge of the supplies of olive oil.

**29** Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the cattle that ate grass in Sharon. Shaphat the son of Adlai was in charge of the cattle in the valleys.

**30** Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels. Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.

**31** Jaziz the Hagerite was in charge of the flocks. All these men were officials in charge of the property of King David.

**32** Jonathan, the uncle of David, was an adviser. He was a wise man and a scribe. Jehiel the son of Hachmoni took care of the sons of the king.

**33** Ahithophel was the adviser of the king. Hushai the Archite was the friend of the king.

**34** After Ahithophel, Jehoiada the son of Benaiah and Abiathar became advisers. Joab was the commander of the army of the king.

## Chapter 28

**1** David brought all the leaders of Israel together in Jerusalem. He brought the leaders of the tribes and the commanders of the groups that served the king. He brought the commanders of 1,000 men and of 100 men. He brought the officials in charge of all the property and animals of the king and his sons. He also brought the officials, the strong soldiers, and all the brave men.

**2** Then King David stood up and said, "Listen to me, my relatives and my people. I wanted to build a house as a place of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD. It was to be a footstool for our God. I prepared to build it.

**3** But God said to me, 'You will not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war. You killed people.'

**4** But the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from all my family to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah to be the leader. From Judah he chose the family of my father. From the sons of my father, he was happy to make me king over all Israel.

**5** The LORD gave me many sons. From all my sons, he chose my son Solomon. Solomon will sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.

**6** The LORD said to me, 'Your son Solomon will build my house and my courtyards. I chose him to be my son, and I will be his father.

**7** I will make his kingdom strong forever, if he continues to obey my commands and my laws, as he does today.'

**8** Now all Israel, the people of the LORD, sees this, and our God hears this. Thus I tell you: Carefully obey all the commands of the LORD your God. Then you will keep this good land. You will give it to your descendants forever.

**9** And you, my son Solomon, know the God of your father. Serve him with all your heart and with a mind that wants to serve him. The LORD looks into all hearts. He understands all thoughts. If you look for him, you will find him. But if you leave him, he will reject you forever.

**10** Be careful now. The LORD chose you to build a house as a holy place. Be strong and do the work."

**11** Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the temple. The plans showed the porch, the buildings, the storerooms, and the upper rooms. They also showed the inner rooms and the room for the mercy seat (the cover of the ark).

**12** He gave him the plans of all that the Spirit put in his mind. He gave the plans for the courtyards of the house of the LORD and all the rooms around it. He gave the plans for the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries for the holy gifts.

**13** He gave him the instructions for the groups of the priests and the Levites. He gave instructions for all the work in the house of the LORD. He gave instructions for all the containers for the service in the house of the LORD.

**14** He told Solomon the weight of the gold for all the gold items for each type of service. He told him the weight of the silver for all the silver items for each type of service.

**15** He told him the weight of the gold for the gold lampstands and their lamps. He told him the weight of each lampstand and its lamps. He told him the weight of the silver for the silver lampstands and their lamps, as each lampstand was used.

**16** He told him the weight of the gold for each table for the holy bread. He told him the weight of the silver for the silver tables.

**17** He told him the weight of the pure gold for the forks, the bowls, and the jars. He told him the weight of the gold for each gold dish and the silver for each silver dish.

**18** He told him the weight of the refined gold for the altar of incense. He gave him the plan for the chariot of the gold cherubim. Their wings opened and covered the ark of the covenant of the LORD.

**19** David said, "The LORD gave me all these plans in a written document. He helped me understand all the details of the plans."

**20** David also said to his son Solomon, "Be strong and brave. Do the work. Do not be afraid. Do not lose courage. The LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you or leave you. He will stay with you until you finish all the work for the service of the house of the LORD.

**21** Look, the groups of the priests and the Levites will help you with all the service of the house of God. Skilled men who want to help will be with you for all types of work. The leaders and all the people will obey all your orders."

## Chapter 29

**1** Then King David said to all the people, "God chose only my son Solomon. But Solomon is young and has no experience. The work is great, because this temple is not for men. It is for the LORD God.

**2** I used all my strength to prepare materials for the house of my God. I prepared gold for the gold items and silver for the silver items. I prepared bronze for the bronze items, iron for the iron items, and wood for the wood items. I prepared many onyx stones, stones to set in the walls, colored stones, all types of valuable stones, and marble.

**3** I also love the house of my God. Thus I give my own gold and silver to the house of my God. I give this in addition to all that I prepared for the holy house.

**4** I give 3,000 talents of gold from Ophir and 7,000 talents of refined silver. These will cover the walls of the buildings.

**5** The gold is for the gold items, and the silver is for the silver items. Skilled workers will use them for all the work. Now, who will give himself to the LORD today?"

**6** Then the leaders of the families and the leaders of the tribes of Israel gave willingly. The commanders of 1,000 men and of 100 men, and the officials in charge of the work of the king, also gave willingly.

**7** For the work of the house of God, they gave 5,000 talents and 10,000 darics of gold. They gave 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron.

**8** The people who had valuable stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD. Jehiel the Gershonite was in charge of the treasury.

**9** The people were happy because their leaders gave willingly. They gave to the LORD with all their hearts. King David also was very happy.

**10** David praised the LORD in front of all the people. David said, "LORD, God of Israel our father, we praise you forever and ever.

**11** LORD, greatness, power, glory, victory, and majesty are yours. All things in heaven and on earth are yours. LORD, the kingdom is yours. You are the ruler over all things.

**12** Wealth and honor come from you. You rule over all things. You have power and strength in your hand. You can make people great and strong.

**13** Now, our God, we thank you. We praise your glorious name.

**14** But I am not important, and my people are not important. We cannot give so much on our own. All things come from you. We only gave you what came from your hand.

**15** We are like foreigners and visitors before you, as all our ancestors were. Our time on earth is like a shadow. It does not continue.

**16** LORD our God, we prepared all these materials to build a house for your holy name. But all these things come from your hand. They are all yours.

**17** My God, I know that you examine the heart. You are happy with honest people. I gave all these things willingly and with an honest heart. Now I saw your people here give willingly to you. I was happy to see this.

**18** LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our ancestors, keep this wish in the hearts of your people always. Keep their hearts loyal to you.

**19** Give my son Solomon a loyal heart. Then he will obey your commands, your laws, and your rules. He will do all these things. He will build the temple that I prepared materials for."

**20** Then David said to all the people, "Praise the LORD your God." All the people praised the LORD, the God of their ancestors. They bowed down and worshipped the LORD. They also bowed down to the king.

**21** On the next day, they made sacrifices to the LORD. They made burnt offerings to the LORD of 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, and 1,000 lambs. They also gave drink offerings and many other sacrifices for all Israel.

**22** That day they ate and drank before the LORD with great joy. Then they made Solomon the son of David king for the second time. They anointed him before the LORD to be the ruler. They anointed Zadok to be the priest.

**23** Then Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king after his father David. Solomon was successful. All Israel obeyed him.

**24** All the leaders, the strong soldiers, and all the sons of King David promised to be loyal to King Solomon.

**25** The LORD made Solomon very great in front of all Israel. He gave Solomon more royal glory than any king of Israel before him.

**26** Thus David the son of Jesse ruled over all Israel.

**27** He ruled over Israel for 40 years. He ruled for 7 years in Hebron and for 33 years in Jerusalem.

**28** He died when he was very old. He had a long life, wealth, and honor. His son Solomon became king after him.

**29** The records of Samuel the seer tell the acts of King David, from the start to the end. The records of Nathan the prophet and the records of Gad the seer also tell them.

**30** These records tell about all his rule and his power. They tell about the events that occurred to him, to Israel, and to all the kingdoms of the other countries.

# 2 Chronicles

## Chapter 1

**1** Solomon, the son of David, made his rule over the kingdom strong. The LORD his God was with him and made him very great.

**2** Solomon spoke to all Israel. He spoke to the commanders of 1,000 men and of 100 men, to the judges, and to all the leaders in Israel. These leaders were the heads of the families.

**3** Solomon and all the assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon. The tent of assembly of God was there. Moses, the servant of the LORD, made that tent in the wilderness.

**4** But David brought the ark of God up from Kirjath-jearim to the place that he prepared for it. David put up a tent for the ark in Jerusalem.

**5** Bezaleel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, made the bronze altar. The bronze altar was in front of the tabernacle of the LORD. Solomon and the assembly went there to ask for the help of the LORD.

**6** Solomon went up to the bronze altar in front of the LORD at the tent of assembly. He offered 1,000 burnt offerings on the altar.

**7** That night God appeared to Solomon. God said to him, "Ask for what you want me to give you."

**8** Solomon said to God, "You showed great kindness to David my father. You made me king in his place.

**9** Now, LORD God, keep your promise to David my father. You made me king over a people. The people are as many as the dust of the earth.

**10** Give me wisdom and knowledge now, so that I can lead this people. Who can judge your people, because they are so many?"

**11** God said to Solomon, "This is the wish of your heart. You did not ask for riches, possessions, or honor. You did not ask for the death of your enemies. You did not ask for a long life. But you asked for wisdom and knowledge, so that you can judge my people. I made you king over them.

**12** Thus I will give you wisdom and knowledge. I will also give you riches, possessions, and honor. No king before you had such things. No king after you will have such things."

**13** Then Solomon came back to Jerusalem from the high place at Gibeon, from the front of the tent of assembly. He ruled over Israel.

**14** Solomon collected chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen. He put them in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem.

**15** In Jerusalem, the king made silver and gold as common as stones. He made cedar wood as common as the sycamore trees in the low hills.

**16** Solomon got horses and linen yarn from Egypt. The merchants of the king bought the linen yarn at a price.

**17** The merchants brought a chariot from Egypt for 600 shekels of silver and a horse for 150 shekels. Thus they also brought horses for all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Syria.

## Chapter 2

**1** Solomon decided to build a house for the name of the LORD and a palace for himself.

**2** Solomon chose 70,000 men to carry loads and 80,000 men to cut stone in the mountains. He chose 3,600 men to supervise them.

**3** Solomon sent a message to Huram, the king of Tyre. He said, "You helped David my father. You sent him cedar wood to build a house to live in. Help me in the same way.

**4** I will build a house for the name of the LORD my God. I will give the house to him. In the house we will burn sweet incense in front of him. We will put out the holy bread at all times. We will offer burnt offerings in the morning and in the evening. We will do this on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the holy feasts of the LORD our God. This is a permanent law for Israel.

**5** The house that I build will be great, because our God is greater than all gods.

**6** But who can build a house for God? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot hold him. Who am I to build a house for him? I can only build a place to burn sacrifices in front of him.

**7** Thus, send me a man with skill to work in gold, silver, bronze, and iron. He must also know how to work in purple, red, and blue cloth. He must know how to cut designs. He will work with the skilled men that are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem. David my father supplied these men.

**8** Also send me cedar, pine, and algum logs from Lebanon. I know that your servants have skill to cut trees in Lebanon. My servants will work with your servants.

**9** They will prepare much wood for me, because the house that I will build will be large and wonderful.

**10** I will give your servants, the men who cut the trees, 20,000 measures of crushed wheat and 20,000 measures of barley. I will also give them 20,000 baths of wine and 20,000 baths of olive oil."

**11** Then Huram, the king of Tyre, wrote a letter and sent it to Solomon. Huram wrote, "The LORD loves his people. Thus he made you king over them."

**12** Huram also wrote, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth. He gave King David a wise son. This son has good judgment and wisdom. He will build a house for the LORD and a palace for himself.

**13** Now I send you a skilled man who understands much. His name is Huram-abi.

**14** His mother is from the tribe of Dan, and his father is a man from Tyre. He has skill to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood. He can work in purple, blue, and red cloth and in fine linen. He can cut all types of designs. He can make each plan that you give him. He will work with your skilled men and with the skilled men of my lord David, your father.

**15** Now, my lord, send to your servants the wheat, the barley, the olive oil, and the wine that you promised.

**16** We will cut all the wood from Lebanon that you need. We will tie the logs together and float them by sea to Joppa. Then you can take the wood up to Jerusalem."

**17** Solomon counted all the foreigners in the land of Israel. He did this after the count that David his father made. There were 153,600 foreigners.

**18** He made 70,000 of them carry loads. He made 80,000 of them cut stone in the mountains. He made 3,600 of them supervisors to make the people work.

## Chapter 3

**1** Then Solomon started to build the house of the LORD at Jerusalem on Mount Moriah. The LORD appeared to David his father there. David prepared that place on the grain floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

**2** Solomon started to build on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his rule.

**3** These are the measurements that Solomon used for the house of God. With the old standard of cubits, the house was 60 cubits long and 20 cubits wide.

**4** The porch at the front of the house was 20 cubits long, the same as the width of the house. The porch was 120 cubits high. Solomon covered the inside of the porch with pure gold.

**5** He covered the main room with pine wood and then covered the wood with fine gold. He put designs of palm trees and chains on it.

**6** He put valuable stones in the house to make it beautiful. The gold was from Parvaim.

**7** He covered the house with gold. He covered the beams, the doorposts, the walls, and the doors with gold. He cut figures of cherubim (angels with wings) on the walls.

**8** He made the most holy room. It was 20 cubits long, the same as the width of the house, and 20 cubits wide. He covered it with 600 talents of fine gold.

**9** The nails weighed 50 shekels of gold. He also covered the upper rooms with gold.

**10** In the most holy room he made 2 statues of cherubim and covered them with gold.

**11** The wings of the cherubim were 20 cubits long in total. One wing of the first cherub was 5 cubits long and touched the wall of the house. The other wing was also 5 cubits long and touched the wing of the second cherub.

**12** One wing of the second cherub was 5 cubits long and touched the other wall of the house. The other wing was also 5 cubits long and touched the wing of the first cherub.

**13** The wings of these cherubim spread out 20 cubits. The cherubim stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the main room.

**14** He made the curtain from blue, purple, and red cloth and from fine linen. He put designs of cherubim on the curtain.

**15** In front of the house he made 2 pillars, 35 cubits high. On the top of each pillar there was a capital 5 cubits high.

**16** He made chains, as in the inner room, and put them on the tops of the pillars. He made 100 pomegranates and put them on the chains.

**17** He put up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right side and one on the left side. He gave the name Jachin to the pillar on the right. He gave the name Boaz to the pillar on the left.

## Chapter 4

**1** He made a bronze altar. It was 20 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, and 10 cubits high.

**2** He also made a large round tank of metal, called the Sea. It was 10 cubits from rim to rim and 5 cubits high. The distance around it was 30 cubits.

**3** Below the rim there were figures of oxen around the Sea, 10 for each cubit. The workers made 2 rows of oxen when they cast the Sea, as one piece with it.

**4** The Sea stood on 12 oxen. 3 oxen looked north, 3 looked west, 3 looked south, and 3 looked east. The Sea was on top of them, and the back parts of the oxen were toward the center.

**5** The metal of the Sea was the width of a hand thick. Its rim was like the rim of a cup, with the shape of a lily flower. The Sea held 3,000 baths of water.

**6** He also made 10 basins for washes. He put 5 on the right side and 5 on the left side. The priests washed the parts of the burnt offerings in them. But the priests used the Sea to wash themselves.

**7** He made 10 gold lampstands, as the plan told him. He put them in the temple, 5 on the right side and 5 on the left side.

**8** He also made 10 tables and put them in the temple, 5 on the right side and 5 on the left side. He made 100 gold bowls.

**9** He made the court of the priests, the large court, and the doors for the court. He covered the doors with bronze.

**10** He put the Sea on the right side of the house, at the southeast corner.

**11** Huram also made the pots, the shovels, and the bowls. Thus Huram completed the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:

**12** He made the 2 pillars and the 2 bowl-shaped capitals on the tops of the pillars. He also made the 2 networks of chains to cover the 2 capitals on the tops of the pillars.

**13** the 400 pomegranates for the 2 networks, 2 rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the 2 bowl-shaped capitals on the pillars;

**14** the stands, and the basins on the stands;

**15** the Sea, and the 12 oxen under it;

**16** the pots, the shovels, the meat forks, and all the related tools. Huram-abi made all these items of polished bronze for King Solomon, for the house of the LORD.

**17** The king made the castings in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan, between Succoth and Zeredathah.

**18** Solomon made very many of these items. Nobody could know the weight of the bronze.

**19** Solomon also made all the items for the house of God. He made the gold altar and the tables for the holy bread.

**20** He made the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold. The lamps burned in front of the inner room, as the law told.

**21** He made the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold, the purest gold.

**22** He made the wick cutters, the bowls, the spoons, and the fire pans of pure gold. The entrance of the house was of gold. The inner doors to the most holy place and the doors of the main room of the temple were also of gold.

## Chapter 5

**1** Thus Solomon completed all the work for the house of the LORD. Then Solomon brought in the items that David his father gave to God. He put the silver, the gold, and all the items in the treasuries of the house of God.

**2** Then Solomon called the elders of Israel to Jerusalem. He called all the heads of the tribes and the leaders of the families of Israel. They came to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD up from the City of David, which is Zion.

**3** All the men of Israel came to the king at the feast in the seventh month.

**4** All the elders of Israel came, and the Levites lifted up the ark.

**5** They brought up the ark, the tent of the assembly, and all the holy items in the tent. The priests and the Levites carried them up.

**6** King Solomon and all the assembly of Israel with him stood in front of the ark. They sacrificed sheep and oxen. There were so many animals that nobody could count them.

**7** The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner room of the house. They put it in the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubim.

**8** The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark. Thus the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.

**9** The poles were very long. People could see the ends of the poles from the front of the inner room, but not from outside. The poles are there to this day.

**10** There was nothing in the ark but the 2 stone tablets. Moses put them there at Horeb. At Horeb the LORD made a covenant with the people of Israel after they came out of Egypt.

**11** Then the priests came out of the holy place. All the priests that were there made themselves holy. They did this without attention to their divisions.

**12** All the Levites who were singers stood at the east side of the altar. These were Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives. They wore fine linen and played cymbals, lyres, and harps. With them, 120 priests blew trumpets.

**13** The trumpet players and the singers made one sound together to praise and thank the LORD. They sang loudly with trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments. They praised the LORD and sang, "He is good. His love continues forever." Then a cloud filled the house of the LORD.

**14** Because of the cloud, the priests could not stand to do their work. The glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

## Chapter 6

**1** Then Solomon said, "The LORD said that he will live in thick darkness.

**2** But I built a great house for you. It is a place for you to live in forever."

**3** Then the king turned around and blessed all the assembly of Israel. All the assembly of Israel stood.

**4** He said, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel. With his power he did the thing that he promised to my father David. He said,

**5** 'I brought my people out of the land of Egypt. Since that day, I did not choose a city in a tribe of Israel for a house for my name. Also, I did not choose a man to rule my people Israel.

**6** But now I chose Jerusalem as the place for my name. I chose David to rule my people Israel.'

**7** David my father wanted to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**8** But the LORD said to David my father, 'You wanted to build a house for my name. It was good that you wanted to do this.

**9** But you will not build the house. Your son, who will come from your body, will build the house for my name.'

**10** Now the LORD did the thing that he promised. I became king after David my father. I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised. I built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**11** I put the ark in the house. In the ark is the covenant that the LORD made with the people of Israel."

**12** Then Solomon stood in front of the altar of the LORD, in front of all the assembly of Israel. He lifted up his hands.

**13** Solomon made a bronze platform, 5 cubits long, 5 cubits wide, and 3 cubits high. He put it in the center of the court. He stood on it. Then he went down on his knees in front of all the assembly of Israel. He lifted his hands toward heaven.

**14** He said, "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth. You keep your covenant. You show love to your servants who obey you with all their heart.

**15** You kept your promise to your servant David, my father. You spoke the promise, and with your power you made it true today.

**16** Now, LORD, God of Israel, keep the other promise to your servant David, my father. You said, 'A man from your family will always sit on the throne of Israel. But your sons must be careful to obey my law, as you obeyed me.'

**17** Now, LORD, God of Israel, make true the word that you spoke to your servant David.

**18** But will God really live on the earth with people? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot hold you. Thus this house that I built cannot hold you!

**19** But, LORD my God, give attention to the prayer of your servant and to his request. Hear the cry and the prayer that your servant prays to you.

**20** Watch over this house day and night. You said that you will put your name in this place. Hear the prayer that your servant prays toward this place.

**21** Hear the requests of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, the place where you live. When you hear, forgive.

**22** A man can do wrong against his neighbor. Then the man must make an oath. He can come and make the oath in front of your altar in this house.

**23** Then hear from heaven and act. Judge your servants. Punish the guilty man, and give him what he deserves. Show that the innocent man is innocent, and reward him for his good actions.

**24** Your people Israel can sin against you, and an enemy can defeat them. Then they can come back to you and praise your name. They can pray to you in this house and ask for your help.

**25** Then hear from heaven. Forgive the sin of your people Israel. Bring them back to the land that you gave to them and to their ancestors.

**26** Your people can sin against you, and you can stop the rain. Then they can pray toward this place and praise your name. They can turn from their sin because you punished them.

**27** Then hear from heaven. Forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Teach them the good way to live. Send rain on your land. You gave this land to your people as their possession.

**28** There can be famine or disease in the land. There can be crop disease, mold, locusts, or grasshoppers. Enemies can attack the cities of the land. There can be any disaster or any sickness.

**29** Then any person or all your people Israel can pray to you. Each person knows his own pain and grief. He can lift up his hands toward this house.

**30** Then hear from heaven, the place where you live, and forgive. Give each person what he deserves for all his actions. You know his heart. Only you know the hearts of all people.

**31** Then they will fear you and obey you all the days that they live in the land. You gave this land to our ancestors.

**32** A foreigner who is not from your people Israel can come from a far country. He will come because of your great name and your great power. He can come and pray toward this house.

**33** Then hear from heaven, the place where you live. Do all the things that the foreigner asks from you. Then all the peoples of the earth will know your name. They will fear you, as your people Israel fear you. They will know that this house that I built has your name.

**34** Your people can go to war against their enemies on the road where you send them. They can pray to you toward this city that you chose and toward the house that I built for your name.

**35** Then hear their prayer and their request from heaven, and give them victory.

**36** Your people can sin against you, because all people sin. You can become angry with them and give them to an enemy. The enemy can take them as prisoners to a land far away or near.

**37** In that land, your people can change their minds. They can turn back to you and pray in the land of their captivity. They can say, 'We sinned. We did wrong. We did evil.'

**38** They can come back to you with all their heart and with all their soul in that land. They can pray toward the land that you gave to their ancestors. They can pray toward the city that you chose and toward the house that I built for your name.

**39** Then hear their prayer and their requests from heaven, the place where you live. Help them. Forgive your people who sinned against you.

**40** Now, my God, watch and listen to the prayers that people pray in this place.

**41** Now, LORD God, go up to the place where you rest, you and the ark of your power. LORD God, let your priests wear salvation as clothes. Let your faithful people be happy because of your goodness.

**42** LORD God, do not turn away from your anointed king. Remember your love for David your servant."

## Chapter 7

**1** When Solomon stopped his prayer, fire came down from heaven. The fire burned the burnt offering and the sacrifices. The glory of the LORD filled the house.

**2** The priests could not go into the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

**3** All the people of Israel saw the fire come down and the glory of the LORD on the house. They went down with their faces to the ground on the stone floor. They worshiped and thanked the LORD. They said, "He is good. His love continues forever."

**4** Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices to the LORD.

**5** King Solomon offered a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. Thus the king and all the people gave the house of God to God.

**6** The priests stood at their posts. The Levites stood with the instruments of music for the LORD. King David made these instruments to thank the LORD, because his love continues forever. David used them when he praised God with the Levites. The priests blew trumpets in front of the Levites, and all Israel stood.

**7** Solomon made the center of the court in front of the house of the LORD holy. There he offered burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings. He did this because the bronze altar that he made was too small. It could not hold the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat.

**8** At that time Solomon held the feast for 7 days, and all Israel with him. It was a very large assembly. The people came from the road to Hamath in the north to the brook of Egypt in the south.

**9** On the eighth day they held a holy assembly. They held the dedication of the altar for 7 days and the feast for 7 days.

**10** On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent the people to their homes. They were glad and happy in their hearts. They were happy because of the good things that the LORD did for David, for Solomon, and for his people Israel.

**11** Thus Solomon completed the house of the LORD and the palace of the king. He did well all the things that he wanted to do in the house of the LORD and in his own palace.

**12** Then the LORD appeared to Solomon at night. The LORD said to him, "I heard your prayer. I chose this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.

**13** I can stop the rain from the sky. I can command the locusts to eat the crops of the land. I can send disease among my people.

**14** Then my people, who have my name, must make themselves humble and pray. They must look for me and turn from their evil ways. Then I will hear from heaven. I will forgive their sin and I will heal their land.

**15** Now I will watch and listen to the prayers that people pray in this place.

**16** Now I chose this house and made it holy, so that my name will be there forever. My eyes and my heart will be there always.

**17** You must obey me as David your father obeyed me. Do all that I command you. Obey my laws and my rules.

**18** Then I will make your royal throne strong. I made this covenant with David your father. I said, 'A man from your family will always rule Israel.'

**19** But you and your people can turn away from me. You can reject my laws and my commands that I gave you. You can go and serve other gods and worship them.

**20** If you do these things, then I will pull my people out of my land that I gave them. I will reject this house that I made holy for my name. All nations will laugh at this house and use it as an example of disaster.

**21** This house is now great. But each person who goes past it will feel horror. He will say, 'Why did the LORD do this to this land and to this house?'

**22** People will answer, 'They left the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of the land of Egypt. They took other gods, worshiped them, and served them. Thus the LORD brought all this disaster on them.'"

## Chapter 8

**1** After 20 years, Solomon completed the house of the LORD and his own palace.

**2** Then Solomon built again the cities that Huram gave to him. He made the people of Israel live there.

**3** Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and took control of it.

**4** He built Tadmor in the wilderness. He built all the store cities in Hamath.

**5** He also built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon. They were strong cities with walls, gates, and bars.

**6** He also built Baalath and all his store cities. He built all the cities for his chariots and his horsemen. He built all the things that he wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land that he ruled.

**7** Some people of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites stayed in the land. These people were not from Israel.

**8** They were the descendants of the people that the Israelites did not kill. Solomon made these descendants do forced work, and they do this work to this day.

**9** But Solomon did not make slaves of the people of Israel for his work. The Israelites were his soldiers, his chief officers, and the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.

**10** King Solomon also had 250 chief officers. These officers ruled over the people.

**11** Solomon brought the daughter of Pharaoh up from the City of David to the palace that he built for her. He said, "My wife must not live in the palace of David, king of Israel. The places where the ark of the LORD came are holy."

**12** Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD. He built this altar in front of the porch.

**13** He offered the sacrifices that the law of Moses told for each day. He offered them on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the 3 yearly feasts. These feasts are the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Shelters.

**14** Solomon obeyed the rules of David his father. He put the priests into their divisions for their work. He put the Levites into their positions to praise God and to help the priests with the work of each day. He also put the gatekeepers into their divisions at each gate. David, the man of God, commanded these things.

**15** The priests and the Levites obeyed all the commands of the king. They obeyed in all things, also in the work of the treasuries.

**16** Thus all the work of Solomon was ready, from the day of the foundation of the house of the LORD until the end. Thus the house of the LORD was complete.

**17** Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth, on the coast of the sea in the land of Edom.

**18** Huram sent ships to him with his servants. These servants knew the sea well. They went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir. There they got 450 talents of gold and brought it to King Solomon.

## Chapter 9

**1** The queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon. She came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with difficult questions. She came with a very large group of people. Her camels carried spices, much gold, and valuable stones. She came to Solomon and talked with him about all the things in her mind.

**2** Solomon answered all her questions. No question was too difficult for Solomon to explain to her.

**3** The queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon and the palace that he built.

**4** She saw the food on his table and the seats of his officials. She saw his servants and their clothes. She saw his cupbearers and their clothes. She saw the burnt offerings that he offered at the house of the LORD. She was very surprised.

**5** She said to the king, "In my own land I heard about your actions and your wisdom. The report was true.

**6** But I did not believe the report until I came and saw it with my eyes. Nobody told me even half of your great wisdom. You are greater than the report that I heard.

**7** Your men are happy! These servants of yours are happy! They always stand in front of you and hear your wisdom.

**8** Praise the LORD your God! He was happy with you and put you on his throne as king for the LORD your God. Your God loves Israel and will make Israel strong forever. Thus he made you king over them. You will do what is fair and right."

**9** Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, very many spices, and valuable stones. Nobody ever gave King Solomon spices like the spices from the queen of Sheba.

**10** The servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon brought gold from Ophir. They also brought algum wood and valuable stones.

**11** The king used the algum wood to make steps for the house of the LORD and for the palace of the king. He also made harps and lyres for the singers. Nobody saw such things before in the land of Judah.

**12** King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all the things that she wanted and asked for. He gave her more than she brought to him. Then she and her servants went back to her own land.

**13** The weight of the gold that Solomon got in one year was 666 talents.

**14** This was in addition to the gold from the traders and the merchants. All the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon.

**15** King Solomon made 200 large shields of hammered gold. He used 600 shekels of hammered gold for each shield.

**16** He also made 300 small shields of hammered gold. He used 300 shekels of gold for each shield. The king put them in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon.

**17** The king also made a large throne of ivory and covered it with pure gold.

**18** The throne had 6 steps and a gold footstool, which joined to the throne. There were armrests on each side of the seat. 2 lions stood next to the armrests.
