**18** They gave shares to all the families in the lists, to their babies, their wives, their sons, and their daughters. They gave shares to all the assembly, because the priests and the Levites faithfully made themselves holy.

**19** Some priests, the descendants of Aaron, lived in the fields near their cities. In each of these cities there were men with assigned names. These men gave shares to all the males among the priests and to all the Levites in the family lists.

**20** Hezekiah did this in all Judah. He did what was good, right, and true in the sight of the LORD his God.

**21** He did all his work for the house of God with all his heart. He obeyed the law and the commands, and he worshiped his God. Thus he was successful.

## Chapter 32

**1** After these faithful actions of Hezekiah, Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, came and attacked Judah. He made camps around the strong cities. He wanted to take control of them.

**2** Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib came and that he wanted to attack Jerusalem.

**3** Then Hezekiah made a plan with his officials and his commanders. They decided to stop the water from the springs outside the city. The officials and the commanders helped him.

**4** Many people came together and stopped all the springs and the stream that went through the land. They said, "Why must the kings of Assyria come and find much water?"

**5** Hezekiah worked hard to make the city strong. He repaired all the broken parts of the wall and built towers on it. He built another wall outside it. He made the Millo in the City of David stronger. He also made many weapons and shields.

**6** He put commanders over the people. He brought the people together in the open area at the city gate. He spoke words of encouragement to them. He said,

**7** "Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid. Do not lose courage because of the king of Assyria or his large army. There is a greater power with us than with him.

**8** He has only human strength. But we have the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles." The people trusted the words of Hezekiah, the king of Judah.

**9** After this, Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, sent his officials to Jerusalem. He and all his army were at Lachish and attacked it. His officials brought a message to Hezekiah, the king of Judah, and to all the people of Judah in Jerusalem. The message said,

**10** "Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, says this: 'What do you trust? Why do you stay in Jerusalem while my army surrounds it?

**11** Hezekiah says to you, "The LORD our God will save us from the king of Assyria." But Hezekiah tricks you. You will die from hunger and thirst.

**12** Hezekiah himself removed the high places and the altars of the LORD. He told Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship at only one altar and burn incense on it."

**13** You know what I and my ancestors did to all the peoples of other lands. The gods of those nations could not save their lands from me.

**14** My ancestors destroyed those nations. None of their gods could save his people from me. Thus your God cannot save you from me!

**15** Do not let Hezekiah trick you. Do not let him persuade you in this way. Do not believe him. No god of any nation or kingdom could save his people from me or from my ancestors. Thus your God can surely not save you from me!'"

**16** The officials of Sennacherib said more things against the LORD God and against his servant Hezekiah.

**17** Sennacherib also wrote letters to insult the LORD, the God of Israel. The letters said, "The gods of the nations of other lands did not save their people from me. Thus the God of Hezekiah will not save his people from me."

**18** The officials shouted loudly in the Hebrew language to the people of Jerusalem on the wall. They wanted to make the people afraid. Then they could take the city.

**19** They spoke about the God of Jerusalem as they spoke about the gods of the other peoples of the earth. Those gods were only things that men made with their hands.

**20** Because of this, King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah, the son of Amoz, prayed and cried out to heaven.

**21** Then the LORD sent an angel. The angel killed all the brave soldiers, the leaders, and the commanders in the camp of the king of Assyria. Thus Sennacherib went back to his own land in shame. He went into the temple of his god. There some of his own sons killed him with the sword.

**22** Thus the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, and from all other enemies. He gave them peace on all sides.

**23** Many people brought gifts for the LORD to Jerusalem. They also brought valuable gifts to Hezekiah, the king of Judah. From then on, all the nations honored Hezekiah.

**24** At that time Hezekiah became so sick that he almost died. He prayed to the LORD. The LORD answered him and gave him a sign.

**25** But Hezekiah did not thank God for this kindness, because he became proud. Thus the anger of God came on him and on Judah and Jerusalem.

**26** Then Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem made themselves humble because of their pride. Thus the anger of the LORD did not come on them while Hezekiah lived.

**27** Hezekiah had very much riches and honor. He made treasuries for his silver, gold, valuable stones, spices, shields, and all types of valuable items.

**28** He also made storehouses for the grain, the new wine, and the olive oil. He made stalls for all types of animals and pens for the flocks.

**29** He built cities for himself. He had very many flocks and herds, because God gave him very many possessions.

**30** Hezekiah also stopped the upper outlet of the Gihon spring. He made the water go down to the west side of the City of David. Hezekiah was successful in all his work.

**31** But the leaders of Babylon sent officials to Hezekiah. They asked about the miracle that occurred in the land. Then God left Hezekiah alone to test him. God wanted to know all the things in his heart.

**32** The other actions of Hezekiah and his good deeds are in the vision of the prophet Isaiah, the son of Amoz. They are also in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

**33** Then Hezekiah died. The people buried him in the highest place among the tombs of the descendants of David. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem honored him at his death. Manasseh his son became king after him.

## Chapter 33

**1** Manasseh was 12 years old when he became king. He ruled for 55 years in Jerusalem.

**2** He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did the detestable things of the nations that the LORD pushed out in front of the people of Israel.

**3** He built again the high places that his father Hezekiah destroyed. He built altars for the Baals and made Asherah poles. He worshiped and served all the stars in the sky.

**4** He built altars in the house of the LORD. The LORD said about this house, "My name will be in Jerusalem forever."

**5** He built altars for all the stars in the sky in the 2 courts of the house of the LORD.

**6** He burned his sons as sacrifices in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom. He used magic, divination, and witchcraft. He asked for advice from people who talked to the spirits of the dead. He did much evil in the sight of the LORD and made him angry.

**7** He made an idol and put it in the house of God. God said about this house to David and to his son Solomon, "I chose Jerusalem from all the tribes of Israel. I will put my name forever in this house and in Jerusalem.

**8** I will not make the Israelites leave the land that I gave to their ancestors again. But they must be careful to obey all my commands. They must obey all the law, the rules, and the decisions that I gave through Moses."

**9** But Manasseh caused Judah and the people of Jerusalem to do wrong. They did more evil than the nations that the LORD destroyed in front of the people of Israel.

**10** The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they did not listen.

**11** Thus the LORD brought the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria against them. They caught Manasseh with hooks and put bronze chains on him. They took him to Babylon.

**12** In his trouble, Manasseh asked the LORD his God for help. He made himself very humble in front of the God of his ancestors.

**13** He prayed to God, and God listened to him. God heard his request and brought him back to Jerusalem and to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.

**14** After this, Manasseh built an outer wall for the City of David. The wall was on the west side of the Gihon spring, in the valley. It went as far as the entrance of the Fish Gate and went around Ophel. He made the wall very high. He put army commanders in all the strong cities of Judah.

**15** He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD. He removed all the altars that he built on the hill of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem. He threw them out of the city.

**16** He repaired the altar of the LORD. He offered peace offerings and thank offerings on it. He commanded Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.

**17** But the people still offered sacrifices at the high places, but only to the LORD their God.

**18** Manasseh did other things. His other actions, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers are in the records of the kings of Israel. These seers spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**19** His prayer and how God heard him are in the records of the seers. All his sins and his unfaithfulness are also there. These records also tell about the places where he built high places and put up Asherah poles and idols before he made himself humble.

**20** Then Manasseh died, and the people buried him in his palace. Amon his son became king after him.

**21** Amon was 22 years old when he became king. He ruled for 2 years in Jerusalem.

**22** He did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh did. Amon offered sacrifices to all the idols that his father Manasseh made, and he served them.

**23** But Amon did not make himself humble in front of the LORD, as his father Manasseh did. Amon sinned more and more.

**24** His officials made a plan against him and killed him in his palace.

**25** But the people of the land killed all the men who made the plan against King Amon. Then the people of the land made Josiah, his son, king after him.

## Chapter 34

**1** Josiah was 8 years old when he became king. He ruled for 31 years in Jerusalem.

**2** He did what was right in the sight of the LORD. He lived in the ways of his ancestor David. He did not turn away to the right or to the left.

**3** In the eighth year of his rule, while he was still young, he started to worship the God of his ancestor David. In the twelfth year, he started to make Judah and Jerusalem clean. He removed the high places, the Asherah poles, the carved idols, and the metal idols.

**4** In his presence the people broke down the altars of the Baals. He cut down the incense altars above them. He broke the Asherah poles, the carved idols, and the metal idols into pieces. He crushed them into dust. He threw the dust on the graves of the people who offered sacrifices to them.

**5** He burned the bones of the priests on their altars. Thus he made Judah and Jerusalem clean.

**6** He did the same in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, and in the ruins around them.

**7** He broke down the altars and the Asherah poles. He crushed the idols into powder. He cut down all the incense altars in all the land of Israel. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

**8** In the eighteenth year of his rule, Josiah made the land and the house of the LORD clean. Then he sent Shaphan, the son of Azaliah, Maaseiah, the governor of the city, and Joah, the son of Joahaz, the record keeper. He sent them to repair the house of the LORD his God.

**9** They came to Hilkiah, the high priest. They gave him the money that the people brought into the house of God. The Levites who guarded the doors collected this money. They collected it from the people of Manasseh, Ephraim, and all the rest of Israel. They also collected it from all Judah and Benjamin. Then they went back to Jerusalem.

**10** They gave the money to the men who supervised the work on the house of the LORD. These men paid the workers who repaired the house of the LORD.

**11** They gave money to the carpenters and the builders. These workers bought cut stone and wood for beams. They used the wood for the buildings that the kings of Judah let fall into ruin.

**12** The men did the work faithfully. Their supervisors were Jahath and Obadiah, Levites from the descendants of Merari. Zechariah and Meshullam, from the descendants of Kohath, also supervised the work. Other Levites who had skill with instruments of music also helped.

**13** These Levites supervised the men who carried loads. They supervised all the workers in all their different work. Some Levites were secretaries, officials, and gatekeepers.

**14** The men brought out the money that people brought into the house of the LORD. At that time Hilkiah the priest found the book of the law of the LORD that God gave through Moses.

**15** Hilkiah said to Shaphan the secretary, "I found the book of the law in the house of the LORD." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.

**16** Shaphan took the book to the king. He also gave the king a report. He said, "Your officials do all the things that you told them to do.

**17** They emptied out the money that was in the house of the LORD. They gave it to the supervisors and to the workers."

**18** Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." Shaphan read from the book to the king.

**19** The king heard the words of the law. Then he tore his clothes.

**20** The king gave a command to Hilkiah, to Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and to Abdon the son of Micah. He also gave it to Shaphan the secretary and to Asaiah, the servant of the king. He said,

**21** "Go and ask the LORD for me and for the people who remain in Israel and in Judah. Ask about the words of this book that Hilkiah found. The LORD is very angry with us. Our ancestors did not obey the word of the LORD. They did not do all the things that this book tells."

**22** Thus Hilkiah and the men that the king sent went to Huldah the prophetess. She was the wife of Shallum, the son of Tikvath, the son of Hasrah. Shallum was in charge of the clothes. Huldah lived in the Second District of Jerusalem. They told her what occurred.

**23** She said to them, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: 'Tell the man who sent you to me,

**24** "The LORD says this: Look, I will bring disaster on this place and on its people. I will bring all the curses that are in the book. The people read this book to the king of Judah.

**25** The people left me. They burned incense to other gods. They made me angry with all the idols that they made with their hands. Thus my anger will come on this place, and nothing will stop it."'

**26** The king of Judah sent you to ask the LORD. Tell him, 'The LORD, the God of Israel, says this about the words that you heard:

**27** "Your heart was sensitive, and you made yourself humble in front of God. You heard his words against this place and against its people. You made yourself humble in front of me, tore your clothes, and cried in front of me. Thus I heard you," says the LORD.

**28** "Look, I will let you die and join your ancestors. You will go to your grave in peace. You will not see the disaster that I will bring on this place and its people."'" The men took her answer back to the king.

**29** Then the king sent messengers and collected all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

**30** The king went up to the house of the LORD. All the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, the priests, and the Levites went with him. All the people, from the least important to the most important, also went. The king read to them all the words of the book of the covenant. Hilkiah found this book in the house of the LORD.

**31** The king stood in his place. He made a covenant in front of the LORD. He agreed to follow the LORD and to obey his commands, his laws, and his rules with all his heart and all his soul. He agreed to obey the words of the covenant in this book.

**32** Then he made all the people in Jerusalem and Benjamin agree to the covenant. The people of Jerusalem obeyed the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.

**33** Josiah removed all the detestable idols from all the land of the Israelites. He made all the people in Israel serve the LORD their God. While Josiah lived, they did not turn away from the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

## Chapter 35

**1** Josiah held a Passover for the LORD in Jerusalem. They killed the Passover lambs on the fourteenth day of the first month.

**2** He put the priests in their positions and encouraged them in the service of the house of the LORD.

**3** He spoke to the Levites who taught all Israel. These Levites were holy to the LORD. He said, "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon built. Solomon was the son of David, the king of Israel. You do not have to carry the ark on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel.

**4** Prepare yourselves by your families and by your divisions. Obey the written rules of David, the king of Israel, and of his son Solomon.

**5** Stand in the holy place in groups. Each group of Levites must help a group of families of the people.

**6** Kill the Passover lambs and make yourselves holy. Prepare the lambs for your relatives. Do what the LORD commanded through Moses."

**7** Josiah gave to the people 30,000 lambs and young goats from his own flocks for the Passover offerings. He also gave 3,000 bulls. He gave these animals to all the people who were there. These animals were from the possessions of the king.

**8** His officials also gave willingly to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel were the officials in charge of the house of God. They gave the priests 2,600 lambs and young goats and 300 oxen for the Passover offerings.

**9** Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethaneel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, also gave animals. They gave the Levites 5,000 lambs and young goats and 500 oxen for the Passover offerings.

**10** Thus the service was ready. The priests stood in their places, and the Levites stood in their divisions, as the king commanded.

**11** They killed the Passover lambs. The priests put the blood on the altar, and the Levites removed the skins of the animals.

**12** They put aside the burnt offerings to give them to the groups of families of the people. The people offered them to the LORD, as the book of Moses tells. They did the same with the oxen.

**13** They roasted the Passover lambs over the fire, as the law told. They boiled the other holy offerings in pots, kettles, and pans. They quickly gave the meat to all the people.

**14** After this, the Levites prepared the meat for themselves and for the priests. The priests, the descendants of Aaron, offered the burnt offerings and the fat until night. Thus the Levites prepared meat for themselves and for the priests, the descendants of Aaron.

**15** The singers, the descendants of Asaph, were in their places, as David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the seer of the king commanded. The gatekeepers stayed at each gate. They did not have to leave their posts, because their relatives the Levites prepared the meat for them.

**16** Thus all the service of the LORD was ready on that day. They held the Passover and offered burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, as King Josiah commanded.

**17** The Israelites who were there held the Passover at that time. They also held the Feast of Unleavened Bread for 7 days.

**18** Nobody held a Passover like it in Israel since the time of Samuel the prophet. None of the kings of Israel held a Passover like the Passover of Josiah. He held it with the priests, the Levites, all Judah and Israel who were there, and the people of Jerusalem.

**19** They held this Passover in the eighteenth year of the rule of Josiah.

**20** After Josiah prepared the temple, Necho, the king of Egypt, went to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates River. Josiah went out to fight against him.

**21** But Necho sent messengers to Josiah. They said, "King of Judah, this war is not your problem. I do not come to attack you today. I come to attack the nation that is at war with me. God told me to go quickly. God is with me. Stop your opposition to God, or he will destroy you."

**22** But Josiah did not turn away from Necho. Josiah changed his clothes so that people did not know him, and he went to fight. He did not listen to the words that God spoke through Necho. He went to fight in the Valley of Megiddo.

**23** Archers shot arrows at King Josiah. The king said to his servants, "Take me away, because I am badly wounded."

**24** Thus his servants took him out of his chariot. They put him in his second chariot and brought him to Jerusalem. There he died. The people buried him in the tombs of his ancestors. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.

**25** Jeremiah wrote songs of grief for Josiah. To this day, all the male and female singers sing about Josiah in their songs of grief. These songs became a custom in Israel. People wrote them in the book of Laments.

**26** The other actions of Josiah and his good deeds in obedience to the law of the LORD

**27** and all his actions, from the start to the end, are in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

## Chapter 36

**1** Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz, the son of Josiah. They made him king in Jerusalem after his father.

**2** Jehoahaz was 23 years old when he became king. He ruled for 3 months in Jerusalem.

**3** The king of Egypt removed him from the throne in Jerusalem. He made the land pay a tax of 100 talents of silver and 1 talent of gold.

**4** The king of Egypt made Eliakim, the brother of Jehoahaz, king over Judah and Jerusalem. He changed the name of Eliakim to Jehoiakim. Necho took Jehoahaz, the brother of Eliakim, to Egypt.

**5** Jehoiakim was 25 years old when he became king. He ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem. He did evil in the sight of the LORD his God.

**6** Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, attacked Jehoiakim. He put bronze chains on him to take him to Babylon.

**7** Nebuchadnezzar also took some items from the house of the LORD to Babylon. He put them in his temple in Babylon.

**8** The other actions of Jehoiakim, the detestable things that he did, and the evil in him are in a book. It is the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. Jehoiachin his son became king after him.

**9** Jehoiachin was 8 years old when he became king. He ruled for 3 months and 10 days in Jerusalem. He did evil in the sight of the LORD.

**10** In the spring, King Nebuchadnezzar sent men and brought Jehoiachin to Babylon. He also took the valuable items from the house of the LORD. He made Zedekiah, the relative of Jehoiachin, king over Judah and Jerusalem.

**11** Zedekiah was 21 years old when he became king. He ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem.

**12** He did evil in the sight of the LORD his God. Jeremiah the prophet spoke the words of the LORD to him. But Zedekiah did not make himself humble in front of Jeremiah.

**13** Zedekiah also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar. Nebuchadnezzar made him promise loyalty with an oath in the name of God. But Zedekiah was stubborn. He refused to turn back to the LORD, the God of Israel.

**14** Also, all the leaders of the priests and the people became more and more unfaithful. They did all the detestable things of the other nations. They made the house of the LORD unclean. The LORD made this house holy in Jerusalem.

**15** The LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent his messengers to them again and again. He did this because he had pity on his people and on his house.

**16** But they made fun of the messengers of God. They hated his words and laughed at his prophets. Finally the anger of the LORD came on his people, and nothing could stop it.

**17** Thus the LORD brought the king of the Babylonians against them. The king killed their young men with the sword in the holy house. He had no pity on young men or young women, on the old or the weak. God gave all of them into the power of the king.

**18** The king of Babylon took to Babylon all the items of the house of God, large and small. He took the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king and of his officials.

**19** The Babylonians burned the house of God and broke down the wall of Jerusalem. They burned all the palaces and destroyed all the valuable items.

**20** The king took the people who escaped the sword to Babylon. They became servants to him and his sons until the kingdom of Persia started to rule.

**21** Thus the word of the LORD through Jeremiah became true. The land had rest for its Sabbaths. During all the time that the land was empty, it had rest, until 70 years were complete.

**22** In the first year of Cyrus, the king of Persia, the LORD made true the word that he spoke through Jeremiah. The LORD caused Cyrus, the king of Persia, to send a message through all his kingdom. Cyrus also wrote the message. It said,

**23** "Cyrus, the king of Persia, says this: 'The LORD, the God of heaven, gave me all the kingdoms of the earth. He told me to build a house for him in Jerusalem, in Judah. Any of his people among you can go up to Jerusalem. May the LORD his God be with him.'"

---

# Ezra

## Chapter 1

**1** In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the LORD caused the words of Jeremiah to come true. The LORD moved the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia. Thus Cyrus sent a message through all his kingdom. He also wrote the message down. The message said:

**2** "Cyrus king of Persia says this: The LORD, the God of heaven, gave me all the kingdoms of the earth. He told me to build a house for him at Jerusalem in Judah.

**3** Any person among you who is one of the people of the LORD can go. Let his God be with him. Let him go up to Jerusalem in Judah. Let him build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel. He is the God who is in Jerusalem.

**4** Some of his people stay in other places. Let the men of each place help those people with silver, gold, goods and animals. They must also give free gifts (freewill offerings) for the house of God in Jerusalem."

**5** Then the leaders of the families of Judah and Benjamin got ready to go. The priests and the Levites also got ready. All the people whose spirit God moved got ready. They prepared to go up and build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.

**6** All their neighbors helped them. The neighbors gave them containers of silver, gold, goods, animals and valuable things. They gave these things in addition to all the freewill offerings.

**7** King Cyrus also brought out the containers from the house of the LORD. Nebuchadnezzar took these containers from Jerusalem. He put them in the house of his gods.

**8** Cyrus king of Persia told Mithredath the treasurer to bring out the containers. Mithredath counted them and gave them to Sheshbazzar, the leader of Judah.

**9** This is the number of the items: 30 gold dishes, 1,000 silver dishes, 29 knives,

**10** 30 gold bowls, 410 silver bowls of a second type, and 1,000 other containers.

**11** There were 5,400 gold and silver containers in total. Sheshbazzar brought all these items with him. He came with the captives who went up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

## Chapter 2

**1** These are the people of the province who came back from captivity. Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon took them away to Babylon. Now they came back to Jerusalem and Judah. Each person went to his own city.

**2** They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum and Baanah. This is the number of the men of the people of Israel:

**3** The descendants of Parosh: 2,172.

**4** The descendants of Shephatiah: 372.

**5** The descendants of Arah: 775.

**6** The descendants of Pahath-moab, through Jeshua and Joab: 2,812.

**7** The descendants of Elam: 1,254.

**8** The descendants of Zattu: 945.

**9** The descendants of Zaccai: 760.

**10** The descendants of Bani: 642.

**11** The descendants of Bebai: 623.

**12** The descendants of Azgad: 1,222.

**13** The descendants of Adonikam: 666.

**14** The descendants of Bigvai: 2,056.

**15** The descendants of Adin: 454.

**16** The descendants of Ater, through Hezekiah: 98.

**17** The descendants of Bezai: 323.

**18** The descendants of Jorah: 112.

**19** The descendants of Hashum: 223.

**20** The descendants of Gibbar: 95.

**21** The people of Bethlehem: 123.

**22** The men of Netophah: 56.

**23** The men of Anathoth: 128.

**24** The people of Azmaveth: 42.

**25** The people of Kirjath-arim, Chephirah and Beeroth: 743.

**26** The people of Ramah and Gaba: 621.

**27** The men of Michmas: 122.

**28** The men of Bethel and Ai: 223.

**29** The people of Nebo: 52.

**30** The people of Magbish: 156.

**31** The descendants of the other Elam: 1,254.

**32** The descendants of Harim: 320.

**33** The people of Lod, Hadid and Ono: 725.

**34** The people of Jericho: 345.

**35** The people of Senaah: 3,630.

**36** The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the family of Jeshua: 973.

**37** The descendants of Immer: 1,052.

**38** The descendants of Pashur: 1,247.

**39** The descendants of Harim: 1,017.

**40** The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, through Hodaviah: 74.

**41** The singers: the descendants of Asaph: 128.

**42** The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita and Shobai: 139 in total.

**43** The temple servants (Nethinims): the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,

**44** Keros, Siaha, Padon,

**45** Lebanah, Hagabah, Akkub,

**46** Hagab, Shalmai, Hanan,

**47** Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah,

**48** Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam,

**49** Uzza, Paseah, Besai,

**50** Asnah, Mehunim, Nephusim,

**51** Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,

**52** Bazluth, Mehida, Harsha,

**53** Barkos, Sisera, Thamah,

**54** Neziah and Hatipha.

**55** The descendants of the servants of Solomon: the descendants of Sotai, Sophereth, Peruda,

**56** Jaalah, Darkon, Giddel,

**57** Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth of Zebaim and Ami.

**58** The Nethinims and the descendants of the servants of Solomon: 392 in total.

**59** Some people came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsa, Cherub, Addan and Immer. But they could not show the family of their fathers. They could not show that they were from Israel.

**60** These were the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah and Nekoda: 652.

**61** Some of the descendants of the priests also could not show their family. These were the descendants of Habaiah, Koz and Barzillai. Barzillai married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite. He took the name of her family.

**62** These men looked for their names in the family records. But they did not find their names. Thus the leaders did not let them work as priests, because they were not clean.

**63** The governor (Tirshatha) told them not to eat the most holy food. They had to wait until a priest came who could use the Urim and Thummim.

**64** The total number of all the people was 42,360.

**65** In addition, there were 7,337 male and female servants. There were also 200 male and female singers.

**66** They had 736 horses and 245 mules.

**67** They had 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.

**68** Some of the family leaders came to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. They gave free gifts for the house of God. They wanted to build the house again on its site.

**69** Each person gave as much as he could to the fund for the work. They gave 61,000 gold coins, 5,000 pounds of silver and 100 clothes for the priests.

**70** The priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers and the Nethinims lived in their cities. All the other people of Israel also lived in their cities.

## Chapter 3

**1** The seventh month came, and the people of Israel were in their cities. Then all the people came together in Jerusalem as one person.

**2** Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brothers the priests started to work. Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers also worked. They built the altar of the God of Israel. They wanted to offer burnt offerings on the altar. The law of Moses, the man of God, tells them to do this.

**3** They put the altar on its foundation. They were afraid of the people of the countries around them. They offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar each morning and each evening.

**4** They also kept the Festival of Shelters (Tabernacles), as the law tells them. Each day they offered the correct number of burnt offerings for that day.

**5** After that, they offered the regular burnt offerings. They offered the offerings for the new moons and for all the holy festivals of the LORD. They also offered the freewill offerings that the people gave to the LORD.

**6** On the first day of the seventh month, they started to offer burnt offerings to the LORD. But they did not yet put down the foundation of the temple of the LORD.

**7** They gave money to the stone workers and to the carpenters. They gave food, drink and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre. Then these people brought cedar trees from Lebanon by sea to Joppa. King Cyrus of Persia gave permission for this.

**8** They came to the house of God at Jerusalem. In the 2nd month of the 2nd year after that, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel started the work. Jeshua the son of Jozadak, the other priests and the Levites helped. All the people who came back from captivity to Jerusalem also helped. They put the Levites who were 20 years old or more in control of the work on the house of the LORD.

**9** Jeshua, his sons and his brothers worked together with Kadmiel and his sons, the descendants of Judah. They controlled the workers on the house of God. The sons of Henadad and their sons and brothers, the Levites, also helped.

**10** The builders put down the foundation of the temple of the LORD. Then the priests stood in their special clothes with trumpets. The Levites, the sons of Asaph, stood with cymbals. They praised the LORD, as David king of Israel told them to do.

**11** They sang in groups. They praised the LORD and gave thanks to him. They sang, "He is good. His love for Israel continues always." All the people shouted loudly and praised the LORD. They shouted because the foundation of the house of the LORD was in its position.

**12** Many of the older priests, Levites and family leaders saw the first house. When they saw the foundation of this new house, they cried loudly. But many other people shouted with joy.

**13** The people could not hear the difference between the shouts of joy and the sounds of the people who cried. The people shouted very loudly. People far away heard the noise.

## Chapter 4

**1** The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the former captives built a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel.

**2** Then the enemies came to Zerubbabel and to the family leaders. They said, "Let us build with you. We worship your God, as you do. We made sacrifices to him since the time of Esarhaddon king of Assyria. He brought us here."

**3** But Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the other family leaders of Israel answered them. They said, "You will not help us build a house for our God. We alone will build it for the LORD, the God of Israel. King Cyrus, the king of Persia, told us to do this."

**4** Then the people of the land tried to make the people of Judah weak. They tried to make the people of Judah afraid to build.

**5** They paid advisers to work against them and to stop their plans. They did this during all the rule of Cyrus king of Persia, until the rule of Darius king of Persia.

**6** At the start of the rule of Ahasuerus, the enemies wrote an accusation against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.

**7** In the time of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and their companions wrote a letter to Artaxerxes king of Persia. They wrote the letter in the Aramaic language. Someone also translated the letter.

**8** Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes. The letter said this:

**9** "From Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe and their companions. The companions are the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites and the Archevites. They are also the Babylonians, the Susanchites, the Dehavites and the Elamites.

**10** They are also the other nations that the great and famous Ashurbanipal (Asnappar) took from their countries. He put them in the cities of Samaria and in the other places west of the Euphrates River."

**11** This is a copy of the letter that they sent to King Artaxerxes: "To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the men west of the river.

**12** We tell the king this: The Jews who came up from you to us went to Jerusalem. They build that bad city again. That city always fights against kings. They finish the walls and repair the foundations.

**13** We tell the king this: If the people build this city and finish the walls, they will not pay taxes. Then the money that comes to the king will become less.

**14** We get our food from the palace of the king. We do not want to see the king lose his honor. Thus we send this message to the king.

**15** Look in the books of records of your fathers. In the records you will find that this city fights against kings and provinces. It causes much trouble. Long ago, the people of the city caused revolts. Because of this, a king destroyed the city.

**16** We tell the king this. Possibly the people will build this city again and finish its walls. If they do, you will lose your control of the land west of the river."

**17** Then the king sent an answer to Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe and their companions in Samaria and west of the river. He wrote, "Peace to you.

**18** My officials read the letter that you sent to us. They read it clearly to me.

**19** I gave an order, and my officials searched the records. They found that, long ago, this city fought against kings. Revolts and fights started there.

**20** Strong kings ruled over Jerusalem. These kings ruled over all the land west of the river. The people paid taxes to them.

**21** Now give an order to stop these men. They must not build this city until I give another order.

**22** Be careful to do this. Do not let more damage come to the kings."

**23** Rehum, Shimshai the scribe and their companions heard the letter of King Artaxerxes. Then they quickly went to the Jews in Jerusalem. They used force to make the Jews stop.

**24** Thus the work on the house of God in Jerusalem stopped. The work stayed stopped until the second year of the rule of Darius king of Persia.

## Chapter 5

**1** Then the prophets Haggai and Zechariah the son of Iddo spoke to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem. They spoke in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.

**2** Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak started to build the house of God in Jerusalem again. The prophets of God were with them and helped them.

**3** At that time Tattenai (Tatnai), the governor west of the river, came to them. Shethar-boznai and their companions also came. They asked the Jews, "Who gave you permission to build this house and to finish this wall?"

**4** They also asked, "What are the names of the men who build this building?"

**5** But God watched over the elders of the Jews. The officials did not stop the work until they sent a report to Darius. They waited for a letter from him about this matter.

**6** This is a copy of the letter that Tatnai, Shethar-boznai and their companions sent to King Darius. Their companions were the officials west of the river.

**7** The letter that they sent to him said this: "To King Darius. All peace to you.

**8** We tell the king this: We went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. The people build it with large stones. They put wood beams in the walls. The work goes quickly and well under their control.

**9** We asked the elders, 'Who gave you permission to build this house and to finish these walls?'

**10** We also asked their names. We wanted to write down the names of their leaders for you.

**11** They gave us this answer: 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth. We build again the house that a great king of Israel built and finished many years ago.

**12** But our fathers made the God of heaven angry. Thus he gave them to Nebuchadnezzar the Chaldean, king of Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar destroyed this house. He took the people away to Babylon.

**13** But in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus gave an order to build this house of God again.

**14** Nebuchadnezzar took the gold and silver containers of the house of God from the temple in Jerusalem. He put them in the temple in Babylon. King Cyrus took these containers out of the temple in Babylon. He gave them to a man with the name Sheshbazzar. Cyrus made Sheshbazzar governor.

**15** Cyrus told him, "Take these containers. Go and put them in the temple in Jerusalem. Build the house of God again on its site."

**16** Then Sheshbazzar came and put down the foundation of the house of God in Jerusalem. From that time until now, the people build it. But the work is not complete.'

**17** If the king agrees, let his officials search the record rooms of the king in Babylon. Let them find if King Cyrus gave an order to build this house of God in Jerusalem. Then let the king send us his decision about this matter."

## Chapter 6

**1** Then King Darius gave an order. His officials searched the record rooms in Babylon, where the treasures were.

**2** In the palace at Ecbatana (Achmetha), in the province of the Medes, they found a scroll. The scroll had this record on it:

**3** "In the first year of King Cyrus, the king gave an order about the house of God at Jerusalem. Let the people build the house again as a place to offer sacrifices. Let them put down strong foundations. The house must be 60 cubits high and 60 cubits wide.

**4** It must have 3 layers of large stones and 1 layer of new wood. The money for the work must come from the treasury of the king.

**5** Nebuchadnezzar took the gold and silver containers of the house of God from the temple in Jerusalem. He brought them to Babylon. Give these containers back. Take each container back to its place in the temple in Jerusalem. Put them in the house of God."

**6** Darius wrote, "Now, Tatnai, governor west of the river, Shethar-boznai and your companions, the officials west of the river: stay away from that place.

**7** Do not stop the work on this house of God. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God on its site.

**8** I also give an order about how you must help these elders of the Jews to build this house of God. Pay all the costs of these men from the money of the king. Use the taxes from the land west of the river. Pay them quickly, so that the work does not stop.

**9** Give the priests in Jerusalem all that they need each day without fail. Give them young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven. Give them wheat, salt, wine and oil, as the priests ask.

**10** Then they can offer sacrifices that please the God of heaven. They can pray for the life of the king and of his sons.

**11** I also give this order: If a person changes this order, pull a wood beam from his house. Put the beam up and hang that person on it. Make his house a pile of waste because of his crime.

**12** God caused his name to live in Jerusalem. Let God destroy any king or nation that tries to change this order or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, give this order. Obey it quickly."

**13** Then Tatnai, governor west of the river, Shethar-boznai and their companions quickly obeyed the order of King Darius.

**14** The elders of the Jews continued to build, and the work went well. The prophet Haggai and Zechariah the son of Iddo encouraged them with their messages. The Jews completed the building. They obeyed the command of the God of Israel. They also obeyed the orders of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia.

**15** The people completed this house on the third day of the month Adar. This was in the sixth year of the rule of King Darius.

**16** Then the people of Israel celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy. The priests, the Levites and all the other former captives were there.

**17** For the dedication of this house of God, they offered 100 bulls, 200 rams and 400 lambs. As a sin offering for all Israel, they offered 12 male goats, 1 for each tribe of Israel.

**18** They put the priests in their groups and the Levites in their divisions for the service of God in Jerusalem. They did this as the book of Moses tells them.

**19** On the 14th day of the first month, the former captives kept the Passover.

**20** The priests and the Levites made themselves clean together. All of them were clean. The Levites killed the Passover lambs for all the former captives, for the priests and for themselves.

**21** The people of Israel who came back from captivity ate the Passover. Other people also ate with them. These people separated themselves from the unclean practices of the nations of the land. They wanted to worship the LORD, the God of Israel.

**22** For 7 days they kept the Festival of Bread Without Yeast with joy. The LORD made them happy. He changed the attitude of the king of Assyria toward them. Thus the king helped them in the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.

## Chapter 7

**1** After these things, during the rule of Artaxerxes king of Persia, there was a man with the name Ezra. Ezra was the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,

**2** the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,

**3** the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,

**4** the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,

**5** the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest.

**6** This Ezra went up from Babylon. He was a scribe who knew the law of Moses very well. The LORD, the God of Israel, gave that law. The LORD his God helped Ezra. Thus the king gave Ezra all that he asked for.

**7** Some of the people of Israel also went up to Jerusalem with him. Some priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers and Nethinims went. This was in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.

**8** Ezra came to Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of the king.

**9** He started the journey from Babylon on the first day of the first month. He came to Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month. The good hand of his God was on him.

**10** Ezra decided to study the law of the LORD and to obey it. He also decided to teach the rules and laws of the LORD in Israel.

**11** This is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra. Ezra was the priest and the scribe. He was a scholar of the commands and the rules that the LORD gave to Israel.

**12** "From Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven. Peace to you.

**13** I give this order: Any person in my kingdom from the people of Israel can go with you to Jerusalem. This includes the priests and the Levites. Each person who wants to go can go.

**14** The king and his 7 advisers send you. Find out about the conditions in Judah and Jerusalem. Use the law of your God, which is in your hand.

**15** Take the silver and gold that the king and his advisers freely give to the God of Israel. His home is in Jerusalem.

**16** Also take all the silver and gold that you can get in the province of Babylon. Take the freewill offerings of the people and of the priests for the house of their God in Jerusalem.

**17** With this money, quickly buy bulls, rams and lambs. Also buy their grain offerings and drink offerings. Offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.

**18** You and your brothers can use the rest of the silver and gold as you think best. Do what your God wants.

**19** The officials will give you containers for the service in the house of your God. Give all these containers to the God of Jerusalem.

**20** The house of your God will need other things. Pay for these things from the treasury of the king.

**21** I, King Artaxerxes, give an order to all the treasurers west of the river. Ezra the priest is the scribe of the law of the God of heaven. Quickly give him all that he asks for.

**22** Give him up to 100 talents of silver and 100 measures of wheat. Give him up to 100 baths of wine and 100 baths of oil. Give him as much salt as he needs.

**23** Carefully do all that the God of heaven commands for his house. Do not let God become angry with the kingdom of the king and his sons.

**24** We also tell you this: You must not make the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinims or other workers of this house of God pay taxes.

**25** You, Ezra, have the wisdom of your God. Use that wisdom to choose officials and judges. They will judge all the people west of the river who know the laws of your God. Teach the laws to the people who do not know them.

**26** Some people will not obey the law of your God and the law of the king. Punish these people quickly. Kill them, or send them away, or take their property, or put them in prison."

**27** Ezra said, "Praise the LORD, the God of our fathers! He caused the king to want to make the house of the LORD in Jerusalem beautiful.

**28** He caused the king, his advisers and all his strong officials to be kind to me. The LORD my God helped me and made me strong. Thus I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me."

## Chapter 8

**1** These are the family leaders who went up with me from Babylon during the rule of King Artaxerxes. These are their family records:

**2** From the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom. From the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel. From the descendants of David, Hattush.

**3** From the descendants of Shechaniah and Pharosh, Zechariah. With him there were 150 males in the family records.

**4** From the descendants of Pahath-moab, Elihoenai the son of Zerahiah, and 200 males with him.

**5** From the descendants of Shechaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and 300 males with him.

**6** From the descendants of Adin, Ebed the son of Jonathan, and 50 males with him.

**7** From the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah, and 70 males with him.

**8** From the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the son of Michael, and 80 males with him.

**9** From the descendants of Joab, Obadiah the son of Jehiel, and 218 males with him.

**10** From the descendants of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and 160 males with him.

**11** From the descendants of Bebai, Zechariah the son of Bebai, and 28 males with him.

**12** From the descendants of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and 110 males with him.

**13** From the last descendants of Adonikam, Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah, and 60 males with them.

**14** From the descendants of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud, and 70 males with them.

**15** I gathered them together at the river that flows to Ahava. We stayed there in tents for 3 days. I looked at the people and the priests. I found no Levites there.

**16** Then I sent for some leaders: Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah and Meshullam. I also sent for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were wise teachers.

**17** I sent them to Iddo, the leader at the place Casiphia. I told them what to say to Iddo and to his relatives, the Nethinims, at Casiphia. They had to ask for workers for the house of our God.

**18** The good hand of our God was on us. Thus they brought us a wise man from the descendants of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel. His name was Sherebiah. They also brought his sons and brothers, 18 men in total.

**19** They also brought Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from the descendants of Merari. They brought the brothers of Jeshaiah and their sons, 20 men in total.

**20** They also brought 220 Nethinims. David and the officials gave the Nethinims the work to help the Levites. We wrote down the name of each of these men.

**21** There, at the river of Ahava, I told the people to fast. We made ourselves humble in front of our God. We asked him for a safe journey for us, our children and all our property.

**22** I felt shame to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the road. We told the king, "The hand of our God is on all who look for him. He helps them. But his power and his anger are against all who leave him."

**23** Thus we fasted and asked our God to protect us. He answered our prayer.

**24** Then I chose 12 of the leaders of the priests: Sherebiah, Hashabiah and 10 of their brothers.

**25** I weighed the silver, the gold and the containers, and gave them to the priests. These items were the offering for the house of our God. The king, his advisers, his officials and all the Israelites there gave this offering.

**26** I weighed and gave to them 650 talents of silver. I also gave them silver containers that weighed 100 talents, and 100 talents of gold.

**27** I also gave them 20 gold bowls with a value of 1,000 darics. I gave them 2 containers of good bronze. These were as valuable as gold.

**28** I told them, "You are holy to the LORD. The containers are also holy. The silver and the gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers.

**29** Guard these things carefully. Weigh them in the rooms of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. Weigh them in front of the leaders of the priests, the Levites and the family leaders of Israel."

**30** Then the priests and the Levites took the silver, the gold and the containers that I weighed. They had to bring these things to the house of our God in Jerusalem.

**31** We left the river of Ahava on the 12th day of the first month to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was on us. He protected us from enemies and from robbers on the road.

**32** We came to Jerusalem and stayed there for 3 days.

**33** On the fourth day, in the house of our God, we weighed the silver, the gold and the containers. We gave them to Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest. Eleazar the son of Phinehas was with him. The Levites Jozabad the son of Jeshua and Noadiah the son of Binnui were also with them.

**34** They counted and weighed each item. They wrote down the total weight at that time.

**35** Then the former captives who came back offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel. They offered 12 bulls for all Israel, 96 rams and 77 lambs. They also offered 12 male goats as a sin offering. All these were a burnt offering to the LORD.

**36** They gave the orders of the king to the officials of the king and to the governors west of the river. Then these officials helped the people and the house of God.

## Chapter 9

**1** After these things, the leaders came to me. They said, "The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites did not separate themselves from the people of the lands. They do the detestable things that those people do. These people are the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians and Amorites.

**2** The Israelites married some of the daughters of these people. They let their sons marry these women too. Thus the holy people mixed with the people of those lands. The leaders and officials were the first to do this wrong."

**3** When I heard this, I tore my clothes and my coat. I pulled out hair from my head and my beard. I sat down. I was very shocked.

**4** Then all the people who feared the words of the God of Israel came to me. They were afraid because of the sin of the former captives. I sat there shocked until the evening sacrifice.

**5** At the time of the evening sacrifice, I stood up from my sadness. I tore my clothes and my coat. Then I went down on my knees. I held out my hands to the LORD my God.

**6** I said, "My God, I feel shame. I cannot lift up my face to you, my God. Our sins are higher than our heads. Our guilt goes up to the heavens.

**7** Since the time of our fathers, our guilt is very great. Because of our sins, you gave us, our kings and our priests to the kings of other lands. They killed us with swords. They took us as captives. They took our property. They made us ashamed, as we are today.

**8** But now, for a short time, the LORD our God was kind to us. He let a small group of us escape. He gave us a safe place in his holy place. Our God gave us hope. He gave us a little new life while we are slaves.

**9** We are slaves. But our God did not leave us while we are slaves. He caused the kings of Persia to be kind to us. He gave us new life. Thus we can build the house of our God again and repair it. He gave us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.

**10** Now, our God, what can we say after this? We did not obey your commands.

**11** You gave these commands through your servants the prophets. They said, 'The land that you will take is unclean. The people of the lands made it unclean with their detestable practices. They filled the land with their dirt from one end to the other.

**12** Thus do not let your daughters marry their sons. Do not let your sons marry their daughters. Never try to make peace with them or help them become rich. Then you will be strong and eat the good things of the land. You will give the land to your children for all time.'

**13** All these bad things came to us because of our evil actions and our great guilt. But you, our God, punished us less than our sins deserve. You let some of us escape.

**14** Thus we must not again disobey your commands. We must not marry the people who do these detestable things. If we do, you will be angry with us. You will destroy us until no person stays alive or escapes.

**15** LORD God of Israel, you are righteous. You let a small group of us escape, as we are today. Look, we stand in front of you with our guilt. Because of this, no person can stand in front of you."

## Chapter 10

**1** Ezra prayed and confessed the sins. He cried and lay on the ground in front of the house of God. A very large group of Israelite men, women and children came to him. The people also cried very much.

**2** Shechaniah the son of Jehiel, from the descendants of Elam, spoke to Ezra. He said, "We were not loyal to our God. We married foreign women from the people of the land. But there is still hope for Israel.

**3** Let us make an agreement (covenant) with our God. We will send away all these wives and their children. We will do as my lord and the people who fear the command of our God advise. We will obey the law.

**4** Stand up. You must control this matter. We will help you. Be brave and do it."

**5** Then Ezra stood up. He made the leaders of the priests, the Levites and all Israel promise to do this. They made the promise.

**6** Then Ezra went away from the house of God. He went into the room of Jehohanan (Johanan) the son of Eliashib. There he did not eat food or drink water. He was very sad because of the sin of the former captives.

**7** Then the leaders sent a message through all Judah and Jerusalem to all the former captives. The message told them to come together in Jerusalem.

**8** The leaders and the elders decided this: If a person does not come within 3 days, they will take all his property. They will also send him out of the group of former captives.

**9** Within 3 days all the men of Judah and Benjamin came together in Jerusalem. It was the 20th day of the ninth month. All the people sat in the square in front of the house of God. They shook with fear because of this matter and because of the heavy rain.

**10** Ezra the priest stood up and spoke to them. He said, "You were not loyal to God. You married foreign women. Thus you made the guilt of Israel greater.

**11** Now confess your sin to the LORD, the God of your fathers. Do what he wants. Separate yourselves from the people of the land and from your foreign wives."

**12** All the people answered with a loud voice. They said, "You are right! We must do as you say.

**13** But there are many people here, and it is the season of heavy rain. We cannot stand outside. This work will take more than 1 or 2 days. Many of us did this sin.

**14** Let our leaders act for all the people. Let each man in our cities who married a foreign woman come at a specified time. Let the elders and judges of each city come with him. Then the strong anger of our God about this matter will go away from us."

**15** Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahaziah the son of Tikvah disagreed with this plan. Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them.

**16** But the former captives did as they agreed. Ezra the priest chose some family leaders, 1 from each family. He chose each leader by name. On the first day of the tenth month, they sat down to examine the matter.

**17** By the first day of the first month, they completed the work. They examined all the men who married foreign women.

**18** Some of the descendants of the priests married foreign women. From the descendants of Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brothers, these men married foreign women: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib and Gedaliah.

**19** These men promised to send away their wives. They were guilty. Thus each man offered a ram from the flock as a guilt offering.

**20** From the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.

**21** From the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel and Uzziah.

**22** From the descendants of Pashur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethaneel, Jozabad and Elasah.

**23** From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (also with the name Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah and Eliezer.

**24** From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem and Uri.

**25** From the other Israelites: From the descendants of Parosh: Ramiah, Jeziah, Malchiah, Miamin, Eleazar, Malchijah and Benaiah.

**26** From the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth and Eliah.

**27** From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad and Aziza.

**28** From the descendants of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai and Athlai.

**29** From the descendants of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal and Ramoth.

**30** From the descendants of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezaleel, Binnui and Manasseh.

**31** From the descendants of Harim: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchiah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,

**32** Benjamin, Malluch and Shemariah.

**33** From the descendants of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattathah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh and Shimei.

**34** From the descendants of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,

**35** Benaiah, Bedeiah, Chelluh,

**36** Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,

**37** Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasau,

**38** Bani, Binnui, Shimei,

**39** Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,

**40** Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,

**41** Azareel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,

**42** Shallum, Amariah and Joseph.

**43** From the descendants of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jadau, Joel and Benaiah.

**44** All these men married foreign women. Some of them had children with these wives.
