**10** and their brothers Shebaniah, Hodijah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,

**11** Micha, Rehob, Hashabiah,

**12** Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,

**13** Hodijah, Bani and Beninu.

**14** The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zatthu, Bani,

**15** Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,

**16** Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,

**17** Ater, Hizkijah, Azzur,

**18** Hodijah, Hashum, Bezai,

**19** Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,

**20** Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,

**21** Meshezabeel, Zadok, Jaddua,

**22** Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,

**23** Hoshea, Hananiah, Hashub,

**24** Hallohesh, Pileha, Shobek,

**25** Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,

**26** Ahijah, Hanan, Anan,

**27** Malluch, Harim and Baanah.

**28** The other people also joined: the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers and the Nethinims. All the people who separated themselves from the people of the lands to obey the law of God joined. Their wives, sons and daughters who could understand also joined.

**29** They joined their brothers, the nobles. They made a solemn promise. They agreed to accept a curse if they did not keep the promise. They promised to obey the law of God that God gave through his servant Moses. They promised to carefully obey all the commands, laws and rules of the LORD our Lord.

**30** "We will not let our daughters marry the people of the land. We will not let our sons marry their daughters.

**31** The people of the land will bring goods or grain to sell on the Sabbath day. We will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on any holy day. Every seventh year we will not farm the land. In that year we will cancel all debts.

**32** We also accept the duty to give one-third of a shekel each year for the service of the house of our God.

**33** This money will pay for the holy bread and the regular grain offerings. It will pay for the regular burnt offerings on the Sabbaths, the new moons and the festivals. It will pay for the holy offerings and for the sin offerings that make atonement for Israel. It will pay for all the work of the house of our God.

**34** We, the priests, the Levites and the people, used lots to choose the times for the wood offering. Each family will bring wood to the house of our God at its specified time each year. The wood will burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as the law says.

**35** Each year we will bring to the house of the LORD the first part of our crops. We will also bring the first fruit of all our trees.

**36** As the law says, we will bring our firstborn sons and the firstborn of our cattle. We will bring the firstborn of our herds and flocks to the house of our God. We will give them to the priests who serve in the house of our God.

**37** We will bring to the priests the first part of our dough and our grain offerings. We will bring the fruit of all our trees, our new wine and our oil. We will bring them to the storerooms of the house of our God. We will bring one-tenth of our crops to the Levites. The Levites will collect the tenth in all the towns where we farm.

**38** A priest, a descendant of Aaron, will be with the Levites when they collect the tenths. The Levites will bring one-tenth of the tenths to the house of our God. They will put it in the storerooms of the treasury.

**39** The people of Israel and the Levites must bring the offerings of grain, new wine and oil to the storerooms. The containers of the temple are in these rooms. The priests who serve, the gatekeepers and the singers stay there. We will not forget the house of our God."

## Chapter 11

**1** The leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem. The other people used lots to choose 1 family from each 10 families to live in Jerusalem, the holy city. The other 9 families lived in other cities.

**2** The people praised all the men who agreed to live in Jerusalem.

**3** These are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem. Other Israelites, priests, Levites, Nethinims and descendants of the servants of Solomon lived in the cities of Judah. Each person lived on his own property in his own city.

**4** Some descendants of Judah and of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. From the descendants of Judah, there was Athaiah the son of Uzziah. Uzziah was the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalaleel. Mahalaleel was from the descendants of Perez.

**5** Also Maaseiah the son of Baruch lived there. Baruch was the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah. Adaiah was the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of Shiloni.

**6** There were 468 brave men from the descendants of Perez who lived in Jerusalem.

**7** These are the descendants of Benjamin. There was Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah. Pedaiah was the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jesaiah.

**8** After him there were Gabbai and Sallai. In total there were 928 men.

**9** Joel the son of Zichri was their supervisor. Judah the son of Senuah was second in command over the city.

**10** From the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, and Jachin.

**11** Seraiah the son of Hilkiah was the leader in the house of God. Hilkiah was the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub.

**12** Their brothers who did the work in the temple were 822 men. Also there was Adaiah the son of Jeroham. Jeroham was the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchiah.

**13** His brothers, who were family leaders, were 242 men. Amashai the son of Azareel was also there. Amashai was the son of Azareel, the son of Ahasai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer.

**14** Their brothers were brave men, 128 in total. Their supervisor was Zabdiel, the son of one of the great men.

**15** From the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hashub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni.

**16** Shabbethai and Jozabad were leaders of the Levites. They controlled the work outside the house of God.

**17** Mattaniah the son of Micha, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, was the leader of the singers. He started the songs of thanks and prayer. Bakbukiah was second among his brothers. Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun, was also there.

**18** There were 284 Levites in total in the holy city.

**19** The gatekeepers were Akkub, Talmon and their brothers, who guarded the gates. There were 172 of them.

**20** The other Israelites, priests and Levites lived in all the cities of Judah. Each person lived on his own property.

**21** The Nethinims lived on the hill of Ophel. Ziha and Gispa were in control of the Nethinims.

**22** The supervisor of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micha. Uzzi was one of the descendants of Asaph, the singers. These singers were in control of the work in the house of God.

**23** The king gave an order about the singers. They had to get a specified share of food each day.

**24** Pethahiah the son of Meshezabeel was from the descendants of Zerah the son of Judah. He helped the king in all matters about the people.

**25** Some of the people of Judah lived in villages with their fields. They lived in Kirjath-arba and its villages, in Dibon and its villages, and in Jekabzeel and its villages.

**26** They lived in Jeshua, Moladah and Beth-phelet.

**27** They lived in Hazar-shual, and in Beersheba and its villages.

**28** They lived in Ziklag, and in Mekonah and its villages.

**29** They lived in En-rimmon, Zareah and Jarmuth.

**30** They lived in Zanoah, Adullam and their villages. They lived in Lachish and its fields, and in Azekah and its villages. Thus they lived from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.

**31** The people of Benjamin from Geba lived in Michmash, Aija, Bethel and their villages.

**32** They lived in Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,

**33** Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,

**34** Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,

**35** Lod and Ono, the valley of the craftsmen.

**36** Some groups of the Levites lived in Judah, and other groups lived in Benjamin.

## Chapter 12

**1** These are the priests and the Levites who came back with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,

**2** Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,

**3** Shechaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,

**4** Iddo, Ginnetho, Abijah,

**5** Miamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,

**6** Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,

**7** Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah and Jedaiah. These were the leaders of the priests and of their brothers in the time of Jeshua.

**8** The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah and Mattaniah. Mattaniah and his brothers were in control of the songs of thanks.

**9** Their brothers Bakbukiah and Unni stood opposite them during the services.

**10** Jeshua became the father of Joiakim. Joiakim became the father of Eliashib. Eliashib became the father of Joiada.

**11** Joiada became the father of Jonathan. Jonathan became the father of Jaddua.

**12** In the time of Joiakim, these priests were the leaders of the families: Meraiah was the leader of the family of Seraiah. Hananiah was the leader of the family of Jeremiah.

**13** Meshullam led the family of Ezra. Jehohanan led the family of Amariah.

**14** Jonathan led the family of Melicu. Joseph led the family of Shebaniah.

**15** Adna led the family of Harim. Helkai led the family of Meraioth.

**16** Zechariah led the family of Iddo. Meshullam led the family of Ginnethon.

**17** Zichri led the family of Abijah. There was also a leader of the family of Miniamin. Piltai led the family of Moadiah.

**18** Shammua led the family of Bilgah. Jehonathan led the family of Shemaiah.

**19** Mattenai led the family of Joiarib. Uzzi led the family of Jedaiah.

**20** Kallai led the family of Sallai. Eber led the family of Amok.

**21** Hashabiah led the family of Hilkiah. Nethaneel led the family of Jedaiah.

**22** In the time of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua, the scribes wrote down the family leaders of the Levites. They also wrote down the family leaders of the priests, until the rule of Darius the Persian.

**23** The family leaders of the descendants of Levi are in the book of the records. The records continue until the time of Johanan the son of Eliashib.

**24** The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel. Their brothers stood opposite them to praise God and to give thanks. Each group answered the other group. David, the man of God, gave this command.

**25** Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon and Akkub were gatekeepers. They guarded the storerooms at the gates.

**26** These men served in the time of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak. They also served in the time of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest and scribe.

**27** The people prepared for the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem. They looked for the Levites in all the places where they lived. They brought the Levites to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with joy. The Levites gave thanks and sang with cymbals, harps and lyres.

**28** The singers came together from the area around Jerusalem. They came from the villages of the Netophathites.

**29** They also came from Beth-gilgal and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth. The singers built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.

**30** The priests and the Levites made themselves clean. Then they made the people, the gates and the wall clean.

**31** Then I brought the leaders of Judah up on top of the wall. I chose 2 large choirs to give thanks. One choir went to the right on the wall, toward the Dung Gate.

**32** Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah followed them.

**33** Azariah, Ezra and Meshullam also followed,

**34** with Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah and Jeremiah.

**35** Some of the sons of the priests also followed with trumpets. One of them was Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah. Shemaiah was the son of Mattaniah, the son of Michaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph.

**36** His brothers also went. They were Shemaiah, Azarael, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethaneel, Judah and Hanani. They had the musical instruments of David, the man of God. Ezra the scribe walked in front of them.

**37** At the Fountain Gate they went straight up the stairs of the City of David. They went up where the wall goes up, above the house of David. They continued to the Water Gate on the east.

**38** The second choir went to the left. I followed them with half of the people on top of the wall. We went past the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall.

**39** We went over the Gate of Ephraim, the Old Gate and the Fish Gate. We went past the Tower of Hananeel and the Tower of Meah to the Sheep Gate. We stopped at the Prison Gate.

**40** Then the 2 choirs that gave thanks took their positions in the house of God. I also stood there with half of the officials.

**41** The priests stood there with trumpets. They were Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Michaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah and Hananiah.

**42** Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam and Ezer also stood there. The singers sang loudly. Jezrahiah was their leader.

**43** On that day the people offered many sacrifices. They were very happy, because God gave them great joy. The women and children were also happy. People far away heard the sound of joy from Jerusalem.

**44** At that time some men had the duty to control the storerooms. These rooms held the offerings, the first part of the crops and the tenths. The men had to collect into these rooms the shares that the law gives to the priests and Levites. They collected these shares from the fields around the cities. The people of Judah were happy with the priests and the Levites who served.

**45** The priests and Levites did the service of their God and the service of purification. The singers and the gatekeepers also did their work. They did all this as David and his son Solomon commanded.

**46** Long ago, in the time of David and Asaph, there were leaders of the singers. There were songs of praise and thanks to God.

**47** In the time of Zerubbabel and of Nehemiah, all Israel gave food each day to the singers and the gatekeepers. They also gave a share to the Levites. The Levites gave a share to the descendants of Aaron.

## Chapter 13

**1** On that day the leaders read the book of Moses to the people. In the book they found this law: No Ammonite or Moabite can ever come into the assembly of God.

**2** The Ammonites and the Moabites did not give food and water to the Israelites. Instead, they paid Balaam to curse the Israelites. But our God changed the curse into a blessing.

**3** When the people heard this law, they separated all foreigners from Israel.

**4** Before this, Eliashib the priest was in control of the storerooms of the house of our God. He was a relative of Tobiah.

**5** Eliashib prepared a large room for Tobiah. Before that time, the priests kept the grain offerings, the frankincense and the containers in that room. They also kept the tenths of the grain, the new wine and the oil there. The law gave these things to the Levites, the singers and the gatekeepers. The room also held the offerings for the priests.

**6** During all this time I was not in Jerusalem. In the 32nd year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, I went back to the king. After some time I asked the king for permission to leave.

**7** Then I came back to Jerusalem. I found out about the evil thing that Eliashib did for Tobiah. Eliashib gave Tobiah a room in the courtyards of the house of God.

**8** I was very angry. I threw all the furniture of Tobiah out of the room.

**9** Then I gave an order, and the people made the rooms clean. Then I brought back the containers of the house of God into the rooms. I also brought back the grain offerings and the frankincense.

**10** I also found out that the people did not give the Levites their shares. Thus the Levites and the singers who did the work went back to their own fields.

**11** Thus I spoke strongly to the officials. I asked them, "Why do you not take care of the house of God?" Then I gathered the Levites and the singers. I put them back at their posts.

**12** Then all the people of Judah brought the tenths of the grain, the new wine and the oil to the storerooms.

**13** I put men in control of the storerooms. I chose Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah, one of the Levites. Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah, helped them. People knew that these men were honest. Their work was to give the shares to their brothers.

**14** My God, remember me for this. Do not forget the good things that I did for the house of my God and for its services.

**15** In those days I saw people in Judah who pressed grapes on the Sabbath. They brought in bundles of grain and put them on donkeys. They also brought wine, grapes, figs and all types of loads into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. I warned them not to sell food on that day.

**16** Men from Tyre also lived in Jerusalem. They brought fish and all types of goods. They sold these things on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.

**17** Then I spoke strongly to the nobles of Judah. I said, "You do an evil thing. You make the Sabbath day unholy.

**18** Your fathers did the same things. Thus our God brought all this trouble on us and on this city. Now you make God more angry with Israel, because you make the Sabbath unholy."

**19** Before the Sabbath, the shadows fell on the gates of Jerusalem. Then I gave an order to close the gates. I told the people not to open the gates until after the Sabbath. I put some of my servants at the gates. They had to make sure that no person brought loads in on the Sabbath day.

**20** Once or twice the merchants and sellers of all types of goods stayed the night outside Jerusalem.

**21** But I warned them. I said, "Why do you stay the night near the wall? If you do this again, I will use force against you." From that time on, they did not come on the Sabbath.

**22** Then I told the Levites to make themselves clean. I told them to come and guard the gates to keep the Sabbath day holy. My God, remember me for this also. Show me kindness because of your great love.

**23** In those days I also saw Jews who married women from Ashdod, Ammon and Moab.

**24** Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or the language of another nation. They could not speak the language of the Jews.

**25** I spoke strongly to these men and cursed them. I hit some of them and pulled out their hair. I made them make a promise in the name of God. I said, "Do not let your daughters marry their sons. Do not let your sons or yourselves marry their daughters.

**26** Solomon king of Israel sinned because of marriages like these. No king in many nations was like him. His God loved him. God made him king over all Israel. But even Solomon sinned because of his foreign wives.

**27** We will not listen to you and let you do this great evil. You are not loyal to our God, because you marry foreign women."

**28** One of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. Thus I sent him away from me.

**29** My God, remember them, because they made the work of the priests unclean. They broke the agreement (covenant) of the priests and the Levites.

**30** Thus I made the priests and Levites clean from all foreign things. I gave the priests and the Levites their duties. Each man had his own work.

**31** I also gave them the duties for the wood offering at the specified times and for the first part of the crops. My God, remember me and be good to me.

---

# Esther

## Chapter 1

**1** This event occurred in the time of King Ahasuerus. Ahasuerus ruled over 127 provinces, from India to Ethiopia.

**2** At that time, King Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom in the fortress city of Susa.

**3** In the 3rd year of his rule, the king gave a feast for all his officials and his servants. The commanders of the army of Persia and Media were there. The nobles and the officials of the provinces were also there.

**4** For 180 days, the king showed the riches of his kingdom. He also showed the honor and the splendor of his great power.

**5** When these days were at an end, the king gave a feast for all the people in the fortress city of Susa. The feast was for important people and for common people. The feast continued for 7 days in the garden court of the king's palace.

**6** White, green, and blue cloth hung there. Cords of fine linen and purple attached the cloth to silver rings and marble pillars. There were couches of gold and silver on a floor of red, blue, white, and black stone.

**7** The servants gave drinks in gold cups. Each cup was different from the other cups. There was much royal wine, as the king was very rich.

**8** The guests drank as the law said: "No person can force a guest to drink." The king told all the officials of his palace to let each man drink as he wanted.

**9** Also, Queen Vashti gave a feast for the women in the royal palace of King Ahasuerus.

**10** On the 7th day, the king was happy because of the wine. He gave an order to the 7 officials who served him. Their names were Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas.

**11** He told them to bring Queen Vashti to him with the royal crown on her head. He wanted to show her beauty to the people and the officials, because she was very beautiful.

**12** But Queen Vashti refused to come when the officials gave her the order of the king. Thus the king became very angry. His anger burned in him.

**13** The king usually asked for advice from men who knew the law and justice. Thus he spoke to the wise men who understood the times.

**14** The men nearest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. They were the 7 officials of Persia and Media. They could come to the king at any time, and they had the highest positions in the kingdom.

**15** The king asked, "What must we do to Queen Vashti by law? She did not obey the order of King Ahasuerus that the officials gave her."

**16** Memucan answered in front of the king and the officials, "Queen Vashti did wrong not only to the king. She also did wrong to all the officials and to all the people in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.

**17** All the women will hear what the queen did. Then they will not respect their husbands. They will say, 'King Ahasuerus told Queen Vashti to come to him, but she did not come.'

**18** Today the noble women of Persia and Media will hear about the act of the queen. They will speak in the same way to all the officials of the king. Thus there will be much disrespect and anger.

**19** If the king agrees, let him send a royal order. Write the order in the laws of Persia and Media, so that no person can change it. The order must say that Vashti will never come to King Ahasuerus again. Then let the king give her royal position to another woman who is better than she is.

**20** The king will make his order known in all his large kingdom. Then all the wives will respect their husbands, from the most important to the least important."

**21** The king and the officials liked this advice. Thus the king did as Memucan said.

**22** He sent letters to all the provinces of the king. He wrote to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language. The letters said that each man must be the ruler in his own house. Each man must speak the language of his own people.

## Chapter 2

**1** After these events, the anger of King Ahasuerus became less. Then he remembered Vashti. He remembered what she did and the order against her.

**2** Then the servants of the king who helped him said, "Let your officials look for beautiful young virgins for the king.

**3** Let the king choose officials in all the provinces of his kingdom. Let these officials bring all the beautiful young virgins to the house of the women in the fortress city of Susa. Put the young women in the care of Hegai, the official of the king who controls the women. Give the young women the oils and creams for their beauty treatment.

**4** Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in the place of Vashti." The king liked this advice, and he did it.

**5** In the fortress city of Susa there was a Jew named Mordecai. He was the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish. Mordecai was from the tribe of Benjamin.

**6** Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, took Mordecai away from Jerusalem. Mordecai was with the prisoners that Nebuchadnezzar took away with Jeconiah, the king of Judah.

**7** Mordecai raised Hadassah. Her other name was Esther. She was the daughter of his uncle. She did not have a father or a mother. The young woman had a good shape and was beautiful. When her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.

**8** The people heard the order and the law of the king. Then the officials brought many young women to the fortress city of Susa, into the care of Hegai. The officials also took Esther to the palace of the king, into the care of Hegai, who controlled the women.

**9** Hegai liked the young woman, and she got his favor. He quickly gave her the oils and creams for her beauty treatment and her special food. He gave her 7 female servants that he chose from the palace of the king. He moved her and her female servants to the best place in the house of the women.

**10** Esther did not tell anyone who her people and her family were, because Mordecai told her not to tell.

**11** Each day Mordecai walked in front of the court of the house of the women. He wanted to know how Esther was and what happened to her.

**12** Before each young woman went to King Ahasuerus, she completed 12 months of beauty treatments. This was the rule for the women. She received 6 months of treatment with oil of myrrh. Then she received 6 months of treatment with perfumes and creams.

**13** Then each young woman went to the king. She could take with her anything that she wanted from the house of the women to the palace of the king.

**14** She went to the king in the evening. In the morning she went back to the second house of the women. There she was in the care of Shaashgaz, the official of the king who controlled the concubines (wives of lower rank). She did not go to the king again unless the king was happy with her and called her by name.

**15** Esther was the daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai. Mordecai took her as his daughter. When it was the time for Esther to go to the king, she asked only for the things that Hegai told her to take. Hegai was the official of the king who controlled the women. All the people who saw Esther liked her.

**16** The officials took Esther to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace. This occurred in the 10th month, the month of Tebeth, in the 7th year of his rule.

**17** The king loved Esther more than all the other women. She got his favor and kindness more than all the other virgins. Thus he put the royal crown on her head and made her queen in the place of Vashti.

**18** Then the king gave a large feast for all his officials and his servants. It was the feast of Esther. He also gave a holiday to the provinces. He gave gifts from his great riches.

**19** The officials brought the virgins together a 2nd time. At that time Mordecai sat at the gate of the king.

**20** Esther did not yet tell anyone about her family or her people, because Mordecai told her not to tell. Esther obeyed Mordecai, as she did when he raised her.

**21** At that time, Mordecai sat at the gate of the king. 2 officials of the king, Bigthan and Teresh, became angry. These men guarded the door. They made a plan to kill King Ahasuerus.

**22** Mordecai learned about the plan and told Queen Esther. Esther told the king about the plan, and she said that the information came from Mordecai.

**23** The officials examined the report and found that it was true. Thus the officials hanged the 2 men on a post. The scribes wrote this event in the book of the records of the kings, in front of the king.

## Chapter 3

**1** After these events, King Ahasuerus gave a higher position to Haman. Haman was the son of Hammedatha the Agagite. The king put Haman in a position above all the other officials.

**2** All the servants of the king at the gate of the king bowed down to Haman and showed respect to him. The king gave an order for them to do this. But Mordecai did not bow down, and he did not show respect to Haman.

**3** Then the servants of the king at the gate said to Mordecai, "Why do you not obey the order of the king?"

**4** Each day they spoke to him, but he did not listen to them. Mordecai told them that he was a Jew. Thus they told Haman about Mordecai. They wanted to see if Haman accepted the reason of Mordecai.

**5** Haman saw that Mordecai did not bow down or show respect to him. Then Haman became very angry.

**6** People told Haman who the people of Mordecai were. Thus Haman did not want to kill only Mordecai. Haman made a plan to destroy all the Jews in the kingdom of Ahasuerus. These Jews were the people of Mordecai.

**7** In the 1st month, the month of Nisan, in the 12th year of King Ahasuerus, Haman's men threw Pur (lots). They threw the lots in front of Haman to choose a day and a month. The lot chose the 12th month, the month of Adar.

**8** Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a group of people in all the provinces of your kingdom. They live in different places among the other peoples. Their laws are different from the laws of all other peoples. They do not obey the laws of the king. Thus it is not good for the king to let them live.

**9** If the king agrees, write an order to destroy these people. I will give 10,000 talents of silver to the officials who do this work. They will put the silver in the treasury of the king."

**10** The king removed his signet ring from his hand. He gave the ring to Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.

**11** The king said to Haman, "Keep the silver. Do with the people as you think is good."

**12** On the 13th day of the 1st month, Haman called the scribes of the king. They wrote all the orders of Haman. They wrote to the high officials of the king, to the governors of each province, and to the officials of each people. They wrote to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language. They wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus and put the seal of the ring of the king on the letters.

**13** Messengers took the letters to all the provinces of the king. The letters gave an order to destroy, to kill, and to remove all the Jews. This order was for young and old people, small children and women. The order was for 1 day, the 13th day of the 12th month, the month of Adar. The letters also said, "Take all the property of the Jews."

**14** A copy of the order went to each province as a law. The officials told all the peoples about the order, so that they could be ready for that day.

**15** The order of the king made the messengers go quickly. The officials also gave the order in the fortress city of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink. But the city of Susa had much confusion and fear.

## Chapter 4

**1** Mordecai learned all that occurred. Then he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth (rough cloth) and ashes. He went out into the middle of the city and cried with a loud and bitter cry.

**2** He went only as far as the gate of the king, because no person in sackcloth could go through the gate of the king.

**3** In each province where the order of the king came, the Jews mourned very much. They fasted, cried, and wailed. Many Jews lay in sackcloth and ashes.

**4** The female servants and the officials of Esther came and told her about Mordecai. The queen became very sad. She sent clothes to Mordecai to wear in the place of his sackcloth. But he did not accept the clothes.

**5** Then Esther called Hatach. He was one of the officials that the king chose to serve her. She sent Hatach to Mordecai to find out what was wrong and why.

**6** Hatach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the gate of the king.

**7** Mordecai told Hatach all that occurred to him. He also told Hatach about the quantity of money that Haman promised to put in the treasury of the king to destroy the Jews.

**8** Mordecai also gave Hatach a copy of the order to destroy the Jews. The officials gave this order in Susa. Mordecai told Hatach to show the order to Esther and to explain it to her. Mordecai told Hatach to tell Esther to go to the king. She must ask the king for mercy and speak to him for her people.

**9** Hatach went back and told Esther the words of Mordecai.

**10** Then Esther spoke to Hatach and told him to give this message to Mordecai:

**11** "All the servants of the king and all the people of his provinces know this law. If a man or a woman goes to the king in the inner court without an order, that person must die. The only exception is if the king holds out his gold scepter (royal rod) to that person. Then that person will live. But the king did not call me to come to him for 30 days."

**12** The servants told Mordecai the words of Esther.

**13** Mordecai told them to give this answer to Esther. "Do not think that you will be safe in the palace of the king. Do not think that only the other Jews will die.

**14** If you do not speak now, help and rescue for the Jews will come from another place. But you and the family of your father will die. Possibly you became queen for a time such as this."

**15** Then Esther told them to give this answer to Mordecai:

**16** "Go and bring together all the Jews in Susa. Fast for me. Do not eat or drink for 3 days, at night or in the day. My female servants and I will also fast in the same way. Then I will go to the king, although that is against the law. If I die, then I die."

**17** Mordecai went away and did all that Esther told him to do.

## Chapter 5

**1** On the 3rd day, Esther put on her royal clothes. She stood in the inner court of the palace of the king, opposite the hall of the king. The king sat on his royal throne in the royal hall, opposite the entrance.

**2** The king saw Queen Esther as she stood in the court, and he was happy with her. The king held out to Esther the gold scepter in his hand. Esther came near and touched the top of the scepter.

**3** Then the king said to her, "What do you want, Queen Esther? What is your request? I will give it to you, up to half of my kingdom."

**4** Esther answered, "If the king agrees, let the king and Haman come today to the feast that I made ready for the king."

**5** Then the king said, "Bring Haman quickly, so that we can do as Esther asks." Thus the king and Haman went to the feast that Esther made ready.

**6** While they drank wine at the feast, the king said to Esther, "What do you want? I will give it to you. What is your request? Even if it is half of my kingdom, I will do it."

**7** Esther answered, "This is what I want and what I ask:

**8** If the king is happy with me, and if he agrees to give me what I want, I have a request. Let the king and Haman come to another feast tomorrow. I will make it ready for them. Then tomorrow I will answer the question of the king."

**9** Haman went out that day happy and glad. But then he saw Mordecai at the gate of the king. Mordecai did not stand up and did not move in front of Haman. Thus Haman became very angry with Mordecai.

**10** But Haman controlled his anger and went home. He called his friends and his wife Zeresh to come to him.

**11** Haman told them about his great riches and his many sons. He told them about all the ways that the king gave him honor. He told them how the king put him above the other officials and servants of the king.

**12** Haman also said, "Queen Esther invited only me to come with the king to the feast that she made ready. Tomorrow she also invited me to come with the king.

**13** But all this does not satisfy me while I see Mordecai the Jew sit at the gate of the king."

**14** Then his wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Make a gallows (a post to hang a person) 50 cubits high. In the morning, tell the king to hang Mordecai on it. Then go with the king to the feast and be happy." Haman liked this advice. Thus he told his servants to make the gallows.

## Chapter 6

**1** That night the king could not sleep. He told a servant to bring the book of the records of the kings. The servants read the book to the king.

**2** The book had a record about Mordecai. The record said that Mordecai told about Bigthana and Teresh. These 2 officials of the king guarded the door. They made a plan to kill King Ahasuerus.

**3** The king asked, "What honor and reward did Mordecai get for this?" The servants of the king who helped him said, "Mordecai got nothing."

**4** The king said, "Who is in the court?" At that time Haman came into the outer court of the palace of the king. Haman wanted to tell the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows that Haman made ready for him.

**5** The servants of the king said to him, "Haman stands in the court." The king said, "Let him come in."

**6** Haman came in, and the king asked him, "What must I do for the man that the king wants to honor?" Haman thought, "The king wants to honor no man more than me."

**7** Thus Haman answered the king, "For the man that the king wants to honor,

**8** let servants bring a royal robe that the king wore. Let them bring a horse that the king rode, with a royal crown on its head.

**9** Give the robe and the horse to one of the most important officials of the king. Let the official put the robe on the man that the king wants to honor. Let the official put the man on the horse and lead him through the city square. Let the official shout in front of him, 'This is what the king does for the man that he wants to honor!'"

**10** Then the king said to Haman, "Go quickly. Take the robe and the horse, as you said. Do all these things for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the gate of the king. Do not omit any of the things that you said."

**11** Thus Haman took the robe and the horse. He put the robe on Mordecai. He led Mordecai on the horse through the city square. He shouted in front of Mordecai, "This is what the king does for the man that he wants to honor!"

**12** Then Mordecai went back to the gate of the king. But Haman went home quickly. He was very sad, and he covered his head.

**13** Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends about all that occurred to him. His wise men and his wife Zeresh said to him, "You started to fall in front of Mordecai. Mordecai is a Jew. Thus you will not win against him. You will surely fall in front of him."

**14** While they spoke to Haman, the officials of the king came. They quickly took Haman to the feast that Esther made ready.

## Chapter 7

**1** Thus the king and Haman went to eat and drink with Queen Esther.

**2** On this 2nd day, while they drank wine, the king asked Esther again, "Queen Esther, what do you want? I will give it to you. What is your request? Even if it is half of my kingdom, I will do it."

**3** Then Queen Esther answered, "King, if you are happy with me, and if you agree, give me my life. This is what I want. Also save my people. This is my request.

**4** People sold me and my people. Now our enemy will destroy us, kill us, and remove us. If they sold us only as male and female slaves, I will not speak. That problem is not sufficient to disturb the king."

**5** Then King Ahasuerus asked Queen Esther, "Who is the man that dared to do this? Where is he?"

**6** Esther said, "The enemy is this evil man Haman!" Then Haman became very afraid in front of the king and the queen.

**7** The king became very angry. He stood up from the feast and went out into the palace garden. Haman knew that the king decided to punish him. Thus Haman stayed and asked Queen Esther to save his life.

**8** Then the king came back from the palace garden to the place of the feast. Haman lay on the couch where Esther was. The king said, "Will he also attack the queen while I am in the house?" When the king said these words, the servants covered the face of Haman.

**9** Harbonah, one of the officials, said to the king, "Look, there is a gallows 50 cubits high at the house of Haman. Haman made it for Mordecai, who gave the report that saved the king." The king said, "Hang Haman on it!"

**10** Thus the servants hanged Haman on the gallows that he made ready for Mordecai. Then the anger of the king became calm.

## Chapter 8

**1** On that day, King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the house of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Mordecai came to the king, because Esther told the king that Mordecai was her relative.

**2** The king removed his signet ring, which he took back from Haman. He gave the ring to Mordecai. Esther put Mordecai in control of the house of Haman.

**3** Then Esther spoke to the king again. She fell down at his feet and cried. She asked him to stop the evil plan of Haman the Agagite against the Jews.

**4** The king held out the gold scepter to Esther. Thus Esther stood up in front of the king.

**5** She said, "If the king agrees, and if he is happy with me, let him write an order. Let the order cancel the letters of Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite. Haman wrote these letters to destroy the Jews in all the provinces of the king. Please do this if the king thinks that it is correct, and if I please him.

**6** I cannot watch while this evil thing occurs to my people. I cannot watch while enemies destroy my family."

**7** Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, "I gave the house of Haman to Esther. My servants hanged Haman on the gallows, because he tried to attack the Jews.

**8** Now write another order for the Jews in the name of the king, as you think is best. Put the seal of the ring of the king on it. No person can cancel an order that officials write in the name of the king and seal with the ring of the king."

**9** Then Mordecai called the scribes of the king. This was on the 23rd day of the 3rd month, the month of Sivan. They wrote all the orders of Mordecai to the Jews. They also wrote to the high officials, the governors, and the officials of the 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. They wrote to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language. They also wrote to the Jews in their own script and language.

**10** Mordecai wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus and put the seal of the ring of the king on the letters. He sent the letters with messengers on fast horses that came from the royal herds.

**11** In these letters, the king gave the Jews in each city the right to come together and protect their lives. The Jews could destroy, kill, and remove any armed force of any people or province that attacked them. This included the children and women of the attackers. The Jews could also take the property of their enemies.

**12** The order was for 1 day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus. The day was the 13th day of the 12th month, the month of Adar.

**13** A copy of the order went to each province as a law. The officials told all the peoples about the order. Thus the Jews could be ready on that day to fight back against their enemies.

**14** The messengers rode out quickly on the fast royal horses, because the order of the king made them hurry. The officials also gave the order in the fortress city of Susa.

**15** Mordecai went out from the king in royal clothes of blue and white. He wore a large gold crown and a robe of fine linen and purple. The city of Susa shouted and was happy.

**16** The Jews had light, happiness, joy, and honor.

**17** In each province and each city where the order of the king came, the Jews were happy and glad. They had a feast and a holiday. Many people of other nations became Jews, because they were afraid of the Jews.

## Chapter 9

**1** The order of the king was to occur on the 13th day of the 12th month, the month of Adar. On that day the enemies of the Jews hoped to defeat the Jews. But the opposite occurred. The Jews defeated the people who hated them.

**2** The Jews came together in their cities in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus. They attacked the people who wanted to hurt them. No person could fight against the Jews, because all the peoples were afraid of them.

**3** All the officials of the provinces, the high officials, the governors, and the officials of the king helped the Jews. They did this because they were afraid of Mordecai.

**4** Mordecai was very important in the palace of the king. People in all the provinces heard about him. Mordecai became more and more powerful.

**5** The Jews attacked all their enemies with the sword. They killed and destroyed them. They did what they wanted to the people who hated them.

**6** In the fortress city of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed 500 men.

**7** They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

**8** Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,

**9** Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vajezatha.

**10** These men were the 10 sons of Haman, the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. The Jews killed them. But the Jews did not take their property.

**11** On that day, the officials told the king the number of men that the Jews killed in the fortress city of Susa.

**12** The king said to Queen Esther, "The Jews killed and destroyed 500 men and the 10 sons of Haman in the fortress city of Susa. They possibly did much more in the other provinces of the king. Now what do you want? I will give it to you. What else do you ask? I will do it."

**13** Esther said, "If the king agrees, let the Jews in Susa do the same thing tomorrow as they did today. Also, hang the bodies of the 10 sons of Haman on the gallows."

**14** Thus the king gave the order to do this. The officials gave the order in Susa. The Jews hanged the bodies of the 10 sons of Haman.

**15** The Jews in Susa came together again on the 14th day of the month of Adar. They killed 300 men in Susa. But they did not take any property.

**16** The other Jews in the provinces of the king also came together to protect their lives. They got peace from their enemies. They killed 75,000 of the people who hated them. But they did not take any property.

**17** This occurred on the 13th day of the month of Adar. On the 14th day they rested. They made that day a day of feasts and happiness.

**18** But the Jews in Susa came together on the 13th day and on the 14th day. On the 15th day they rested. They made that day a day of feasts and happiness.

**19** Thus the Jews who live in the villages without walls make the 14th day of the month of Adar a day of happiness and feasts. It is a holiday. On that day they send gifts of food to each other.

**20** Mordecai wrote a record of these events. He sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, near and far.

**21** He told them to celebrate the 14th day and the 15th day of the month of Adar each year.

**22** These were the days when the Jews got peace from their enemies. In that month their sadness changed to joy, and their grief changed to a holiday. Mordecai told them to make these days, days of feasts and joy. On these days they must send gifts of food to each other and gifts to poor people.

**23** Thus the Jews agreed to continue the celebration that they started. They agreed to do what Mordecai wrote to them.

**24** Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, was the enemy of all the Jews. He made a plan to destroy the Jews. He threw Pur (the lot) to kill and destroy them.

**25** But Esther went to the king. Then the king gave an order in letters. The order made the evil plan of Haman against the Jews come back on Haman. The king told his servants to hang Haman and his sons on the gallows.

**26** Thus the Jews called these days Purim, from the word Pur. The Jews read all the words of the letter of Mordecai. They knew what they saw and what occurred to them.

**27** Thus the Jews made a rule for themselves, for their descendants, and for all people who join them. They must always celebrate these 2 days each year. They must do this as the letter said, at the correct time.

**28** All generations, all families, all provinces, and all cities must remember and celebrate these days. The Jews must never stop the celebration of Purim. Their descendants must never forget these days.

**29** Then Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with full authority. They wrote this 2nd letter about Purim to make it a law.

**30** Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus. The letters had words of peace and truth.

**31** The letters made the days of Purim a law at their correct times. Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther gave this order. The Jews also made rules about the fasts and the times of grief, for themselves and for their descendants.

**32** The order of Esther made the rules of Purim a law. A scribe wrote these rules in a book.

## Chapter 10

**1** King Ahasuerus made the people of the land and of the islands of the sea pay a tax.

**2** All the powerful acts of King Ahasuerus are in the book of the records of the kings of Media and Persia. The full report of the greatness of Mordecai is also in that book. The king made Mordecai a very important man.

**3** Mordecai the Jew was 2nd in rank after King Ahasuerus. He was important among the Jews, and many of his people respected him. He worked for the good of his people. He spoke for the peace of all his descendants.

# Job

## Chapter 1

**1** A man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a good and honest man. He feared God, and he kept away from evil.

**2** Job had 7 sons and 3 daughters.

**3** He had 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pairs of oxen, and 500 female donkeys. He also had very many servants. He was the most important man of all the people in the east.

**4** The sons of Job usually gave feasts in their houses. Each son had his own day for a feast. They invited their 3 sisters to eat and drink with them.

**5** After each period of feasts, Job sent for his children and made them clean for God. He got up early in the morning. He gave a burnt offering for each of his children. Job thought, "Possibly my sons sinned and cursed God in their hearts." Job always did this.

**6** One day the angels (sons of God) came to stand in front of the LORD. Satan also came with them.

**7** The LORD said to Satan, "Where did you come from?" Satan answered the LORD, "I came from the earth. I went everywhere on the earth."

**8** Then the LORD said to Satan, "Did you look at my servant Job? There is no other person on the earth like him. He is a good and honest man. He fears God, and he keeps away from evil."

**9** Satan answered the LORD, "Job fears God because he gets something for it.

**10** You always protect him, his family, and all his property. You bless all the work that he does. His herds become larger and larger in the land.

**11** But hold out your hand now and take away all that he has. Then he will curse you to your face."

**12** The LORD said to Satan, "All that Job has is now in your power. But do not touch Job himself." Then Satan went away from the LORD.

**13** One day the sons and daughters of Job ate food and drank wine in the house of their oldest brother.

**14** A messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen pulled the plows, and the donkeys ate grass near them.

**15** Then the Sabeans attacked and took the animals. They killed the servants with swords. Only I escaped to tell you."

**16** While he spoke, another messenger came and said, "Fire from God fell from the sky. The fire burned and killed the sheep and the servants. Only I escaped to tell you."

**17** While he spoke, another messenger came and said, "The Chaldeans made 3 groups and attacked the camels. They took the camels away and killed the servants with swords. Only I escaped to tell you."

**18** While he spoke, another messenger came and said, "Your sons and daughters ate food and drank wine in the house of their oldest brother.

**19** Then a strong wind came from the desert. The wind hit the 4 corners of the house. The house fell on the young people, and they died. Only I escaped to tell you."

**20** Then Job stood up and tore his robe. He shaved his head. He fell down on the ground and worshipped God.

**21** He said, "I had no clothes when I came from the body of my mother. I will have no clothes when I go back to the earth. The LORD gave, and the LORD took away. Praise the name of the LORD."

**22** In all these things, Job did not sin. He did not say that God did wrong.

## Chapter 2

**1** On another day the angels (sons of God) came to stand in front of the LORD. Satan also came with them to stand in front of the LORD.

**2** The LORD said to Satan, "Where did you come from?" Satan answered the LORD, "I came from the earth. I went everywhere on the earth."

**3** Then the LORD said to Satan, "Did you look at my servant Job? There is no other person on the earth like him. He is a good and honest man. He fears God, and he keeps away from evil. He continues to be honest. But you caused me to attack him and to destroy him for no reason."

**4** Satan answered the LORD, "A man will give all that he has to save his own life.

**5** But hold out your hand now and hurt his bones and his body. Then he will curse you to your face."

**6** The LORD said to Satan, "Job is in your power. But do not kill him."

**7** Thus Satan went away from the LORD. Satan put painful sores on Job, from the bottom of his feet to the top of his head.

**8** Job took a piece of a broken pot to scratch his skin. He sat in the ashes.

**9** Then his wife said to him, "Do you still continue to be honest? Curse God and die!"

**10** But Job said to her, "You speak like a foolish woman. We accept good things from God. We must also accept trouble from God." In all these things, Job did not sin with his words.

**11** Job had 3 friends: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah. They heard about all the trouble that came to Job. Each man came from his own home. They agreed to meet and to go to Job. They wanted to show him their sorrow and to comfort him.

**12** They saw Job from far away, but they did not recognize him. They cried loudly. Each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head.

**13** Then they sat on the ground with Job for 7 days and 7 nights. None of them said a word to him, because they saw that his pain was very great.

## Chapter 3

**1** After this, Job spoke. He cursed the day of his birth.

**2** Job said,

**3** "Let the day of my birth disappear. Let the night disappear when someone said, 'A boy is in the womb.'

**4** Let that day become dark. Let God above forget it. Do not let light shine on it.

**5** Let darkness and deep shadow take it back. Let a cloud stay over it. Let black darkness frighten it.

**6** Let thick darkness take that night. Do not include it in the days of the year. Do not count it in the months.

**7** Let that night have no children born in it. Let no person shout with joy in it.

**8** Let the people who curse days curse that day. These people know how to wake up Leviathan (the sea monster).

**9** Let the stars of its early morning be dark. Let that night wait for light, but get none. Do not let it see the first light of the morning.

**10** That night did not close the womb of my mother. Thus it did not keep trouble away from my eyes.

**11** Why did I not die at birth? Why did I not die when I came out of the body of my mother?

**12** Why did a mother take me on her knees? Why did she give me milk from her breasts?

**13** If I died at birth, then now I lie down in peace. I sleep and I have rest.

**14** Then I rest with the kings and advisers of the earth. They built cities for themselves that are now ruins.

**15** Or I rest with rulers who had gold and filled their houses with silver.

**16** Or I am like a baby that died before birth and that people buried secretly. I am like a baby that never saw light.

**17** In the grave, evil people stop their trouble. In the grave, tired people rest.

**18** In the grave, prisoners rest together. They do not hear the shout of the man who forces them to work.

**19** Common people and important people are there. The slave is free from his master.

**20** Why does God give light to people who suffer? Why does he give life to people who are very sad?

**21** These people want to die, but death does not come. They look for death more than for hidden treasure.

**22** They are very happy when they find the grave.

**23** Why does God give life to a man who cannot see his way? God put a wall around that man.

**24** I cry before I eat. My painful cries flow like water.

**25** The thing that I feared most occurred to me. The thing that frightened me came to me.

**26** I have no peace. I have no quiet. I have no rest. Only trouble comes."

## Chapter 4

**1** Then Eliphaz from Teman answered,

**2** "If someone speaks to you, will you become angry? But no person can be silent now.

**3** You taught many people. You gave strength to weak people.

**4** Your words helped people who started to fall. You gave strength to people whose knees were weak.

**5** But now trouble comes to you, and you become weak. Trouble hits you, and you are afraid.

**6** You fear God. Is that not your confidence? You live an honest life. Is that not your hope?

**7** Think about this: Did an innocent person ever die like this? Did God ever destroy good people?

**8** I see this: People who plan evil and do wrong things get evil and trouble in return.

**9** The breath of God destroys them. The strong wind of his anger kills them.

**10** The lion roars, and the young lion shouts. But God breaks the teeth of the strong lions.

**11** The strong lion dies because it cannot find food. The young lions go away in all directions.

**12** A message came to me secretly. I heard only a quiet voice.

**13** It came in a dream at night, when people are in a deep sleep.

**14** I became afraid and shook. All my bones shook.

**15** A spirit went past my face. The hair on my body stood up.

**16** The spirit stopped, but I could not see its shape. A form was in front of my eyes. There was silence. Then I heard a voice that said,

**17** 'Can a man be more just than God? Can a man be more pure than his Maker?

**18** God does not trust his servants. He finds errors in his angels.

**19** Thus he trusts men much less. Men live in bodies of clay. Their bodies come from the dust. A moth can easily crush them.

**20** Between morning and evening, people die. They disappear forever, and no person notices.

**21** Their life ends like a tent when someone pulls out its cords. They die without wisdom.'

## Chapter 5

**1** "Call for help if you want, but no person will answer you. None of the holy angels will help you.

**2** Anger kills a foolish man. Jealousy kills a person who is not wise.

**3** I saw a foolish man who was successful. But suddenly I cursed his home.

**4** His children are not safe. Other people defeat them in court. No person helps them.

**5** Hungry people eat his harvest. They take it even from among the thorns. Thieves take his riches.

**6** Trouble does not grow from the dust. Problems do not grow out of the ground.

**7** But from birth, man has trouble. This is as certain as the sparks that fly up from a fire.

**8** In your place, I will ask God for help. I will give my problem to God.

**9** He does great things that no person can understand. He does more wonderful things than any person can count.

**10** He gives rain to the earth. He sends water to the fields.

**11** He puts humble people in a high position. He keeps sad people safe.

**12** He stops the plans of clever people. Thus they cannot be successful.

**13** He catches wise people in their own tricks. He quickly stops the plans of dishonest people.

**14** These people find darkness in the day. At noon they feel their way as if it is night.

**15** But God saves poor people from the cruel words of their enemies. He saves them from the power of strong people.

**16** Thus poor people have hope, and evil people become silent.

**17** The man that God corrects is fortunate. Thus do not refuse the correction of the Almighty (God).

**18** God hurts, but he also puts bandages on the wounds. He causes injury, but his hands also heal.

**19** He will save you from 6 troubles. In 7 troubles, no evil will touch you.

**20** When there is no food, he will save you from death. In war, he will save you from the sword.

**21** He will protect you from the cruel words of people. You will not be afraid when destruction comes.

**22** You will laugh at destruction and hunger. You will not be afraid of the wild animals.

**23** The stones in the fields will not cause problems for you. The wild animals will be at peace with you.

**24** You will know that your home is safe. You will look at your property, and you will find all your things there.

**25** You will know that you will have many children. Your descendants will be as many as the grass on the earth.

**26** You will be very old when you die. You will be like grain that people harvest at the correct time.

**27** We examined these things, and they are true. Listen to this advice and use it for your good."

## Chapter 6

**1** Then Job answered,

**2** "I wish that someone could weigh my pain. I wish that someone could put all my trouble on a scale.

**3** Now my grief is heavier than the sand of the sea. That is why my words were wild.

**4** The arrows of the Almighty are in me. My spirit drinks their poison. The terrors of God attack me like an army.

**5** A wild donkey does not make a noise when it has grass. An ox does not make a noise when it has food. Thus I complain because I have a reason.

**6** No person eats food with no taste without salt. The white of an egg has no taste.

**7** I refuse to touch such food. It makes me sick.

**8** I wish that God will give me what I ask. I wish that he will give me what I want.

**9** I want God to destroy me. I want him to use his power to kill me.

**10** Then I will still have comfort. I will be happy, although I have pain that does not stop. I did not refuse the words of the Holy God.

**11** I do not have the strength to continue to hope. I have no future. Thus I have no reason to be patient.

**12** I am not strong like a stone. My body is not bronze.

**13** I have no power to help myself. All my success is gone.

**14** A person who has troubles must get kindness from his friends. If not, he can stop his fear of the Almighty.

**15** But my friends are not loyal to me. They are like streams in the desert that become dry.

**16** In winter the streams are dark because of the ice and the melted snow.

**17** But in the dry season, the water disappears. When it is hot, the water dries up.

**18** Groups of traders leave their path to find water. They go into the desert and die.

**19** The traders from Tema look for water. The travelers from Sheba hope to find water.

**20** They are sad because they trusted the streams. They arrive there, but they find no water.

**21** Now you are like those streams. You see my trouble, and you are afraid.

**22** I did not say, 'Give me something.' I did not say, 'Pay money for me from your riches.'

**23** I did not say, 'Save me from my enemy.' I did not say, 'Pay to rescue me from cruel people.'

**24** Teach me, and I will be silent. Show me how I did wrong.

**25** Honest words have power. But your arguments prove nothing.

**26** You want to correct my words. But the words of a man without hope are only wind.

**27** You even attack the orphan. You dig a pit for your friend.

**28** Now please look at me. I will not tell a lie to your face.

**29** Stop, and do not be unfair. Think again, because I am not guilty.

**30** I do not say evil things. I can know when something is wrong.

## Chapter 7

**1** "Life on earth is hard like the life of a soldier. The days of a man are like the days of a worker who works for pay.

**2** A man is like a slave who wants the shade of evening. He is like a worker who waits for his pay.

**3** I get months of no value. I get nights of trouble.

**4** When I lie down, I think, 'When will I get up?' The night is long. I turn from side to side until the morning.

**5** Worms and dirt cover my body. My skin breaks open and becomes infected.

**6** My days go faster than the shuttle of a weaver. They come to an end without hope.

**7** God, remember that my life is only a breath. I will not see good things again.

**8** The people who see me now will not see me again. You will look for me, but I will not be there.

**9** A cloud disappears and goes away. In the same way, a person who goes down to the grave does not come back.

**10** He will not come back to his house. The people of his home will not know him again.

**11** Thus I will not be silent. I will speak about the pain of my spirit. I will complain because I am very sad.

**12** Am I the sea or a sea monster? Why do you put a guard over me?

**13** I think, 'My bed will comfort me. My couch will make my complaint easier.'

**14** But then you frighten me with dreams. You make me afraid with visions.

**15** Thus I prefer to choke and die. I prefer death to this body.

**16** I hate my life. I do not want to live forever. Let me be alone, because my days have no meaning.

**17** Man is not important. Why do you think he is so important? Why do you pay so much attention to him?

**18** Why do you examine him each morning? Why do you test him at all times?

**19** You never look away from me. You do not let me be alone for even a short time.

**20** If I sinned, what did I do to you? You watch all men. Why do you make me your target? Why am I a burden to you?

**21** Why do you not forgive my sins? Why do you not take away my wrong acts? Soon I will lie in the dust. You will look for me, but I will not be there."

## Chapter 8

**1** Then Bildad from Shuah answered,

**2** "How long will you speak like this? Your words are like a strong wind.

**3** God is never unfair. The Almighty never does wrong to justice.

**4** Your children sinned against God. Thus he punished them for their sins.

**5** But you must look for God. Ask the Almighty for mercy.

**6** If you are pure and honest, he will quickly help you. He will give you back the home that you deserve.

**7** At first you had little. But in the future you will have very much.

**8** Ask the old people. Learn what their ancestors found out.

**9** Our life started only a short time ago, and we know nothing. Our days on earth are like a shadow.

**10** The old people will teach you and tell you. They will tell you what they understand.

**11** Papyrus cannot grow without mud. Reeds cannot grow without water.

**12** While they are still green and nobody cuts them, they dry up faster than other plants.

**13** People who forget God are like these plants. The hope of evil people will disappear.

**14** The things that they trust are weak. Their trust is like the web of a spider.

**15** They lean against the web, but it breaks. They hold it tightly, but it does not stay.

**16** An evil person is like a plant with much water in the sun. Its branches grow over the garden.

**17** Its roots go around a pile of rocks. They hold the stones.

**18** But when someone pulls the plant from its place, that place will forget it. The place will say, 'I never saw you.'

**19** That is the end of the happiness of an evil person. Then other plants will grow from the same ground.

**20** God does not refuse an honest man. And God does not help evil people.

**21** God will again cause you to laugh. He will again cause you to shout with joy.

**22** Shame will cover the people who hate you. The homes of evil people will disappear."

## Chapter 9

**1** Then Job answered,

**2** "I know that this is true. But how can a man be right with God?

**3** If a man wants to argue with God, he cannot answer 1 question in 1,000.

**4** God is wise and very strong. No person can fight against him and be safe.

**5** He moves mountains, and they do not know it. In his anger he turns them over.

**6** He shakes the earth from its place. He causes its foundations to shake.

**7** He tells the sun not to shine, and it does not shine. He hides the stars.

**8** Only he spread out the skies. He walks on the waves of the sea.

**9** He made the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades (groups of stars). He made the groups of stars in the south.

**10** He does great things that no person can understand. He does more wonderful things than any person can count.

**11** He goes past me, but I cannot see him. He moves near me, but I do not know it.

**12** He takes things away, and no person can stop him. No person can say to him, 'What do you do?'

**13** God does not stop his anger. Even the helpers of Rahab (the sea monster) bowed down at his feet.

**14** Thus I cannot answer God. I cannot find the words to argue with him.

**15** Although I am innocent, I cannot answer him. I can only ask my Judge for mercy.

**16** If I call him and he answers, I will not believe that he listens to me.

**17** He attacks me with a storm. He gives me many wounds for no reason.

**18** He does not let me get my breath. He fills me with bitter troubles.

**19** If it is a matter of strength, God is strong. If it is a matter of justice, who will call him to court?

**20** Although I am innocent, my own words will make me guilty. Although I am honest, my words will prove that I am bad.

**21** I am innocent, but I do not care about myself. I hate my life.

**22** It is all the same. Thus I say, 'God destroys innocent people and evil people.'

**23** When a disaster suddenly kills people, God laughs at the pain of innocent people.

**24** God gives the earth into the power of evil people. He covers the eyes of the judges. If God does not do this, who does?

**25** My days go faster than a man who runs. They go away quickly, and they see no happiness.

**26** They go past like fast boats. They are like an eagle that flies down to catch its food.

**27** I can say, 'I will forget my complaint. I will change my sad face and smile.'

**28** But I am still afraid of all my pain. I know that you will not say that I am innocent.

**29** You will say that I am guilty. Thus why must I try for no reason?

**30** I can wash myself with soap. I can make my hands very clean.

**31** But you will push me into a hole of mud. Then even my clothes will hate me.

**32** God is not a man like me. I cannot answer him. We cannot go to court together.

**33** There is no judge between us. There is no person who can put his hand on both of us.

**34** I want God to take away his rod from me. Then his power will not frighten me.

**35** Then I will speak and not fear him. But now I cannot do that.

## Chapter 10

**1** "I hate my life. Thus I will speak freely about my complaint. I will speak about my bitter feelings.

**2** I will say to God, 'Do not say that I am guilty. Tell me why you argue with me.

**3** Is it good for you to be cruel to me? Why do you refuse me, whom your hands made? Why do you make the plans of evil people successful?

**4** You do not have the eyes of a man. You do not see as a man sees.

**5** Your life is not short like the life of a man. Your years are not like the years of a man.

**6** Thus why do you look for my wrong acts? Why do you search for my sins?

**7** You know that I am not guilty. No person can save me from your power.

**8** Your hands shaped me and made me. But now you destroy me.

**9** Remember that you made me from clay. Will you change me back into dust?

**10** You poured me out like milk. You made me solid like cheese.

**11** You put skin and flesh on me. You joined my bones and muscles together.

**12** You gave me life and showed me kindness. Your care kept my spirit alive.

**13** But you hid a different plan in your heart. I know that this was in your mind.

**14** If I sin, you watch me. You will not forgive my wrong acts.

**15** If I am guilty, I will have much trouble. If I am innocent, I still cannot lift my head with honor. I am full of shame. Look at my trouble.

**16** If I lift my head, you hunt me like a lion. You show your great power against me again.

**17** You bring new witnesses against me. Your anger against me becomes larger. You send new armies against me.

**18** Why did you bring me out of the womb? I wish that I died before any person saw me.

**19** I wish that I never lived. I wish that I went from the womb to the grave.

**20** My life is almost at an end. Let me be alone, so that I can have a little comfort.

**21** Soon I will go to the land of darkness and deep shadow. I will not come back from that place.

**22** It is a land of very deep darkness, and it has no order. In that land, even the light is like darkness.'"

## Chapter 11

**1** Then Zophar from Naamah answered,

**2** "Someone must answer all these words. A man who speaks much is not right because of his many words.

**3** Your foolish talk will not make men silent. When you insult God, someone must make you ashamed.

**4** You say to God, 'My message is correct. I am pure in your eyes.'

**5** But I wish that God will speak. I wish that he will answer you.

**6** I wish that he will show you the secrets of wisdom. True wisdom has 2 sides. Know this: God punishes you less than your sins deserve.

**7** You cannot know all the secrets of God. You cannot learn the limits of the Almighty.

**8** His wisdom is higher than the skies. What can you do? It is deeper than the grave. What can you know?

**9** It is longer than the earth. It is wider than the sea.

**10** If God puts a person in prison or brings him to court, no person can stop God.

**11** God knows which people are false. When he sees evil, he pays attention to it.

**12** A foolish man will become wise only when a wild donkey gives birth to a man.

**13** But you must make your heart ready. Lift your hands to God in prayer.

**14** If you do wrong, stop it. Do not let evil live in your house.

**15** Then you can lift up your face without shame. You will be strong and not afraid.

**16** You will forget your trouble. You will remember it only as water that flowed away.

**17** Your life will be brighter than the sun at noon. The darkness will become like the morning.

**18** You will feel safe, because you will have hope. You will look around you and rest in safety.

**19** You will lie down, and no person will frighten you. Many people will ask you for help.

**20** But the eyes of evil people will become weak. They will not escape. Their only hope is death."

## Chapter 12

**1** Then Job answered,

**2** "Surely you think that you are the only wise people. You think that wisdom will die when you die.

**3** But I have good sense as you do. I am not less than you. All people know these things.

**4** My friends laugh at me. I called to God, and he answered me. But people laugh at me, although I am good and honest.

**5** People who live in comfort hate the people who have trouble. They think that God hurts only the people who are ready to fall.

**6** But the tents of robbers have peace. People who make God angry are safe. They think that their power is their god.

**7** But ask the animals, and they will teach you. Ask the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.

**8** Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you. The fish of the sea will tell you.

**9** All these creatures know that the LORD made them with his hand.

**10** The life of each creature and the breath of all people are in the power of God.

**11** The ear tests words as the mouth tastes food.

**12** Old people have wisdom. A long life gives knowledge.

**13** But God has true wisdom and power. He has good advice and knowledge.

**14** If God breaks something down, no person can build it again. If he puts a man in prison, no person can let him out.

**15** If God stops the rain, the land becomes dry. If he lets the water go, it floods the land.

**16** God has strength and wisdom. He controls the person who tricks others. He also controls the person whom others trick.

**17** God takes away the wisdom of advisers. He makes judges foolish.

**18** He removes the authority of kings. He puts a cloth around their bodies like prisoners.

**19** He takes away the power of priests. He defeats strong people.

**20** He makes trusted advisers silent. He takes away the wisdom of old people.

**21** He makes rulers ashamed. He takes away the strength of powerful people.

**22** He shows the secrets that darkness hides. He brings deep shadows into the light.

**23** He makes nations great, and then he destroys them. He makes nations larger, and then he sends them away.

**24** He takes away the good sense of the leaders of the earth. He makes them go in all directions in a desert with no path.

**25** They feel their way in the dark without light. He makes them go from side to side like drunk men.

## Chapter 13

**1** "I saw all this with my eyes. I heard it with my ears and understood it.

**2** I know what you know. I am not less than you.

**3** But I want to speak to the Almighty. I want to argue my case with God.

**4** You hide the truth with lies. You are all like doctors who cannot heal.

**5** I wish that you will be silent. That will be wise for you.

**6** Now listen to my argument. Hear the words that I say in my defense.

**7** Will you say wrong things for God? Will you tell lies for him?

**8** Will you be on his side? Will you argue for God?

**9** If God examines you, will he find good things? Can you trick God as you trick a man?

**10** If you secretly take the side of God, he will surely punish you.

**11** His power will frighten you. You will be very afraid of him.

**12** Your wise words have no more value than ashes. Your arguments are weak like clay.

**13** Be silent and let me speak. Let anything occur to me.

**14** I will put my life in danger. I will take this risk.

**15** If God kills me, I will still trust him. But I will argue my case in front of him.

**16** This possibly will save me, because an evil person cannot come in front of God.

**17** Listen carefully to my words. Hear what I tell you.

**18** I made my case ready. I know that God will say that I am innocent.

**19** Can any person show that I am wrong? If someone can, I will be silent and die.

**20** God, give me only 2 things. Then I will not hide from you.

**21** Take your hand far away from me. Do not frighten me with your power.

**22** Then call me, and I will answer. Or let me speak, and then answer me.

**23** How many wrong acts and sins did I do? Show me my wrong acts and my sin.

**24** Why do you hide your face from me? Why do you think that I am your enemy?

**25** I am like a leaf that the wind blows. Will you frighten me? I am like dry grass. Will you chase me?

**26** You write bitter charges against me. You punish me for the sins that I did when I was young.

**27** You put my feet in chains. You watch all my paths. You put marks around the bottoms of my feet.

**28** Thus I become weak like rotten wood. I am like a coat that moths eat."

## Chapter 14

**1** "A man that a woman gives birth to lives only a short time. His life is full of trouble.

**2** He grows like a flower, and then he dies. He goes away like a shadow, and he does not stay.
