**3** Do you watch such a weak person? Do you bring me to court in front of you?

**4** No person can make a clean thing from a thing that is not clean.

**5** You decide how long a man will live. You know the number of his months. You set limits that he cannot go past.

**6** Thus look away from him and let him rest. Let him have peace, like a worker at the end of his day.

**7** If a person cuts down a tree, the tree has hope. It can grow again. New branches will continue to grow from it.

**8** Its roots can become old in the ground. Its stump can die in the soil.

**9** But when the tree gets water, it will grow again. It will make branches like a young plant.

**10** But a man dies and becomes weak. He takes his last breath, and then he is gone.

**11** Water disappears from a lake. A river becomes dry.

**12** In the same way, a man lies down and does not get up again. Until the skies disappear, dead people will not wake up from their sleep.

**13** I wish that you will hide me in the grave. Hide me until your anger stops. Then choose a time and remember me.

**14** If a man dies, will he live again? I will wait during all my hard days until my relief comes.

**15** You will call, and I will answer you. You will want to see me again, because you made me.

**16** Then you will count my steps, but you will not look for my sins.

**17** You will close my wrong acts in a bag and seal it. You will cover my sins.

**18** But a mountain falls and breaks into pieces. A rock moves from its place.

**19** Water wears away stones. Floods wash away the soil. In the same way, you destroy the hope of man.

**20** You always defeat a man, and he goes away. You change his face in death and send him away.

**21** If people give honor to his sons, he does not know it. If people bring shame to his sons, he does not see it.

**22** He feels only the pain of his own body. He mourns only for himself."

## Chapter 15

**1** Then Eliphaz from Teman answered,

**2** "A wise man does not answer with words that have no value. He does not fill himself with hot wind.

**3** He does not argue with talk that has no use. He does not use words that do no good.

**4** But you destroy respect for God. You stop prayer to God.

**5** Your sin teaches your mouth what to say. You speak like a clever, dishonest person.

**6** Your own mouth says that you are guilty, not I. Your own words speak against you.

**7** Are you the first man that a woman gave birth to? Did God make you before he made the hills?

**8** Do you listen to the secret council of God? Do you think that only you are wise?

**9** You know nothing that we do not know. You understand nothing that we do not understand.

**10** Old men with gray hair agree with us. They are older than your father.

**11** God comforts you and speaks gently to you. Is that not sufficient for you?

**12** Why do you let your feelings control you? Why do your eyes show anger?

**13** You turn your spirit against God. You say such words against him.

**14** No man can be pure. No person that a woman gives birth to can be good.

**15** God does not trust even his holy angels. Even the skies are not pure in his eyes.

**16** Thus man is much less pure. Man is bad and evil. He drinks sin like water.

**17** Listen to me, and I will explain to you. I will tell you what I saw.

**18** Wise men told these things. They learned them from their ancestors and did not hide them.

**19** God gave the land only to these ancestors. No foreigners lived among them.

**20** An evil man has pain during all his life. A cruel man does not know how many years he will live.

**21** He hears terrible sounds. When all is well, a robber will attack him.

**22** He does not think that he will escape from darkness. He knows that someone will kill him with a sword.

**23** He goes from place to place to look for food. He knows that the day of darkness is near.

**24** Trouble and pain frighten him. They attack him like a king who is ready for battle.

**25** He does this because he lifts his fist against God. He fights against the Almighty.

**26** He runs to attack God. He holds a thick, strong shield.

**27** His face is fat, and his body is heavy with fat.

**28** He will live in ruined cities. He will live in houses where no person lives. These houses will soon become piles of stones.

**29** He will not stay rich. His riches will not continue. His property will not spread over the land.

**30** He will not escape from darkness. Fire will dry up his branches. The breath of God will blow him away.

**31** He must not trust in things that have no value. If he does, he deceives himself. He will get nothing in return.

**32** He will die before his time. He will be like a branch that does not grow green.

**33** He will be like a vine that drops its grapes before they are ready. He will be like an olive tree that drops its flowers.

**34** The groups of evil people will have no children. Fire will burn the homes of people who take bribes.

**35** They plan trouble and do evil. Their minds make plans to deceive other people."

## Chapter 16

**1** Then Job answered,

**2** "I heard many words like these before. You are all bad comforters.

**3** Will your useless words never stop? What makes you continue to argue?

**4** I also could speak as you do, if you were in my position. I could say many words against you. I could shake my head at you.

**5** But I can give you strength with my words. My words can make your pain less.

**6** If I speak, my pain does not become less. If I am silent, the pain does not go away.

**7** But now God makes me very tired. He destroyed all my family.

**8** He made my skin thin and wrinkled, and this is a witness against me. My thin body speaks against me.

**9** God attacks me and tears me in his anger, because he hates me. He grinds his teeth at me. My enemy looks at me with sharp eyes.

**10** People open their mouths to laugh at me. They hit me on the face to insult me. They come together against me.

**11** God gave me to evil people. He put me in the power of wicked people.

**12** I was at peace, but he broke me. He held me by the neck and broke me into pieces. He made me his target.

**13** His archers are all around me. He cuts my body open and does not show mercy. He pours out my blood on the ground.

**14** He attacks me again and again. He runs at me like a soldier.

**15** I put on sackcloth over my skin. I put my strength down in the dust.

**16** My face is red because I cry. Dark shadows are around my eyes.

**17** But I did nothing violent. My prayer is pure.

**18** Earth, do not hide my blood. Do not let my cry for justice stop.

**19** Even now my witness is in heaven. The person who speaks for me is on high.

**20** My friends laugh at me. But my eyes cry to God.

**21** I want someone to speak to God for me, as a man speaks for his friend.

**22** In only a few years, I will go on the path from which I will not come back.

## Chapter 17

**1** "My spirit has no strength. My days are at an end. The grave waits for me.

**2** People laugh at me all around me. My eyes must watch them insult me.

**3** God, give me a guarantee. No other person will promise to help me.

**4** You closed their minds so that they do not understand. Thus you will not let them win.

**5** A man who turns against his friends for a reward will receive punishment. His children will suffer.

**6** God made people use my name as an insult. People spit in my face.

**7** My eyes became weak because of my sorrow. My body is thin like a shadow.

**8** Honest people feel shock at this. Innocent people become angry with evil people.

**9** But good people continue to do good. People who do right become stronger and stronger.

**10** But come back, all of you, and try again. I will not find a wise man among you.

**11** My life is at an end. My plans are gone. The things that I wanted are gone.

**12** My friends say that night is day. They say, 'Light is near,' but there is only darkness.

**13** The only home that I hope for is the grave. I will make my bed in the darkness.

**14** I say to the grave, 'You are my father.' I say to the worm, 'You are my mother and my sister.'

**15** Thus where is my hope? No person can see any hope for me.

**16** Will my hope go down with me to the gates of the grave? Will we go down together into the dust?"

## Chapter 18

**1** Then Bildad from Shuah answered,

**2** "When will you stop this talk? Think, and then we can speak.

**3** Why do you think that we are like animals? Why do you think that we are stupid?

**4** You hurt yourself in your anger. Must the earth become empty because of you? Must rocks move from their places for you?

**5** The light of an evil man will go out. The flame of his fire will stop.

**6** The light in his tent will become dark. His lamp will go out.

**7** His strong steps will become weak. His own plans will cause him to fall.

**8** His feet take him into a net. He walks into a trap.

**9** A trap catches him by the heel. A snare holds him tightly.

**10** Someone hides a rope on the ground for him. A trap waits for him on his path.

**11** Terrible things frighten him on all sides. They follow him at each step.

**12** Hunger takes away his strength. Disaster waits to make him fall.

**13** Disease eats his skin. The worst disease eats his arms and legs.

**14** Something takes him away from the safety of his tent. It brings him to death, the king of terrors.

**15** Other people will live in his tent. Burning sulfur will fall on his home.

**16** His roots will dry up below. His branches will die above.

**17** People on the earth will forget him. No person in the streets will remember his name.

**18** People will push him from light into darkness. They will chase him out of the world.

**19** He will have no children or descendants among his people. No person from his family will be alive where he lived.

**20** People in the west will feel shock at what occurs to him. People in the east will be afraid.

**21** This is what occurs to the homes of evil people. This is what occurs to a person who does not know God."

## Chapter 19

**1** Then Job answered,

**2** "How long will you cause me pain? How long will you hurt me with your words?

**3** You insulted me 10 times now. You attack me, and you feel no shame.

**4** If I did wrong, my error is my own problem.

**5** You think that you are better than me. You use my trouble as proof against me.

**6** But know that God did wrong to me. He caught me in his net.

**7** I shout, 'Help! Someone hurts me!' But I get no answer. I call for help, but there is no justice.

**8** God put a wall across my road, and I cannot go past. He covered my paths with darkness.

**9** He took away my honor. He took the crown from my head.

**10** He breaks me down on all sides until I am gone. He pulls up my hope like a tree.

**11** His anger burns against me. He thinks that I am one of his enemies.

**12** His armies come together and attack me. They make a road to attack me. They put their camps around my tent.

**13** God sent my brothers far away from me. My friends became strangers to me.

**14** My relatives went away. My close friends forgot me.

**15** My guests and my female servants think that I am a stranger. They look at me as a foreigner.

**16** I call my servant, but he does not answer. I must ask him with my own mouth.

**17** My wife hates my breath. My own brothers hate me.

**18** Even young children laugh at me. When I stand up, they speak against me.

**19** All my close friends hate me. The people that I love turned against me.

**20** I am only skin and bones. I am almost dead.

**21** My friends, have pity on me, have pity on me! The hand of God hit me.

**22** Why do you chase me as God does? Why do you not stop your attacks on me?

**23** I wish that someone will write down my words. I wish that someone will write them in a book.

**24** I wish that someone will cut them in rock forever with an iron tool and lead.

**25** But I know that my Redeemer (the one who saves me) lives. In the end he will stand on the earth.

**26** After worms destroy my skin, I will still see God in my body.

**27** I myself will see him. I will see him with my own eyes, not someone else. I want this very much.

**28** You say, 'We will attack him. The cause of his trouble is in him.'

**29** But you must be afraid of the sword. God will punish sin with the sword. Then you will know that there is judgment."

## Chapter 20

**1** Then Zophar from Naamah answered,

**2** "My thoughts cause me to answer, because I am very troubled.

**3** I heard your insult against me. My spirit gives me knowledge, and it causes me to answer.

**4** You surely know this. Since the time when God put man on the earth, this was true:

**5** The joy of an evil man is short. The happiness of a person without God continues only for a short time.

**6** His pride can go as high as the skies. His head can touch the clouds.

**7** But he will disappear forever, like his own dung. People who saw him will say, 'Where is he?'

**8** He will fly away like a dream, and no person will find him. He will disappear like a vision at night.

**9** People who saw him will not see him again. His home will not see him again.

**10** His children must pay back the poor people. His own hands must give back his riches.

**11** His bones were full of the strength of youth. But that strength will lie down with him in the dust.

**12** Evil is sweet in his mouth. He hides it under his tongue.

**13** He keeps it in his mouth. He does not want to let it go.

**14** But his food becomes sour in his stomach. It becomes like the poison of a snake in him.

**15** He swallows riches, but he will vomit them out. God will make his stomach throw them out.

**16** He will suck the poison of snakes. The fangs of a snake will kill him.

**17** He will not enjoy the rivers and streams of honey and cream.

**18** He must give back the things that he worked for. He cannot enjoy them. He will not enjoy the profit of his business.

**19** He was cruel to poor people and left them with nothing. He took houses that he did not build.

**20** His desires are never satisfied. His riches will not save him.

**21** He leaves nothing for others to eat. Thus his riches will not continue.

**22** When he has plenty, trouble will come to him. Much trouble will attack him.

**23** When he fills his stomach, God will send his angry fire against him. God will rain punishment on him while he eats.

**24** He will run away from an iron weapon. But an arrow from a bronze bow will go through him.

**25** He pulls the arrow out of his back. The bright point comes out of his liver. Terrible fear comes on him.

**26** Complete darkness waits for his riches. A fire that no person lit will burn him. It will destroy all that remains in his tent.

**27** The skies will show his sin. The earth will speak against him.

**28** Floods will take away the riches of his house. They will flow away on the day of the anger of God.

**29** This is what God gives to an evil man. This is what God decides for him."

## Chapter 21

**1** Then Job answered,

**2** "Listen carefully to my words. Let this be the comfort that you give me.

**3** Be patient while I speak. After I speak, you can continue to laugh at me.

**4** My complaint is not against a man. Thus I have a reason to be impatient.

**5** Look at me and feel shock. Put your hand over your mouth.

**6** When I think about this, I am afraid. My body shakes.

**7** Why do evil people continue to live? Why do they become old and very powerful?

**8** They see their children grow up around them. They see their descendants.

**9** Their homes are safe, and they have no fear. God does not punish them.

**10** Their bulls always make their cows pregnant. Their cows have calves, and the calves do not die.

**11** They send out their children like a flock of lambs. Their children dance.

**12** They sing to the music of the tambourine and the harp. They are happy at the sound of the flute.

**13** They spend their lives with riches. Then they die quickly and peacefully.

**14** They say to God, 'Go away from us! We do not want to know your ways.

**15** Who is the Almighty? Why must we serve him? What will we get if we pray to him?'

**16** But their riches do not come from their own power. I do not agree with the advice of evil people.

**17** How often does the lamp of evil people go out? How often does disaster come to them? How often does God punish them in his anger?

**18** How often are they like straw in the wind? How often are they like chaff that a storm blows away?

**19** You say, 'God keeps the punishment of an evil man for his children.' But God must punish the man himself, so that he knows it.

**20** Let him see his own destruction with his own eyes. Let him drink from the anger of the Almighty.

**21** When his life is at an end, he does not care about his family.

**22** No person can teach God anything. God judges even the angels in heaven.

**23** One man dies when he is very strong. He is completely safe and comfortable.

**24** His body is well fed. His bones are strong.

**25** Another man dies with a bitter spirit. He never had any good things.

**26** Both men lie in the dust together. Worms cover them both.

**27** I know your thoughts. I know your plans to hurt me.

**28** You ask, 'Where is the house of the great man now? Where are the tents of evil people?'

**29** Did you not ask travelers? Did you not listen to their reports?

**30** Evil people are safe on the day of disaster. They escape on the day of anger.

**31** No person speaks against an evil man to his face. No person pays him back for what he did.

**32** People carry him to the grave. They put a guard at his tomb.

**33** The soil of the valley is soft on him. All people follow him to death, as many people went before him.

**34** Thus your empty words cannot comfort me. Your answers are only lies."

## Chapter 22

**1** Then Eliphaz from Teman answered,

**2** "A man cannot help God. Even a wise man helps only himself.

**3** If you are good, the Almighty gets no pleasure from it. If you live an honest life, he gets nothing from it.

**4** God does not punish you because you fear him. He does not take you to court because of that.

**5** No, your evil is very great. Your sins have no end.

**6** You took things from your brothers as a guarantee for no reason. You took the clothes from poor people, and they had nothing to wear.

**7** You did not give water to tired people. You did not give food to hungry people.

**8** You were a powerful man and owned land. People gave you honor, and you lived on the land.

**9** You sent widows away with nothing. You crushed the strength of orphans.

**10** Thus traps are all around you. Sudden danger frightens you.

**11** Darkness is around you, and you cannot see. A flood of water covers you.

**12** God is high in the skies. Look at the highest stars. See how high they are!

**13** But you say, 'What does God know? Can he judge through the dark clouds?

**14** Thick clouds cover him, and he cannot see us. He walks on the circle of the sky.'

**15** Will you continue on the old path of evil people?

**16** They died before their time. A flood washed away their foundations.

**17** They said to God, 'Go away from us! The Almighty can do nothing to us.'

**18** But God filled their houses with good things. I do not agree with the advice of evil people.

**19** Good people see the destruction of evil people, and they are glad. Innocent people laugh at the evil people.

**20** They say, 'God destroys our enemies. Fire burns their riches.'

**21** Agree with God, and be at peace with him. Then good things will come to you.

**22** Accept the law from his mouth. Keep his words in your heart.

**23** If you come back to the Almighty, he will make you strong again. Remove evil far from your home.

**24** Then you will have as much gold as dust. You will have as much gold from Ophir as there are stones in the streams.

**25** The Almighty will protect you. You will have much silver.

**26** Then you will have joy in the Almighty. You will look up to God.

**27** You will pray to him, and he will hear you. You will do what you promised him.

**28** You will decide to do something, and you will be successful. Light will shine on your path.

**29** When God makes people low, you will say, 'Lift them up!' Then God will save the humble person.

**30** He will even save a guilty person. He will save that person because your hands are clean."

## Chapter 23

**1** Then Job answered,

**2** "Today my complaint is still bitter. God's hand is heavy on me, although I cry.

**3** I wish that I knew where to find God. Then I will go to his home.

**4** I will explain my case to him. I will give him all my arguments.

**5** I will learn how he will answer me. I will understand what he will say to me.

**6** Will he use his great power to argue against me? No, he will listen to me.

**7** There an honest man can explain his case to God. Then my Judge will make me free forever.

**8** I go to the east, but God is not there. I go to the west, but I do not find him.

**9** When he works in the north, I do not see him. When he goes to the south, I cannot see him.

**10** But he knows the path that I take. When he tests me, I will come out pure like gold.

**11** My feet follow his steps closely. I keep on his path and do not turn away from it.

**12** I obey the orders that he gives. I think that his words are more important than my daily food.

**13** But God does not change his mind. No person can stop him. He does what he wants.

**14** He will do what he decided for me. He has many such plans.

**15** Thus I am afraid of him. When I think about this, I am afraid of him.

**16** God makes me weak. The Almighty frightens me.

**17** But darkness does not make me silent. The thick darkness that covers my face does not make me silent.

## Chapter 24

**1** "The Almighty knows the times of judgment. Why do the people who know him not see these days?

**2** Evil people move the stones that mark the limits of land. They steal flocks and keep them as their own.

**3** They take the donkey of orphans. They take the ox of a widow as a guarantee for a debt.

**4** They push poor people off the road. All the poor people of the land must hide.

**5** Poor people are like wild donkeys in the desert. They go out early to look for food. They find food for their children in the desert.

**6** They collect grain in fields that are not theirs. They collect grapes in the vineyards of evil people.

**7** They have no clothes, and they sleep without clothes at night. They have nothing to cover themselves in the cold.

**8** The rain in the mountains makes them wet. They hold close to the rocks because they have no shelter.

**9** Evil people take babies with no father from their mothers. They take the babies of poor people as a guarantee for a debt.

**10** Poor people go without clothes. They are hungry, but they must carry bundles of grain.

**11** They press olives to make oil inside the walls of evil people. They crush grapes to make wine, but they are thirsty.

**12** In the city, dying people cry. Wounded people call for help. But God does not say that any person did wrong.

**13** Some people fight against the light. They do not know its ways. They do not stay on its paths.

**14** The murderer gets up early in the morning. He kills poor people and people who need help. At night he is like a thief.

**15** The man who commits adultery waits for the evening. He thinks, 'No person will see me.' He covers his face.

**16** At night, thieves break into houses. In the day they hide. They do not want to see the light.

**17** For all of them, the morning is like deep darkness. They are friends with the terrors of darkness.

**18** But evil people are like foam on the water. God puts a curse on their land. No person goes to their vineyards.

**19** Heat and dry weather take away the melted snow. In the same way, the grave takes away people who sin.

**20** Their mothers will forget them. Worms will eat them. No person will remember them. Evil will fall like a tree that someone cuts down.

**21** They are cruel to women who have no children. They do not help widows.

**22** But God uses his power to remove powerful people. When God acts, they cannot be sure of their life.

**23** God lets them feel safe and secure. But he watches all that they do.

**24** For a short time, evil people are important. Then they are gone. They fall down and die like all other people. God cuts them off like the tops of the grain.

**25** If this is not true, who can prove that I am a liar? Who can show that my words are wrong?"

## Chapter 25

**1** Then Bildad from Shuah answered,

**2** "God rules with power. All people must fear him. He makes peace in the highest heaven.

**3** No person can count his armies. His light shines on all things.

**4** Thus a man cannot be right in front of God. A person that a woman gives birth to cannot be pure.

**5** Even the moon is not bright to God. Even the stars are not pure in his eyes.

**6** Thus man is much less pure. Man is like a maggot. A human is like a worm."

## Chapter 26

**1** Then Job answered,

**2** "You did not help a weak person! You did not save a man with no strength!

**3** You gave no good advice to a person without wisdom! You did not give much useful information!

**4** Who helped you to say these words? Whose spirit spoke through you?

**5** The dead shake with fear under the waters. All the creatures in the waters shake.

**6** The grave is open in front of God. The place of destruction has no cover.

**7** God spreads out the northern sky over empty space. He hangs the earth on nothing.

**8** He holds the water in his thick clouds. The clouds do not break under the weight of the water.

**9** He covers the face of the full moon. He spreads his clouds over it.

**10** He makes a line on the surface of the waters. This line is the limit between light and darkness.

**11** The pillars of the skies shake. They are afraid when God speaks angrily.

**12** With his power he makes the sea calm. With his wisdom he destroys Rahab (the sea monster).

**13** His breath makes the skies clear. His hand kills the snake that moves quickly.

**14** These are only a small part of what God does. We hear only a quiet sound of him. No person can understand the thunder of his power!"

## Chapter 27

**1** Job continued to speak,

**2** "God took away my rights. The Almighty made my life bitter. But as surely as God lives, I promise this:

**3** While I have breath, and while God gives breath to me,

**4** I will not say evil things. I will not tell lies.

**5** I will never agree that you are right. Until I die, I will say that I am innocent.

**6** I will continue to say that I am good. I will not stop. My conscience does not accuse me for any day of my life.

**7** Let my enemy be like evil people. Let the people who attack me be like wrong people.

**8** When God takes the life of an evil person, that person has no hope. His riches do not help him.

**9** When trouble comes, God does not hear his cry.

**10** He does not get joy from the Almighty. He does not always pray to God.

**11** I will teach you about the power of God. I will not hide the plans of the Almighty.

**12** You all saw these things yourselves. Thus why do you say these words that have no meaning?

**13** This is what God does to an evil man. This is what cruel people will get from the Almighty.

**14** He can have many children, but a sword will kill them. His descendants will never have sufficient food.

**15** Disease will kill the people of his family who remain. Their widows will not cry for them.

**16** He can collect silver like dust. He can collect clothes like piles of clay.

**17** But good people will wear his clothes. Innocent people will divide his silver.

**18** The house that he builds is weak like the home of a moth. It is like a hut that a guard makes.

**19** He goes to bed rich, but he will not stay rich. When he opens his eyes, all his riches are gone.

**20** Terror attacks him like a flood. A storm takes him away in the night.

**21** The east wind carries him away, and he is gone. It takes him from his place.

**22** The wind attacks him without mercy. He tries to escape from its power.

**23** People clap their hands at him and laugh. They whistle at him as he leaves his place."

## Chapter 28

**1** There is a mine for silver. There is a place where workers make gold pure.

**2** Men take iron out of the earth. They melt copper out of the stone.

**3** A miner puts an end to darkness. He searches to the farthest limits for ore in the dark and in deep shadow.

**4** He cuts a shaft far from the places where people live. Travelers do not know that place. The miners hang and swing far from other men.

**5** Food comes from the surface of the earth. But below, the earth changes as if fire turns it over.

**6** Sapphires are in the stones of the earth. The dust of the earth contains gold.

**7** No bird of prey knows the path to the mine. The eye of the falcon did not see that path.

**8** The proud animals did not walk on it. The fierce lion did not go by it.

**9** The miner puts his hand on the hard rock. He turns the mountains over at their base.

**10** He cuts channels through the rocks. His eye sees all the valuable things.

**11** He stops the streams so that they do not flow. He brings hidden things into the light.

**12** But where can a person find wisdom? Where is the place of knowledge?

**13** Man does not know the value of wisdom. A person cannot find wisdom in the land of people who live.

**14** The deep water says, "Wisdom is not in me." The sea says, "Wisdom is not with me."

**15** A person cannot buy wisdom with gold. He cannot weigh silver to pay for it.

**16** The gold of Ophir cannot pay for wisdom. Valuable onyx and sapphire cannot pay for it.

**17** Gold and crystal are not equal to wisdom. A person cannot exchange wisdom for jewels of fine gold.

**18** Coral and crystal are not important in comparison. The value of wisdom is more than the value of rubies.

**19** The topaz of Ethiopia is not equal to wisdom. Pure gold cannot pay for it.

**20** Then where does wisdom come from? Where is the place of knowledge?

**21** Wisdom hides from the eyes of all things that live. The birds of the sky cannot see it.

**22** Destruction and Death say, "We heard only a report about wisdom."

**23** God understands the way to wisdom. He knows the place of wisdom.

**24** He looks to the farthest parts of the earth. He sees everything below the sky.

**25** He gave a weight to the wind. He measured the quantity of the waters.

**26** He made a law for the rain. He made a path for the lightning and the thunder.

**27** At that time he saw wisdom and told its value. He made wisdom firm and examined it.

**28** He said to man, "Look, to respect the Lord with fear is wisdom. To go away from evil is good sense."

## Chapter 29

**1** Job continued to speak. He said,

**2** "I want to be as I was in the past months. I want the days again when God kept me safe.

**3** At that time, his lamp gave light above my head. By his light, I walked through the darkness.

**4** I was in the best days of my life. At that time, God was a close friend in my tent.

**5** The Almighty was still with me. My children were around me.

**6** I had much milk and cream. The rock poured out streams of olive oil for me.

**7** I went out to the gate of the city. I took my seat in the public square.

**8** The young men saw me and stepped back. The old men stood up to show respect.

**9** The leaders stopped their talk. They put their hands on their mouths.

**10** The important men did not speak. They kept their tongues still.

**11** All who heard me said good things about me. All who saw me spoke well of me.

**12** I helped the poor man who cried for help. I helped the orphan and the person who had no helper.

**13** The man who was near death blessed me. I caused the widow's heart to sing with joy.

**14** I did what was right, and righteousness was like clothing on me. My justice was like a robe and a turban.

**15** I was eyes for the blind man. I was feet for the lame man.

**16** I was a father to the poor. I examined the case of the stranger.

**17** I broke the power of the wicked man. I took his victims away from him.

**18** Then I said, 'I will die in my own home. My days will be as many as the grains of sand.

**19** I am like a tree with roots that go down to the water. The dew stays all night on my branches.

**20** My honor will stay new. My strength will stay new, like a new bow in my hand.'

**21** Men listened to me and waited. They did not speak when I gave advice.

**22** After I spoke, they did not speak again. My words fell gently on them.

**23** They waited for me as for the rain. They opened their mouths for my words, as for the spring rain.

**24** When I smiled at them, they could not believe it. The light of my face gave them courage.

**25** I chose the way for them. I sat as their chief. I lived like a king among his army. I was like a man who comforts sad people."

## Chapter 30

**1** "But now men who are younger than I laugh at me. I did not think that their fathers were good enough to work with my sheep dogs.

**2** The strength of their hands was of no use to me. Their vigor was gone.

**3** They were thin because they had no food. They ate dry roots in the desert at night, in the empty waste land.

**4** They picked salt plants among the bushes. The roots of the broom tree were their food.

**5** People sent them away from the community. People shouted at them as at a thief.

**6** They had to live in the dry beds of the valleys. They lived in holes in the ground and among the rocks.

**7** They made noises like animals among the bushes. They lay together under the thorn plants.

**8** They were the sons of fools and of men with no name. People drove them out of the land.

**9** And now the sons of these men sing songs to laugh at me. I am a joke to them.

**10** They hate me and stay far away from me. They spit in my face.

**11** God made me weak and caused me trouble. Thus they act without control in front of me.

**12** On my right side, a mob of young men attacks. They push my feet away. They build ramps to attack and destroy me.

**13** They block my path. They make my trouble worse. They need no person to help them.

**14** They come at me as through a wide hole in a wall. They roll over me in the ruins.

**15** Terrors attack me. They chase away my honor as the wind does. My safety goes away like a cloud.

**16** Now my life flows out of me. Days of pain hold me.

**17** At night, pain goes deep into my bones. The pains that attack me do not stop.

**18** With great force, God holds my clothing. He holds me tightly like the collar of my coat.

**19** He threw me into the mud. I am like dust and ashes.

**20** God, I cry to you, but you do not answer me. I stand up, but you only look at me.

**21** You are cruel to me. You attack me with the power of your hand.

**22** You lift me up on the wind. You cause the wind to carry me. You throw me about in the storm.

**23** I know that you will bring me to death. You will bring me to the place where all people who live will go.

**24** But a man in ruins lifts out his hand for help. In his trouble, he cries out.

**25** I cried for the man who had trouble. I was sad for the poor.

**26** I hoped for good, but evil came to me. I waited for light, but darkness came.

**27** My body is full of pain without rest. Days of pain come against me.

**28** I go around sad and dark, without the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

**29** I am like a brother to the jackals. I am like a companion to the ostriches.

**30** My skin becomes black and falls off. My body burns with fever.

**31** My harp plays only sad music. My flute makes the sound of people who weep."

## Chapter 31

**1** "I made an agreement (covenant) with my eyes. I promised not to look with desire at a young woman.

**2** What does God above give to such a man? What does the Almighty on high give him as an inheritance?

**3** God sends disaster to the wicked. He sends trouble to the people who do evil.

**4** God sees my ways. He counts all my steps.

**5** Maybe I lived a false life. Maybe my feet went quickly to deceive people.

**6** If so, let God weigh me on honest scales. Then God will know that I am innocent.

**7** Maybe my steps went away from the right path. Maybe my heart followed my eyes. Maybe my hands became dirty with sin.

**8** If so, let another man eat what I planted. Let other people pull up my crops.

**9** Maybe a woman caused my heart to desire her. Maybe I waited at the door of my neighbor.

**10** If so, let my wife grind grain for another man. Let other men sleep with her.

**11** That is a very bad crime. That is a sin that the judges must punish.

**12** That sin is a fire that burns everything until nothing stays. It burns up all my harvest.

**13** Maybe I did not give justice to my male or female servant when they had a complaint against me.

**14** If so, what will I do when God stands up to judge me? When he examines me, what will I tell him?

**15** God made me in my mother's womb. He made my servant too. The same God formed both of us before birth.

**16** Maybe I did not give to the poor what they needed. Maybe I caused the widow to lose hope.

**17** Maybe I ate my food alone. Maybe I did not share it with the orphan.

**18** But from my youth I raised the orphan as a father does. From my birth I guided the widow.

**19** Maybe I saw a person who died because he had no clothing. Maybe I saw a poor man without a coat.

**20** Maybe that man did not thank me, because I did not make him warm with wool from my sheep.

**21** Possibly I raised my hand against the orphan because I knew that the judges at the gate will support me.

**22** If so, let my arm fall from my shoulder. Let my arm break off at the joint.

**23** I was afraid of disaster from God. Because of his majesty, I could not do these things.

**24** Maybe I trusted in gold. Maybe I said to pure gold, 'You keep me safe.'

**25** Maybe I was glad because I had much wealth. Maybe I was glad because my hand got much money.

**26** Maybe I looked at the sun when it was bright. Maybe I looked at the moon as it moved in its glory.

**27** Maybe my heart secretly wanted to worship them. Maybe I kissed my hand to show them honor.

**28** That is also a sin that the judges must punish. If I did that, I was not loyal to God above.

**29** Maybe I was glad when my enemy had trouble. Maybe I was happy when disaster found him.

**30** But I did not let my mouth sin. I did not ask for a curse on his life.

**31** The men of my household always said, 'All people get enough meat from Job.'

**32** No stranger had to sleep in the street. I opened my doors to the traveler.

**33** Maybe I hid my sins as other men do. Maybe I kept my guilt secret in my heart.

**34** Maybe I was afraid of the crowd. Maybe the contempt of families frightened me. Maybe I stayed quiet and did not go out of my door.

**35** I want a person to hear me! Here is my signature. Let the Almighty answer me. Let my accuser write down his charges against me.

**36** Then I will carry the charges on my shoulder. I will wear them like a crown.

**37** I will tell God about every step that I took. I will come near to him as a prince.

**38** Maybe my land cries out against me. Maybe the furrows of my land cry together.

**39** Maybe I ate the crops of the land without payment. Maybe I caused the owners of the land to die.

**40** If so, let thorns grow on my land instead of wheat. Let weeds grow instead of barley." The words of Job are at an end.

## Chapter 32

**1** These 3 men stopped their answers to Job, because Job thought that he was righteous.

**2** Then Elihu became very angry. Elihu was the son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram. Elihu was angry with Job, because Job said that he was right and that God was wrong.

**3** Elihu was also angry with the 3 friends of Job. They found no answer to Job, but they said that Job was guilty.

**4** Elihu waited until Job stopped his words, because the other men were older than Elihu.

**5** Elihu saw that the 3 men had no answer. Then he became angry.

**6** Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite spoke. He said, "I am young, and you are very old. Thus I was afraid. I did not dare to tell you my opinion.

**7** I said, 'Older people must speak. Many years of life must teach wisdom.'

**8** But there is a spirit in man. The breath of the Almighty gives people knowledge.

**9** Men are not wise only because they are old. Old men do not always understand what is right.

**10** Thus I say, 'Listen to me. I will also tell you my opinion.'

**11** Look, I waited while you spoke. I listened to your reasons while you searched for words.

**12** I paid careful attention to you. But no person among you showed that Job was wrong. No person among you answered his words.

**13** Do not say, 'We found wisdom. God must defeat Job, not man.'

**14** Job did not speak his words against me. I will not answer him with your arguments.

**15** These men feel surprise. They do not answer anymore. They have no more words.

**16** I waited, but they do not speak. They stand there and do not answer.

**17** Now I will also give my answer. I will also tell my opinion.

**18** I am full of words. The spirit in me pushes me to speak.

**19** I am like wine in a closed container. I am like a new wineskin that is about to burst.

**20** I must speak to get relief. I must open my lips and answer.

**21** I will not show favor to any man. I will not use false praise for any person.

**22** I do not know how to use false praise. If I do that, my Maker will quickly take me away."

## Chapter 33

**1** "Job, please hear my speech. Listen to all my words.

**2** Look, I open my mouth. My tongue is ready to speak.

**3** My words come from an honest heart. My lips speak the truth clearly.

**4** The Spirit of God made me. The breath of the Almighty gives me life.

**5** If you can, answer me. Put your arguments in order and stand up to speak.

**6** Look, I am the same as you in front of God. God also made me from clay.

**7** Thus you must not be afraid of me. I will not put a heavy pressure on you.

**8** I heard you speak. I heard the sound of your words. You said,

**9** 'I am clean and without sin. I am innocent. There is no guilt in me.

**10** Look, God finds reasons to attack me. He thinks that I am his enemy.

**11** He puts my feet in chains. He watches all my paths.'

**12** But I tell you that you are not right in this. God is greater than man.

**13** Why do you argue against God? He does not have to explain his actions to any person.

**14** God speaks one time, and then again, but man does not notice it.

**15** God speaks in a dream, in a vision at night. He speaks when people are in deep sleep on their beds.

**16** Then God speaks into the ears of men. He frightens them with warnings.

**17** He does this to turn a man away from wrong actions. He does this to keep a man from pride.

**18** God keeps the man's soul from the pit of death. He keeps the man's life from death by the sword.

**19** God also corrects a man with pain on his bed. The man feels continuous pain in his bones.

**20** Then the man hates food. He does not want even the best food.

**21** His body becomes very thin. His bones stick out where people did not see them before.

**22** His soul comes near to the pit of death. His life comes near to the messengers of death.

**23** Maybe an angel is near him to speak for him. That angel is one of 1,000. He tells the man what is right for him.

**24** The angel is kind to the man. The angel says to God, 'Save him from the pit of death. I found a price to set him free.'

**25** Then the man's body becomes new again, like the body of a child. He becomes as strong as in his youth.

**26** The man prays to God, and God accepts him. The man sees the face of God and shouts with joy. God makes him righteous again.

**27** Then the man sings to other people. He says, 'I sinned. I made the right thing wrong. But God did not punish me as I deserved.

**28** God saved my soul from the pit of death. I will live and see the light.'

**29** Look, God does all these things to a man 2 or 3 times.

**30** God brings back his soul from the pit of death. Then the man can enjoy the light of life.

**31** Pay attention, Job, and listen to me. Be quiet, and I will speak.

**32** If you have something to say, answer me. Speak, because I want to show that you are right.

**33** If you have nothing to say, then listen to me. Be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom."

## Chapter 34

**1** Then Elihu continued and said,

**2** "Hear my words, you wise men. Listen to me, you men who have knowledge.

**3** The ear tests words as the mouth tastes food.

**4** We must choose for ourselves what is right. We must decide together what is good.

**5** Job says, 'I am innocent, but God does not give me justice.

**6** I am right, but people say that I am a liar. No person can heal my wound, but I did not sin.'

**7** What man is like Job? He drinks up contempt as if it is water.

**8** He goes with people who do evil. He walks with wicked men.

**9** He says, 'A man gets no advantage when he tries to please God.'

**10** Thus listen to me, you men of good sense. God never does evil. The Almighty never does wrong.

**11** God pays back each man for what he does. God gives each man what his actions deserve.

**12** It is true that God will not do evil. The Almighty will not make justice wrong.

**13** No person put God in charge of the earth. No person gave him control of the whole world.

**14** If God decides to take back his spirit and his breath,

**15** then all things that live will die together. Man will become dust again.

**16** If you have good sense, then hear this. Listen to my words.

**17** Can a person who hates justice rule? Will you say that the righteous and mighty God is guilty?

**18** God says to a king, 'You are worthless.' He says to rulers, 'You are wicked.'

**19** God does not show favor to princes. He does not give more respect to the rich than to the poor. He made all of them with his hands.

**20** They die suddenly in the middle of the night. God shakes the people, and they go away. God removes mighty people without a human hand.

**21** God watches the ways of man. He sees all the steps of each man.

**22** There is no darkness and no deep shadow where evil people can hide from God.

**23** God does not have to examine a man again. Man does not have to come to God for judgment.

**24** God breaks mighty men without an investigation. He puts other men in their place.

**25** God knows what they do. Thus he defeats them in the night, and he destroys them.

**26** He strikes them for their wickedness where other people can see it.

**27** They turned away from God. They did not respect any of his ways.

**28** They caused the poor to cry out to God. God hears the cry of people who suffer.

**29** If God stays quiet, who can say that he is wrong? If God hides his face, who can see him? God rules over nations and over each man.

**30** He does this to stop godless men from rule. He does this to keep people safe from their traps.

**31** Maybe a man says to God, 'I am guilty. I will not sin again.

**32** Teach me what I do not see. If I did wrong, I will not do it again.'

**33** Then must God reward the man in the way you want? You refuse to accept God's way. You must decide, not I. Thus tell me what you know.

**34** Men of good sense will say to me, and the wise man who hears me will say,

**35** 'Job speaks without knowledge. His words do not show wisdom.'

**36** I want people to test Job completely, because he answers like a wicked man.

**37** He adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands in contempt among us. He speaks many words against God."

## Chapter 35

**1** Then Elihu continued and said,

**2** "Do you think that this is right? You say, 'I am more righteous than God.'

**3** You ask God, 'What advantage do I get? What do I get if I do not sin?'

**4** I will answer you and your friends.

**5** Look up at the sky and see. Look at the clouds, which are high above you.

**6** If you sin, how does that hurt God? If you sin many times, what do you do to him?

**7** If you are righteous, what do you give to God? What does God get from your hand?

**8** Your wickedness hurts only people like you. Your righteousness helps only other humans.

**9** People cry out because powerful men oppress them very much. They cry for help against the power of the strong.

**10** But no person says, 'Where is God, my Maker? He gives songs in the night.

**11** He teaches us more than he teaches the animals of the earth. He makes us wiser than the birds of the sky.'

**12** People cry out there, but God does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.

**13** It is true that God does not hear empty cries. The Almighty does not pay attention to them.

**14** You say that you do not see God. But your case is in front of God, and you must wait for him.

**15** You say that God does not punish in his anger. You say that God does not notice wickedness.

**16** Thus Job opens his mouth to speak empty words. He speaks many words without knowledge."

## Chapter 36

**1** Elihu continued and said,

**2** "Be patient with me a little longer, and I will show you. I have more to say for God.

**3** I will get my knowledge from far away. I will show that my Maker is righteous.

**4** It is true that my words are not false. A man with complete knowledge is with you.

**5** Look, God is mighty, but he does not hate any person. He is mighty in strength and in wisdom.

**6** God does not keep the wicked alive. He gives justice to the people who suffer.

**7** God always watches the righteous. He puts them on thrones with kings. He gives them honor for all time.

**8** But sometimes people are in chains. Sometimes ropes of trouble hold them.

**9** Then God tells them what they did. He shows them that they sinned with pride.

**10** He causes them to hear his correction. He commands them to turn away from evil.

**11** If they obey and serve him, then they will have good days. They will have pleasant years.

**12** But if they do not obey, then they will die by the sword. They will die without knowledge.

**13** The godless people keep their anger in their hearts. When God puts them in chains, they do not cry for help.

**14** They die while they are young. They die in shame, with the male prostitutes of the temples.

**15** God saves the people who suffer through their pain. He speaks to them in their trouble.

**16** God wants to take you out of trouble too. He wants to bring you into an open place without problems. He wants to put the best food on your table.

**17** But now you are full of the judgment that the wicked deserve. Judgment and justice hold you.

**18** Be careful. Do not let riches cause you to do wrong. Do not let a large bribe turn you away.

**19** Your wealth cannot help you in trouble. All your strength cannot help you.

**20** Do not want the night, when God removes people from their places.

**21** Be careful. Do not turn to evil. You chose evil instead of pain.

**22** Look, God is great in his power. No teacher is like God.

**23** No person tells God which way to go. No person can say to God, 'You did wrong.'

**24** Remember to praise God's work. People sing songs about his work.

**25** All people see God's work. Men see it from far away.

**26** Look, God is great, and we do not completely know him. No person can count the number of his years.

**27** God pulls up the drops of water. The water vapor becomes rain.

**28** The clouds pour down the rain. Much rain falls on people.

**29** No person can understand how the clouds spread out. No person can understand the thunder from God's tent.

**30** Look, God spreads his lightning around him. He covers the depths of the sea.

**31** By these things God controls the nations. He gives food in large quantities.

**32** He holds the lightning in his hands. He commands the lightning to hit its target.

**33** The thunder tells about the storm. The cattle also know that the storm comes."

## Chapter 37

**1** "My heart shakes at the storm. My heart jumps in my chest.

**2** Listen carefully to the thunder of God's voice. Listen to the sound that comes from his mouth.

**3** God sends his lightning under the whole sky. He sends it to the farthest parts of the earth.

**4** After the lightning, God's voice roars. He thunders with his majestic voice. He does not stop the lightning while people hear his voice.

**5** God thunders with his voice in a wonderful way. He does great things that we cannot understand.

**6** God says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth.' He says the same to the light rain and to the heavy rain.

**7** God stops the work of every man. He does this so that all men will know his work.

**8** Then the animals go into their dens. They stay in their places.

**9** The storm comes from the south. The cold comes from the north winds.

**10** The breath of God makes ice. The wide waters become frozen.

**11** God fills the thick clouds with water. He scatters his lightning through the clouds.

**12** The clouds turn around and around as God directs them. They do all that he commands on the surface of the whole earth.

**13** God causes the clouds to come for different purposes. He sends them to punish people, or to water his land, or to show his love.

**14** Listen to this, Job. Stop and think about the wonderful works of God.

**15** Do you know how God controls the clouds? Do you know how he causes his lightning to shine?

**16** Do you know how the clouds float in the sky? These are the wonderful works of God, who has complete knowledge.

**17** You feel hot in your clothes when the land is still under the south wind.

**18** Can you, like God, spread out the sky? The sky is as hard as a metal mirror.

**19** Tell us what we must say to God. We cannot prepare our arguments, because we are in the dark.

**20** Must a person tell God that I want to speak? No man wants God to destroy him.

**21** Now people cannot look at the sun when it is bright in the sky. The wind blows and makes the sky clear.

**22** A golden light comes from the north. God comes with terrible majesty.

**23** We cannot reach the Almighty. He is very great in power. He is just and very righteous. He does not oppress people.

**24** Thus people respect him with fear. He does not pay attention to people who think that they are wise."

## Chapter 38

**1** Then the LORD answered Job from the storm. He said,

**2** "Who is this man who makes my plan dark with words without knowledge?

**3** Prepare yourself like a man. I will ask you questions, and you must answer me.

**4** Where were you when I made the foundation of the earth? Tell me, if you understand.

**5** Who decided the size of the earth? Surely you know! Who measured it with a line?

**6** What holds up the base of the earth? Who put its cornerstone in its place?

**7** At that time, the morning stars sang together. All the angels shouted with joy.

**8** Who closed the doors to hold in the sea? The sea burst out, as a baby comes out of the womb.

**9** I made the clouds its clothing. I wrapped it in thick darkness.

**10** I made a limit for the sea. I put its bars and doors in their place.

**11** I said, 'You can come this far, but no farther. Your proud waves must stop here.'

**12** In your life, did you ever command the morning to start? Did you show the dawn its place?

**13** Did you cause the dawn to hold the edges of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?

**14** The earth changes shape like clay under a seal. The features of the earth stand out like the folds of clothing.

**15** God takes the light away from the wicked. He breaks their arm that they raise to attack.

**16** Did you go to the springs at the bottom of the sea? Did you walk in the deepest parts of the ocean?

**17** Did a person show you the gates of death? Did you see the gates of the deep darkness?

**18** Do you understand how wide the earth is? Tell me, if you know all this.

**19** Where is the path to the home of light? Where does darkness live?

**20** Can you take them to their places? Do you know the paths to their homes?

**21** Surely you know these things, because you were alive then! You lived very many years!

**22** Did you go into the storehouses of the snow? Did you see the storehouses of the hail?

**23** I keep them for the time of trouble. I keep them for the day of battle and war.

**24** What is the path to the place where the lightning spreads out? Where is the place from which the east wind blows across the earth?

**25** Who cuts a channel for the heavy rain? Who makes a path for the thunderstorm?

**26** Who causes rain to fall on land where no person lives? Who causes rain on the desert where there are no people?

**27** The rain satisfies the dry and empty ground. The rain causes the new grass to grow.

**28** Does the rain have a father? Who is the father of the drops of dew?

**29** Who is the mother of the ice? Who gives birth to the frost from the sky?

**30** The waters become as hard as stone. The surface of the deep water becomes frozen.

**31** Can you tie together the stars of the Pleiades? Can you loosen the belt of Orion?

**32** Can you bring out the stars of Mazzaroth at their correct time? Can you guide the Bear and its cubs?

**33** Do you know the laws of the sky? Can you make those laws control the earth?

**34** Can you shout to the clouds and cause much rain to cover you?

**35** Can you send out the lightning? Will the lightning come to you and say, 'We are here'?

**36** Who put wisdom in the heart? Who gives knowledge to the mind?

**37** Who is wise enough to count the clouds? Who can pour out the water from the sky,

**38** when the dust becomes hard and the soil sticks together?

**39** Can you hunt food for the lioness? Can you satisfy the hunger of the young lions,

**40** when they lie in their dens? Can you feed them when they wait in the bushes to attack?

**41** Who gives food to the raven when its young birds cry out to God? Who feeds them when they have no food and move about?"

## Chapter 39

**1** "Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the deer give birth to their young?

**2** Can you count the months until they give birth? Do you know the time when they give birth?

**3** They bend down and give birth to their young. Then their pain stops.

**4** Their young become strong and grow in the open fields. They go away and do not come back.

**5** Who set the wild donkey free? Who removed its ropes?

**6** I gave it the desert as its home. I gave it the salt land as its place to live.

**7** It laughs at the noise of the city. It does not hear the shouts of a driver.

**8** It goes through the mountains to find food. It searches for every green plant.

**9** Will the wild ox agree to serve you? Will it stay at night near your feed box?

**10** Can you tie the wild ox with a rope to plow a furrow? Will it break up the soil in the valleys for you?

**11** Will you trust the wild ox because its strength is great? Will you give your heavy work to it?

**12** Can you trust it to bring your grain home? Will it collect the grain to the floor where you beat the grain?

**13** The wings of the ostrich move with joy. But its wings and feathers do not show love like the wings of the stork.

**14** The ostrich puts her eggs on the ground. She lets the sand keep them warm.

**15** She does not think that a foot can crush the eggs. She does not think that a wild animal can break them.

**16** She is cruel to her young, as if they are not hers. She is not afraid that her work is for no purpose.

**17** God did not give her wisdom. He did not give her good sense.

**18** But when she runs fast, she laughs at the horse and its rider.

**19** Do you give the horse its strength? Do you put the mane on its neck?

**20** Can you cause the horse to jump like a locust? Its proud snort causes fear.

**21** It paws the ground in the valley and is glad in its strength. It runs out to meet the weapons.

**22** It laughs at fear and is not afraid. It does not turn back from the sword.

**23** The quiver of arrows rattles on its side. The spear and the javelin shine there.

**24** It runs quickly over the ground with fierce excitement. It cannot stand still when the trumpet sounds.

**25** When the trumpet sounds, it says, 'Aha!' It smells the battle from far away. It hears the shouts of the commanders and the battle cry.

**26** Does the hawk fly because of your wisdom? Does it spread its wings to the south because you know how?

**27** Does the eagle fly high because you command it? Does it make its nest high in the mountains because of you?

**28** The eagle lives on the high rock. It stays at night on the cliff, in a strong place.

**29** From there, it looks for food. Its eyes see the food from far away.

**30** Its young birds drink blood. Where there are dead bodies, the eagle is there."

## Chapter 40

**1** The LORD continued to speak to Job. He said,

**2** "Will the man who argues with the Almighty correct him? The man who says that God is wrong must answer."

**3** Then Job answered the LORD. He said,

**4** "Look, I am not important. What can I say to you? I put my hand over my mouth.

**5** I spoke one time, but I will not answer again. I spoke 2 times, but I will say nothing more."

**6** Then the LORD answered Job from the storm. He said,

**7** "Prepare yourself like a man. I will ask you questions, and you must answer me.

**8** Will you say that my justice is wrong? Will you say that I am guilty so that you can be right?

**9** Is your arm as strong as God's arm? Can you thunder with a voice like his voice?

**10** If so, put on majesty and honor. Put on glory and splendor as clothing.

**11** Pour out the power of your anger. Look at every proud person and make him humble.

**12** Look at every proud person and bring him down. Crush the wicked where they stand.

**13** Bury all of them together in the dust. Lock them in the grave.

**14** Then I will also agree that your own right hand can save you.

**15** Look at Behemoth. I made him as I made you. He eats grass like an ox.

**16** Look, his strength is in his hips. His power is in the muscles of his stomach.

**17** His tail is as stiff as a cedar tree. The muscles of his thighs are strong and tight.

**18** His bones are like tubes of bronze. His legs are like bars of iron.

**19** He is the first among the works of God. Only his Maker can come near him with a sword.

**20** The mountains give him food, where all the wild animals play.

**21** He lies under the lotus plants. He hides among the reeds in the marsh.

**22** The lotus plants cover him with their shade. The willows near the stream are around him.

**23** Look, if the river floods, he is not afraid. He is calm even when the Jordan River rushes against his mouth.

**24** Can a person catch him while he watches? Can a person put a ring through his nose with a trap?"

## Chapter 41

**1** "Can you pull out Leviathan with a fishhook? Can you tie down his tongue with a rope?

**2** Can you put a rope through his nose? Can you put a hook through his jaw?

**3** Will he ask you many times for mercy? Will he speak gentle words to you?

**4** Will he make an agreement (covenant) with you? Will you make him your slave for all time?

**5** Will you play with him as with a bird? Will you put him on a leash for your young girls?

**6** Will traders buy and sell him? Will they divide him among the merchants?

**7** Can you fill his skin with harpoons? Can you fill his head with fish spears?

**8** Put your hand on him one time. You will remember the fight, and you will not do it again.

**9** Look, any hope to defeat him is false. Only the sight of him makes a person fall down.

**10** No person is fierce enough to wake him up. Thus who can stand in front of me?

**11** Who gave something to me first, so that I must pay him back? Everything under the whole sky is mine.

**12** I will speak about the parts of Leviathan's body. I will tell about his great strength and his good form.

**13** Who can pull off his outer skin? Who can come near him with a bridle?

**14** Who can open the doors of his mouth? His teeth cause terror all around.

**15** His back has rows of shields. They stay tightly together, as with a seal.

**16** Each one is so near to the next one that no air can go between them.

**17** They join one to another. They hold together, and no person can separate them.

**18** When he sneezes, light flashes. His eyes are like the first light of the morning.

**19** Burning torches come out of his mouth. Sparks of fire jump out.

**20** Smoke comes out of his nose, as from a pot that boils over a fire of reeds.

**21** His breath sets coals on fire. A flame comes out of his mouth.

**22** His neck is very strong. Terror goes in front of him.

**23** The folds of his skin join tightly together. They are firm, and no person can move them.

**24** His heart is as hard as a stone. It is as hard as the lower millstone.

**25** When he stands up, the mighty are afraid. They step back because of his attack.

**26** A sword that hits him has no effect. Spears, darts and javelins also have no effect.

**27** He thinks that iron is like straw. He thinks that bronze is like rotten wood.

**28** Arrows do not cause him to run away. Stones from a sling are like dry grass to him.

**29** He thinks that clubs are like dry grass. He laughs at the noise of a spear.

**30** His lower parts are like sharp pieces of broken pots. He leaves marks in the mud like a sledge that beats the grain.

**31** He causes the deep water to boil like a pot. He causes the sea to bubble like a pot of perfume.

**32** He leaves a bright path behind him. A person thinks that the deep water has white hair.

**33** Nothing on earth is equal to him. He is a creature without fear.

**34** He looks down on all the proud animals. He is king over all the proud creatures."

## Chapter 42

**1** Then Job answered the LORD. He said,

**2** "I know that you can do all things. No person can stop your plans.

**3** You asked, 'Who is this man who hides my plan without knowledge?' I spoke about things that I did not understand. These things were too wonderful for me to know.

**4** You said, 'Listen now, and I will speak. I will ask you questions, and you must answer me.'

**5** Before, I only heard about you with my ears. But now I see you with my eyes.

**6** Thus I hate what I said. I sit in dust and ashes, and I change my mind (repent)."

**7** The LORD finished his words to Job. Then the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "I am angry with you and with your 2 friends. You did not speak the truth about me, as my servant Job did.

**8** Thus take 7 bulls and 7 rams now. Go to my servant Job. Give them as a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer. Then I will not punish you for your foolishness. You did not speak the truth about me, as my servant Job did."

**9** So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went. They did what the LORD commanded them. The LORD accepted the prayer of Job.

**10** Job prayed for his friends. Then the LORD gave back to Job all his prosperity. The LORD gave Job 2 times as much as he had before.

**11** Then all the brothers and sisters of Job came to him. All the people who knew him before also came. They ate food with him in his house. They showed him sympathy. They comforted him for all the trouble that the LORD brought on him. Each person gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.

**12** The LORD blessed the last part of Job's life more than the first part. Job had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pairs of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys.

**13** He also had 7 sons and 3 daughters.

**14** He gave the name Jemimah to the first daughter. He gave the name Keziah to the second daughter. He gave the name Keren-Happuch to the third daughter.

**15** In all the land, no women were as beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance with their brothers.

**16** After this, Job lived 140 years. He saw his children and his grandchildren for 4 generations.

**17** Then Job died. He was very old, and he had a long and full life.

# Psalms

## Chapter 1

**1** A man who does not follow the advice of wicked people is blessed. He does not stand in the path of sinners. He does not sit with people who mock.

**2** But he is glad to obey the law of the LORD. He thinks about the law of the LORD day and night.

**3** He is like a tree that grows near streams of water. The tree gives its fruit at the correct time. Its leaves do not become dry. All that this man does is successful.

**4** The wicked are not like that. They are like chaff that the wind blows away.

**5** Thus the wicked will not stand firm on the day of judgment. Sinners will not stand in the assembly of the righteous.

**6** The LORD knows and protects the way of the righteous. But the way of the wicked will lead to destruction.

## Chapter 2

**1** Why do the nations become angry? Why do the peoples make useless plans?

**2** The kings of the earth prepare for war. The rulers make plans together against the LORD and against his anointed king. They say,

**3** "We must break their chains. We must throw off their ropes."

**4** God sits on his throne in heaven and laughs. The Lord laughs at them with contempt.

**5** Then he speaks to them in his anger. He frightens them in his great anger.

**6** He says, "I put my king on Zion, my holy hill."

**7** I will tell about the decree of the LORD. The LORD said to me, "You are my Son. Today I became your father.

**8** Ask me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance. I will give you the farthest parts of the earth as your property.

**9** You will break them with an iron rod. You will break them into pieces like a clay pot."

**10** Thus, you kings, be wise. Learn from this, you rulers of the earth.

**11** Serve the LORD with fear. Be glad, but shake with fear.

**12** Kiss the Son. If you do not, he will become angry, and you will die on your way. His anger can start quickly. All people who trust in him are blessed.

## Chapter 3

**1** LORD, I have very many enemies! Many people attack me.

**2** Many people say about me, "God will not save him." Selah.

**3** But you, LORD, are a shield around me. You give me honor. You give me courage again.

**4** I cry out to the LORD with my voice. He answers me from his holy hill. Selah.

**5** I lie down and sleep. I wake up again, because the LORD keeps me safe.

**6** I will not be afraid of 10,000 people who attack me from all sides.

**7** Stand up, LORD! Save me, my God! You hit all my enemies on the face. You break the teeth of the wicked.

**8** Salvation comes from the LORD. Bless your people. Selah.

## Chapter 4

**1** Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness. You gave me relief when I was in trouble. Be kind to me and hear my prayer.

**2** You men, how long will you bring shame on my honor? How long will you love empty things and look for lies? Selah.

**3** But know that the LORD chose the godly man for himself. The LORD will hear me when I call to him.

**4** Shake with fear and do not sin. Think deeply in your heart on your bed, and be quiet. Selah.

**5** Give the correct sacrifices. Put your trust in the LORD.

**6** Many people say, "Who will show us good things?" LORD, let the light of your face shine on us.

**7** You put more joy in my heart than people have when they have much grain and new wine.

**8** I will lie down and sleep in peace. Only you, LORD, keep me safe.

## Chapter 5

**1** Hear my words, LORD. Think about my sad thoughts.

**2** Listen to my cry for help, my King and my God. I pray to you.

**3** LORD, you will hear my voice in the morning. In the morning, I will put my requests in front of you, and I will wait.

**4** You are not a God who likes evil. Evil people cannot live with you.

**5** Proud people will not stand in front of you. You hate all people who do evil.

**6** You destroy people who tell lies. The LORD hates people who are violent and dishonest.

**7** But because of your great love, I will come into your house. With respect, I will bow down toward your holy temple.

**8** Lead me, LORD, in your righteousness, because I have enemies. Make your path straight in front of me.

**9** My enemies do not say anything true. Their hearts are full of destruction. Their throat is like an open grave. They use their tongues to lie with false praise.

**10** God, show that they are guilty. Let their own plans cause them to fall. Throw them out because of their many sins. They rebelled against you.

**11** But let all people who trust in you be glad. Let them always sing with joy, because you protect them. Let people who love your name be happy in you.

**12** LORD, you bless the righteous. You cover them with your kindness as with a shield.

## Chapter 6

**1** LORD, do not correct me in your anger. Do not punish me in your great anger.

**2** Be kind to me, LORD, because I am weak. Heal me, LORD, because my bones shake.

**3** My soul also has much trouble. LORD, how long will this continue?

**4** Come back, LORD, and save my life. Save me because of your faithful love.

**5** Dead people do not remember you. In the grave, no person thanks you.

**6** I am weak because I cry with pain. All night my bed is wet with my tears. I make my bed wet when I cry.

**7** My eyes become weak because of sorrow. They become weak because of all my enemies.

**8** Go away from me, all you people who do evil! The LORD hears the sound when I cry.

**9** The LORD hears my request for help. The LORD accepts my prayer.

**10** All my enemies will have shame and much trouble. They will turn back with sudden shame.

## Chapter 7

**1** LORD my God, I go to you for protection. Save me from all the people who chase me. Rescue me.

**2** If you do not, they will tear me apart like a lion. They will tear me into pieces, and no person will save me.

**3** LORD my God, maybe I did this wrong thing. Maybe my hands did evil.

**4** Maybe I did evil to my friend. Maybe I robbed my enemy without a reason.

**5** If so, let my enemy chase me and catch me. Let him crush my life into the ground. Let him put my honor in the dust. Selah.

**6** Stand up in your anger, LORD! Fight against the anger of my enemies. Wake up, my God, and give the justice that you command.

**7** Let the people of the nations come around you. Rule over them from your high throne.

**8** The LORD judges the peoples. Judge me, LORD, because I am righteous and innocent.

**9** Stop the evil of the wicked. Make the righteous safe. You are a righteous God. You examine the minds and hearts of people.

**10** God is my shield. He saves the people who have honest hearts.

**11** God is a righteous judge. Every day, God is angry with the wicked.

**12** If a person does not change, then God will make his sword sharp. God bends his bow and prepares it.

**13** God prepares his deadly weapons. He makes his arrows into arrows of fire.

**14** Look, the wicked man plans evil. He thinks of trouble and causes lies.

**15** He digs a pit to trap other people. But he falls into the pit that he made.

**16** The trouble that he causes comes back on him. His violence falls on his own head.

**17** I will thank the LORD because he is righteous. I will sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.

## Chapter 8

**1** LORD, our Lord, your name is very great in all the earth! You put your glory above the sky.

**2** You cause small children and babies to praise your strength. You do this because of your enemies. Thus you stop the enemy and the person who wants revenge.

**3** I look at the sky, which you made with your fingers. I see the moon and the stars, which you put in their places.

**4** Then I ask, "What is man, that you think about him? What is a human, that you take care of him?"

**5** You made man a little lower than the angels. You gave him glory and honor like a crown.

**6** You made man the ruler over all the things that you made. You put all things under his control.

**7** You put all the sheep and the oxen under his control. You also put the wild animals under him.

**8** You put the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea under him. You put all things that swim in the sea under him.

**9** LORD, our Lord, your name is very great in all the earth!

## Chapter 9

**1** I will thank you, LORD, with all my heart. I will tell about all your wonderful works.

**2** I will be happy and glad in you. I will sing praise to your name, Most High God.

**3** My enemies turn back. They fall and die in front of you.

**4** You gave me justice and supported my case. You sit on your throne as a righteous judge.

**5** You punished the nations. You destroyed the wicked. You removed their names for all time.

**6** The enemy is completely destroyed for all time. You destroyed their cities. No person remembers them.

**7** But the LORD rules for all time. He prepares his throne for judgment.

**8** He judges the world in righteousness. He judges the peoples with honesty.

**9** The LORD is a safe place for people who suffer. He is a safe place in times of trouble.

**10** People who know your name trust in you. LORD, you do not leave the people who look for you.

**11** Sing praises to the LORD, who lives in Zion. Tell the nations what he did.

**12** God punishes murderers, and he remembers their victims. He does not forget the cry of the people who suffer.

**13** Be kind to me, LORD. See how my enemies cause me to suffer. You can lift me up from the gates of death.

**14** Then I will praise you at the gates of Zion. I will be glad because you save me.

**15** The nations fell into the pit that they dug. The net that they hid catches their feet.

**16** The LORD shows who he is by his justice. The work of the wicked traps them. Higgaion. Selah.

**17** The wicked will go to the place of the dead (Sheol). All the nations that forget God will go there.

**18** God will not always forget the people in need. The hope of the poor will not go away for all time.

**19** Stand up, LORD! Do not let man win. Judge the nations in front of you.

**20** Make the nations afraid, LORD. Let them know that they are only men. Selah.

## Chapter 10

**1** LORD, why do you stand far away? Why do you hide in times of trouble?

**2** In his pride, the wicked man chases the poor. Let the plans that the wicked make catch them.

**3** The wicked man boasts about the things that his heart wants. He blesses greedy people, but the LORD hates them.

**4** In his pride, the wicked man does not look for God. In all his thoughts, he says, "There is no God."

**5** His ways are always successful. Your laws are too high for him to see. He laughs at all his enemies.

**6** He says in his heart, "Nothing will move me. I will never have trouble."

**7** His mouth is full of curses, lies and threats. His tongue speaks trouble and evil.
