**10** Then a woman came out to meet him. She wore clothes like a prostitute, and she had a dishonest plan.

**11** She is loud and she does not obey. She does not stay at home.

**12** Sometimes she is in the street and sometimes in the market. She waits at every corner.

**13** She took hold of the young man and kissed him. With a bold face she said to him,

**14** "I made peace offerings today. I did the things that I promised to God.

**15** So I came out to meet you. I looked for you, and I found you.

**16** I put beautiful covers on my bed. I put colored linen from Egypt on it.

**17** I put perfume on my bed. I used myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.

**18** Come, we will make love until the morning. We will enjoy our love.

**19** My husband is not at home. He went on a long journey.

**20** He took a bag of money with him. He will not come home until the full moon."

**21** She used her many sweet words to persuade him. Her false words caused him to agree.

**22** He followed her immediately. He went like an ox that goes to its death. He went like a deer that goes into a trap.

**23** He went until an arrow went into his body. He went like a bird that flies quickly into a trap. He did not know that the trap will kill him.

**24** Now, children, listen to me. Pay attention to my words.

**25** Do not let your heart turn to her ways. Do not go on her paths.

**26** She caused many men to fall. She killed many strong men.

**27** Her house is the road to the grave. It goes down to the rooms of death.

## Chapter 8

**1** Wisdom calls out. Understanding raises her voice.

**2** She stands on the high places beside the road. She stands where the paths meet.

**3** She calls out at the gates at the entrance to the city. She calls at the doors.

**4** She says, "People, I call to you. I speak to all humans.

**5** Simple people, learn to be careful. Fools, learn to have good sense.

**6** Listen, because I will tell you very good things. My lips will say what is right.

**7** My mouth speaks the truth. My lips hate wicked words.

**8** All my words are honest. None of my words are dishonest or false.

**9** All my words are clear to the people who understand. They are correct to the people who have knowledge.

**10** Accept my instruction instead of silver. Accept knowledge instead of the best gold.

**11** Wisdom is better than rubies. Nothing that you want is equal to her.

**12** I, Wisdom, live with good sense. I have knowledge and good judgment.

**13** The fear of the LORD is to hate evil. I hate pride and arrogance. I hate the evil way and dishonest words.

**14** I give advice and good wisdom. I have good sense and strength.

**15** Kings rule with my help. Rulers make fair laws with my help.

**16** Princes rule with my help. All nobles and judges of the earth rule with my help.

**17** I love the people who love me. The people who look for me will find me.

**18** I have wealth and honor. I give wealth that lasts, and I give justice.

**19** My gifts are better than gold, even the best gold. What I give is better than the best silver.

**20** I walk in the way of what is right. I walk on the paths of justice.

**21** I give wealth to the people who love me. I fill their storehouses.

**22** The LORD made me at the start of his work. He made me before his first acts.

**23** He put me in my place a very long time ago. He made me at the start, before he made the earth.

**24** He made me before there were oceans. He made me before there were springs full of water.

**25** He made me before he put the mountains in their places. He made me before the hills.

**26** He made me before he made the earth and the fields. He made me before he made the first dust of the world.

**27** I was there when he put the heavens in their place. I was there when he drew the horizon on the surface of the ocean.

**28** I was there when he put the clouds in the sky. I was there when he made the springs of the ocean strong.

**29** I was there when he gave the sea its limits, so that the waters obey his command. I was there when he marked the foundations of the earth.

**30** I was near him like a skilled worker. I gave him pleasure every day. I was always happy in front of him.

**31** I was happy with the whole world that he made. I enjoyed the human race.

**32** Now, children, listen to me. The people who obey my ways are happy.

**33** Listen to my instruction and be wise. Do not refuse my instruction.

**34** The person who listens to me is happy. He watches at my gates every day. He waits at my doors.

**35** The person who finds me finds life. The LORD will be kind to him.

**36** But the person who does not find me hurts himself. All the people who hate me love death."

## Chapter 9

**1** Wisdom built her house. She cut her 7 columns.

**2** She killed animals for a meal. She mixed her wine. She made her table ready.

**3** She sent out her female servants to invite people. She calls from the highest places in the city.

**4** She says, "Simple people, come in here." She says to people who have no sense,

**5** "Come, eat my food. Drink the wine that I mixed.

**6** Stop your foolish ways, and live. Walk in the way of good sense."

**7** If you correct a mocker, he will insult you. If you correct a wicked man, he will hurt you.

**8** Do not correct a mocker, because he will hate you. Correct a wise man, and he will love you.

**9** Teach a wise man, and he will become wiser. Teach a good man, and he will learn more.

**10** Fear of the LORD is the start of wisdom. Knowledge of the Holy One gives good sense.

**11** Wisdom will give you more days. She will add years to your life.

**12** If you are wise, your wisdom will help you. If you mock, you alone will suffer.

**13** The foolish woman is loud. She has no sense, and she knows nothing.

**14** She sits at the door of her house. She sits on a seat in the high places of the city.

**15** She calls to the people who go past. She calls to the people who walk straight on their way.

**16** She says, "Simple people, come in here." She says to people who have no sense,

**17** "Stolen water is sweet. Food that you eat in secret gives much pleasure."

**18** But the simple man does not know that the dead are in her house. Her guests are in the deepest part of the grave.

## Chapter 10

**1** These are the proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes his father happy. But a foolish son makes his mother sad.

**2** Wealth that a person gets by wicked acts has no value. But good acts save a person from death.

**3** The LORD does not let good people become hungry. But he takes away the things that wicked people want.

**4** Lazy hands make a man poor. But hard work makes a man rich.

**5** A son who collects the crops in summer is wise. But a son who sleeps at the harvest causes shame.

**6** Blessings come to good people. But the words of wicked people hide violence.

**7** People remember good people with blessings. But people will soon forget wicked people.

**8** A wise person accepts commands. But a fool who talks too much will fall.

**9** The honest person lives safely. But people will discover the dishonest person.

**10** The person who winks to deceive causes trouble. A fool who talks too much will fall.

**11** The words of a good man are like a spring of life. But the words of wicked people hide violence.

**12** Hate causes arguments. But love forgives all wrongs.

**13** People find wisdom in the words of a person with good sense. But a person with no sense will get punishment with a stick.

**14** Wise people collect knowledge. But the words of a fool bring destruction near.

**15** The wealth of a rich man protects him like a strong city. Poverty destroys poor people.

**16** The pay of good people brings life. The pay of wicked people brings sin.

**17** The person who accepts correction is on the path to life. But the person who refuses correction goes the wrong way.

**18** The person who hides hate with lies is a fool. The person who tells false stories is a fool.

**19** When you speak too many words, sin comes easily. But the person who controls his words is wise.

**20** The words of a good person are like the best silver. But the thoughts of a wicked person have little value.

**21** The words of good people help many people. But fools die because they have no sense.

**22** The blessing of the LORD makes a person rich. And the LORD adds no sadness to it.

**23** A fool enjoys evil acts. But a man with good sense enjoys wisdom.

**24** The thing that a wicked person fears will come to him. But good people will get what they want.

**25** When the storm goes past, wicked people are gone. But good people stand firm for all time.

**26** Vinegar hurts the teeth and smoke hurts the eyes. A lazy person is the same to the people who send him.

**27** Fear of the LORD gives a long life. But the years of wicked people will be short.

**28** The hope of good people will bring joy. But the hope of wicked people will come to nothing.

**29** The way of the LORD protects honest people. But it destroys the people who do evil.

**30** Good people will always be safe. But wicked people will not stay in the land.

**31** The mouth of a good person speaks wisdom. But God will stop the tongue that tells lies.

**32** Good people know the correct words to say. But wicked people say dishonest things.

## Chapter 11

**1** The LORD hates false scales. But correct weights give him pleasure.

**2** When pride comes, shame also comes. But wisdom is with humble people.

**3** Honesty leads honest people. But dishonesty destroys wicked people.

**4** Wealth will not help on the day of God's anger. But good acts save a person from death.

**5** Good acts make the path of honest people straight. But wicked people fall because of their wicked acts.

**6** Good acts save honest people. But the desires of wicked people catch them.

**7** When a wicked man dies, his hope stops. All that he expected from his wealth comes to nothing.

**8** God saves good people from trouble. Then the trouble comes on wicked people instead.

**9** A person who does not love God destroys his neighbor with his words. But knowledge saves good people.

**10** When good people succeed, the city is happy. When wicked people die, the people shout with joy.

**11** The blessing of honest people makes a city great. But the words of wicked people destroy a city.

**12** A person with no sense insults his neighbor. But a person with good sense stays quiet.

**13** A gossip tells secrets. But a faithful person keeps a secret.

**14** A nation with no good leaders will fall. But many advisers make a nation safe.

**15** If you promise to pay the debt of a stranger, you will suffer. If you refuse to make such promises, you will be safe.

**16** A kind woman gets honor. Strong men get only wealth.

**17** A kind man helps himself. But a cruel man hurts himself.

**18** A wicked man gets pay that has no value. But a person who does good gets a true reward.

**19** A person who does good things will live. But a person who follows evil goes to his death.

**20** The LORD hates people with dishonest hearts. But people who live honestly give him pleasure.

**21** Be sure of this: wicked people will get punishment. But the children of good people will be safe.

**22** A beautiful woman without good sense is like a gold ring in the nose of a pig.

**23** The desire of good people brings only good things. But the hope of wicked people brings anger.

**24** One person gives freely, but he gets more. Another person keeps too much, but he becomes poor.

**25** A person who gives generously will have more. A person who helps others will get help.

**26** People curse the man who keeps his grain for a higher price. But they bless the man who sells his grain.

**27** The person who looks for good will get kindness. But evil will come to the person who looks for evil.

**28** The person who trusts in his wealth will fall. But good people will grow like green leaves.

**29** The person who causes trouble for his family will get nothing. The fool will become the servant of the wise person.

**30** The work of good people is like a tree that gives life. A wise person brings people to life.

**31** Good people get their reward on earth. Thus, wicked people and sinners will surely get their punishment.

## Chapter 12

**1** The person who loves correction loves knowledge. But the person who hates correction is stupid.

**2** The LORD is kind to a good man. But the LORD condemns a man who makes evil plans.

**3** Wicked acts do not make a person safe. But good people stand firm like a tree with deep roots.

**4** A good wife is like a crown to her husband. But a wife who causes shame is like a disease in his bones.

**5** The plans of good people are fair. But the advice of wicked people is false.

**6** The words of wicked people are like a trap that kills. But the words of honest people save them.

**7** Wicked people fall and are gone. But the families of good people will continue.

**8** People praise a man for his wisdom. But people hate a man with a dishonest mind.

**9** It is better to be a common man who has a servant. It is worse to act important and have no food.

**10** A good man takes care of his animals. But even the kindest acts of wicked people are cruel.

**11** The man who works his land will have much food. But the man who follows foolish plans has no sense.

**12** Wicked people want the things that evil men steal. But good people are like a tree with deep roots that gives fruit.

**13** The wicked person's sinful words trap him. But a good person escapes from trouble.

**14** Good words bring good things to a man. The work of a man's hands brings him reward.

**15** A fool thinks that his own way is correct. But a wise man listens to advice.

**16** A fool shows his anger immediately. But a wise man ignores an insult.

**17** An honest witness tells the truth. But a false witness tells lies.

**18** Some people speak careless words that cut like a sword. But the words of wise people heal.

**19** True words will last for all time. But lies last only for a short time.

**20** People who plan evil have dishonest hearts. But people who make peace have joy.

**21** No harm will come to good people. But wicked people will have much trouble.

**22** The LORD hates lies. But honest people give him pleasure.

**23** A wise man does not show all that he knows. But a fool shows his foolishness to all people.

**24** People who work hard will become rulers. But lazy people will become slaves.

**25** Worry makes a person sad. But a kind word makes him happy.

**26** A good person gives good advice to his friend. But the way of wicked people causes them to go the wrong way.

**27** A lazy man does not cook the animal that he caught. But a man who works hard keeps his wealth.

**28** The path of good acts leads to life. On that path there is no death.

## Chapter 13

**1** A wise son listens to the instruction of his father. But a mocker does not listen to correction.

**2** A good man gets good things from his words. But dishonest people want violence.

**3** The person who controls his words protects his life. But the person who speaks carelessly will come to ruin.

**4** A lazy person wants things, but he gets nothing. A person who works hard gets all that he needs.

**5** A good man hates lies. But a wicked man causes shame and disgrace.

**6** Good acts protect an honest person. But wicked acts destroy a sinner.

**7** One person acts rich, but he has nothing. Another person acts poor, but he has much wealth.

**8** A rich man must use his wealth to save his life. But a poor man does not hear threats.

**9** The life of good people is like a bright light. But the life of wicked people is like a lamp that goes out.

**10** Pride causes only arguments. But people who accept advice are wise.

**11** Money that comes easily will disappear. But money that comes from hard work will increase.

**12** When hope comes late, the heart becomes sick. But when a desire comes true, it is like a tree of life.

**13** The person who hates the word of God will come to ruin. But the person who respects the command will get a reward.

**14** The law of wise people is like a spring of life. It keeps a person away from the traps of death.

**15** Good sense makes people like you. But the way of dishonest people is hard.

**16** A wise person thinks before he acts. But a fool shows his foolishness.

**17** A wicked messenger causes trouble. But a faithful messenger brings health.

**18** The person who refuses correction will become poor and have shame. But the person who accepts correction will get honor.

**19** When a desire comes true, it is sweet to the soul. But fools hate to turn away from evil.

**20** If you walk with wise people, you will become wise. If you are a friend of fools, you will suffer harm.

**21** Trouble follows sinners. But good things come to good people.

**22** A good man leaves wealth to his grandchildren. But the wealth of a sinner will go to good people.

**23** The field of a poor man can give much food. But injustice takes it away.

**24** A father who does not punish his son hates his son. But a father who loves his son corrects him carefully.

**25** A good person has enough food to eat. But wicked people will be hungry.

## Chapter 14

**1** A wise woman builds her house. But a foolish woman destroys her house with her own hands.

**2** The person who lives honestly fears the LORD. But the person who is dishonest hates the LORD.

**3** The words of a fool bring punishment on him because of his pride. But the words of wise people protect them.

**4** If there are no oxen, the feed box is empty. But strong oxen give a large harvest.

**5** An honest witness does not lie. But a false witness tells lies.

**6** A mocker looks for wisdom, but he does not find it. But knowledge comes easily to a person with good sense.

**7** Go away from a foolish man. You will not hear knowledge from him.

**8** The wisdom of a wise man helps him to understand his way. But the foolishness of fools deceives them.

**9** Fools laugh at sin. But honest people accept one another.

**10** Each heart knows its own sadness. No other person can share its joy.

**11** God will destroy the house of wicked people. But the tent of honest people will grow strong.

**12** A way can look correct to a man. But at the end, that way leads to death.

**13** Even when a person laughs, his heart can be sad. Joy can end in sadness.

**14** A faithless person will get the result of his ways. A good man will get the reward of his good acts.

**15** A simple person believes every word. But a wise person thinks carefully about his steps.

**16** A wise man is careful and stays away from evil. But a fool is angry and too sure of himself.

**17** A person who gets angry quickly does foolish things. People hate a man who makes evil plans.

**18** Simple people get foolishness as their reward. But wise people get knowledge as their crown.

**19** Evil people will bow down in front of good people. Wicked people will bow at the gates of good people.

**20** Even his neighbors do not like a poor man. But a rich man has many friends.

**21** The person who hates his neighbor sins. But the person who is kind to poor people is happy.

**22** People who plan evil go the wrong way. But people who plan good get love and faithfulness.

**23** All hard work brings a profit. But only talk brings poverty.

**24** Wise people get wealth as their crown. But the foolishness of fools brings only more foolishness.

**25** An honest witness saves lives. But a false witness tells lies.

**26** The person who fears the LORD has a strong hope. His children will have a safe place.

**27** Fear of the LORD is like a spring of life. It keeps a person away from the traps of death.

**28** A king with many people has honor. But a prince without people comes to ruin.

**29** A person who is slow to get angry has much wisdom. But a person who gets angry quickly shows foolishness.

**30** A calm heart gives life to the body. But envy is like a disease in the bones.

**31** The person who is cruel to poor people insults their Maker. But the person who is kind to poor people honors God.

**32** The wicked acts of wicked people destroy them. But good people have hope even at death.

**33** Wisdom stays in the heart of a person with good sense. Even fools can know wisdom.

**34** Good acts make a nation great. But sin brings shame to all people.

**35** A king is kind to a wise servant. But he is angry with a servant who causes shame.

## Chapter 15

**1** A gentle answer stops anger. But harsh words cause anger.

**2** Wise people use knowledge correctly. But fools speak foolishness.

**3** The eyes of the LORD are in every place. He watches evil people and good people.

**4** Kind words are like a tree of life. But dishonest words hurt the spirit.

**5** A fool hates the correction of his father. But the person who accepts correction is wise.

**6** Good people have much wealth in their houses. But the profit of wicked people brings trouble.

**7** Wise people tell others about knowledge. But fools do not do this.

**8** The LORD hates the sacrifice of wicked people. But the prayer of honest people gives him pleasure.

**9** The LORD hates the way of wicked people. But he loves the people who try to do good.

**10** The person who leaves the correct way will get hard punishment. The person who hates correction will die.

**11** The LORD sees the place of the dead and destruction. Thus he surely sees the hearts of humans.

**12** A mocker does not like the person who corrects him. He will not go to wise people.

**13** A happy heart makes a happy face. But a sad heart breaks the spirit.

**14** A person with good sense looks for knowledge. But fools feed on foolishness.

**15** All the days of a person in trouble are bad. But a happy heart is like a continuous feast.

**16** It is better to have a little and fear the LORD. It is worse to have much wealth with trouble.

**17** It is better to eat vegetables with love. It is worse to eat the best meat with hate.

**18** An angry man causes arguments. But a person who is slow to get angry stops arguments.

**19** The way of a lazy man is like a hedge of thorns. But the path of honest people is level.

**20** A wise son makes his father happy. But a foolish man hates his mother.

**21** Foolishness gives joy to a person with no sense. But a man with good sense goes straight ahead.

**22** Plans fail when there is no advice. But plans succeed when there are many advisers.

**23** A good answer gives a man joy. A word at the correct time is very good.

**24** The path of life goes up for the wise man. It keeps him away from the grave below.

**25** The LORD destroys the house of proud people. But he protects the land of a widow.

**26** The LORD hates the thoughts of wicked people. But kind words give him pleasure.

**27** A greedy person causes trouble for his family. But the person who refuses bribes will live.

**28** A good person thinks before he answers. But a wicked person speaks evil things.

**29** The LORD is far from wicked people. But he hears the prayer of good people.

**30** A happy face makes the heart happy. Good news makes the body healthy.

**31** The person who listens to correction that gives life will live among wise people.

**32** The person who refuses correction hurts himself. But the person who listens to correction gets good sense.

**33** Fear of the LORD teaches wisdom. Humility comes before honor.

## Chapter 16

**1** A man can make plans in his heart. But the LORD gives the correct words to speak.

**2** A man thinks that all his ways are pure. But the LORD examines the motives.

**3** Give all your work to the LORD. Then your plans will succeed.

**4** The LORD made all things for his purpose. He made even the wicked person for the day of punishment.

**5** The LORD hates all proud people. Be sure of this: they will get punishment.

**6** Love and faithfulness remove sin. Fear of the LORD keeps people away from evil.

**7** When the ways of a man give pleasure to the LORD, the LORD makes even his enemies peaceful with him.

**8** It is better to have a little and be honest. It is worse to have much money and be dishonest.

**9** A man plans his way in his heart. But the LORD controls his steps.

**10** A king speaks as if God gives him the words. He must not make an unfair judgment.

**11** Honest scales and balances come from the LORD. He made all the weights in the bag.

**12** Kings hate wicked acts, because good acts make a throne strong.

**13** Kings like honest words. They love the person who speaks the truth.

**14** The anger of a king can bring death. But a wise man will make the king calm.

**15** When the king is happy, there is life. His kindness is like a cloud that brings rain in spring.

**16** It is much better to get wisdom than gold. It is much better to get good sense than silver.

**17** The road of honest people goes away from evil. The person who watches his way protects his life.

**18** Pride comes before destruction. A proud spirit comes before a fall.

**19** It is better to be humble with poor people. It is worse to share stolen goods with proud people.

**20** The person who pays attention to good advice will succeed. The person who trusts in the LORD is happy.

**21** People call a wise person intelligent. Kind words help people to learn.

**22** Understanding is like a spring of life to the person who has it. But fools get punishment for their foolishness.

**23** The heart of a wise man controls his mouth. His words help people to learn.

**24** Kind words are like honey. They are sweet to the soul and healthy for the body.

**25** A way can look correct to a man. But at the end, that way leads to death.

**26** The hunger of a worker makes him work. His hunger pushes him.

**27** A wicked man makes evil plans. His words are like a hot fire.

**28** A dishonest man causes arguments. A gossip separates close friends.

**29** A violent man persuades his neighbor to do wrong. He leads his neighbor on a bad path.

**30** A person who winks plans dishonest things. A person who closes his lips tightly causes evil.

**31** Gray hair is a crown of glory. A person gets gray hair if he lives a good life.

**32** A patient person is better than a strong soldier. A person who controls his anger is better than a person who captures a city.

**33** People throw lots to make a decision. But the LORD makes each decision.

## Chapter 17

**1** It is better to eat a dry piece of bread in peace. It is worse to have a house full of food and arguments.

**2** A wise servant will rule a son who causes shame. The servant will get a part of the family's property.

**3** A pot makes silver pure, and a fire makes gold pure. But the LORD tests the heart.

**4** An evil person listens to evil words. A liar listens to cruel words.

**5** The person who mocks poor people insults their Maker. The person who is happy about the trouble of others will get punishment.

**6** Grandchildren are the crown of old people. Parents are the pride of their children.

**7** Good words do not suit a fool. Lies suit a ruler even less.

**8** A bribe is like a magic stone to the person who gives it. He thinks that it will help him wherever he goes.

**9** The person who forgives a wrong makes love grow. But the person who talks about the wrong separates close friends.

**10** One correction teaches a wise man more than 100 hits teach a fool.

**11** An evil man wants only to fight against authority. Thus a cruel messenger will go against him.

**12** It is better to meet a mother bear that lost her cubs. It is worse to meet a fool in his foolishness.

**13** If a person pays back good with evil, evil will not leave his house.

**14** The start of an argument is like a hole in a dam. Thus stop the argument before it starts.

**15** The LORD hates the person who says that the guilty are innocent. He hates the person who condemns innocent people.

**16** A fool can have money to buy wisdom. But he does not want to learn, so the money has no use.

**17** A friend loves at all times. A brother comes into the world to help in times of trouble.

**18** A man with no sense promises to pay the debt of his neighbor. He makes an agreement for his neighbor.

**19** The person who loves arguments loves sin. The person who builds a high gate asks for destruction.

**20** A person with a dishonest heart does not succeed. A person who tells lies falls into trouble.

**21** A man whose son is a fool has sadness. The father of a fool has no joy.

**22** A happy heart is good medicine. But a sad spirit makes the body dry.

**23** A wicked man takes a bribe in secret. He uses it to make judgment unfair.

**24** A person with good sense keeps wisdom in front of him. But the eyes of a fool look to the ends of the earth.

**25** A foolish son makes his father sad. He makes his mother bitter.

**26** It is not good to punish innocent people. It is not correct to hit honest leaders.

**27** A person with knowledge uses few words. A person with good sense stays calm.

**28** Even a fool seems wise when he is quiet. When he closes his lips, people think that he has good sense.

## Chapter 18

**1** A person who stays away from others follows only his own desires. He argues against all good advice.

**2** A fool does not enjoy good sense. He only wants to tell his own opinions.

**3** When a wicked person comes, hate also comes. Shame comes with disgrace.

**4** The words of a man can be like deep waters. Wisdom is like a stream that flows.

**5** It is not good to favor wicked people. It is not good to refuse justice to innocent people.

**6** The words of a fool cause arguments. His mouth asks for blows.

**7** The words of a fool destroy him. His lips are a trap for his soul.

**8** The words of a gossip are like tasty food. They go deep into the body.

**9** A lazy worker is like a brother to a person who destroys things.

**10** The name of the LORD is a strong tower. Good people run into it and are safe.

**11** The wealth of a rich man is like a strong city to him. He thinks that his wealth is a high wall around him.

**12** Before destruction, the heart of a man is proud. But humility comes before honor.

**13** If a person answers before he listens, he is foolish and he has shame.

**14** The spirit of a man can help him in sickness. But no person can live with a broken spirit.

**15** The heart of a wise person gets knowledge. The ear of a wise person looks for knowledge.

**16** A gift opens the way for the person who gives it. It brings him to important people.

**17** The first person who tells his case seems correct. Then another person comes and asks him questions.

**18** Lots stop arguments. They make the decision between strong opponents.

**19** It is harder to make peace with an angry brother than to capture a strong city. Arguments are like the locked gates of a fort.

**20** The words of a man bring him results. He will get the results of what he says.

**21** The tongue has the power of life and death. The people who like to talk will get the results of their words.

**22** The man who finds a wife finds a good thing. The LORD is kind to him.

**23** A poor man asks for help politely. But a rich man answers harshly.

**24** Some friends cause harm to a person. But there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.

## Chapter 19

**1** It is better to be poor and honest. It is worse to be a fool who tells lies.

**2** It is not good to have desire without knowledge. A person who acts too quickly makes mistakes.

**3** The foolishness of a man destroys his life. Then he is angry with the LORD.

**4** Wealth brings many friends. But the friends of a poor man leave him.

**5** A false witness will get punishment. A person who tells lies will not escape.

**6** Many people try to please a ruler. Every person is a friend to a man who gives gifts.

**7** All the brothers of a poor man hate him. His friends go far away from him. He calls after them, but they are gone.

**8** The person who gets wisdom loves himself. The person who keeps good sense will succeed.

**9** A false witness will get punishment. A person who tells lies will die.

**10** It is not correct for a fool to live in luxury. It is much worse for a slave to rule princes.

**11** A wise man is slow to get angry. It is his honor to forgive a wrong.

**12** The anger of a king is like the roar of a lion. But his kindness is like dew on the grass.

**13** A foolish son causes disaster for his father. A wife who argues is like water that drips continuously.

**14** A man gets a house and wealth from his parents. But a wise wife comes from the LORD.

**15** Laziness causes deep sleep. A lazy person will be hungry.

**16** The person who obeys the commands protects his life. But the person who does not care about his ways will die.

**17** The person who is kind to poor people lends to the LORD. The LORD will pay him back for his kindness.

**18** Correct your son while there is hope. Do not cause his death.

**19** An angry man must pay the penalty. If you save him, you must do it again.

**20** Listen to advice and accept correction. Then you will be wise at the end of your life.

**21** A man can make many plans. But the plan of the LORD will succeed.

**22** People want a person who is loyal. It is better to be poor than to be a liar.

**23** Fear of the LORD leads to life. The person who fears the LORD will have all that he needs, and evil will not hurt him.

**24** A lazy man puts his hand in the dish. But he does not even lift the food to his mouth.

**25** Punish a mocker, and simple people will learn to be careful. Correct a wise person, and he will get more knowledge.

**26** A son who robs his father and sends away his mother causes shame and disgrace.

**27** My son, if you stop and do not listen to correction, you will turn away from the words of knowledge.

**28** A wicked witness mocks justice. Wicked people enjoy evil as if it is food.

**29** Punishment is ready for mockers. Beatings are ready for the backs of fools.

## Chapter 20

**1** Wine makes people mock. Strong drink makes people fight. A person who lets alcohol control him is not wise.

**2** The anger of a king is like the roar of a lion. The person who makes the king angry puts his own life in danger.

**3** It is an honor for a man to stay away from arguments. But every fool starts arguments.

**4** A lazy person does not plow in the cold season. Thus at the harvest he looks for food and finds nothing.

**5** The plans in the heart of a man are like deep water. But a man with good sense can find them.

**6** Many men say that they are loyal. But it is hard to find a faithful man.

**7** A good man lives an honest life. His children after him are happy.

**8** When a king sits on his throne to judge, he sees all evil and sends it away.

**9** No person can say, "My heart is pure. I am clean from my sin."

**10** The LORD hates false weights and false measures.

**11** Even a child shows what he is by his acts. People can see if his acts are pure and correct.

**12** The LORD made ears to hear and eyes to see.

**13** Do not love sleep, or you will become poor. Stay awake, and you will have much food.

**14** The buyer says, "This is bad. This is bad." But when he goes away, he boasts about his good purchase.

**15** There is gold and there are many rubies. But words of knowledge are more valuable than jewels.

**16** If a man promises to pay the debt of a stranger, take his coat as security. If he does this for a foreign woman, keep his coat.

**17** Food that a person gets by lies tastes sweet. But later his mouth will be full of gravel.

**18** Get advice when you make plans. Get good advice before you go to war.

**19** A gossip tells secrets. Thus do not be a friend of a person who talks too much.

**20** If a person curses his father or his mother, his life will end in complete darkness.

**21** A person can get wealth quickly at the start. But at the end that wealth will not bring blessing.

**22** Do not say, "I will pay back evil." Wait for the LORD, and he will save you.

**23** The LORD hates false weights. False scales are not good.

**24** The LORD controls the steps of a man. Thus a man cannot understand his own way.

**25** It is dangerous to make a promise to God too quickly. Do not think about the promise only after you make it.

**26** A wise king separates wicked people from good people. He punishes the wicked people severely.

**27** The spirit of a man is like a lamp from the LORD. It examines the deepest parts of the man.

**28** Love and faithfulness protect the king. Love makes his throne strong.

**29** The strength of young men is their glory. The gray hair of old men is their honor.

**30** Hard blows remove evil. Punishment makes the inner self clean.

## Chapter 21

**1** The heart of the king is in the hand of the LORD. The LORD controls it as he controls a stream of water. He turns it in the direction that he wants.

**2** A man thinks that all his ways are correct. But the LORD examines the heart.

**3** The LORD prefers that you do what is right and fair. He prefers this to sacrifice.

**4** Proud eyes and a proud heart are sin. All that wicked people do is sin.

**5** The plans of hard workers bring profit. But all people who act too quickly become poor.

**6** Wealth that a person gets with lies disappears like a breath. It leads to death.

**7** The violence of wicked people will destroy them, because they refuse to do what is right.

**8** The way of a guilty man is dishonest. But the acts of a pure person are correct.

**9** It is better to live in a corner of the roof. It is worse to live in a large house with a wife who argues.

**10** A wicked person wants evil. He shows no kindness to his neighbor.

**11** When a mocker gets punishment, simple people become wise. When a wise person gets instruction, he gets more knowledge.

**12** God, who is good, watches the house of wicked people. He destroys the wicked people because of their evil.

**13** If a person does not listen when poor people call for help, then no person will listen when he calls.

**14** A secret gift stops anger. A secret bribe stops strong anger.

**15** When people do justice, good people are happy. But evil people are afraid.

**16** A person who goes away from the way of good sense will stay with the dead.

**17** The person who loves pleasure will become poor. The person who loves wine and oil will not be rich.

**18** The wicked person will suffer the trouble that the good person escapes. The dishonest person will suffer the trouble that the honest person escapes.

**19** It is better to live in the desert. It is worse to live with a wife who argues and gets angry.

**20** A wise person keeps valuable things and oil in his house. But a foolish man uses up all that he has.

**21** The person who tries to be good and kind will find life, goodness and honor.

**22** A wise man can attack a city of strong soldiers. He can destroy the walls that they trust.

**23** The person who controls his mouth and tongue keeps himself out of trouble.

**24** A proud and arrogant person is a mocker. He acts with great pride.

**25** The desires of a lazy person kill him, because his hands refuse to work.

**26** All day the lazy person wants more. But a good person gives freely and does not keep back.

**27** The LORD hates the sacrifice of wicked people. He hates it more when they give it with evil motives.

**28** A false witness will die. But the words of a man who listens carefully will last.

**29** A wicked man acts boldly. But an honest person thinks carefully about his way.

**30** No wisdom, no insight and no plan can succeed against the LORD.

**31** People make horses ready for the day of battle. But the LORD gives the victory.

## Chapter 22

**1** Choose a good name instead of much wealth. Choose the respect of people instead of silver and gold.

**2** Rich people and poor people are the same in one thing. The LORD made all of them.

**3** A wise man sees danger and hides. But simple people go on and suffer for it.

**4** Humility and fear of the LORD bring wealth, honor and life.

**5** Thorns and traps are on the path of dishonest people. The person who protects his life stays far from them.

**6** Teach a child the correct way to live. When he is old, he will not turn away from it.

**7** Rich people rule poor people. The person who borrows is the servant of the person who lends.

**8** The person who does injustice will get trouble. His power to hurt others will end.

**9** A generous person will get blessings, because he shares his food with poor people.

**10** Send away the mocker, and arguments will go away. Fights and insults will stop.

**11** The person who loves a pure heart and speaks kindly will have the king as his friend.

**12** The eyes of the LORD protect knowledge. But he destroys the words of dishonest people.

**13** The lazy man says, "There is a lion outside! It will kill me in the street!"

**14** The words of an adulterous woman are like a deep pit. The person with whom the LORD is angry will fall into it.

**15** Foolishness is in the heart of a child. But correction will send it far from him.

**16** A person who is cruel to poor people to get more wealth will become poor. A person who gives gifts to rich people will become poor.

**17** Listen carefully to the words of wise people. Use your mind to learn what I teach.

**18** It is good to keep these words in your heart. Have all of them ready to speak.

**19** I teach you these words today so that you will trust in the LORD.

**20** I wrote 30 good sayings for you. These sayings give advice and knowledge.

**21** They teach you true and correct words. Then you can give true answers to the people who send you.

**22** Do not rob poor people because they are poor. Do not be cruel to people in need at the court.

**23** The LORD will defend them. He will take the lives of the people who rob them.

**24** Do not be a friend of an angry man. Do not go with a man who gets angry quickly.

**25** If you do, you will learn his ways. Then you will be in a trap.

**26** Do not make promises to pay the debts of other people.

**27** If you cannot pay, then the lender will take your bed from under you.

**28** Do not move the old boundary stone that your ancestors put in its place.

**29** Look at a man who has skill and works hard. He will work for kings. He will not work for unimportant people.

## Chapter 23

**1** When you sit to eat with a ruler, think carefully about what is in front of you.

**2** If you have a strong desire for food, control yourself as if a knife is at your throat.

**3** Do not want the good food of the ruler. That food can deceive you.

**4** Do not work hard only to become rich. Do not trust your own wisdom about this.

**5** Riches can go away very quickly. Riches are like a bird that flies away into the sky like an eagle.

**6** Do not eat the bread of a selfish man. Do not want his good food.

**7** The selfish man always thinks about the cost. He tells you, "Eat and drink." But he does not really want to give it to you.

**8** You will vomit the small quantity of food that you ate. You will lose your kind words to him.

**9** Do not speak to a fool. He will hate the wisdom of your words.

**10** Do not move the old boundary stone. Do not take the fields of children who have no father.

**11** The defender of these children is strong. He will speak for them against you.

**12** Give your attention to instruction. Listen to the words of knowledge.

**13** Do not stop the correction of a child. If you hit him with a stick, he will not die.

**14** Hit him with a stick, and you will save his life from death (Sheol).

**15** My son, if you become wise, then I will be very glad.

**16** I will be glad in my deepest feelings when you speak correct things.

**17** Do not be jealous of sinners. All the time, respect and fear the LORD.

**18** There is a good future for you. Your hope will not stop.

**19** My son, listen and become wise. Keep your mind on the correct road.

**20** Do not stay with people who drink too much wine. Do not stay with people who eat too much meat.

**21** People who drink too much and eat too much will become poor. Too much sleep will cause a man to wear old, torn clothes.

**22** Listen to your father, who gave you life. Do not hate your mother when she is old.

**23** Get the truth, and do not sell it. Also get wisdom, instruction and insight.

**24** The father of a righteous child will be very glad. A man who has a wise child will have joy because of that child.

**25** Let your father and your mother be glad. Let your mother, who gave birth to you, have joy.

**26** My son, give me your attention. Watch my ways and learn from them.

**27** A prostitute is like a deep hole. A wife of another man is like a narrow pit.

**28** She waits to catch men, as a robber waits. She causes many men to be unfaithful.

**29** Who has trouble? Who has sorrow? Who has arguments? Who has complaints? Who has injuries for no reason? Who has red eyes?

**30** The people who stay a long time with wine have these things. The people who look for mixed wine have these things.

**31** Do not look at the wine when it is red. Do not look at it when it shines in the cup and goes down easily.

**32** At the end, the wine bites like a snake. It hurts like a poisonous snake.

**33** Your eyes will see strange things. Your mind will think and say wrong things.

**34** You will be like a man who lies down in the middle of the sea. You will be like a man who lies at the top of the mast of a ship.

**35** You will say, "People hit me, but I did not feel pain. People beat me, but I did not know it. When will I wake up? I will look for more wine."

## Chapter 24

**1** Do not be jealous of evil men. Do not want to be with them.

**2** Evil men think about how to cause damage. Their words speak about trouble.

**3** A man builds a house with wisdom. He makes the house strong with insight.

**4** With knowledge, he fills the rooms with all types of valuable and good things.

**5** A wise man is strong. A man with knowledge increases his strength.

**6** You must have wise advice before you go to war. With many advisers, you will win.

**7** Wisdom is too high for a fool. In the assembly at the city gate, the fool does not speak.

**8** People will call a man who plans evil a troublemaker.

**9** The plans of a foolish man are sin. People hate a man who mocks others.

**10** If you become weak at the time of trouble, then your strength is small.

**11** Save the people whom others take away to death. Stop the people who go to kill them.

**12** You can say, "We did not know about it." But God examines the heart, and He knows. He keeps your life, and He knows. He will give to each person what that person's actions deserve.

**13** My son, eat honey because it is good. The honey from the comb is sweet to your taste.

**14** Wisdom is like honey for your soul. If you find wisdom, then you will have a good future. Your hope will not stop.

**15** Wicked man, do not wait to attack the house of a righteous man. Do not destroy his home.

**16** A righteous man can fall 7 times, but he gets up again. But disaster makes the wicked fall.

**17** Do not be glad when your enemy falls. Do not be happy when he trips.

**18** If you are glad, the LORD will see it and He will not be happy. Then He can stop His anger against your enemy.

**19** Do not worry because of evil men. Do not be jealous of the wicked.

**20** The evil man has no future. The life of the wicked will stop, as a lamp goes out.

**21** My son, fear the LORD and the king. Do not join with people who rebel.

**22** Disaster will come to them suddenly. Nobody knows what destruction the LORD and the king can cause.

**23** These are also words of wise people. It is not good to show special favor to some people when you judge.

**24** A man can say to a guilty person, "You are innocent." People will curse that man. Nations will hate him.

**25** But people who correct the guilty person will have good things. Good blessings will come to them.

**26** An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.

**27** First, do your work outside and make your fields ready. After that, build your house.

**28** Do not speak against your neighbor without a reason. Do not use your words to deceive.

**29** Do not say, "I will do to him what he did to me. I will pay the man back for what he did."

**30** I went past the field of a lazy man. I went past the vineyard of a man without good sense.

**31** Thorns grew everywhere on the field. Weeds covered the ground. The stone wall fell down.

**32** I looked at it and thought about it. I learned a lesson from what I saw.

**33** You sleep a little and rest a little. You fold your hands a little to sleep.

**34** Then poverty will come to you suddenly, like a robber. Need will come to you like an armed man.

## Chapter 25

**1** These are also proverbs of Solomon. The men of Hezekiah, king of Judah, copied them.

**2** God gets honor when He keeps a thing secret. Kings get honor when they examine a matter.

**3** The sky is very high and the earth is very deep. Also, nobody can know the mind of kings.

**4** Remove the waste metal from the silver. Then the metalworker can make a good container.

**5** Remove the wicked from the presence of the king. Then righteousness will make his throne strong.

**6** Do not try to look important in front of the king. Do not stand in the place of great men.

**7** It is better if the king tells you, "Come up here." That is better than if he puts you lower in front of an important person.

**8** Do not go quickly to the court to argue. At the end, your neighbor can prove you are wrong. Then what will you do?

**9** Discuss your argument with your neighbor himself. Do not tell the secret of another person.

**10** If you tell it, then the person who hears it can bring shame on you. Your bad name will not go away.

**11** A word that a person speaks at the correct time is beautiful. It is like gold apples in a silver frame.

**12** A wise correction to a person who listens is valuable. It is like a gold ring for the ear or a jewel of fine gold.

**13** A faithful messenger is like cold snow at the time of harvest. He refreshes the masters who send him.

**14** A man who boasts about a gift that he does not give is like clouds and wind without rain.

**15** With patience, a person can persuade a ruler. Gentle words can break strong opposition.

**16** If you find honey, eat only the quantity that you need. If you eat too much, you will vomit it.

**17** Do not go too often to the house of your neighbor. If you do, he will become tired of you and hate you.

**18** A man who tells lies against his neighbor in court is dangerous. He is like a club, a sword or a sharp arrow.

**19** To trust an unfaithful man at a time of trouble is bad. It is like a broken tooth or a lame foot.

**20** Do not sing happy songs to a person who is very sad. That is like when you take away a coat on a cold day. It is like when you pour vinegar on soda.

**21** If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink.

**22** Your kindness will make him ashamed, like hot coals on his head. And the LORD will reward you.

**23** The north wind brings rain. Secret talk against other people brings angry faces.

**24** It is better to live in a corner of the roof than in a large house with a woman who argues.

**25** Good news from a far country is like cold water to a thirsty person.

**26** A righteous man who gives way to the wicked is like a dirty spring or a polluted well.

**27** It is not good to eat too much honey. It is not good to look for honor for yourself.

**28** A man who cannot control himself is like a city with broken walls.

## Chapter 26

**1** Snow is not correct in summer. Rain is not correct at harvest. Also, honor is not correct for a fool.

**2** A bird that flies around does not land. Also, a curse without a reason will not come to a person.

**3** A whip is for the horse. A bridle is for the donkey. A stick is for the back of a fool.

**4** Do not answer a fool in his foolish way. If you do, you will become like him.

**5** Answer a fool as his foolishness deserves. If you do not, he will think that he is wise.

**6** A man who sends a message with a fool causes damage to himself. It is as if he cuts off his own feet.

**7** The legs of a lame man hang weak. Also, a proverb in the mouth of fools has no strength.

**8** To give honor to a fool is like tying a stone in a sling.

**9** A proverb in the mouth of fools is like a thorn in the hand of a drunk man.

**10** An employer who hires a fool or a person who passes by is like an archer who injures everyone.

**11** A dog goes back to its vomit. Also, a fool does his foolish things again.

**12** Do you see a man who thinks that he is wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

**13** The lazy man says, "There is a lion on the road. A lion is in the streets."

**14** A door turns on its hinges. Also, a lazy man turns on his bed.

**15** The lazy man puts his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring the food back to his mouth.

**16** The lazy man thinks that he is wiser than 7 men who give good answers.

**17** A man goes by and gets involved in an argument of other people. He is like a man who takes a dog by the ears.

**18** A crazy man throws sticks that burn, arrows and death.

**19** A man who deceives his neighbor and then says, "I only made a joke," is like that crazy man.

**20** Without wood, a fire goes out. Without a person who gossips, an argument stops.

**21** Coals keep a fire hot, and wood keeps a fire alive. Also, a man who argues causes more arguments.

**22** The words of a gossip are like tasty food. People take those words deep inside themselves.

**23** Kind words from an evil heart are like a cheap clay pot with a silver cover.

**24** A man who hates you hides his hate with his words. Inside, he keeps his deceit.

**25** When he speaks kindly, do not believe him. His heart is full of 7 bad things that God hates.

**26** He can hide his hate with deceit. But all the people will see his wickedness.

**27** A man who digs a pit will fall into it. A man who rolls a stone will be hurt by the stone.

**28** A person who lies hates the people whom he hurts. A person who flatters causes destruction.

## Chapter 27

**1** Do not boast about tomorrow. You do not know what will occur in one day.

**2** Let another man praise you, not your own mouth. Let a stranger praise you, not your own lips.

**3** A stone is heavy and sand is heavy. But the anger of a fool is heavier than both.

**4** Anger is cruel and rage is like a flood. But nobody can stand against jealousy.

**5** Open correction is better than hidden love.

**6** A friend can hurt you, but you can trust him. An enemy can kiss you many times, but he deceives you.

**7** A person who is full does not want honey. But a hungry person thinks that bitter food is sweet.

**8** A man who goes away from his home is like a bird that goes away from its nest.

**9** Oil and perfume make the heart glad. Also, the honest advice of a friend is sweet.

**10** Do not leave your friend or the friend of your father. When you have a disaster, do not go to the house of your brother. A neighbor who is near is better than a brother who is far away.

**11** My son, be wise and make me glad. Then I can answer the person who insults me.

**12** A careful man sees danger and hides. But a foolish man continues and he suffers.

**13** If a man promises to pay the debt of a stranger, take his coat. If he promises for a foreign woman, keep his coat as a guarantee.

**14** A man can bless his friend with a loud voice early in the morning. His friend will think that it is a curse.

**15** A wife who argues is like water that drops all the time on a rainy day.

**16** To control her is like when you try to control the wind. It is like when you try to hold oil in your hand.

**17** Iron makes iron sharp. Also, one man makes his friend better.

**18** A man who takes care of a fig tree will eat its fruit. A man who serves his master well will get honor.

**19** Water shows the reflection of a face. Also, the heart of a man shows what the man is.

**20** Death and destruction always want more. Also, the eyes of man always want more.

**21** People test silver and gold in a hot fire. People test a man by the praise that he gets.

**22** You can crush a fool with grain in a bowl. But you cannot remove his foolishness from him.

**23** Know the condition of your sheep carefully. Take good care of your cattle.

**24** Riches do not continue forever. A crown does not continue to all generations.

**25** The hay goes away and the new grass grows. People gather the plants from the mountains.

**26** The lambs will give wool for your clothes. The goats will give you the money to buy a field.

**27** You will have sufficient milk from the goats for your food. You will have food for your family and for your female servants.

## Chapter 28

**1** The wicked run away when nobody chases them. But the righteous are brave like a lion.

**2** When a country rebels, it has many rulers. But a man with insight and knowledge keeps order for a long time.

**3** A poor man who oppresses the poor is like a hard rain that destroys the crops.

**4** People who do not obey the law praise the wicked. But people who obey the law fight against the wicked.

**5** Evil men do not understand justice. But people who look for the LORD understand all things.

**6** A poor man who lives honestly is better than a rich man who lives in a dishonest way.

**7** A son who obeys the law is wise. But a son who is a friend of greedy eaters brings shame to his father.

**8** A man can get rich with high interest and dishonest profit. But his money will go to a man who is kind to the poor.

**9** If a man does not listen to the law, then God hates his prayer.

**10** A man can cause the righteous to go on an evil road. That man will fall into his own pit. But the honest will get good things.

**11** A rich man thinks that he is wise. But a poor man with insight sees the truth about him.

**12** When the righteous win, there is a great celebration. But when the wicked get power, people hide.

**13** A man who hides his sins will not have success. But a man who confesses his sins and stops them will get mercy.

**14** A man who always fears the LORD is happy. But a man who makes his heart hard will fall into trouble.

**15** A wicked ruler over poor people is like a lion that roars or a bear that attacks.

**16** A ruler without insight oppresses the people very much. But a ruler who hates greed will have a long life.

**17** A man who is guilty of murder will run until he dies. Do not help him.

**18** A man who lives honestly will be safe. But a man who lives in a dishonest way will fall suddenly.

**19** A man who works his land will have much bread. But a man who follows foolish plans will be very poor.

**20** A faithful man will get many blessings. But a man who tries to become rich quickly will get punishment.

**21** It is not good to show special favor to some people. But a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.

**22** A greedy man tries to become rich quickly. He does not know that poverty will come to him.

**23** A man who corrects another man will get more thanks at the end than a man who flatters.

**24** A man can rob his father or his mother and say, "That is not wrong." That man is like a person who destroys.

**25** A greedy man causes arguments. But a man who trusts the LORD will have many good things.

**26** A man who trusts his own mind is a fool. But a man who lives wisely will be safe.

**27** A man who gives to the poor will not need anything. But a man who does not see the poor will get many curses.

**28** When the wicked get power, people hide. But when the wicked die, the righteous increase.

## Chapter 29

**1** A man can refuse correction many times. Suddenly, destruction will come to that man. Nothing will help him.

**2** When the righteous have power, the people are glad. But when a wicked man rules, the people are sad.

**3** A man who loves wisdom makes his father glad. But a man who stays with prostitutes wastes his money.

**4** A king who gives justice makes the country strong. But a king who takes bribes destroys the country.

**5** A man who flatters his neighbor puts a trap for his feet.

**6** The sin of an evil man is a trap for him. But a righteous man sings and is glad.

**7** A righteous man knows the rights of the poor. But a wicked man does not care about the poor.

**8** Men who mock other people cause trouble in a city. But wise men stop anger.

**9** A wise man can take a fool to court. The fool gets angry or laughs, and there is no peace.

**10** Murderers hate an honest man. But the righteous try to protect his life.

**11** A fool shows all his anger. But a wise man controls his anger.

**12** If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials become wicked.

**13** The poor man and the cruel man are the same in one thing. The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.

**14** A king can judge the poor honestly. The rule of that king will continue forever.

**15** The stick and correction give wisdom. But a child who does what he wants brings shame to his mother.

**16** When the wicked increase, sin increases. But the righteous will see the fall of the wicked.

**17** Correct your son, and he will give you peace. He will give joy to you.

**18** When the people do not get a message from God, they do what they want. But a man who obeys the law is happy.

**19** Words alone will not correct a servant. He understands, but he does not obey.

**20** Do you see a man who speaks too quickly? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

**21** A man can give his servant everything from childhood. At the end, the servant will cause him grief.

**22** An angry man causes arguments. A man with a hot temper does much wrong.

**23** The pride of a man will make him low. But a humble man will get honor.

**24** A man who is a partner of a thief hates his own life. He hears the oath in court, but he does not tell the truth.

**25** Fear of people is like a trap. But a man who trusts the LORD will be safe.

**26** Many people want the favor of a ruler. But justice for a man comes from the LORD.

**27** The righteous hate a dishonest man. The wicked hate an honest man.

## Chapter 30

**1** These are the words of Agur, the son of Jakeh. This is his message. He spoke to Ithiel, to Ithiel and to Ucal.

**2** "I am more foolish than all other men. I do not have the wisdom of a man.

**3** I did not learn wisdom. I do not have the knowledge of the Holy God.

**4** Who went up into heaven and came down? Who held the wind in his hands? Who wrapped the waters in a cloth? Who set all the ends of the earth? What is his name? What is the name of his son? Tell me if you know!

**5** Every word of God is true. He is a shield to the people who trust Him.

**6** Do not add to His words. If you do, He will correct you. He will show that you are a liar.

**7** God, I ask You for 2 things. Give them to me before I die.

**8** Keep lies and false words far from me. Do not make me poor or rich. Give me only the food that I need.

**9** If I have too much, I can refuse You and say, 'Who is the LORD?' If I am poor, I can steal. Then I will bring shame to the name of my God.

**10** Do not speak against a servant to his master. If you do, the servant will curse you, and you will be guilty.

**11** Some people curse their father. They do not bless their mother.

**12** Some people think that they are clean. But they did not wash away their dirt.

**13** Some people are very proud. They look down on other people.

**14** Some people have teeth like swords and jaws like knives. They destroy the poor on the earth and the needy among men.

**15** The leech has 2 daughters. Their names are 'Give' and 'Give.' 3 things are never satisfied. 4 things never say, 'That is sufficient.'

**16** These are the grave and a woman who cannot have children. They are also dry land that always needs water, and fire that never says, 'That is sufficient.'

**17** A person can mock his father and refuse to obey his mother. The ravens of the valley will pick out his eye. The young eagles will eat it.

**18** 3 things are too wonderful for me. 4 things I do not understand.

**19** These are the path of an eagle in the sky and the path of a snake on a rock. They are also the path of a ship on the sea and the way of a man with a young woman.

**20** This is the way of an unfaithful wife. She eats and wipes her mouth. Then she says, 'I did nothing wrong.'

**21** 3 things make the earth shake. 4 things the earth cannot carry.

**22** These are a servant who becomes king and a fool who has too much food.

**23** They are also a hated woman who gets married and a female servant who takes the place of her mistress.

**24** 4 things on the earth are small, but they are very wise.

**25** The ants are not strong. But they store their food in the summer.

**26** The rock badgers are not strong. But they make their homes in the rocks.

**27** The locusts have no king. But all of them go forward in groups.

**28** You can hold a lizard in your hands. But a lizard lives in the palaces of kings.

**29** 3 things walk with pride. 4 things move in a proud way.

**30** One is the lion. It is the strongest of the animals, and it does not turn away from anything.

**31** The others are the rooster, the male goat and a king with his army around him.

**32** You can be foolish and make yourself proud, or you can plan evil. Then stop and put your hand over your mouth.

**33** When you stir milk, you make butter. When you hit a nose, you cause blood. Also, when you cause anger, you cause arguments."

## Chapter 31

**1** These are the words of King Lemuel. His mother taught him this message.

**2** "My son, what must I tell you? You are the son that I gave birth to. You are the son that I prayed for.

**3** Do not give your strength to women. Do not give your life to the women who destroy kings.

**4** Lemuel, kings must not drink wine. Rulers must not want strong drink.

**5** If they drink, they can forget the law. They can take away the rights of the poor.

**6** Give strong drink to the man who is about to die. Give wine to the people who are very sad.

**7** Let them drink and forget their poverty. Let them not remember their trouble.

**8** Speak for the people who cannot speak for themselves. Speak for the rights of all helpless people.

**9** Speak and judge honestly. Defend the rights of the poor and needy."

**10** Who can find a good wife? She is worth much more than jewels.

**11** Her husband trusts her completely. He will always have sufficient money.

**12** She does good things for him, not bad things, all the days of her life.

**13** She finds wool and linen. She works with her hands willingly.

**14** She is like the ships of merchants. She brings her food from far away.

**15** She gets up while it is still night. She gives food to her family. She gives work to her female servants.

**16** She looks at a field and buys it. With the money that she earns, she plants a vineyard.

**17** She works with strength. Her arms are strong.

**18** She knows that her trade gives a good profit. Her lamp burns all night.

**19** She puts her hands on the spindle. She holds the thread in her hands.

**20** She gives help to the poor. She reaches out her hands to the needy.

**21** She is not afraid of the snow for her family. All her family wear warm, red clothes.

**22** She makes covers for her beds. She wears clothes of fine linen and purple cloth.

**23** People know her husband in the city gates. He sits among the leaders of the country.

**24** She makes linen clothes and sells them. She gives belts to the merchants.

**25** She is strong and people respect her. She laughs without fear of the future.

**26** She speaks with wisdom. She teaches with kindness.

**27** She watches carefully all the work of her family. She is never lazy.

**28** Her children stand up and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her.

**29** He says, "Many women do good things, but you are better than all of them."

**30** Charm can deceive, and beauty does not continue. But a woman who fears the LORD will get praise.

**31** Give her the reward that she earns. Let her work bring her praise in the city gates.
