# Ecclesiastes

## Chapter 1

**1** These are the words of the Teacher. He was the son of David and the king in Jerusalem.

**2** The Teacher says, "Nothing has meaning. Nothing has meaning. All things have no meaning."

**3** A man works hard on the earth all his life. What does he get for all his work?

**4** One generation goes, and another generation comes. But the earth stays forever.

**5** The sun comes up and the sun goes down. Then it moves quickly back to the place where it comes up.

**6** The wind blows to the south and turns to the north. The wind turns around and around. It always comes back on its circuit.

**7** All the rivers flow into the sea, but the sea is never full. The rivers go back to their start, and they flow again.

**8** All things make people tired. Nobody can fully tell about them. The eye always wants to see more. The ear always wants to hear more.

**9** The things that occurred before will occur again. The things that people did before, they will do again. There is nothing new on the earth.

**10** Can a person show something and say, "Look, this is new"? No. That thing was there a long time before us.

**11** People do not remember the people of the past. Also, the people who come later will not remember the people who come before them.

**12** I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

**13** I used my wisdom to study all the things that people do on the earth. God gives people a heavy load of work to do.

**14** I saw all the things that people do on the earth. All of it has no meaning. It is like when you try to catch the wind.

**15** People cannot make straight a thing that is bent. People cannot count a thing that is not there.

**16** I said to myself, "I am great. I have more wisdom than all the kings in Jerusalem before me. I know much about wisdom and knowledge."

**17** I tried to understand wisdom. I also tried to understand madness and foolishness. But I learned that this is also like when you try to catch the wind.

**18** With much wisdom comes much sorrow. A person who gets more knowledge gets more pain.

## Chapter 2

**1** I said to myself, "I will test pleasure. I will enjoy good things." But this also had no meaning.

**2** I said, "Laughter is foolish. Pleasure does nothing good."

**3** I decided to make myself happy with wine. But I let wisdom guide my mind. I tried foolishness too. I wanted to learn what is good for people to do during their short life on the earth.

**4** I did great things. I built houses for myself. I planted vineyards.

**5** I made gardens and parks. I planted all types of fruit trees in them.

**6** I made pools of water. I used the water for the many trees that grew in the forest.

**7** I bought male and female slaves. Some slaves had their birth in my house. I also had more cattle and sheep than all the people in Jerusalem before me.

**8** I also collected silver and gold and the treasures of kings and countries. I got men and women to sing for me. I also got musical instruments of all types.

**9** So I became great. I became greater than all the people in Jerusalem before me. And my wisdom stayed with me.

**10** I got all the things that I wanted. I did not refuse myself any pleasure. My work made me happy. That joy was my reward for all my work.

**11** Then I looked at all the things that I did. I looked at all the hard work. But all of it had no meaning. It was like when you try to catch the wind. Nothing on the earth gave a true profit.

**12** Then I started to think about wisdom, madness and foolishness. What can the next king do? He can only do what the king before him did.

**13** Then I saw that wisdom is better than foolishness. Wisdom is better as light is better than darkness.

**14** A wise man can see where he goes. But a fool walks in darkness. Yet I saw that the same end comes to both of them.

**15** I said to myself, "The end of the fool will also be my end. So why did I become very wise?" I said to myself, "This also has no meaning."

**16** People will not remember the wise man forever, and they will not remember the fool. In the future, people will forget both of them. The wise man dies as the fool dies.

**17** So I hated life. All the work on the earth gave me grief. All of it had no meaning. It was like when you try to catch the wind.

**18** I hated all the work that I did on the earth. I must leave the results of that work to the man who comes after me.

**19** Nobody knows if that man will be wise or foolish. But he will control all the things that I made with my work and my wisdom. This also has no meaning.

**20** So I started to lose hope about all my hard work on the earth.

**21** A man can work with wisdom, knowledge and skill. Then he must leave all the results to a man who did not work for them. This also has no meaning, and it is very bad.

**22** A man works hard and worries on the earth. What does he get from all that work?

**23** All his days, his work gives him pain and grief. Even at night, his mind does not rest. This also has no meaning.

**24** Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I saw that this also comes from the hand of God.

**25** Without God, nobody can eat or have joy.

**26** God gives wisdom, knowledge and joy to the man who pleases Him. But God gives the sinner the work to collect and store things. Then God gives those things to the man who pleases Him. This also has no meaning. It is like when you try to catch the wind.

## Chapter 3

**1** There is a time for every thing. There is a time for every activity on the earth.

**2** There is a time for birth and a time to die. There is a time to plant and a time to pull up plants.

**3** There is a time to kill and a time to heal. There is a time to tear down and a time to build.

**4** There is a time to cry and a time to laugh. There is a time to be sad and a time to dance.

**5** There is a time to throw away stones and a time to collect stones. There is a time to hold people close and a time to stop.

**6** There is a time to get things and a time to lose things. There is a time to keep things and a time to throw things away.

**7** There is a time to tear and a time to sew. There is a time to be quiet and a time to speak.

**8** There is a time to love and a time to hate. There is a time for war and a time for peace.

**9** What does a worker get from all his hard work?

**10** I saw the heavy load that God gives people to carry.

**11** God made every thing beautiful at the correct time. He also put a feeling of eternity into the minds of people. But people cannot understand all of the work of God from the start to the end.

**12** I know that nothing is better for people than to be happy and do good during their life.

**13** Every person must eat and drink and enjoy the good results of his work. This is a gift from God.

**14** I know that all that God does will continue forever. Nobody can add to it or remove from it. God does this so that people will fear Him.

**15** The things that occur now occurred before. The things that will occur occurred before. God makes the past occur again.

**16** I also saw this on the earth. In the place of justice, there was wickedness. In the place of righteousness, there was wickedness.

**17** I said to myself, "God will judge the righteous and the wicked. There is a time for every activity and every action."

**18** I said to myself, "God tests people. God shows people that they are like animals."

**19** The same end comes to people and to animals. Both die. Both have the same breath. People are not better than animals. All things have no meaning.

**20** All go to the same place. All come from dust, and all go back to dust.

**21** Nobody knows if the spirit of a person goes up. Nobody knows if the spirit of an animal goes down into the earth.

**22** So I saw that nothing is better for a man than to enjoy his work. That is his reward. Nobody can show him what will occur after he dies.

## Chapter 4

**1** Again I looked at all the cruel things that people do on the earth. I saw the tears of the oppressed people. Nobody gave them comfort. Their oppressors had power. And nobody gave the oppressed people comfort.

**2** So I said that the dead people are more fortunate than the people who are still alive.

**3** But the person who is not yet born is better than both. That person did not see the evil things that people do on the earth.

**4** I saw that people work hard and with skill because they are jealous of their neighbors. This also has no meaning. It is like when you try to catch the wind.

**5** The fool folds his hands and does no work. He destroys himself.

**6** One handful with peace is better than 2 handfuls with hard work. Hard work for more is like when you try to catch the wind.

**7** Again I saw something on the earth that has no meaning.

**8** There is a man who is alone. He has no son and no brother. But he never stops his work. He is never satisfied with his riches. He does not ask, "For whom do I work? Why do I refuse myself pleasure?" This also has no meaning. It is a sad situation.

**9** 2 people are better than 1. Together they get a good reward for their work.

**10** If one person falls, the other person can help him up. But it is bad for a person who is alone when he falls. Nobody will help him up.

**11** Also, if 2 people lie down together, they keep warm. But a person who is alone cannot get warm.

**12** An enemy can defeat one person, but 2 people can defend themselves. A rope of 3 strands does not break quickly.

**13** A poor, wise young man is better than an old, foolish king. The old king does not listen to advice any more.

**14** The young man can come out of prison and become king. He can have his birth in that kingdom as a poor man.

**15** I saw all the people on the earth follow the young man. He took the place of the old king.

**16** There was no end to all the people that he led. But the people who come later will not be happy with him. This also has no meaning. It is like when you try to catch the wind.

## Chapter 5

**1** Be careful when you go to the house of God. Go to listen. Do not give foolish sacrifices as fools do. Fools do not know that they do wrong.

**2** Do not speak too quickly. Do not make quick promises to God. God is in heaven and you are on the earth. So say only a few words.

**3** Too much worry causes bad dreams. Too many words cause foolish talk.

**4** When you make a promise (a vow) to God, do it quickly. God is not happy with fools. Do what you promise.

**5** It is better not to make a vow than to make a vow and not do it.

**6** Do not let your words cause you to sin. Do not tell the priest, "My vow was a mistake." Why make God angry about your words? He can destroy the work of your hands.

**7** Too many dreams and too many words have no meaning. Fear God.

**8** In a country, you can see that people oppress the poor. You can see that they refuse justice to the poor. Do not feel surprise. An official watches the official below him. Higher officials watch both of them.

**9** All people get the profit of the land. The king also gets food from the fields.

**10** A man who loves money will never have sufficient money. A man who loves riches will never have sufficient income. This also has no meaning.

**11** When a man gets more things, more people come to use them. The owner only gets to look at them.

**12** A worker sleeps well, if he eats little or much. But the riches of a rich man do not let him sleep.

**13** I saw a very bad thing on the earth. A man kept his riches, but the riches caused him damage.

**14** He lost his riches in a bad business deal. Then he had a son, but he had nothing to give to his son.

**15** A man comes from his mother with no clothes. He will go away with no clothes. He will take nothing from his work in his hand.

**16** This also is a very bad thing. A man goes away the same as he comes. What does he get from his work? He works for the wind.

**17** All his life, he eats in darkness. He has much worry, sickness and anger.

**18** I saw that it is good and correct for a man to eat and drink. He must enjoy his work on the earth during the short life that God gives him. That is his reward.

**19** God gives some people riches and property. God also lets them enjoy these things. They accept their reward and are happy in their work. This is a gift from God.

**20** These people do not think much about the short time of their life. God keeps them busy with joy.

## Chapter 6

**1** I saw another bad thing on the earth. It is heavy on people.

**2** God gives a man riches, property and honor. The man has all that he wants. But God does not let him enjoy these things. A stranger enjoys them. This has no meaning. It is a very bad thing.

**3** A man can have 100 children and live many years. But possibly he does not enjoy good things and does not get a correct burial. Then a baby who is dead at birth is better than that man.

**4** That baby comes with no meaning and goes into darkness. Darkness covers its name.

**5** That baby never sees the sun and never knows anything. But it has more rest than that man.

**6** That man can live 2,000 years and not enjoy good things. All people go to the same place.

**7** A man works only to get food for his mouth. But he is never satisfied.

**8** What advantage does a wise man have over a fool? What advantage does a poor man get if he knows how to act in front of other people?

**9** It is better to enjoy what you have than to want more. A desire for more has no meaning. It is like when you try to catch the wind.

**10** All things that occur already have a name. People know what man is. A man cannot argue with God, who is stronger than he is.

**11** More words give less meaning. Words do not help a man.

**12** Nobody knows what is good for a man during his short life. His life goes quickly like a shadow. Nobody can tell a man what will occur on the earth after he dies.

## Chapter 7

**1** A good name is better than expensive perfume. The day of death is better than the day of birth.

**2** It is better to go to a house of sorrow than to a house of celebration. Death is the end of all people. The people who are alive must think about this.

**3** Sorrow is better than laughter. A sad face can make the heart better.

**4** A wise man thinks about death. A fool thinks only about pleasure.

**5** It is better to hear the correction of a wise man than to hear the songs of fools.

**6** The laughter of a fool is like the noise of thorns that burn under a pot. This also has no meaning.

**7** Oppression makes a wise man foolish. A bribe destroys the mind.

**8** The end of a thing is better than its start. Patience is better than pride.

**9** Do not become angry quickly. Anger stays in the mind of fools.

**10** Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these days?" That is not a wise question.

**11** Wisdom is good, as an inheritance is good. Wisdom helps the people who are alive.

**12** Wisdom protects, as money protects. But knowledge has this advantage: wisdom keeps alive the person who has it.

**13** Think about the work of God. Nobody can make straight a thing that God makes bent.

**14** When times are good, be happy. When times are bad, think about this. God makes both good times and bad times. So a man cannot know his future.

**15** During my short life, I saw all these things. A righteous man can die in his righteousness. A wicked man can live long in his wickedness.

**16** Do not be too righteous or too wise. Why destroy yourself?

**17** Do not be too wicked, and do not be a fool. Why die before your time?

**18** It is good to hold on to one thing and not let go of the other. A man who fears God will avoid both extremes.

**19** Wisdom makes one wise man stronger than 10 rulers in a city.

**20** There is no righteous man on the earth who always does good and never sins.

**21** Do not listen to all the things that people say. If you listen, you can hear your servant curse you.

**22** You know that you also cursed other people many times.

**23** I tested all these things with wisdom. I said, "I will be wise." But wisdom was far from me.

**24** Wisdom is far away and very deep. Nobody can find it.

**25** I decided to know, to study and to look for wisdom and the reason for things. I wanted to know that wickedness is foolish and that foolishness is madness.

**26** I found something more bitter than death. It is a woman who sets traps for men. Her love is like a net, and her hands are like chains. A man who pleases God will escape from her. But she will catch the sinner.

**27** The Teacher says, "Look, this is what I found. I put one thing with another thing to find the answer.

**28** I continue to look, but I do not find the answer. I found 1 good man in 1,000. But I did not find 1 good woman among them.

**29** I found only this: God made people honest. But people looked for many evil plans."

## Chapter 8

**1** Who is like the wise man? Who knows the meaning of things? Wisdom makes a man's face shine. It makes his hard face gentle.

**2** I tell you to obey the command of the king. You made a promise to God about this.

**3** Do not leave the king quickly. Do not take part in an evil plan. The king does what he wants.

**4** The word of the king has power. Nobody can ask him, "Why do you do this?"

**5** A person who obeys the command will have no trouble. A wise man knows the correct time and the correct way to act.

**6** There is a correct time and way for every action. But a man has many troubles.

**7** Nobody knows the future. Nobody can tell a man what will occur.

**8** Nobody has the power to stop the wind. Nobody has power over the day of his death. Nobody is free from that war. Wickedness will not save the wicked.

**9** I saw all this. I thought about all the things that people do on the earth. Sometimes one person has power over another person and causes him damage.

**10** Then I saw the burial of wicked people. They often went into and out of the holy place. People praised them in the city where they did evil things. This also has no meaning.

**11** People do not punish crime quickly. So people decide to do evil things.

**12** A sinner can do evil 100 times and still live a long life. But I know that it will be better for people who fear God and respect Him.

**13** But it will not be good for the wicked. Their lives will not continue long. Their lives are like a shadow, because they do not fear God.

**14** There is another thing on the earth that has no meaning. Some righteous people get the punishment that the wicked deserve. Some wicked people get the reward that the righteous deserve. I said that this also has no meaning.

**15** So I recommend joy. Nothing is better for a man on the earth than to eat, drink and be happy. Then joy will stay with him in his work during the life that God gives him.

**16** I tried to know wisdom. I tried to see all the work that people do on the earth. Some people do not sleep in the day or in the night.

**17** Then I saw all the work of God. A man cannot understand the things that occur on the earth. He can work hard to look for the answer, but he will not find it. A wise man can say that he knows. But he cannot understand it.

## Chapter 9

**1** I thought about all this, and I saw that God controls the righteous and the wise and their actions. Nobody knows if love or hate will come to him.

**2** The same end comes to all people. It comes to the righteous and the wicked. It comes to the good, the clean and the unclean. It comes to people who give sacrifices and people who do not give sacrifices. It comes to the good man and the sinner. It comes to people who make oaths and people who fear to make oaths.

**3** This is the evil in all things that occur on the earth. The same end comes to all people. Also, the hearts of people are full of evil. They are foolish during their life, and after that, they die.

**4** But a person who is alive has hope. A dog that is alive is better than a dead lion.

**5** The people who are alive know that they will die. But the dead know nothing. They get no more reward. People forget them.

**6** Their love, their hate and their jealousy stopped long ago. They will never again take part in the things that occur on the earth.

**7** Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a happy heart. God already accepts what you do.

**8** Always wear white clothes. Always put oil on your head.

**9** Enjoy life with the wife whom you love. Enjoy all the days of the short life that God gives you on the earth. That is your reward in life and in your hard work on the earth.

**10** Do all your work with all your strength. You go to the grave (Sheol). In the grave, there is no work, no plan, no knowledge and no wisdom.

**11** I saw something else on the earth. The fastest runner does not always win the race. The strongest soldier does not always win the battle. The wise do not always have food. The intelligent do not always have riches. The skilled do not always get favor. Time and chance come to all of them.

**12** Nobody knows when his time will come. People are like fish that a net catches. People are like birds that a trap catches. A bad time comes to people suddenly.

**13** I also saw this example of wisdom on the earth. I thought that it was very important.

**14** There was a small city with few men in it. A powerful king came against the city. He put his army around it and built large siege walls against it.

**15** A poor, wise man lived in that city. He saved the city with his wisdom. But nobody remembered that poor man.

**16** So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." But people hated the wisdom of the poor man. They did not listen to his words.

**17** It is better to listen to the quiet words of a wise man than to the shouts of a ruler of fools.

**18** Wisdom is better than weapons of war. But one sinner can destroy many good things.

## Chapter 10

**1** Dead flies make perfume smell bad. Also, a small quantity of foolishness can destroy much wisdom and honor.

**2** The mind of a wise man goes to the correct side. But the mind of a fool goes to the wrong side.

**3** When a fool walks on the road, he does not use good sense. He shows everyone that he is a fool.

**4** If a ruler becomes angry with you, do not leave your work. If you stay calm, you can stop large mistakes.

**5** I saw an evil thing on the earth. It is a type of mistake that rulers make.

**6** Rulers give high positions to fools. Rich people get low positions.

**7** I saw slaves on horses. I saw princes walk on the ground like slaves.

**8** A man who digs a pit can fall into it. A snake can bite a man who breaks through a wall.

**9** A man who cuts stones can get hurt by them. A man who cuts wood can get injured.

**10** If an ax is not sharp and a man does not sharpen it, he must use more strength. But wisdom helps a man to have success.

**11** If a snake bites before the charmer controls it, the charmer gets no profit.

**12** The words of a wise man bring him favor. But the words of a fool destroy him.

**13** A fool starts to speak with foolishness. He ends his talk with dangerous madness.

**14** A fool talks too much. Nobody knows what will occur. Nobody can tell a man what will occur after him.

**15** The work of a fool makes him tired. He does not even know the road to the city.

**16** It is bad for a country when its king is a young boy. It is bad when its leaders feast in the morning.

**17** It is good for a country when its king is from a noble family. It is good when its leaders eat at the correct time. They eat for strength, not to become drunk.

**18** If a man is lazy, the roof becomes weak. If he does not use his hands, water comes into the house.

**19** People make feasts to laugh. Wine makes people happy. Money gets all things.

**20** Do not curse the king, even in your thoughts. Do not curse a rich man, even in your bedroom. A bird can carry your words. A bird can tell what you said.

## Chapter 11

**1** Send your bread on the waters. After many days, you will find it again.

**2** Divide your possessions among 7 or 8 people. You do not know what disaster will come on the earth.

**3** When clouds are full of rain, they pour the rain on the earth. A tree can fall to the south or to the north. The tree will stay where it falls.

**4** A farmer who waits for the correct wind will not plant. A farmer who watches the clouds will not harvest.

**5** You do not know the path of the wind. You do not know how a baby grows inside its mother. Also, you do not know the work of God, who makes all things.

**6** Plant your seed in the morning. Do not stop your work in the evening. You do not know which work will have success. Both can be good.

**7** Light is sweet. It is good for the eyes to see the sun.

**8** A man can live many years. He must enjoy all of them. But he must also remember that the dark days will be many. All that comes has no meaning.

**9** Young man, be happy while you are young. Let your heart give you joy in the days of your youth. Do what you want and what you see. But know that God will judge you for all these things.

**10** So remove worry from your mind. Keep away pain from your body. Youth and the strength of youth go quickly.

## Chapter 12

**1** Remember your Creator while you are young. Remember Him before the bad days come. Remember Him before the years come when you will say, "I have no pleasure in them."

**2** Remember Him before the sun, the light, the moon and the stars become dark for you. Remember Him before the clouds come back after the rain.

**3** At that time, your arms will shake and your legs will become weak. Your teeth will be few and stop their work. Your eyes will become dim.

**4** Your ears will close to the noise of the street. The sound of the mill will be quiet. You will wake up when a bird sings. But you will hardly hear songs.

**5** You will be afraid of high places and of danger on the road. Your hair will become white like the almond tree in bloom. You will drag yourself along like a grasshopper. Your desire will stop. Then you go to your eternal home, and people cry in the streets.

**6** Remember your Creator before the silver cord breaks and the gold bowl breaks. Remember Him before the jar breaks at the spring and the wheel breaks at the well.

**7** Then the body will go back to the dust of the earth. The spirit will go back to God, who gave it.

**8** The Teacher says, "Nothing has meaning. All things have no meaning."

**9** The Teacher was wise. He also taught knowledge to the people. He thought about many proverbs. He studied them and put them in order.

**10** The Teacher tried to find the correct words. He wrote words that were honest and true.

**11** The words of wise people are like sticks that guide cattle. Their collected sayings are like nails that a man hammers in firmly. One Shepherd gives these words.

**12** My son, be careful of anything more than these words. People will never stop when they write books. Too much study makes the body tired.

**13** This is the end of the matter. You heard all of it. Fear God and obey His commands. This is the duty of all people.

**14** God will judge every action and every secret thing. He will judge the good and the evil.

# Song of Solomon

## Chapter 1

**1** This is the best song. Solomon wrote it.

**2** The woman says, "I want him to kiss me with his mouth. Your love is better than wine.

**3** Your perfume smells good. Your name is like perfume that a person pours out. So the young women love you.

**4** Take me with you. We will run together. The king brought me into his rooms. We will be glad and have joy in you. We will praise your love more than wine. It is correct that the women love you."

**5** "Women of Jerusalem, my skin is dark, but I am beautiful. I am dark like the tents of Kedar. I am beautiful like the curtains of Solomon.

**6** Do not look at me because my skin is dark. The sun made it dark. My brothers were angry with me. They made me work in the vineyards. But I did not take care of my own vineyard, my own body.

**7** You are the man whom I love. Tell me where you feed your sheep. Tell me where your sheep rest at noon. I do not want to look for you like a stranger among the sheep of your friends."

**8** The friends say, "You are the most beautiful of women. If you do not know, follow the tracks of the sheep. Feed your young goats near the tents of the shepherds."

**9** The man says, "My love, you are like a beautiful horse among the chariots of Pharaoh.

**10** Your cheeks are beautiful with jewels. Your neck is beautiful with gold chains.

**11** We will make gold chains for you, with silver decorations."

**12** The woman says, "While the king sat at his table, my perfume gave its sweet smell.

**13** My love is like a small bag of myrrh to me. He will rest all night between my breasts.

**14** My love is like a group of henna flowers to me. They are the flowers in the vineyards of En-gedi."

**15** The man says, "My love, you are beautiful. You are very beautiful. Your eyes are gentle like doves."

**16** The woman says, "My love, you are handsome. You are very pleasant. The green grass is our bed.

**17** The cedar trees are the beams of our house. The fir trees are our roof."

## Chapter 2

**1** The woman says, "I am only a flower of Sharon. I am only a lily of the valleys."

**2** The man says, "My love among the other young women is like a lily among thorns."

**3** The woman says, "My love among the other young men is like an apple tree among the trees of the forest. I sat in his shade with great pleasure. His fruit was sweet to my taste.

**4** He brought me to the house of the feast. His love was like a flag over me.

**5** Give me raisins to make me strong. Give me apples to refresh me. My love for him makes me weak.

**6** His left hand is under my head. His right hand holds me.

**7** Women of Jerusalem, make a promise to me by the deer and the wild animals of the field. Do not wake up love until the correct time."

**8** "I hear the voice of my love! Look, he comes! He jumps over the mountains. He runs over the hills.

**9** My love is like a deer or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall. He looks through the windows. He looks through the openings in the wall.

**10** My love spoke to me. He said, 'Get up, my love, my beautiful one. Come away with me.

**11** Look, the winter is past. The rain stopped and went away.

**12** Flowers grow in the land. The time for birds to sing comes. We hear the sound of the dove in our land.

**13** The fig tree makes its first figs. The vines have flowers and give a sweet smell. Get up, my love, my beautiful one. Come away with me.'"

**14** The man says, "My love, you are like a dove that hides in the openings in the rock. You hide in the secret places on the mountain. Let me see your face. Let me hear your voice. Your voice is sweet, and your face is beautiful."

**15** "Catch the foxes for us. Catch the little foxes that destroy the vineyards. Our vineyards have flowers now."

**16** The woman says, "My love is mine, and I am his. He feeds his sheep among the lilies.

**17** My love, before the morning comes and the shadows go away, come back. Be like a deer or a young stag on the rough mountains."

## Chapter 3

**1** The woman says, "At night on my bed, I looked for the man whom I love. I looked for him, but I did not find him.

**2** I said, 'I will get up now and go around the city. I will look in the streets and in the squares for the man whom I love.' I looked for him, but I did not find him.

**3** The guards who go around the city found me. I asked them, 'Did you see the man whom I love?'

**4** I went only a short distance past them. Then I found the man whom I love. I held him, and I did not let him go. I brought him into the house of my mother. I brought him into the room where she gave birth to me.

**5** Women of Jerusalem, make a promise to me by the deer and the wild animals of the field. Do not wake up love until the correct time."

**6** Who is this that comes from the desert like a column of smoke? The perfume of myrrh and incense comes from it. It has all the spices of the merchants.

**7** Look, it is the carriage of Solomon. 60 strong soldiers are around it. They are the best soldiers of Israel.

**8** All of them hold swords. All of them are experts in war. Every man has his sword at his side, ready for the dangers of the night.

**9** King Solomon made a carriage for himself. He made it from the wood of Lebanon.

**10** He made its posts of silver. He made its back of gold. He made its seat of purple cloth. The women of Jerusalem decorated the inside with love.

**11** Women of Zion, go out and look at King Solomon. He wears the crown that his mother put on him on the day of his wedding. That was the day when his heart was very happy.

## Chapter 4

**1** The man says, "My love, you are beautiful. You are very beautiful. Behind your veil, your eyes are gentle like doves. Your hair is like a group of black goats that come down from Mount Gilead.

**2** Your teeth are white like a group of sheep with new-cut wool. The sheep come up from the place where people wash them. Each tooth has its pair, and none is absent.

**3** Your lips are like a red thread. Your mouth is beautiful. Behind your veil, your cheeks are red like a piece of a pomegranate.

**4** Your neck is tall like the tower of David. David built that tower for weapons. 1,000 shields hang on the tower. All of them are the shields of strong soldiers.

**5** Your 2 breasts are like 2 young deer. They are twins that feed among the lilies.

**6** Before the morning comes and the shadows go away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh. I will go to the hill of incense.

**7** My love, you are completely beautiful. You have no fault.

**8** My bride, come with me from Lebanon. Come with me from Lebanon. Come down from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon. Come from the homes of the lions and the mountains of the leopards.

**9** My sister, my bride, you took my heart. You took my heart with one look of your eyes. You took it with one jewel of your necklace.

**10** My sister, my bride, your love is very beautiful. Your love is much better than wine. The smell of your perfume is better than all spices.

**11** My bride, your lips are sweet like honey. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your clothes is like the smell of Lebanon.

**12** My sister, my bride, you are like a garden that has a lock. You are like a spring that someone closed. You are like a fountain that has a seal.

**13** You are like a garden of pomegranate trees with the best fruit. You have henna and nard plants.

**14** You have nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon. You have all types of incense trees. You have myrrh and aloes and all the best spices.

**15** You are like a fountain in a garden. You are like a well of fresh water. You are like streams that flow down from Lebanon."

**16** The woman says, "North wind, wake up! South wind, come! Blow on my garden, and spread its sweet smells. Let my love come into his garden. Let him eat its best fruits."

## Chapter 5

**1** The man says, "My sister, my bride, I came into my garden. I gathered my myrrh and my spice. I ate my honey and the honeycomb. I drank my wine and my milk." The friends say, "Eat, friends! Drink! Drink much of love!"

**2** The woman says, "I slept, but my heart was awake. I heard my love knock on the door. He said, 'Open the door to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one. My head is wet with dew. My hair is wet with the drops of the night.'

**3** I said, 'I took off my clothes. Must I put them on again? I washed my feet. Must I make them dirty again?'

**4** My love put his hand through the hole in the door. My heart beat fast for him.

**5** I got up to open the door to my love. My hands were wet with myrrh. My fingers were wet with myrrh on the handles of the lock.

**6** I opened the door to my love. But my love turned and went away. My heart failed when he spoke. I looked for him, but I did not find him. I called him, but he did not answer.

**7** The guards who go around the city found me. They hit me and hurt me. The guards of the walls took my veil from me.

**8** Women of Jerusalem, make a promise to me. If you find my love, tell him that my love for him makes me weak."

**9** The friends say, "You are the most beautiful of women. Why is your love better than other men? Why do you ask us to make this promise?"

**10** The woman says, "My love is handsome and strong. He is the best among 10,000 men.

**11** His head is like the best gold. His hair is wavy and black like a raven.

**12** His eyes are like doves beside streams of water. They are white like milk, and they sit in their places like jewels.

**13** His cheeks are like beds of spices with a sweet smell. His lips are like lilies that drip with myrrh.

**14** His arms are like gold rods with jewels. His body is like bright ivory with sapphires on it.

**15** His legs are like pillars of marble on bases of fine gold. He is tall like Lebanon. He is excellent like the cedar trees.

**16** His mouth is very sweet. He is completely beautiful. Women of Jerusalem, this is my love. This is my friend."

## Chapter 6

**1** The friends say, "You are the most beautiful of women. Where did your love go? Which way did he turn? We will look for him with you."

**2** The woman says, "My love went down to his garden, to the beds of spices. He went to feed his sheep in the gardens and to collect lilies.

**3** I am his, and my love is mine. He feeds his sheep among the lilies."

**4** The man says, "My love, you are beautiful like the city of Tirzah. You are lovely like Jerusalem. You are as impressive as an army with flags.

**5** Turn your eyes away from me. They make me helpless. Your hair is like a group of black goats that come down from Gilead.

**6** Your teeth are white like a group of sheep that come up from the place where people wash them. Each tooth has its pair, and none is absent.

**7** Behind your veil, your cheeks are red like a piece of a pomegranate.

**8** There are 60 queens and 80 secondary wives (concubines). There are more young women than anyone can count.

**9** But my dove, my perfect one, is the only one for me. She is the special daughter of her mother. She is the favorite of the mother who gave birth to her. The young women saw her and called her blessed. The queens and the concubines praised her."

**10** They said, "Who is this woman? She looks out like the morning. She is beautiful like the moon and bright like the sun. She is as impressive as an army with flags."

**11** The woman says, "I went down to the garden of nut trees. I wanted to see the new plants in the valley. I wanted to see if the vines had buds and if the pomegranate trees had flowers.

**12** Before I knew it, my desire put me among the chariots of my people's prince."

**13** The friends say, "Come back, come back, Shulamite woman! Come back, come back, so that we can look at you!" The woman says, "Why do you want to look at the Shulamite woman, as at a dance between 2 groups?"

## Chapter 7

**1** The man says, "Daughter of a prince, your feet are beautiful in sandals. The curves of your legs are like jewels. A skilled worker made them.

**2** Your navel is like a round bowl that is always full of wine. Your waist is like a pile of wheat with lilies around it.

**3** Your 2 breasts are like 2 young deer that are twins.

**4** Your neck is like a tower of ivory. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon, near the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon that looks toward Damascus.

**5** Your head is beautiful like Mount Carmel. Your hair shines like purple cloth. Your hair holds the king like a prisoner.

**6** My love, you are very beautiful and very pleasant. You give me much delight.

**7** You are tall like a palm tree. Your breasts are like clusters of fruit.

**8** I said, 'I will climb the palm tree. I will hold its branches.' Let your breasts be like clusters of grapes. Let your breath smell like apples.

**9** Let your kisses be like the best wine." The woman says, "Let the wine go down smoothly to my love. Let it flow gently over the lips of people who sleep.

**10** I am my love's, and he wants me.

**11** Come, my love, we will go out to the fields. We will stay the night in the villages.

**12** We will get up early and go to the vineyards. We will see if the vines have buds and the flowers open. We will see if the pomegranate trees have flowers. There I will give you my love.

**13** The mandrake plants give a sweet smell. At our door there are all types of good fruits, new and old. I kept them for you, my love.

## Chapter 8

**1** I want you to be like my brother, who drank milk from my mother. Then I can kiss you if I find you outside. Nobody will think badly of me.

**2** I will lead you and bring you into the house of my mother. She taught me. I will give you spiced wine to drink. I will give you the juice of my pomegranates.

**3** His left hand is under my head. His right hand holds me.

**4** Women of Jerusalem, make a promise to me. Do not wake up love until the correct time."

**5** The friends say, "Who is this woman? She comes up from the desert and leans on her love." The woman says, "I woke you under the apple tree. There your mother gave birth to you. There she had the pain of birth.

**6** Put me like a seal on your heart. Put me like a seal on your arm. Love is as strong as death. Jealousy is as strong as the grave. Love burns like a very hot fire.

**7** Much water cannot stop love. Rivers cannot drown love. A man can give all his riches for love. But people will laugh at him."

**8** The brothers say, "We have a young sister. Her breasts are still small. What will we do for our sister on the day when a man asks to marry her?

**9** If she is like a wall, we will build silver towers on her. If she is like a door, we will protect her with boards of cedar."

**10** The woman says, "I am like a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So in his eyes I am a woman who brings peace.

**11** Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He gave the vineyard to farmers to take care of it. Each farmer had to pay 1,000 pieces of silver for its fruit.

**12** But my vineyard belongs to me. Solomon, you can have the 1,000 pieces of silver. The farmers who take care of the fruit can have 200 pieces."

**13** The man says, "You live in the gardens. My friends listen to your voice. Let me hear your voice."

**14** The woman says, "Come quickly, my love. Be like a deer or a young stag on the mountains of spices."

# Isaiah

## Chapter 1

**1** This is the vision that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem. He saw it during the rule of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, the kings of Judah.

**2** Heavens, hear me! Earth, listen! The LORD speaks: "I fed my children and I made them grow. But they turned against me.

**3** The ox knows its owner. The donkey knows the feed box of its master. But Israel does not know me. My people do not understand."

**4** You sinful nation, you are in very bad trouble! You are a people with a heavy load of sin. You are the children of evil people. You do corrupt things. You left the LORD. You made the Holy One of Israel angry. You turned away from him.

**5** Why do you want more punishment? Why do you continue to turn against the LORD? Your whole head is sick. Your whole heart is weak.

**6** From the bottom of the foot to the top of the head, no part of the body is healthy. There are only cuts, bruises, and open sores. Nobody cleaned them. Nobody put bandages or oil on them.

**7** Your country is empty and in ruins. Fire burned your cities. Foreign people eat the crops of your land while you watch. The land is in ruins, as when foreign people destroy a land.

**8** The city of Zion is alone, as a small shelter in a vineyard. It is as a hut in a field of cucumbers. It is as a city that an enemy surrounds.

**9** The LORD of armies kept a small number of us alive. Because of this, we did not become as Sodom. We did not become as Gomorrah.

**10** Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

**11** The LORD says, "Your many sacrifices are of no use to me. I have too many burnt offerings of rams and fat from fed animals. I do not like the blood of bulls, lambs, or goats.

**12** You come to my temple to meet me. But who told you to do this? Who told you to walk on the floors of my courts?

**13** Do not bring more offerings that have no value. I hate your incense. I cannot accept your festivals of the new moon, your Sabbaths, and your assemblies. I cannot accept your sin together with your holy assemblies.

**14** I hate your festivals of the new moon and your other festivals. They are a heavy load for me. I feel tired of them.

**15** When you lift your hands to pray, I will not look at you. When you make many prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are full of blood.

**16** Wash yourselves and make yourselves clean. Remove your evil actions from my sight. Stop doing evil.

**17** Learn to do good. Look for justice. Help the people who suffer. Defend the rights of children with no father. Speak for the widows in court.

**18** Come now, and we will talk about this together," says the LORD. "Your sins are as red as scarlet, but they will become as white as snow. They are as red as crimson, but they will become as white as wool.

**19** If you agree and obey, you will eat the good food of the land.

**20** But if you refuse and turn against me, the sword will kill you." The LORD himself speaks these words.

**21** The faithful city became as a prostitute! Before, the city was full of justice. Good people lived in it. But now murderers live in it.

**22** Your silver became waste metal. Your wine has water in it.

**23** Your leaders turn against God. They are friends of thieves. They all love bribes and they try to get payments. They do not defend the rights of children with no father. They do not hear the case of the widow.

**24** Thus the Lord, the LORD of armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says, "I will punish my enemies. I will take revenge on the people who are against me.

**25** I will turn my hand against you. I will make you clean, as fire removes waste from metal. I will remove all your impurities.

**26** I will give you good judges again, as at the start. I will give you good advisors, as before. After that, people will call you 'The city of righteousness, the faithful city.'"

**27** The LORD will save Zion with justice. He will save the people of Zion who turn back to him with righteousness.

**28** But the LORD will destroy the sinners and the people who turn against him together. The people who leave the LORD will die.

**29** You will feel shame because of the sacred oak trees that you loved. You will feel shame because of the gardens that you chose for your idols.

**30** You will be as an oak tree with dry leaves. You will be as a garden that has no water.

**31** The strong man will be as dry fiber. His work will be as a spark. They will both burn together. Nobody will stop the fire.

## Chapter 2

**1** This is the message that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem.

**2** In the last days, the mountain of the temple of the LORD will become the highest of all mountains. It will be higher than the hills. People from all nations will come to it.

**3** Many people will come and say, "Come, we will go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the temple of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways. We will live as he tells us." The law will come from Zion. The word of the LORD will come from Jerusalem.

**4** The LORD will judge between the nations. He will settle the arguments of many peoples. They will hammer their swords into plows. They will make their spears into tools to cut plants. Nations will not fight against nations. They will not train for war again.

**5** People of Jacob, come! We will live in the light of the LORD.

**6** LORD, you left your people, the family of Jacob. They are full of customs from the east. They use magic as the Philistines do. They make agreements with foreign people.

**7** Their land is full of silver and gold. Their treasures have no end. Their land is full of horses. Their chariots have no end.

**8** Their land is full of idols. They worship the things that their own hands made. They worship the things that their own fingers made.

**9** So all people will become low. Each person will be humble. LORD, do not forgive them.

**10** Go into the rocks. Hide in the ground. Hide from the terror of the LORD and from his great glory.

**11** The LORD will make proud people humble. He will put arrogant men down. Only the LORD will be great on that day.

**12** The LORD of armies has a day. On that day he will punish all proud and arrogant people. He will make all high things low.

**13** He will punish all the tall cedar trees of Lebanon and all the oak trees of Bashan.

**14** He will punish all the high mountains and all the tall hills.

**15** He will punish every high tower and every strong wall.

**16** He will punish all the ships of Tarshish and all the beautiful boats.

**17** The LORD will put proud men down. He will make arrogant men low. Only the LORD will be great on that day.

**18** The LORD will remove all the idols.

**19** People will go into caves in the rocks and holes in the ground. They will hide from the terror of the LORD and from his great glory. They will hide when he comes to shake the earth.

**20** On that day people will throw away their idols of silver and gold. They made these idols for worship. But they will throw them to the moles and to the bats.

**21** People will go into the cracks of the rocks and into the high cliffs. They will hide from the terror of the LORD and from his great glory. They will hide when he comes to shake the earth.

**22** Stop your trust in humans. Humans are only breath. They have no value.

## Chapter 3

**1** Look! The Lord, the LORD of armies, will take away from Jerusalem and Judah all the things that they depend on. He will take away all their food and all their water.

**2** He will take away the soldiers and the men of war. He will take away the judges, the prophets, the people who tell the future, and the old leaders.

**3** He will take away the officers of the army and the important men. He will take away the advisors, the skilled workers, and the people who use magic.

**4** The LORD says, "I will make boys their leaders. Children will rule them."

**5** The people will be cruel to each other. Each man will be cruel to his neighbor. Young people will be rude to old people. Bad people will be rude to good people.

**6** A man will hold his brother in the house of his father and say, "You have a coat. Be our ruler! Take control of this ruined country!"

**7** But on that day the brother will refuse. He will say, "I cannot solve your problems. I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me ruler of the people."

**8** Jerusalem will fall. Judah will fall into ruin. The words and actions of the people are against the LORD. They insult his glory.

**9** The look on their faces shows that they are guilty. They show their sin as Sodom did. They do not hide it. They are in very bad trouble. They cause their own disaster.

**10** Tell the righteous people that good things will come to them. They will get the good results of their actions.

**11** But evil people are in very bad trouble. Bad things will come to them. They will get punishment for their actions.

**12** Young people are cruel to my people. Women rule over them. My people, your leaders cause you to go the wrong way. They make you lose the correct path.

**13** The LORD stands up to start his case in court. He stands to judge the people.

**14** The LORD starts to judge the old men and the leaders of his people. He says, "You destroyed my vineyard. The things that you stole from the poor are in your houses.

**15** Why do you crush my people? Why do you hurt the poor people so much?" says the Lord GOD of armies.

**16** The LORD says, "The women of Zion are proud. They walk with their heads high. They look at men with desire. They take small steps when they walk. Their ankle ornaments make noise.

**17** Thus the Lord will put sores on the heads of the women of Zion. The LORD will make them bald."

**18** On that day the Lord will take away their beautiful things. He will take away their ankle ornaments, their headbands, and their moon-shaped necklaces.

**19** He will take away their earrings, their bracelets, and their veils.

**20** He will take away their hats, their ankle chains, their belts, their bottles of perfume, and their charms.

**21** He will take away their rings and their nose rings.

**22** He will take away their fine clothes, their coats, their scarves, and their purses.

**23** He will take away their mirrors, their linen clothes, their head covers, and their long veils.

**24** They will smell bad, not good. They will wear a rope, not a belt. They will be bald, not have beautiful hair. They will wear rough cloth (sackcloth), not fine clothes. They will have marks of shame, not beauty.

**25** Your men will die by the sword. Your soldiers will die in the war.

**26** The people at the gates of Jerusalem will cry and mourn. The city will be empty. It will sit on the ground.

## Chapter 4

**1** On that day 7 women will take hold of 1 man. They will say, "We will get our own food and our own clothes. Only let us use your name. Take away our shame."

**2** On that day the branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious. The fruit of the land will be the pride of the people of Israel who stay alive.

**3** The people who stay in Zion and Jerusalem will be holy. God wrote their names in the list of the people who are alive in Jerusalem.

**4** The Lord will wash away the dirt of the women of Zion. He will clean the blood out of Jerusalem. He will do this with a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.

**5** Then the LORD will put a cloud of smoke over all of Mount Zion during the day. He will put a bright fire over it during the night. He will put it over all the places where the people meet. The glory of the LORD will cover and protect everything.

**6** It will be a shelter that gives shade from the heat in the day. It will be a safe place to hide from storms and rain.

## Chapter 5

**1** I will sing a song for the man that I love. The song is about his vineyard. My friend had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.

**2** He dug the ground and removed the stones. He planted the best vines in it. He built a tower in the middle of it. He also cut a winepress in it. He expected it to grow good grapes. But it grew bad grapes.

**3** "Now, people who live in Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.

**4** What more could I do for my vineyard? I did everything for it. I expected it to grow good grapes. Why did it grow bad grapes?

**5** Now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard. I will remove its hedge, and animals will eat it. I will break down its wall, and animals will walk on it.

**6** I will make it a waste area. Nobody will cut the vines or dig the ground. Thorns and weeds will grow there. I will tell the clouds not to rain on it."

**7** The vineyard of the LORD of armies is the nation of Israel. The people of Judah are the plants that he loved. He expected justice, but he saw murder. He expected righteousness, but he heard cries for help.

**8** You are in very bad trouble, you who buy house after house and field after field! You take all the land. You want to live alone in the land.

**9** The LORD of armies told me this: "Many houses will be empty. Large and beautiful houses will have no people in them.

**10** A vineyard of 10 acres will make only 6 gallons of wine. 10 bushels of seed will make only 1 bushel of grain."

**11** You are in very bad trouble, you who get up early in the morning to drink beer! You stay up late at night until wine makes you drunk.

**12** You have harps, lyres, tambourines, flutes, and wine at your feasts. But you do not think about the work of the LORD. You do not see what his hands do.

**13** Thus enemies will take my people away as prisoners, because they do not know me. Their important men will be hungry. All the people will be very thirsty.

**14** Thus the grave (Sheol) will open its mouth very wide. The leaders of Jerusalem and the noisy, happy crowds will go down into it.

**15** All people will become low. Each person will be humble. The proud people will look down in shame.

**16** But the LORD of armies will be great because of his justice. The holy God will show that he is holy by his righteousness.

**17** Then lambs will eat grass in the ruins as in their own fields. Strangers will eat in the ruined places of the rich.

**18** You are in very bad trouble, you who pull your sins behind you with ropes of lies! You pull sin as with the ropes of a cart.

**19** You say, "Let God hurry and do his work, so that we can see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come, so that we can know it!"

**20** You are in very bad trouble, you who say that evil is good and good is evil! You say that darkness is light and light is darkness. You say that bitter is sweet and sweet is bitter.

**21** You are in very bad trouble, you who think that you are wise! You think that you are clever.

**22** You are in very bad trouble, you who are strong when you drink wine! You are brave when you mix drinks.

**23** You take bribes and you let guilty people go free. You do not give justice to innocent people.

**24** Fire burns dry grass. Flames burn straw. In the same way, the roots of these people will rot. Their flowers will blow away as dust. They refused the law of the LORD of armies. They hated the word of the Holy One of Israel.

**25** Thus the LORD is angry with his people. He lifted his hand against them and he hit them. The mountains shook. Dead bodies lay in the streets as garbage. But after all this, his anger did not stop. His hand is still ready to punish.

**26** The LORD will lift up a flag as a signal to a far nation. He will whistle to call the people from the ends of the earth. Look! They will come very quickly.

**27** None of the soldiers will feel tired or fall. None of them will sleep. Their belts will stay tight. The straps of their sandals will not break.

**28** Their arrows are sharp. All their bows are ready. The hooves of their horses are as hard as stone. The wheels of their chariots turn as fast as a storm.

**29** Their shout is as the roar of a lion. They roar as young lions. They growl and catch their prey. They carry it away, and nobody can save it.

**30** On that day they will roar over Israel as the sea roars. A person will look at the land and see only darkness and trouble. Clouds will make even the light dark.

## Chapter 6

**1** In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord. He sat on a high throne. The bottom of his robe filled the temple.

**2** Seraphim stood above him. Each seraph had 6 wings. With 2 wings each seraph covered his face. With 2 wings he covered his feet. With 2 wings he flew.

**3** The seraphim called to each other. They said, "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!"

**4** Their voices shook the posts of the doors. Smoke filled the temple.

**5** Then I said, "I am in very bad trouble! My end is near! My lips are not clean. I live among people whose lips are not clean. But my eyes saw the King, the LORD of armies!"

**6** Then one of the seraphim flew to me. He held a hot coal in his hand. He took the coal from the altar with tongs.

**7** He touched my mouth with the coal. He said, "Look, this coal touched your lips. God removed your guilt. He forgave your sin."

**8** Then I heard the voice of the Lord. He said, "Whom will I send? Who will go for us?" I said, "I am here. Send me!"

**9** The Lord said, "Go and tell these people: 'You will hear and hear, but you will not understand. You will look and look, but you will not know what you see.'

**10** Make the minds of these people dull. Make their ears deaf. Close their eyes. If you do not, they will see with their eyes. They will hear with their ears. They will understand with their minds. Then they will turn back to me and I will heal them."

**11** Then I said, "Lord, how long must I do this?" He said, "Do it until the cities are in ruins and have no people. Do it until the houses are empty and the land is completely empty.

**12** Do it until the LORD sends the people far away. The land will be empty.

**13** Even if 1 tenth of the people stay in the land, the LORD will destroy them again. But a terebinth tree or an oak tree leaves a stump when a person cuts it down. In the same way, a holy part of the people will stay as a stump."

## Chapter 7

**1** Ahaz was the son of Jotham and the grandson of Uzziah. Ahaz was the king of Judah. During his rule, Rezin, the king of Syria, attacked Jerusalem. Pekah the son of Remaliah, the king of Israel, attacked with him. But they could not defeat the city.

**2** A messenger told the family of David, "Syria made an agreement with Ephraim." Then Ahaz and his people were very afraid. They shook as the trees of a forest shake in the wind.

**3** Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out with your son Shear-Jashub and meet Ahaz. Meet him at the end of the water channel of the upper pool. It is on the road to the field where people wash cloth.

**4** Tell Ahaz, 'Be careful and stay calm. Do not be afraid. Do not lose courage because of these 2 men. Rezin of Syria and the son of Remaliah are very angry. But they are only as the smoke of 2 burned sticks.

**5** Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah made an evil plan against you. They said,

**6** "We will attack Judah and make the people afraid. We will defeat Judah and take it for us. We will make the son of Tabeal the king of Judah."'

**7** But the Lord GOD says, 'Their plan will not succeed. It will not happen.

**8** Damascus is the capital of Syria. Rezin is only the king of Damascus. In 65 years Ephraim will break into pieces. It will not be a nation.

**9** Samaria is the capital of Ephraim. The son of Remaliah is only the king of Samaria. If you do not stay firm in your faith, you will not stay firm at all.'"

**10** The LORD spoke to Ahaz again. He said,

**11** "Ask the LORD your God for a sign. Ask for a sign from the deepest place or from the highest place."

**12** But Ahaz said, "I will not ask. I will not test the LORD."

**13** Then Isaiah said, "Listen, family of David! You make people tired. Is that not sufficient? Must you also make my God tired?

**14** Thus the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look! A virgin will become pregnant. She will give birth to a son. She will call him Immanuel.

**15** He will eat butter and honey when he becomes old enough to know right from wrong.

**16** Before the boy knows how to refuse evil and choose good, the land of the 2 kings that you fear will be empty.

**17** The LORD will bring a time of trouble on you, on your people, and on the family of your father. This time will be worse than any time since Ephraim separated from Judah. The LORD will bring the king of Assyria."

**18** On that day the LORD will whistle for the flies from the far rivers of Egypt. He will whistle for the bees from the land of Assyria.

**19** They will come and stay in the steep valleys and in the holes of the rocks. They will be on all the thorn bushes and all the fields.

**20** On that day the Lord will use the king of Assyria as a razor. The Lord will hire the king from the other side of the Euphrates River. The Lord will shave your head and the hair of your legs. He will also cut off your beard.

**21** On that day a man will keep only 1 young cow and 2 goats alive.

**22** But they will give a large quantity of milk. The man will eat butter. All the people who stay in the land will eat butter and honey.

**23** On that day, thorns and weeds will cover each place that had 1,000 vines. Each of these vineyards had a value of 1,000 silver coins.

**24** Men will go there with bows and arrows to hunt. Thorns and weeds will cover all the land.

**25** People will not go to the hills that farmers dug before. They will be afraid of the thorns and weeds. Cattle and sheep will eat grass there.

## Chapter 8

**1** The LORD said to me, "Take a large scroll. Write these words on it with an ordinary pen: 'Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz.'"

**2** I got 2 reliable men as witnesses. They were Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

**3** Then I had sex with my wife, the prophetess. She became pregnant and gave birth to a son. The LORD said to me, "Call him Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz.

**4** Before the boy can say 'My father' or 'My mother,' the king of Assyria will take away the riches of Damascus. He will also take away the goods of Samaria."

**5** The LORD spoke to me again. He said,

**6** "These people refuse the calm water of the Shiloah channel. They are happy with Rezin and the son of Remaliah.

**7** Thus the Lord will bring the king of Assyria and all his army against them. The king will be as the strong flood of the Euphrates River. He will fill all the channels and go over all the banks.

**8** He will move through Judah as a flood. The water will come up to the neck of the people. His army will spread out as wings and cover all your land, Immanuel!"

**9** Nations, make your war cries! But you will break into pieces. Listen, all you far countries! Prepare for war, but you will break into pieces! Prepare for war, but you will break into pieces!

**10** Make your plans, but they will fail. Give your orders, but they will not succeed. God is with us.

**11** The LORD held me with his strong hand. He told me not to live as these people live. He said,

**12** "Do not call everything a conspiracy, as these people do. Do not fear what they fear. Do not be afraid.

**13** The LORD of armies is holy. Honor him only. Fear him only. Respect him with fear.

**14** He will be a safe place. But for the 2 kingdoms of Israel, he will be a stone that causes people to fall. He will be a rock that makes them trip. For the people of Jerusalem, he will be a trap and a net.

**15** Many of them will fall over this stone. They will fall and break. The trap will catch them."

**16** Keep this message safe. Seal the law and give it to my disciples.

**17** I will wait for the LORD. He hides his face from the family of Jacob. But I will trust him.

**18** I and the children that the LORD gave me are signs in Israel. We are warnings from the LORD of armies. He lives on Mount Zion.

**19** People will tell you, "Ask the people who speak with the dead. Ask the people who whisper and mumble magic words." But people must ask their God. Why ask the dead to help the people who are alive?

**20** Go to the law and the testimony of God! If people do not speak by this word, they have no light.

**21** They will walk through the land in trouble and hunger. When they are hungry, they will become angry. They will curse their king and their God. They will look up,

**22** and then they will look at the earth. But they will see only trouble and darkness. They will see terrible gloom. Someone will push them into complete darkness.

## Chapter 9

**1** But the people in trouble will not always be in darkness. Before, God made the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali humble. But in the future, he will give honor to Galilee of the nations. Galilee is by the road to the sea, on the other side of the Jordan.

**2** The people who walked in darkness saw a great light. A light shone on the people who lived in the land of deep darkness.

**3** LORD, you made the nation large. You made the people very happy. They are happy in your presence, as people are happy at the harvest. They are happy as soldiers when they divide the goods that they took.

**4** You broke the heavy load on their shoulders. You broke the rod of the man who was cruel to them. You did this as you did on the day when you defeated Midian.

**5** Fire will burn every boot of the soldiers. It will burn every coat with blood on it.

**6** A woman gives birth to a child for us. God gives a son to us. He will rule over us. His names will be Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, and Prince of Peace.

**7** His rule and his peace will grow. They will have no end. He will rule from the throne of David over his kingdom. He will make it strong with justice and righteousness from now until always. The strong love of the LORD of armies will do this.

**8** The Lord sent a message against Jacob. The message will come on Israel.

**9** All the people will know it. The people of Ephraim and Samaria will know it. They say with pride and arrogance,

**10** "The bricks fell down, but we will build with cut stones. Enemies cut down the fig trees, but we will put cedar trees in their place."

**11** But the LORD will make the enemies of Rezin strong against Israel. He will cause their enemies to attack.

**12** The Syrians will come from the east. The Philistines will come from the west. They will eat Israel with open mouths. But after all this, the anger of the LORD will not stop. His hand is still ready to punish.

**13** But the people do not turn back to the LORD, who punishes them. They do not look for the LORD of armies.

**14** Thus the LORD will cut off the head and the tail of Israel in 1 day. He will cut off the palm branch and the reed.

**15** The old and important leaders are the head. The prophets who teach lies are the tail.

**16** The leaders of these people cause them to go the wrong way. The people who follow them go to destruction.

**17** Thus the Lord is not happy with the young men. He will not show mercy to the children with no father and the widows. All the people are godless and evil. Each mouth speaks foolish things. But after all this, the anger of the LORD will not stop. His hand is still ready to punish.

**18** Evil burns as a fire. It burns the thorns and weeds. It burns the thick trees of the forest. Thick smoke goes up.

**19** The anger of the LORD of armies burns the land. The people are as fuel for the fire. No man shows mercy to his brother.

**20** People will take food on the right but they will still be hungry. They will eat on the left but they will still want more. Each man will eat the flesh of his own arm.

**21** Manasseh will fight Ephraim. Ephraim will fight Manasseh. Together they will fight Judah. But after all this, the anger of the LORD will not stop. His hand is still ready to punish.

## Chapter 10

**1** You are in very bad trouble, you who make unfair laws! You write rules that cause pain.

**2** You do not give justice to the poor. You take the rights of the poor people of God. You steal from widows. You rob children with no father.

**3** What will you do on the day of punishment? What will you do when disaster comes from far away? To whom will you run for help? Where will you put your riches?

**4** You will bow down among the prisoners. You will fall among the dead. But after all this, the anger of the LORD will not stop. His hand is still ready to punish.

**5** "Assyria, you are in very bad trouble! Assyria is the rod of my anger. The stick in the hand of Assyria is my anger.

**6** I send Assyria against a godless nation. I order Assyria to attack the people that make me angry. I tell Assyria to take their goods. Assyria will walk on them as on mud in the streets.

**7** But the king of Assyria does not think this. That is not his plan. He only wants to destroy many nations.

**8** He says, 'All my commanders are as kings.

**9** I defeated Calno, as I defeated Carchemish. I defeated Hamath, as I defeated Arpad. I defeated Samaria, as I defeated Damascus.

**10** I defeated the kingdoms of the idols. Their idols were more than the idols of Jerusalem and Samaria.

**11** I destroyed Samaria and its idols. I will do the same to Jerusalem and its idols.'"

**12** The Lord will finish all his work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem. Then he will say, "I will punish the king of Assyria for his proud heart. I will punish him for his arrogant look.

**13** He says, 'I did this with my own strength. I did it with my wisdom, because I am clever. I removed the borders of nations. I took their treasures. I defeated their kings as a strong bull.

**14** I took the riches of the nations, as a person takes eggs from a nest. I took all the earth, as a person takes eggs that a bird left. No bird moved its wings or opened its mouth to make a noise.'"

**15** Can an ax be prouder than the man who uses it? Can a saw be greater than the man who cuts with it? A rod cannot lift the man who holds it! A stick of wood cannot lift a person!

**16** Thus the Lord, the LORD of armies, will send a disease among the strong soldiers of Assyria. Their bodies will become thin. A fire will burn under their glory.

**17** The Light of Israel will become a fire. The Holy One of Israel will become a flame. In 1 day he will burn the thorns and weeds of Assyria.

**18** He will completely destroy the beautiful forests and the fertile fields of Assyria. Assyria will become weak as a sick man.

**19** Only a few trees of its forest will stay. A child will be able to count them.

**20** On that day the people of Israel who stay alive will not trust Assyria again. The people of Jacob who escape will not trust the nation that defeated them. They will truly trust the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.

**21** A small number of people will come back. A small number of the people of Jacob will come back to the Mighty God.

**22** Israel, your people are as many as the sand of the sea. But only a small number will come back. God decided to destroy the nation, and his decision is fair.

**23** The Lord GOD of armies will destroy all the land, as he decided.

**24** Thus the Lord GOD of armies says, "My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrians. They hit you with a rod. They lift a stick against you, as Egypt did.

**25** But very soon my anger against you will stop. Then I will turn my anger against them and destroy them."

**26** The LORD of armies will hit them with a whip. He will do this as he defeated Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will lift his rod over the sea, as he did in Egypt.

**27** On that day the LORD will remove the heavy load of Assyria from your shoulder. He will remove their yoke from your neck. The yoke will break because you will become strong.

**28** The Assyrian army comes to Aiath. It goes through Migron. It keeps its supplies at Michmash.

**29** The soldiers go through the pass. They stay at Geba for the night. The people of Ramah are afraid. The people of Gibeah of Saul run away.

**30** Shout loudly, people of Gallim! Listen, people of Laish! Poor people of Anathoth!

**31** The people of Madmenah run away. The people of Gebim look for a place to hide.

**32** Today the army will stop at Nob. The king of Assyria will shake his fist at Mount Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

**33** Look! The Lord, the LORD of armies, will cut off the branches with great power. He will cut down the tall trees. He will make the high trees fall.

**34** He will cut down the thick forest with an ax. Lebanon will fall in front of the Mighty One.

## Chapter 11

**1** A new shoot will grow from the stump of Jesse. A Branch will grow from his roots and give fruit.

**2** The Spirit of the LORD will stay on him. It is the Spirit of wisdom and insight. It is the Spirit of good advice and power. It is the Spirit of knowledge and respect for the LORD.

**3** He will be happy when he obeys the LORD. He will not judge by what he sees with his eyes. He will not decide by what he hears with his ears.

**4** He will judge the poor fairly. He will make fair decisions for the humble people of the earth. His words will be as a rod that punishes the earth. With his breath he will kill the evil people.

**5** He will wear righteousness as a belt. He will wear faithfulness as a belt around his waist.

**6** The wolf will live with the lamb. The leopard will lie down with the young goat. The calf, the young lion, and the fat cattle will be together. A small child will lead them.

**7** The cow and the bear will eat together. Their young will lie down together. The lion will eat straw as the ox does.

**8** A baby will play near the hole of a cobra. A young child will put his hand into the nest of a poisonous snake.

**9** Nothing will hurt or destroy on all my holy mountain. The earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the water fills the sea.

**10** On that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a flag for the peoples. The nations will come to him. The place where he lives will be glorious.

**11** On that day the Lord will reach out his hand a second time. He will bring back the people of Israel who stay alive. He will bring them back from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.

**12** He will lift up a flag for the nations. He will bring together the people of Israel whom enemies sent away. He will collect the scattered people of Judah from the 4 corners of the earth.

**13** Ephraim will not be jealous again. The LORD will destroy the enemies of Judah. Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah. Judah will not be an enemy of Ephraim.

**14** Together they will attack the Philistines in the west. Together they will take the goods of the people of the east. They will take control of Edom and Moab. The people of Ammon will obey them.

**15** The LORD will dry up the bay of the Egyptian sea. He will move his hand over the Euphrates River with a hot wind. He will divide the river into 7 small streams. People will walk across it in sandals.

**16** There will be a road for his people who stay alive in Assyria. It will be as the road that Israel had when the people came out of Egypt.

## Chapter 12

**1** On that day you will say, "LORD, I will praise you! You were angry with me. But your anger stopped, and you comfort me.

**2** God is my salvation. I will trust him and I will not be afraid. The LORD God is my strength and my song. He saved me."

**3** You will be very happy when you get water from the wells of salvation.

**4** On that day you will say, "Praise the LORD! Call on his name! Tell the nations what he did! Tell them that his name is great!

**5** Sing to the LORD, because he did wonderful things! Let all the earth know about them!

**6** People of Zion, shout and sing with joy! The Holy One of Israel, who lives among you, is great!"

## Chapter 13

**1** This is the message about Babylon that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw.

**2** Lift up a flag on a bare hill! Call loudly to the soldiers! Wave your hand to them! Tell them to go in through the gates of the important people.

**3** I gave orders to my holy soldiers. I called my strong warriors to show my anger. They are proud and happy in my power.

**4** Listen to the noise on the mountains! It is the noise of a large crowd. It is the noise of kingdoms and nations that come together. The LORD of armies prepares an army for battle.

**5** The soldiers come from far countries, from the ends of the sky. The LORD and the weapons of his anger come to destroy the whole land.
