**6** Cry loudly, because the day of the LORD is near! It will come as destruction from the Almighty God.

**7** Thus all hands will become weak. All men will lose their courage.

**8** They will feel terror. Pain and sorrow will take hold of them. They will have pain as a woman who gives birth. They will look at each other in shock. Their faces will be red as fire.

**9** Look! The day of the LORD comes. It will be a cruel day of great anger. The LORD will make the land empty. He will destroy the sinners in it.

**10** The stars and the constellations will not give light. The sun will be dark when it rises. The moon will not shine.

**11** The LORD says, "I will punish the world for its evil. I will punish the evil people for their sins. I will stop the pride of proud people. I will make cruel people humble.

**12** I will make people more rare than pure gold. People will be more rare than the gold of Ophir.

**13** I will make the sky shake. The earth will move from its place. The LORD of armies will do this because he is very angry on that day.

**14** The people in Babylon will run as a deer that a hunter chases. They will be as sheep that have no shepherd. Each man will go back to his own people. Each man will run to his own land.

**15** The enemy will kill each person that they find. The sword will kill each person that they catch.

**16** The enemy will crush their babies while they watch. The enemy will rob their houses and rape their wives.

**17** Look! I will cause the Medes to attack Babylon. The Medes do not want silver. They do not want gold.

**18** Their bows will kill the young men. They will have no mercy on babies. They will not show pity to children.

**19** Babylon is the most beautiful kingdom. The Chaldeans are very proud of it. But God will destroy it as he destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.

**20** Nobody will live there again for all time. No Arab will put up his tent there. No shepherd will keep his sheep there.

**21** Only wild animals of the desert will stay there. Owls will fill the houses. Ostriches will live there. Wild goats will jump there.

**22** Hyenas will cry in its towers. Jackals will live in its beautiful palaces. The time of Babylon is near. Its days will not be long."

## Chapter 14

**1** The LORD will have mercy on Jacob. He will choose Israel again. He will put the people in their own land. Foreign people will join them. They will join the family of Jacob.

**2** Nations will take the people of Israel and bring them back to their own land. Then Israel will make those people its servants in the land of the LORD. The people of Israel will capture the people who captured them. They will rule the people who were cruel to them.

**3** The LORD will give you rest from your pain, trouble, and hard work. He will free you from the slavery that you suffered.

**4** On that day you will sing this song against the king of Babylon: "The cruel king came to an end! His anger stopped!

**5** The LORD broke the rod of the evil people. He broke the power of the cruel rulers.

**6** The king of Babylon hit the nations in anger. He did not stop. He ruled the nations in anger. He attacked them all the time.

**7** Now all the earth has rest and peace. The people start to sing.

**8** Even the pine trees and the cedars of Lebanon are happy that you fell. They say, 'Since you fell, nobody comes to cut us down.'

**9** The place of the dead (Sheol) below is full of excitement to meet you when you come. It wakes up the dead to meet you. It wakes up all the leaders of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations get up from their thrones.

**10** They all will say to you, 'Now you are weak, as we are! You became the same as us!'

**11** Your glory and the music of your harps went down to the place of the dead. Maggots are your bed. Worms are your blanket.

**12** You fell from the sky, morning star, son of the dawn! You defeated nations, but now God cuts you down to the ground!

**13** You said in your heart, 'I will go up to heaven. I will put my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mountain where the gods meet, far in the north.

**14** I will go up above the tops of the clouds. I will be the same as the Most High God.'

**15** But God brought you down to the place of the dead (Sheol). He brought you down to the bottom of the pit.

**16** The people who see you will look at you closely. They will think about you and say, 'Is this the man who made the earth shake? Is this the man who made kingdoms afraid?

**17** He made the world into a desert. He destroyed its cities. He did not let his prisoners go home.'

**18** All the kings of the nations lie in honor. Each king lies in his own tomb.

**19** But God throws you out of your tomb as a branch that nobody wants. Dead soldiers that swords killed cover you. You will go down to the stones of the pit. You are as a dead body that people walk on.

**20** You will not have a burial with the other kings. You destroyed your land and you killed your people. Nobody will remember the children of evil people.

**21** Prepare to kill the sons of the king because of the sins of their fathers. Do not let them take control of the earth. Do not let them fill the world with their cities."

**22** The LORD of armies says, "I will attack Babylon. I will destroy the name of Babylon and the people who stay alive. I will destroy its children and its descendants," says the LORD.

**23** "I will make Babylon a place for owls. I will make it a swamp. I will sweep it away with a broom of destruction," says the LORD of armies.

**24** The LORD of armies made a promise. He said, "My plan will happen. What I decided will occur.

**25** I will break the Assyrian army in my land. I will crush his soldiers on my mountains. I will remove his yoke from my people. I will remove his heavy load from their shoulders."

**26** This is the plan for the whole earth. The hand of the LORD is ready to punish all the nations.

**27** The LORD of armies made his plan. Nobody can stop it. His hand is ready to punish. Nobody can turn it back.

**28** This message came in the year that King Ahaz died.

**29** People of Philistia, do not be happy that the rod that hit you is now in pieces. A more dangerous snake will come from the root of that snake. Its child will be a snake that flies, with poison as fire.

**30** The poorest people will have food. The needy people will lie down in safety. But I will kill your root with hunger. I will kill your people who stay alive.

**31** Cry, gates! Shout, city! People of Philistia, you will lose all your courage! Smoke comes from the north. It is an army, and no soldier leaves his place.

**32** What will we tell the messengers of that nation? We will tell them, "The LORD built Zion. His poor people will find a safe place there."

## Chapter 15

**1** This is the message about Moab. In 1 night enemies destroyed the city of Ar in Moab. In 1 night enemies destroyed the city of Kir in Moab.

**2** The people of Moab go up to the temple and to Dibon. They go to the high places to cry. They cry about Nebo and Medeba. They shave all their heads. They cut off all their beards.

**3** In the streets they wear rough cloth (sackcloth). On the roofs and in the public places they all cry. They cry very much.

**4** The people of Heshbon and Elealeh cry out. People hear their voices as far as Jahaz. Thus the soldiers of Moab shout. They are very afraid.

**5** My heart cries for Moab. Its people run away to Zoar and to Eglath-Shelishiyah. They cry as they go up the hill to Luhith. On the road to Horonaim they cry about their destruction.

**6** The water of Nimrim dries up. The grass dies. Nothing green stays.

**7** Thus the people carry their riches across the Valley of Willows. They carry all the things that they saved.

**8** Their cries go around all the borders of Moab. People hear them as far as Eglaim and Beer-Elim.

**9** The water of Dimon is full of blood. But I will bring more trouble on Dimon. I will send a lion against the people of Moab who escape. I will send it against the people who stay in the land.

## Chapter 16

**1** People of Moab, send a lamb as a gift to the ruler of the land. Send it from Sela across the desert to the mountain of Zion.

**2** The women of Moab are at the places where people cross the Arnon River. They are as birds that fell out of their nest.

**3** "Give us advice. Make a decision. Give us shade, as the night gives shade at noon. Hide the people who run away. Do not tell the enemy about the refugees.

**4** Let the refugees from Moab live with you. Hide them from the destroyer." The cruel ruler will come to an end. The destruction will stop. The attackers will go away from the land.

**5** Then God will make a throne strong with love. A faithful king will sit on it, from the family of David. He will judge fairly. He will look for justice. He will be quick to do what is right.

**6** We heard about the pride of Moab. Moab is very proud. Its people are arrogant and full of anger. But their boasts are not true.

**7** Thus the people of Moab cry. They all cry together for Moab. They cry and mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir-Hareseth.

**8** The fields of Heshbon die. The vines of Sibmah die. The rulers of the nations broke the best vines. The vines went as far as Jazer and into the desert. Their shoots went across the sea.

**9** Thus I cry with the people of Jazer for the vines of Sibmah. Heshbon and Elealeh, my tears fall on you. The shouts of joy for your summer fruit and your harvest stopped.

**10** Joy and happiness are gone from the good fields. Nobody sings or shouts in the vineyards. Nobody crushes grapes in the winepresses. I stopped the shouts of the harvest.

**11** Thus my heart cries for Moab as the sad music of a harp. My inner body cries for Kir-Hareseth.

**12** The people of Moab will go to their high places to worship. They will become tired there. They will go to their temple to pray. But their prayers will not help them.

**13** The LORD spoke this message about Moab in the past.

**14** But now the LORD says, "In exactly 3 years, the glory of Moab will come to an end. A hired worker counts the years of his contract exactly. In 3 years, the people of Moab will have no honor. Only a few of them will stay alive. They will be weak."

## Chapter 17

**1** This is the message about Damascus. Look! Damascus will not be a city again. It will become a pile of ruins.

**2** The people will leave the cities of Aroer. Flocks of sheep will lie down there. Nobody will make them afraid.

**3** The strong cities of Ephraim will be gone. Damascus will lose its kingdom. The people of Syria who stay alive will lose their glory, as the people of Israel did, says the LORD of armies.

**4** "On that day the glory of Jacob will become small. His fat body will become thin.

**5** It will be as when a farmer collects the grain in the field. He cuts the heads of grain with his arm. It will be as when a person collects the grain that remains in the Valley of Rephaim.

**6** But a few people will stay, as a few olives stay on a tree after people shake it. 2 or 3 olives stay at the top of the highest branch. 4 or 5 olives stay on the outer branches," says the LORD, the God of Israel.

**7** On that day people will look to God, who made them. They will look to the Holy One of Israel.

**8** They will not look to the altars that their hands made. They will not trust the Asherah poles or the incense altars that their fingers made.

**9** On that day their strong cities will be empty, as the forests and hilltops that the Amorites left when Israel came. Everything will be in ruins.

**10** You forgot God, who saves you. You did not remember the Rock, who is your strength. So you plant beautiful gardens. You plant vines from foreign countries.

**11** You make your plants grow on the day that you plant them. You make them flower in the morning. But you will get no harvest. You will have only sickness and pain that nobody can cure.

**12** The many nations are in very bad trouble! They roar as the sea roars. The peoples make a loud noise as strong waters.

**13** The nations roar as the noise of large waters. But when God speaks strongly to them, they run far away. The wind blows them as dry grass on the hills. A storm blows them as dust.

**14** In the evening there is terror. Before the morning, the enemies are gone. This is what happens to the people who rob us. This is the result for the people who steal from us.

## Chapter 18

**1** The land where insects buzz is in very bad trouble! That land is on the other side of the rivers of Cush.

**2** It sends messengers on the Nile River in boats made of reeds. Go, quick messengers, to a tall people with smooth skin. Go to a people that all nations fear. They are a strong nation that defeats other nations. Rivers divide their land.

**3** All you people of the world, look when a flag goes up on the mountains! Listen when the trumpet sounds!

**4** The LORD said to me, "I will wait quietly and watch from the place where I live. I will be calm, as the heat on a sunny day. I will be calm, as the dew on a hot harvest day."

**5** Before the harvest, when the flowers are gone and the grapes become ripe, he will cut off the shoots with knives. He will cut away the branches that spread.

**6** He will leave the bodies of the soldiers for the birds of the mountains and the wild animals. The birds will eat them during the summer. The wild animals will eat them during the winter.

**7** At that time the tall people with smooth skin will bring gifts to the LORD of armies. All nations fear this strong people, which defeats other nations. Rivers divide their land. They will bring the gifts to Mount Zion, the place of the name of the LORD of armies.

## Chapter 19

**1** This is the message about Egypt. Look! The LORD comes on a fast cloud to Egypt. The idols of Egypt shake in front of him. The Egyptians lose their courage.

**2** "I will make the Egyptians fight against each other. Brothers will fight brothers. Neighbors will fight neighbors. Cities will fight cities. Kingdoms will fight kingdoms.

**3** The Egyptians will lose their courage. I will spoil their plans. They will ask their idols, the ghosts, the mediums, and the people who speak with the dead for help.

**4** I will give the Egyptians to a cruel master. A strong king will rule them," says the Lord, the LORD of armies.

**5** The water of the Nile will dry up. The river will become completely dry.

**6** The channels will smell bad. The streams of Egypt will become low and dry. The reeds and the rushes will die.

**7** The plants along the Nile and at its mouth will die. All the crops in the fields near the Nile will dry up. The wind will blow them away. Nothing will stay.

**8** The fishermen will cry. All the people who fish with hooks in the Nile will mourn. The people who throw nets on the water will become weak.

**9** The people who make linen from flax will lose hope. The people who weave fine cloth will be afraid.

**10** The workers who make cloth will be sad. All the hired workers will be unhappy.

**11** The leaders of Zoan are foolish. The wise advisors of Pharaoh give stupid advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am one of the wise men. I am a descendant of the old kings"?

**12** Pharaoh, where are your wise men now? Let them tell you what the LORD of armies plans against Egypt.

**13** The leaders of Zoan became foolish. The leaders of Memphis believe lies. The leaders of the tribes of Egypt cause Egypt to go the wrong way.

**14** The LORD gave them a spirit of confusion. They cause Egypt to go the wrong way in all that it does. Egypt is as a drunk man who walks unsteadily in his vomit.

**15** Nobody in Egypt can do anything to help. The leaders and the common people cannot help.

**16** On that day the Egyptians will be weak as women. They will shake with fear when the LORD of armies lifts his hand against them.

**17** The land of Judah will make the Egyptians terrified. All the people who hear the name of Judah will be afraid. They will be afraid of the plan that the LORD of armies made against them.

**18** On that day 5 cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan. They will promise to be loyal to the LORD of armies. People will call 1 of these cities the City of Destruction.

**19** On that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of Egypt. There will be a monument to the LORD at its border.

**20** It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of armies in the land of Egypt. The Egyptians will cry to the LORD because cruel people attack them. Then the LORD will send them a savior who will defend them and rescue them.

**21** The LORD will show himself to the Egyptians. On that day they will know the LORD. They will worship him with sacrifices and offerings. They will make promises to the LORD and they will keep them.

**22** The LORD will punish Egypt. Then he will heal Egypt. The Egyptians will turn back to the LORD. He will hear their prayers and he will heal them.

**23** On that day there will be a road from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will go to Egypt. The Egyptians will go to Assyria. The Egyptians and the Assyrians will worship together.

**24** On that day Israel will be the third nation with Egypt and Assyria. Israel will be a blessing to the whole earth.

**25** The LORD of armies will bless them. He will say, "I bless Egypt, my people. I bless Assyria, the nation that I made. I bless Israel, my own possession."

## Chapter 20

**1** Sargon, the king of Assyria, sent his commander to Ashdod. The commander attacked Ashdod and captured it.

**2** At that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah the son of Amoz. The LORD said, "Remove the rough cloth (sackcloth) from your body. Remove the sandals from your feet." Isaiah obeyed. He walked around with no clothes and no sandals.

**3** Then the LORD said, "My servant Isaiah walked with no clothes and no sandals for 3 years. This is a sign and a wonder against Egypt and Cush.

**4** The king of Assyria will take away the people of Egypt and Cush as prisoners. He will take the young and the old. They will have no clothes and no sandals. Their buttocks will be bare. This will bring shame to Egypt.

**5** The people who trusted Cush will be afraid. The people who were proud of Egypt will feel shame.

**6** On that day the people who live on this coast will say, 'Look what happened to the nations that we trusted! We ran to them for help against the king of Assyria. How can we escape now?'"

## Chapter 21

**1** This is the message about the desert by the sea. An enemy comes from the desert, from a terrible land. It comes as a storm that moves across the south.

**2** God showed me a terrible vision. I saw a traitor who betrays. I saw a destroyer who destroys. Elam, attack! Media, surround the city! I will stop all the pain that Babylon caused.

**3** Thus my body is full of pain. Pain takes hold of me as the pain of a woman who gives birth. What I hear makes me weak. What I see makes me afraid.

**4** My heart beats fast. I shake with fear. I wanted a calm evening, but now I feel terror.

**5** They prepare the table. They put out the rugs. They eat and drink. Get up, commanders! Put oil on your shields!

**6** The Lord said to me, "Go and put a guard in his place. Let him tell what he sees.

**7** He will see chariots with pairs of horsemen. He will see riders on donkeys and riders on camels. He must watch very carefully."

**8** Then the guard shouted as a lion, "My lord, I stand on the watchtower each day. I stay at my place every night.

**9** Look! A man comes in a chariot with a pair of horses." Then the man said, "Babylon fell! Babylon fell! All the idols of its gods lie broken on the ground!"

**10** My people, enemies crushed you as grain on a floor where people beat the grain. I told you what I heard from the LORD of armies, the God of Israel.

**11** This is the message about Dumah. Someone calls to me from Seir, "Guard, how much of the night remains? Guard, how much of the night remains?"

**12** The guard says, "The morning comes, but the night comes again. If you want to ask, ask. Then come back again."

**13** This is the message about Arabia. Groups of travelers from Dedan, you will stay the night in the thick bushes of Arabia.

**14** People of Tema, bring water to the thirsty people. Bring food to the people who run away.

**15** They run from the swords. They run from the swords that are ready to kill. They run from the bows that are ready to shoot. They run from the terrible battle.

**16** The Lord said to me, "In exactly 1 year, all the glory of Kedar will end. A hired worker counts the years of his contract exactly.

**17** Only a few of the soldiers of Kedar with bows will stay alive." The LORD, the God of Israel, says this.

## Chapter 22

**1** This is the message about the Valley of Vision. What is wrong with you? Why did all of you go up to the roofs?

**2** The city is full of noise. It is a happy city full of parties. But your dead did not die by the sword. They did not die in battle.

**3** All your leaders ran away together. The enemy captured them before they could use a bow. The enemy captured all the people that it found, while they ran far away.

**4** Thus I say, "Do not look at me. Let me cry bitterly. Do not try to comfort me. Enemies destroyed my people."

**5** The Lord GOD of armies brings a day of terror and confusion in the Valley of Vision. The enemy breaks down the walls. The people shout to the mountains for help.

**6** The soldiers of Elam carry bags of arrows. They come with chariots and horses. The soldiers of Kir take the covers off their shields.

**7** Chariots fill your best valleys. Horsemen get ready at the gates of the city.

**8** God removed the protection of Judah. On that day you looked to the weapons in the Palace of the Forest.

**9** You saw that the walls of the City of David had many holes. You collected water in the lower pool.

**10** You counted the houses of Jerusalem. You broke down houses to make the wall stronger.

**11** You made a pool between the 2 walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to God, who made it. You did not respect him, who planned it long ago.

**12** On that day the Lord GOD of armies told you to cry and mourn. He told you to shave your heads and wear rough cloth (sackcloth).

**13** But look! You are happy and have parties. You kill cattle and sheep. You eat meat and drink wine. You say, "We will eat and drink, because tomorrow we will die!"

**14** The LORD of armies told me this: "I will not forgive this sin until you die," says the Lord GOD of armies.

**15** The Lord GOD of armies says, "Go to Shebna, the manager of the palace. Tell him,

**16** 'What are you doing here? Who gave you permission to cut a tomb for yourself here? You cut your tomb on a high place. You cut a grave for yourself in the rock.

**17** Look! The LORD will throw you away violently, strong man. He will take hold of you.

**18** He will roll you up as a ball. He will throw you into a large country. You will die there. Your beautiful chariots will stay there. You bring shame on the house of your master!

**19** I will remove you from your office. God will pull you down from your position.

**20** On that day I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah.

**21** I will put your robe on him. I will put your belt on him. I will give him your authority. He will be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the family of Judah.

**22** I will give him the key of the house of David. When he opens a door, nobody can shut it. When he shuts a door, nobody can open it.

**23** I will make him firm, as a peg that a man hammers into a strong wall. He will bring honor to the family of his father.

**24** All the members of his family will depend on him. His children and his relatives will be as small pots and bowls that hang from a peg.'"

**25** The LORD of armies says, "On that day the peg in the strong wall will become loose. It will break and fall. Everything that hangs on it will fall." The LORD says this.

## Chapter 23

**1** This is the message about Tyre. Cry, ships of Tarshish! Enemies destroyed Tyre. No house or harbor stays. The sailors got the news on the island of Cyprus.

**2** Be silent, you people who live on the coast. The merchants of Sidon traveled across the sea and made you rich.

**3** Ships brought grain from Egypt across the large sea. The harvest of the Nile was the income of Tyre. Tyre was the market of the nations.

**4** Feel shame, Sidon! The sea speaks. The strong fortress of the sea says, "I did not have pain to give birth. I did not give birth to children. I did not raise sons or daughters."

**5** When the news comes to Egypt, the Egyptians will be very sad about Tyre.

**6** Go across the sea to Tarshish! Cry, you people who live on the coast!

**7** Is this your happy city? Tyre is a very old city. Its people traveled to far lands to live there.

**8** Who planned this against Tyre? Tyre gave crowns to kings. Its merchants were as princes. Its traders were famous on the earth.

**9** The LORD of armies planned it. He wanted to stop their pride in their glory. He wanted to make all the famous people of the earth humble.

**10** People of Tarshish, go through your land as the Nile goes. You have no harbor now.

**11** The LORD lifted his hand over the sea. He made the kingdoms shake. He gave an order against Phoenicia to destroy its fortresses.

**12** He said, "You will not be happy again, people of Sidon. You are as a young woman whom an enemy attacked. Get up and go across the sea to Cyprus. Even there you will have no rest."

**13** Look at the land of the Chaldeans! That nation does not exist now. The Assyrians made it a place for wild animals. They built siege towers against Babylon. They destroyed its palaces. They made it a ruin.

**14** Cry, ships of Tarshish! Enemies destroyed your fortress.

**15** On that day people will forget Tyre for 70 years. That is the life of 1 king. After 70 years, Tyre will be as the prostitute in the song:

**16** "Take a harp and walk around the city, you prostitute that people forgot. Play the harp well. Sing many songs, so that people will remember you."

**17** After 70 years, the LORD will help Tyre again. Tyre will start to trade again. It will sell its goods to all the kingdoms of the earth, as a prostitute sells herself.

**18** But the money that Tyre earns will belong to the LORD. Tyre will not keep it or save it. The money will buy food and fine clothes for the people who serve the LORD.

## Chapter 24

**1** Look! The LORD will make the earth empty and destroy it. He will damage its surface. He will scatter its people.

**2** The same thing will happen to all people. It will happen to the priests and the people. It will happen to the servants and their masters. It will happen to the women servants and their mistresses. It will happen to the buyers and the sellers. It will happen to the lenders and the borrowers. It will happen to the people who owe money and to the people who get money.

**3** The earth will be completely empty. All its riches will be gone. The LORD spoke this message.

**4** The earth dries up and dies. The world becomes weak and dies. The important people of the earth become weak.

**5** The people of the earth made it dirty. They did not obey the laws. They changed the rules. They broke the covenant that God made to last always.

**6** Thus a curse destroys the earth. Its people must suffer for their guilt. Thus fire burns the people of the earth. Only a few people stay alive.

**7** The new wine dries up. The vines die. All the happy people are sad.

**8** The happy sound of the tambourines stops. The noise of the people at parties ends. The happy music of the harp stops.

**9** People do not drink wine with songs. Beer is bitter for the people who drink it.

**10** The ruined city falls down. People lock the doors of all the houses. Nobody can go in.

**11** People in the streets shout for wine. All joy changes to sadness. All happiness goes from the land.

**12** The city is in ruins. The enemy breaks down its gates.

**13** This is what will happen on the earth among the nations. Only a few people will stay, as a few olives stay on a tree after people shake it. They will be as the few grapes that stay after the harvest.

**14** The people who stay alive will shout with joy. From the west they will sing about the greatness of the LORD.

**15** Thus give glory to the LORD in the east. Give glory to the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, on the islands of the sea.

**16** We hear songs from the ends of the earth: "Glory to the Righteous One!" But I say, "I am weak! I am weak! I am in very bad trouble! Traitors betray. Traitors betray very badly."

**17** People of the earth, terror, pits, and traps wait for you.

**18** The person who runs from the noise of terror will fall into a pit. A trap will catch the person who climbs out of the pit. The windows of the sky open for a flood. The foundations of the earth shake.

**19** The earth breaks apart. The earth splits open. The earth shakes very much.

**20** The earth moves unsteadily as a drunk man. It moves as a hut in the wind. The guilt of its sin is heavy on it. It will fall and it will not get up again.

**21** On that day the LORD will punish the powers in the sky above. He will punish the kings on the earth below.

**22** He will put them together as prisoners in a pit. He will lock them in a prison. After a long time, he will punish them.

**23** The moon will feel shame. The sun will feel shame. The LORD of armies will rule as king on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem. He will show his glory to the leaders of his people.

## Chapter 25

**1** LORD, you are my God. I will honor you and praise your name. You did wonderful things. You planned them long ago, and you did them faithfully.

**2** You made the city a pile of stones. You made the strong city a ruin. You destroyed the palace of foreign people. Nobody will build it again.

**3** Thus strong nations will give you glory. The cities of cruel nations will respect you.

**4** You are a safe place for the poor. You are a safe place for the needy people in their trouble. You are a shelter from the storm and shade from the heat. The attacks of cruel people are as a storm against a wall.

**5** They are as the heat in a desert. But you stop the noise of the foreign people. A cloud makes shade and stops the heat. In the same way, you stop the song of the cruel people.

**6** On this mountain the LORD of armies will make a feast for all peoples. He will give them the best food and the best old wine. He will give them the best meat and the finest wine.

**7** On this mountain he will remove the cloth of sadness that covers all peoples. He will remove the cloth that covers all nations.

**8** He will destroy death for all time. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from all faces. He will remove the shame of his people from all the earth. The LORD says this.

**9** On that day people will say, "Look! This is our God! We trusted him, and he saved us. This is the LORD! We trusted him. We will be happy and full of joy because he saves us."

**10** The hand of the LORD will protect this mountain. But he will crush Moab under his feet, as people walk on straw in manure.

**11** The people of Moab will spread out their hands in it, as a man spreads his hands when he swims. But the LORD will stop their pride. He will remove the skill of their hands.

**12** He will break down the high, strong walls of Moab. He will throw them down to the ground. He will put them in the dust.

## Chapter 26

**1** On that day the people in the land of Judah will sing this song: "We have a strong city. God protects its walls.

**2** Open the gates and let the righteous nation come in. It is a nation that stays faithful.

**3** LORD, you give complete peace to the people who always think about you. They trust you.

**4** Trust the LORD always. The LORD God is a Rock that will always stay.

**5** He makes proud people humble. He destroys the high city. He throws it down to the ground. He puts it in the dust.

**6** The poor and the needy people walk over it."

**7** The path of the righteous people is level. LORD, you are fair. You make their path smooth.

**8** LORD, we wait for you to judge. We want to honor your name. We want to remember you.

**9** At night I want you. In the morning my spirit looks for you. When you judge the earth, the people of the world learn to do what is right.

**10** You show kindness to evil people, but they do not learn to do what is right. Even in a land of honest people, they continue to do wrong. They do not see the greatness of the LORD.

**11** LORD, your hand is ready to punish, but they do not see it. Let them see how you love your people, and let them feel shame. Let the fire that you keep for your enemies burn them.

**12** LORD, you give us peace. All the good things that we do, you do for us.

**13** LORD our God, other masters ruled over us. But we only honor your name.

**14** Those masters are dead now. They will not live again. Their spirits will not get up. You punished them and destroyed them. You made people forget them.

**15** LORD, you made our nation larger. You made our nation larger, and you got glory for yourself. You made the borders of the land wider.

**16** LORD, in their trouble they looked for you. When you punished them, they could only whisper prayers.

**17** A pregnant woman has pain and cries out when she is near the time of the birth. LORD, we were the same because of you.

**18** We were pregnant and had pain. But we gave birth only to wind. We did not save the land. We did not bring new people into the world.

**19** But your dead people will live again. Their bodies will get up. You who lie in the dust, wake up and shout with joy! Your dew is as the dew of the morning. The earth will give birth to its dead.

**20** My people, go into your rooms. Close the doors behind you. Hide for a short time until the anger of the LORD stops.

**21** Look! The LORD comes from his place to punish the people of the earth for their sins. The earth will show the blood that people spilled on it. It will not hide the people that others killed.

## Chapter 27

**1** On that day the LORD will use his hard, large, strong sword. He will punish Leviathan, the snake that moves fast. He will punish Leviathan, the snake that twists. He will kill the monster of the sea.

**2** On that day, sing about a good vineyard:

**3** "I, the LORD, protect it. I water it all the time. I guard it day and night, so that nobody can damage it.

**4** I am not angry with it. If I find thorns and weeds, I will fight against them. I will burn them all.

**5** But if they want my protection, let them make peace with me. Let them make peace with me."

**6** In the days to come, the people of Jacob will put down roots. Israel will grow buds and flowers. They will fill the whole world with fruit.

**7** Did the LORD hit Israel as he hit the enemies of Israel? Did he kill the people of Israel as he killed their enemies?

**8** No, he punished Israel when he sent the people away. He removed them with his strong wind, as on a day when the east wind blows.

**9** In this way the LORD will forgive the guilt of Jacob. The result will be that he removes the sin of Jacob. The people will crush the stones of the altars to powder, as chalk. No Asherah poles or incense altars will stay.

**10** The strong city is empty. Nobody lives in it. It is as a desert. Calves eat grass there. They lie down there and they eat the branches.

**11** When the branches are dry, they break off. Women make fires with them. The people do not understand. Thus God, who made them, will not show them mercy. He who made them will not be kind to them.

**12** On that day the LORD will collect his people as a farmer collects grain. He will collect them from the Euphrates River to the stream of Egypt. People of Israel, he will collect you 1 by 1.

**13** On that day someone will blow a large trumpet. The people who almost died in Assyria will come back. The people whom enemies sent away to Egypt will come back. They will worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

## Chapter 28

**1** Samaria is in very bad trouble! Samaria is the proud crown of the drunk people of Ephraim. Its beauty is as a flower that dies. The city is on the hill above a fertile valley. Its people are drunk with wine.

**2** Look! The Lord has a person who is strong and powerful. He is as a storm of hail and a destructive wind. He is as a flood of strong water. He will throw Samaria down to the ground.

**3** The enemy will walk on the proud crown of the drunk people of Ephraim.

**4** Samaria is beautiful, on the hill above a fertile valley. But it is as a flower that dies. It is as an early fig before the summer. A person sees it, takes it, and eats it immediately.

**5** On that day the LORD of armies will be a beautiful crown for his people who stay alive. He will be a beautiful crown of glory for them.

**6** He will give a spirit of justice to the people who judge. He will give strength to the soldiers who push back the enemy at the gate.

**7** But the leaders of Judah also walk unsteadily because of wine. Beer makes them confused. The priests and the prophets are drunk with beer and wine. They walk unsteadily because of beer. They make mistakes when they see visions. They make mistakes when they decide cases.

**8** Vomit covers all their tables. No place is clean.

**9** The leaders say, "Who is this man to teach us? To whom does he explain his message? Does he teach babies who stopped their mother's milk?

**10** He tells us one rule after another rule, one line after another line. He teaches a little here and a little there."

**11** So God will speak to these people through foreign people with strange languages.

**12** God told them, "This is the place of rest. Let the tired people rest. This is the place of peace." But they did not listen.

**13** So the word of the LORD to them will be one rule after another rule, one line after another line. It will be a little here and a little there. Thus they will fall back and break. A trap will catch them.

**14** Thus hear the word of the LORD, you men who laugh at God! You rule these people in Jerusalem.

**15** You say, "We made a covenant with death. We made an agreement with the place of the dead. The flood of disaster will not touch us when it comes. We use lies as our safe place. We hide behind lies."

**16** Thus the Lord GOD says, "Look! I put a stone in Zion as a foundation. It is a tested stone, a valuable cornerstone. It is a strong foundation. The person who believes will not be afraid.

**17** I will use justice as a line to measure. I will use righteousness as a plumb line. Hail will remove your safe place of lies. Water will flood the place where you hide.

**18** Your covenant with death will end. Your agreement with the place of the dead will fail. When the flood of disaster comes, it will crush you.

**19** Each time it comes, it will take you. It will come each morning, during the day and during the night." When you understand this message, you will feel terror.

**20** You will be as a man whose bed is too short for him. His blanket is too narrow to cover him.

**21** The LORD will get up and fight as he did at Mount Perazim. He will be angry as he was in the Valley of Gibeon. He will do his work, his strange work. He will do his task, his unusual task.

**22** So do not laugh at God. If you do not stop, your chains will become stronger. I heard the Lord GOD of armies. He decided to destroy the whole land.

**23** Listen to me. Hear what I say. Pay attention.

**24** A farmer does not plow his field all the time. He does not dig and break up the ground all the time.

**25** He makes the ground level. Then he plants the seeds of dill and cumin. He plants wheat in rows and barley in its place. He plants spelt at the edge of the field.

**26** His God teaches him the correct way to do these things.

**27** A farmer does not use a heavy tool to crush dill. He does not roll a wheel over cumin. He hits dill with a stick. He hits cumin with a rod.

**28** He crushes grain to make bread. But he does not crush it for all time. He does not crush it to powder with the wheels of his cart and his horses.

**29** The LORD of armies also teaches this. His advice is wonderful. His wisdom is great.

## Chapter 29

**1** Ariel is in very bad trouble! Ariel is the city where David lived. Continue to have your festivals each year. Continue to make your sacrifices.

**2** But I will attack Ariel. The city will cry and mourn. It will be as an altar where people burn sacrifices.

**3** I will put my army around you. I will put towers around you. I will build ramps against your walls.

**4** God will throw you down. You will speak from the ground. Your words will be low, from the dust. Your voice will be as the voice of a ghost from the ground. You will whisper from the dust.

**5** But your many enemies will become as fine dust. The cruel armies will be as straw that the wind blows away. This will happen suddenly.

**6** The LORD of armies will come with thunder, an earthquake, and a loud noise. He will come with a storm, a strong wind, and a fire that burns everything.

**7** Then the armies of all the nations that fight against Ariel will disappear as a dream. They attack the city and its fortress. They make the city suffer. But they will be as a dream in the night.

**8** A hungry man dreams that he eats. But when he wakes up, he is still hungry. A thirsty man dreams that he drinks. But when he wakes up, he is still weak and thirsty. The armies of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion will be the same.

**9** Stop and feel surprise! Make yourselves blind, and stay blind! You are drunk, but not from wine. You walk unsteadily, but not from beer.

**10** The LORD made you sleep deeply. He closed your eyes, which are the prophets. He covered your heads, which are the seers.

**11** All this vision is as the words of a book with a seal for you. People give the book to a man who can read. They say, "Please read this." But he says, "I cannot, because the book has a seal."

**12** Then people give the book to a man who cannot read. They say, "Please read this." But he says, "I cannot read."

**13** The Lord says, "These people come to me with their mouths. They honor me with their lips. But their hearts are far from me. Their worship of me is only rules that men taught them.

**14** Thus I will again do wonderful things to these people. I will do wonderful and strange things. The wisdom of their wise men will disappear. The insight of their clever men will go away."

**15** You are in very bad trouble, you who try to hide your plans from the LORD! You do your work in the dark. You say, "Who sees us? Who will know?"

**16** You make everything upside down. You think that the potter is the same as the clay! Can a thing that a man made say to him, "He did not make me"? Can a pot say to the potter, "He does not understand anything"?

**17** In a very short time, Lebanon will become a fertile field. The fertile field will become a forest.

**18** On that day deaf people will hear the words of the book. Blind people will see. Their eyes will see out of the gloom and the darkness.

**19** Humble people will be happy in the LORD again. The poor people will be full of joy in the Holy One of Israel.

**20** The cruel people will be gone. The people who laugh at God will disappear. The LORD will destroy all the people who plan evil.

**21** They make false statements against people in court. They put traps for people who defend justice at the city gate. They tell lies to refuse justice to innocent people.

**22** Thus the LORD, who saved Abraham, says this about the family of Jacob: "The people of Jacob will not feel shame again. Their faces will not become pale with fear again.

**23** They will see their children, whom I made, among them. Then they will honor my name as holy. They will honor the Holy One of Jacob. They will respect the God of Israel with fear.

**24** The people with confused minds will understand. The people who complain will learn the truth."

## Chapter 30

**1** The LORD says, "My stubborn children are in very bad trouble! They make plans, but not my plans. They make agreements, but not by my Spirit. They add sin to sin.

**2** They go down to Egypt, but they do not ask me. They look for protection from Pharaoh. They want to hide in the shade of Egypt.

**3** But the protection of Pharaoh will bring shame on you. The shade of Egypt will bring disgrace on you.

**4** Your officials went to Zoan. Your messengers went to Hanes.

**5** But they will all feel shame because of a people that cannot help them. Egypt will give no help or advantage. It will only bring shame and disgrace."

**6** This is the message about the animals of the Negev. The messengers go through a land of trouble and danger. In that land there are lions and poisonous snakes and snakes that fly. The messengers carry their riches on the backs of donkeys. They carry their treasures on the humps of camels. They take them to a nation that cannot help them.

**7** The help of Egypt has no value. Thus I call Egypt "Rahab who does nothing."

**8** Now go and write this on a tablet for them. Write it in a book. It will be a witness for all time in the future.

**9** These people are stubborn. They are children who tell lies. They refuse to hear the law of the LORD.

**10** They tell the seers, "Do not see visions!" They tell the prophets, "Do not tell us what is true! Tell us nice things. Tell us false things.

**11** Go away from the correct path. Do not tell us about the Holy One of Israel again!"

**12** Thus the Holy One of Israel says, "You refuse this message. You trust in cruelty and lies. You depend on them.

**13** Thus this sin will be as a crack in a high wall. The wall bends out, and it is ready to fall. Suddenly it will fall down in an instant.

**14** It will break as a clay pot that someone breaks into pieces. No piece will be large enough to carry coals from a fire. No piece will be large enough to take water from a well."

**15** The Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, says, "Turn back to me and be calm, and I will save you. Be quiet and trust me, and you will be strong." But you refused.

**16** You said, "No, we will run away on horses." So you will run away! You said, "We will ride fast horses." So the people who chase you will be fast!

**17** 1,000 of you will run away when 1 enemy shouts. All of you will run away when 5 enemies shout. Only a few of you will stay, as a flagpole alone on top of a mountain. You will be as a flag alone on a hill.

**18** But the LORD waits to be kind to you. He gets up to show you mercy. The LORD is a God of justice. All the people who wait for him are blessed.

**19** People of Zion who live in Jerusalem, you will not cry again. The LORD will be kind to you when you cry for help. When he hears you, he will answer you.

**20** The Lord will give you trouble as your bread and pain as your water. But your Teacher will not hide again. You will see your Teacher with your eyes.

**21** When you turn to the right or to the left, you will hear a voice behind you. It will say, "This is the correct way. Walk on it."

**22** Then you will treat your idols of silver and gold as dirty things. You will throw them away as dirty cloths. You will tell them, "Go away!"

**23** Then the LORD will give you rain for the seed that you plant in the ground. The land will give you much good food. On that day your cattle will eat grass in large fields.

**24** The oxen and donkeys that plow the ground will eat good food. Farmers will clean the food for them with a shovel and a fork.

**25** On that day there will be streams of water on every high mountain and every hill. On that day the enemies will kill many people, and the towers will fall.

**26** The moon will be as bright as the sun. The sun will be 7 times brighter, as the light of 7 days. This will happen on the day when the LORD puts bandages on his people. He will heal the wounds that he gave them.

**27** Look! The LORD comes from far away. His anger burns. Thick smoke comes up. His lips are full of anger. His tongue is as a fire that burns everything.

**28** His breath is as a flood that comes up to the neck. He will shake the nations in a sieve of destruction. He will put a bridle in the mouths of the peoples to lead them to ruin.

**29** But you will sing, as on the night of a holy festival. Your hearts will be happy, as people who walk to the music of a flute. They go to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.

**30** The LORD will make people hear his glorious voice. He will show his arm as it comes down in anger. He will come with a fire that burns everything. He will come with a storm, rain, and hail.

**31** The voice of the LORD will break the Assyrians. He will hit them with his rod.

**32** Each time the LORD hits them with his rod, his people will play tambourines and harps. The LORD will fight against the Assyrians with his strong arm.

**33** Long ago God prepared a place to burn the king of Assyria. It is deep and wide. It has much fire and wood. The breath of the LORD will start the fire, as a stream of sulfur that burns.

## Chapter 31

**1** The people who go down to Egypt for help are in very bad trouble! They depend on horses. They trust in their many chariots and their strong horsemen. But they do not look to the Holy One of Israel. They do not ask the LORD for help.

**2** But the LORD is wise. He will bring disaster. He will not change what he said. He will attack the evil people. He will attack the people who help them.

**3** The Egyptians are humans, not God. Their horses are animals, not spirits. When the LORD lifts his hand, Egypt will fall. The people that Egypt helps will also fall. They will all die together.

**4** The LORD said to me, "A lion growls over the animal that it killed. Many shepherds come together and shout at it. But the lion is not afraid of their shouts. It does not run away from their noise. In the same way, the LORD of armies will come down to fight for Mount Zion and its hill.

**5** Birds fly over their nests to protect them. In the same way, the LORD of armies will protect Jerusalem. He will defend the city and save it. He will pass over it and rescue it."

**6** People of Israel, you turned far away from the LORD. Come back to him!

**7** On that day each of you will throw away your idols of silver and gold. Your sinful hands made them.

**8** "Assyria will fall by a sword, but not the sword of a man. A sword, but not the sword of a human, will kill the Assyrians. They will run away from the sword. Their young men will become slaves.

**9** Their strong fortress will fall because of terror. Their commanders will see the battle flag and they will have much fear," says the LORD. His fire is in Zion. His furnace is in Jerusalem.

## Chapter 32

**1** Look! A king will rule with righteousness. Leaders will rule with justice.

**2** Each of them will be as a shelter from the wind and a safe place from the storm. They will be as streams of water in the desert. They will be as the shade of a large rock in a dry land.

**3** Then the eyes of the people who see will not close. The ears of the people who hear will listen.

**4** The people who do things quickly without thought will understand. The people who cannot speak well will speak clearly.

**5** People will not call a fool noble. People will not respect a dishonest man.

**6** A fool says foolish things. His mind plans evil. He does wicked things. He says wrong things about the LORD. He does not give food to hungry people. He does not give water to thirsty people.

**7** A dishonest man uses evil methods. He makes evil plans. He destroys the poor with lies, even when the poor man is right.

**8** But a noble man makes noble plans. He stays firm because of his noble actions.

**9** You women who feel safe, get up and listen to me! You women who have no worries, listen to what I say!

**10** In a little more than a year you will be afraid, you who have no worries. The grape harvest will fail. The fruit harvest will not come.

**11** Shake with fear, you women who feel safe! Be afraid, you who have no worries! Remove your fine clothes. Put rough cloth (sackcloth) around your waists.

**12** Beat your chests and cry for the good fields and the fruitful vines.

**13** Cry for the land of my people. Thorns and weeds will grow there. Cry for all the happy houses in this happy city.

**14** The people will leave the palace. The busy city will be empty. The fortress and the watchtower will become caves for all time. Wild donkeys will play there. Flocks of sheep will eat grass there.

**15** This will continue until God pours his Spirit on us from heaven. Then the desert will become a fertile field. The fertile field will become as a forest.

**16** Justice will live in the desert. Righteousness will stay in the fertile field.

**17** Righteousness will bring peace. Righteousness will bring calm and safety for all time.

**18** My people will live in peaceful homes. They will live in safe houses and in quiet places of rest.

**19** But hail will destroy the forest. The city will be completely flattened.

**20** You are blessed, you who plant seeds near every stream. You let your cattle and donkeys walk free.

## Chapter 33

**1** You destroyer, you are in very bad trouble! Nobody destroyed you. You traitor, nobody betrayed you. When you stop your destruction, someone will destroy you. When you stop your betrayal, someone will betray you.

**2** LORD, be kind to us. We wait for you. Be our strength each morning. Save us in times of trouble.

**3** The peoples run away when they hear your loud voice. The nations scatter when you get up.

**4** Your enemies will collect the goods of the nations as young locusts collect food. They will jump on the goods as locusts jump.

**5** The LORD is great. He lives in heaven. He will fill Zion with justice and righteousness.

**6** He will make your times safe. He will give you much salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. Respect for the LORD is the treasure of Zion.

**7** Look! The brave soldiers cry in the streets. The messengers who wanted peace cry bitterly.

**8** The roads are empty. No travelers go on them. The enemy broke the agreement. He hates the witnesses. He does not respect anybody.

**9** The land mourns and becomes weak. Lebanon feels shame and it dies. Sharon is as a desert. The trees of Bashan and Carmel lose their leaves.

**10** "Now I will get up," says the LORD. "Now I will show my greatness. Now I will show my power.

**11** Your plans are as dry grass. Your actions are as straw. Your breath is a fire that will burn you.

**12** The fire will burn the peoples to powder. They will burn as thorns that people cut and throw into the fire.

**13** You people who are far away, hear what I did. You people who are near, know my power."

**14** The sinners in Zion are afraid. The godless people shake with fear. They say, "Who among us can live with this fire that burns everything? Who among us can live with this fire that always burns?"

**15** The person who does what is right and speaks honestly can live there. He refuses money that people get by cruel actions. He does not take bribes. He refuses to listen to plans of murder. He closes his eyes so that he does not see evil.

**16** That person will live in a high place. The rocks of the mountains will be his fortress. He will always have food. He will always have water.

**17** Your eyes will see the king in his beauty. You will see a land that extends far away.

**18** You will think about your terror in the past. You will say, "Where is the officer who counted the money? Where is the officer who weighed the tax? Where is the officer who counted the towers?"

**19** You will not see those proud foreign people again. You will not hear their strange language. You did not understand what they said.

**20** Look at Zion, the city of our festivals! Your eyes will see Jerusalem as a calm place to live. It will be as a tent that nobody moves. Nobody will pull up its tent pegs. Nobody will break its ropes.

**21** There the LORD will show us his great power. Zion will be as a place of wide rivers and streams. But no enemy ships with oars will go on them. No large ships will sail there.

**22** The LORD is our judge. The LORD gives us our laws. The LORD is our king. He will save us.

**23** The ropes of the enemy ships are loose. They cannot hold the mast firmly. They cannot open the sail. Then the people of Zion will divide much loot. Even lame people will take loot.

**24** Nobody who lives in Zion will say, "I am sick." God will forgive the sins of the people who live there.

## Chapter 34

**1** Come near, nations, and hear! Listen, peoples! Let the earth and all the things in it listen! Let the world and all the things that come from it listen!

**2** The LORD is angry with all the nations. He is very angry with all their armies. He will completely destroy them. He will give them to their killers.

**3** Their dead bodies will lie on the ground. The bodies will smell bad. Their blood will flow down the mountains.

**4** All the stars in the sky will disappear. The sky will roll up as a scroll. All the stars will fall as leaves fall from a vine. They will fall as dry figs fall from a fig tree.

**5** The LORD says, "My sword is ready in the sky. Look! It will come down on Edom to judge it. It will come down on the people that I decided to destroy."

**6** Blood and fat cover the sword of the LORD. It has the blood of lambs and goats. It has the fat from the kidneys of rams. The LORD will make a sacrifice in Bozrah. He will kill many people in the land of Edom.

**7** Wild oxen will die with them. Young bulls and strong bulls will die. Blood will cover the land. Fat will cover the ground.

**8** The LORD has a day of revenge. It is a year when he will pay back the enemies of Zion.

**9** The streams of Edom will become tar. Its dust will become sulfur that burns. Its land will become tar that burns.

**10** The fire will burn day and night. Nobody will stop it. Its smoke will go up always. The land will be empty for all generations. Nobody will travel through it again.

**11** Desert owls and hedgehogs will take control of it. Large owls and ravens will live there. God will measure Edom with a line of destruction. He will use a plumb line to make it empty.

**12** Its important people will have no kingdom to rule. All its leaders will disappear.

**13** Thorns will grow in its palaces. Weeds and thorn bushes will grow in its fortresses. It will be a home for jackals and a place for ostriches.

**14** Desert animals will meet with hyenas. Wild goats will call to each other. Night animals will rest there and find a place to stay.

**15** Owls will make their nests there. They will lay eggs and hatch their young. They will protect their young under their wings. Hawks will also come there, each with its mate.

**16** Look in the book of the LORD and read it. None of these animals will be absent. Each animal will have its mate. The LORD gave the order. His Spirit will bring the animals together.

**17** He divided the land and gave each animal its part. He measured the land for them with a line. They will own the land for all time. They will live there for all generations.

## Chapter 35

**1** The desert and the dry land will be happy. The wilderness will be full of joy and it will flower as a crocus.

**2** It will be full of flowers. It will shout and sing with joy. God will give it the beauty of Lebanon. He will give it the glory of Carmel and Sharon. The people will see the glory of the LORD and the greatness of our God.

**3** Make the weak hands strong. Make the weak knees firm.

**4** Tell the people who are afraid, "Be strong! Do not be afraid! Look, your God will come. He will take revenge on your enemies. He will pay them back. He will come and save you."

**5** Then the eyes of blind people will open. The ears of deaf people will hear.

**6** Then lame people will jump as a deer. People who cannot speak will shout with joy. Water will flow in the desert. Streams will flow in the dry land.

**7** The hot sand will become a pool. The dry ground will have springs of water. Grass, reeds, and rushes will grow in the places where jackals lived.

**8** A road will go through that land. People will call it "The Way of Holiness." Unclean people will not travel on it. It will be only for the people of God. Even foolish people will not go the wrong way on it.

**9** No lion will be there. No dangerous animal will come on it. The people whom the LORD saved will walk on it.

**10** The people whom the LORD rescued will come back. They will come to Zion with songs. Joy will be on their heads always. They will be happy and full of joy. Sadness and tears will go away.

## Chapter 36

**1** In the 14th year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, attacked all the strong cities of Judah. He captured them.

**2** The king of Assyria sent his field commander from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem. The commander came with a large army. He stopped at the water channel of the upper pool. It is on the road to the field where people wash cloth.

**3** Eliakim the son of Hilkiah came out to meet him. Eliakim was the manager of the palace. Shebna the secretary and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder, also came out.

**4** The field commander said to them, "Tell Hezekiah this. The great king, the king of Assyria, says: 'Why are you so confident?

**5** You say that you have plans and power for war. But your words have no value. Whom do you trust? Why do you turn against me?

**6** Look! You trust Egypt. But Egypt is as a broken reed. If a man leans on it as a stick, it will cut his hand. Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, is the same for all the people who trust him.

**7** But maybe you will tell me, "We trust the LORD our God." But Hezekiah removed the high places and the altars of the LORD! He told Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship at this altar."

**8** Now make an agreement with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you 2,000 horses, if you can find riders for them!

**9** You cannot defeat even 1 officer, the least important of the servants of my master. Why do you trust Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

**10** Did I come to attack and destroy this land without the LORD? No! The LORD told me to attack this land and destroy it.'"

**11** Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the field commander, "Please speak to your servants in the Aramaic language. We understand it. Do not speak to us in the Hebrew language. The people on the wall can hear you."

**12** But the field commander said, "My master did not send me to speak these words only to your master and to you. He sent me to speak to the men who sit on the wall. They also will eat their own excrement and drink their own urine, as you will."

**13** Then the field commander stood up and shouted in Hebrew. He said, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!

**14** The king says: Do not let Hezekiah trick you. He cannot save you.

**15** Do not let Hezekiah make you trust the LORD. He says, 'The LORD will save us. The king of Assyria will not capture this city.'

**16** Do not listen to Hezekiah! The king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat fruit from your own vine and your own fig tree. Each of you will drink water from your own well.

**17** Then I will come and take you to a land that is the same as your land. It is a land of grain and new wine. It is a land of bread and vineyards.

**18** Do not let Hezekiah trick you when he says, 'The LORD will save us.' The gods of the other nations did not save their lands from the king of Assyria.

**19** Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they save Samaria from me?

**20** None of the gods of these lands saved its land from me. So how can the LORD save Jerusalem from me?"

**21** But the people were silent. They did not say anything, because King Hezekiah told them, "Do not answer him."

**22** Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, the manager of the palace, went to Hezekiah. Shebna the secretary and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder, went with him. They tore their clothes. They told Hezekiah what the field commander said.

## Chapter 37

**1** When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes. He put on rough cloth (sackcloth). He went into the temple of the LORD.

**2** He sent Eliakim, the manager of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the leaders of the priests to the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz. They all wore rough cloth.

**3** They said to Isaiah, "Hezekiah says: Today is a day of trouble, punishment, and shame. We are as a woman who is ready to give birth. But she has no strength to give birth to the baby.

**4** The king of Assyria sent his field commander to insult the God who lives. Possibly the LORD your God will hear his words. Possibly he will punish him for the words that the LORD your God heard. Thus pray for the people who stay alive."

**5** The officials of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

**6** Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master: The LORD says, 'Do not be afraid of the words that you heard. The servants of the king of Assyria insulted me with these words.

**7** Listen! I will put a spirit in the king of Assyria. He will hear a report and go back to his own country. I will make him die by the sword in his own country.'"

**8** The field commander heard that the king of Assyria left Lachish. So he went back and found the king. The king fought against Libnah.

**9** Then the king of Assyria got news that Tirhakah, the king of Cush, came to fight against him. When he heard this, he sent messengers to Hezekiah. He told them,

**10** "Tell Hezekiah, the king of Judah: Do not let the God that you trust trick you. Do not believe him when he says, 'The king of Assyria will not capture Jerusalem.'

**11** Look! You heard what the kings of Assyria did to all the countries. They destroyed them completely. Do you think that you will escape?

**12** My ancestors destroyed the nations of Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph. They destroyed the people of Eden who lived in Telassar. The gods of these nations did not save them.

**13** Where is the king of Hamath? Where is the king of Arpad? Where are the kings of the cities of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?"

**14** Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the temple of the LORD. He opened the letter in front of the LORD.

**15** Hezekiah prayed to the LORD. He said,

**16** "LORD of armies, God of Israel, you sit on your throne above the cherubim. Only you are God of all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.

**17** LORD, listen and hear. LORD, open your eyes and see. Hear all the words that Sennacherib sent to insult the God who lives.

**18** LORD, it is true that the kings of Assyria destroyed all these nations and their lands.

**19** They threw the gods of these nations into the fire. But those were not gods. They were only wood and stone that men made with their hands. Thus the Assyrians destroyed them.

**20** Now, LORD our God, save us from the king of Assyria. Then all the kingdoms of the earth will know that only you are the LORD."

**21** Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah. He said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says: You prayed to me about Sennacherib, the king of Assyria.

**22** This is the message that the LORD speaks against him: 'The young woman, Zion, hates you and laughs at you. The city of Jerusalem shakes her head at you.

**23** Whom did you insult? Against whom did you speak bad words? Against whom did you shout with pride? You did this against the Holy One of Israel!

**24** You used your servants to insult the Lord. You said, "With my many chariots I went up to the tops of the mountains. I went up to the highest parts of Lebanon. I cut down its tallest cedar trees and its best pine trees. I went to its highest places and its best forests.

**25** I dug wells and I drank water in foreign lands. With my feet I dried up all the streams of Egypt."

**26** Did you not hear? Long ago I planned this. In the past I decided it. Now I made it happen. I let you make strong cities into piles of stones.

**27** Their people had no power. They were afraid and ashamed. They were as grass in the field and as young plants. They were as grass on a roof that dries up before it grows.

**28** But I know where you stay. I know when you go out and when you come in. I know how angry you are with me.

**29** You are angry with me and proud. I heard it. So I will put my hook in your nose. I will put my bridle in your mouth. I will make you go back on the road that you came on.'

**30** Hezekiah, this will be a sign for you: This year you will eat the grain that grows by itself. Next year you will eat the grain that grows from that grain. But in the third year you will plant seeds and collect the harvest. You will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

**31** The people of Judah who stay alive will again put roots down into the ground. They will give fruit above the ground.

**32** A small number of people will go out from Jerusalem. A group of survivors will come from Mount Zion. The strong love of the LORD of armies will do this.

**33** Thus the LORD says this about the king of Assyria: 'He will not come into this city. He will not shoot an arrow here. He will not come near it with shields. He will not build a ramp against its walls.

**34** He will go back on the road that he came on. He will not come into this city,' says the LORD.

**35** 'I will defend this city and save it. I will do this for my own honor and for my servant David.'"

**36** Then the angel of the LORD went out. He killed 185,000 soldiers in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up early in the morning, they saw that all the soldiers were dead.

**37** So Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, went away. He went back to Nineveh and stayed there.

**38** One day he worshipped in the temple of his god Nisroch. His sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with a sword. Then they escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon became king after him.

## Chapter 38

**1** At that time Hezekiah became very sick and almost died. The prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz came to him. He said, "The LORD says: Put everything in your house in order, because you will die. You will not get well."

**2** Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.

**3** He said, "LORD, please remember that I was faithful to you. I served you with all my heart. I did what was good in your sight." Then Hezekiah cried very much.

**4** Then the LORD gave a message to Isaiah. He said,

**5** "Go and tell Hezekiah: The LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: I heard your prayer. I saw your tears. Look! I will give you 15 more years of life.

**6** I will save you and this city from the king of Assyria. I will defend this city.

**7** The LORD will give you this sign. It will show that the LORD will do what he promised:

**8** Look! I will make the shadow on the stairway of Ahaz go back 10 steps." So the shadow of the sun went back the 10 steps that it went down.

**9** Hezekiah, the king of Judah, wrote this after he was sick and got well:

**10** I said, "In the middle of my life I must go to the gates of the place of the dead (Sheol). I must lose the rest of my years."

**11** I said, "I will not see the LORD again in the land of the people who live. I will not see people again among the people who live in the world.

**12** Someone pulls down my life and takes it away from me, as a tent of a shepherd. My life ends, as a weaver cuts cloth from the loom. From day until night you bring me to an end.

**13** I waited calmly until morning. But he broke all my bones as a lion does. From day until night you bring me to an end.

**14** I cried as a swallow or a crane. I made sad sounds as a dove. My eyes became tired as I looked up to heaven. Lord, I am in trouble! Help me!

**15** But what can I say? He spoke to me, and he did it. I will walk humbly all my years because of the bitterness of my life.

**16** Lord, people live because of these things. My spirit also finds life in them. You made me healthy. You let me live.

**17** Look! My great bitterness was for my good. In your love you saved my life from the pit of destruction. You put all my sins behind your back.

**18** The dead in the grave cannot praise you. Death cannot sing praises to you. The people who go down into the pit cannot hope for your faithfulness.

**19** The people who live, only the people who live, praise you, as I do today. Fathers tell their children about your faithfulness.

**20** The LORD will save me. So we will play music on stringed instruments in the temple of the LORD. We will do this all the days of our lives."

**21** Isaiah said, "Make a paste of figs and put it on the sore. Then Hezekiah will get well."

**22** Hezekiah asked, "What will be the sign that I will go up to the temple of the LORD?"

## Chapter 39

**1** At that time Merodach-Baladan the son of Baladan, the king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah. He heard that Hezekiah was sick and that he got well.

**2** Hezekiah was happy and welcomed the messengers. He showed them his storehouse. He showed them the silver, the gold, the spices, and the expensive oil. He showed them his whole armory and all his treasures. Hezekiah showed them everything in his palace and in all his kingdom.

**3** Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah. He asked, "What did these men say? Where did they come from?" Hezekiah said, "They came to me from a far country. They came from Babylon."

**4** Isaiah asked, "What did they see in your palace?" Hezekiah said, "They saw everything in my palace. I showed them all my treasures."

**5** Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the message of the LORD of armies:

**6** Look! A time will come when people will take everything in your palace to Babylon. They will take all the treasures that your ancestors saved until now. Nothing will stay," says the LORD.

**7** "They will take some of your own sons, your descendants. Your sons will become servants (eunuchs) in the palace of the king of Babylon."

**8** Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The message of the LORD that you spoke is good." He thought, "There will be peace and safety during my life."

## Chapter 40

**1** "Comfort my people. Comfort them," says your God.

**2** "Speak kindly to the people of Jerusalem. Tell them that their hard service is at an end. Tell them that I forgave their sin. The LORD punished them 2 times for all their sins."

**3** A voice calls, "Prepare a road for the LORD in the wilderness! Make a straight road in the desert for our God!

**4** Fill every valley. Make every mountain and hill low. Make the rough ground level. Make the hilly places flat.

**5** Then the glory of the LORD will appear. All people will see it together. The LORD himself says this."

**6** A voice says, "Call out!" I said, "What must I call out?" "All people are as grass. All their beauty is as the flowers in the field.

**7** The grass dries up and the flowers die, when the breath of the LORD blows on them. Truly, the people are as grass.

**8** The grass dries up and the flowers die. But the word of our God will stay always."

**9** Zion, you bring good news. Go up on a high mountain. Jerusalem, you bring good news. Shout it loudly! Shout it, and do not be afraid! Tell the cities of Judah, "Here is your God!"

**10** Look! The Lord GOD comes with power. He rules with his strong arm. Look! He brings his reward with him. He brings the people that he won.

**11** He takes care of his flock as a shepherd. He collects the lambs in his arms. He carries them close to his heart. He gently leads the sheep that have young.

**12** Who measured the water of the sea in his hand? Who measured the sky with his fingers? Who put all the dust of the earth in a basket? Who weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills on a balance?

**13** Who can know the Spirit of the LORD? Who can be his advisor and teach him?

**14** God did not ask anyone for advice. Nobody taught him the correct path. Nobody gave him knowledge. Nobody showed him the way of wisdom.

**15** Look! The nations are as a drop of water in a bucket. They are as dust on a scale. He lifts the islands as fine dust.

**16** All the trees of Lebanon are not sufficient for the fire on his altar. All the animals of Lebanon are not sufficient for a burnt offering.

**17** All the nations are as nothing in front of him. He thinks that they are less than nothing. They have no value to him.

**18** To whom can you compare God? What image can you compare with him?

**19** A worker makes an idol from metal. A goldsmith covers it with gold. He makes silver chains for it.

**20** A poor man cannot give that much. So he chooses wood that will not rot. He looks for a skilled worker to make an idol that will not fall over.

**21** Do you not know? Did you not hear? Did nobody tell you from the start? Do you not understand how God made the earth?

**22** God sits on his throne above the circle of the earth. The people on the earth are as grasshoppers to him. He spreads out the sky as a curtain. He spreads it out as a tent to live in.

**23** He makes rulers into nothing. He makes the judges of the world as nothing.

**24** They are as new plants. As soon as they start to grow, he blows on them. Then they dry up. The wind takes them away as straw.

**25** "To whom can you compare me? Who is equal to me?" says the Holy One.

**26** Look up at the sky. Who made all the stars? He leads them out as an army, and he counts them. He calls each star by its name. His power is great and his strength is strong. Thus not 1 star is absent.

**27** People of Jacob, why do you complain? People of Israel, why do you say, "The LORD does not see my trouble. My God does not give me justice"?

**28** Do you not know? Did you not hear? The LORD is the eternal God. He made all the earth. He does not become weak or tired. Nobody can know how great his wisdom is.

**29** He gives strength to tired people. He gives more power to weak people.

**30** Even young people become tired and weak. Young men fall down.

**31** But the people who trust the LORD will get new strength. They will fly high as eagles. They will run and not become tired. They will walk and not become weak.

## Chapter 41

**1** "Islands, be silent in front of me! Let the nations get new strength. Let them come near and speak. We will meet together in court.

**2** Who caused the man from the east to come? Who called him to serve with righteousness? The LORD gives nations to him and makes him defeat kings. His sword makes them as dust. His bow blows them away as straw.

**3** He chases them and goes on safely. He goes on a road where his feet did not go before.

**4** Who did this? Who caused the generations to start from the beginning? I, the LORD, did it. I was there at the start. I will be there at the end. I am God.

**5** The islands saw it and they were afraid. The ends of the earth shook with fear. They came near.
