**4** Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them. Then they ran away. They went out of the city at night by the path of the garden of the king. They went through the gate between the 2 walls. They went toward the Jordan Valley.

**5** But the army of the Chaldeans chased them. The army caught Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They captured him and took him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah, in the land of Hamath. There Nebuchadnezzar judged Zedekiah.

**6** At Riblah the king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah in front of him. The king of Babylon also killed all the important men of Judah.

**7** Then he removed the eyes of Zedekiah. He put bronze chains on Zedekiah to take him to Babylon.

**8** The Chaldeans burned the palace of the king and the houses of the people. They broke down the walls of Jerusalem.

**9** Then Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took the people who stayed in the city to Babylon as prisoners. He also took the people who went over to him and all the other people who stayed.

**10** But Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, let some of the poor people stay in the land of Judah. These people had nothing. At that time he gave them vineyards and fields.

**11** Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon gave commands about Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard. He said,

**12** "Take Jeremiah and take good care of him. Do not hurt him. Do for him what he asks you."

**13** Thus Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, sent for Jeremiah. Nebushazban the chief officer, Nergal-Sharezer the high official and all the officials of the king of Babylon also sent for him.

**14** They took Jeremiah out of the courtyard of the guard. They gave him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, to take him home. Thus Jeremiah lived among the people.

**15** While Jeremiah was a prisoner in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD came to him. The LORD said,

**16** "Go and speak to Ebed-Melech from Ethiopia. Tell him, 'The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this: Look! I will do to this city what I said. I will bring disaster and not good. On that day you will see it happen.

**17** But I will rescue you on that day,' says the LORD. 'I will not give you to the men that you are afraid of.

**18** I will certainly save you. The sword will not kill you. You will stay alive, because you trust in me,' says the LORD."

## Chapter 40

**1** The word came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, released him at Ramah. Nebuzaradan found Jeremiah in chains among all the prisoners from Jerusalem and Judah. The enemy took these prisoners to Babylon.

**2** The commander of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, "The LORD your God said that this disaster will come to this place.

**3** Now the LORD caused it to happen. He did what he said. This happened because you people sinned against the LORD. You did not obey him.

**4** But today I release you from the chains on your hands. If you want to come with me to Babylon, come. I will take good care of you. But if you do not want to come with me to Babylon, then do not come. Look, all the land is in front of you. Go where you think is good and right."

**5** Jeremiah did not go away yet. Thus Nebuzaradan said, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan. The king of Babylon made him governor of the cities of Judah. Live with him among the people. Or go to any other place that you want." Then the commander of the guard gave Jeremiah food and a gift and let him go.

**6** Thus Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. Jeremiah lived with him among the people who stayed in the land.

**7** Some army commanders and their men were still in the fields. They heard that the king of Babylon made Gedaliah son of Ahikam governor of the land. They heard that the king gave Gedaliah charge of the men, women and children who did not go to Babylon. These were the poorest people of the land.

**8** Thus these commanders and their men came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth. They were also the sons of Ephai from Netophah and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite.

**9** Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, made a promise to them and their men. He said, "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon. Then things will go well for you.

**10** I will live at Mizpah. I will speak for you to the Chaldeans who come to us. But you must collect wine, summer fruit and olive oil. Put them in your jars. Live in the towns that you took."

**11** All the Jews in Moab, Ammon, Edom and all the other countries heard the news. They heard that the king of Babylon let some people stay in Judah. They heard that he made Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, governor over them.

**12** Thus all these Jews came back from all the places where they went. They came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They collected very much wine and summer fruit.

**13** Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders who were in the fields came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.

**14** They said to him, "Do you know that Baalis king of the Ammonites sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

**15** Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke in secret to Gedaliah at Mizpah. He said, "Please let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah. No person will know. Why must Ishmael kill you? If he kills you, all the Jews who gathered around you will scatter. The rest of the people of Judah will die."

**16** But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this! What you say about Ishmael is not true."

## Chapter 41

**1** In the 7th month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, came with 10 men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. Ishmael was from the royal family. He was one of the officers of the king. They ate a meal together at Mizpah.

**2** Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the 10 men with him got up. They killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword. The king of Babylon made Gedaliah governor of the land, but Ishmael killed him.

**3** Ishmael also killed all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah. He also killed the Chaldean soldiers who were there.

**4** On the day after Ishmael killed Gedaliah, no person knew about it yet.

**5** Then 80 men came from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria. They shaved their beards, tore their clothes and cut themselves. They brought grain offerings and incense to the house of the LORD.

**6** Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them. He cried while he walked. When he met them, he said, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."

**7** The men went into the city. Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the men with him killed them. They threw the bodies into a well.

**8** But 10 of the men said to Ishmael, "Do not kill us! We have wheat, barley, olive oil and honey hidden in a field." Thus Ishmael did not kill them with the other men.

**9** Ishmael threw all the bodies of the men that he killed into a large well. King Asa made this well long ago to defend himself against Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled the well with the dead bodies.

**10** Then Ishmael took all the other people at Mizpah as prisoners. He took the daughters of the king and all the other people who stayed at Mizpah. Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, gave these people to the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them and started to go to the Ammonites.

**11** Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him heard about all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah did.

**12** Thus they took all their men and went to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They found him near the large pool at Gibeon.

**13** All the people with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and the army commanders with him. Then the people were glad.

**14** All the people that Ishmael took from Mizpah turned around. They went back to Johanan son of Kareah.

**15** But Ishmael son of Nethaniah and 8 of his men escaped from Johanan. They went to the Ammonites.

**16** Ishmael killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam. After that, Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him took all the people that they rescued from Ishmael at Mizpah. They brought these people back from Gibeon. The people were soldiers, women, children and palace officials.

**17** They went and stayed at Geruth Chimham, near Bethlehem. They wanted to go to Egypt.

**18** They wanted to escape from the Chaldeans. They were afraid of the Chaldeans, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam. The king of Babylon made Gedaliah governor of the land.

## Chapter 42

**1** Then all the army commanders came to Jeremiah. Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah and all the people came, from the least important to the most important.

**2** They said to the prophet Jeremiah, "Please listen to our request. Pray to the LORD your God for us, for all these people who stay alive. Before, we were many. But now only a few of us stay alive, as you can see.

**3** Pray that the LORD your God will tell us where we must go and what we must do."

**4** The prophet Jeremiah said to them, "I hear you. I will pray to the LORD your God as you ask. I will tell you all that the LORD answers. I will not hide anything from you."

**5** Then they said to Jeremiah, "We will do all that the LORD your God tells us through you. If we do not do this, let the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us.

**6** We will obey the LORD our God, to whom we send you. We will obey him if his message is good or bad. If we obey the LORD our God, then things will go well for us."

**7** After 10 days, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.

**8** Then Jeremiah called Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him. He called all the people, from the least important to the most important.

**9** He said to them, "You sent me to give your request to the LORD, the God of Israel. The LORD says this:

**10** 'If you stay in this land, I will build you up and not break you down. I will plant you and not pull you up. I am sorry for the disaster that I brought on you.

**11** Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon. You are afraid of him now, but do not be afraid,' says the LORD. 'I am with you to save you and rescue you from his power.

**12** I will show mercy to you. Thus the king of Babylon will show mercy to you. He will let you go back to your own land.'

**13** "But you possibly say, 'We will not stay in this land.' Possibly you will not obey the LORD your God.

**14** Possibly you will say, 'No! We will go to Egypt. There we will not see war. We will not hear the sound of the war trumpet. We will not be hungry. We will live there.'

**15** Then listen to the word of the LORD, you people of Judah who stay alive. The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this: 'If you decide to go to Egypt and live there,

**16** then the war that you are afraid of will catch you there in Egypt. The famine that you are afraid of will follow you to Egypt. You will die there.

**17** All the people who decide to go and live in Egypt will die by war, famine and disease. None of them will escape from the disaster that I will bring on them.'

**18** The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this: 'I showed my anger and fury against the people of Jerusalem. In the same way, I will show my fury against you when you go to Egypt. People will curse you and insult you. They will feel shock at you. You will never see this place again.'

**19** "Remaining people of Judah, the LORD tells you, 'Do not go to Egypt!' Know this clearly: I warn you today.

**20** You made a bad mistake when you sent me to the LORD your God. You said, 'Pray to the LORD our God for us. Tell us all that the LORD our God says, and we will do it.'

**21** Today I told you, but you do not obey the LORD your God. You do not obey anything that he sent me to tell you.

**22** Thus know this clearly: You will die by war, famine and disease in the place where you want to go and live."

## Chapter 43

**1** Jeremiah told all the people all the words of the LORD their God. The LORD sent him to tell them all these words. Jeremiah finished his message.

**2** Then Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah and all the proud men said to Jeremiah, "You tell lies! The LORD our God did not send you to say, 'Do not go to Egypt to live there.'

**3** Baruch son of Neriah causes you to speak against us. He wants to give us to the Chaldeans. Then they will kill us or take us to Babylon as prisoners."

**4** Thus Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders and all the people did not obey the LORD. They did not stay in the land of Judah.

**5** Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders took all the rest of the people of Judah. These people came back from all the nations where they went. They came back to live in the land of Judah.

**6** Johanan and the commanders took the men, the women, the children and the daughters of the king. Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, left these people with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan. Johanan and the commanders also took the prophet Jeremiah and Baruch son of Neriah.

**7** They went into the land of Egypt, because they did not obey the LORD. They went as far as Tahpanhes.

**8** At Tahpanhes the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah. The LORD said,

**9** "Take some large stones in your hands. Bury them in the clay of the brick floor at the entrance of the palace of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes. Do this while the men of Judah watch.

**10** Then say to them, 'The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this: Look! I will send for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I will put his throne over these stones that I buried here. He will put up his royal tent over them.

**11** He will come and attack Egypt. The people that I chose for death will die. The people that I chose to be prisoners will become prisoners. The people that I chose for the sword will die by the sword.

**12** I will start a fire in the temples of the gods of Egypt. Nebuchadnezzar will burn the temples and take the gods away. He will clean the land of Egypt as a shepherd cleans his coat. Then he will go away from there safely.

**13** He will break the stone pillars in the temple of the sun (Beth Shemesh) in Egypt. He will burn the temples of the gods of Egypt.'"

## Chapter 44

**1** This word came to Jeremiah about all the Jews who lived in Egypt. They lived at Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis and in the land of Pathros. The LORD said,

**2** "The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this. You saw all the disaster that I brought on Jerusalem and on all the cities of Judah. Today they are ruins. No people live in them.

**3** This is because of the evil that the people did. They made me angry. They burned incense and served other gods. They, you and your ancestors did not know those gods.

**4** I sent all my servants the prophets to you again and again. They said, 'Do not do this evil thing that I hate!'

**5** But the people did not listen or pay attention. They did not stop their evil. They did not stop. They continued to burn incense to other gods.

**6** Thus I showed my fury and anger. My anger burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Today they are empty ruins.

**7** "Now the LORD God of armies, the God of Israel, says this: Why do you do such great harm to yourselves? You will cause all the men, women, children and babies to die from among the people of Judah. None of your people will stay alive.

**8** Why do you make me angry with the idols that you make? You burn incense to other gods in Egypt, where you live now. Thus you will destroy yourselves. All the nations of the earth will curse you and insult you.

**9** Did you forget the evil that your ancestors did? Did you forget the evil that the kings of Judah and their wives did? Did you forget the evil that you and your wives did in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

**10** To this day, you do not make yourselves humble. You do not respect me. You do not obey my law and my rules that I gave to you and your ancestors.

**11** "Thus the LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this: Look! I decided to bring disaster on you. I will destroy all of Judah.

**12** The rest of the people of Judah decided to go to Egypt and live there. I will destroy them all in Egypt. They will die by war and famine. All of them will die, from the least important to the most important. People will curse them and insult them. People will feel shock at them.

**13** I punished Jerusalem with war, famine and disease. In the same way, I will punish the people who live in Egypt.

**14** None of the rest of the people of Judah who went to live in Egypt will escape. They want to go back and live in the land of Judah. But none of them will go back, only a few people who escape."

**15** Then all the men who knew that their wives burned incense to other gods answered Jeremiah. All the women who stood there also answered him. This was a large group. All the people who lived in Pathros in Egypt were there. They said,

**16** "We will not listen to the message that you speak to us in the name of the LORD.

**17** We will certainly do all that we promised. We will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven. We will pour out drink offerings to her. We, our ancestors, our kings and our officials did this in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. At that time we had much food. Things went well for us, and we had no trouble.

**18** But then we stopped. We did not burn incense to the Queen of Heaven. We did not pour out drink offerings to her. Since that time we have nothing. War and famine destroy us."

**19** The women said, "We burned incense to the Queen of Heaven. We poured out drink offerings to her. We made cakes with her picture on them. Our husbands knew and agreed to all these things."

**20** Then Jeremiah spoke to all the people, the men and the women, who gave him that answer. He said,

**21** "The LORD remembered the incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. You, your ancestors, your kings, your officials and the people of the land burned it. The LORD did not forget this.

**22** The LORD could not accept your evil actions and the evil things that he hates, which you did. Thus your land is an empty ruin today. People curse it and they feel shock at it. No people live in it.

**23** You burned incense and sinned against the LORD. You did not obey the LORD. You did not follow his law, his rules and his commands. Thus this disaster came to you, as you see today."

**24** Then Jeremiah spoke to all the people and to all the women. He said, "All you people of Judah in Egypt, listen to the word of the LORD.

**25** The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this: 'You and your wives do what you say. You said, "We will certainly do what we promised. We will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven. We will pour out drink offerings to her." Thus go and do what you promised! Keep your promises!

**26** But listen to the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who live in Egypt. The LORD says, "I make a promise by my great name. No person from Judah in all of Egypt will use my name again. No person will say, 'As surely as the Lord GOD lives.'

**27** Look! I watch over them to bring disaster and not good. All the people of Judah in Egypt will die by war and famine until all of them are dead.

**28** Only a few people will escape the sword. They will come back from Egypt to the land of Judah. Then all the rest of the people of Judah who went to live in Egypt will know whose words come true. They will know if my words or their words come true.

**29** This will be the sign to you," says the LORD, "that I will punish you in this place. Then you will know that my words against you will certainly come true.

**30** The LORD says this: Look! I will give Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt to his enemies who want to kill him. I did the same to Zedekiah king of Judah. I gave Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, who wanted to kill him."'"

## Chapter 45

**1** In the 4th year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, Baruch son of Neriah wrote the words of Jeremiah on a scroll. Then the prophet Jeremiah said this message to Baruch:

**2** "The LORD, the God of Israel, says this to you, Baruch:

**3** You said, 'I have much trouble! The LORD adds sorrow to my pain. I am weary from my cries. I find no rest.'

**4** Tell Baruch this: 'The LORD says this: I will break down what I built. I will pull up what I planted. I will do this in all the land.

**5** Do you want great things for yourself? Do not ask for them. Look! I will bring disaster on all people,' says the LORD. 'But I will let you stay alive in all the places where you go.'"

## Chapter 46

**1** This is the word of the LORD that came to the prophet Jeremiah about the nations.

**2** This is about Egypt. It is about the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt. His army was at Carchemish near the Euphrates River. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated this army in the 4th year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:

**3** "Prepare your small and large shields. Go into battle!

**4** Put the harnesses on the horses. Get on the horses, you riders! Stand in your positions with your helmets on. Make your spears sharp. Put on your armor!

**5** But what do I see? The soldiers are very afraid. They run back. The enemy beats down their strong soldiers. They run away fast and do not look back. There is terror on every side," says the LORD.

**6** "The fast soldiers cannot run away. The strong soldiers cannot escape. In the north, near the Euphrates River, they fall down.

**7** "Who is this that rises like the Nile River? Who is this that is like rivers with strong water?

**8** Egypt rises like the Nile. Egypt is like rivers with strong water. Egypt says, 'I will rise and cover the earth. I will destroy cities and their people.'

**9** Attack, horses! Drive fast, chariots! Let the soldiers go out! Let the men of Cush and Put who carry shields go out. Let the men of Lydia who use the bow go out.

**10** But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of armies. It is a day of punishment. On that day he will punish his enemies. The sword will kill until it is full. It will drink their blood until it is full. The Lord GOD of armies will kill his enemies like a sacrifice. This will be in the land of the north, near the Euphrates River.

**11** "Go up to Gilead and get medicine, people of Egypt. You use many medicines, but they are of no use. You will not become well.

**12** The nations hear about your shame. Your cries fill the earth. One strong soldier falls over another strong soldier. Both of them fall together."

**13** This is the word that the LORD spoke to the prophet Jeremiah. It is about the time when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon will come to attack Egypt:

**14** "Tell this in Egypt. Speak it in Migdol, Memphis and Tahpanhes. Say, 'Stand in your positions and be ready! The sword kills the people around you.'

**15** Why do your strong soldiers fall? They cannot stand, because the LORD pushes them down.

**16** Many of them fall. They fall over each other. They say, 'Get up! We must go back to our own people and our native land. We must escape from the cruel sword.'

**17** There they shout, 'Pharaoh king of Egypt is only a loud noise. He lost his chance.'

**18** "As surely as I live," says the King, whose name is the LORD of armies, "a strong enemy will come. He will be high like Mount Tabor among the mountains. He will be high like Mount Carmel over the sea.

**19** People of Egypt, prepare your bags to go away as prisoners. The enemy will destroy Memphis. It will be an empty ruin, and no people will live there.

**20** "Egypt is like a beautiful young cow. But an enemy comes from the north to attack her like a fly that bites.

**21** The soldiers that Egypt paid are like fat calves. They also turn and run away together. They do not stand to fight. This is because the day of their disaster comes. The time of their punishment comes.

**22** Egypt will make a sound like a snake that moves away. The enemy army comes. They attack Egypt with axes, like men who cut down trees.

**23** They will cut down her forest," says the LORD. "Her forest is very thick, but they will cut it down. The enemy soldiers are more than the locusts. No person can count them.

**24** Egypt will feel shame. The people of the north will defeat her."

**25** The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this: "Look! I will punish Amon, the god of Thebes. I will punish Pharaoh, Egypt, its gods and its kings. I will punish Pharaoh and all the people who trust in him.

**26** I will give them to the people who want to kill them. I will give them to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But after that, people will live in Egypt again, as in the past," says the LORD.

**27** "But do not be afraid, Jacob my servant. Do not be very afraid, Israel. Look! I will save you from a far place. I will save your descendants from the land where they are prisoners. Jacob will come back and have peace and safety. No person will cause him to be afraid.

**28** Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant," says the LORD, "because I am with you. I will fully destroy all the nations where I sent you. But I will not fully destroy you. I will punish you correctly. I will not let you be free from all punishment."

## Chapter 47

**1** This is the word of the LORD that came to the prophet Jeremiah about the Philistines. This was before Pharaoh attacked Gaza.

**2** The LORD says this: "Look! An enemy will come from the north like water that rises. It will be like a river that floods. It will cover the land and all that is in it. It will cover the cities and the people in them. The people will cry out. All the people of the land will cry loudly.

**3** They will hear the noise of the feet of the horses. They will hear the loud noise of the chariots and their wheels. The fathers will not turn back to help their children, because the fathers will be too weak.

**4** The day will come to destroy all the Philistines. It will come to kill all the people who could help Tyre and Sidon. The LORD will destroy the Philistines, the rest of the people from Caphtor (Crete).

**5** The people of Gaza will shave their heads in sorrow. The people of Ashkelon will be silent. Remaining people of the valley, how long will you cut yourselves in sorrow?

**6** "Sword of the LORD, when will you stop? Go back into your cover. Rest and be quiet!"

**7** But the sword cannot be quiet, because the LORD gave it a command. He commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the coast of the sea.

## Chapter 48

**1** The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this about Moab: "Nebo will have much trouble, because the enemy will destroy it. The enemy will capture Kiriathaim, and its people will feel shame. The enemy will break down the fortress, and its people will feel shame and terror.

**2** People will not praise Moab again. In Heshbon the enemy plans the fall of Moab. They say, 'Come, let us destroy Moab as a nation.' The town of Madmen will also be silent. The sword will chase you.

**3** Hear the cries from Horonaim! There is destruction and great ruin.

**4** The enemy will destroy Moab. Her children will cry out.

**5** The people go up the road to Luhith and cry all the time. On the road down to Horonaim, people hear cries of pain because of the destruction.

**6** Run! Save your lives! Be like a small bush in the desert.

**7** You trust in the things that you made and in your treasures. Thus the enemy will capture you. Your god Chemosh will go away as a prisoner with his priests and officials.

**8** The destroyer will come against each city. No city will escape. The enemy will ruin the valley and destroy the plain, as the LORD said.

**9** Put salt on Moab, because she will become a ruin. Her cities will become empty, with no people in them.

**10** Cursed is the person who is lazy in the work of the LORD. Cursed is the person who does not use his sword to kill.

**11** "Moab was at peace since the time that she was young. Moab is like wine that people leave in the jar. People did not pour Moab from jar to jar. Moab did not go away as a prisoner. Thus Moab tastes the same as before. Its smell is the same.

**12** But the days will come," says the LORD, "when I will send men who pour out wine from jars. They will pour Moab out. They will empty his jars and break them.

**13** Then Moab will feel shame because of his god Chemosh. In the same way, the people of Israel felt shame when they trusted in the god at Bethel.

**14** "How can you say, 'We are strong soldiers, ready for war'?

**15** The enemy will destroy Moab and attack its towns. His best young men will die," says the King, whose name is the LORD of armies.

**16** "The disaster of Moab will come soon. His trouble comes fast.

**17** All the nations around Moab, mourn for him. All the people who know his fame, mourn for him. Say, 'Someone broke the strong rod of power! Someone broke the beautiful stick of power!'

**18** "People of Dibon, come down from your place of honor. Sit on the dry ground. The destroyer of Moab will attack you. He will destroy your strong cities.

**19** People who live in Aroer, stand near the road and watch. Ask the man and the woman who run away. Ask them, 'What happened?'

**20** Moab feels shame, because the enemy broke it. Cry and shout! Tell the people near the Arnon River that the enemy destroyed Moab.

**21** Punishment comes to the plain. It comes to Holon, Jahzah and Mephaath.

**22** It comes to Dibon, Nebo and Beth Diblathaim.

**23** It comes to Kiriathaim, Beth Gamul and Beth Meon.

**24** It comes to Kerioth and Bozrah. It comes to all the towns of Moab, far and near.

**25** The enemy cut off the power of Moab. The enemy broke his arm," says the LORD.

**26** "Make Moab drunk, because he was proud against the LORD. Let Moab roll in his vomit. Let people laugh at him.

**27** Moab, you laughed at Israel. Did people catch Israel among thieves? Each time that you spoke about Israel, you shook your head in mockery.

**28** People of Moab, leave your towns. Live among the rocks. Be like a dove that makes its nest at the entrance of a cave.

**29** "We heard about the pride of Moab. He is very proud. He thinks that he is better than other people. He is arrogant. His heart is very proud.

**30** I know about his anger," says the LORD. "But his boasts are empty. His actions do nothing.

**31** Thus I will cry for Moab. I will cry for all the people of Moab. I will mourn for the men of Kir Hareseth.

**32** I will cry for you, vineyard of Sibmah, more than I cry for Jazer. Your branches went out as far as the sea. They went as far as Jazer. But the destroyer attacks your summer fruit and your grapes.

**33** Joy and happiness are gone from the good farmland of Moab. I stopped the flow of wine from the winepresses. No person crushes the grapes with shouts of joy. The shouts are not shouts of joy.

**34** "The people of Heshbon cry out. Their cries go to Elealeh and Jahaz. Their cries go from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath Shelishiyah. Even the waters of Nimrim become dry.

**35** I will stop the people in Moab who give offerings at the high places," says the LORD. "I will stop the people who burn incense to their gods.

**36** "Thus my heart is sad for Moab, like the sad music of a flute. My heart is sad for the men of Kir Hareseth, like the music of a flute. This is because all the wealth that they got is gone.

**37** Each person shaves his head and cuts his beard in sorrow. Each person cuts his hands. Each person wears sackcloth around his waist.

**38** On all the roofs in Moab and in its streets, people mourn. This is because I broke Moab like a jar that no person wants," says the LORD.

**39** "The enemy broke Moab! The people cry! Moab turns away in shame! All the people around Moab laugh at him. They feel horror when they look at him."

**40** The LORD says this: "Look! An enemy flies down like an eagle. He spreads his wings over Moab.

**41** The enemy will capture Kerioth and the fortresses. On that day the soldiers of Moab will be afraid. Their hearts will be like the heart of a woman who gives birth to a child.

**42** I will destroy Moab as a nation, because he was proud against the LORD.

**43** People of Moab, terror, a hole and a trap wait for you," says the LORD.

**44** "The person who runs away from the terror will fall into the hole. The trap will catch the person who climbs out of the hole. I will bring the year of punishment on Moab," says the LORD.

**45** "The people who run away stand without strength near Heshbon. But a fire comes out from Heshbon. A flame comes from the city of Sihon. It burns the land of Moab. It burns the heads of the proud people who make loud noise.

**46** Moab, you will have much trouble! The people of Chemosh will die. The enemy will take your sons and your daughters as prisoners.

**47** "But in the last days I will make the people of Moab free again," says the LORD. This is the end of the judgment against Moab.

## Chapter 49

**1** The LORD says this about the Ammonites: "Does Israel not have sons? Does Israel have no person to get his land? Then why does the god Milcom take the land of Gad? Why do his people live in the towns of Gad?

**2** Thus the days will come," says the LORD, "when I will cause Rabbah of the Ammonites to hear the sound of war. Rabbah will become a pile of ruins. The enemy will burn its villages. Then Israel will take back the land from the people who took it," says the LORD.

**3** "People of Heshbon, cry loudly, because the enemy destroys Ai! People of the villages of Rabbah, cry out! Put on sackcloth and mourn. Run here and there inside the walls. This is because the god Milcom will go away as a prisoner with his priests and officials.

**4** You boast about your valleys and your rich valley. You are a people who turned away from me. You trust in your treasures. You say, 'No person will attack us.'

**5** Look! I will bring terror on you from all the people around you," says the Lord GOD of armies. "I will send each of you away. No person will gather the people who run away.

**6** "But after that, I will make the Ammonites free again," says the LORD.

**7** The LORD of armies says this about Edom: "Is there no more wisdom in Teman? Do the wise men have no more good advice? Is their wisdom gone?

**8** People of Dedan, turn and run away! Hide in deep caves! I will bring disaster on Esau (Edom). The time comes for me to punish him.

**9** When people pick grapes, they leave some grapes on the vines. When thieves come at night, they take only what they want.

**10** But I will take everything from Esau. I will show all the places where he hides. He will not be able to hide. I will destroy his children, his relatives and his neighbors. Edom will be gone.

**11** Leave your orphans. I will keep them alive. Your widows can trust in me."

**12** The LORD says this: "Some people did not deserve to drink from the cup of punishment. But they had to drink from it. Thus you will certainly not be free from punishment. You must drink from the cup.

**13** I make a promise by my own name," says the LORD, "that Bozrah will become a ruin. People will feel horror at it, insult it and curse it. All its towns will be ruins always."

**14** I heard a message from the LORD. He sent a messenger to the nations. The messenger said, "Gather together and attack Edom! Get ready for battle!"

**15** "Look! I will make you small among the nations. People will hate you.

**16** You live in the holes of the rocks. You live on the tops of the hills. You think that you are strong, and other people are afraid of you. But your pride tricks you. You make your home high like the nest of an eagle. But I will bring you down from there," says the LORD.

**17** "Edom will become a ruin. All the people who go past it will feel horror. They will whistle because of all its wounds.

**18** I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them," says the LORD. "In the same way, no person will live in Edom. No person will stay there.

**19** "Look! An enemy will come like a lion from the thick bushes near the Jordan River. He will attack the strong fields where the sheep are. Suddenly I will chase Edom from its land. I will put over it the person that I choose. No person is like me. No person can tell me what to do. No leader can stand against me."

**20** Thus listen to the plan of the LORD against Edom. Listen to what he plans against the people of Teman. The enemy will certainly pull away even the smallest sheep of the flock. The LORD will certainly destroy their fields because of them.

**21** The earth will shake at the noise of the fall of Edom. People will hear their cries at the Red Sea.

**22** Look! An enemy will fly up like an eagle. He will spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day the soldiers of Edom will be afraid. Their hearts will be like the heart of a woman who gives birth to a child.

**23** This is about Damascus: "The people of Hamath and Arpad feel shame, because they hear bad news. They are weak with fear. They have no peace, like the sea, which cannot be quiet.

**24** Damascus becomes weak. Its people turn to run away. Terror takes hold of them. Pain and sorrow take hold of them, like a woman who gives birth to a child.

**25** The famous city that gave me joy is now empty!

**26** Thus her young men will fall in the streets. All her soldiers will die on that day," says the LORD of armies.

**27** "I will start a fire in the walls of Damascus. The fire will burn the palaces of Ben-Hadad."

**28** This is about Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked. The LORD says this: "Get up and attack Kedar! Destroy the people of the east!

**29** The enemy will take their tents and their flocks. The enemy will take their tent curtains, all their goods and their camels. The enemy will shout to them, 'Terror on every side!'

**30** "Run! Go far away! Hide in deep caves, people of Hazor," says the LORD. "Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made a plan against you. He decided to attack you.

**31** "Get up and attack the nation that lives in peace and safety," says the LORD. "That nation has no gates or bars on its gates. Its people live alone.

**32** The enemy will take their camels and their many cattle. I will scatter in all directions the people who cut the corners of their hair. I will bring disaster on them from all sides," says the LORD.

**33** "Hazor will become a place where jackals live. It will be an empty ruin always. No person will live there. No person will stay there."

**34** At the start of the rule of Zedekiah king of Judah, this word of the LORD came to the prophet Jeremiah about Elam:

**35** The LORD of armies says this: "Look! I will break the bow of Elam. The bow is their best weapon.

**36** I will bring the 4 winds against Elam from the 4 directions of the sky. I will scatter the people of Elam in all these directions. The people who run away from Elam will go to every nation.

**37** I will make Elam afraid in front of their enemies who want to kill them. I will bring disaster on them in my strong anger," says the LORD. "I will send the sword to chase them until I destroy them.

**38** I will put my throne in Elam. I will destroy its king and officials," says the LORD.

**39** "But in the last days I will make Elam free again," says the LORD.

## Chapter 50

**1** This is the word that the LORD spoke through the prophet Jeremiah about Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans:

**2** "Tell the nations and speak this news! Put up a flag and tell the news! Do not hide it! Say, 'The enemy will capture Babylon. The god Bel will feel shame. The god Marduk will be afraid. The idols of Babylon will feel shame. Her false gods will be afraid.'

**3** A nation from the north will attack Babylon. It will make her land empty. No person will live in it. People and animals will run away.

**4** "In those days, at that time," says the LORD, "the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come together. They will come with tears to look for the LORD their God.

**5** They will ask the way to Zion and turn their faces toward it. They will say, 'Come, let us join with the LORD in a covenant that will continue always. We will never forget it.'

**6** "My people were like lost sheep. Their shepherds caused them to go the wrong way. They caused them to go here and there on the mountains. My people went from mountain to hill. They forgot the place where they rest.

**7** All the people who found them ate them. Their enemies said, 'We are not guilty, because they sinned against the LORD. The LORD is their true home. The LORD is the hope of their ancestors.'

**8** "Run away from Babylon! Leave the land of the Chaldeans! Be like the male goats that go in front of the flock.

**9** Look! I will cause a group of great nations from the north to attack Babylon. They will prepare to fight against her. They will capture her from the north. Their arrows will be like arrows from a skilled soldier. Their arrows will always hit the target.

**10** The enemy will take all the wealth of the land of the Chaldeans. All the people who take her wealth will get all that they want," says the LORD.

**11** "People of Babylon, you destroyed my land, and you were glad. You were happy. You jump around like a young cow in the grass. You make noise like strong horses.

**12** But your mother city will feel much shame. The city that gave you birth will lose her honor. Look! Babylon will be the least important of the nations. She will be a desert, a dry land and a wilderness.

**13** Because of the anger of the LORD, no person will live in Babylon. She will be fully empty. All the people who go past Babylon will feel horror. They will whistle because of all her wounds.

**14** "All you soldiers who use the bow, get into your positions around Babylon. Shoot at her. Use all your arrows, because she sinned against the LORD.

**15** Shout against her from all sides! She surrenders. Her towers fall. The enemy breaks down her walls. This is the punishment of the LORD. Punish her! Do to her what she did to other people.

**16** Remove from Babylon the person who plants seeds. Remove the person who uses the sickle at harvest time. Because of the cruel sword, each person will go back to his own people. Each person will run away to his own land.

**17** "Israel is like sheep that lions scattered. First the king of Assyria ate Israel. Then Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon broke his bones."

**18** Thus the LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this: "I punished the king of Assyria. In the same way, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land.

**19** I will bring Israel back to his own field. He will eat food on Carmel and in Bashan. He will eat until he is full in the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.

**20** In those days, at that time," says the LORD, "people will look for the sins of Israel, but they will find none. They will look for the sins of Judah, but they will not find them. This is because I will forgive the people that I keep alive.

**21** "Attack the land of Merathaim and the people of Pekod. Kill them and fully destroy them," says the LORD. "Do all that I command you.

**22** The noise of battle is in the land. It is the noise of great destruction.

**23** Babylon was like a hammer that hit all the earth. But now someone broke that hammer into pieces! Babylon became a ruin among the nations!

**24** Babylon, I put a trap for you, and the trap caught you. You did not know it. I found you and captured you, because you fought against the LORD.

**25** The LORD opened the room where he keeps his weapons. He brought out the weapons of his anger. The Lord GOD of armies has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.

**26** Attack Babylon from far away. Open her storerooms. Put her goods in piles like grain. Fully destroy her. Leave nothing alive.

**27** Kill all her young soldiers! Let them go down to die! They will have much trouble, because the day of their punishment comes.

**28** Listen to the people who run away and escape from Babylon. They tell the people in Zion how the LORD our God punishes Babylon. He punishes Babylon for what she did to his temple.

**29** "Call the soldiers who use the bow to attack Babylon. Put soldiers around her on all sides. Let no person escape. Punish her for what she did. Do to her what she did to other people. She was proud and rebelled against the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.

**30** Thus her young men will fall in the streets. All her soldiers will die on that day," says the LORD.

**31** "Look! I am against you, you proud nation," says the Lord GOD of armies. "Your day comes. The time comes for me to punish you.

**32** The proud nation will fall. No person will help it to get up. I will start a fire in its cities. The fire will burn all the land around it."

**33** The LORD of armies says this: "Enemies are cruel to the people of Israel and Judah. All the people who captured them hold them tightly. They refuse to let them go.

**34** But their Savior is strong. His name is the LORD of armies. He will defend them fully. He will give peace to their land. But he will cause trouble to the people of Babylon.

**35** "A sword comes against the Chaldeans," says the LORD. "It comes against the people of Babylon, her officials and her wise men.

**36** A sword comes against her false prophets, and they will become fools. A sword comes against her soldiers, and they will be afraid.

**37** A sword comes against her horses and chariots. It comes against all the foreign soldiers in her. They will become weak like women. A sword comes against her treasures, and people will steal them.

**38** A dry time comes against her waters, and they will become dry. This is because Babylon is a land of idols. The people are crazy about their idols.

**39** "Thus wild animals of the desert and jackals will live there. Owls will live there. No person will live in Babylon again. No people will live there for all time.

**40** God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them," says the LORD. "In the same way, no person will live in Babylon. No person will stay there.

**41** "Look! An army comes from the north. A great nation and many kings will come from the ends of the earth.

**42** They have bows and spears. They are cruel and show no mercy. Their voices roar like the sea. They ride on horses. They come in battle positions to attack you, Babylon.

**43** The king of Babylon hears the news about them. His hands become weak. Pain takes hold of him, like the pain of a woman who gives birth to a child.

**44** Look! An enemy will come like a lion from the thick bushes near the Jordan River. He will attack the strong fields where the sheep are. Suddenly I will chase Babylon from its land. I will put over it the person that I choose. No person is like me. No person can tell me what to do. No leader can stand against me."

**45** Thus listen to the plan of the LORD against Babylon. Listen to what he plans against the land of the Chaldeans. The enemy will certainly pull away even the smallest sheep of the flock. The LORD will certainly destroy their fields because of them.

**46** The earth will shake at the noise of the capture of Babylon. The nations will hear her cries.

## Chapter 51

**1** The LORD says this: "I will send a wind that destroys against Babylon. I will send it against the people who live in Leb Kamai, the center of my enemies.

**2** I will send foreign men to Babylon. These men will scatter Babylon like wind scatters chaff. They will make her land empty. On the day of trouble, they will attack her from all sides.

**3** Do not let the archer of Babylon pull his bow. Do not let him stand up in his armor. Do not spare her young men. Destroy all her army completely.

**4** The dead will fall in the land of the Chaldeans. Men with deep wounds will fall in her streets.

**5** The LORD of armies, the God of Israel and Judah, did not leave his people. But the land of the Chaldeans is full of sin against the Holy One of Israel.

**6** Run away from Babylon! Each person must save his life. Do not die because of the sin of Babylon. This is the time when the LORD punishes Babylon. He will give her the punishment that she must get.

**7** Babylon was a gold cup in the hand of the LORD. She made all the earth drunk. The nations drank her wine. Thus the nations became mad.

**8** Babylon will fall suddenly, and the enemy will destroy her. Cry loudly for her! Get medicine for her pain. Possibly she will become well.

**9** "We tried to heal Babylon, but she did not become well. Leave her. Each person must go to his own country. Her punishment is as high as the sky."

**10** "The LORD showed that we are right. Come, we will tell the people in Zion what the LORD our God did."

**11** Make the arrows sharp! Get the shields ready! The LORD caused the kings of the Medes to act. He plans to destroy Babylon. The LORD will punish Babylon because Babylon destroyed his temple.

**12** Put up a flag against the walls of Babylon! Make the guard strong. Put guards in their positions. Prepare men to attack by surprise. The LORD will do what he said against the people of Babylon.

**13** Babylon, you live near many rivers, and you have much treasure. But your end has come. The time to stop your greed is here.

**14** The LORD of armies made a promise by his own name. He said, "I will fill you with enemy soldiers, as many as locusts. They will shout in victory against you."

**15** The LORD made the earth with his power. He made the world firm with his wisdom. He spread out the sky with his knowledge.

**16** When he speaks, the waters in the sky make a loud noise. He causes clouds to go up from the ends of the earth. He makes flashes of light for the rain. He sends out the wind from his storehouses.

**17** All people are stupid and know nothing. Each metal worker feels shame because of his idols. His metal idols are false. They have no breath in them.

**18** The idols are worthless. People will laugh at them. When God punishes, the idols will be gone.

**19** The God of Jacob is not like these idols. He made all things. Israel is the tribe that belongs to him. His name is the LORD of armies.

**20** The LORD says, "Babylon, you are my war club and my weapon. With you I break the nations into pieces. With you I destroy kingdoms.

**21** With you I break the horse and its rider. With you I break the chariot and its driver.

**22** With you I break man and woman. With you I break the old and the young. With you I break the young man and the young woman.

**23** With you I break the shepherd and his flock. With you I break the farmer and his oxen. With you I break governors and officials.

**24** But now you will see me punish Babylon and all the people of Chaldea. I will punish them for all the evil that they did in Zion," says the LORD.

**25** The LORD says, "Babylon, I am against you. You are like a mountain that destroys all the earth. I will put out my hand against you. I will roll you down from the rocks. I will make you a mountain that the fire burns.

**26** People will not take a stone from you for a corner or for a foundation. You will be empty for all time," says the LORD.

**27** Put up a flag in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Prepare the nations for war against Babylon. Call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz against her. Choose a commander against her. Send the horses against her, as many as locusts.

**28** Prepare the nations for war against her. Prepare the kings of the Medes, their governors, their officials, and all the countries that they rule.

**29** The land shakes and has pain. The LORD will do what he plans against Babylon. He will make the land of Babylon empty, with no people in it.

**30** The soldiers of Babylon stop the fight. They stay in their forts. Their strength is gone. They became weak like women. The enemy burned the houses of Babylon. The enemy broke the bars of her gates.

**31** One messenger runs after another messenger. They go to tell the king of Babylon that the enemy took all his city.

**32** The enemy took the river crossings. The enemy burned the marshes with fire. The soldiers of Babylon are afraid.

**33** The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says this: "Babylon is like a floor where people beat grain. It is the time to beat her flat. Soon the time of her harvest will come."

**34** Jerusalem says, "Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, ate me. He crushed me. He made me an empty jar. He swallowed me like a large snake. He filled his stomach with my good food. Then he threw me out.

**35** The people of Zion say, 'Let Babylon get the same cruelty that she did to us.' Jerusalem says, 'Let the people of Chaldea pay for our blood.'"

**36** Thus the LORD says this: "Jerusalem, I will defend you. I will punish Babylon for what she did to you. I will make her sea dry. I will make her springs dry.

**37** Babylon will become a pile of ruins. Jackals will live there. People will feel horror when they see her. They will make sounds of contempt. No person will live there.

**38** The people of Babylon roar together like lions. They make noise like young lions.

**39** While they are hungry, I will give them a feast. I will make them drunk, so that they shout with joy. Then they will sleep for all time and not wake up," says the LORD.

**40** "I will bring them down like lambs that people kill. I will bring them down like rams and male goats.

**41** The enemy took Sheshach, which is Babylon! All the earth praised Babylon, but the enemy took her. Now the nations feel horror when they look at Babylon.

**42** The sea came up over Babylon. Its loud waves covered her.

**43** Her towns are empty. They are a dry land and a desert. No person lives there. No person travels through that land.

**44** I will punish Bel, the god of Babylon. I will make him give back what he swallowed. The nations will not come to him again. The wall of Babylon will fall.

**45** My people, go out of Babylon! Each person must save his life from the strong anger of the LORD.

**46** Do not become weak. Do not be afraid of the news that people hear in the land. One year a report will come. The next year another report will come. There will be violence in the land. One ruler will fight against another ruler.

**47** Thus the time will come when I will punish the idols of Babylon. All her land will feel shame. All her dead people will lie in her streets.

**48** Then the heavens and the earth and all things in them will sing with joy because of Babylon. Destroyers will come against her from the north," says the LORD.

**49** "Babylon caused the death of many people of Israel. Thus the people of Babylon will die. Babylon killed people in all the earth.

**50** You people who did not die by the sword, go away! Do not stay. Remember the LORD in the far country. Think about Jerusalem."

**51** "We feel shame because people insult us. Shame covers our faces. Foreigners went into the holy places of the house of the LORD."

**52** "Thus the time will come," says the LORD, "when I will punish the idols of Babylon. In all her land, wounded people will cry with pain.

**53** Babylon can go up to the sky. She can make her high forts strong. But I will send destroyers against her," says the LORD.

**54** "Listen! There is a cry from Babylon. There is the sound of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans.

**55** The LORD destroys Babylon. He stops her loud noise. Her enemies come like waves of the sea. Their noise is very loud.

**56** A destroyer comes against Babylon. The enemy captures her soldiers and breaks their bows. The LORD is a God who punishes. He will give Babylon all the punishment that she must get.

**57** I will make her officials and wise men drunk. I will make her governors, her officials, and her soldiers drunk. They will sleep for all time and not wake up," says the King. His name is the LORD of armies.

**58** The LORD of armies says this: "The enemy will break down the thick walls of Babylon completely. The enemy will burn her high gates with fire. The work of the nations will have no value. Their work will become fuel for the fire. The people will become tired."

**59** This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah, the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah. Seraiah went to Babylon with Zedekiah, the king of Judah. This was in the 4th year of the rule of Zedekiah. Seraiah was the chief officer for the journey.

**60** Jeremiah wrote on a scroll about all the disasters that will come on Babylon. He wrote all these words about Babylon.

**61** Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you go to Babylon, make sure that you read all these words aloud.

**62** Then say, 'LORD, you said that you will destroy this place. No person or animal will live in it. It will be empty for all time.'

**63** When you read all of this scroll, tie a stone to it. Throw it into the middle of the Euphrates River.

**64** Then say, 'Babylon will sink like this stone. She will not rise again because of the disaster that the LORD will bring on her. Her people will become tired.'" The words of Jeremiah stop here.

## Chapter 52

**1** Zedekiah was 21 years old when he became king. He ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

**2** Zedekiah did evil things in the sight of the LORD. He did all the things that Jehoiakim did.

**3** Because of the anger of the LORD, these things happened to Jerusalem and Judah. At last the LORD sent them away from him. Zedekiah fought against the king of Babylon.

**4** Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, came with all his army against Jerusalem. This was in the 9th year of the rule of Zedekiah, on the 10th day of the 10th month. The army made a camp near the city. They built walls for attack around the city.

**5** The army stayed around the city until the 11th year of king Zedekiah.

**6** On the 9th day of the 4th month, the famine in the city was very bad. The people of the land had no food.

**7** Then the enemy broke through the city wall. All the soldiers ran away. They went out of the city at night through the gate between the 2 walls, near the garden of the king. The Chaldeans were all around the city. The soldiers went toward the Jordan Valley.

**8** But the army of the Chaldeans chased the king. They caught Zedekiah in the plains near Jericho. All his army left him and went in different directions.

**9** The Chaldeans captured the king. They took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath. There the king of Babylon decided his punishment.

**10** At Riblah the king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah while Zedekiah watched. He also killed all the officials of Judah.

**11** Then he removed the eyes of Zedekiah. The king of Babylon put him in bronze chains and took him to Babylon. He kept Zedekiah in prison until the day of his death.

**12** On the 10th day of the 5th month, Nebuzaradan came to Jerusalem. This was in the 19th year of the rule of Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon. Nebuzaradan was the commander of the guard and served the king of Babylon.

**13** He burned the house of the LORD and the palace of the king. He burned all the houses in Jerusalem. He burned all the important buildings.

**14** All the army of the Chaldeans with the commander of the guard broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.

**15** Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took some of the poorest people as prisoners. He also took the other people who stayed in the city. He took the people who went over to the king of Babylon. He took the other workers who stayed.

**16** But Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, left some of the poorest people of the land. He left them to work in the vineyards and the fields.

**17** The Chaldeans broke the bronze pillars in the house of the LORD. They broke the bronze stands and the large bronze bowl, called "the Sea." They took all the bronze to Babylon.

**18** They also took the pots, the shovels, the wick cutters, the bowls and the dishes. They took all the bronze tools that the priests used in the temple.

**19** The commander of the guard took the basins, the fire pans, the bowls, the pots, the lampstands, the dishes, and the cups. He took all the things of gold or silver.

**20** King Solomon made the 2 pillars, the Sea, the 12 bronze bulls under the Sea, and the stands for the house of the LORD. The bronze of all these things was too heavy to weigh.

**21** Each pillar was 18 cubits high. A line of 12 cubits went around each pillar. The metal was 4 fingers thick. The pillar was hollow.

**22** A bronze top was on each pillar. Each top was 5 cubits high. A net and pomegranates of bronze went all around the top. The second pillar, with its pomegranates, was the same.

**23** There were 96 pomegranates on the sides. In total there were 100 pomegranates on the net around the top.

**24** The commander of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest as prisoners. He also took the 3 doorkeepers.

**25** From the city he took the officer who commanded the soldiers. He took 7 advisers of the king who were still in the city. He took the scribe of the army commander, who listed the people of the land for the army. He also took 60 men of the land who were in the city.

**26** Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took all these people to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

**27** The king of Babylon killed them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus the Babylonians took the people of Judah away from their land as prisoners.

**28** This is the number of people that Nebuchadnezzar took away as prisoners. In the 7th year, he took 3,023 Jews.

**29** In the 18th year of Nebuchadnezzar, he took 832 people from Jerusalem.

**30** In the 23rd year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took 745 Jews. In total, the Babylonians took 4,600 people.

**31** In the 37th year after the Babylonians took Jehoiachin, the king of Judah, as a prisoner, Evil-Merodach became king of Babylon. On the 25th day of the 12th month of that first year, he was kind to Jehoiachin. He released him from prison.

**32** He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin. He gave him a seat of more honor than the seats of the other kings with him in Babylon.

**33** Jehoiachin removed his prison clothes. For all the other days of his life, he ate at the table of the king.

**34** Each day the king of Babylon gave Jehoiachin an amount of food. The king did this until the day of the death of Jehoiachin, for all the days of his life.

# Lamentations

## Chapter 1

**1** The city of Jerusalem was full of people, but now she is alone! She is like a widow! She was great among the nations. She was a princess among the provinces. Now she is a slave who must pay tax!

**2** She cries bitterly at night. Tears are on her face. All her lovers left her, and none of them comforts her. All her friends turned against her. They became her enemies.

**3** Judah went away into exile after much pain and hard work as slaves. She lives among the other nations. She finds no rest. All the people who chase her caught her in her troubles.

**4** The roads to Zion are sad, because no people come to the holy festivals. All her gates are empty. Her priests cry with pain. Her young women are sad. Zion has bitter sorrow.

**5** Her enemies became her masters. Her enemies have success. The LORD caused her pain because of her many sins. Her children went away as prisoners in front of the enemy.

**6** All the beauty of Zion is gone. Her officials are like deer that find no grass. They have no strength, and they run away in front of the hunter.

**7** In the days of her pain and her trouble, Jerusalem remembers all her good things from past times. Her people fell into the hands of the enemy, and no person helped her. Her enemies looked at her. They laughed at her ruin.

**8** Jerusalem did very bad sins. Thus she became unclean. All the people who honored her now hate her, because they saw her shame. She cries with pain and turns away.

**9** Her dirt is on her clothes. She did not think about her future. Thus her fall was terrible. No person comforts her. "LORD, look at my pain, because the enemy won!"

**10** The enemy put his hand on all her valuable things. She saw foreign nations go into her temple. LORD, you commanded that these nations must not go into your assembly.

**11** All her people cry with pain while they look for bread. They give their valuable things for food to stay alive. "LORD, look at me and think about me. People hate me now."

**12** "You people who go past, does this not have importance to you? Look and see. Is there any pain like my pain? The LORD caused this pain on the day of his strong anger.

**13** He sent fire from above into my bones. He put a net in front of my feet to catch me. He turned me back. He made me empty and weak all day.

**14** He tied my sins together like a yoke. He put them on my neck. He took away my strength. The Lord gave me to enemies whom I cannot fight.

**15** The Lord rejected all my strong soldiers. He called an army against me to crush my young men. The Lord crushed the people of Judah as a person crushes grapes in a winepress.

**16** Because of these things, I cry. Tears flow from my eyes. No person is near to comfort me. No person is near to give me strength again. My children are alone, because the enemy won."

**17** Zion holds out her hands, but no person comforts her. The LORD commanded the neighbors of Jacob to be his enemies. Jerusalem became an unclean thing among them.

**18** "The LORD is right, because I disobeyed his command. Listen, all you people. Look at my pain. My young women and my young men went away as prisoners.

**19** I called to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and my leaders died in the city. They looked for food to stay alive.

**20** LORD, look at me, because I am in distress! I have pain inside me. My heart has no peace, because I disobeyed you very much. Outside, the sword kills. Inside the house, there is death.

**21** People heard my cries, but no person comforts me. All my enemies heard about my trouble. They are glad that you did this to me. Bring the day that you promised. Then my enemies will be like me.

**22** Look at all their evil. Do to them what you did to me because of all my sins. I cry with pain many times, and my heart is weak."

## Chapter 2

**1** The Lord was angry, and he covered Zion with a dark cloud! He threw the glory of Israel down from the sky to the earth. On the day of his anger, he did not remember his temple, which is his footstool.

**2** The Lord destroyed all the homes of Jacob, and he had no pity. In his anger he broke down the forts of Judah. He threw them to the ground. He brought shame on the kingdom and its officials.

**3** In his strong anger he took away all the strength of Israel. He took back his right hand when the enemy came. He burned against Jacob like a fire that destroys all things around it.

**4** He pulled his bow like an enemy. He held up his right hand like an enemy. He killed all the people whom Zion loved. He poured out his anger like fire on the tents of Zion.

**5** The Lord was like an enemy. He destroyed Israel. He destroyed all her palaces and her forts. He caused much sorrow and many tears among the people of Judah.

**6** He broke down his temple as a person breaks down a garden hut. He destroyed the place where his people met. The LORD caused the people of Zion to forget the holy festivals and the Sabbaths. In his strong anger he rejected the king and the priest.

**7** The Lord rejected his altar. He hated his holy place. He gave the walls of her palaces to the enemy. The enemy shouted in the house of the LORD as people shout on a festival day.

**8** The LORD decided to destroy the wall of Zion. He measured the wall with a line. He did not stop his destruction. He caused the walls and the defenses to become sad. They fell together.

**9** Her gates went down into the ground. He destroyed and broke the bars of her gates. Her king and her officials are in exile among the nations. No person teaches the law now. Her prophets get no vision from the LORD.

**10** The leaders of Zion sit on the ground in silence. They put dust on their heads. They wear sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem bow their heads to the ground.

**11** My eyes are weak from tears. I have pain inside me. My heart is full of sorrow because the enemy destroyed my people. Children and babies become weak in the streets of the city.

**12** The children say to their mothers, "Where is the bread and the wine?" They become weak like wounded men in the streets of the city. Their lives go away in the arms of their mothers.

**13** Jerusalem, what can I say to you? What can I compare you to? How can I comfort you, Zion? Your ruin is as large as the sea. Who can heal you?

**14** Your prophets saw false and foolish visions for you. They did not show you your sins. If they did, you could avoid exile. They gave you false messages that caused you to go away.

**15** All the people who go past clap their hands at you. They make sounds of contempt and shake their heads at Jerusalem. They say, "Is this the city that people called perfect in beauty, the joy of all the earth?"

**16** All your enemies open their mouths against you. They make sounds of contempt and grind their teeth. They say, "We destroyed her! This is the day that we waited for. Now we see it!"

**17** The LORD did what he planned. He did what he said a long time ago. He destroyed you and did not have pity. He caused your enemies to be glad about you. He made your enemies strong.

**18** The hearts of the people cry to the Lord. Wall of Zion, let your tears flow like a river, day and night. Do not rest. Do not let your eyes stop their tears.

**19** Get up and cry out in the night. At the start of each part of the night, tell the Lord all that is in your heart. Lift up your hands to him. Pray for the lives of your children. They become weak from hunger at the corner of each street.

**20** "LORD, look and think! You never did this to any other people. Must the women eat their own children, whom they hold and love? Must the enemy kill the priest and the prophet in the temple of the Lord?

**21** The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets. My young women and my young men died by the sword. You killed them on the day of your anger. You killed them and did not have pity.

**22** You called terrors against me from all sides, as people call others to a festival. On the day of the anger of the LORD, no person escaped. My enemy killed the children that I held and raised."

## Chapter 3

**1** I am a man who saw much pain. God punished me with the rod of his anger.

**2** He made me walk in darkness, not in light.

**3** He hits me again and again with his hand all day.

**4** He made my flesh and my skin old. He broke my bones.

**5** He built walls against me. He put bitterness and trouble around me.

**6** He made me live in darkness, like people who died a long time ago.

**7** He put a wall around me, and I cannot go out. He put heavy chains on me.

**8** I call out and shout for help, but he does not listen to my prayer.

**9** He blocked my roads with walls of stone. He made my paths crooked.

**10** He waited for me like a bear. He hid like a lion in a secret place.

**11** He pulled me off the road and tore me to pieces. He left me helpless.

**12** He pulled his bow. He made me the target for his arrows.

**13** He shot his arrows deep into my body.

**14** All my people laugh at me. They sing songs about me all day.

**15** He filled me with bitterness. He made me drink bitter things.

**16** He broke my teeth with stones. He pushed me down into the dust.

**17** I have no peace. I forgot what good times are.

**18** I said, "My strength is gone. I have no more hope in the LORD."

**19** Remember my pain and my trouble, my bitterness and my pain.

**20** I remember these things all the time. My spirit is low inside me.

**21** But I think about this, and thus I have hope:

**22** Because of the faithful love of the LORD, we are still alive. His mercy does not stop.

**23** His mercy is new each morning. LORD, you are very faithful.

**24** I say, "The LORD is all that I have. Thus I will put my hope in him."

**25** The LORD is good to people who wait for him. He is good to the person who looks for him.

**26** It is good to wait quietly for the LORD to save us.

**27** It is good for a man to carry a yoke while he is young.

**28** Let him sit alone in silence when the LORD puts the yoke on him.

**29** Let him bow down with his face in the dust. Possibly there is still hope.

**30** Let him turn his cheek to the person who hits him. Let him accept insults.

**31** The Lord will not reject people for all time.

**32** The Lord causes sorrow, but he will also show mercy. His faithful love is very great.

**33** He does not want to cause pain or sorrow to people.

**34** People crush all the prisoners of the earth under their feet.

**35** People refuse justice to a man in front of the Most High.

**36** People do wrong to a man in court. The Lord does not approve of these things.

**37** Who can speak and cause something to happen, if the Lord does not command it?

**38** Both bad things and good things come from the command of the Most High.

**39** Why does a man who is alive complain when God punishes him for his sins?

**40** We must examine our ways and test them. We must come back to the LORD.

**41** We must lift up our hearts and our hands to God in heaven.

**42** "We sinned and disobeyed you. You did not forgive us.

**43** You covered yourself with anger, and you chased us. You killed us and did not have pity.

**44** You covered yourself with a cloud. Thus our prayers cannot go through to you.

**45** You made us like dirt and garbage among the nations.

**46** All our enemies open their mouths to insult us.

**47** Fear and traps came on us. Ruin and destruction came on us."

**48** Rivers of tears flow from my eyes, because the enemy destroyed my people.

**49** My tears flow and do not stop. They flow all the time.

**50** My tears will flow until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.

**51** My eyes cause me pain because of the sorrow of all the women of my city.

**52** My enemies hunted me like a bird. They had no reason to hate me.

**53** They threw me alive into a pit. They threw stones at me.

**54** Water flowed over my head. I said, "I will die."

**55** LORD, I called to you from the bottom of the pit.

**56** You heard my voice. Do not close your ear to my cry for help.

**57** You came near on the day that I called to you. You said, "Do not be afraid."

**58** Lord, you defended me. You saved my life.

**59** LORD, you saw the wrong that people did to me. Judge my case.

**60** You saw all their hate. You saw all their plans against me.

**61** LORD, you heard their insults and all their plans against me.

**62** My enemies talk against me and plan against me all day.

**63** Look at them! When they sit down and when they stand up, they sing songs about me to laugh at me.

**64** LORD, punish them for what they did.

**65** Make their hearts hard. Put your curse on them.

**66** In your anger, chase them and destroy them from under the sky of the LORD.

## Chapter 4

**1** The gold lost its shine! The pure gold changed! The holy stones lie at the corner of each street.

**2** The valuable people of Zion were worth their weight in pure gold. Now people think that they are only clay jars that a potter made!

**3** Even jackals give milk to their young. But my people became cruel, like ostriches in the desert.

**4** The tongues of babies stick to the top of their mouths because they are thirsty. The children ask for bread, but no person gives them bread.

**5** The people who ate good food now die in the streets. The people who wore expensive clothes now lie on piles of garbage.

**6** The punishment of my people is greater than the punishment of Sodom. God destroyed Sodom suddenly, and no human hands helped her.

**7** Her princes were cleaner than snow and whiter than milk. Their bodies were redder than rubies. Their appearance was like sapphire.

**8** Now their faces are blacker than coal. People do not know them in the streets. Their skin is tight on their bones. Their skin became dry like wood.

**9** The people who died by the sword were better than the people who died from hunger. The hungry people became weak and died because there was no food from the fields.

**10** Women who were kind cooked their own children with their own hands. The children became food for them when the enemy destroyed my people.

**11** The LORD showed all his anger. He poured out his strong anger. He started a fire in Zion that burned her foundations.

**12** The kings of the earth and all the people of the world did not believe this. They did not believe that an enemy could go through the gates of Jerusalem.

**13** But this happened because of the sins of her prophets and the evil of her priests. They killed good people in the city.

**14** Now these leaders wander in the streets like blind men. Blood makes them unclean. Thus no person can touch their clothes.

**15** People shouted at them, "Go away! You are unclean! Go away! Do not touch us!" Thus they ran away and wandered. The people of the other nations said, "They cannot stay here."

**16** The LORD in his anger sent them in different directions. He will not look after them again. The people did not respect the priests. They did not honor the leaders.

**17** Our eyes became tired while we looked for help. But no help came. We watched for a nation that could not save us.

**18** The enemy watched our steps. Thus we could not walk in our streets. Our end was near. Our days came to an end. Our end came.

**19** The people who chased us were faster than eagles in the sky. They chased us on the mountains. They waited to attack us in the desert.

**20** The king whom the LORD chose was as important to us as our breath. But the enemy caught him in their traps. We said, "He will protect us among the nations."

**21** People of Edom, who live in the land of Uz, be happy and glad for now. But the cup of punishment will also come to you. You will become drunk and naked.

**22** People of Zion, your punishment is complete. The LORD will not send you into exile again. But people of Edom, he will punish your sins. He will show your evil.

## Chapter 5

**1** LORD, remember what happened to us. Look and see our shame.

**2** Strangers took our land. Foreigners took our houses.

**3** We are orphans with no fathers. Our mothers are like widows.

**4** We must pay money for our water. We must buy our wood.

**5** The enemy is close behind us. We are weary, and we have no rest.

**6** We made agreements with Egypt and Assyria to get enough food.

**7** Our fathers sinned, and they are dead. Now we get the punishment for their sins.

**8** Slaves rule over us. No person saves us from their power.

**9** We risk our lives to get food, because of the killers in the desert.
