**10** Our skin is hot like an oven because of the terrible hunger.

**11** The enemy raped the women in Zion and the young women in the towns of Judah.

**12** The enemy hanged our princes by their hands. They did not respect our old leaders.

**13** The young men must grind grain at the mill. The boys fall down under heavy loads of wood.

**14** The old men do not sit at the city gate now. The young men stopped their music.

**15** The joy in our hearts stopped. Our dances changed into sorrow.

**16** The crown fell from our head. We have great trouble, because we sinned!

**17** Because of this, our hearts are weak. Because of these things, our eyes are dark.

**18** Mount Zion is empty, and foxes walk on it.

**19** But you, LORD, rule for all time. Your throne continues for all generations.

**20** Why do you always forget us? Why do you leave us for such a long time?

**21** LORD, bring us back to you, and we will come back. Make our lives new, as in past times.

**22** Or did you completely reject us? Are you very angry with us?

---

# Ezekiel

## Chapter 1

**1** In the 30th year, on the 5th day of the 4th month, I was with the exiles near the Chebar River. The heavens opened, and I saw visions from God.

**2** It was the 5th day of the month, in the 5th year of the exile of King Jehoiachin.

**3** The LORD spoke his word to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi. This occurred in the land of the Chaldeans, near the Chebar River. There the power of the LORD came on Ezekiel.

**4** I looked and saw a storm wind that came from the north. I saw a large cloud with fire that flashed in it. A bright light was around the cloud. In the center of the fire there was something that shone like bright metal.

**5** In the center of the fire there were shapes like 4 creatures that were alive. The creatures had the shape of a man.

**6** Each creature had 4 faces and 4 wings.

**7** Their legs were straight. Their feet were like the feet of a calf. They shone like polished bronze.

**8** Under their wings on their 4 sides, the creatures had the hands of a man. All 4 creatures had faces and wings.

**9** The wings of each creature touched the wings of the other creatures. The creatures did not turn when they moved. Each creature went straight forward.

**10** Each of the 4 creatures had the face of a man at the front. Each had the face of a lion on the right side. Each had the face of an ox on the left side. Each also had the face of an eagle.

**11** These were their faces. Their wings spread out above them. Each creature had 2 wings that touched the wings of the creatures next to it. Its 2 other wings covered its body.

**12** Each creature went straight forward. They went to the place where the spirit went. They did not turn when they moved.

**13** The creatures looked like coals of fire that burned, or like torches. Fire moved back and forth among the creatures. The fire was bright, and flashes of light came out of the fire.

**14** The creatures moved quickly forward and back like flashes of light.

**15** While I looked at the creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground next to each creature. There were 4 wheels, one for each creature.

**16** The wheels shone like beryl, a yellow stone. All 4 wheels looked the same. Each wheel looked like a wheel inside another wheel.

**17** When the wheels moved, they went in any of the 4 directions. They did not turn when they moved.

**18** The rims of the wheels were very high and terrible. The rims of all 4 wheels were full of eyes all around.

**19** When the creatures moved, the wheels moved next to them. When the creatures went up from the ground, the wheels also went up.

**20** The creatures went to the place where the spirit went. The wheels went up with the creatures, because the spirit of the creatures was in the wheels.

**21** When the creatures moved, the wheels moved. When the creatures stopped, the wheels stopped. When the creatures went up from the ground, the wheels went up with them. The spirit of the creatures was in the wheels.

**22** Above the heads of the creatures there was a shape like a dome. The dome shone like ice and caused fear. The dome spread out above their heads.

**23** Under the dome, the wings of each creature spread straight out toward the other creatures. Each creature also had 2 wings that covered its body.

**24** When the creatures moved, I heard the noise of their wings. The noise was like the noise of a large flood. It was like the voice of the Almighty. It was like the noise of an army. When the creatures stopped, they lowered their wings.

**25** When the creatures stopped and lowered their wings, a voice came from above the dome over their heads.

**26** Above the dome over their heads there was a shape like a throne. The throne looked like sapphire. On the throne there was a shape like a man.

**27** From his waist up, he looked like bright metal with fire all around inside it. From his waist down, he looked like fire. A bright light was all around him.

**28** The light around him looked like a rainbow in the clouds on a day of rain. This was the appearance of the glory of the LORD. When I saw it, I fell down with my face to the ground. Then I heard a voice that spoke.

## Chapter 2

**1** He said to me, "Son of man, stand up. I will speak to you."

**2** While he spoke to me, the Spirit came into me. The Spirit put me on my feet. Then I heard the voice that spoke to me.

**3** He said to me, "Son of man, I send you to the people of Israel. They are a nation that rebels against me. They and their ancestors sinned against me until this day.

**4** The people are stubborn, and their hearts are hard. I send you to them. You will say to them, 'The Lord GOD says this.'

**5** Possibly they will listen, and possibly they will not listen, because they are a people who rebel. But they will know that a prophet was among them.

**6** Son of man, do not be afraid of them or their words. Thorns and sharp plants are around you, and you live among scorpions. But do not be afraid of their words. Do not be afraid of their angry faces. They are a people who rebel.

**7** You must speak my words to them. Possibly they will listen, and possibly they will not listen. They are a people who rebel very much.

**8** But you, son of man, listen to what I tell you. Do not rebel like those people who rebel. Open your mouth and eat what I give you."

**9** Then I looked and saw a hand that reached out to me. In the hand there was a scroll.

**10** He opened the scroll in front of me. There were words on the front and on the back. The words were about sad songs, sorrow, and trouble.

## Chapter 3

**1** He said to me, "Son of man, eat what you find. Eat this scroll. Then go and speak to the people of Israel."

**2** Thus I opened my mouth, and he gave me the scroll to eat.

**3** He said to me, "Son of man, eat this scroll that I give you. Fill your stomach with it." Thus I ate the scroll. It was as sweet as honey in my mouth.

**4** He said to me, "Son of man, go to the people of Israel. Speak my words to them.

**5** I do not send you to a people with a strange language that is difficult. I send you to the people of Israel.

**6** I do not send you to many nations with strange and difficult languages. You cannot understand their words. If I send you to those nations, they will listen to you.

**7** But the people of Israel will not listen to you, because they do not want to listen to me. All the people of Israel are stubborn, and their hearts are hard.

**8** But I made you as stubborn as they are. I made your face as hard as their faces.

**9** I made your forehead as hard as a diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them. Do not be afraid of their angry faces. They are a people who rebel."

**10** He also said to me, "Son of man, listen carefully to all the words that I tell you. Keep them in your heart.

**11** Go to your people who are in exile. Speak to them. Tell them, 'The Lord GOD says this.' Possibly they will listen, and possibly they will not listen."

**12** Then the Spirit lifted me up. Behind me I heard the sound of a loud noise. The voice said, "Praise the glory of the LORD in his place!"

**13** I heard the noise of the wings of the creatures as they touched each other. I heard the noise of the wheels next to them. It was the sound of a loud noise.

**14** The Spirit lifted me up and took me away. I went with bitterness and anger in my spirit. The power of the LORD was strong on me.

**15** I came to the exiles at Tel Abib, who lived near the Chebar River. I sat among them for 7 days. I was very shocked.

**16** At the end of the 7 days, the LORD spoke his word to me. He said,

**17** "Son of man, I made you a guard for the people of Israel. When you hear a word from me, you must warn them for me.

**18** I can say to an evil man, 'You will surely die.' If you do not warn him, he will die because of his sin. If you do not tell him to stop his evil ways to save his life, he will die. But I will make you responsible for his death.

**19** But if you warn the evil man, and he does not stop his evil ways, he will die because of his sin. But you will save your own life.

**20** A good man can stop his good life and do evil. Then I will put an obstacle in front of him, and he will die. If you did not warn him, he will die because of his sin. People will not remember the good things that he did. But I will make you responsible for his death.

**21** But if you warn the good man not to sin, and he does not sin, he will surely live because he obeyed you. And you will save your own life."

**22** The power of the LORD came on me there. He said to me, "Get up and go out to the plain. I will speak to you there."

**23** Thus I got up and went out to the plain. The glory of the LORD was there. It was like the glory that I saw near the Chebar River. I fell down with my face to the ground.

**24** Then the Spirit came into me and put me on my feet. He spoke to me and said, "Go and lock yourself inside your house.

**25** Son of man, the people will tie you with ropes. Thus you cannot go out among them.

**26** I will make your tongue stick to the top of your mouth. You will not be able to speak. You will not be able to correct them, because they are a people who rebel.

**27** But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth. Then you will say to them, 'The Lord GOD says this.' Some people will listen. Some people will refuse to listen. They are a people who rebel."

## Chapter 4

**1** "Son of man, take a clay brick. Put it in front of you. Draw a picture of the city of Jerusalem on the brick.

**2** Show an army that attacks the city. Build a siege wall against it. Build a ramp of dirt against it. Put army camps around it. Put heavy logs around it to break the walls.

**3** Then take an iron plate. Put it as a wall of iron between you and the city. Turn your face toward the city. The city will be under attack, and you will attack it. This will be a sign to the people of Israel.

**4** Then lie down on your left side. Put the sin of the people of Israel on yourself. You will carry their sin for the number of days that you lie on your side.

**5** I give you 1 day for each year of their sin. Thus you will carry the sin of the people of Israel for 390 days.

**6** When you finish these days, lie down again on your right side. Then you will carry the sin of the people of Judah for 40 days. I give you 1 day for each year.

**7** Turn your face toward the attack on Jerusalem. Show your bare arm. Speak as a prophet against the city.

**8** I will tie you with ropes. Thus you cannot turn from one side to the other side until you finish the days of your attack.

**9** Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Put them in one jar and make bread from them. You will eat this bread for the 390 days that you lie on your side.

**10** You must weigh the food that you eat. Eat 20 shekels of food each day. Eat it at set times.

**11** You must also measure the water that you drink. Drink 1/6 of a hin of water each day. Drink it at set times.

**12** Eat the food as you eat barley cakes. Bake it over a fire of dried human dung while the people watch."

**13** The LORD said, "Thus the people of Israel will eat unclean food among the nations. I will send them to these nations."

**14** Then I said, "Oh, Lord GOD! I never made myself unclean. From the time that I was young until now, I never ate an animal that died naturally. I never ate an animal that wild animals killed. No unclean meat ever went into my mouth."

**15** Then he said to me, "Look, I will let you use cow dung instead of human dung. You can bake your bread over the cow dung."

**16** He also said to me, "Son of man, I will stop the supply of bread in Jerusalem. The people will weigh their bread and eat it with worry. They will measure their water and drink it with fear.

**17** They will not have bread or water. They will look at each other with shock. They will become weak and die because of their sin."

## Chapter 5

**1** "Son of man, take a sharp sword. Use it as a razor. Shave your head and your beard. Then take scales and divide the hair into 3 parts.

**2** When the days of the attack on the city end, burn 1 third of the hair in the center of the city. Take another third of the hair and cut it with the sword around the city. Throw the last third into the wind. I will chase them with a sword.

**3** Take a small number of hairs and tie them in the edge of your clothes.

**4** Then take some of these hairs again and throw them into the fire. Burn them. A fire will come from there against all the people of Israel.

**5** The Lord GOD says this: "This is Jerusalem. I put her in the center of the nations, with countries around her.

**6** But she rebelled against my laws and my rules. She did more evil than the nations and the countries around her. Her people rejected my laws. They did not obey my rules.

**7** Thus the Lord GOD says this: You caused more trouble than the nations around you. You did not obey my rules. You did not keep my laws. You did not even obey the laws of the nations around you.

**8** Thus the Lord GOD says this: I am against you, Jerusalem. I will punish you while the nations watch.

**9** Because of all your detestable idols, I will do to you what I never did before. I will never do it again.

**10** Thus in Jerusalem fathers will eat their sons, and sons will eat their fathers. I will punish you. I will throw all your people who stay alive to the winds.

**11** As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, I will cut you down. You made my holy temple unclean with all your detestable idols and evil things. I will not spare you. I will have no pity.

**12** One third of your people will die from disease and famine in the city. One third will die by the sword around the city. I will throw one third to the winds and chase them with a sword.

**13** Then my anger will be complete. I will pour out my anger on them, and then I will be calm. When I complete my anger against them, they will know that I, the LORD, spoke because of my strong love.

**14** I will make you a ruin. The nations around you will insult you. All the people who go past will see this.

**15** You will become a thing that the nations around you insult and laugh at. You will be an example that teaches and frightens them. This will occur when I punish you with anger and strong correction. I, the LORD, said it.

**16** I will send against you the terrible arrows of famine that destroy. I will send them to destroy you. I will make the famine worse. I will stop your supply of bread.

**17** I will send famine and wild animals against you. They will kill your children. Disease and violent death will go through your land. I will bring the sword against you. I, the LORD, said it."

## Chapter 6

**1** The LORD spoke his word to me. He said,

**2** "Son of man, turn your face toward the mountains of Israel. Speak as a prophet against them.

**3** Say, 'Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD. The Lord GOD says this to the mountains, the hills, the ravines, and the valleys: I will bring a sword against you. I will destroy your high places of worship.

**4** Your altars will become ruins. I will break your incense altars. I will throw down your dead people in front of your idols.

**5** I will put the dead bodies of the people of Israel in front of their idols. I will throw your bones around your altars.

**6** In all the places where you live, your towns will become ruins. Your high places will be empty. Your altars will be ruins. People will break your idols, and the idols will stop. People will cut down your incense altars. All that you made will be gone.

**7** Your people will die among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**8** But I will let some of you stay alive. Some of you will escape the sword. I will send you to live among other nations and countries.

**9** The people who escape will remember me in the nations where they are prisoners. They will remember how I felt pain because of their unfaithful hearts. They left me and chased their idols. Then they will hate themselves for all the evil and detestable things that they did.

**10** They will know that I am the LORD. They will know that my threat to bring this disaster on them was not empty.

**11** The Lord GOD says this: Clap your hands and stamp your foot. Say, "Oh, how terrible are all the evil and detestable acts of the people of Israel!" They will die by the sword, by famine, and by disease.

**12** People who are far away will die from disease. People who are near will die by the sword. People who stay in the city under attack will die from famine. Thus I will complete my anger against them.

**13** Their dead people will lie among their idols around their altars. They will lie on each high hill, on all the tops of the mountains, and under each green tree and each thick oak. In these places they burned incense to all their idols. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**14** I will put out my hand against them. I will make the land empty, from the desert to Diblah. I will make all the places where they live empty. Then they will know that I am the LORD.'"

## Chapter 7

**1** The LORD spoke his word to me again. He said,

**2** "Son of man, the Lord GOD says this to the land of Israel: The end comes! The end comes on all 4 corners of the land.

**3** Now the end comes on you. I will send my anger against you. I will judge you for your actions. I will punish you for all your detestable acts.

**4** I will not spare you. I will have no pity. I will punish you for your actions and for your detestable acts among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**5** The Lord GOD says this: Disaster comes! One disaster after another disaster comes!

**6** The end comes! The end comes! It is ready to attack you. It comes!

**7** People of the land, your destruction comes. The time comes. The day of trouble is near. There will be no shouts of joy on the mountains.

**8** Soon I will pour out my anger on you. I will complete my anger against you. I will judge you for your actions. I will punish you for all your detestable acts.

**9** I will not spare you. I will have no pity. I will punish you for your actions and for your detestable acts among you. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am the one who punishes you.

**10** Look, the day comes! Your destruction comes! Violence grows like a plant. Pride grows like a flower.

**11** Violence grows into a rod to punish evil. None of the people will stay alive. None of their crowds and none of their wealth will stay. Nothing of value will stay among them.

**12** The time comes. The day is near. The buyer must not be glad. The seller must not be sad. My anger is on all the crowds of people.

**13** The seller will not get back what he sold, while both of them are alive. My vision is for all the crowd, and it will not change. No person will save his life because of his sin.

**14** The people blow the trumpet and make all things ready. But no person goes to the battle, because my anger is on all the crowd.

**15** Outside the city, there is the sword. Inside the city, there are disease and famine. People in the field will die by the sword. Famine and disease will kill the people in the city.

**16** Some people will escape to the mountains. They will be like doves of the valleys. Each person will cry in sorrow for his sin.

**17** All hands will become weak. All knees will become as weak as water.

**18** They will wear sackcloth, and terror will cover them. Shame will be on all their faces. They will shave all their heads.

**19** They will throw their silver into the streets. Their gold will be like an unclean thing. Their silver and gold cannot save them on the day of the anger of the LORD. Their money cannot satisfy their hunger or fill their stomachs. Their money caused them to sin.

**20** They were proud of their beautiful jewelry. They used it to make their detestable idols. Thus I will make their jewelry an unclean thing to them.

**21** I will give their wealth to foreigners. Evil people of the earth will take it and make it unclean.

**22** I will turn my face away from my people. Robbers will go into my holy place and make it unclean.

**23** Make chains, because the land is full of murder and the city is full of violence.

**24** I will bring the most evil of the nations. They will take the houses of my people. I will stop the pride of the strong. Their holy places will become unclean.

**25** Terror comes! The people will look for peace, but they will find no peace.

**26** Disaster after disaster will come. One bad report after another bad report will come. The people will look for a vision from the prophet. But the priests will not teach the law, and the leaders will not give advice.

**27** The king will cry in sorrow. The prince will be full of despair. The hands of the people of the land will shake with fear. I will do to them what they did. I will judge them as they judged other people. Then they will know that I am the LORD."

## Chapter 8

**1** In the 6th year, on the 5th day of the 6th month, I sat in my house. The leaders of Judah sat in front of me. There the power of the Lord GOD came on me.

**2** I looked and saw a shape like a man. From his waist down, he looked like fire. From his waist up, he was bright like polished metal.

**3** He put out a shape like a hand and took me by the hair of my head. The Spirit lifted me up between the earth and the sky. In visions from God he took me to Jerusalem. He took me to the entrance of the north gate of the inner court. There was an idol in that place. The idol caused God to become angry and jealous.

**4** The glory of the God of Israel was there. It was like the vision that I saw in the plain.

**5** Then he said to me, "Son of man, look toward the north." Thus I looked toward the north. North of the altar gate, at the entrance, I saw the idol that caused jealousy.

**6** He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they do? The people of Israel do very detestable things here. These things push me away from my holy place. But turn again, and you will see things that are more detestable."

**7** Then he took me to the entrance of the court. I looked and saw a hole in the wall.

**8** He said to me, "Son of man, dig through the wall." Thus I dug through the wall and found a door.

**9** He said to me, "Go in and see the evil and detestable things that they do here."

**10** Thus I went in and looked. On all the walls I saw pictures of all types of animals that crawl and unclean animals. I also saw all the idols of the people of Israel.

**11** In front of these pictures stood 70 leaders of the people of Israel. Jaazaniah, the son of Shaphan, stood among them. Each man had a pan for incense in his hand. A thick cloud of the smoke of incense went up.

**12** He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what the leaders of Israel do in the dark? Each man is in the room of his own idol. They say, 'The LORD does not see us. The LORD left the land.'"

**13** He also said to me, "Turn again, and you will see them do things that are more detestable."

**14** Then he took me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD. I saw women who sat there. They cried for the god Tammuz.

**15** He said to me, "Son of man, do you see this? Turn again, and you will see things that are more detestable than these."

**16** Then he took me into the inner court of the house of the LORD. At the entrance of the temple, between the porch and the altar, there were about 25 men. Their backs were toward the temple of the LORD, and their faces were toward the east. They bowed down to the sun in the east.

**17** He said to me, "Son of man, do you see this? Are these detestable things that the people of Judah do here a small matter? They fill the land with violence. They make me angry again and again. Look, they put a branch to their nose to insult me.

**18** Thus I will act in my anger. I will not spare them. I will have no pity. They will shout in my ears with a loud voice, but I will not listen to them."

## Chapter 9

**1** Then I heard him shout with a loud voice. He said, "Bring near the men who will punish the city. Each man must have a weapon in his hand to destroy."

**2** I saw 6 men come from the upper gate, which faces north. Each man had a weapon in his hand to kill. With them was a man who wore linen clothes. He had a writer's case at his side. They went in and stood next to the bronze altar.

**3** Then the glory of the God of Israel went up from above the cherub, an angel with wings. The glory moved to the entrance of the temple. The LORD called to the man who wore linen clothes and had the writer's case at his side.

**4** The LORD said to him, "Go through all the city of Jerusalem. Put a mark on the foreheads of the men who are sad and cry about all the detestable things that people do in the city."

**5** I heard him say to the other men, "Follow him through the city and kill. Do not spare any person. Have no pity.

**6** Kill old men, young men, young women, little children, and women. But do not touch any person who has the mark. Start at my holy temple." Thus they started with the leaders who were in front of the temple.

**7** He said to them, "Make the temple unclean. Fill the courts with dead bodies. Go!" Thus they went out and killed the people in the city.

**8** While they killed the people, I was alone. I fell down with my face to the ground. I cried out, "Oh, Lord GOD! Will you destroy all the people of Israel who stay alive, when you pour out your anger on Jerusalem?"

**9** He said to me, "The sin of the people of Israel and Judah is very great. The land is full of murder. The city is full of injustice. They say, 'The LORD left the land. The LORD does not see.'

**10** Thus I will not spare them. I will have no pity. I will punish them for what they did."

**11** Then the man who wore linen clothes and had the writer's case at his side came back. He said, "I did all that you commanded me."

## Chapter 10

**1** Then I looked at the dome above the heads of the cherubim. Above them I saw a shape like a throne. It looked like a sapphire stone.

**2** The LORD said to the man who wore linen clothes, "Go in between the wheels under the cherubim. Fill your hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim. Throw the coals over the city." While I watched, the man went in.

**3** When the man went in, the cherubim stood on the south side of the temple. A cloud filled the inner court.

**4** Then the glory of the LORD went up from above the cherub. It moved to the entrance of the temple. The cloud filled the temple. The court was full of the bright light of the glory of the LORD.

**5** People could hear the sound of the wings of the cherubim in the outer court. It was like the voice of God Almighty when he speaks.

**6** The LORD commanded the man who wore linen clothes, "Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubim." Then the man went in and stood next to a wheel.

**7** One cherub put out his hand to the fire between the cherubim. He took some of the fire and put it into the hands of the man who wore linen clothes. The man took the fire and went out.

**8** The cherubim had the shape of the hands of a man under their wings.

**9** I looked and saw 4 wheels next to the cherubim, one wheel next to each cherub. The wheels shone like a beryl stone.

**10** All 4 wheels looked the same. Each wheel looked like a wheel inside another wheel.

**11** When the wheels moved, they went in any of the 4 directions. They did not turn when they moved. The wheels went in the direction that the head of the cherub faced. They did not turn when they moved.

**12** The whole bodies of the cherubim were full of eyes. Their backs, their hands, their wings, and their 4 wheels were full of eyes all around.

**13** I heard a voice that called the wheels "the whirlwind."

**14** Each cherub had 4 faces. The first face was the face of a cherub. The second face was the face of a man. The third face was the face of a lion. The fourth face was the face of an eagle.

**15** Then the cherubim went up. These were the creatures that I saw near the Chebar River.

**16** When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved next to them. When the cherubim spread their wings to go up from the ground, the wheels stayed next to them.

**17** When the cherubim stopped, the wheels stopped. When the cherubim went up, the wheels went up with them. The spirit of the creatures was in the wheels.

**18** Then the glory of the LORD went away from the entrance of the temple. It stopped above the cherubim.

**19** While I watched, the cherubim spread their wings and went up from the ground. The wheels went with them. They stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD. The glory of the God of Israel was above them.

**20** These were the creatures that I saw under the God of Israel near the Chebar River. I knew that they were cherubim.

**21** Each cherub had 4 faces and 4 wings. Under their wings there was a shape like the hands of a man.

**22** Their faces looked the same as the faces that I saw near the Chebar River. Each cherub went straight forward.

## Chapter 11

**1** Then the Spirit lifted me up and took me to the east gate of the house of the LORD. At the entrance of the gate there were 25 men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah, the son of Azzur, and Pelatiah, the son of Benaiah. These men were leaders of the people.

**2** The LORD said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who plan evil and give bad advice in this city.

**3** They say, 'Soon we will build houses again. This city is a pot, and we are the meat in it. The pot will keep us safe.'

**4** Thus speak as a prophet against them. Speak as a prophet, son of man."

**5** Then the Spirit of the LORD came on me. He told me to say, "The LORD says this: People of Israel, I know what you say. I know all your thoughts.

**6** You killed many people in this city. You filled its streets with dead bodies.

**7** Thus the Lord GOD says this: The people that you killed in the city are the meat. The city is the pot. But I will take you out of the city.

**8** You are afraid of the sword. Thus I will bring the sword against you, says the Lord GOD.

**9** I will take you out of the city. I will give you to foreigners. I will punish you.

**10** You will die by the sword. I will punish you at the border of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**11** This city will not be a pot to protect you. You will not be the meat in it. I will punish you at the border of Israel.

**12** Then you will know that I am the LORD. You did not obey my rules or keep my laws. You followed the customs of the nations around you."

**13** While I spoke as a prophet, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. I fell down with my face to the ground. I cried with a loud voice, "Oh, Lord GOD! Will you destroy all the people of Israel who stay alive?"

**14** The LORD spoke his word to me again. He said,

**15** "Son of man, the people in Jerusalem speak about your brothers, your relatives, and all the people of Israel in exile. They say, 'Those people are far away from the LORD. The LORD gave this land to us.'

**16** Thus say, 'The Lord GOD says this: I sent my people far away among the nations. I sent them to many countries. But for a short time, I am a holy place for them in the countries where they went.'

**17** Thus say, 'The Lord GOD says this: I will bring you back from the nations. I will gather you from the countries where I sent you. I will give you the land of Israel again.'

**18** They will come back to the land. They will remove all its evil idols and all its detestable things.

**19** I will give them one heart. I will put a new spirit inside them. I will take away their heart of stone. I will give them a heart of flesh.

**20** Then they will obey my rules and keep my laws. They will be my people, and I will be their God.

**21** But some people love their evil idols and detestable things. I will punish them for what they did, says the Lord GOD."

**22** Then the cherubim spread their wings, and the wheels were next to them. The glory of the God of Israel was above them.

**23** The glory of the LORD went up from the city. It stopped above the mountain on the east side of the city.

**24** Then the Spirit lifted me up. In a vision from the Spirit of God, he took me to the exiles in Chaldea. Then the vision went away from me.

**25** I told the exiles all the things that the LORD showed me.

## Chapter 12

**1** The LORD spoke his word to me. He said,

**2** "Son of man, you live among a people who rebel. They have eyes to see, but they do not see. They have ears to hear, but they do not hear. They are a people who rebel.

**3** Thus, son of man, prepare a bag for exile. In the day, while they watch, leave your place and go to another place. Possibly they will understand, but they are a people who rebel.

**4** In the day, while they watch, bring out your bag as a bag for exile. In the evening, while they watch, go out like people who go into exile.

**5** While they watch, dig a hole through the wall. Carry your bag out through the hole.

**6** While they watch, put the bag on your shoulder. Carry it out in the dark. Cover your face so that you cannot see the land. I made you a sign to the people of Israel."

**7** I did what the LORD commanded me. In the day, I brought out my bag as a bag for exile. In the evening, I dug through the wall with my hands. I took my bag out in the dark. I carried it on my shoulder while they watched.

**8** In the morning, the LORD spoke his word to me. He said,

**9** "Son of man, the people of Israel, who rebel, asked you, 'What do you do?'

**10** Say to them, 'The Lord GOD says this: This message is about the prince in Jerusalem and all the people of Israel who live there.'

**11** Say, 'I am a sign to you. The same thing that I did will happen to you. You will go into exile as prisoners.'

**12** The prince among them will put his bag on his shoulder in the dark and go out. The people will dig a hole through the wall for him. He will cover his face so that he cannot see the land.

**13** I will put my net over him, and my trap will catch him. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans. But he will not see that land, and he will die there.

**14** I will send all the people around him in all directions. I will send away his helpers and all his soldiers. I will chase them with a sword.

**15** When I send them among the nations and the countries, they will know that I am the LORD.

**16** But I will let a few of them escape the sword, famine, and disease. They will tell about all their detestable acts among the nations where they go. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD."

**17** The LORD spoke his word to me again. He said,

**18** "Son of man, shake with fear while you eat your bread. Shake with worry while you drink your water.

**19** Then tell the people of the land, 'The Lord GOD says this about the people of Jerusalem and the land of Israel. They will eat their bread with worry. They will drink their water with fear. The violence of all the people who live there will cause their land to lose all things in it.

**20** The towns where people live will become ruins. The land will be empty. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"

**21** The LORD spoke his word to me. He said,

**22** "Son of man, the people of Israel say a proverb. They say, 'Time goes by, and each vision fails.' Why do they say this?

**23** Thus tell them, 'The Lord GOD says this: I will stop this proverb. People will not use it in Israel again.' Tell them, 'The time is near when each vision will come true.'

**24** There will be no more false visions or false messages among the people of Israel.

**25** I am the LORD. I will speak, and my word will come true without delay. You people who rebel, in your lifetime I will speak my word and do it, says the Lord GOD."

**26** The LORD spoke his word to me again. He said,

**27** "Son of man, the people of Israel say, 'His visions are for a time many years from now. He speaks about the far future.'

**28** Thus tell them, 'The Lord GOD says this: There will be no more delay for my words. What I say will happen, says the Lord GOD.'"

## Chapter 13

**1** The LORD spoke his word to me. He said,

**2** "Son of man, speak against the prophets of Israel who now speak as prophets. Speak to the prophets who invent their messages. Say, 'Hear the word of the LORD.

**3** The Lord GOD says this: Terrible things will happen to the foolish prophets. They follow their own ideas and saw nothing.

**4** Israel, your prophets are like foxes among ruins.

**5** You did not go up to repair the holes in the wall. You did not build the wall again for the people of Israel. Thus they cannot stand in the battle on the day of the LORD.

**6** Their visions are false and their messages are lies. They say, "The LORD says this." But the LORD did not send them. They expect him to make their words come true.

**7** Your visions are false, and your messages are lies. You say, "The LORD says this." But I did not speak.

**8** Thus the Lord GOD says this: You speak false words and see false visions. Thus I am against you, says the Lord GOD.

**9** I will put my hand against the prophets who see false visions and speak lies. They will not be in the assembly of my people. Their names will not be in the record of the people of Israel. They will not go into the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.

**10** They told lies to my people. They said, "There is peace," but there is no peace. My people build a weak wall, and the prophets cover it with whitewash.

**11** Tell the prophets who cover the wall with whitewash that the wall will fall. Heavy rain will come. I will send large hailstones. A strong wind will break the wall.

**12** When the wall falls, people will ask you, "Where is the whitewash that you put on the wall?"

**13** Thus the Lord GOD says this: In my anger I will send a strong wind against the wall. In my anger I will send heavy rain and large hailstones to destroy it.

**14** I will break down the wall that you covered with whitewash. I will push it down to the ground. People will see its foundation. When the wall falls, you will die under it. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**15** Thus I will use all my anger against the wall and against the people who covered it with whitewash. I will say to you, "The wall is gone, and the men who covered it are gone."

**16** These men are the prophets of Israel who spoke about Jerusalem. They saw visions of peace for her, but there is no peace, says the Lord GOD.'

**17** Son of man, turn your face against the women of your people who invent their messages. Speak as a prophet against them.

**18** Say, 'The Lord GOD says this: Terrible things will happen to the women who sew magic charms for all wrists. They make veils of all sizes for the heads of people. They use these things to trap people. You trap the lives of my people, but you try to save your own lives.

**19** You made me unclean among my people for some barley and some pieces of bread. You killed people who must not die. You kept alive people who must not live. You did this with lies to my people, who listen to lies.

**20** Thus the Lord GOD says this: I am against your magic charms. You use them to trap people like birds. I will tear the charms from your arms. I will set free the people that you trap like birds.

**21** I will also tear your veils. I will save my people from your power. They will not be in your power again. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**22** With your lies, you made good people sad, but I did not make them sad. You helped evil people continue in their evil ways. You did not tell them to stop their evil ways to save their lives.

**23** Thus you will not see false visions or do magic again. I will save my people from your power. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"

## Chapter 14

**1** Some of the leaders of Israel came to me and sat in front of me.

**2** Then the LORD spoke his word to me. He said,

**3** "Son of man, these men put idols in their hearts. They put their sin in front of their faces, and it causes them to fall. Must I let them ask me for help?

**4** Thus speak to them. Tell them, 'The Lord GOD says this: Some of the people of Israel put idols in their hearts. They put their sin in front of their faces, and it causes them to fall. Then they come to a prophet. I, the LORD, will answer each of these people as their many idols deserve.

**5** I will do this to win back the hearts of the people of Israel. All of them left me because of their idols.'

**6** Thus tell the people of Israel, 'The Lord GOD says this: Repent! Turn away from your idols. Turn your faces away from all your detestable acts.

**7** Some people of Israel, or some foreigners who live in Israel, leave me. They put idols in their hearts. They put their sin in front of their faces, and it causes them to fall. Then they come to a prophet to ask about me. I, the LORD, will answer them myself.

**8** I will turn my face against that person. I will make him a sign and an example of shame. I will remove him from my people. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**9** If someone tricks a prophet and the prophet gives a message, I, the LORD, let someone trick that prophet. I will put my hand against him. I will destroy him from among my people Israel.

**10** They will get the punishment for their sin. The prophet will get the same punishment as the person who asks him for help.

**11** Then the people of Israel will not go away from me again. They will not make themselves unclean again with all their sins. They will be my people, and I will be their God, says the Lord GOD.'"

**12** The LORD spoke his word to me again. He said,

**13** "Son of man, a land can sin against me and be unfaithful. Then I will put out my hand against it. I will stop its supply of bread. I will send famine on it. I will kill its people and animals.

**14** Possibly these 3 men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, will be in that land. But because they are good, they will save only their own lives, says the Lord GOD.

**15** Possibly I will send wild animals through the land to kill its children. The land will become empty. No person will go through it because of the animals.

**16** As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, these 3 men will not save their sons or daughters. They will save only themselves. The land will become empty.

**17** Possibly I will bring a sword against that land. I will say, 'Sword, go through the land.' I will kill its people and animals.

**18** As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, these 3 men will not save their sons or daughters. They will save only themselves.

**19** Possibly I will send disease into that land. I will pour out my anger on it with death. I will kill its people and animals.

**20** As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, Noah, Daniel, and Job will not save their sons or daughters. Because they are good, they will save only their own lives.

**21** The Lord GOD says this: My punishment on Jerusalem will be much worse. I will send my 4 terrible punishments against Jerusalem. I will send the sword, famine, wild animals, and disease to kill its people and animals.

**22** But some people will stay alive. Some sons and daughters will come out of the city. They will come to you. You will see their ways and their actions. Then you will feel comfort about the disaster that I brought on Jerusalem. You will feel comfort about all the things that I brought on the city.

**23** You will feel comfort when you see their ways and their actions. You will know that I had a good reason for all that I did in Jerusalem, says the Lord GOD."

## Chapter 15

**1** The LORD spoke his word to me. He said,

**2** "Son of man, is the wood of a vine better than the wood of other trees? Is a vine branch better than the branches of the trees in the forest?

**3** Can people use its wood to make something useful? Can people make a peg from it to hang things on?

**4** No, people throw it into the fire as fuel. The fire burns both ends, and it burns the center. Is it useful for any work now?

**5** When it was complete, people could not use it for any work. Now the fire burned it. Thus it is even less useful for any work.

**6** Thus the Lord GOD says this: I gave the wood of the vine to the fire as fuel. In the same way, I will give the people of Jerusalem to the fire.

**7** I will turn my face against them. They escaped from one fire, but another fire will burn them. When I turn my face against them, you will know that I am the LORD.

**8** I will make the land empty, because the people were unfaithful to me, says the Lord GOD."

## Chapter 16

**1** The word of the LORD came to me again. He said,

**2** "Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her hateful actions.

**3** Say, 'The Lord GOD says this to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth are from the land of Canaan. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.

**4** On the day of your birth, no person cut your cord. No person washed you with water to make you clean. No person rubbed you with salt or put cloths around you.

**5** No person felt pity for you or did these things for you. No person showed you kindness. On the day of your birth, people threw you out into the open field because they hated you.

**6** I went past you and I saw you. You moved about in your blood. While you lay in your blood, I said to you, "Live!" I said to you again, "Live!"

**7** I caused you to grow like a plant in the field. You grew and became tall. You became very beautiful. Your breasts became full and your hair grew. But you were naked and you had no clothes.

**8** Then I went past you again and I looked at you. You were at the age for love. I put the edge of my robe over you and I covered your naked body. I made a promise to you. I made an agreement (covenant) with you, says the Lord GOD. Then you became mine.

**9** I washed you with water. I washed all the blood from you. Then I put oil on you.

**10** I put clothes with decorations on you. I gave you shoes of fine leather. I put fine linen and silk on you.

**11** I gave you jewelry. I put bracelets on your arms and a chain on your neck.

**12** I put a ring in your nose and earrings in your ears. I put a beautiful crown on your head.

**13** Thus you had gold and silver jewelry. Your clothes were of fine linen, silk and cloth with decorations. You ate fine flour, honey and oil. You became very beautiful, and you became a queen.

**14** The nations heard about your beauty. Your beauty was perfect because of the glory that I gave you, says the Lord GOD.

**15** "But you trusted in your beauty. You used your fame to become a prostitute. You gave yourself to each man who went past. You let him have your beauty.

**16** You took some of your clothes. You made shrines with many colors on the high places. There you acted as a prostitute. Such things must not occur, and they will not occur again.

**17** You took the beautiful jewelry of gold and silver that I gave you. You used it to make male idols, and you worshipped them as a prostitute does.

**18** You took your clothes with decorations and you put them on the idols. You put my oil and my incense in front of the idols.

**19** I gave you food: fine flour, oil and honey. You put this food in front of the idols as an offering with a pleasant smell. That is what you did, says the Lord GOD.

**20** You took the sons and the daughters that you gave birth to for me. You sacrificed them to the idols as food. Your prostitution was not sufficient for you.

**21** You killed my children. You gave them to the idols and you burned them in the fire.

**22** You did all your hateful actions and your prostitution. But you did not remember the days when you were young. Then you were naked and you had no clothes, and you moved about in your blood.

**23** "'You did all these bad things. Then trouble will come to you! Trouble will come to you! says the Lord GOD.

**24** You built a shrine for yourself. You made a high place in each public area.

**25** You built your high place at the start of each street. You made your beauty a hateful thing. You offered your body to each man who went past. You did more and more acts of prostitution.

**26** You did acts of prostitution with your neighbors, the Egyptians, who have strong sexual desire. You did more and more acts of prostitution to make me angry.

**27** Thus I put out my hand against you. I decreased the food that I gave you. I gave you to the women who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines. They felt shame because of your bad actions.

**28** You also acted as a prostitute with the Assyrians, because you were never satisfied. You did acts of prostitution with them. But you were still not satisfied.

**29** You did more acts of prostitution with Babylonia, the land of the merchants. But even then you did not have enough.

**30** "'Your heart is very weak, says the Lord GOD. You do all these things. You act like a prostitute who has no shame.

**31** You built your shrine at the start of each street. You made your high place in each public area. But you were not like a prostitute, because you did not take payment.

**32** You are like a wife who commits adultery. She takes strangers into her bed in place of her husband.

**33** Men give payment to all prostitutes. But you gave gifts to all your lovers. You paid them to come to you from all directions for your prostitution.

**34** You are different from other women in your prostitution. No man asks you to become a prostitute. You give payment, but no man gives payment to you. Thus you are different.

**35** "'Thus, you prostitute, hear the word of the LORD!

**36** The Lord GOD says this: You showed your lust. You showed your naked body in your prostitution with your lovers and with all your hateful idols. You gave the blood of your children to the idols.

**37** Thus I will gather all your lovers. I will gather the people that you loved and the people that you hated. I will gather them around you to attack you. I will show your naked body to them, and they will see all of it.

**38** I will punish you as judges punish women who commit adultery and kill people. My anger and my jealousy will cause your blood to flow.

**39** I will give you to your lovers. They will break down your shrines and your high places. They will take off your clothes and your beautiful jewelry. They will leave you naked, with no clothes.

**40** They will bring a crowd against you. The crowd will throw stones at you and cut you with their swords.

**41** They will burn your houses. They will punish you while many women watch. I will stop your prostitution. You will not pay lovers again.

**42** Then my anger against you will stop. My jealousy will go away from you. I will be calm, and I will not be angry again.

**43** "'You did not remember the days when you were young. You made me angry with all these things. Thus I will punish you for what you did, says the Lord GOD. You added this sexual sin to all your other hateful actions.

**44** "'Each person who uses proverbs will say this proverb about you: "The daughter is like her mother."

**45** You are the daughter of your mother. She hated her husband and her children. You are the sister of your sisters. They hated their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father was an Amorite.

**46** Your older sister is Samaria. She lives with her daughters to the north of you. Your younger sister is Sodom. She lives with her daughters to the south of you.

**47** You did the same hateful actions as they did. But soon you did worse things than they did in all your ways.

**48** As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters did not do the things that you did. You and your daughters did worse.

**49** "'This was the sin of your sister Sodom. She and her daughters were proud. They had much food and much free time. But they did not help the poor and the needy.

**50** They were proud and they did hateful things in front of me. Thus I removed them when I saw what they did.

**51** Samaria did not do half of your sins. You did more hateful things than your sisters did. Your sins make your sisters seem good.

**52** You must feel your shame. Your sins were worse than the sins of your sisters, and thus they seem more righteous than you. Feel your shame, because you made your sisters seem good.

**53** "'I will make Sodom and her daughters wealthy again. I will make Samaria and her daughters wealthy again. And I will make you wealthy again with them.

**54** Then you will feel your shame. You will feel shame because of all that you did. Your sins will comfort your sisters.

**55** Your sisters, Sodom and Samaria, and their daughters will return to their old condition. Then you and your daughters will also return to your old condition.

**56** At the time of your pride, you did not speak about your sister Sodom.

**57** That was before the people saw your bad actions. Now the daughters of Syria and all the people around her speak badly about you. The daughters of the Philistines and all the nations around you hate you.

**58** You must feel the punishment for your sexual sins and your hateful actions, says the LORD.

**59** "'The Lord GOD says this: I will do to you what you did. You did not obey your promise, and you broke the covenant.

**60** But I will remember the covenant that I made with you when you were young. I will make a covenant with you that will continue for all time.

**61** Then you will remember your ways, and you will feel shame. You will receive your sisters, the older and the younger. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of your covenant.

**62** I will make my covenant with you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**63** I will forgive you for all that you did. Then you will remember and feel shame. You will not speak again because of your shame, says the Lord GOD.'"

## Chapter 17

**1** The word of the LORD came to me. He said,

**2** "Son of man, tell a riddle to the people of Israel. Tell them a story with a meaning.

**3** Say, 'The Lord GOD says this: A large eagle came to Lebanon. The eagle had large, long wings and many feathers of many colors. The eagle took the top of a cedar tree.

**4** The eagle broke off the highest branch. The eagle took it to a land of trade. The eagle put it in a city of merchants.

**5** Then the eagle took some seed from the land of Israel. The eagle planted the seed in good soil near much water. The eagle planted it like a willow tree.

**6** The seed grew and became a low vine that spread out. The branches of the vine turned toward the eagle, and its roots stayed under the eagle. Thus it became a vine with many branches and leaves.

**7** "'There was another large eagle with large wings and many feathers. The vine turned its roots toward this eagle. The vine sent its branches toward this eagle to get water from it.

**8** But the first eagle planted the vine in good soil near much water. The vine could grow branches and fruit, and become a good vine.'

**9** "Say, 'The Lord GOD says this: Will the vine grow well? No! The first eagle will pull up its roots and remove its fruit. Then the vine will become dry. All its new leaves will become dry. No strong army and no large group of people will be necessary to pull up the vine.

**10** The vine is in the ground now, but will it grow well? No! It will become dry when the east wind touches it. It will become dry in the soil where it grew.'"

**11** Then the word of the LORD came to me. He said,

**12** "Speak to these people who rebel against me. Say, 'Do you not know the meaning of these things?' Tell them, 'The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem. He took the king of Jerusalem and the officials and brought them to Babylon.

**13** Then he took a man from the royal family and made an agreement with him. He made the man promise to obey him. He also took away the important men of the land.

**14** He did this to make the kingdom weak, so that it could not become strong again. The kingdom could continue only if the king obeyed the agreement.

**15** But the king of Judah rebelled against the king of Babylon. He sent officials to Egypt to get horses and a large army. Will the king of Judah succeed? Will he escape after he does these things? He broke the agreement. Will he escape? No!

**16** As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, the king of Judah will die in Babylon. He will die in the country of the king who made him king. He did not obey his promise to that king, and he broke the agreement.

**17** Pharaoh, with his strong army and his large group of soldiers, will not help the king of Judah in the war. The Babylonians will build ramps and walls to kill many people.

**18** The king of Judah did not obey his promise and he broke the agreement. He gave his hand to make a promise, but he did all these things. He will not escape.

**19** "'Thus the Lord GOD says this: As surely as I live, I will punish him. He did not obey my promise, and he broke my covenant.

**20** I will put my net over him, and my trap will catch him. I will take him to Babylon. There I will judge him because he was not loyal to me.

**21** The enemy will kill all his best soldiers with the sword. The people who stay alive will go away in all directions. Then you will know that I, the LORD, spoke.'

**22** "The Lord GOD says this: 'I will take a small branch from the top of a tall cedar. I will plant it. I will break off a soft new shoot from the highest branches. I will plant it on a high mountain.

**23** I will plant it on the high mountain of Israel. It will grow branches and fruit, and it will become a good cedar. All types of birds will live under it. They will live in the shade of its branches.

**24** Then all the trees of the field will know that I am the LORD. I bring down the tall tree and make the low tree tall. I make the green tree dry and I make the dry tree grow. I, the LORD, spoke, and I will do it.'"

## Chapter 18

**1** The word of the LORD came to me again. He said,

**2** "Why do you use this proverb about the land of Israel? You say, 'The fathers ate sour grapes, but the teeth of the children feel the sour taste.'

**3** As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, you will not use this proverb in Israel again.

**4** All people are mine. The father is mine, and the son is mine. The person who sins is the person who will die.

**5** "Think about a man who is righteous. He does what is fair and correct.

**6** He does not eat at the shrines on the mountains. He does not worship the idols of the people of Israel. He does not have sex with the wife of his neighbor. He does not have sex with a woman during her monthly period.

**7** He does not cause injury to other people. He gives back what a borrower gave him as a guarantee. He does not steal. He gives his food to hungry people and he gives clothes to people who have no clothes.

**8** He does not lend money for interest or take profit from a loan. He does not do wrong things. He judges fairly between people.

**9** He obeys my laws and keeps my rules. He is loyal. That man is righteous. He will surely live, says the Lord GOD.

**10** "But possibly that man has a son who is violent. The son steals and kills people. He does these bad things.

**11** The father does not do these things, but the son does. The son eats at the shrines on the mountains. He has sex with the wife of his neighbor.

**12** He causes injury to the poor and the needy. He steals. He does not give back what a borrower gave him as a guarantee. He worships idols and he does hateful things.

**13** He lends money for interest and takes profit. Will that son live? No, he will not live! He did all these hateful things. He will surely die. He is responsible for his death.

**14** "But possibly that son has a son of his own. The grandson sees all the sins of his father. He thinks about them and he does not do such things.

**15** He does not eat at the shrines on the mountains. He does not worship the idols of the people of Israel. He does not have sex with the wife of his neighbor.

**16** He does not cause injury to other people. He does not keep what a borrower gave him as a guarantee. He does not steal. He gives his food to hungry people and he gives clothes to people who have no clothes.

**17** He does not cause injury to the poor. He does not take interest or profit. He obeys my rules and my laws. He will not die for the sins of his father. He will surely live.

**18** But his father caused injury to other people and stole from his brother. He did bad things among his people. Thus the father will die because of his sins.

**19** "But you ask, 'Why does the son not get the punishment for the sins of his father?' The son did what is fair and correct. He obeyed all my laws. Thus he will surely live.

**20** The person who sins is the person who will die. The son will not get the punishment for the sins of his father. The father will not get the punishment for the sins of his son. A righteous person will get the result of his righteous actions. A wicked person will get the result of his wicked actions.

**21** "But possibly a wicked person stops all the sins that he did. He obeys all my laws and does what is fair and correct. Then he will surely live. He will not die.

**22** I will not remember any of his sins. He will live because of the righteous things that he did.

**23** Do I like to see the death of a wicked person? says the Lord GOD. No! I want him to stop his bad ways and live.

**24** "But possibly a righteous person stops his righteous actions and starts to sin. He does all the hateful things that the wicked person does. Will he live? No! I will not remember any of the righteous things that he did. He was not loyal and he sinned. Thus he will die.

**25** "But you say, 'The way of the Lord is not fair.' Hear me, people of Israel! My way is fair. It is your ways that are not fair.

**26** If a righteous person stops his righteous actions and starts to sin, then he will die. He will die because of the sin that he did.

**27** If a wicked person stops his wicked actions and does what is fair and correct, then he will save his life.

**28** He thinks about his sins and he stops all of them. Thus he will surely live. He will not die.

**29** But the people of Israel say, 'The way of the Lord is not fair.' People of Israel, my ways are fair. It is your ways that are not fair.

**30** "Thus I will judge each of you, people of Israel, by what you do, says the Lord GOD. Repent! Stop all your sins. Then your sins will not destroy you.

**31** Throw away all the sins that you did. Get a new heart and a new spirit. People of Israel, why do you want to die?

**32** I do not like to see the death of any person, says the Lord GOD. Thus repent and live!"

## Chapter 19

**1** "Sing a sad song about the princes of Israel.

**2** Say, 'Your mother was like a female lion among lions. She lay down among the young lions and fed her cubs.

**3** She raised one of her cubs, and he became a strong young lion. He learned to catch prey, and he ate people.

**4** The nations heard about him. They caught him in their pit. They put hooks in him and took him to the land of Egypt.

**5** The mother lion waited, but then she saw that she had no hope. Thus she took another of her cubs and made him a strong young lion.

**6** He walked among the lions and became a strong young lion. He learned to catch prey, and he ate people.

**7** He destroyed their strong buildings and their cities. The land and all the people in it were afraid of the noise of his roar.

**8** Then the nations from all the areas around attacked him. They put their net over him, and they caught him in their pit.

**9** They put hooks in him and put him in a cage. They took him to the king of Babylon. They put him in a prison. Thus people did not hear his roar on the mountains of Israel again.

**10** "'Your mother was like a vine that someone planted near water. She had much fruit and many branches because she had much water.

**11** Her branches were strong, and they were good for the scepters of rulers. The vine grew tall above the other branches. People saw her height and her many branches.

**12** But an angry person pulled up the vine and threw her on the ground. The east wind made her fruit dry. Her strong branches broke and became dry. Fire burned them.

**13** Now the vine grows in the desert, in a dry land with no water.

**14** Fire came out from one of her main branches and burned her fruit. She has no strong branch now that can become a scepter for a ruler.' This is a sad song. People will sing it as a sad song."

## Chapter 20

**1** Some of the elders of Israel came to ask the LORD for advice. That was in the 7th year, in the 5th month, on the 10th day of the month. They sat down in front of me.

**2** Then the word of the LORD came to me. He said,

**3** "Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel. Tell them, 'The Lord GOD says this: Did you come to ask me for advice? As surely as I live, I will not give you an answer, says the Lord GOD.'

**4** "Will you judge them, son of man? Will you judge them? Then cause them to know the hateful actions of their ancestors.

**5** Tell them, 'The Lord GOD says this: I chose Israel. I lifted my hand and made a promise to the family of Jacob. I showed myself to them in the land of Egypt. I lifted my hand and said, "I am the LORD your God."

**6** On that day I lifted my hand and made a promise to them. I promised to bring them out of the land of Egypt. I promised to bring them into a land that I found for them. That land has much milk and honey. It is the most beautiful of all lands.

**7** I said to them, "Each of you must throw away the hateful idols that you love. Do not make yourselves unclean with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."

**8** "'But they rebelled against me. They did not listen to me. They did not throw away the hateful idols that they loved. They did not leave the idols of Egypt. Thus I said, "I will show my anger against them in the land of Egypt."

**9** But I did not do it, because I wanted to protect my name. I did not want the nations to dishonor my name. The nations around Israel saw me when I showed myself to Israel. They saw me when I brought Israel out of Egypt.

**10** Thus I brought the people out of the land of Egypt. I brought them into the desert.

**11** I gave them my laws and I showed them my rules. If a person obeys them, then he will live.

**12** I also gave them my Sabbaths as a sign between me and them. The Sabbaths showed that I am the LORD who makes them holy.

**13** "'But the people of Israel rebelled against me in the desert. They did not obey my laws. They refused my rules, but a person who obeys them will live. They made my Sabbaths unholy. Thus I said, "I will show my anger against them in the desert and destroy them."

**14** But I did not do it, because I wanted to protect my name. I did not want the nations to dishonor my name. The nations saw me when I brought Israel out of Egypt.

**15** But I lifted my hand in the desert and made a promise. I promised not to bring them into the land that I gave them. That land has much milk and honey, and it is the most beautiful of all lands.

**16** I did this because they refused my rules and did not obey my laws. They made my Sabbaths unholy. Their hearts wanted their idols.

**17** But I felt pity for them, and I did not destroy them. I did not kill all of them in the desert.

**18** "'I said to their children in the desert, "Do not live as your ancestors lived. Do not obey their rules. Do not make yourselves unclean with their idols.

**19** I am the LORD your God. Obey my laws and keep my rules.

**20** Keep my Sabbaths holy. The Sabbaths will be a sign between me and you. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God."

**21** "'But the children rebelled against me. They did not obey my laws or keep my rules, but a person who obeys them will live. They made my Sabbaths unholy. Thus I said, "I will show my anger against them in the desert."

**22** But I stopped my hand. I did not punish them, because I wanted to protect my name. I did not want the nations to dishonor my name. The nations saw me when I brought Israel out of Egypt.

**23** I also lifted my hand in the desert and made a promise. I promised to send them away among the nations and into other countries.

**24** I did this because they did not obey my rules and they refused my laws. They made my Sabbaths unholy, and they wanted the idols of their ancestors.

**25** Thus I let them follow laws that were not good. I let them follow rules that could not give them life.

**26** I let them make themselves unclean with their gifts. They burned each first son as an offering. I did this to fill them with horror. Then they will know that I am the LORD.'

**27** "Thus, son of man, speak to the people of Israel. Tell them, 'The Lord GOD says this: Your ancestors also insulted me when they were not loyal to me.

**28** I brought them into the land that I promised to give them. They saw each high hill and each thick tree. There they offered their sacrifices and their offerings, and they made me angry. There they burned incense with a pleasant smell and poured out their drink offerings.

**29** Then I said to them, "What is this high place where you go?" People still call it "Bamah" (high place) today.'

**30** "Thus say to the people of Israel, 'The Lord GOD says this: You make yourselves unclean as your ancestors did. You follow their hateful idols as a prostitute does.

**31** You offer your gifts and burn your sons in the fire. You make yourselves unclean with all your idols, even today. People of Israel, must I give you an answer when you ask me for advice? As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, I will not give you an answer.

**32** You say, "We want to be like the nations and the families of other countries. We want to worship wood and stone." But that will never occur.

**33** As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, I will rule over you with a strong hand and a powerful arm. I will rule over you with great anger.

**34** I will bring you out from the nations. I will gather you from the countries where you are. I will do this with a strong hand, with a powerful arm and with great anger.

**35** I will bring you into the desert of the nations. There I will judge you face to face.

**36** I judged your ancestors in the desert of the land of Egypt. I will judge you in the same way, says the Lord GOD.

**37** I will examine you as a shepherd examines his sheep. I will make you obey the covenant.

**38** I will remove from you the people who rebel against me and do wrong to me. I will bring them out of the countries where they live now. But they will not go into the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**39** "'People of Israel, the Lord GOD says this: Go and worship your idols, each of you, if you will not listen to me. But do not dishonor my holy name again with your gifts and your idols.

**40** All the people of Israel will worship me in the land on my holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord GOD. There I will accept them. There I will ask for your offerings, your best gifts and all your holy sacrifices.

**41** I will bring you out from the nations. I will gather you from the countries where you are now. Then I will accept you as an offering with a pleasant smell. I will show the nations that I am holy through you.

**42** I will bring you into the land of Israel. I lifted my hand and promised to give this land to your ancestors. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**43** There you will remember your ways and all the actions that made you unclean. You will hate yourselves for all the bad things that you did.

**44** I will help you because I want to protect my name. I will not punish you as your bad ways and your bad actions deserve. Then you will know that I am the LORD, people of Israel, says the Lord GOD.'"

**45** The word of the LORD came to me. He said,

**46** "Son of man, turn your face toward the south. Speak against the south. Prophesy against the forest of the south country.

**47** Say to the forest of the south, 'Hear the word of the LORD. The Lord GOD says this: I will start a fire in you. The fire will burn each green tree and each dry tree. No person will stop the fire. The fire will burn all faces from the south to the north.

**48** All people will see that I, the LORD, started the fire. No person will stop it.'"

**49** Then I said, "Lord GOD, the people say this about me: 'He only tells stories with hidden meanings.'"

## Chapter 21

**1** The word of the LORD came to me. He said,

**2** "Son of man, turn your face toward Jerusalem. Speak against the holy places. Prophesy against the land of Israel.

**3** Say to the land of Israel, 'The LORD says this: I am against you. I will take my sword out of its cover. I will kill the righteous people and the wicked people in you.

**4** I will kill the righteous people and the wicked people. Thus my sword will come out of its cover against all people from the south to the north.

**5** Then all people will know that I, the LORD, took my sword out of its cover. I will not put it back again.'

**6** "Son of man, groan in front of the people! Groan with a broken heart and with much sadness.

**7** They will ask you, 'Why do you groan?' Then tell them, 'I groan because of the news that comes. Each heart will become weak with fear. All hands will become weak. Each spirit will become weak. All knees will become as weak as water. The news comes, and it will occur, says the Lord GOD.'"

**8** The word of the LORD came to me again. He said,

**9** "Son of man, prophesy and say, 'The LORD says this: A sword! A sword! The sword is sharp and it shines.

**10** The sword is sharp to kill many people. Someone made it bright to shine like lightning. Must we be happy? My son, the king, did not obey correction. The sword will destroy all such rulers.

**11** Someone made the sword bright, and it is ready to use. The sword is sharp and bright. It is ready for the hand of the killer.'

**12** "Cry and shout, son of man! The sword is against my people. It is against all the princes of Israel. The sword will kill the princes with my people. Thus hit your thigh to show your sadness.

**13** This is a test. What will occur if the scepter of Judah does not obey? The scepter will stop, says the Lord GOD.

**14** "Thus, son of man, prophesy and hit your hands together. Let the sword attack 2 times, 3 times. It is a sword to kill people. It is a sword to kill many people. It will surround them and attack them.

**15** Their hearts will become weak with fear, and many people will fall. I put the sword at all their gates to kill people. The sword shines like lightning. It is ready to kill.

**16** Sword, cut to the right! Cut to the left! Cut in each direction that your edge points!

**17** I will also hit my hands together. Then my anger will stop. I, the LORD, spoke."

**18** The word of the LORD came to me again. He said,

**19** "Son of man, mark 2 roads for the sword of the king of Babylon. The 2 roads must start in the same country. Put a sign at the place where the road divides toward the cities.

**20** Mark one road for the sword to go to Rabbah of the Ammonites. Mark the other road to go to Judah and to Jerusalem, which has strong walls.

**21** The king of Babylon stands at the place where the road divides into 2 roads. He uses magic to choose his road. He shakes arrows. He asks his idols for advice. He examines the liver of an animal.

**22** In his right hand the magic chooses Jerusalem. He will put rams there to break walls. He will tell his soldiers to shout and kill. He will put rams against the gates. He will build ramps and walls against the city.

**23** The people of Jerusalem will think that the magic is false. They made promises to the king of Babylon. But he will remind them of their sin, and he will capture them.

**24** "Thus the Lord GOD says this: 'You caused people to remember your sins. You showed your sins openly. People see your sins in all that you do. Thus your enemy will remember you and capture you.

**25** "'You wicked prince of Israel, you are not holy! Your day of punishment comes. Your sin will come to an end.

**26** The Lord GOD says this: Remove the turban and take off the crown! Things will not stay as they are. Lift up the low person and bring down the high person.

**27** I will destroy the kingdom. I will destroy it! I will destroy it! The kingdom will not be there until the correct ruler comes. I will give the kingdom to him.'

**28** "Son of man, prophesy and say, 'The Lord GOD says this about the Ammonites and their insults: A sword! A sword is ready to kill! It is bright to destroy and to shine like lightning.

**29** Your prophets see false visions about you. They tell you lies with magic. The sword will kill you with the other wicked people. Their day of punishment comes. Their sin will come to an end.

**30** Put the sword back into its cover! I will judge you in the place where I made you, in the land where your life started.

**31** I will pour out my anger on you. I will blow my hot anger on you like fire. I will give you to cruel men who know how to destroy.

**32** You will be fuel for the fire. Your blood will flow in the land. People will not remember you again. I, the LORD, spoke.'"

## Chapter 22

**1** The word of the LORD came to me. He said,

**2** "Son of man, will you judge? Will you judge this city that kills people? Then show her all her hateful actions.

**3** Say, 'The Lord GOD says this: You are a city that kills people in your streets. Thus your time of punishment comes. You make idols, and they make you unclean.

**4** You are guilty because of the blood that you caused to flow. You made yourself unclean with the idols that you made. You caused your end to come near. Your years are at an end. Thus I made you a thing of shame to the nations. All the countries laugh at you.

**5** The countries near you and far from you will laugh at you. You have a bad name, and you are full of confusion.

**6** "'Look! Each of the princes of Israel in you uses his power to kill people.
