# Hosea

## Chapter 1

**1** This is the word of the LORD that came to Hosea, the son of Beeri. It came during the rule of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, the kings of Judah. It also came during the rule of Jeroboam, the son of Joash, the king of Israel.

**2** This is the start of the word of the LORD through Hosea. The LORD said to Hosea, "Go and marry a woman who is not faithful. Have children with her. The children will also be the children of an unfaithful woman. I tell you to do this because the people of the land are not faithful to me. They go away from the LORD."

**3** So Hosea went and married Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim. She became pregnant and gave birth to a son for Hosea.

**4** The LORD said to Hosea, "Give the son the name Jezreel. Soon I will punish the family of Jehu for the blood that Jehu spilled at Jezreel. I will stop the kingdom of Israel.

**5** At that time I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel. Thus I will break the military power of Israel."

**6** Gomer became pregnant again and gave birth to a daughter. God said to Hosea, "Give her the name Lo-ruhamah, which means 'No mercy.' I will not show mercy to the people of Israel again. I will take them away completely.

**7** But I will show mercy to the people of Judah. I, the LORD their God, will save them. I will not save them with bows, swords, or battles. I will not save them with horses or men on horses."

**8** Lo-ruhamah stopped her diet of milk from Gomer. Then Gomer became pregnant again and gave birth to a son.

**9** God said, "Give the son the name Lo-ammi, which means 'Not my people.' I say this because you are not my people. And I will not be your God.

**10** But a day will come. Then the people of Israel will be as many as the grains of sand by the sea. Nobody can measure or count the sand. People said to them in a place, 'You are not my people.' In that place people will say to them, 'You are the sons of the God who lives.'

**11** The people of Judah and the people of Israel will come together again. They will choose 1 leader for themselves. They will come up out of the land. The day of Jezreel will be a great day."

## Chapter 2

**1** "Speak to your brothers and call them 'Ammi,' which means 'My people.' Speak to your sisters and call them 'Ruhamah,' which means 'Mercy.'

**2** Accuse your mother. Accuse her, because she is not my wife and I am not her husband. Tell her to stop her unfaithful acts. Tell her to stop her adultery.

**3** If she does not stop, I will remove her clothes. I will make her naked, as on the day of her birth. I will make her like a desert. I will make her like a dry land. I will kill her with thirst.

**4** I will not show mercy to her children, because they are the children of an unfaithful woman.

**5** Their mother was not faithful. The woman who gave birth to them did shameful things. She said, 'I will go after my lovers. They give me my bread and my water. They give me my wool, my linen, my oil, and my drinks.'

**6** Thus I will block her road with thorns. I will build a wall in front of her, and she will not find her paths.

**7** She will run after her lovers, but she will not catch them. She will look for them, but she will not find them. Then she will say, 'I will go back to my first husband. My life was better then than it is now.'

**8** She did not know that I gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil. I gave her much silver and gold. But the people used that silver and gold for Baal.

**9** Thus I will take back my grain at the time of the harvest. I will take back my new wine in its season. I will take back my wool and my linen. I gave her these to cover her naked body.

**10** Now I will show her shame in front of her lovers. Nobody will save her from my power.

**11** I will stop all her joy. I will stop her festivals, her new moon celebrations, her Sabbaths, and all her special feasts.

**12** I will destroy her vines and her fig trees. She said, 'These are my payment. My lovers gave them to me.' I will change her vines and fig trees into a forest. The wild animals will eat them.

**13** I will punish her for the days when she worshipped the Baals. She burned incense to the Baals. She put on her earrings and her jewelry and went after her lovers. But she forgot me," the LORD says.

**14** "Thus I will attract her back to me. I will bring her into the desert. There I will speak kindly to her.

**15** There I will give her vineyards back to her. I will make the Valley of Achor, which means 'Trouble,' a door of hope. She will sing there as in the days when she was young. She will sing as on the day when she came out of the land of Egypt.

**16** At that time," the LORD says, "you will call me 'Ishi,' which means 'My husband.' You will not call me 'Baali,' which means 'My master,' again.

**17** I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth. People will not remember their names again.

**18** At that time I will make an agreement (covenant) for my people with the wild animals and the birds of the sky. It will include the animals that move on the ground. I will remove the bow, the sword, and war from the land. I will let my people sleep safely.

**19** I will make you my wife for all time. I will make you my wife with righteousness and justice. I will make you my wife with love and mercy.

**20** I will make you my wife with faithfulness. Then you will know the LORD.

**21** At that time I will answer," the LORD says. "I will answer the sky. The sky will answer the earth with rain.

**22** The earth will answer with grain, new wine, and oil. And these will answer Jezreel.

**23** I will plant her in the land for myself. I will show mercy to Lo-ruhamah, who did not get mercy. I will say to Lo-ammi, who was not my people, 'You are my people.' And they will say, 'You are my God.'"

## Chapter 3

**1** The LORD said to me, "Go again and love a woman. Another man loves her, and she does adultery. Love her as the LORD loves the people of Israel. The LORD loves them, but they turn to other gods. They love cakes of raisins that they give to idols."

**2** So I bought her for 15 pieces of silver and about 9 baskets (1.5 homers) of barley.

**3** I said to her, "You must stay with me for many days. You must not be unfaithful. You must not have sex with another man. I also will stay with you."

**4** In the same way, the people of Israel will live for many days with no king and no prince. They will have no sacrifice and no sacred stone. They will have no ephod and no household idols.

**5** After that, the people of Israel will come back. They will look for the LORD their God and for David their king. In the last days they will come to the LORD with fear. They will come to him for his goodness.

## Chapter 4

**1** People of Israel, hear the word of the LORD. The LORD accuses the people who live in the land. There is no truth, no faithful love, and no knowledge of God in the land.

**2** The people curse, tell lies, kill, steal, and do adultery. They break all the laws. They do one murder after another murder.

**3** Thus the land becomes dry. All the people who live in the land become weak. The wild animals, the birds of the sky, and even the fish in the sea die.

**4** But no person must accuse another person. No person must blame another person. My accusation is against you, the priests.

**5** You will fall during the day. The prophets will also fall with you during the night. I will destroy your mother, Israel.

**6** My people die because they do not know me. You priests refused to know me. Thus I refuse to let you be my priests. You forgot the law of your God. Thus I will also forget your children.

**7** The more the priests increased, the more they sinned against me. I will change their honor into shame.

**8** The priests get food from the sin offerings of my people. Thus they want the people to sin more.

**9** The people and the priests will get the same punishment. I will punish them for their ways. I will pay them back for what they did.

**10** They will eat, but they will not have enough. They will have sex with prostitutes, but they will not have more children. They stopped their obedience to the LORD.

**11** Prostitution, wine, and new wine take away the good judgment of my people.

**12** My people ask a piece of wood for advice. A stick tells them what to do. A spirit of unfaithfulness causes them to go the wrong way. They are not faithful to their God.

**13** They offer sacrifices on the tops of the mountains. They burn incense on the hills under oak trees, poplar trees, and other big trees, because the shade is good. Thus your daughters become prostitutes. Your daughters-in-law do adultery.

**14** I will not punish your daughters when they become prostitutes. I will not punish your daughters-in-law when they do adultery. I will not punish them, because the men also go with prostitutes. The men offer sacrifices with temple prostitutes. People who do not understand will fall.

**15** Israel, you are not faithful, but Judah must not become guilty. Do not go to Gilgal. Do not go up to Beth-aven. Do not make a promise with the words, "As the LORD lives."

**16** Israel is stubborn, like a stubborn young cow. Thus the LORD cannot feed Israel like a lamb in a large field.

**17** Ephraim joined with idols. Let Ephraim go its own way.

**18** When their drinks are gone, they go to prostitutes. Their rulers love shameful things.

**19** A wind will take them away. They will feel shame because of their sacrifices.

## Chapter 5

**1** "Priests, hear this. People of Israel, listen. Family of the king, listen. The judgment is against you. You were like a trap at Mizpah. You were like a net on Mount Tabor.

**2** The rebels go deep into murder. But I will punish all of them.

**3** I know Ephraim. Israel cannot hide from me. Ephraim, you are now unfaithful. Israel is not clean.

**4** Their actions do not let them come back to their God. A spirit of unfaithfulness is in them. They do not know the LORD.

**5** The pride of Israel is a witness against Israel. Israel and Ephraim will fall because of their sin. Judah will also fall with them.

**6** They will go with their flocks and their herds to look for the LORD. But they will not find him. He went away from them.

**7** They were not faithful to the LORD. They had children who are not his. Now in 1 month destruction will come on them and on their fields.

**8** Blow the horn in Gibeah. Blow the trumpet in Ramah. Shout loudly at Beth-aven to tell the danger. Benjamin, the enemy is behind you.

**9** Ephraim will become empty on the day of punishment. I tell the tribes of Israel what will surely occur.

**10** The leaders of Judah are like men who move the stones that show the borders of land. I will pour my anger on them like water.

**11** Ephraim suffers. Judgment crushes Ephraim, because Ephraim chose to follow idols.

**12** I will be like a moth to Ephraim. I will be like rot to the people of Judah.

**13** Ephraim saw its sickness. Judah saw its wound. Then Ephraim went to Assyria and sent a message to the great king. But the king could not cure you. He could not heal your wound.

**14** I will be like a lion to Ephraim. I will be like a young lion to the people of Judah. I myself will tear them into pieces and go away. I will carry them away, and nobody will save them.

**15** Then I will go back to my place. I will wait until they admit their guilt. I will wait until they look for me. In their trouble they will look for me quickly."

## Chapter 6

**1** "Come, we will go back to the LORD. He tore us into pieces, but he will heal us. He hurt us, but he will put bandages on our wounds.

**2** After 2 days he will give us new life. On the third day he will lift us up. Then we will live in front of him.

**3** We will know the LORD. We will try hard to know him. He will surely come, as the sun comes in the morning. He will come to us like the rain. He will come like the spring rain that waters the land."

**4** "Ephraim, what will I do with you? Judah, what will I do with you? Your love is like a morning cloud. Your love goes away quickly, like the dew in the early morning.

**5** Thus I cut you into pieces with my prophets. I killed you with the words from my mouth. My judgments go out like the light.

**6** I want faithful love, not sacrifice. I want people to know God more than I want burnt offerings.

**7** But the people broke my covenant, as Adam did. There they were not faithful to me.

**8** Gilead is a city of people who do evil. Blood stains its streets.

**9** Groups of robbers wait to attack a man. In the same way, groups of priests kill people on the road to Shechem. They do shameful crimes.

**10** I saw a terrible thing in the nation of Israel. Ephraim is unfaithful there. Israel is not clean.

**11** Judah, a time of harvest is also ready for you. That time will come when I bring my people back from captivity."

## Chapter 7

**1** "When I want to heal Israel, the sin of Ephraim becomes clear. The crimes of Samaria also become clear. The people lie to each other. Thieves go into houses. Groups of robbers attack in the streets.

**2** The people do not think that I remember all their evil. Their sins are all around them. Their sins are always in front of me.

**3** The people make the king happy with their evil. They make the leaders happy with their lies.

**4** All of them do adultery. Their desire is hot like an oven. The baker does not make the fire hotter while the dough rises.

**5** On the festival day of our king, the leaders became sick with wine. The king joined with people who laugh at God.

**6** Their hearts are hot like an oven while they wait to attack. Their anger sleeps all night. In the morning their anger burns like a fire.

**7** All of them are hot like an oven. They kill their rulers. All their kings fall. Not one of them calls to me.

**8** Ephraim mixes with the other nations. Ephraim is like bread that someone cooked on only 1 side.

**9** Foreign people take away his strength, but he does not know it. His hair becomes gray, but he does not know it.

**10** The pride of Israel is a witness against Israel. But the people do not come back to the LORD their God. They do not look for him, after all these troubles.

**11** Ephraim is like a dove that is easy to trick and has no sense. The people call to Egypt for help. Then they go to Assyria.

**12** When they go, I will throw my net over them. I will pull them down like birds from the sky. I will punish them, as I told their assembly.

**13** They will have much trouble, because they went away from me. Destruction will come on them, because they rebelled against me. I wanted to save them, but they told lies about me.

**14** They do not cry to me from their hearts. They cry loudly on their beds. They gather together for grain and new wine. But they turn away from me.

**15** I trained them and made their arms strong. But they plan evil against me.

**16** They turn, but not to the Most High God. They are like a bow that does not shoot straight. Their leaders will die by the sword because of their angry words. Thus the people of Egypt will laugh at them."

## Chapter 8

**1** "Put the trumpet to your mouth. An enemy comes like an eagle against the house of the LORD. The people broke my covenant. They rebelled against my law.

**2** Israel cries to me, 'Our God, we know you.'

**3** But Israel refused what is good. Thus an enemy will chase Israel.

**4** They made kings, but I did not choose those kings. They chose leaders, but I did not approve the leaders. They used their silver and gold to make idols for themselves. Thus destruction will come on them.

**5** Samaria, I refuse your calf idol. My anger burns against the people. How long will they continue to be guilty?

**6** That calf comes from Israel. A worker made it, so it is not God. The calf of Samaria will break into pieces.

**7** They plant the wind, and they will harvest a storm. The grain has no head, and it will make no flour. If it makes flour, foreign people will eat it.

**8** Other nations swallow up Israel. Now Israel is among the nations like a pot that nobody wants.

**9** They went up to Assyria, like a wild donkey that goes alone. Ephraim paid lovers to help him.

**10** They paid the nations for help, but now I will gather them for punishment. Soon they will become weak under the heavy load of the great king.

**11** Ephraim built many altars to take away sin. But those altars became places to sin.

**12** I wrote many laws for Ephraim. But the people thought that my laws were strange.

**13** They offer sacrifices of meat to me and they eat the meat. But the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their sin. He will punish their sins. They will go back to Egypt.

**14** Israel forgot his Maker and built palaces. Judah built many cities with strong walls. But I will send a fire on their cities. The fire will destroy their strong buildings."

## Chapter 9

**1** Israel, do not be happy. Do not celebrate like the other nations. You were not faithful to your God. You loved the pay of a prostitute on every floor where people beat grain.

**2** The floor where people beat grain and the winepress will not feed the people. The new wine will not be sufficient for them.

**3** They will not stay in the land of the LORD. Ephraim will go back to Egypt. They will eat food that is not clean in Assyria.

**4** They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD. Their sacrifices will not make him happy. Their sacrifices will be like the bread that people eat at a funeral. All people who eat that bread will become not clean. Their bread will be only for themselves. Their bread will not come into the house of the LORD.

**5** What will you do on the day of the special festival? What will you do on the day of the feast of the LORD?

**6** The people run away from destruction. But Egypt will gather them, and Memphis will bury them. Weeds will grow over their treasures of silver. Thorns will grow in their tents.

**7** The days of punishment come. The days of payment come. Israel will know it. Because of your many sins and your great hatred, you say, "The prophet is a fool. The man of the Spirit is crazy."

**8** The prophet is a guard over Ephraim for my God. But people put traps for him on all his paths. The people hate him in the house of his God.

**9** The people did very bad crimes, as in the days of Gibeah. God will remember their sin. He will punish their sins.

**10** "When I found Israel, it was like a discovery of grapes in the desert. When I saw your ancestors, it was like the first fruit on a fig tree. But they went to Baal-peor and gave themselves to that shameful idol. They became filthy, like the idol that they loved.

**11** The glory of Ephraim will fly away like a bird. There will be no births, no pregnancies, and no conceptions.

**12** If they raise children, I will take those children from them. No person will remain. They will have much trouble when I go away from them.

**13** I saw Ephraim like the city of Tyre, planted in a pleasant place. But Ephraim will bring out his children to the killer."

**14** LORD, give them what they deserve. What will you give them? Give them wombs that lose babies. Give them breasts that are dry.

**15** "All their evil started at Gilgal. I started to hate them there. Because of their evil actions, I will push them out of my house. I will not love them again. All their leaders are rebels.

**16** Ephraim is like a plant with dry roots. It will make no fruit. If they have children, I will kill their loved children."

**17** My God will refuse them, because they did not obey him. They will wander among the nations.

## Chapter 10

**1** Israel is like a vine that grows much. It makes fruit for itself. When its fruit increased, it built more altars. When its land became better, it made better sacred stones.

**2** Their hearts are not loyal. Now they must suffer for their guilt. The LORD will break their altars. He will destroy their sacred stones.

**3** Then they will say, "We have no king because we did not fear the LORD. But what can a king do for us?"

**4** They speak empty words. They make false promises when they make agreements. Thus lawsuits grow like poisonous weeds in a plowed field.

**5** The people who live in Samaria will be afraid for the calf idol of Beth-aven. Its people will cry for it. Its priests, who celebrated it, will also cry. They will cry because its glory goes away from it.

**6** The enemy will carry the calf to Assyria as a gift for the great king. Ephraim will feel shame. Israel will feel shame because of its idol.

**7** The king of Samaria will come to an end. He will be like a stick that floats away on the water.

**8** Someone will destroy the high places of Aven. Those places are the sin of Israel. Thorns and weeds will grow on their altars. Then the people will say to the mountains, "Cover us." They will say to the hills, "Fall on us."

**9** "Israel, you sinned from the days of Gibeah. You did not change since that time. Will war not come to the evil people in Gibeah?

**10** I will punish them when I want. The nations will gather against them. They will punish them for their 2 sins.

**11** Ephraim was like a trained young cow that loves to crush the grain. But I will put a yoke on her good neck. I will make Ephraim pull a load. Judah will plow. Jacob will break up the ground.

**12** Plant righteousness for yourselves. Then you will harvest faithful love. Plow your unused ground. It is time to look for the LORD. Look for him until he comes and makes righteousness fall on you like rain.

**13** But you planted evil, and you harvested sin. You ate the fruit of lies. You trusted in your own way. You trusted in your many soldiers.

**14** Thus the noise of war will start among your people. The enemy will destroy all your strong cities. Shalman destroyed Beth-arbel in the battle. There the enemy killed the mothers together with their children.

**15** The same thing will occur to you, Bethel, because your evil is very large. At dawn the king of Israel will come to a complete end."

## Chapter 11

**1** "When Israel was a child, I loved him. I called my son out of Egypt.

**2** But the more I called them, the more they went away from me. They offered sacrifices to the Baals. They burned incense to idols.

**3** I taught Ephraim to walk. I held them in my arms. But they did not know that I healed them.

**4** I led them with kindness and with love. I was like a person who lifts a yoke from the neck of an animal. I bent down and fed them.

**5** They will not go back to the land of Egypt. But Assyria will rule them, because they refused to come back to me.

**6** War will go through their cities. The enemy will destroy the bars of their gates. The enemy will destroy them because of their bad plans.

**7** My people continue to go away from me. They call to the Most High God, but he will not lift them up.

**8** Ephraim, how can I give you up? Israel, how can I give you to your enemies? How can I make you like the city of Admah? How can I destroy you like Zeboim? My heart changes inside me. All my pity becomes strong.

**9** I will not punish you with my strong anger. I will not destroy Ephraim again. I am God, and not a man. I am the Holy One among you. I will not come against you in anger.

**10** They will follow the LORD. He will roar like a lion. When he roars, his children will come from the west with fear.

**11** They will come quickly from Egypt like birds. They will come from the land of Assyria like doves. I will put them in their houses again," the LORD says.

**12** "Ephraim surrounds me with lies. The people of Israel surround me with tricks. And Judah still goes away from God. Judah goes away from the Holy One, who is faithful."

## Chapter 12

**1** Ephraim tries to feed on the wind. All day it chases the hot east wind. It increases its lies and its violence. It makes an agreement with Assyria. It sends olive oil to Egypt.

**2** The LORD also accuses Judah. He will punish Jacob for his ways. He will pay him back for what he did.

**3** Before birth, Jacob held the heel of his brother. As a man, Jacob fought with God.

**4** He fought with the angel and won. He cried and asked the angel for a blessing. He found God at Bethel. God spoke with us there.

**5** That God is the LORD God of armies. "The LORD" is the name that people use to remember him.

**6** Thus you must come back to your God. Be faithful in love and justice. Always trust your God.

**7** Ephraim is like a merchant who uses dishonest scales. He loves to cheat.

**8** Ephraim said, "I am rich. I got much wealth for myself. In all my work, nobody will find a sin or a crime in me."

**9** "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. I will make you live in tents again, as in the days of the special festival.

**10** I spoke to the prophets. I gave them many visions. I gave messages through the prophets with stories."

**11** Gilead is evil. Its people are worth nothing. The people offer bulls as sacrifices in Gilgal. Their altars will become piles of stones in the plowed fields.

**12** Jacob ran away to the country of Aram. Israel worked to get a wife. To pay for a wife, he kept sheep.

**13** The LORD used a prophet to bring Israel out of Egypt. Through a prophet the LORD kept Israel safe.

**14** But Ephraim made the LORD very angry. Thus his Lord will make Ephraim guilty for the blood that Ephraim spilled. His Lord will pay him back for his shameful actions.

## Chapter 13

**1** When Ephraim spoke, people were afraid. Ephraim was important in Israel. But Ephraim became guilty when it worshipped Baal. Then Ephraim died.

**2** Now the people sin more and more. They use their silver to make metal idols. They make idols with their own skill. Workers make all of these idols. The people say about the idols, "Offer human sacrifices and kiss the calf idols."

**3** Thus the people will be like a morning cloud. They will be like the early dew that goes away quickly. They will be like the chaff that the wind blows from a floor where people beat grain. They will be like smoke that goes out of a window.

**4** "But I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. You must know no god but me. There is no Savior but me.

**5** I took care of you in the desert, in a very dry land.

**6** When I fed them, they became full. When they were full, they became proud. Thus they forgot me.

**7** So I will be like a lion to them. I will wait by the road like a leopard.

**8** I will attack them like a bear that lost her cubs. I will tear open their chests. I will eat them like a lion. Like a wild animal, I will tear them into pieces.

**9** Israel, you destroyed yourself because you are against me. I am your help.

**10** Where is your king now? He cannot save you in all your cities. Where are your rulers? You said, 'Give us a king and leaders.'

**11** In my anger I gave you a king. In my anger I took him away.

**12** I keep a record of the sin of Ephraim. I keep the record of his sins in a safe place.

**13** Pain will come to him, as pain comes to a woman who gives birth. But he is a foolish son. When the time of birth comes, he does not come out of the womb.

**14** I will save them from the power of the grave. I will save them from death. Death, where are your diseases? Grave, where is your destruction? I will not show pity.

**15** Ephraim grows among his brothers. But the LORD will send a hot east wind. The wind will come from the desert. His springs and his wells will become dry. The enemy will take all his valuable treasures.

**16** The people of Samaria will become guilty, because they rebelled against their God. They will die by the sword. The enemy will throw their small children to the ground. The enemy will cut open their pregnant women."

## Chapter 14

**1** Israel, come back to the LORD your God. Your sins caused you to fall.

**2** Take words with you and come back to the LORD. Say to him, "Take away all our sin. Accept us with kindness. Then we will give you praise from our lips as an offering.

**3** Assyria will not save us. We will not ride on war horses. We will not say again to the idols that we made, 'You are our gods.' You show mercy to children who have no father."

**4** "I will heal them of their unfaithfulness. I will love them freely. My anger went away from them.

**5** I will be like the dew to Israel. Israel will grow like a lily. Israel will push down roots like the cedar trees of Lebanon.

**6** His branches will grow. He will be beautiful like an olive tree. He will smell good like the cedar trees of Lebanon.

**7** People will live again in his shade. They will grow like grain. They will grow like a vine. People will remember Israel like the wine of Lebanon.

**8** Ephraim, I will have nothing to do with idols again. I answer you and I take care of you. I am like a green pine tree. Your fruit comes from me."

**9** A wise person will understand these things. A person with good sense will know them. The ways of the LORD are right. Righteous people follow those ways. But rebels fall on those ways.

---

# Joel

## Chapter 1

**1** This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel, the son of Pethuel.

**2** Old men, hear this. All people who live in the land, listen. Did a thing like this occur during your life? Did it occur during the life of your ancestors?

**3** Tell your children about it. Your children must tell their children. And their children must tell the next generation.

**4** The first group of locusts ate some of the crops. The large groups of locusts ate what remained. The young locusts ate what remained after that. The other locusts ate what remained after that.

**5** Wake up, you drunk people, and cry. All you people who drink wine, cry loudly. The new wine is gone from your mouths.

**6** An army of locusts came against my land. It is strong, and nobody can count it. Its teeth are like the teeth of a lion. It has the jaws of a strong lion.

**7** It destroyed my vines. It broke my fig trees. It removed all the bark and threw it away. The branches became white.

**8** Cry like a young woman who wears sackcloth because her husband died.

**9** The grain offering and the drink offering stop at the house of the LORD. The priests, who serve the LORD, are sad.

**10** The fields are in ruins. The ground is sad, because the grain is gone. The new wine is dry. The olive oil is gone.

**11** Farmers, feel shame. People who work in the vineyards, cry loudly. Cry for the wheat and for the barley, because the harvest of the field is gone.

**12** The vine is dry. The fig tree becomes weak. The pomegranate tree, the palm tree, the apple tree, and all the trees of the field are dry. The joy of the people is gone.

**13** Priests, put on sackcloth and cry. You who serve at the altar, cry loudly. You who serve my God, come and stay all night in sackcloth. The grain offering and the drink offering stop at the house of your God.

**14** Announce a holy fast. Call a special assembly. Gather the elders and all the people who live in the land. Bring them into the house of the LORD your God. Cry to the LORD.

**15** That day will be terrible. The day of the LORD is near. It will come as destruction from the Almighty.

**16** Our food is gone in front of our eyes. Joy and happiness are gone from the house of our God.

**17** The seeds become dry under the ground. The storehouses are empty. The barns fall down, because the grain is dry.

**18** The animals make sad noises. The herds of cattle wander, because they have no grass. Even the flocks of sheep suffer.

**19** LORD, I cry to you. Fire destroyed the grass in the desert. Flames burned all the trees of the field.

**20** Even the wild animals cry to you. The streams of water are dry. Fire destroyed the grass in the desert.

## Chapter 2

**1** Blow the trumpet in Zion. Make an alarm on my holy mountain. All the people who live in the land must shake with fear. The day of the LORD comes. It is near.

**2** It is a day of darkness and gloom. It is a day of clouds and thick darkness. A large and strong army spreads over the mountains, like the light at dawn. There was never an army like it before. There will never be an army like it again, for many generations.

**3** In front of the army, a fire destroys everything. Behind the army, a flame burns. In front of the army, the land is like the garden of Eden. Behind the army, the land is an empty desert. Nothing escapes from the army.

**4** They look like horses. They run like war horses.

**5** They jump on the tops of the mountains with a noise like chariots. They make a noise like a fire that burns dry grass. They are like a strong army that is ready for battle.

**6** When the people see the army, they are very afraid. All their faces become pale.

**7** They run like soldiers. They climb the walls like warriors. Each of them goes straight ahead. They do not move out of their lines.

**8** They do not push each other. Each of them goes on his own path. They go through the defenses, and nobody can stop them.

**9** They attack the city. They run on the walls. They climb into the houses. They go in through the windows like thieves.

**10** The earth shakes in front of them. The sky shakes. The sun and the moon become dark. The stars stop their light.

**11** The LORD shouts in front of his army. His army is very large. The army that obeys his command is strong. The day of the LORD is great and very terrible. Nobody can survive it.

**12** "But even now," the LORD says, "come back to me with all your heart. Do not eat food. Cry and show your sadness when you come back to me."

**13** Tear your hearts, not your clothes. Come back to the LORD your God. He is kind and merciful. He is slow to become angry, and his love is very large. He changes his mind and does not send disaster.

**14** Maybe he will change his mind and give a blessing to you. Then you can give a grain offering and a drink offering to the LORD your God.

**15** Blow the trumpet in Zion. Announce a holy fast. Call a special assembly.

**16** Gather the people. Make the assembly holy. Bring the elders together. Gather the children, and also the babies who drink milk from their mothers. The husband must come out of his room. The bride must come out of her room.

**17** The priests, who serve the LORD, must cry between the porch of the temple and the altar. They must say, "LORD, save your people. Do not let other people laugh at the nation that belongs to you. Do not let the nations rule them. Do not let the nations say, 'Where is their God?'"

**18** Then the LORD became protective of his land. He showed pity to his people.

**19** The LORD answered his people. He said, "I will send you grain, new wine, and olive oil. You will have sufficient food. I will not let the nations laugh at you again.

**20** I will send the army from the north far away from you. I will push it into a dry and empty land. Its front lines will go into the eastern sea. Its back lines will go into the western sea. Its dead bodies will smell very bad. I will do this because the army did terrible things."

**21** Land, do not be afraid. Be glad and celebrate, because the LORD did great things.

**22** Wild animals, do not be afraid. The grass in the desert becomes green. The trees make their fruit. The fig tree and the vine give many crops.

**23** People of Zion, be glad. Celebrate because of the LORD your God. He gives you the autumn rain in the correct quantity. He sends you the rain. He sends the autumn rain and the spring rain, as before.

**24** The floors where people beat grain will be full of grain. The containers will be full of new wine and olive oil.

**25** "I will give back to you the crops that the locusts ate in those years. I sent the large groups of locusts, the young locusts, the other locusts, and the first group of locusts. They were my large army that I sent against you.

**26** You will have much food to eat, and you will have enough. You will praise the name of the LORD your God. He did wonderful things for you. My people will never feel shame again.

**27** Then you will know that I am among the people of Israel. You will know that I am the LORD your God, and that there is no other God. My people will never feel shame again.

**28** After that, I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and your daughters will speak as prophets. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.

**29** At that time I will also pour out my Spirit on the male servants and the female servants.

**30** I will show wonders in the sky and on the earth. There will be blood, fire, and columns of smoke.

**31** The sun will become dark. The moon will become red like blood. These things will occur before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.

**32** Then the LORD will save each person who calls to him. There will be people who escape on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, as the LORD said. The LORD will call the people who remain."

## Chapter 3

**1** "At that time I will bring back the captives of Judah and Jerusalem.

**2** Then I will gather all the nations. I will bring them down into the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will judge them for what they did to my people Israel. They scattered my people among the nations. They divided my land.

**3** They threw lots for my people. They gave a boy to pay for a prostitute. They sold a girl to get wine to drink.

**4** Tyre, Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia, what do you have against me? Do you try to pay me back for something? If you try to pay me back, I will quickly pay you back for what you did.

**5** You took my silver and my gold. You carried my valuable treasures into your temples.

**6** You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks. You sent them far away from their land.

**7** I will bring my people out of the places where you sold them. I will pay you back for what you did.

**8** I will sell your sons and your daughters to the people of Judah. The people of Judah will sell them to the Sabeans, a nation far away. The LORD said this."

**9** Announce this among the nations: "Prepare for war. Wake up the soldiers. All the warriors must come near and attack.

**10** Change your plows into swords. Change the knives that cut your vines into spears. The weak person must say, 'I am strong.'

**11** All you nations around Israel, come quickly. Gather together there." LORD, send your warriors down.

**12** "The nations must wake up. They must come to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will sit to judge all the nations around Israel.

**13** Use the sickle, because the harvest is ready. Come and crush the grapes, because the winepress is full. The containers are too full, because the evil of the nations is very large."

**14** Very large crowds of people are in the valley of decision. The day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.

**15** The sun and the moon become dark. The stars stop their light.

**16** The LORD roars from Zion. He shouts from Jerusalem. The sky and the earth shake. But the LORD is a safe place for his people. He is a strong place of protection for the people of Israel.

**17** "Then you will know that I am the LORD your God. I live in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy. Foreign armies will not go through Jerusalem again.

**18** At that time the mountains will be full of new wine. Milk will flow from the hills. Water will flow in all the streams of Judah. A spring will come out of the house of the LORD. The spring will give water to the Valley of Shittim.

**19** Egypt will become empty. Edom will become an empty desert. The people of Egypt and Edom attacked the people of Judah. They killed innocent people in the land of Judah.

**20** But people will live in Judah for all time. People will live in Jerusalem for all generations.

**21** I will forgive the guilt of their blood that I did not forgive before. The LORD lives in Zion."

---

# Amos

## Chapter 1

**1** These are the words of Amos. He was one of the shepherds from Tekoa. He saw these things about Israel during the rule of Uzziah, the king of Judah. It was also during the rule of Jeroboam, the son of Joash, the king of Israel. It was 2 years before the earthquake.

**2** Amos said, "The LORD roars from Zion. He shouts from Jerusalem. The fields of the shepherds become dry. The top of Mount Carmel becomes dry."

**3** The LORD says this: "The people of Damascus sinned again and again. Thus I will not stop their punishment. They crushed the people of Gilead with iron tools, as farmers crush grain.

**4** I will send a fire on the house of Hazael. The fire will destroy the strong buildings of Ben-hadad.

**5** I will break the gate of Damascus. I will destroy the people who live in the Valley of Aven. I will destroy the ruler of Beth-eden. The people of Aram will go as captives to Kir," the LORD says.

**6** The LORD says this: "The people of Gaza sinned again and again. Thus I will not stop their punishment. They took all the people of a region as captives. They sold the captives to Edom.

**7** I will send a fire on the walls of Gaza. The fire will destroy its strong buildings.

**8** I will destroy the people who live in Ashdod. I will destroy the ruler of Ashkelon. I will use my power against Ekron. The Philistines who remain will die," the Lord GOD says.

**9** The LORD says this: "The people of Tyre sinned again and again. Thus I will not stop their punishment. They sold all the people of a region as captives to Edom. They did not remember their agreement of friendship (covenant) with their brothers.

**10** I will send a fire on the walls of Tyre. The fire will destroy its strong buildings."

**11** The LORD says this: "The people of Edom sinned again and again. Thus I will not stop their punishment. Edom chased his brother with the sword. Edom showed no pity. His anger did not stop. He kept his anger for all time.

**12** I will send a fire on Teman. The fire will destroy the strong buildings of Bozrah."

**13** The LORD says this: "The people of Ammon sinned again and again. Thus I will not stop their punishment. They cut open the pregnant women of Gilead. They did this to make their own country larger.

**14** I will start a fire on the walls of Rabbah. The fire will destroy its strong buildings. There will be shouts on the day of battle. The attack will be like a storm on a day of strong wind.

**15** Their king will go into captivity. He and his leaders will go together," the LORD says.

## Chapter 2

**1** The LORD says this: "The people of Moab sinned again and again. Thus I will not stop their punishment. They burned the bones of the king of Edom until the bones became lime.

**2** I will send a fire on Moab. The fire will destroy the strong buildings of Kerioth. Moab will die in a loud battle. There will be shouts and the sound of the trumpet.

**3** I will destroy the ruler of Moab. I will kill all its leaders with him," the LORD says.

**4** The LORD says this: "The people of Judah sinned again and again. Thus I will not stop their punishment. They refused the law of the LORD. They did not obey his commands. Their ancestors followed false gods. Those same false gods caused the people of Judah to go the wrong way.

**5** I will send a fire on Judah. The fire will destroy the strong buildings of Jerusalem."

**6** The LORD says this: "The people of Israel sinned again and again. Thus I will not stop their punishment. They sell innocent people for silver. They sell poor people for a pair of sandals.

**7** They push the heads of poor people into the dust. They do not let humble people get justice. A man and his father have sex with the same young woman. Thus they make my holy name not holy.

**8** They lie down next to every altar on clothes that they took from the poor as payment for a debt. In the house of their god, they drink wine that they took from people as fines.

**9** But I destroyed the Amorites in front of my people. The Amorites were as tall as cedar trees. They were as strong as oak trees. But I destroyed them completely, from the fruit above to the roots below.

**10** I brought you up from the land of Egypt. I led you through the desert for 40 years. I gave you the land of the Amorites.

**11** I chose some of your sons to be prophets. I chose some of your young men to be Nazirites. People of Israel, this is true," the LORD says.

**12** "But you made the Nazirites drink wine. You commanded the prophets, 'Do not prophesy.'

**13** Thus I will crush you, as a cart that is full of grain crushes the ground.

**14** The fast runner will not escape. The strong man will not have strength. The soldier will not save his life.

**15** The man with the bow will not stand. The fast runner will not escape. The man on the horse will not save his life.

**16** On that day even the bravest soldiers will run away without their clothes," the LORD says.

## Chapter 3

**1** People of Israel, hear this word that the LORD speaks against you. He speaks against all the families that he brought up from the land of Egypt. He says,

**2** "Of all the families of the earth, I chose only you. Thus I will punish you for all your sins."

**3** Can 2 people walk together if they do not agree to meet?

**4** Does a lion roar in the forest if it has no animal to eat? Does a young lion growl in its cave if it caught nothing?

**5** Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground if there is no bait? Does a trap close if it caught nothing?

**6** If a trumpet sounds in a city, the people become afraid. If a disaster comes to a city, the LORD caused it.

**7** The Lord GOD does nothing until he tells his plan to his servants, the prophets.

**8** The lion roared. Who will not be afraid? The Lord GOD spoke. Who can stop himself? He must prophesy.

**9** Announce this to the strong buildings of Ashdod and the strong buildings of the land of Egypt. Say, "Gather on the mountains around Samaria. Look at the great confusion in Samaria. Look at how the people there hurt each other."

**10** "The people do not know how to do right," the LORD says. "They store violence and stolen things in their strong buildings."

**11** Thus the Lord GOD says this: "An enemy will surround the land. The enemy will destroy your defenses. The enemy will take everything from your strong buildings."

**12** The LORD says this: "A shepherd tries to save his sheep from a lion. But he saves only 2 leg bones or a piece of an ear. In the same way, I will save only a small part of the people of Israel. Those people live in Samaria and sit on the corners of beds and on the cushions of couches."

**13** "Hear this and warn the family of Jacob," the Lord GOD, the God of armies, says.

**14** "On the day when I punish Israel for its sins, I will also destroy the altars of Bethel. Someone will cut off the horns of the altar, and they will fall to the ground.

**15** I will destroy the winter houses and the summer houses. The houses with ivory decorations will fall. The large houses will come to an end," the LORD says.

## Chapter 4

**1** Hear this word, you women of Samaria. You are like the fat cows of Bashan on the mountain of Samaria. You hurt the poor people. You crush the needy people. You say to your husbands, "Bring us drinks."

**2** The Lord GOD made a promise by his holiness. He said, "The time will come when the enemy will take you away with hooks. The enemy will take the last of you with fishhooks.

**3** You will go out through the holes in the walls, each woman straight ahead. The enemy will throw you out toward Harmon," the LORD says.

**4** "Go to Bethel and sin. Go to Gilgal and sin more. Bring your sacrifices every morning. Bring your tithes every 3 days.

**5** Offer bread with yeast as a sacrifice of thanks. Announce your free offerings loudly, so that all people know. You love to do this, people of Israel," the Lord GOD says.

**6** "I caused hunger in all your cities. You had no bread in all your towns. But you did not come back to me," the LORD says.

**7** "I also stopped the rain when the harvest was still 3 months away. I sent rain on 1 city, but I did not send rain on another city. Rain fell on 1 field. Another field did not get rain, and it became dry.

**8** The people of 2 or 3 cities went to 1 city to get water to drink. But they did not get sufficient water. But you did not come back to me," the LORD says.

**9** "I destroyed your crops with hot winds and with disease. The locusts ate your many gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees. But you did not come back to me," the LORD says.

**10** "I sent diseases among you, as I did in Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword. I let the enemy take away your horses. I filled your noses with the smell of the dead bodies in your camps. But you did not come back to me," the LORD says.

**11** "I destroyed some of you, as I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. You were like a stick that someone pulled out of a fire while it burned. But you did not come back to me," the LORD says.

**12** "Thus I will punish you, Israel. Because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel."

**13** God made the mountains. He makes the wind. He tells people his thoughts. He changes the dawn into darkness. He walks on the high places of the earth. His name is the LORD, the God of armies.

## Chapter 5

**1** People of Israel, hear this word. I sing this sad song about you:

**2** "The young woman Israel fell. She will not get up again. She lies alone on her land. Nobody lifts her up."

**3** The Lord GOD says this: "A city in Israel sends out 1000 soldiers, but only 100 will come back. A town sends out 100 soldiers, but only 10 will come back."

**4** The LORD says this to the people of Israel: "Come to me, and you will live.

**5** Do not go to Bethel to worship. Do not go into Gilgal. Do not go to Beersheba. The people of Gilgal will surely go into captivity. Bethel will become nothing."

**6** Come to the LORD, and you will live. If you do not come to him, he will attack the people of Joseph like a fire. The fire will destroy Bethel, and nobody will stop the fire.

**7** You change justice into something bitter. You throw righteousness to the ground.

**8** God made the stars of the Pleiades and Orion. He changes the deep darkness into morning. He makes the day dark like night. He calls the water from the sea. He pours the water on the land. His name is the LORD.

**9** He quickly destroys the strong people. He destroys their strong cities.

**10** You hate the person who tells the truth in the court. You hate the person who speaks honestly.

**11** You hurt the poor people. You take their grain as taxes. Thus you will not live in the stone houses that you built. You will not drink the wine from the good vineyards that you planted.

**12** I know your many crimes and your large sins. You attack innocent people. You take bribes. You refuse justice to the poor people in the court.

**13** Thus wise people stay silent at that time, because it is an evil time.

**14** Look for good, not evil, so that you will live. Then the LORD, the God of armies, will be with you, as you say.

**15** Hate evil and love good. Make sure that there is justice in the court. Maybe the LORD God of armies will show kindness to the people of Joseph who remain.

**16** Thus the LORD, the God of armies, the Lord, says this: "People will cry in all the public places. They will say in all the streets, 'We are sad! We are sad!' They will call the farmers to cry. They will call the professional mourners to cry loudly.

**17** People will cry in all the vineyards, because I will come through your land to punish you," the LORD says.

**18** You want the day of the LORD to come, but you will have much trouble. Why do you want the day of the LORD? That day will be darkness, not light.

**19** It will be like a man who runs away from a lion, but a bear meets him. It will be like a man who goes into his house and puts his hand on the wall, but a snake bites him.

**20** The day of the LORD will be darkness, not light. It will be very dark, with no light.

**21** "I hate your festivals. I refuse them. I do not like your special assemblies.

**22** You offer me burnt offerings and grain offerings, but I will not accept them. You offer peace offerings of fat animals, but I will not look at them.

**23** Take away the noise of your songs. I will not listen to the music of your harps.

**24** But let justice flow like a river. Let righteousness flow like a stream that never becomes dry.

**25** People of Israel, did you bring me sacrifices and offerings during the 40 years in the desert?

**26** You carried the shrine of your king Moloch. You carried Chiun, your idols. You carried the star of your god. You made these things for yourselves.

**27** Thus I will send you into captivity, to a place farther than Damascus," the LORD says. His name is the God of armies.

## Chapter 6

**1** You will have much trouble, you people who feel safe in Zion. You will have much trouble, you people who trust in the mountain of Samaria. You are the important leaders of the first nation. The people of Israel come to you for help.

**2** Go to Calneh and look. Go from there to the great city of Hamath. Then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than those kingdoms? Is their land larger than your land?

**3** You refuse to think about the day of disaster. But you bring near a time of violence.

**4** You lie on beds decorated with ivory. You relax on your couches. You eat the best lambs from the flock. You eat the best calves from the barn.

**5** You sing songs with the music of harps. Like David, you make musical instruments for yourselves.

**6** You drink wine from large bowls. You put the best oils on your bodies. But you are not sad about the destruction of Joseph.

**7** Thus you will be the first people to go into captivity. Your parties, where you relax, will stop.

**8** The Lord GOD made a promise by himself. The LORD, the God of armies, says this: "I hate the pride of Jacob. I hate his strong buildings. I will give the city and all its people to the enemy."

**9** If 10 men remain in 1 house, they will all die.

**10** A relative, who must burn the dead bodies, will come to take the bodies out of the house. He will call to a person who hides in the house, "Is there another person with you?" The person will say, "No." Then the relative will say, "Be quiet. We must not say the name of the LORD."

**11** The LORD gives the command. He will break the large houses into pieces. He will break the small houses into small pieces.

**12** Horses do not run on rocks. People do not plow the sea with oxen. But you changed justice into poison. You changed the fruit of righteousness into a bitter plant.

**13** You are happy about Lo-debar, which means "Nothing." You say, "We took Karnaim with our own strength."

**14** "People of Israel, I will send a nation against you," the LORD, the God of armies, says. "That nation will hurt you from Lebo-hamath to the stream of the Arabah."

## Chapter 7

**1** The Lord GOD showed me a vision. He made a swarm of locusts. This occurred when the second crop started to grow. That crop came after the king took his share of the harvest.

**2** The locusts ate all the plants in the land. Then I said, "Lord GOD, please forgive your people. How can Jacob survive? He is very small."

**3** So the LORD changed his mind. "This will not occur," the LORD said.

**4** The Lord GOD showed me another vision. The Lord GOD called for a fire to punish the people. The fire dried up the deep water and started to destroy the land.

**5** Then I said, "Lord GOD, please stop. How can Jacob survive? He is very small."

**6** So the LORD changed his mind. "This also will not occur," the Lord GOD said.

**7** The LORD showed me another vision. The Lord stood next to a wall that a builder made straight with a plumb line. The Lord held a plumb line in his hand.

**8** The LORD asked me, "Amos, what do you see?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "I will use a plumb line to examine my people Israel. I will not forgive them again.

**9** The high places of Isaac will become empty. The holy places of Israel will become ruins. I will attack the family of Jeroboam with the sword."

**10** Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent a message to Jeroboam, the king of Israel. He said, "Amos makes a plan against you among the people of Israel. The land cannot accept all his words.

**11** Amos says, 'Jeroboam will die by the sword. The people of Israel will surely go as captives away from their land.'"

**12** Then Amaziah said to Amos, "You prophet, go away. Go back to the land of Judah. Eat your bread there. Prophesy there.

**13** But do not prophesy at Bethel again. Bethel is the holy place of the king. It is the temple of the kingdom."

**14** Amos answered Amaziah, "I was not a prophet. I was not the son of a prophet. I was a shepherd. I also took care of fig trees.

**15** But the LORD took me away from my work with the flock. The LORD said to me, 'Go and prophesy to my people Israel.'

**16** Now hear the word of the LORD. You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel. Do not preach against the family of Isaac.'

**17** Thus the LORD says this: 'Your wife will become a prostitute in the city. Your sons and your daughters will die by the sword. Other people will measure and divide your land. You will die in a foreign land that is not clean. The people of Israel will surely go as captives away from their land.'"

## Chapter 8

**1** The Lord GOD showed me another vision. I saw a basket of ripe summer fruit.

**2** He asked, "Amos, what do you see?" I said, "A basket of ripe summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end comes for my people Israel. I will not forgive them again.

**3** On that day the songs in the temple will change into loud cries of sorrow," the Lord GOD says. "There will be many dead bodies in all places. People will throw the bodies out in silence."

**4** Hear this, you people who walk on the needy. You try to destroy the poor people of the land.

**5** You say, "When will the new moon festival end? Then we can sell grain. When will the Sabbath end? Then we can sell wheat. We will make the measure smaller. We will make the price larger. We will cheat with false scales.

**6** We will buy poor people with silver. We will buy needy people for a pair of sandals. We will even sell the bad parts of the wheat."

**7** The LORD made a promise by the pride of Jacob. He said, "I will never forget anything that they did.

**8** Because of these sins, the land will shake. All the people who live in the land will be sad. The whole land will rise like the Nile River. It will move up and down, and then go down again like the river of Egypt.

**9** On that day," the Lord GOD says, "I will make the sun go down at noon. I will make the earth dark during the day.

**10** I will change your festivals into times of sadness. I will change all your songs into sad songs. I will make all of you wear sackcloth. I will make you shave your heads. It will be like the sadness for an only son who died. The end of that day will be very bitter.

**11** The days will come," the Lord GOD says, "when I will send a famine on the land. It will not be a famine of bread. It will not be a thirst for water. The people will not hear the words of the LORD.

**12** People will wander from sea to sea. They will go from the north to the east. They will run here and there to look for the word of the LORD. But they will not find it.

**13** On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will become weak from thirst.

**14** Some people make promises by the shameful idol of Samaria. They say, 'Dan, we promise by your god, who lives.' They say, 'We promise by the god of Beersheba, who lives.' Those people will fall and never get up again."

## Chapter 9

**1** I saw the Lord. He stood next to the altar. He said, "Hit the tops of the columns, so that the foundations shake. Make the building fall on the heads of all the people. I will kill with the sword the people who remain. Not one of them will run away. Not one of them will escape.

**2** If they dig down into the grave, I will take them out from there. If they climb up into the sky, I will bring them down from there.

**3** If they hide on the top of Mount Carmel, I will find them and take them from there. If they hide from me at the bottom of the sea, I will command the sea snake to bite them there.

**4** If their enemies take them into captivity, I will command the sword to kill them there. I will watch them to cause them harm, not to help them."

**5** The Lord GOD of armies touches the land, and the land melts. All the people who live in the land are sad. The whole land rises like the Nile River. Then it goes down again like the river of Egypt.

**6** He builds his rooms in the sky. He puts the base of the sky on the earth. He calls the water from the sea. He pours the water on the land. His name is the LORD.

**7** "People of Israel, to me you are the same as the people of Cush," the LORD says. "I brought Israel up from the land of Egypt. I also brought the Philistines from Caphtor. I also brought the people of Aram from Kir.

**8** I, the Lord GOD, watch the sinful kingdom. I will destroy it from the earth. But I will not destroy all the family of Jacob," the LORD says.

**9** "I will give the command. I will shake the people of Israel among all the nations, as a person shakes grain in a sieve. But not one small stone will fall to the ground.

**10** All the sinners among my people will die by the sword. They say, 'Disaster will not come near us. Disaster will not catch us.'

**11** On that day I will build again the fallen house of David. I will repair the holes in its walls. I will build again its ruins. I will make it as it was in the past.

**12** Then my people will take what remains of Edom. They will take all the nations that belong to my name," the LORD says. The LORD will do this.

**13** "The days will come," the LORD says, "when the harvest will be very large. The plowman will plow before the harvester finishes the harvest. The person who crushes grapes will work before the farmer finishes his work with the seed. Sweet wine will flow from the mountains. Wine will flow from all the hills.

**14** I will bring my people Israel back from captivity. They will build again the destroyed cities and live in them. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine. They will make gardens and eat their fruit.

**15** I will plant my people in their land. Nobody will pull them out of the land that I gave them again," the LORD your God says.

---

# Obadiah

## Chapter 1

**1** This is the vision that Obadiah saw. The Lord GOD speaks about Edom. We heard a message from the LORD. The LORD sent a messenger to the nations. The messenger said, "Get up! We will go and fight against Edom."

**2** The LORD says to Edom, "I will make you small among the nations. People will hate you very much."

**3** "Your pride tricked you. You live in the holes of the rock, and your home is high. You say to yourself, 'No one can bring me down to the ground.'

**4** You can go up high like an eagle. You can put your nest among the stars. But I will bring you down from there," says the LORD.

**5** "If thieves came to you at night, they took only what they wanted. If people came to collect your grapes, they left some grapes. But your enemies will destroy you completely!

**6** The enemies will search all the property of Esau. They will find all his hidden valuable things.

**7** All your allies will push you out to the border. The men who were your friends will trick you and defeat you. The men who eat your bread will set a trap for you. Edom will not understand it.

**8** On that day I will destroy the wise men of Edom," says the LORD. "I will remove wisdom from the mountain of Esau.

**9** Teman, your strong soldiers will be very afraid. Thus the enemies will kill all the people of the mountain of Esau.

**10** You did violent things to your brother Jacob. Thus shame will cover you, and I will destroy you for all time.

**11** On that day you stood and watched. Strangers took away the army of Jacob as prisoners. Foreigners went into the gates of Jerusalem. The foreigners threw lots for the city. You were like one of these foreigners.

**12** You must not look with pleasure at the bad day of your brother. You must not be happy when enemies destroy the people of Judah. You must not speak proudly on their day of trouble.

**13** You must not go into the gate of my people on the day of their disaster. You must not look with pleasure at their trouble on that day. You must not take their property on the day of their disaster.

**14** You must not stand at the crossroads to kill the people who escape. You must not give the survivors to their enemies on the day of trouble.

**15** The day of the LORD is near for all the nations. The LORD will do to you the same things that you did. The bad things that you did will come back on you.

**16** You drank on my holy mountain. In the same way, all the nations will drink my punishment continually. They will drink and swallow it. Then they will be as if they did not exist.

**17** But some people will escape and live on Mount Zion. Mount Zion will be holy. The people of Jacob will take back their land.

**18** The people of Jacob will be like a fire. The people of Joseph will be like a flame. The people of Esau will be like dry grass. Jacob and Joseph will burn Esau and destroy him. No one from the people of Esau will stay alive. The LORD said this.

**19** The people from the south will take the mountain of Esau. The people from the low hills will take the land of the Philistines. They will take the fields of Ephraim and the fields of Samaria. Benjamin will take Gilead.

**20** The army of Israelite prisoners will take the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath. The prisoners from Jerusalem who live in Sepharad will take the cities of the south.

**21** Rescuers will go up on Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau. The kingdom will belong to the LORD."

---

# Jonah

## Chapter 1

**1** The LORD spoke a message to Jonah, the son of Amittai. The LORD said,

**2** "Get up and go to Nineveh, the large city. Speak against the city. I see the evil things that its people do."

**3** But Jonah got up and ran away from the LORD to Tarshish. He went down to Joppa. There he found a ship that went to Tarshish. He paid the price of the trip and went onto the ship. He wanted to go with the sailors to Tarshish, away from the LORD.

**4** But the LORD sent a strong wind onto the sea. A very bad storm started on the sea. The storm almost broke the ship.

**5** The sailors were afraid. Each sailor called to his own god for help. The sailors threw the cargo into the sea to make the ship lighter. But Jonah went down into the lowest part of the ship. He lay down there and slept deeply.

**6** The captain of the ship came to Jonah. The captain said, "Why do you sleep? Get up! Call to your God. Maybe your God will think about us. Then we will not die."

**7** The sailors said to each other, "Come, we will throw lots. Then we will know who caused this trouble." The sailors threw lots, and the lot showed Jonah.

**8** Then the sailors said to Jonah, "Please tell us who caused this trouble. What is your work? Where do you come from? What is your country? What is your nation?"

**9** Jonah said to them, "I am a Hebrew. I respect and worship the LORD, the God of heaven. He made the sea and the dry land."

**10** Then the men were very afraid. They said to Jonah, "What did you do?" The men knew that Jonah ran away from the LORD, because Jonah told them.

**11** The sea became more and more violent. The sailors said to Jonah, "What must we do to you? We want the sea to become calm."

**12** Jonah said to them, "Lift me up and throw me into the sea. Then the sea will become calm for you. I know that this large storm came on you because of me."

**13** But the men rowed hard to bring the ship back to the land. They could not do it, because the sea became more and more violent against them.

**14** Then the men called to the LORD. They said, "Please, LORD, do not let us die for the life of this man. Do not blame us for the death of an innocent man. You, LORD, did what you wanted to do."

**15** Then the men lifted Jonah and threw him into the sea. The sea stopped its violent movement.

**16** The men feared the LORD very much. They gave a sacrifice to the LORD and made promises (vows) to him.

**17** The LORD prepared a large fish to swallow Jonah. Jonah was in the stomach of the fish for 3 days and 3 nights.

## Chapter 2

**1** Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the stomach of the fish.

**2** Jonah said, "I was in trouble, and I called to the LORD. The LORD answered me. I called for help from the place of the dead. You heard my voice.

**3** You threw me into the deep water, into the middle of the seas. The water flowed all around me. All your large waves went over me.

**4** Then I said, 'You sent me away from your sight. But I will look again at your holy temple.'

**5** The water closed around me and almost killed me. The deep sea was all around me. Seaweed was around my head.

**6** I went down to the bottom of the mountains. The earth closed its gates on me for all time. But you, LORD my God, brought my life up from the pit.

**7** When my life became weak, I remembered the LORD. My prayer came to you, into your holy temple.

**8** People who worship false gods turn away from the love that God can give them.

**9** But I will sing thanks to you and give a sacrifice to you. I will do what I promised. The LORD is the one who saves."

**10** Then the LORD spoke to the fish. The fish vomited Jonah out onto the dry land.

## Chapter 3

**1** The LORD spoke a message to Jonah a second time. The LORD said,

**2** "Get up and go to Nineveh, the large city. Tell the people the message that I give you."

**3** Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, as the LORD told him. Nineveh was a very large city. A person needed 3 days to walk across it.

**4** Jonah went into the city and walked for 1 day. He shouted, "After 40 more days, God will destroy Nineveh!"

**5** The people of Nineveh believed God. They told all the people to fast. All the people put on sackcloth, from the most important to the least important.

**6** The king of Nineveh heard the message. He got up from his throne and took off his royal clothes. He put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.

**7** The king and his officials sent an order through Nineveh. The order said, "People and animals must not eat anything. The cattle and the sheep must not eat anything. They must not eat food or drink water.

**8** People and animals must put on sackcloth. All people must pray strongly to God. Each person must stop his evil actions and his violence.

**9** Maybe God will change his mind. Maybe he will stop his strong anger. Then we will not die."

**10** God saw what the people did. He saw that they stopped their evil actions. Thus God changed his mind. He did not cause the disaster that he said he will cause.

## Chapter 4

**1** But Jonah did not like this at all. He became very angry.

**2** Jonah prayed to the LORD. He said, "LORD, I said this when I was still in my country! Thus I ran away to Tarshish at the start. I knew that you are a kind and merciful God. You do not become angry quickly. You have much love. You change your mind and do not send disaster.

**3** Now, LORD, please take my life. It is better for me to die than to live."

**4** The LORD said, "Is it right for you to be angry?"

**5** Jonah went out of the city and sat down at the east side of the city. There he made a shelter. He sat under the shelter in the shade. He waited to see what will happen to the city.

**6** The LORD God prepared a vine. The LORD God made the vine grow up over Jonah. The vine gave shade over his head and made him feel better. Jonah was very happy about the vine.

**7** But at sunrise on the next day, God prepared a worm. The worm attacked the vine, and the vine became dry.

**8** When the sun came up, God prepared a hot east wind. The sun shone on the head of Jonah, and he became weak. Jonah wanted to die. He said, "It is better for me to die than to live."

**9** God said to Jonah, "Is it right for you to be angry about the vine?" Jonah said, "Yes, it is right for me to be angry, even to death."

**10** The LORD said, "You feel sorry for the vine. You did not work for the vine, and you did not make it grow. The vine grew in 1 night and died in 1 night.

**11** Nineveh is a large city. More than 120,000 people live in it. These people do not know the difference between their right hand and their left hand. Also, many animals live in Nineveh. Thus I must feel sorry for Nineveh too."
