# Micah

## Chapter 1

**1** The LORD gave this message to Micah from Moresheth. Micah received the message when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah. Micah saw these things about Samaria and Jerusalem.

**2** Listen, all you nations! Listen, earth and all the things on it! The Lord GOD will speak against you. The Lord will speak from his holy temple.

**3** Look, the LORD comes out from his place. He will come down and walk on the high places of the earth.

**4** The mountains will melt under him. The valleys will break open. They will be like wax near a fire. They will be like water that flows down a steep slope.

**5** All this will occur because of the sins of Jacob and the sins of the people of Israel. What is the sin of Jacob? It is Samaria. What is the center of false worship in Judah? It is Jerusalem.

**6** "Thus I will make Samaria a pile of stones in a field. Samaria will be a place to plant vines. I will push its stones down into the valley. I will make its foundations bare.

**7** People will break all the idols of Samaria into pieces. Fire will burn all the gifts from her temple prostitutes. I will destroy all her idols. She got these things with the pay of a prostitute. Her enemies will use them again as the pay of prostitutes."

**8** Because of this, I will cry loudly. I will walk without shoes and without clothes. I will cry like a jackal. I will make a sad sound like an owl.

**9** Nobody can cure the wound of Samaria. The disaster comes to Judah. The disaster comes to the gate of my people, to Jerusalem.

**10** Do not tell the news in Gath. Do not cry at all. In Beth-le-aphrah, roll in the dust.

**11** People of Shaphir, go away as prisoners, naked and ashamed. The people of Zaanan will not come out. Beth-ezel will cry, and it will not give you protection.

**12** The people of Maroth wait anxiously for good things. But the LORD sent disaster down to the gate of Jerusalem.

**13** People of Lachish, attach fast horses to your chariots. Lachish started the sin of the people of Zion. The sins of Israel were in Lachish.

**14** Thus you will give farewell gifts to Moresheth-gath. The towns of Achzib will not help the kings of Israel. Achzib will disappoint them.

**15** People of Mareshah, I will bring an enemy who will take your land. The great men of Israel will hide in the cave of Adullam.

**16** Shave your heads and cut your hair to show your sadness. Mourn for the children that you love. Make yourselves bald like a vulture. Your enemies will take your children away as prisoners.

## Chapter 2

**1** Disaster will come to the people who plan evil things! They lie in their beds and plan bad actions. In the morning they do these bad actions, because they have the power.

**2** They want fields, and they take the fields by force. They want houses, and they take the houses. They cheat a man and take his house. They take the property of his family.

**3** Thus the LORD says, "I plan a disaster against these people. You will not escape from this disaster. You will not walk proudly, because it will be a bad time.

**4** On that day people will make a sad song about you. They will cry and say, 'We are completely destroyed! The LORD took away the land of my people. He took the land from me! He gave our fields to our enemies.'"

**5** Thus none of you will get a part of the land when the people of the LORD divide the land.

**6** The false prophets say, "Do not prophesy. Do not prophesy about these things. Disgrace will not come on us."

**7** People of Jacob, must people say this? "The Spirit of the LORD is not patient. The LORD does not do these things." My words do good to the person who lives correctly.

**8** But recently my people became like an enemy. You take the coats from people who pass by. These people feel safe, like men who come back from war.

**9** You push the women of my people out of their good houses. You take my blessing away from their children for all time.

**10** Get up and go away! This land is not a place of rest for you. Sin made this land unclean. Thus the land will destroy you completely.

**11** A man can tell lies and say, "I will prophesy to you about wine and strong drink." That man is the right prophet for these people!

**12** "Jacob, I will certainly bring all of you together. I will certainly collect the remnant of Israel. I will put them together like sheep in a pen. They will be like a flock in its field. The place will be full of people and noise.

**13** The one who breaks open the way will go in front of them. They will break through the gate and go out. Their king will go in front of them. The LORD will lead them."

## Chapter 3

**1** I said, "Listen, leaders of Jacob and rulers of Israel! You must know what is just.

**2** But you hate good and love evil. You pull the skin off my people. You pull the flesh off their bones.

**3** You eat the flesh of my people. You pull off their skin and break their bones. You cut them into pieces like meat for a pot."

**4** Then these leaders will call to the LORD for help. But the LORD will not answer them. At that time he will hide his face from them, because they did evil things.

**5** The prophets lead my people the wrong way. The LORD says this about them: "When people give these prophets food, the prophets say, 'You will have peace.' When people do not give them food, the prophets start a war against them.

**6** Thus night will come on you, and you will not see visions. Darkness will come on you, and you will not tell the future. The sun will go down on the prophets. The day will become dark for them.

**7** The seers will feel shame. The people who tell the future will lose their honor. They will all cover their faces, because God will not answer them."

**8** But the Spirit of the LORD fills me with power. He gives me justice and strength. Thus I can tell Jacob about his crimes. I can tell Israel about his sin.

**9** Listen to this, leaders of Jacob and rulers of Israel! You hate justice. You make right things wrong.

**10** You build Zion with murder. You build Jerusalem with evil actions.

**11** The leaders of the city judge for bribes. The priests teach for pay. The prophets tell the future for money. But they lean on the LORD. They say, "The LORD is with us. No disaster will come to us."

**12** Because of you, enemies will plow Zion like a field. Jerusalem will become a pile of stones. Trees and bushes will cover the hill of the temple.

## Chapter 4

**1** In the last days, the mountain of the temple of the LORD will be the highest mountain. It will be higher than the hills. People from many nations will go to it.

**2** Many nations will come and say, "Come, we will go up to the mountain of the LORD. We will go to the temple of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways. We will obey him." The law will come from Zion. The word of the LORD will come from Jerusalem.

**3** The LORD will judge between many nations. He will settle the arguments of strong nations far away. They will make their swords into plows. They will make their spears into tools to cut vines. Nations will not fight against other nations. They will not train for war again.

**4** Each man will sit under his own grapevine and his own fig tree. No person will make them afraid. The LORD of armies said this.

**5** All the nations follow their own gods. But we will follow the LORD our God for all time.

**6** "On that day," says the LORD, "I will bring together the people who are lame. I will collect the people whom enemies sent away. I will collect the people whom I punished.

**7** I will make the lame people a remnant. I will make the people who were far away a strong nation. The LORD will rule them on Mount Zion from that time and for all time.

**8** Jerusalem, you are like a watchtower for a flock. You are the fortress of the people of Zion. Your old power will come back to you. The kingdom will come back to the people of Jerusalem."

**9** Now why do you cry loudly? Do you have no king? Did your adviser die? You feel pain like a woman who gives birth.

**10** People of Zion, have pain and push like a woman who gives birth. Now you must go out of the city and live in the fields. You will go to Babylon. There the LORD will save you. He will rescue you from your enemies.

**11** Now many nations are together against you. They say, "Let Zion become unclean. We want to look at Zion and be glad."

**12** But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD. They do not understand his plan. He will collect them like bundles of grain on the floor where people beat the grain.

**13** "People of Zion, get up and crush them! I will make you strong like an ox with horns of iron. I will make your hooves of bronze. You will break many nations into pieces. You will give their stolen wealth to the LORD. You will give their property to the Lord of all the earth."

## Chapter 5

**1** City of soldiers, now collect your troops. The enemy attacks us. The enemy will hit the ruler of Israel on the cheek with a stick.

**2** "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, are small among the clans of Judah. But a ruler of Israel will come out from you for me. His family starts from very old times, from long ago."

**3** Thus the LORD will leave Israel to its enemies until the woman in labor gives birth. Then the rest of his brothers will come back to the people of Israel.

**4** The ruler will stand and take care of his people like a shepherd. He will do this in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. His people will live safely. His greatness will go to the ends of the earth.

**5** He will be our peace. The Assyrians will come into our land and walk through our fortresses. Then we will send 7 shepherds and 8 leaders against them.

**6** These leaders will rule the land of Assyria with the sword. They will rule the land of Nimrod at its gates. The ruler will save us from the Assyrians when they come into our land and cross our borders.

**7** The remnant of Jacob will live among many nations. They will be like dew from the LORD. They will be like rain on the grass. The rain does not wait for people.

**8** The remnant of Jacob will live among the nations. They will be like a lion among the animals of the forest. They will be like a young lion among flocks of sheep. When the lion goes through, it pushes the sheep down and tears them. No one can save the sheep.

**9** You will defeat your enemies. You will destroy all your enemies.

**10** "On that day," says the LORD, "I will take your horses away from you. I will destroy your chariots.

**11** I will destroy the cities of your land. I will pull down all your fortresses.

**12** I will stop your witchcraft. You will not have fortune-tellers again.

**13** I will destroy your idols and your sacred stones. You will not worship the things that you make with your hands again.

**14** I will pull up your Asherah poles from among you. I will destroy your cities.

**15** I will punish the nations that do not obey me. I will punish them with anger and fury. The nations never heard of a punishment like this."

## Chapter 6

**1** Listen to what the LORD says: "Get up and state your case in front of the mountains. Let the hills hear your voice."

**2** Mountains, listen to the accusation of the LORD. Strong foundations of the earth, listen. The LORD has a case against his people. He will argue against Israel.

**3** "My people, what did I do to you? How did I make you tired? Tell me!

**4** I brought you out of the land of Egypt. I freed you from slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to lead you.

**5** My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned. Remember how Balaam the son of Beor answered him. Remember your trip from Shittim to Gilgal. Then you will know that the LORD does right things."

**6** What must I bring when I come to the LORD? What must I bring when I bow down to God most high? Must I come with burnt offerings? Must I bring calves that are 1 year old?

**7** Will the LORD be happy with 1,000s of rams? Will he be happy with 10,000s of rivers of olive oil? Must I give my firstborn child for my sins? Must I give my child for the sin of my soul?

**8** Man, the LORD showed you what is good. The LORD wants you to do what is right. He wants you to love mercy. He wants you to live humbly with your God.

**9** The LORD calls to the city. A wise person respects your name. Listen to the punishment and to the one who sends it.

**10** Wicked people still keep treasures that they got by evil means. They still use false measures. I hate these false measures.

**11** Must I say that a man is innocent if he uses false scales? Must I say that he is innocent if he has a bag of false weights?

**12** The rich people of the city are full of violence. The people who live there tell lies. Their words are false.

**13** Thus I will hit you and make you sick. I will destroy you because of your sins.

**14** You will eat, but you will not be full. Your stomach will stay empty. You will try to save your property, but you will not save it. I will give to the sword the things that you save.

**15** You will plant seeds, but you will not harvest the crops. You will crush olives, but you will not put the oil on your body. You will crush grapes, but you will not drink the wine.

**16** You obey the laws of Omri. You do all the things that the family of Ahab did. You follow their advice. Thus I will destroy you. People will laugh at the people of your city. You will feel the shame of my people."

## Chapter 7

**1** I am very sad! I am like a person who comes after the summer harvest. The workers collected all the grapes. There is no fruit to eat. I want to eat the first figs, but there are none.

**2** All the good people are gone from the land. No honest person remains. All the people hide and wait to kill. Each man hunts his brother with a net.

**3** The people are good at evil things with both hands. The ruler and the judge ask for bribes. The important man tells what he wants. Together they plan evil.

**4** The best of them is like a thorny bush. The most honest of them is worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your punishment comes. Your watchmen told you about this day. Now the people will not know what to do.

**5** Do not trust a neighbor. Do not trust a friend. Be careful what you say, even to your wife.

**6** A son does not respect his father. A daughter goes against her mother. A daughter-in-law goes against her mother-in-law. The enemies of a man are the people of his own family.

**7** But I will look to the LORD. I will wait for God, who saves me. My God will hear me.

**8** My enemy, do not be happy about my trouble. When I fall, I will get up again. When I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.

**9** I sinned against the LORD. Thus I will accept his anger until he takes my side and gives me justice. He will bring me out into the light. I will see his righteousness.

**10** Then my enemy will see this, and shame will cover her. She said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" I will see her fall. People will walk on her like mud in the streets.

**11** A day will come when people build your walls again. On that day your borders will become larger.

**12** On that day people will come to you from Assyria and from the cities of Egypt. They will come from Egypt to the Euphrates River, from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.

**13** But the earth will become empty because of the people who live on it. This will occur because of the evil things that they do.

**14** LORD, take care of your people with your staff, like a shepherd. Your people are like a flock. They live alone in a forest, in the middle of fertile land. Let them eat in Bashan and Gilead, as in the old days.

**15** "I will show them wonderful things, as when you came out of the land of Egypt."

**16** The nations will see this and feel shame for all their power. They will put their hands over their mouths. Their ears will become deaf.

**17** They will lick the dust like a snake. They will come out of their holes like worms. They will come to the LORD our God in fear. They will be afraid of you.

**18** No god is like you. You forgive sin. You forgive the crimes of the remnant of your people. You do not stay angry for all time, because you like to show mercy.

**19** You will have pity on us again. You will defeat our sins. You will throw all our sins into the deep sea.

**20** You will be faithful to Jacob. You will show your love to Abraham. You promised these things to our ancestors long ago.

---

# Nahum

## Chapter 1

**1** This is the message about Nineveh. This is the book of the vision of Nahum, the man from Elkosh.

**2** God is a jealous God, and the LORD punishes his enemies. The LORD punishes, and he is very angry. The LORD will punish the people who are against him. He keeps his anger for his enemies.

**3** The LORD is slow to become angry, and he has great power. The LORD will not let guilty people go free. The LORD moves in the strong wind and in the storm. The clouds are like the dust below his feet.

**4** He gives a command to the sea, and the sea becomes dry. He causes all the rivers to become dry. The land of Bashan and the land of Carmel become weak. The flowers of Lebanon become dry and die.

**5** The mountains shake in front of him, and the hills melt. The earth shakes when he comes. The world and all the people who live in it shake.

**6** Who can stand in front of his anger? Who can stay alive when his anger is strong? His anger flows out like fire. He breaks the rocks into pieces.

**7** The LORD is good. He is a strong place of safety in the time of trouble. He knows the people who trust him.

**8** But he will send a large flood and he will fully destroy Nineveh. He will send his enemies into darkness.

**9** What do you plan against the LORD? He will fully destroy his enemies. Trouble will not come a second time.

**10** The enemies are like thorn bushes that grow together. They are like drunk men. Fire will burn them as it burns dry straw.

**11** A man came out from you, Nineveh. He plans evil against the LORD. He gives bad advice.

**12** The LORD says this: "The Assyrians are strong, and there are many of them. But I will cut them down, and they will go away. Judah, I caused you trouble before. But I will not cause you trouble again.

**13** Now I will break the heavy load that the Assyrians put on you. I will break the chains that hold you."

**14** The LORD gave a command about you, king of Assyria: "You will have no sons to keep your name alive. I will remove the carved idols and the metal idols from the temple of your gods. I will make your grave, because you are very bad."

**15** Look! A man comes on the mountains. He brings good news, and he tells about peace. People of Judah, keep your holy festivals. Do the things that you promised to do. The evil enemy will not attack you again. The LORD will fully destroy him.

## Chapter 2

**1** Nineveh, an enemy comes to attack you and break you into pieces. Guard your strong walls. Watch the road. Make yourself ready for war. Make your army very strong.

**2** The enemies took everything from the people of Jacob. They destroyed their vines. But the LORD will make the people of Jacob great again, as the people of Israel were great before.

**3** The shields of the enemy soldiers are red. The brave soldiers wear red clothes. The metal on the chariots shines like fire on the day that the soldiers prepare for war. The soldiers shake their spears of fir wood.

**4** The chariots move very quickly in the streets. They hit one another in the wide roads. They look like torches of fire. They move as fast as lightning.

**5** The king of Nineveh calls his best officers. But they fall as they walk. They run quickly to the wall of the city. The enemy puts a shield in position to protect the soldiers who attack.

**6** The enemy opens the gates of the rivers, and the palace falls down.

**7** The enemy takes away the queen of the city as a prisoner. Her women servants make sad sounds like doves. They hit their chests because they are sad.

**8** Nineveh was full of people as a pool is full of water. But now the people run away. Some people shout, "Stop! Stop!" But no person turns back.

**9** Take the silver! Take the gold! The city has a very large quantity of valuable things. There is no end to the treasure.

**10** The enemy takes everything from Nineveh, and the city is empty and destroyed. The people are very afraid, and their knees shake. Their bodies have much pain. All their faces become pale.

**11** Where is the home of the lions now? Where is the place where the young lions ate? The male lion, the female lion and the young lions walked there. No person made them afraid.

**12** The lion killed enough food for his young lions. He killed animals for his female lions. He filled his caves with the animals that he killed.

**13** The LORD of armies says, "I am against you, Nineveh. I will burn your chariots, and they will become smoke. The sword will kill your young soldiers. I will stop you. You will not take things from the earth again. People will not hear the voices of your messengers again."

## Chapter 3

**1** Nineveh will have much trouble! The people of that city killed many people. The city is full of lies and of things that people stole. The people in the city always take things from other people.

**2** Listen to the sound of the whips! Listen to the noise of the wheels! Hear the horses that run and the chariots that jump!

**3** The horsemen attack with bright swords and spears that shine. They kill very many people. There are very many dead bodies. People fall over the dead bodies.

**4** All this happens because Nineveh is like a beautiful prostitute. She uses magic to get power. She makes nations into slaves by her prostitution. She controls families with her magic.

**5** The LORD of armies says, "I am against you, Nineveh. I will lift your skirt up over your face. I will show your naked body to the nations. The kingdoms will see your shame.

**6** I will throw dirt on you. I will cause people to think that you are worthless. I will make you an example for all people to see.

**7** All the people who see you will run away from you. They will say, 'Nineveh is a ruin. Who will be sad for her?' Nineveh, I cannot find a person who will comfort you."

**8** Nineveh, are you better than the city of Thebes? Thebes was near the Nile River, and water was all around it. The river was its wall of defense. The water protected it.

**9** Ethiopia and Egypt gave Thebes very much strength. Put and Libya also helped Thebes.

**10** But the enemy took the people of Thebes away as prisoners. The enemy killed her young children at the corners of all the streets. The enemy threw lots for her important men. They put chains on all her leaders.

**11** Nineveh, you will also become like a drunk person. You will try to hide. You will look for a place of safety from your enemy.

**12** All your strong towers are like fig trees with the first ripe figs. When a person shakes the trees, the figs fall into the mouth of the person who eats them.

**13** Look at your soldiers. They are weak like women. The gates of your land are open to your enemies. Fire burns the bars of your gates.

**14** Get water to prepare for the attack. Make your strong towers stronger. Go and get clay. Push the clay with your feet to make mud. Make bricks in the oven.

**15** But the fire will burn you there. The sword will kill you. The sword will destroy you as locusts eat plants. Make your people as many as the locusts. Make your people as many as the grasshoppers.

**16** You made your merchants more than the stars in the sky. But they are like locusts that eat everything and then fly away.

**17** Your officials are like locusts. Your officers are like large grasshoppers. Grasshoppers stay in the walls on a cold day. But when the sun comes up, they fly away. No person knows where they go.

**18** King of Assyria, your leaders are asleep. Your important men lie down and rest. Your people are in many different places on the mountains. No person brings them together.

**19** No person can make your injury better. Your wound is very bad. All the people who hear the news about you will clap their hands with joy. All people felt the pain of your cruel actions all the time.

---

# Habakkuk

## Chapter 1

**1** This is the message that Habakkuk the prophet saw.

**2** LORD, how long must I call to you for help? You do not hear me. I shout to you about violence, but you do not save us.

**3** Why do you show me bad actions? Why do you cause me to see trouble? People destroy things and do violent actions in front of me. People fight and argue.

**4** Thus people do not obey the law. Judges never give fair decisions. Evil people are all around the good people. Thus the judges give wrong decisions.

**5** "Look at the nations and watch carefully. You will be very surprised. I will do a thing in your time that you will not believe. You will not believe it when people tell you about it.

**6** I will cause the Chaldeans to become strong. They are a cruel nation that moves quickly. They will go across all the earth. They will take homes that are not theirs.

**7** People are very afraid of the Chaldeans. The Chaldeans make their own laws. They give honor to themselves.

**8** Their horses are faster than leopards. Their horses are more dangerous than wolves in the evening. Their horsemen come from far away. They attack quickly, as an eagle flies down quickly to eat its food.

**9** All of the Chaldeans come to do violence. Their army moves forward like the east wind. They take very many prisoners, as many as the grains of sand.

**10** The Chaldeans laugh at kings. They laugh at rulers. They laugh at all the strong cities. They put earth up against the walls, and they capture the cities.

**11** Then they move on quickly like the wind. They are guilty, because their strength is their god."

**12** LORD, you lived always, from the start of time. You are my God and my Holy One. We will not die. LORD, you chose the Chaldeans to punish us. Mighty God, you made them strong to correct us.

**13** Your eyes are too pure to look at evil. You cannot look at bad actions. Thus why do you look at people who are not loyal? Why are you silent when evil people destroy people who are better than them?

**14** You make people like the fish in the sea. You make them like small animals that have no ruler.

**15** The enemy catches all of these people with hooks. He catches them in his net. He gathers them in his large net. Thus he is very happy.

**16** Thus he offers sacrifices to his net. He burns incense to his large net. His net gives him a rich life and much good food.

**17** Will he always empty his net? Will he always kill the nations without pity?

## Chapter 2

**1** I will stand at my place of watch. I will stay on the tower. I will watch to see what the LORD will say to me. I will see what answer I must give about my complaint.

**2** The LORD answered me. He said, "Write the vision. Write it clearly on tablets. Then a messenger can read it easily and run with the message.

**3** The vision will come true at the correct time. At the end, the vision will become true. It will not be false. If it is slow, wait for it. It will certainly come, and it will not be late.

**4** Look! The proud man does not have a good spirit. But the good person will live by his faith.

**5** Wine makes the proud man do wrong things. He is proud and he does not stay at home. He always wants more, as the grave always wants more people. He is like death and is never satisfied. He takes all the nations for himself. He gathers all the peoples for himself.

**6** All these nations will laugh at him. They will speak a song about him and say, 'He will have much trouble! He takes things that are not his. How long will he do this? He makes himself rich with things that he took from other people.'

**7** Your enemies will suddenly attack you. They will wake up and cause you to be afraid. They will take your possessions.

**8** You stole from many nations. Thus all the people who stay alive will steal from you. You killed many people. You did violent actions to the land, to the cities and to all the people who live in them.

**9** The man who gets money for his family by evil actions will have much trouble! He builds his house in a high place. He thinks that he will be safe from danger there.

**10** You made plans to kill many people. These plans bring shame on your family. You sinned against yourself.

**11** The stones in the wall will shout against you. The wood in the roof will say the same thing.

**12** The man who builds a town with the blood of people will have much trouble! The man who makes a city strong by evil actions will have much trouble!

**13** The LORD of armies decided that the work of the nations will burn in the fire. The peoples will become tired for nothing.

**14** The waters fill the sea. In the same way, the knowledge of the glory of the LORD will fill the earth.

**15** The man who gives wine to his neighbor will have much trouble! He makes his neighbor drunk. Then he looks at the naked bodies of the people.

**16** You will be full of shame and not of honor. Now you must drink too, and show your naked body. The LORD will give you the cup of punishment from his right hand. Shame will cover your honor.

**17** You did violent actions to the forests of Lebanon. Now violence will come on you. You killed the animals, and now you will be afraid. You killed people. You did violent actions to the land, to the cities and to all the people who live in them.

**18** An idol does not help a person. A man makes an idol from wood or from metal. The idol teaches lies. The man who makes the idol trusts in his own work. But idols cannot speak.

**19** The man who says to a piece of wood, 'Wake up!' will have much trouble! He says to a stone that cannot speak, 'Get up!' Can the idol teach? Look! Gold and silver cover it. But it has no breath in it.

**20** But the LORD is in his holy temple. All the earth must be silent in front of him."

## Chapter 3

**1** This is a prayer of Habakkuk the prophet. It is a song.

**2** LORD, I heard about you, and I am afraid of the things that you did. LORD, do your work again in our time. Make your work known in our time. When you are angry, remember to show mercy.

**3** God came from Teman. The Holy One came from Mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the skies. The earth was full of his praise.

**4** His brightness was like the sun. Light came from his hand. His power was there, in a secret place.

**5** Disease went in front of him. Death followed behind him.

**6** He stood and shook the earth. He looked at the nations, and they shook with fear. The very old mountains broke into pieces. The old hills fell down. His ways are always the same.

**7** I saw the people of Cushan in trouble. The people in the tents of Midian shook with fear.

**8** LORD, were you angry with the rivers? Were you angry with the sea? You rode on your horses and in your chariots to save your people.

**9** You took out your bow. You used your arrows as you promised. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.

**10** The mountains saw you, and they shook. Water flowed past in a flood. The deep water made a loud noise. The waves went up high.

**11** The sun and the moon stopped in the sky. They stopped when they saw the light of your arrows and your spear that shines.

**12** You went across the earth in anger. You walked on the nations in anger.

**13** You went out to save your people. You went to save your chosen king. You killed the leader of the evil nation. You destroyed his house fully, from the base to the top. Selah.

**14** The enemy soldiers came like a storm to scatter us. They were happy, as if they were about to destroy poor people in secret. But you killed their leader with his own spear.

**15** You walked on the sea with your horses. You moved through the large waves.

**16** I heard this, and my body shook. My lips shook at the sound. My bones became weak. My legs shook below me. But I will wait quietly for the day of trouble. That day will come to the nation that attacks us.

**17** Maybe the fig trees will have no flowers, and the vines will have no grapes. Maybe the olive trees will have no olives, and the fields will make no food. Maybe the sheep will die in the field, and there will be no cattle in the barns.

**18** But I will be happy in the LORD. I will have joy in the God who saves me.

**19** The LORD God is my strength. He makes my feet strong like the feet of a deer. He lets me walk on the high places. For the music director. Play this song on stringed instruments.

# Zephaniah

## Chapter 1

**1** The LORD gave this message to Zephaniah. Zephaniah was the son of Cushi. Cushi was the son of Gedaliah. Gedaliah was the son of Amariah, and Amariah was the son of Hezekiah. The LORD spoke to Zephaniah when Josiah, the son of Amon, was king of Judah.

**2** The LORD says, "I will fully destroy all things on the surface of the earth.

**3** I will destroy people and animals. I will destroy the birds in the sky and the fish in the sea. I will destroy the idols that cause people to sin, and I will destroy evil people. I will remove all people from the earth," says the LORD.

**4** "I will punish Judah and all the people who live in Jerusalem. I will remove from this place all the things that people use to worship Baal. I will remove the names of the idol priests and the other priests.

**5** I will destroy the people who worship the stars from the roofs of their houses. I will destroy the people who worship the LORD and also make promises in the name of Molech.

**6** I will destroy the people who turn away from the LORD. I will destroy the people who do not look for the LORD or ask him for help."

**7** Be silent in front of the Lord GOD! The day of the LORD is near. The LORD prepared a sacrifice. He told his guests to make themselves holy.

**8** "On the day of the LORD's sacrifice, I will punish the officials and the sons of the king. I will punish all the people who wear the clothes of foreign nations.

**9** On that day, I will punish all the people who worship as foreigners do. They fill the houses of their masters with violence and lies."

**10** The LORD says, "On that day, people will shout from the Fish Gate. People will cry loudly in the new part of the city. People will hear a loud noise of destruction from the hills.

**11** Cry loudly, you people who live in the market area! All the merchants will die. All the people who trade with silver will die.

**12** At that time, I will use lamps to look carefully in all of Jerusalem. I will punish the people who are lazy and satisfied. They think, 'The LORD will not do good. He will not do bad.'

**13** Thus enemies will steal their possessions. Enemies will destroy their houses. The people will build houses, but they will not live in them. They will plant vineyards, but they will not drink the wine."

**14** The great day of the LORD is near. It is near and it comes very quickly. Listen! On the day of the LORD, the strong soldiers will cry loudly in pain.

**15** That day will be a day of anger. It will be a day of trouble and pain. It will be a day of ruin and destruction. It will be a day of darkness and gloom. It will be a day of clouds and thick darkness.

**16** It will be a day when soldiers blow the trumpets and shout for war. They will attack the strong cities and the high towers.

**17** "I will bring trouble on the people. They will walk like blind men, because they sinned against the LORD. Their blood will flow out like dust on the ground. Their dead bodies will lie like waste on the ground.

**18** Their silver and their gold will not save them on the day of the LORD's anger. The fire of his jealous anger will destroy all the earth. He will suddenly destroy all the people who live on the earth."

## Chapter 2

**1** Come together, you shameful nation. Come together.

**2** Do this before the LORD's decision becomes true. Do this before the day goes away like dust in the wind. Do this before the strong anger of the LORD comes on you. Do this before the day of the LORD's anger comes.

**3** All you humble people of the earth, look for the LORD. You obey his laws. Look for what is right. Be humble. Maybe the LORD will protect you on the day of his anger.

**4** No people will live in Gaza. Ashkelon will become a ruin. Enemies will force the people of Ashdod out at noon. Enemies will destroy Ekron.

**5** The people who live by the sea, the nation of the Cherethites, will have much trouble! The LORD speaks against you, Canaan, the land of the Philistines. "I will destroy you, and no people will live in you."

**6** The land by the sea will become fields for shepherds. It will have places for sheep.

**7** The land by the sea will belong to the people of Judah who stay alive. They will feed their sheep there. In the evening, they will lie down in the houses of Ashkelon. The LORD their God will help them. He will bring back their prisoners.

**8** "I heard the insults of Moab and the insults of the people of Ammon. They insulted my people. They said proud things about their land and tried to take it.

**9** Thus, as I live," says the LORD of armies, the God of Israel, "Moab will become like Sodom. The people of Ammon will become like Gomorrah. Their land will be full of weeds and salt pits. It will always be a ruin. My people who stay alive will take their possessions. My people will take their land."

**10** Moab and Ammon will get this punishment because of their pride. They insulted the people of the LORD of armies and said proud things against them.

**11** The LORD will cause these people to be very afraid. He will destroy all the gods of the earth. Then all the nations will worship the LORD, each nation in its own land.

**12** "You people of Ethiopia, my sword will also kill you."

**13** The LORD will use his power against the north and destroy Assyria. He will make Nineveh a ruin. Nineveh will become dry like a desert.

**14** Flocks of sheep and all types of animals will lie down in the city. Owls will sleep on the tops of the broken columns. Their calls will come through the windows. There will be ruins at the doors. The LORD will remove the cedar wood from the buildings.

**15** Nineveh was a happy city that felt safe. The people of Nineveh said to themselves, "We are the most important city. There is no other city like us." But now Nineveh is a ruin, a place where wild animals lie down! All the people who go past the city laugh at it. They wave their fists at it.

## Chapter 3

**1** Jerusalem will have much trouble! The city does not obey God, and it is not clean. The people in the city are cruel to other people.

**2** The people do not obey the voice of the LORD. They do not accept correction. They do not trust in the LORD. They do not come near to their God.

**3** The officials in the city are like lions that roar. Her judges are like wolves in the evening. In the morning, they leave nothing.

**4** Her prophets are proud, and people cannot trust them. Her priests make the holy place unclean. They break the law.

**5** But the LORD is in the city, and he is fair. He does no wrong. Every morning he gives fair decisions. He never fails. But the evil people feel no shame.

**6** "I destroyed nations. I destroyed their towers. I made their streets empty, and no person goes on them. I destroyed their cities. No person lives there now.

**7** I said to Jerusalem, 'Surely you will respect me now. You will accept correction.' Then I will not destroy her houses or punish her. But the people were eager to do more evil actions."

**8** The LORD says, "Thus wait for me. Wait until the day that I stand up to accuse the nations. I decided to gather the nations and the kingdoms. I will show them all my strong anger. The fire of my jealous anger will destroy all the earth.

**9** Then I will make the speech of the peoples pure. Then all of them will call on the name of the LORD. They will all serve him together.

**10** My people are in many places, even on the other side of the rivers of Ethiopia. They will pray to me and bring offerings to me.

**11** On that day, you will not feel shame for the wrong things that you did against me. I will remove the proud people from the city. You will not be proud again on my holy mountain.

**12** But I will keep in the city a group of humble and poor people. They will trust in the name of the LORD.

**13** The people of Israel who stay alive will not do wrong things. They will not tell lies. They will not try to trick other people. They will eat and rest. No person will make them afraid."

**14** Sing, people of Zion! Shout, people of Israel! Be happy and have joy with all your heart, people of Jerusalem!

**15** The LORD stopped your punishment. He sent your enemies away. The LORD, the king of Israel, is with you. You will not be afraid of harm again.

**16** On that day, people will say to Jerusalem, "Do not be afraid, Zion. Do not let your hands become weak.

**17** The LORD your God is with you. He is strong, and he will save you. He will be very happy about you. He will be quiet in his love for you. He will sing with joy about you."

**18** "I will gather the people who are sad because they cannot go to the holy festivals. They belong to you. Their shame was a heavy load for them.

**19** At that time, I will punish all the people who caused you trouble. I will save the people who cannot walk well. I will gather the people whom enemies forced away. I will give them praise and honor in every land where people put shame on them.

**20** At that time, I will gather you and bring you home. I will make you famous and give you praise among all the peoples of the earth. You will see me bring back your possessions," says the LORD.

# Haggai

## Chapter 1

**1** This occurred in the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month. The LORD gave a message through the prophet Haggai. The message was for Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah. It was also for Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest. The message said:

**2** "The LORD of armies says this: 'These people say, "The time did not come yet to build the house of the LORD."'"

**3** Then the LORD gave a message through the prophet Haggai. The message said:

**4** "You live in houses with good wood panels on the walls. But my house is in ruins. Is it correct for you to do this?"

**5** Thus the LORD of armies says this: "Think carefully about what you do.

**6** You put much seed in the ground, but you get only a small harvest. You eat, but you do not have sufficient food. You drink, but you are still thirsty. You put on clothes, but no person is warm. A worker gets his pay, but the money goes away as if into a bag with holes."

**7** The LORD of armies says this: "Think carefully about what you do.

**8** Go up to the mountains. Bring wood and build my house. Then the house will make me glad, and people will give me honor," says the LORD.

**9** "You expected much, but you got only a little. When you brought the harvest home, I blew it away. Why did I do this?" says the LORD of armies. "I did this because my house is in ruins. But each one of you is busy with his own house.

**10** Thus the sky above you holds back the dew. The earth holds back its crops.

**11** I caused a time with no rain on the land and on the mountains. The dry time came on the grain, the new wine, and the olive oil. It came on all the crops of the ground. It came on people and on animals, and on all the work of your hands."

**12** Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, obeyed the voice of the LORD their God. All the people who remained obeyed too. They obeyed the words of the prophet Haggai, because the LORD their God sent him. The people had fear and respect for the LORD.

**13** Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, gave the message of the LORD to the people. He said, "The LORD says, 'I am with you.'"

**14** The LORD gave new energy to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah. He gave new energy to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest. He gave new energy to all the people who remained. They came and started to work on the house of the LORD of armies, their God.

**15** They started on the 24th day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.

## Chapter 2

**1** On the 21st day of the seventh month, the LORD gave a message through the prophet Haggai. The message said:

**2** "Speak to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah. Speak to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest. Speak to the people who remain. Tell them this:

**3** 'Which of you saw this house in its first glory? How does the house look to you now? To you, it seems to be nothing.

**4** But now be strong, Zerubbabel,' says the LORD. 'Be strong, Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,' says the LORD. 'Do the work, because I am with you,' says the LORD of armies.

**5** 'I made a promise to you when you came out of Egypt. Because of that promise, my Spirit stays among you. Do not be afraid.'

**6** The LORD of armies says this: 'After a short time, I will shake the heavens and the earth one more time. I will shake the sea and the dry land.

**7** I will shake all the nations. Then the valuable things of all the nations will come here. I will fill this house with glory,' says the LORD of armies.

**8** 'The silver is mine and the gold is mine,' says the LORD of armies.

**9** 'The glory of this new house will be greater than the glory of the old house,' says the LORD of armies. 'In this place I will give peace,' says the LORD of armies."

**10** On the 24th day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the LORD gave a message to the prophet Haggai. The message said:

**11** "The LORD of armies says this: 'Ask the priests a question about the law.

**12** A man carries holy meat in the fold of his clothes. Then his clothes touch bread, soup, wine, olive oil, or other food. Does that food become holy?'" The priests answered, "No."

**13** Then Haggai said, "A person touches a dead body, and thus he becomes unclean. Then he touches one of these foods. Does that food become unclean?" The priests answered, "Yes, it becomes unclean."

**14** Then Haggai said, "The LORD says, 'These people and this nation are the same in my view. All the work of their hands is unclean. All that they offer there is unclean.

**15** Now think carefully about the time before today. Think about the time before you put one stone on another stone in the temple of the LORD.

**16** In that time, a man came to a pile of grain and expected 20 measures. But he found only 10. A man came to the wine container to get 50 measures. But he found only 20.

**17** I attacked all the work of your hands with hot wind, plant disease, and hail. But you did not come back to me,' says the LORD.

**18** 'Think carefully about the time from today forward. Today is the 24th day of the ninth month. On this day you put down the base of the temple of the LORD. Think about it carefully.

**19** Is there seed in the storage building now? The vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate tree, and the olive tree did not produce fruit yet. But from today I will bless you.'"

**20** On the 24th day of the month, the LORD gave a second message to Haggai. The message said:

**21** "Speak to Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah. Tell him, 'I will shake the heavens and the earth.

**22** I will throw down the thrones of kingdoms. I will destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations. I will throw down the chariots and the men in them. The horses and their riders will fall. Each man will kill another man with his sword.

**23** "At that time," says the LORD of armies, "I will take you, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, my servant," says the LORD. "I will make you like my seal ring, because I chose you," says the LORD of armies.'"

---

# Zechariah

## Chapter 1

**1** In the eighth month of the second year of Darius, the LORD gave a message to the prophet Zechariah. Zechariah was the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo. The message said:

**2** "The LORD was very angry with your ancestors.

**3** Thus tell the people this. The LORD of armies says, 'Come back to me.' The LORD of armies says, 'Then I will come back to you.'

**4** Do not be like your ancestors. The prophets before you called out to them. The prophets said, "The LORD of armies says this: Turn away from your evil ways and your evil actions." But your ancestors did not listen. They did not obey me,' says the LORD.

**5** 'Where are your ancestors now? Do the prophets live forever?

**6** I gave my words and my laws to my servants the prophets. My words and laws came true against your ancestors. Then your ancestors turned back. They said, "The LORD of armies did to us what he decided to do. He punished us because of our ways and our actions."'"

**7** It was the second year of Darius. On the 24th day of the eleventh month, the month Shebat, the LORD gave a message to the prophet Zechariah. Zechariah was the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo. Zechariah said:

**8** In the night I saw a vision. A man sat on a red horse. He stood among the myrtle trees in a valley. Behind him were red horses, brown horses, and white horses.

**9** I asked, "My lord, what are these horses?" The angel who spoke with me said, "I will show you what they are."

**10** The man who stood among the myrtle trees answered. He said, "The LORD sent these riders to go across all the earth."

**11** The riders spoke to the angel of the LORD, who stood among the myrtle trees. They said, "We went across all the earth. All the earth is quiet and at peace."

**12** Then the angel of the LORD said, "LORD of armies, how long will you not show mercy to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah? You were angry with them for 70 years."

**13** The LORD answered the angel who spoke with me. The LORD spoke good words and words of comfort.

**14** Then the angel who spoke with me said to me, "Call out this message. 'The LORD of armies says this. I have a very strong love for Jerusalem and for Zion.

**15** I am very angry with the nations that feel safe. I was only a little angry with my people. But the nations made the punishment worse than I wanted.'

**16** Thus the LORD says this: 'I will come back to Jerusalem with mercy. The people will build my house in Jerusalem,' says the LORD of armies. 'A builder will put a line across Jerusalem to measure it.'

**17** Call out again: 'The LORD of armies says this: My cities will again have many good things. The LORD will again comfort Zion. He will again choose Jerusalem.'"

**18** Then I looked up and saw 4 horns.

**19** I said to the angel who spoke with me, "What are these horns?" He answered me, "These are the horns that sent Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem away into many countries."

**20** Then the LORD showed me 4 metal workers.

**21** I asked, "What will these men do?" He said, "These horns sent Judah away into many countries. Thus no person in Judah could lift up his head. But these workers came to make the horns afraid. They will throw down the horns of the nations. Those nations used their power against the land of Judah to send its people away."

## Chapter 2

**1** I looked up again and saw a man with a line in his hand. He used the line to measure things.

**2** I asked, "Where are you going?" He said to me, "I will measure Jerusalem. I will find its width and its length."

**3** Then the angel who spoke with me went out. Another angel came out to meet him.

**4** The second angel said to him, "Run and tell this young man: 'Jerusalem will be like towns with no walls. Jerusalem will have too many people and animals for walls.

**5** "I will be a wall of fire around Jerusalem," says the LORD. "I will be the glory in Jerusalem."'

**6** "Come! Run away from the land of the north," says the LORD. "I sent you away to all parts of the earth, as the 4 winds of the sky go out," says the LORD.

**7** "Come, Zion! Escape, you people who live in Babylon!"

**8** The LORD of armies says this: "After the glory, he sent me to the nations that took your possessions. A person who attacks you attacks the most valuable thing to the LORD.

**9** I will raise my hand against those nations. Their slaves will take their possessions. Then you will know that the LORD of armies sent me.

**10** Sing and be glad, people of Zion! I come, and I will live among you," says the LORD.

**11** "At that time, many nations will join the LORD. They will become my people. I will live among you. Then you will know that the LORD of armies sent me to you."

**12** The LORD will take Judah as his own part in the holy land. He will choose Jerusalem again.

**13** All people, be quiet in front of the LORD! He comes out of his holy home to act.

## Chapter 3

**1** Then the angel showed me Joshua the high priest. Joshua stood in front of the angel of the LORD. Satan stood at the right side of Joshua to accuse him.

**2** The LORD said to Satan, "The LORD tells you to stop, Satan! The LORD who chose Jerusalem tells you to stop! This man is like a stick that someone pulled out of the fire."

**3** Joshua wore very dirty clothes. He stood in front of the angel.

**4** The angel spoke to the others who stood in front of him. He said, "Take the dirty clothes off Joshua." Then he said to Joshua, "Look, I took your sin away from you. I will put fine clothes on you."

**5** Then I said, "Put a clean turban on his head." So they put a clean turban on his head and put clothes on him. The angel of the LORD stood near.

**6** Then the angel of the LORD spoke strongly to Joshua. He said:

**7** "The LORD of armies says this: 'Live as I tell you, and do the work that I give you. Then you will rule my house and keep my courtyards. I will let you go among these angels who stand here.

**8** Listen, Joshua the high priest! Listen, you and your friends who sit in front of you. These men are a sign of things that will come. I will bring my servant, the Branch.

**9** Look at the stone that I put in front of Joshua. The stone has 7 eyes. I will cut words into the stone,' says the LORD of armies. 'I will take away the sin of this land in one day.

**10** At that time,' says the LORD of armies, 'each one of you will invite his neighbor. You will sit together under your vine and under your fig tree.'"

## Chapter 4

**1** The angel who spoke with me came back. He woke me as a person wakes a man from sleep.

**2** He asked me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a lampstand of gold. A bowl is on the top of the lampstand. The lampstand has 7 lamps on it. Each lamp has pipes that connect to it.

**3** Two olive trees are near the lampstand. One tree is on the right side of the bowl, and one tree is on the left side."

**4** I asked the angel who spoke with me, "My lord, what are these things?"

**5** The angel who spoke with me answered, "Do you not know what these things are?" I said, "No, my lord."

**6** Then he said to me, "This is the message of the LORD to Zerubbabel: 'You will not succeed by strength or by power. You will succeed by my Spirit,' says the LORD of armies.

**7** 'Large problems are like a large mountain in front of Zerubbabel. But the mountain will become flat ground. Zerubbabel will put the last stone on the temple. The people will shout, "God is kind to it! God is kind to it!"'"

**8** Then the LORD gave me another message. He said:

**9** "The hands of Zerubbabel put down the base of this temple. His hands will also complete the temple. Then you will know that the LORD of armies sent me to you.

**10** Some people thought that this small start was not important. But they will be glad when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. The 7 lamps are the eyes of the LORD. They look at all the earth."

**11** Then I asked the angel, "What are these 2 olive trees on the right side and the left side of the lampstand?"

**12** I asked him again, "What are these 2 olive branches? They pour golden oil through the 2 gold pipes."

**13** He said to me, "Do you not know what these things are?" I said, "No, my lord."

**14** He said, "These are the 2 men whom God chose and put oil on. They stand near the Lord of all the earth."

## Chapter 5

**1** Then I looked up again. I saw a scroll that flew in the air.

**2** The angel asked me, "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a scroll that flies. It is 20 cubits long and 10 cubits wide."

**3** Then he said to me, "This scroll is the curse that goes out over all the land. One side of the scroll says that every thief will go away from the land. The other side says that every person who makes false promises will go away.

**4** The LORD of armies says, 'I will send the curse out. It will go into the house of the thief. It will go into the house of the person who makes a false promise with my name. The curse will stay in his house. It will destroy the house, its wood, and its stones.'"

**5** Then the angel who spoke with me came forward. He said to me, "Look up and see this thing that comes out."

**6** I asked, "What is it?" He said, "It is a basket that people use to measure grain (an ephah). It shows the sin of the people in all the land."

**7** Then someone lifted a lead cover off the basket. A woman sat in the basket.

**8** The angel said, "This woman is evil." He pushed her back into the basket. He put the heavy lead cover on the top of the basket.

**9** Then I looked up and saw 2 women come out. They had wings like the wings of a stork. The wind was in their wings. They lifted the basket up between the earth and the sky.

**10** I asked the angel who spoke with me, "Where do these women take the basket?"

**11** He said to me, "They will build a house for the basket in the land of Shinar. When the house is ready, they will put the basket there on its base."

## Chapter 6

**1** Then I looked up again. I saw 4 chariots come out from between 2 mountains. The mountains were bronze.

**2** Red horses pulled the first chariot. Black horses pulled the second chariot.

**3** White horses pulled the third chariot. Strong horses with spots pulled the fourth chariot.

**4** I asked the angel who spoke with me, "My lord, what are these chariots?"

**5** The angel answered me, "These are the 4 spirits of heaven. They stood in front of the Lord of all the earth. Now they go out.

**6** The chariot with the black horses goes to the land of the north. The white horses go after them. The horses with spots go to the land of the south."

**7** The strong horses went out. They wanted to go across all the earth. The angel said, "Go across the earth!" So they went across all the earth.

**8** Then the angel called to me. He said, "Look, the horses that go to the land of the north made my Spirit calm there."

**9** Then the LORD gave me a message. He said:

**10** "Take gifts from the people who came back from Babylon. Take gifts from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah. Go on that same day to the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah.

**11** Take the silver and gold and make a crown. Put the crown on the head of Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest.

**12** Tell him, 'The LORD of armies says this: Look, here is the man whose name is the Branch. He will grow up from his place. He will build the temple of the LORD.

**13** He will build the temple of the LORD. He will receive royal honor. He will sit on his throne and rule. He will also be a priest on his throne. The king and the priest will agree and work together in peace.'

**14** The crown will stay in the temple of the LORD. It will help the people remember Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen the son of Zephaniah.

**15** People from far away will come and help to build the temple of the LORD. Then you will know that the LORD of armies sent me to you. This will occur if you carefully obey the voice of the LORD your God."

## Chapter 7

**1** In the fourth year of King Darius, the LORD gave a message to Zechariah. This occurred on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month Kislev.

**2** At that time, the people of Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech and their men. These men went to ask the LORD for his favor.

**3** They asked the priests of the house of the LORD of armies and the prophets a question. They said, "For many years we cried and did not eat in the fifth month. Must we continue to do this?"

**4** Then the LORD of armies gave me a message. He said:

**5** "Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests. Tell them, 'For 70 years you did not eat and you were sad in the fifth and seventh months. But did you really do this for me?

**6** When you ate and drank, you did it only for yourselves.

**7** The LORD spoke these words through the prophets before you. At that time Jerusalem and the cities around it had many people and many good things. People lived in the south and in the low hills. You must listen to those words.'"

**8** The LORD gave this message to Zechariah:

**9** "The LORD of armies says this: 'Judge honestly. Show kindness and mercy to each other.

**10** Do not be cruel to widows, to children with no father, to foreigners, or to poor people. Do not make evil plans against each other.'

**11** But the people did not listen. They turned their backs. They closed their ears so that they could not hear.

**12** They made their hearts as hard as stone. They did not listen to the law. They did not listen to the words that the LORD of armies sent by his Spirit through the prophets before them. Thus the LORD of armies became very angry.

**13** "I called to them, but they did not listen. Thus when they called to me, I did not listen," says the LORD of armies.

**14** "I sent them away to all the nations that they did not know. I scattered them as a storm wind scatters dust. Then the land became empty. No person went through it or came back. Thus the people made the good land empty."

## Chapter 8

**1** The LORD of armies gave me another message. He said:

**2** "The LORD of armies says this: 'I have a very strong love for Zion. I am very angry with her enemies because of this love.'

**3** The LORD says this: 'I will come back to Zion. I will live in Jerusalem. People will call Jerusalem the City of Truth. They will call the mountain of the LORD of armies the Holy Mountain.'

**4** The LORD of armies says this: 'Old men and old women will again sit in the streets of Jerusalem. Each one will hold a stick in his hand because of his old age.

**5** The streets of the city will be full of boys and girls who play there.'

**6** The LORD of armies says this: 'This will seem too wonderful to the people who remain at this time. But it is not too wonderful for me,' says the LORD of armies.

**7** The LORD of armies says this: 'I will save my people from the lands of the east and the lands of the west.

**8** I will bring them back. They will live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God. I will be faithful and good to them.'

**9** The LORD of armies says this: 'Be strong! At this time you hear the words of the prophets. The prophets spoke on the day when the people put down the base of the house of the LORD of armies. They spoke so that you will build the temple.

**10** Before that time, no person got pay for his work or for the work of his animals. Enemies caused trouble, and thus no person could travel safely. I made each man fight against his neighbor.

**11** But now I will not treat the people who remain as I did before,' says the LORD of armies.

**12** 'The seeds will grow well. The vine will give its fruit. The ground will give its crops. The sky will give its dew. I will give all these things to the people who remain.

**13** People of Judah and people of Israel, the nations used your name as a curse. But I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid. Be strong.'

**14** The LORD of armies says this: 'Your ancestors made me angry. Thus I decided to punish you, and I did not change my decision,' says the LORD of armies.

**15** 'Now I decided to do good to Jerusalem and to the people of Judah again. Do not be afraid.

**16** These are the things that you must do. Tell the truth to each other. In your courts, judge honestly and make decisions that bring peace.

**17** Do not make evil plans against your neighbor. Do not make false promises. I hate all these things,' says the LORD."

**18** The LORD of armies gave me another message. He said:

**19** "The LORD of armies says this: 'The people of Judah do not eat on special days in the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months. These days will become times of joy and happy festivals. Thus love truth and peace.'

**20** The LORD of armies says this: 'People will come again from many cities.

**21** The people of one city will go to another city. They will say, "Come, we must go quickly to ask the LORD for his favor. We will look for the LORD of armies. I will go too."

**22** Many people and strong nations will come to Jerusalem. They will come to look for the LORD of armies and to ask for his favor.'

**23** The LORD of armies says this: 'At that time, 10 men from all the nations and languages will hold the clothes of one Jew. They will say, "We will go with you, because we heard that God is with you."'"

## Chapter 9

**1** This is a message from the LORD. The message is against the land of Hadrach and the city of Damascus. The eyes of all people and of all the tribes of Israel look to the LORD.

**2** The message is also against Hamath, which is near Damascus. It is against Tyre and Sidon, though their people think that they are very wise.

**3** Tyre built a strong wall around itself. The people of Tyre put together silver as common as dust. They put together gold as common as mud in the streets.

**4** But the Lord will take away the possessions of Tyre. He will destroy the power of Tyre on the sea. Fire will burn up the city.

**5** The city of Ashkelon will see this and be afraid. The city of Gaza will see this and feel very much pain. The city of Ekron will also feel pain, because its hope will fail. The king of Gaza will die. No people will live in Ashkelon.

**6** Foreigners will live in Ashdod. I will destroy the pride of the Philistines.

**7** I will take the blood out of their mouths. I will take the unclean food from between their teeth. The people who remain will belong to our God. They will become like a family group in Judah. The people of Ekron will become like the Jebusites.

**8** I will put my army around my house to protect it from enemy armies. No cruel ruler will attack my people again, because now I watch over them.

**9** Be very glad, people of Zion! Shout, people of Jerusalem! Look, your king comes to you. He is good and he brings victory. He is humble. He sits on a donkey, on a young male donkey.

**10** I will take the chariots away from Ephraim. I will take the war horses away from Jerusalem. I will break the bows of war. Your king will tell the nations about peace. He will rule from sea to sea. He will rule from the Euphrates River to the ends of the earth.

**11** Because of the blood of my agreement (covenant) with you, I will free your prisoners. I will take them out of the pit with no water.

**12** Prisoners who have hope, come back to your safe place. Today I tell you that I will give you 2 times more good things than you lost.

**13** I will use Judah as my bow. I will use Ephraim as my arrow. Zion, I will send your sons against the sons of Greece. I will make you like the sword of a strong soldier.

**14** The LORD will appear above his people. His arrow will go out as fast as lightning. The Lord GOD will blow the trumpet. He will go out in storms from the south.

**15** The LORD of armies will protect his people. They will destroy their enemies. They will throw down their enemies with stones from slings. They will drink and shout like men who drink wine. They will be full like the bowls that the priests use at the corners of the altar.

**16** At that time, the LORD their God will save his people as a shepherd saves his sheep. They will shine on his land like the jewels in a crown.

**17** They will be very good and very beautiful. Grain will make the young men strong. New wine will make the young women strong.

## Chapter 10

**1** Ask the LORD for rain in the spring. The LORD makes the storm clouds. He gives rain to all people. He makes the plants grow in the field for each person.

**2** The idols give false messages. The people who tell the future see false visions. They tell false dreams. Their comfort has no value. Thus the people go away like sheep. They have trouble, because they have no shepherd.

**3** "I am very angry with the shepherds. I will punish the leaders. The LORD of armies takes care of his flock, the people of Judah. He will make them like a proud horse in a battle.

**4** From Judah will come the cornerstone. From Judah will come the tent peg. From Judah will come the bow of war. From Judah will come every ruler.

**5** The people of Judah will be like strong soldiers in a battle. They will push their enemies down into the mud of the streets. They will fight, because the LORD is with them. They will put the enemy riders on horses to shame.

**6** I will make the people of Judah strong. I will save the people of Joseph. I will bring them back, because I have mercy on them. They will be as if I did not send them away. I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.

**7** The people of Ephraim will be like strong soldiers. They will be glad like men who drink wine. Their children will see it and be glad. They will be happy because of the LORD.

**8** I will whistle to call them, and I will bring them together. I will free them. They will become many people again, as they were before.

**9** I sent them away among the nations. But in far countries they will remember me. They and their children will live, and they will come back.

**10** I will bring them back from the land of Egypt. I will bring them together from Assyria. I will bring them to the land of Gilead and to Lebanon. There will not be sufficient space for them all.

**11** They will go through the sea of trouble. The LORD will hit the waves of the sea. All the deep water of the Nile River will become dry. The LORD will throw down the pride of Assyria. He will take away the power of Egypt.

**12** I will make my people strong in the LORD. They will live as he tells them," says the LORD.

## Chapter 11

**1** Open your gates, Lebanon, so that fire can burn your cedar trees.

**2** Cry aloud, you cypress trees, because the cedar tree fell. Enemies destroyed the strong trees. Cry aloud, you oak trees of Bashan, because the thick forest fell.

**3** Listen to the shepherds who cry aloud. Their good fields are ruins. Listen to the young lions that roar. The thick plants near the Jordan River are ruins.

**4** The LORD my God says this: "Be the shepherd of the flock that the owners will kill.

**5** The people who buy the sheep kill them, and nobody punishes those people. The people who sell the sheep say, 'Praise the LORD, I am rich!' Their own shepherds do not feel sorry for them.

**6** I will not feel sorry for the people of the land again," says the LORD. "I will put each person into the power of his neighbor and of his king. They will destroy the land. I will not save the people from their power."

**7** So I became the shepherd of the flock that the owners will kill. I took care of the weakest sheep in the flock. I took 2 sticks. I called one stick Favor and the other stick Union. Then I took care of the flock.

**8** In one month I removed 3 shepherds. I became tired of the sheep, and the sheep hated me.

**9** Then I said, "I will not be your shepherd. Let the sheep that die, die. Let the enemy destroy the sheep that he wants to destroy. Let the sheep that remain eat each other."

**10** I took my stick named Favor and broke it. Thus I broke the agreement that I made with all the nations.

**11** I broke the agreement on that day. The weakest sheep watched me, and they knew that this was the message of the LORD.

**12** I said to them, "If you think that it is good, pay me. If not, do not pay me." So they paid me 30 pieces of silver.

**13** The LORD said to me, "Throw the silver to the potter. That is the fine price that they put on me!" So I took the 30 pieces of silver. I threw them to the potter in the house of the LORD.

**14** Then I broke my second stick, named Union. Thus I broke the family connection between Judah and Israel.

**15** Then the LORD said to me, "Again take the equipment of a foolish shepherd.

**16** I will put a new shepherd over the land. He will not take care of the sheep that go away. He will not look for the young sheep. He will not heal the hurt sheep. He will not feed the healthy sheep. But he will eat the meat of the fat sheep and tear off their feet.

**17** Terrible things will occur to the bad shepherd who leaves the flock! A sword will cut his arm and his right eye. His arm will become fully weak. His right eye will become fully blind."

## Chapter 12

**1** This is a message from the LORD about Israel. The LORD spread out the heavens. He made the base of the earth. He made the spirit in each person. The LORD says:

**2** "I will make Jerusalem like a cup of strong wine. All the nations around her will drink it and fall. They will attack Jerusalem and Judah.

**3** At that time, I will make Jerusalem like a very heavy stone for all the nations. All the nations of the earth will come together against Jerusalem. But all who try to lift her will hurt themselves badly.

**4** At that time," says the LORD, "I will make every horse afraid. I will make every rider crazy. I will watch over the people of Judah. But I will make the horses of the nations blind.

**5** Then the leaders of Judah will say to themselves, 'The people of Jerusalem are strong, because the LORD of armies is their God.'

**6** At that time, I will make the leaders of Judah like a fire in a pile of wood. They will be like a torch of fire among dry grain. They will destroy all the nations around them, on the right side and on the left side. But the people of Jerusalem will stay safe in their city.

**7** The LORD will save the homes of Judah first. Thus the family of David and the people of Jerusalem will not have more honor than the rest of Judah.

**8** At that time, the LORD will protect the people of Jerusalem. The weakest person among them will be strong like David. The family of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD who goes in front of them.

**9** At that time, I will destroy all the nations that attack Jerusalem.

**10** I will give a spirit of kindness and prayer to the family of David and to the people of Jerusalem. They will look at me, the one whom they stabbed. They will cry for him, as a person cries for an only son. They will feel very sad for him, as a person feels sad for a first son who died.

**11** At that time, the people of Jerusalem will cry very much. It will be like the sorrow for Hadad Rimmon in the valley of Megiddo.

**12** All the land will cry, each family alone. The family of David will cry alone, and their wives will cry alone. The family of Nathan will cry alone, and their wives will cry alone.

**13** The family of Levi will cry alone, and their wives will cry alone. The family of Shimei will cry alone, and their wives will cry alone.

**14** All the other families will cry, each family alone, and their wives will cry alone."

## Chapter 13

**1** "At that time, a spring of water will open for the family of David and for the people of Jerusalem. The water will wash away their sin and their uncleanness.

**2** At that time," says the LORD of armies, "I will remove the names of the idols from the land. People will not remember the idols again. I will also remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.

**3** If a person continues to speak as a prophet, his own father and mother will speak to him. They will say, 'You must die, because you tell lies in the name of the LORD.' Then his own father and mother will stab him when he speaks as a prophet.

**4** At that time, each prophet will feel shame about his vision when he speaks. He will not wear a rough coat of hair to trick people.

**5** Each one will say, 'I am not a prophet. I am a farmer. I worked on a farm since I was young.'

**6** Then someone will ask him, 'What are these wounds on your body?' He will answer, 'My friends gave me these wounds in their house.'

**7** Sword, wake up and attack my shepherd! Attack the man who is near to me," says the LORD of armies. "Kill the shepherd, and the sheep will run away in all directions. I will turn my hand against the small sheep.

**8** In all the land," says the LORD, "2 of 3 parts of the people will die. But 1 part will remain in the land.

**9** I will put that third part through the fire. I will make them clean as a worker makes silver clean. I will test them as a worker tests gold. They will call to me, and I will answer them. I will say, 'They are my people.' They will say, 'The LORD is our God.'"

## Chapter 14

**1** A day of the LORD will come. On that day, your enemies will take your possessions and divide them in your city.

**2** I will bring all the nations together to fight against Jerusalem. They will capture the city. They will take the possessions from the houses. They will attack the women. Half of the people of the city will go away as prisoners. But the rest of the people will stay in the city.

**3** Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations. He will fight as he fought in battles before.

**4** On that day, he will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The Mount of Olives will break into 2 parts, from east to west. A very large valley will form. Half of the mountain will move to the north, and half will move to the south.

**5** You will run away through this valley between the mountains, because it will go as far as Azel. You will run away as your ancestors ran from the earthquake in the time of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all his holy ones will come with him.

**6** On that day there will be no light, no cold, and no frost.

**7** It will be one special day that only the LORD knows. There will be no difference between day and night. When evening comes, there will still be light.

**8** On that day, fresh water will flow out from Jerusalem. Half of the water will flow east to the Dead Sea. Half will flow west to the Mediterranean Sea. The water will flow in summer and in winter.

**9** The LORD will be king over all the earth. On that day, the LORD will be the only LORD. His name will be the only name.

**10** All the land from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem, will become flat. But Jerusalem will stay high in its place. People will live in Jerusalem from the Benjamin Gate to the place of the First Gate and the Corner Gate. They will live there from the Tower of Hananel to the winepresses of the king.

**11** People will live in Jerusalem. God will not destroy the city again. Jerusalem will be safe.

**12** The LORD will send a terrible disease on all the nations that fought against Jerusalem. Their bodies will rot while they stand on their feet. Their eyes will rot in their heads. Their tongues will rot in their mouths.
