**15** One of the men at the table heard these things. He said to Jesus, "Blessed is the person who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God."

**16** Jesus said to him, "A man prepared a large supper, and he invited many people.

**17** At the time of the supper, he sent his servant to the guests. The servant said, 'Come, because everything is ready now.'

**18** But all the guests started to give excuses. The first guest said, 'I bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please accept my excuse.'

**19** Another guest said, 'I bought 5 pairs of oxen, and I will go and test them. Please accept my excuse.'

**20** Another guest said, 'I married a wife, and thus I cannot come.'

**21** The servant came back and told his master these things. The master of the house became angry. He said to his servant, 'Go out quickly into the streets and roads of the city. Bring in the poor people, the crippled people, the blind people, and the lame people.'

**22** The servant said, 'Master, I did what you told me. But there is still space.'

**23** The master said to the servant, 'Go out to the roads and the country paths. Tell the people to come in. I want my house to be full.

**24** I tell you, none of the men whom I invited will eat my supper.'"

**25** Large crowds went with Jesus. He turned and said to them,

**26** "If a person comes to me, he must love me more than his father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters. He must love me more than his own life. If not, he cannot be my disciple.

**27** If a person does not carry his cross and follow me, he cannot be my disciple.

**28** Think about a man who wants to build a tower. First he will sit down and calculate the cost. He must know if he has sufficient money to complete the tower.

**29** If he puts down the base and cannot complete the tower, all the people who see it will laugh at him.

**30** They will say, 'This man started to build, but he could not complete the work.'

**31** Or think about a king who goes to war against another king. First he will sit down and think. He has 10,000 soldiers. He must know if he can fight against the other king who comes with 20,000 soldiers.

**32** If he cannot, he will send messengers to the other king while that king is still far away. The messengers will ask for peace.

**33** In the same way, each of you must give up all that you have. If not, you cannot be my disciple.

**34** Salt is good. But if salt loses its taste, you cannot make it salty again.

**35** It is not good for the soil or for the manure pile. People throw it out. If you have ears, listen!"

## Chapter 15

**1** All the tax collectors and sinners came near to Jesus to hear him.

**2** The Pharisees and the teachers of the law complained. They said, "This man accepts sinners and eats with them."

**3** Then Jesus told them this parable:

**4** "Think about a man who has 100 sheep and loses 1 of them. He will leave the 99 sheep in the wilderness. He will go and look for the lost sheep until he finds it.

**5** When he finds the sheep, he will put it on his shoulders with joy.

**6** He will go home and call his friends and neighbors together. He will say to them, 'Be happy with me, because I found my lost sheep.'

**7** I tell you, in the same way there will be joy in heaven over 1 sinner who repents. That joy will be more than the joy over 99 good people who do not need to repent.

**8** Or think about a woman who has 10 silver coins and loses 1 coin. She will light a lamp and clean the house. She will look carefully until she finds the coin.

**9** When she finds the coin, she will call her friends and neighbors together. She will say, 'Be happy with me, because I found the coin that I lost.'

**10** In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in front of the angels of God over 1 sinner who repents."

**11** Jesus said, "A man had 2 sons.

**12** The younger son said to his father, 'Father, give me my part of your property.' So the father divided his property between the 2 sons.

**13** After a few days, the younger son collected all his things. He went on a journey to a country far away. There he lived a wild life and wasted all his money.

**14** After he spent all his money, there was a very bad famine in that country. The son did not have the things that he needed.

**15** So he went to work for a man of that country. The man sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

**16** The son was so hungry that he wanted to eat the pods that the pigs ate. But no person gave him food.

**17** Then he started to think clearly. He said, 'All the workers of my father have more than sufficient food. But I die of hunger here!

**18** I will get up and go to my father. I will say to him, "Father, I sinned against heaven and against you.

**19** I am not good enough to be your son. Make me one of your workers."'

**20** So he got up and went to his father. While the son was still far away, his father saw him and felt pity for him. The father ran to his son. He put his arms around his son and kissed him.

**21** The son said to him, 'Father, I sinned against heaven and against you. I am not good enough to be your son.'

**22** But the father said to his servants, 'Quickly bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.

**23** Bring the fat calf and kill it. We will eat and celebrate.

**24** This son of mine was dead, and now he is alive again. He went away from us, and now he came back.' And they started to celebrate.

**25** The older son was in the field. When he came near the house, he heard music and people who danced.

**26** He called one of the servants. He asked the servant what these things meant.

**27** The servant said to him, 'Your brother came home. Your father killed the fat calf because your brother is safe and well.'

**28** The older son became angry and did not want to go in. So his father came out and asked him to come in.

**29** But the son said to his father, 'Look, for many years I worked for you like a slave. I always obeyed your commands. But you never gave me even a young goat to celebrate with my friends.

**30** But this son of yours wasted your money on prostitutes. When he came home, you killed the fat calf for him.'

**31** The father said to him, 'Son, you are always with me. All that I have is yours.

**32** But it was correct for us to celebrate and be happy. Your brother was dead, and now he is alive again. He went away from us, and now he came back.'"

## Chapter 16

**1** Jesus also said to his disciples, "There was a rich man who had a manager. People told the rich man that the manager wasted his property.

**2** So the rich man called the manager and said to him, 'What is this that I hear about you? Give me a report of your work. You cannot be my manager anymore.'

**3** The manager thought, 'What will I do? My master will take my job from me. I am not strong enough to dig. I have too much shame to beg.

**4** I know what I will do. Then, when I lose my job, people will accept me into their houses.'

**5** So the manager called each person who owed money to his master. He said to the first person, 'How much do you owe my master?'

**6** The man said, '100 measures of olive oil.' The manager said to him, 'Take your bill. Sit down quickly and write 50.'

**7** Then the manager said to another person, 'How much do you owe?' The man said, '100 measures of wheat.' The manager said to him, 'Take your bill and write 80.'

**8** The master praised the dishonest manager because the manager acted wisely. The people of this world are wiser with other people of their kind than the people of the light are.

**9** I tell you, use the money of this world to make friends for yourselves. Then, when the money is gone, they will accept you into the homes that last for all time.

**10** A person whom you can trust with a small thing, you can also trust with a large thing. A person who is dishonest with a small thing is also dishonest with a large thing.

**11** If you are not honest with the money of this world, then no person will trust you with the true riches.

**12** If you are not honest with the property of another person, then no person will give you property of your own.

**13** No servant can serve 2 masters. He will hate one and love the other. Or he will be loyal to one and not respect the other. You cannot serve God and money."

**14** The Pharisees loved money. They heard all these things, and they laughed at Jesus.

**15** Jesus said to them, "You try to make yourselves look good to people. But God knows your hearts. The things that people think are important are very bad to God.

**16** The law and the prophets were the message until John came. Since that time, people tell the good news of the kingdom of God. And all people try hard to go into it.

**17** It is easier for heaven and earth to disappear than for the smallest mark of the law to fail.

**18** A man who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery. And a man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

**19** There was a rich man who wore purple clothes and fine linen. Every day he ate very expensive food.

**20** A poor man with the name Lazarus lay at the gate of the rich man. Lazarus had sores on all of his body.

**21** Lazarus wanted to eat the small pieces of food that fell from the table of the rich man. Also, the dogs came and licked his sores.

**22** Then the poor man died. The angels carried him to the side of Abraham. The rich man also died, and people buried him.

**23** The rich man was in hell and he felt much pain. He looked up and saw Abraham far away. He saw Lazarus at the side of Abraham.

**24** The rich man shouted, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me! Send Lazarus to put the end of his finger in water and cool my tongue. I feel very much pain in this fire.'

**25** But Abraham said, 'Son, remember this. In your life you got good things, and Lazarus got bad things. Now Lazarus gets comfort here, and you feel pain.

**26** Also, there is a large deep space between us and you. People who want to go from here to you cannot go. And no person can come from there to us.'

**27** The rich man said, 'Then, father, please send Lazarus to the house of my father.

**28** I have 5 brothers. Lazarus must warn them. Then they will not also come to this place of pain.'

**29** But Abraham said, 'They have the writings of Moses and the prophets. Your brothers must listen to them.'

**30** The rich man said, 'No, father Abraham! But if a person from the dead goes to them, they will repent.'

**31** Abraham said to him, 'They do not listen to Moses and the prophets. Thus they will not believe a person who comes back from the dead.'"

## Chapter 17

**1** Jesus said to his disciples, "Things that cause people to sin will certainly come. But how terrible it will be for the person who causes these things!

**2** It is better for that person to go into the sea with a heavy millstone around his neck. That is better than to cause 1 of these little ones to sin.

**3** Be careful! If your brother sins against you, tell him that he is wrong. If he repents, forgive him.

**4** He can sin against you 7 times in a day. And he can come back to you 7 times and say, 'I repent.' You must forgive him each time."

**5** The apostles said to the Lord, "Make our faith larger."

**6** The Lord said, "Your faith can be as small as a mustard seed. Then you can say to this mulberry tree, 'Pull yourself out of the ground and go into the sea.' And the tree will obey you.

**7** Think about a servant of yours who plows a field or keeps the sheep. When he comes in from the field, you will not say to him, 'Come now and sit down to eat.'

**8** No, you will say to him, 'Prepare my supper. Put on your work clothes and serve me while I eat and drink. After that, you can eat and drink.'

**9** You do not thank the servant because he did what you told him.

**10** You must do the same. When you do all the things that God tells you, say, 'We are servants who have no special value. We only did our work.'"

**11** Jesus went on his journey to Jerusalem. He went along the border between Samaria and Galilee.

**12** He went into a village. There 10 men who had leprosy came to meet him. They stood far away.

**13** They shouted, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"

**14** Jesus saw them and said to them, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." While the men went, their leprosy went away.

**15** One of the men saw that he became well. He came back and praised God with a loud voice.

**16** He fell down on his face at the feet of Jesus and thanked him. This man was a Samaritan.

**17** Jesus said, "I healed 10 men. Where are the other 9?

**18** Only this foreigner came back to praise God."

**19** Then Jesus said to the man, "Get up and go. Your faith healed you."

**20** The Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God will come. Jesus answered, "The kingdom of God does not come with signs that you can watch for.

**21** People will not say, 'Look, the kingdom is here!' or 'The kingdom is there!' The kingdom of God is among you."

**22** Then Jesus said to the disciples, "A time will come when you will want to see 1 of the days of the Son of Man. But you will not see it.

**23** People will say to you, 'Look, he is there!' or 'Look, he is here!' Do not go out and follow them.

**24** Lightning flashes and lights the sky from one side to the other. The Son of Man will be like that on his day.

**25** But first he must suffer many things. The people of this time will refuse him.

**26** The days of the Son of Man will be like the days of Noah.

**27** In the days of Noah, the people ate and drank, and they married. They did these things until the day when Noah went into the ark. Then the flood came and killed all of them.

**28** It will also be like the days of Lot. The people ate and drank. They bought and sold. They planted and built.

**29** But on the day when Lot went out of Sodom, fire and sulfur fell from the sky. The fire and sulfur killed all of the people.

**30** It will be the same on the day when the Son of Man shows himself.

**31** On that day, a person can possibly be on the roof of his house, and his things can be in the house. He must not go down to get them. Also, a person in the field must not go back.

**32** Remember the wife of Lot!

**33** If a person tries to save his life, he will lose it. If a person loses his life, he will keep it.

**34** I tell you, on that night 2 people will be in 1 bed. God will take one and leave the other.

**35** 2 women will grind grain together. God will take one and leave the other.

**36** 2 men will be in the field. God will take one and leave the other."

**37** The disciples asked him, "Where, Lord?" Jesus said to them, "Where there is a dead body, the vultures will gather."

## Chapter 18

**1** Jesus told his disciples a parable. He wanted to teach them that they must always pray and not stop.

**2** He said, "In a city there was a judge. He did not fear God, and he did not respect people.

**3** In that city there was a widow. She came to the judge many times. She said, 'Give me justice against my enemy.'

**4** For some time the judge refused. But then he thought, 'I do not fear God, and I do not respect people.

**5** But this widow continues to give me trouble. So I will give her justice. If not, she will make me tired with her visits.'"

**6** The Lord said, "Listen to what the unjust judge said.

**7** God will certainly give justice to his chosen people who call to him day and night. He will not wait a long time to help them.

**8** I tell you, he will give them justice quickly. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?"

**9** Some people were sure that they were good, and they thought that other people had no value. Jesus told them this parable:

**10** "2 men went up to the temple to pray. One man was a Pharisee, and the other man was a tax collector.

**11** The Pharisee stood and prayed about himself. He said, 'God, I thank you that I am not like other people. I do not steal. I am not dishonest. I do not commit adultery. I am not like this tax collector.

**12** I fast 2 times each week. I give one tenth of all that I get.'

**13** But the tax collector stood far away. He did not even look up to heaven. He hit his chest and said, 'God, have mercy on me, because I am a sinner.'

**14** I tell you, the tax collector went home and God accepted him as righteous. God did not accept the Pharisee. All people who make themselves important will become low. And all people who make themselves low will become important."

**15** People also brought babies to Jesus. They wanted him to touch the babies. When the disciples saw this, they told the people to stop.

**16** But Jesus called the children to him. He said, "Let the little children come to me. Do not stop them. The kingdom of God belongs to people like these children.

**17** I tell you the truth: If a person does not accept the kingdom of God like a little child, he will never go into it."

**18** A leader asked Jesus, "Good Teacher, what must I do to get eternal life?"

**19** Jesus said to him, "Why do you call me good? Only God is good.

**20** You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about other people. Respect your father and your mother.'"

**21** The man said, "I obeyed all these commandments since I was young."

**22** When Jesus heard this, he said to the man, "You must still do 1 thing. Sell all that you have and give the money to the poor people. Then you will have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow me."

**23** When the man heard this, he became very sad, because he was very rich.

**24** Jesus saw that the man was very sad. Jesus said, "It is very difficult for rich people to go into the kingdom of God!

**25** It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle. It is more difficult for a rich man to go into the kingdom of God."

**26** The people who heard this said, "Then who can God save?"

**27** Jesus said, "Things that are not possible for people are possible for God."

**28** Peter said, "Look, we left all that we had, and we followed you."

**29** Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth: Some people left their house, parents, brothers, wife, or children for the kingdom of God.

**30** These people will get much more in this life. And in the future world they will get eternal life."

**31** Jesus took the 12 disciples to one side. He said to them, "Look, we go up to Jerusalem. There all the things that the prophets wrote about the Son of Man will occur.

**32** People will give him to the Gentiles. The Gentiles will laugh at him, insult him, and spit on him.

**33** They will hit him with whips and kill him. On the third day he will come back to life."

**34** But the disciples did not understand any of these things. God hid the meaning of the words from them. They did not know what Jesus talked about.

**35** Jesus came near to Jericho. A blind man sat at the side of the road and begged.

**36** The blind man heard the crowd go past. He asked what this was.

**37** The people told him, "Jesus of Nazareth goes past."

**38** The blind man shouted, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"

**39** The people at the front of the crowd told him to be quiet. But he shouted more loudly, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"

**40** Jesus stopped. He told the people to bring the man to him. When the man came near, Jesus asked him,

**41** "What do you want me to do for you?" The man said, "Lord, I want to see again."

**42** Jesus said to him, "See again. Your faith healed you."

**43** Immediately the man could see. He followed Jesus and praised God. All the people saw this, and they also praised God.

## Chapter 19

**1** Jesus went into Jericho and went through the city.

**2** There was a man with the name Zacchaeus. He was the chief tax collector, and he was rich.

**3** Zacchaeus wanted to see who Jesus was. But he was a short man, and he could not see over the crowd.

**4** So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus. Jesus was about to go along that road.

**5** When Jesus came to the place, he looked up. He said to him, "Zacchaeus, come down quickly. Today I must stay at your house."

**6** Zacchaeus came down quickly. He was very happy to receive Jesus.

**7** All the people saw this, and they complained. They said, "Jesus went to be the guest of a sinner."

**8** Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord, I will give half of my property to the poor people. If I took money from a person dishonestly, I will pay him back 4 times as much."

**9** Jesus said to him, "Today salvation came to this house, because this man is also a son of Abraham.

**10** The Son of Man came to look for and save the people who went away from God."

**11** The people listened to these things. Jesus was near Jerusalem, and the people thought that the kingdom of God will come immediately. So Jesus told them a parable.

**12** He said, "A nobleman went to a country far away. He went there to become king. Then he wanted to come back.

**13** Before he went, he called 10 of his servants. He gave each servant 1 coin of high value. He said to them, 'Use this money to do business until I come back.'

**14** But the people of his country hated him. They sent messengers after him. The messengers said, 'We do not want this man to be our king.'

**15** But the nobleman became king and came back home. Then he told the servants to come to him. He wanted to know how much money each servant made with the coin.

**16** The first servant came and said, 'Master, your 1 coin made 10 more coins.'

**17** The king said to him, 'Good work! You are a good servant. You were faithful with a very small thing. So I give you authority over 10 cities.'

**18** The second servant came and said, 'Master, your 1 coin made 5 more coins.'

**19** The king said to him, 'I give you authority over 5 cities.'

**20** Another servant came and said, 'Master, here is your coin. I kept it in a cloth.

**21** I was afraid of you, because you are a hard man. You take what you did not put in. You harvest what you did not plant.'

**22** The king said to him, 'You are a bad servant! I will judge you with your own words. You knew that I am a hard man. You knew that I take what I did not put in, and harvest what I did not plant.

**23** Then why did you not put my money in the bank? Then, when I came back, I could get my money with interest.'

**24** The king said to the people who stood there, 'Take the coin from him. Give it to the servant who has 10 coins.'

**25** They said to him, 'Master, he already has 10 coins!'

**26** The king said, 'I tell you, people who have something will get more. But people who have nothing will lose even what they have.

**27** Now bring my enemies here. They did not want me to be their king. Kill them in front of me.'"

**28** After Jesus said these things, he went ahead of the people. He went up to Jerusalem.

**29** Jesus came near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the hill with the name the Mount of Olives. There he sent 2 of his disciples ahead.

**30** He said, "Go into the village in front of you. When you go in, you will find a young donkey tied there. No person ever sat on it. Untie the donkey and bring it here.

**31** If a person asks you, 'Why do you untie the donkey?' tell him, 'The Lord needs it.'"

**32** The 2 disciples went and found everything as Jesus told them.

**33** While they untied the young donkey, its owners said to them, "Why do you untie the donkey?"

**34** The disciples said, "The Lord needs it."

**35** They brought the donkey to Jesus. They put their coats on the donkey, and they put Jesus on it.

**36** While Jesus went along, people put their coats on the road in front of him.

**37** Jesus came near to the road that goes down the Mount of Olives. There all the crowd of disciples started to be happy. They praised God with loud voices for all the miracles that they saw.

**38** They said, "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory to God in the highest place!"

**39** Some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus, "Teacher, tell your disciples to stop."

**40** Jesus answered them, "I tell you, if these people stop, the stones will shout."

**41** Jesus came near to Jerusalem. He saw the city and cried for it.

**42** He said, "I wish that you knew today the things that will give you peace! But now you cannot see these things.

**43** A time will come when your enemies will build walls around you. They will surround you and attack you from all sides.

**44** They will destroy you and your children in you. They will not leave 1 stone on another stone. This will occur because you did not know the time when God came to you."

**45** Jesus went into the temple. He started to push out the people who sold things there.

**46** He said to them, "The scriptures say, 'My house will be a house of prayer.' But you made it a place where thieves hide."

**47** Every day Jesus taught in the temple. The chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the leaders of the people wanted to kill him.

**48** But they could not find a way to do it, because all the people listened carefully to him.

## Chapter 20

**1** One day Jesus taught the people in the temple and told them the good news. The chief priests and the teachers of the law came to him with the elders.

**2** They said to him, "Tell us, what authority do you have to do these things? Who gave you this authority?"

**3** Jesus answered them, "I will also ask you a question. Answer me.

**4** Did the baptism of John come from heaven or from people?"

**5** They talked about this among themselves. They said, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will say, 'Then why did you not believe John?'

**6** But if we say, 'From people,' all the people will kill us with stones. The people are sure that John was a prophet."

**7** So they answered, "We do not know where it came from."

**8** Jesus said to them, "Then I will not tell you what authority I have to do these things."

**9** Then Jesus told the people this parable: "A man planted a vineyard. He rented it to some farmers. Then he went to another country for a long time.

**10** At harvest time, he sent a servant to the farmers. The servant had to get some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers hit the servant and sent him away with nothing.

**11** The man sent another servant. The farmers also hit him and insulted him. They sent him away with nothing.

**12** The man sent a third servant. The farmers injured him and threw him out.

**13** Then the owner of the vineyard said, 'What will I do? I will send my son whom I love. Maybe they will respect him.'

**14** But when the farmers saw the son, they talked among themselves. They said, 'This is the son who will get the vineyard. Come, we will kill him. Then the vineyard will be ours.'

**15** So they threw the son out of the vineyard and killed him. What will the owner of the vineyard do to them?

**16** He will come and kill these farmers. He will give the vineyard to other people." When the people heard this, they said, "We hope that this never occurs!"

**17** Jesus looked at them and said, "Then what is the meaning of this scripture: 'The builders refused a stone. That stone became the most important stone of the building'?

**18** Each person who falls on that stone will break into pieces. And the stone will crush each person on whom it falls."

**19** The chief priests and the teachers of the law knew that Jesus told this parable against them. So they wanted to arrest him immediately. But they were afraid of the people.

**20** They watched Jesus carefully. They sent spies who acted as honest men. The spies wanted to catch Jesus in his words. Then they could give him to the power and authority of the governor.

**21** The spies asked him, "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach what is correct. You do not show favor to any person. You teach the way of God truly.

**22** Does our law let us pay taxes to Caesar, or not?"

**23** But Jesus knew their tricks. He said to them, "Why do you try to trap me?

**24** Show me a coin. Whose picture and name are on it?" They answered, "Caesar's."

**25** Jesus said to them, "Then give to Caesar the things that belong to Caesar. And give to God the things that belong to God."

**26** They could not catch Jesus in his words in front of the people. They felt wonder at his answer, and they did not speak.

**27** Some Sadducees came to Jesus. The Sadducees say that dead people do not come back to life. They asked him a question.

**28** They said, "Teacher, Moses wrote a law for us. If a man dies and has a wife but no children, his brother must marry the widow. Then they must have children for the dead brother.

**29** There were 7 brothers. The first brother married a wife and died with no children.

**30** The second brother married her, and he died with no children.

**31** The third brother married her. All 7 brothers did the same. They died and left no children.

**32** Then the woman also died.

**33** When the dead come back to life, whose wife will she be? All 7 brothers married her."

**34** Jesus said to them, "The people of this world marry.

**35** But some people are good enough to be in the future world, and to come back to life from the dead. Those people will not marry.

**36** They cannot die again, because they are like the angels. They are children of God, because God brought them back to life.

**37** Moses also showed that the dead come back to life. In the story of the bush that burned, Moses called the Lord 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'

**38** God is not the God of dead people. He is the God of people who live. All people are alive to God."

**39** Some of the teachers of the law answered, "Teacher, you spoke well."

**40** After that, no person was brave enough to ask him more questions.

**41** Then Jesus said to them, "Why do people say that the Christ is the son of David?

**42** David himself says in the book of Psalms, 'The LORD said to my Lord, "Sit at my right side

**43** until I put your enemies under your feet."'

**44** David calls him 'Lord.' Then how can the Christ be the son of David?"

**45** While all the people listened, Jesus said to his disciples,

**46** "Be careful of the teachers of the law. They like to walk around in long robes. They like people to greet them with respect in the markets. They want the most important seats in the synagogues and the best places at feasts.

**47** They take the houses of widows. They say long prayers so that people will see them. God will punish these men more severely."

## Chapter 21

**1** Jesus looked up. He saw rich people who put their gifts into the box for offerings in the temple.

**2** He also saw a poor widow who put in 2 very small copper coins.

**3** Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: This poor widow put in more than all the other people.

**4** All these people gave from the extra money that they have. But she is poor, and she gave all the money that she had for her life."

**5** Some people talked about the temple. They said that it had beautiful stones and gifts on it. Jesus said,

**6** "You see these things. But a time will come when people will destroy all of them. Not 1 stone will stay on another stone."

**7** The people asked him, "Teacher, when will these things occur? What sign will show that they are about to occur?"

**8** Jesus said, "Be careful that no person tricks you. Many people will come and use my name. They will say, 'I am the Christ,' and 'The time is near.' Do not follow them.

**9** You will hear about wars and fights. Do not be afraid. These things must occur first. But the end will not come immediately."

**10** Then he said to them, "Nations will fight against nations. Kingdoms will fight against kingdoms.

**11** There will be large earthquakes in many places. There will be famines and diseases. There will be terrible things and large signs from the sky.

**12** But before all these things occur, people will arrest you and persecute you. They will take you to the synagogues and put you in prisons. They will bring you in front of kings and governors because of my name.

**13** This will give you the opportunity to tell about me.

**14** Thus, decide now that you will not worry about what you will say.

**15** I will give you words and wisdom. None of your enemies will be able to resist or argue against these words.

**16** Even your parents, brothers, relatives, and friends will betray you. They will cause some of you to die.

**17** All people will hate you because of my name.

**18** But you will not lose 1 hair of your head.

**19** Stay strong, and you will save your lives.

**20** When you see armies around Jerusalem, then know that the destruction of the city is near.

**21** Then the people in Judea must run away to the mountains. The people in the city must go out. The people in the country must not go into the city.

**22** These are the days of punishment. All the things that the scriptures say will occur.

**23** In those days, it will be very bad for women who are pregnant and for women who feed babies! There will be much trouble in the land. God will be angry with this people.

**24** Their enemies will kill some of them with swords. They will take other people as prisoners to all nations. The Gentiles will walk on Jerusalem until the time of the Gentiles is complete.

**25** There will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars. On the earth the nations will have much trouble. The noise of the sea and the waves will confuse them.

**26** People will become weak with fear. They will be afraid of the things that will occur in the world. God will shake the powers in the sky.

**27** Then people will see the Son of Man come in a cloud with power and large glory.

**28** When these things start to occur, stand up and look up. Your rescue will be near."

**29** Then Jesus told them a parable: "Look at the fig tree and all the trees.

**30** When their leaves start to grow, you see this. Then you know that summer is near.

**31** In the same way, when you see these things occur, know that the kingdom of God is near.

**32** I tell you the truth: The people of this time will not die before all these things occur.

**33** Heaven and earth will disappear. But my words will never disappear.

**34** Be careful! Do not let your hearts become heavy with too much food and drink, or with the worries of this life. If you do, that day will come on you suddenly.

**35** That day will come like a trap on all the people who live on the whole earth.

**36** Thus, watch and pray at all times. Pray for strength to escape all these things that will occur. Pray that you can stand in front of the Son of Man."

**37** Each day Jesus taught in the temple. Each night he went out and stayed on the hill with the name the Mount of Olives.

**38** All the people came early in the morning to the temple to hear him.

## Chapter 22

**1** The Feast of Unleavened Bread came near. People also call this feast the Passover.

**2** The chief priests and the teachers of the law looked for a way to kill Jesus. They were afraid of the people.

**3** Then Satan went into Judas, who had the name Iscariot. Judas was 1 of the 12 apostles.

**4** Judas went to the chief priests and the officers of the temple guards. He talked with them about how he could give Jesus to them.

**5** They were happy. They agreed to give him money.

**6** Judas agreed. He looked for an opportunity to give Jesus to them when there was no crowd.

**7** The day of Unleavened Bread came. On that day the people had to kill the lamb for the Passover.

**8** Jesus sent Peter and John. He said, "Go and prepare the Passover meal for us to eat."

**9** They asked him, "Where do you want us to prepare it?"

**10** Jesus said to them, "When you go into the city, a man will meet you. He will carry a jar of water. Follow him into the house that he goes into.

**11** Say to the owner of the house, 'The Teacher asks you: Where is the guest room where I will eat the Passover with my disciples?'

**12** The owner will show you a large upstairs room with furniture. Prepare the meal there."

**13** Peter and John went. They found everything as Jesus told them. They prepared the Passover meal.

**14** When the time came, Jesus sat at the table with the 12 apostles.

**15** He said to them, "I wanted very much to eat this Passover meal with you before I suffer.

**16** I tell you, I will not eat it again until it becomes complete in the kingdom of God."

**17** Then Jesus took a cup and gave thanks. He said, "Take this cup and share it among you.

**18** I tell you, I will not drink wine again until the kingdom of God comes."

**19** Then Jesus took bread and gave thanks. He broke the bread and gave it to them. He said, "This is my body, which I give for you. Do this to remember me."

**20** After the supper, he took the cup in the same way. He said, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which I pour out for you.

**21** But look! The person who will betray me is with me at this table.

**22** The Son of Man will go as God decided. But how terrible it will be for that man who betrays him!"

**23** The apostles started to ask each other which of them will do this.

**24** Then the apostles started to argue. They argued about which of them was the most important.

**25** Jesus said to them, "The kings of the Gentiles rule over their people. The people call those rulers 'friends of the people.'

**26** But you must not be like that. The most important person among you must be like the youngest. The leader must be like a servant.

**27** Who is more important, the person who sits at the table or the person who serves? It is the person who sits at the table. But I am among you as a person who serves.

**28** You stayed with me in my troubles.

**29** My Father gave me a kingdom. In the same way, I give you a kingdom.

**30** You will eat and drink at my table in my kingdom. You will sit on thrones and judge the 12 tribes of Israel."

**31** The Lord said, "Simon, Simon, listen! Satan asked to test all of you, as a farmer separates wheat from the bad parts.

**32** But I prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. When you come back to me, make your brothers strong."

**33** Peter said to him, "Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison and to death."

**34** Jesus said, "Peter, I tell you, the rooster will not crow today before you say 3 times that you do not know me."

**35** Then Jesus said to them, "I sent you out with no money, no bag, and no sandals. Did you need anything?" They said, "No, nothing."

**36** He said to them, "But now, if you have money, take it. Also take a bag. If you do not have a sword, sell your coat and buy one.

**37** I tell you, the scripture says, 'People thought that he was a criminal.' These words must come true about me. The things that the scriptures say about me will come true."

**38** The disciples said, "Lord, look, here are 2 swords." He said to them, "That is sufficient."

**39** Jesus went out of the city to the Mount of Olives, as he usually did. His disciples followed him.

**40** When they came to the place, he said to them, "Pray that you will not go into temptation."

**41** Jesus went away from them about the distance that a person can throw a stone. He kneeled down and prayed.

**42** He said, "Father, if you agree, take this cup of pain away from me. But do what you want, not what I want."

**43** An angel from heaven came to him and made him strong.

**44** Jesus was in very much pain, and he prayed more strongly. His sweat was like large drops of blood that fell to the ground.

**45** He got up from prayer and went back to the disciples. He found them asleep because they were very sad.

**46** He said to them, "Why do you sleep? Get up and pray that you will not go into temptation."

**47** While Jesus still spoke, a crowd came. Judas, 1 of the 12 apostles, led them. Judas came near to Jesus to kiss him.

**48** But Jesus said to him, "Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?"

**49** The disciples near Jesus saw what was about to occur. They said, "Lord, must we attack with our swords?"

**50** One of them hit the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.

**51** But Jesus said, "Stop! No more of this." He touched the ear of the servant and healed him.

**52** The chief priests, the officers of the temple guards, and the elders came to Jesus. Jesus said to them, "Do you come with swords and clubs as if I am a criminal?

**53** Every day I was with you in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But this is your time, and the time when darkness has power."

**54** They arrested Jesus and took him to the house of the high priest. Peter followed far behind.

**55** The people made a fire in the middle of the yard and sat down together. Peter sat down among them.

**56** A servant girl saw Peter while he sat near the fire. She looked carefully at him and said, "This man was also with Jesus."

**57** But Peter said that this was not true. He said, "Woman, I do not know him."

**58** After a short time, another person saw Peter. He said, "You are also one of them." Peter said, "Man, I am not."

**59** About 1 hour later, another man said strongly, "This man was certainly with Jesus. He is from Galilee."

**60** But Peter said, "Man, I do not know what you talk about." Immediately, while Peter still spoke, a rooster crowed.

**61** The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the words of the Lord. Jesus told him, "Before the rooster crows today, you will say 3 times that you do not know me."

**62** Peter went outside and cried bitterly.

**63** The men who guarded Jesus laughed at him and hit him.

**64** They covered his eyes and hit him in the face. They said, "Prophesy! Tell us who hit you!"

**65** They said many other insults to him.

**66** In the morning, the elders of the people, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law met together. They took Jesus to their council.

**67** They said, "If you are the Christ, tell us." Jesus said to them, "If I tell you, you will not believe me.

**68** If I ask you a question, you will not answer me. And you will not let me go.

**69** But from now on, the Son of Man will sit at the right side of the powerful God."

**70** They all said, "Then are you the Son of God?" He said to them, "You say that I am."

**71** Then they said, "We do not need more witnesses. We heard him say it with his own mouth."

## Chapter 23

**1** Then all the members of the council got up. They took Jesus to Pilate.

**2** They started to accuse Jesus. They said, "We found that this man tells our nation to do wrong things. He tells people not to pay taxes to Caesar. He says that he is Christ, a king."

**3** Pilate asked Jesus, "Are you the King of the Jews?" Jesus answered him, "You say so."

**4** Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowd, "I do not find that this man is guilty of a crime."

**5** But they spoke more strongly. They said, "He causes trouble among the people with his words. He taught in all of Judea. He started in Galilee and now he is here."

**6** When Pilate heard the word "Galilee," he asked if Jesus was from Galilee.

**7** Pilate learned that Jesus was under the authority of Herod. So Pilate sent Jesus to Herod. At that time Herod was also in Jerusalem.

**8** When Herod saw Jesus, he was very happy. He heard many things about Jesus, and he wanted to see him for a long time. Herod hoped to see Jesus do a miracle.

**9** Herod asked Jesus many questions. But Jesus did not answer him.

**10** The chief priests and the teachers of the law stood there. They accused Jesus very strongly.

**11** Herod and his soldiers insulted Jesus and laughed at him. They put a beautiful robe on him. Then Herod sent Jesus back to Pilate.

**12** Before that day, Pilate and Herod were enemies. But on that day they became friends.

**13** Pilate called together the chief priests, the leaders, and the people.

**14** He said to them, "You brought this man to me. You said that he tells the people to do wrong things. I asked him questions in front of you. I did not find that he is guilty of the things that you say.

**15** Herod also did not find him guilty, because Herod sent him back to us. Look, this man did nothing that must have the punishment of death.

**16** So I will hit him with whips, and then I will let him go free."

**17** At each Passover feast, Pilate had to let 1 prisoner go free for the people.

**18** But all the people shouted together, "Kill this man! Let Barabbas go free for us!"

**19** Barabbas was in prison because he started a fight against the government in the city. He also committed murder.

**20** Pilate wanted to let Jesus go free. So he spoke to the people again.

**21** But they shouted, "Crucify him! Crucify him!"

**22** Pilate spoke to them a third time. He said, "Why? What crime did this man commit? I did not find a reason to kill him. So I will hit him with whips, and then I will let him go free."

**23** But the people continued to shout loudly. They demanded that Pilate crucify Jesus. Their shouts and the shouts of the chief priests won.

**24** Pilate decided to give the people what they demanded.

**25** Pilate let Barabbas go free. Barabbas was the man who was in prison for a fight against the government and for murder. The people asked for Barabbas. But Pilate gave Jesus to them to do what they wanted.

**26** The soldiers took Jesus away. On the road they took hold of a man with the name Simon, from Cyrene. Simon came into the city from the country. The soldiers put the cross on Simon. They made him carry it behind Jesus.

**27** A large crowd of people followed Jesus. In the crowd there were women who cried and were very sad for him.

**28** Jesus turned to the women and said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not cry for me. Cry for yourselves and for your children.

**29** A time will come when people will say, 'Blessed are the women who cannot have children. Blessed are the women who never had babies and never fed babies.'

**30** Then people will say to the mountains, 'Fall on us!' They will say to the hills, 'Cover us!'

**31** People do these things to me now, while times are good. So the things that will occur when times are bad will be worse."

**32** The soldiers also led 2 other men with Jesus to kill them. These men were criminals.

**33** They came to the place with the name Calvary. There they crucified Jesus and the criminals. One criminal was at the right side of Jesus, and the other criminal was at his left side.

**34** Jesus said, "Father, forgive them, because they do not know what they do." The soldiers threw lots to divide the clothes of Jesus among them.

**35** The people stood there and watched. The leaders laughed at Jesus. They said, "He saved other people. If he is the Christ, the chosen one of God, he must save himself."

**36** The soldiers also laughed at him. They came to him and gave him sour wine.

**37** They said, "If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself!"

**38** Above Jesus there was a sign. Someone wrote it in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew. The sign said: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

**39** One of the criminals on a cross insulted Jesus. He said, "If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!"

**40** But the other criminal told him that he was wrong. He said, "You also have the same punishment. Do you not fear God?

**41** Our punishment is correct, because we get what our actions deserve. But this man did nothing wrong."

**42** Then he said to Jesus, "Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom."

**43** Jesus said to him, "I tell you the truth: Today you will be with me in paradise."

**44** At about 12 noon, darkness came over all the land. The darkness stayed until 3 o'clock in the afternoon.

**45** The sun stopped. It gave no light. The curtain in the temple tore into 2 pieces.

**46** Jesus shouted with a loud voice, "Father, I put my spirit into your hands." After he said this, he died.

**47** The Roman officer saw what occurred. He praised God and said, "This man was certainly innocent."

**48** A crowd of people came together to watch. They saw what occurred. Then they hit their chests in sorrow and went home.

**49** All the friends of Jesus stood far away and watched these things. The women who followed him from Galilee also stood there.

**50** There was a man with the name Joseph. He was a member of the council. He was a good and righteous man.

**51** Joseph did not agree with the decision and the actions of the council. He came from Arimathea, a city of the Jews. He waited for the kingdom of God.

**52** Joseph went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

**53** He took the body down from the cross and wrapped it in linen cloth. He put the body in a tomb that workers cut in rock. No person was in this tomb before.

**54** That day was the Day of Preparation. The Sabbath was about to start.

**55** The women who came with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph. They saw the tomb and how Joseph put the body of Jesus in it.

**56** Then they went home and prepared spices and perfumes. On the Sabbath day they rested, as the law of God commands.

## Chapter 24

**1** On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women went to the tomb. They took the spices that they prepared. Some other women went with them.

**2** They found that someone rolled the stone away from the tomb.

**3** They went into the tomb, but they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

**4** The women did not know what to think about this. Suddenly 2 men in very bright clothes stood next to them.

**5** The women were afraid and bowed their faces to the ground. The men said to them, "Why do you look for a person who lives among the dead?

**6** Jesus is not here. He came back to life! Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee.

**7** He said, 'Sinful men must take the Son of Man and crucify him. On the third day he will come back to life.'"

**8** Then the women remembered the words of Jesus.

**9** They went back from the tomb. They told all these things to the 11 apostles and to all the other disciples.

**10** The women were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and some other women. They told these things to the apostles.

**11** But the apostles thought that the words of the women were nonsense. The apostles did not believe them.

**12** But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. He bent down and looked in. He saw only the linen cloths. Then he went home. He was very surprised at what occurred.

**13** On that same day, 2 of the disciples went to a village with the name Emmaus. This village was about 11 kilometers from Jerusalem.

**14** They talked together about all the things that occurred.

**15** While they talked and discussed these things, Jesus came near and walked with them.

**16** But something stopped their eyes, and they did not know who he was.

**17** Jesus said to them, "What do you talk about while you walk?" They stopped, and they looked sad.

**18** One of them, with the name Cleopas, answered him. He said, "Are you the only visitor in Jerusalem who does not know the things that occurred there in these days?"

**19** Jesus said to them, "What things?" They said to him, "The things about Jesus of Nazareth. He was a prophet. He had much power in what he did and said in front of God and all the people.

**20** Our chief priests and leaders gave him to the Romans. The Romans sentenced him to death and crucified him.

**21** We hoped that he was the man who will make Israel free. Also, today is the third day since these things occurred.

**22** And some women of our group surprised us. They went to the tomb early this morning.

**23** They did not find his body there. They came back and said that they saw angels in a vision. The angels said that Jesus was alive.

**24** Some of our group went to the tomb. They found it as the women said. But they did not see Jesus."

**25** Then Jesus said to them, "You are foolish people! You are very slow to believe all the things that the prophets said.

**26** The Christ had to suffer these things before he went into his glory."

**27** Then Jesus explained to them what all the scriptures said about him. He started with the books of Moses and continued through all the prophets.

**28** They came near the village where they went. Jesus acted as if he will go farther.

**29** But they asked him strongly to stay. They said, "Stay with us, because it is almost evening. The day is almost done." So Jesus went in to stay with them.

**30** Jesus sat at the table with them. He took the bread and blessed it. Then he broke it and gave it to them.

**31** Then their eyes opened, and they knew who he was. Then he disappeared.

**32** They said to each other, "When he talked with us on the road, our hearts felt hot inside us. We felt this when he explained the scriptures to us."

**33** They got up immediately and went back to Jerusalem. There they found the 11 apostles and the people with them together.

**34** These people said, "It is true! The Lord came back to life. He showed himself to Simon."

**35** Then the 2 disciples told what occurred on the road. They told how they knew Jesus when he broke the bread.

**36** While they talked about these things, Jesus himself stood among them. He said to them, "Peace to you."

**37** But they were very afraid. They thought that they saw a spirit.

**38** Jesus said to them, "Why are you troubled? Why do you have doubts in your hearts?

**39** Look at my hands and my feet. It is I! Touch me and see. A spirit does not have flesh and bones. But you see that I have them."

**40** After he said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.

**41** They were very happy and surprised, but they still did not believe it. Jesus said to them, "Do you have any food here?"

**42** They gave him a piece of cooked fish and some honeycomb.

**43** He took the food and ate it in front of them.

**44** Jesus said to them, "When I was with you, I told you these words. All the things that the law of Moses, the prophets, and the Psalms say about me must come true."

**45** Then he made their minds open to understand the scriptures.

**46** He said to them, "The scriptures say that the Christ must suffer. They say that he must come back to life from the dead on the third day.

**47** People must tell all nations to repent. They must tell all nations that God forgives sins through the name of the Christ. They must start in Jerusalem.

**48** You saw these things, and you will tell people about them.

**49** Look, I will send to you what my Father promised. But stay in the city until you get power from heaven."

**50** Jesus led them out of the city to near Bethany. He lifted up his hands and blessed them.

**51** While he blessed them, he went away from them. God took him up into heaven.

**52** They worshiped him. Then they went back to Jerusalem with much joy.

**53** They were always in the temple, and they praised God. Amen.

# John

## Chapter 1

**1** At the start, the Word was there. The Word was with God, and the Word was God.

**2** At the start, the Word was with God.

**3** God made all things through the Word. Nothing that exists came into existence without the Word.

**4** Life was in the Word. That life was the light for all people.

**5** The light shines in the darkness. The darkness did not defeat the light.

**6** God sent a man with the name John.

**7** John came as a witness. He came to tell people about the light. He came so that all people will believe through him.

**8** John was not the light. He came to tell people about the light.

**9** The true light, which gives light to all people, was about to come into the world.

**10** The Word was in the world. God made the world through him. But the world did not know him.

**11** He came to his own people, but his own people did not accept him.

**12** But some people accepted him and believed in his name. He gave these people the right to become children of God.

**13** They did not become children of God by a human birth. A human father did not decide this. God made them his children.

**14** The Word became a human and lived among us. We saw his glory. It was the glory of the only Son of the Father. He was full of grace and truth.

**15** John told people about him. John shouted, "This is the man about whom I spoke. I said, 'The man who comes after me is more important than I. He existed before me.'"

**16** We all received from his fullness. He gave us grace after grace.

**17** God gave the law through Moses. Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

**18** No person ever saw God. But the only Son, who is very near to the Father, showed us who God is.

**19** The Jewish leaders in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to John. They asked him, "Who are you?" This is what John told them.

**20** John did not refuse to answer. He said clearly, "I am not the Christ."

**21** They asked him, "Then who are you? Are you Elijah?" John said, "I am not." They asked, "Are you the Prophet?" He answered, "No."

**22** Then they said to him, "Who are you? We must give an answer to the people who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"

**23** John said, "I am the voice of a person who shouts in the wilderness: 'Make a straight road for the Lord.' The prophet Isaiah said this."

**24** The Pharisees sent these men.

**25** They asked John, "You are not the Christ, Elijah, or the Prophet. Then why do you baptize people?"

**26** John answered them, "I baptize with water. But a man stands among you whom you do not know.

**27** He comes after me, but he is more important than I. I am not good enough to untie his sandals."

**28** These things occurred in Bethabara on the other side of the Jordan River. John baptized people there.

**29** On the next day, John saw Jesus come to him. John said, "Look, here is the Lamb of God! He takes away the sin of the world.

**30** This is the man about whom I spoke. I said, 'A man who comes after me is more important than I. He existed before me.'

**31** I did not know him. But I came to baptize with water so that the people of Israel will know him."

**32** Then John said, "I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove. The Spirit stayed on him.

**33** I did not know him. But God sent me to baptize with water. God told me, 'You will see the Spirit come down and stay on a man. That man will baptize with the Holy Spirit.'

**34** I saw this. I tell you that this man is the Son of God."

**35** On the next day, John was there again with 2 of his disciples.

**36** John saw Jesus walk past. John said, "Look, here is the Lamb of God!"

**37** The 2 disciples heard John say this, and they followed Jesus.

**38** Jesus turned and saw them follow him. He said to them, "What do you want?" They said to him, "Rabbi, where do you stay?" ("Rabbi" means "Teacher.")

**39** Jesus said to them, "Come and see." So they went and saw where he stayed. They stayed with him that day. It was about 4 o'clock in the afternoon.

**40** One of the 2 disciples who heard John and followed Jesus was Andrew. Andrew was the brother of Simon Peter.

**41** First, Andrew found his brother Simon. He said to Simon, "We found the Messiah." ("Messiah" means "Christ.")

**42** Andrew brought Simon to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, "You are Simon, the son of John. You will have the name Cephas." ("Cephas" means "a rock.")

**43** On the next day, Jesus decided to go to Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, "Follow me."

**44** Philip was from the town of Bethsaida. Andrew and Peter also came from that town.

**45** Philip found Nathanael and said to him, "Moses wrote about a man in the law. The prophets also wrote about him. We found this man. He is Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."

**46** Nathanael said to Philip, "Can anything good come from Nazareth?" Philip said to him, "Come and see."

**47** Jesus saw Nathanael come to him. Jesus said about him, "Look, here is a true Israelite. He does not lie."

**48** Nathanael said to Jesus, "How do you know me?" Jesus answered, "I saw you under the fig tree before Philip called you."

**49** Nathanael answered, "Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!"

**50** Jesus said to him, "Do you believe because I said that I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than this."

**51** Then Jesus said to him, "I tell you the truth: You will see heaven open. You will see the angels of God go up and come down on the Son of Man."

## Chapter 2

**1** On the third day, there was a wedding in Cana in Galilee. The mother of Jesus was there.

**2** People also invited Jesus and his disciples to the wedding.

**3** When all the wine was gone, the mother of Jesus said to him, "They have no more wine."

**4** Jesus said to her, "Woman, why do you tell me this? My time did not come yet."

**5** His mother said to the servants, "Do what he tells you."

**6** There were 6 stone water jars there. The Jews used these jars for their ceremonies to make things clean. Each jar held 80 to 120 liters.

**7** Jesus said to the servants, "Fill the jars with water." So they filled the jars to the top.

**8** Then he said to them, "Now take out some water and give it to the man who controls the feast." So they did.

**9** The man who controlled the feast tasted the water. The water became wine. He did not know where the wine came from. But the servants who took out the water knew. Then the man called the bridegroom.

**10** He said to the bridegroom, "All people serve the good wine first. When the guests drink much, then they serve the cheaper wine. But you kept the good wine until now!"

**11** This was the first of the miraculous signs of Jesus. He did it in Cana in Galilee. Thus he showed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.

**12** After this, Jesus went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers, and his disciples. They stayed there for a few days.

**13** It was almost time for the Jewish Passover. So Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

**14** In the temple, he found people who sold cattle, sheep, and doves. He also found men who sat at tables and exchanged money.

**15** Jesus made a whip from ropes. He pushed all the people and the sheep and cattle out of the temple. He threw the coins of the money changers on the ground and turned over their tables.

**16** He said to the people who sold doves, "Take these things out of here! Do not make the house of my Father into a market!"

**17** His disciples remembered that the scriptures say, "My strong love for your house will burn in me like a fire."

**18** The Jewish leaders said to Jesus, "You do these things. What miraculous sign can you show us to prove your authority?"

**19** Jesus answered them, "Destroy this temple, and in 3 days I will build it again."

**20** The Jewish leaders said, "People worked for 46 years to build this temple. Will you build it again in 3 days?"

**21** But the temple about which Jesus spoke was his body.

**22** Later Jesus came back to life from the dead. Then his disciples remembered that he said this. They believed the scriptures and the words that Jesus said.

**23** Jesus was in Jerusalem during the Passover feast. Many people saw the miraculous signs that he did, and they believed in his name.

**24** But Jesus did not trust them, because he knew all people.

**25** He did not need a person to tell him about people. He knew what was in their hearts.

## Chapter 3

**1** There was a Pharisee with the name Nicodemus. He was a leader of the Jews.

**2** Nicodemus came to Jesus at night. He said to him, "Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who came from God. No person can do the miraculous signs that you do if God is not with him."

**3** Jesus answered him, "I tell you the truth: If a person does not get a new birth, he cannot see the kingdom of God."

**4** Nicodemus said to him, "How can a man get a new birth when he is old? He cannot go into the body of his mother a second time and get birth again!"

**5** Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth. If a person does not get birth from water and the Spirit, he cannot go into the kingdom of God.

**6** Human parents give birth to a human body. But the Spirit gives birth to a spirit.

**7** Do not feel wonder that I tell you, 'You must get a new birth.'

**8** The wind blows where it wants to blow. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. All people who get birth from the Spirit are like that."

**9** Nicodemus said to him, "How can these things be possible?"

**10** Jesus answered him, "You are a teacher of Israel. Do you not understand these things?

**11** I tell you the truth: We speak about what we know. We tell people about what we saw. But you people do not accept what we tell you.

**12** I told you about things on earth, and you do not believe. Then you will not believe if I tell you about things in heaven.

**13** No person ever went up to heaven except the Son of Man. He came down from heaven.

**14** Moses lifted up the bronze snake on a pole in the wilderness. In the same way, people must lift up the Son of Man.

**15** Then all people who believe in him will have eternal life.

**16** God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son. All people who believe in him will not die, but they will have eternal life.

**17** God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world as guilty. God sent him to save the world.

**18** God does not judge as guilty the person who believes in the Son. But the person who does not believe is already guilty. He is guilty because he does not believe in the name of the only Son of God.

**19** This is the reason for the judgment: The light came into the world. But people loved the darkness more than the light, because their actions were evil.

**20** All people who do evil hate the light. They do not come to the light, because they do not want people to see their evil actions.

**21** But the person who obeys the truth comes to the light. Then all people will see that he does his actions through God."

**22** After this, Jesus and his disciples went into the land of Judea. He stayed there with them and baptized people.

**23** John also baptized people at Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there. People came to John, and he baptized them.

**24** This was before people put John in prison.

**25** Some disciples of John argued with a Jew about the ceremonies to make things clean.

**26** They came to John and said to him, "Rabbi, a man was with you on the other side of the Jordan River. You told people about him. Look, now he baptizes people, and all people go to him."

**27** John answered, "A person can get only what God gives him from heaven.

**28** You heard me say, 'I am not the Christ. God sent me ahead of him.'

**29** The bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom stands near and listens to him. The friend is very happy when he hears the voice of the bridegroom. In the same way, my joy is now complete.

**30** He must become more important, and I must become less important."

**31** The man who comes from above is more important than all people. A person who comes from the earth belongs to the earth, and he speaks about things on the earth. The man who comes from heaven is more important than all people.

**32** He tells about what he saw and heard. But people do not accept what he tells them.

**33** The person who accepts what he tells shows that God is true.

**34** God sent him, and he speaks the words of God. God gives him the Spirit with no limit.

**35** The Father loves the Son. He put all things under the control of the Son.

**36** The person who believes in the Son has eternal life. The person who does not obey the Son will not see life. The anger of God stays on that person.

## Chapter 4

**1** The Pharisees heard that Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John. The Lord knew that the Pharisees heard this.

**2** But Jesus himself did not baptize people. His disciples baptized them.

**3** So Jesus left Judea and went back to Galilee.

**4** He had to go through Samaria.

**5** He came to a town in Samaria with the name Sychar. This town was near the field that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.

**6** The well of Jacob was there. Jesus was weary from his journey, so he sat down next to the well. It was about 12 noon.

**7** A woman of Samaria came to get water. Jesus said to her, "Give me some water to drink."

**8** His disciples went into the town to buy food.

**9** The woman of Samaria said to him, "You are a Jew, and I am a woman of Samaria. Why do you ask me for a drink?" She said this because the Jews do not associate with the Samaritans.

**10** Jesus answered her, "You do not know the gift of God. You do not know who asks you for a drink. If you knew, you will ask him. Then he will give you water that gives life."

**11** The woman said to him, "Sir, you have no bucket, and the well is deep. Where can you get that water that gives life?

**12** Our father Jacob gave us this well. He drank from it, and his sons and his animals also drank from it. Are you more important than Jacob?"

**13** Jesus answered her, "All people who drink this water will be thirsty again.

**14** But the people who drink the water that I give will never be thirsty again. The water that I give will become a spring of water in them. That spring will give them eternal life."

**15** The woman said to him, "Sir, give me this water. Then I will not be thirsty, and I will not have to come here to get water."

**16** Jesus said to her, "Go, call your husband, and come back here."

**17** The woman answered, "I have no husband." Jesus said to her, "You speak correctly when you say that you have no husband.

**18** You had 5 husbands. The man with whom you live now is not your husband. What you said is true."

**19** The woman said to him, "Sir, I see that you are a prophet.

**20** Our ancestors worshiped on this mountain. But you Jews say that people must worship in Jerusalem."

**21** Jesus said to her, "Woman, believe me. A time will come when you will not worship the Father on this mountain or in Jerusalem.

**22** You Samaritans worship what you do not know. We Jews worship what we know, because salvation comes from the Jews.

**23** But a time will come, and it is here now, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. The Father wants people who worship him like that.

**24** God is spirit. The people who worship him must worship in spirit and truth."

**25** The woman said to him, "I know that the Messiah will come. People call him the Christ. When he comes, he will explain all things to us."

**26** Jesus said to her, "I am the Messiah. I am the man who speaks to you now."

**27** At that time, his disciples came back. They felt wonder that Jesus talked with a woman. But no person asked, "What do you want?" or "Why do you talk with her?"

**28** Then the woman left her water jar. She went back into the town and said to the people,

**29** "Come and see a man who told me all the things that I ever did. Can he be the Christ?"

**30** The people went out of the town and came to Jesus.

**31** While this occurred, the disciples asked Jesus strongly, "Rabbi, eat something."

**32** But he said to them, "I have food to eat that you do not know about."

**33** So the disciples said to each other, "Did a person bring him food?"

**34** Jesus said to them, "My food is to do what God, who sent me, wants. My food is to complete his work.

**35** You say, 'There are 4 more months until the harvest.' But I tell you, look at the fields! The crops are ready for harvest now.

**36** The person who harvests gets his pay now. He gathers crops for eternal life. Thus the person who plants and the person who harvests can be happy together.

**37** These words are true: 'One person plants, and another person harvests.'

**38** I sent you to harvest crops for which you did not work. Other people did the hard work, and you get the result of their work."

**39** Many Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the words of the woman. She said, "He told me all the things that I ever did."

**40** So the Samaritans came to Jesus and asked him to stay with them. He stayed there for 2 days.

**41** Many more people believed because of the words that Jesus spoke.

**42** They said to the woman, "Now we believe, but not because of what you told us. We heard him ourselves. Now we know that this man is truly the Savior of the world."

**43** After 2 days, Jesus left that place and went to Galilee.

**44** Jesus himself said that people do not respect a prophet in his own country.

**45** When Jesus came to Galilee, the people of Galilee accepted him. They saw all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the Passover feast, because they also went to the feast.

**46** Jesus went again to Cana in Galilee, where he changed the water into wine. There was an officer of the king in Capernaum. The son of this officer was ill.

**47** The officer heard that Jesus came from Judea to Galilee. He went to Jesus and asked him to come down and heal his son. His son was about to die.

**48** Jesus said to him, "If you people do not see miraculous signs and wonders, you will not believe."

**49** The officer said to him, "Sir, come down before my child dies."

**50** Jesus said to him, "Go home. Your son will live." The man believed the words of Jesus, and he went home.

**51** While he was on his way home, his servants came to meet him. They told him, "Your son is alive and well."

**52** He asked them at what time his son started to become better. They said to him, "The fever left him yesterday at 1 o'clock in the afternoon."

**53** The father knew that this was the same time when Jesus told him, "Your son will live." So he and all his family believed in Jesus.

**54** This was the second miraculous sign that Jesus did after he came from Judea to Galilee.

## Chapter 5

**1** After this, there was a Jewish feast. Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

**2** In Jerusalem, near the Sheep Gate, there is a pool. In the Hebrew language, its name is Bethesda. The pool has 5 covered porches.

**3** Many ill people lay in these porches. Some were blind, some were lame, and some could not move their bodies. They waited for the water to move.

**4** At certain times an angel came down into the pool and moved the water. After the water moved, the first person who went into the pool became well. He became well from all his diseases.

**5** A man was there who was ill for 38 years.

**6** Jesus saw the man lie there. Jesus knew that the man was ill for a long time. Jesus said to him, "Do you want to become well?"

**7** The ill man answered him, "Sir, when the water moves, I have no person to put me into the pool. While I try to go into the pool, another person goes in before me."

**8** Jesus said to him, "Get up, pick up your mat, and walk."

**9** Immediately the man became well. He picked up his mat and walked. That day was the Sabbath.

**10** So the Jewish leaders said to the man whom Jesus healed, "Today is the Sabbath. The law does not let you carry your mat."

**11** He answered them, "The man who made me well told me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"

**12** They asked him, "Who is the man who told you, 'Pick up your mat and walk'?"

**13** But the man whom Jesus healed did not know who Jesus was. Jesus went away into the crowd in that place.

**14** Later, Jesus found the man in the temple. He said to him, "Look, you are well now. Do not sin again. If you sin, something worse will occur to you."

**15** The man went away. He told the Jewish leaders that Jesus was the man who made him well.

**16** Jesus did these things on the Sabbath day. So the Jewish leaders persecuted Jesus and wanted to kill him.

**17** But Jesus answered them, "My Father always works until now, and I also work."

**18** Because of this, the Jewish leaders tried more to kill him. Jesus did not obey their rules for the Sabbath. Also, he said that God was his own Father. Thus he made himself equal with God.

**19** Jesus answered them, "I tell you the truth: The Son can do nothing by himself. He can do only what he sees the Father do. The Son does the same things that the Father does.

**20** The Father loves the Son and shows him all the things that he does. The Father will show the Son greater works than these. Then you will feel wonder.

**21** The Father brings dead people back to life and gives them life. In the same way, the Son gives life to the people whom he chooses.

**22** The Father does not judge any person. He gave all judgment to the Son.

**23** He did this so that all people will honor the Son as they honor the Father. If a person does not honor the Son, he does not honor the Father who sent the Son.

**24** I tell you the truth: A person who hears my words and believes God, who sent me, has eternal life. God will not judge him as guilty. He left death and came into life.

**25** I tell you the truth. A time will come, and it is here now. Then the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God. The people who hear his voice will live.

**26** The Father has life in himself. In the same way, he gave the Son life in himself.

**27** The Father also gave the Son authority to judge, because he is the Son of Man.

**28** Do not feel wonder at this. A time will come when all the dead people in the graves will hear his voice.

**29** They will come out of the graves. The people who did good things will come back to life and live. The people who did evil things will come back to life and get judgment.

**30** I can do nothing by myself. I judge only as the Father tells me. My judgment is fair, because I do not try to do what I want. I do what the Father, who sent me, wants.

**31** If I alone tell about myself, people cannot accept my words as true.

**32** But another person tells about me. I know that the things that he says about me are true.

**33** You sent messengers to John, and he told them the truth.

**34** I do not need the words of a human to prove who I am. But I tell you these things so that God can save you.

**35** John was like a lamp that burned and gave light. For a short time, you were happy to enjoy his light.

**36** But I have a better proof than the words of John. The Father gave me works to complete. These works that I do show that the Father sent me.

**37** The Father who sent me also told about me. You never heard his voice, and you never saw his shape.

**38** His word does not stay in you, because you do not believe the Son whom he sent.

**39** You study the scriptures carefully, because you think that they give you eternal life. The scriptures tell about me.

**40** But you refuse to come to me to get life.

**41** I do not accept praise from people.

**42** But I know you. I know that you do not have love for God in your hearts.

**43** I came with the authority of my Father, but you do not accept me. If another person comes with his own authority, you will accept him.

**44** You accept praise from each other. But you do not try to get the praise that comes from the only God. So how can you believe?

**45** Do not think that I will accuse you in front of the Father. Moses will accuse you. You hope in Moses.
