**16** Paul waited for Silas and Timothy in Athens. He saw that the city was full of idols. This made him very troubled.

**17** So he discussed with the Jews and the devout Greeks in the synagogue. Each day he also discussed with the people in the marketplace.

**18** Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers argued with Paul. Some of them said, "This man talks too much. What does he try to say?" Other people said, "He seems to tell us about foreign gods." They said this because Paul preached about Jesus and the resurrection.

**19** They took Paul to the Areopagus (the city council). They said, "Can we know what this new message is that you speak about?

**20** You tell us strange things. We want to know the meaning of these things."

**21** All the people of Athens and the foreigners who lived there used all their time in one way. They only wanted to tell or hear the newest ideas.

**22** Paul stood in front of the council of the Areopagus. He said, "Men of Athens, I see that you are very religious in all things.

**23** I walked through your city and looked at the things that you worship. I found an altar with these words on it: 'TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.' You worship this God, but you do not know him. I tell you about him now.

**24** God made the world and all things in it. He is the Lord of heaven and earth. He does not live in temples that people built.

**25** People do not serve him with their hands, because he does not need anything. He gives life and breath and all things to all people.

**26** From one man, God made all the nations of people. He made them so that they live on all the earth. He decided their times in history and the borders of their lands.

**27** God did this so that people will look for him. Maybe they will try to find him and will find him. But God is not far from each of us.

**28** Through God we live and move and exist. Some of your own poets said this: 'We are his children.'

**29** We are the children of God. Thus, we must not think that God is like an image of gold, silver or stone. People make images with their skill and their ideas.

**30** In the past, people did not know about God, and God did not punish them for this. But now God tells all people everywhere to repent.

**31** God chose a day when he will judge the world fairly. He will judge through the man that he chose. God proved this to all people when he raised this man from the dead."

**32** Some of the people heard Paul speak about the resurrection of the dead. They laughed at him. But other people said, "We want to hear you speak about this again."

**33** Then Paul left the council.

**34** But some men joined Paul and believed. One of them was Dionysius, a member of the council of the Areopagus. A woman with the name Damaris and some other people also believed.

## Chapter 18

**1** After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

**2** In Corinth, Paul met a Jew with the name Aquila. Aquila came from Pontus. Aquila and his wife Priscilla came from Italy a short time before. They left Italy because Claudius ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them.

**3** Aquila and Priscilla made tents, and Paul did the same work. So he stayed with them and worked with them.

**4** On every Sabbath day, Paul discussed the Scriptures in the synagogue. He tried to make Jews and Greeks believe.

**5** Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia. Then Paul used all his time to preach. He told the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

**6** But the Jews spoke against Paul and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes to warn them. He said to them, "If God punishes you, it is your own fault. I am not responsible. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."

**7** Paul left the synagogue and went to the house of a man with the name Titius Justus. Justus worshipped God. His house was next to the synagogue.

**8** Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and all his family believed in the Lord. Many people in Corinth heard Paul. They believed and received baptism.

**9** One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision. The Lord said, "Do not be afraid. Continue to speak and do not stop.

**10** I am with you. Nobody will attack you or hurt you. Many of my people live in this city."

**11** So Paul stayed there for 1 year and 6 months. He taught the word of God to the people.

**12** At that time, Gallio was the governor of Achaia. The Jews joined together and attacked Paul. They took him to the court.

**13** They said, "This man tells people to worship God in ways that are against the law."

**14** Paul was ready to speak. But Gallio said to the Jews, "If this man did a wrong act or a serious crime, I will listen to you.

**15** But this is a question about words, names and your own law. You must solve this problem yourselves. I will not be a judge of these things."

**16** Then Gallio made them leave the court.

**17** Then all the people took Sosthenes, the leader of the synagogue. They beat him in front of the court. But Gallio did not care about these things.

**18** Paul stayed in Corinth for many more days. Then he said goodbye to the brothers and sailed to Syria. Priscilla and Aquila went with him. In Cenchreae, Paul cut his hair because he made a promise to God.

**19** They came to Ephesus. There Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. Paul went into the synagogue and discussed with the Jews.

**20** The Jews asked Paul to stay with them for a longer time. But he did not agree.

**21** He said goodbye to them. He said, "I must keep the festival that will come in Jerusalem. But if God wants, I will come back to you." Then he sailed from Ephesus.

**22** Paul arrived in Caesarea. He went up to Jerusalem and greeted the church. Then he went down to Antioch.

**23** Paul stayed in Antioch for some time. Then he left and went from place to place through Galatia and Phrygia. He made all the disciples strong.

**24** A Jew with the name Apollos came to Ephesus. His birthplace was Alexandria. He was a good speaker and knew the Scriptures very well.

**25** Apollos learned about the way of the Lord. He spoke with much enthusiasm. He taught correctly about Jesus. But he knew only about the baptism of John.

**26** Apollos started to speak boldly in the synagogue. Priscilla and Aquila heard him. They took him aside. They explained the way of God to him more correctly.

**27** Apollos wanted to go to Achaia. The brothers encouraged him. They wrote to the disciples in Achaia and told them to receive him. When Apollos arrived, he gave much help to the people who believed through the grace of God.

**28** In public, Apollos argued strongly against the Jews and proved that they were wrong. He used the Scriptures to show that Jesus is the Christ.

## Chapter 19

**1** While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul went through the inland areas and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples.

**2** Paul said to them, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" They said, "No. We did not hear that there is a Holy Spirit."

**3** Paul said, "Then what baptism did you receive?" They said, "We received the baptism of John."

**4** Paul said, "John baptized people who repented. He told the people to believe in the man who will come after him. That man is Jesus."

**5** The disciples heard this. Then they received baptism in the name of the Lord Jesus.

**6** Paul put his hands on them, and the Holy Spirit came on them. They spoke in other languages and prophesied.

**7** There were about 12 men in the group.

**8** Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly for 3 months. He discussed with the people and tried to make them believe about the kingdom of God.

**9** But some of the Jews refused to believe. In front of the crowd, they said bad things about the Way. So Paul left them and took the disciples with him. Each day he discussed in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

**10** Paul did this for 2 years. Thus, all the Jews and Greeks who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord.

**11** God did special miracles through Paul.

**12** People took cloths that touched Paul to the sick people. Then their diseases went away, and the evil spirits left them.

**13** Some Jews went from place to place and forced evil spirits out of people. They tried to use the name of the Lord Jesus on people with evil spirits. They said, "In the name of Jesus, whom Paul preaches, I command you to come out!"

**14** 7 sons of Sceva did this. Sceva was a Jewish chief priest.

**15** But the evil spirit said to them, "I know Jesus, and I know about Paul. But who are you?"

**16** Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them. He was stronger than all of them. He beat them so badly that they ran out of the house without clothes and with wounds.

**17** All the Jews and Greeks who lived in Ephesus heard about this. They were all afraid. They gave much honor to the name of the Lord Jesus.

**18** Many believers came and told the people about the bad things that they did.

**19** Many of the believers used magic before. They brought their books of magic and burned them in front of all the people. They calculated the value of the books. The value was 50,000 silver coins.

**20** In this way, the word of the Lord spread to more people and became very strong.

**21** After these things, Paul decided to go through Macedonia and Achaia and then go to Jerusalem. He said, "After I go there, I must also visit Rome."

**22** Paul sent 2 of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But Paul stayed in Asia for some more time.

**23** At that time, there was much trouble about the Way.

**24** A silversmith with the name Demetrius made small silver models of the temple of Artemis. This work gave much money to the workers.

**25** Demetrius called these workers and other workers with similar work. He said, "Men, you know that we get much money from this work.

**26** You see and hear what this Paul does. He says that the gods that people make with their hands are not gods. He changed the minds of many people in Ephesus and in almost all of Asia.

**27** There is a danger that people will think that our work is bad. There is also a danger that people will not respect the temple of the great goddess Artemis. All Asia and all the world worship her. But she will lose her greatness."

**28** The men heard this and became very angry. They shouted, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

**29** All the city became confused. The people took Gaius and Aristarchus, 2 men from Macedonia who traveled with Paul. All the people ran together into the theater.

**30** Paul wanted to go into the crowd, but the disciples did not let him.

**31** Some officials of the province of Asia were friends of Paul. They sent him a message. They asked him not to go into the theater.

**32** Some people in the crowd shouted one thing, and other people shouted a different thing. There was much confusion in the crowd. Most of the people did not know why they came together.

**33** The Jews pushed a man with the name Alexander to the front. Some people in the crowd told him what to say. Alexander moved his hand because he wanted to make a defense to the people.

**34** But the crowd learned that he was a Jew. Then all the people shouted together for about 2 hours. They shouted, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

**35** Then the city clerk made the crowd quiet. He said, "Men of Ephesus, all people know that Ephesus guards the temple of the great Artemis. All people know that our city also guards her sacred stone that fell from the sky.

**36** Nobody can say that these things are not true. Thus, you must be calm. Do not do anything quickly. First think carefully.

**37** You brought these men here. But they did not rob temples. They did not insult our goddess.

**38** Maybe Demetrius and his workers have a complaint against someone. If so, the courts are open, and there are governors. They can take their complaints to the courts.

**39** If you want something more, the official assembly of the citizens must decide it.

**40** There is a danger that the government will accuse us of a riot because of today. We have no reason for this disorder. We cannot explain this crowd."

**41** After he said these things, he sent the people away.

## Chapter 20

**1** The trouble stopped. Then Paul sent for the disciples and encouraged them. He said goodbye and left for Macedonia.

**2** He went through those areas and encouraged the believers with many words. Then he came to Greece.

**3** He stayed there for 3 months. He was ready to sail to Syria. But the Jews made a plan against him. So he decided to go back through Macedonia.

**4** Some men went with Paul. They were Sopater from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe and Timothy also went. Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia also went.

**5** These men went before us and waited for us in Troas.

**6** After the Festival of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi. After 5 days we joined them in Troas. We stayed there for 7 days.

**7** On the first day of the week, the disciples met to break bread. Paul spoke to them. He wanted to leave on the next day. So he continued to speak until midnight.

**8** There were many lamps in the room upstairs where they met.

**9** A young man with the name Eutychus sat in a window. Paul spoke for a long time, and Eutychus became very sleepy. He fell asleep and fell from the third floor to the ground. The people picked him up, and he was dead.

**10** Paul went down and lay on the young man. He held him and said, "Do not worry. He is alive."

**11** Paul went upstairs again. He broke the bread and ate. He talked with them for a long time, until the sun came up. Then he left.

**12** The people took the young man home alive. They were very comforted.

**13** We went to the ship before Paul and sailed to Assos. We planned to get Paul there. Paul told us to do this because he wanted to walk to Assos.

**14** Paul met us in Assos. We took him on the ship and went to Mitylene.

**15** We sailed from there and on the next day arrived near Chios. On the day after that, we went to Samos. On the next day, we came to Miletus.

**16** Paul decided not to stop at Ephesus. He did not want to use much time in Asia. He went quickly because he wanted to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost, if possible.

**17** From Miletus, Paul sent a message to Ephesus. He asked the elders of the church to come to him.

**18** The elders came to him. Paul said to them, "You know how I lived among you all the time. I lived this way from the first day that I came to Asia.

**19** I served the Lord humbly. I cried many times. I had many troubles because the Jews made plans against me.

**20** You know that I told you all things that can help you. I taught you in public and in your houses.

**21** I told Jews and Greeks that they must turn to God and repent. I told them that they must believe in our Lord Jesus.

**22** And now the Spirit makes me go to Jerusalem. I do not know what will occur to me there.

**23** I only know that the Holy Spirit warns me in every city. The Spirit tells me that prison and troubles wait for me.

**24** But my life is not important to me. I only want to complete my work with joy. I want to complete the work that the Lord Jesus gave me. This work is to tell the good news about the grace of God.

**25** I went among you all and preached the kingdom of God. Now I know that you will never see me again.

**26** So today I tell you this: I am not guilty of the blood of any person.

**27** I did not stop. I told you all that God wants you to know.

**28** Be careful about yourselves and all the believers. The Holy Spirit made you leaders of these people. Take care of the church of God, as shepherds take care of sheep. God bought the church with his own blood.

**29** I know that after I leave, bad people will come among you. They will be like fierce wolves. They will not leave the believers alone.

**30** Even some men from your own group will become bad. They will teach false things. They will try to make the disciples follow them.

**31** So be careful! Remember that for 3 years I warned each of you, night and day. I warned you with tears.

**32** Now, brothers, I give you to the care of God and to the message of his grace. This message can make you strong. It can give you a share of the blessings with all the holy people of God.

**33** I did not want the silver, gold or clothes of any person.

**34** You know that I worked with my own hands. I got the things that I needed and the things that my friends needed.

**35** In all things I showed you that you must work hard and help the weak people. Remember the words of the Lord Jesus. He said, 'It is better to give than to receive.'"

**36** After Paul said these things, he kneeled down with all of them and prayed.

**37** They all cried very much. They put their arms around Paul and kissed him.

**38** They were very sad because Paul said that they will never see him again. Then they went with him to the ship.

## Chapter 21

**1** We left the elders and sailed directly to Cos. On the next day we went to Rhodes. From there we went to Patara.

**2** We found a ship that went to Phoenicia. We went on the ship and sailed.

**3** We saw Cyprus on our left side and sailed past it to Syria. We arrived at Tyre because the ship had to unload its cargo there.

**4** We found the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them for 7 days. Through the Spirit, the disciples told Paul not to go to Jerusalem.

**5** At the end of the 7 days, we left and continued our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, went with us out of the city. We all kneeled on the beach and prayed.

**6** We said goodbye to each other. Then we went on the ship, and the disciples went back to their homes.

**7** We continued our journey from Tyre and arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers there and stayed with them for 1 day.

**8** On the next day we left and went to Caesarea. We went to the house of Philip the evangelist and stayed with him. He was one of the 7 helpers.

**9** Philip had 4 daughters. They were virgins. They prophesied.

**10** We stayed there for many days. Then a prophet with the name Agabus came from Judea.

**11** Agabus came to us and took the belt of Paul. He tied his own feet and hands with it. He said, "The Holy Spirit says this: 'The Jews in Jerusalem will tie up the owner of this belt in this way. Then they will give him to the Gentiles.'"

**12** We and the people of that place heard this. We asked Paul not to go to Jerusalem.

**13** But Paul answered, "Why do you cry and make me sad? I am ready to go to prison for the name of the Lord Jesus. I am also ready to die in Jerusalem for him."

**14** We could not change his mind. So we stopped and said, "We want the Lord to do what he wants."

**15** After this, we prepared and went to Jerusalem.

**16** Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us. They took us to the house of Mnason. We stayed with him. He was from Cyprus and was one of the first disciples.

**17** We arrived in Jerusalem, and the brothers were happy to receive us.

**18** On the next day, Paul went with us to visit James. All the elders were there.

**19** Paul greeted them. Then he told them all that God did among the Gentiles through his work. He told them each thing.

**20** The elders heard this and praised God. Then they said to Paul, "Brother, you see that many thousands of Jews believe. They all obey the law with much enthusiasm.

**21** They heard reports about you. People say that you teach the Jews who live among the Gentiles to leave the law of Moses. They say that you tell the Jews not to circumcise their children. They also say that you tell the Jews not to obey our customs.

**22** What must we do? The believers will hear that you came.

**23** So do what we tell you. 4 men among us made a promise to God.

**24** Take these men and do the purification ceremony with them. Pay the cost for them so that they can shave their heads. Then all the people will know that the reports about you are not true. They will know that you also obey the law.

**25** About the Gentile believers, we wrote a letter to them. We told them that they must not eat food that people gave to idols. They must not eat blood or the meat of animals that people choked to death. They must not commit sexual sin."

**26** On the next day, Paul took the men and did the purification ceremony with them. Then he went into the temple. He told the priests the day when the time of purification will end. On that day, the priests will make an offering for each of the men.

**27** The 7 days were almost at an end. Some Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They made all the crowd angry and took hold of Paul.

**28** They shouted, "Men of Israel, help us! This man teaches all people everywhere against our people, our law and this temple. Also, he brought Greeks into the temple. He made this holy place unclean!"

**29** They said this because they saw Trophimus from Ephesus with Paul in the city before. They thought that Paul took Trophimus into the temple.

**30** All the city became very angry. The people ran together and took Paul. They pulled him out of the temple. Immediately the temple gates closed.

**31** The people tried to kill Paul. Then the commander of the Roman soldiers heard that there was a riot in all of Jerusalem.

**32** Immediately the commander took soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. The people saw the commander and the soldiers. Then the people did not hit Paul any more.

**33** The commander came to Paul and arrested him. He told the soldiers to put 2 chains on Paul. Then he asked, "Who is this man? What did he do?"

**34** Some people in the crowd shouted one thing, and other people shouted a different thing. The commander could not learn the truth because of the noise. So he told the soldiers to take Paul into the fortress.

**35** Paul came to the stairs. The crowd was very violent, so the soldiers had to carry Paul.

**36** The crowd followed and shouted, "Kill him!"

**37** The soldiers were ready to take Paul into the fortress. Paul said to the commander, "Can I say something to you?" The commander said, "Can you speak Greek?

**38** I think that you are the man from Egypt. Some time ago, you started a revolt. You led 4,000 terrorists into the desert."

**39** Paul said, "I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia. I am a citizen of an important city. Please let me speak to the people."

**40** The commander gave his permission. Paul stood on the stairs and moved his hand to the people. They became very quiet. Paul spoke to them in the Hebrew language. He said,

## Chapter 22

**1** "Brothers and fathers, listen to me now. I will make my defense to you."

**2** The people heard that Paul spoke to them in the Hebrew language. So they became more quiet. Paul said,

**3** "I am a Jew. My mother gave birth to me in Tarsus in Cilicia, but I grew up in this city. Gamaliel was my teacher. He taught me carefully about the law of our ancestors. I worked hard for God, as all of you do today.

**4** I attacked the people who followed this Way. I caused some of them to die. I arrested men and women and put them in prison.

**5** The high priest and all the council of elders know that this is true. They gave me letters to the Jewish brothers in Damascus. I went there to arrest the followers of the Way. I wanted to bring them back to Jerusalem as prisoners for punishment.

**6** At about noon I came near Damascus. Suddenly a bright light from heaven shone around me.

**7** I fell to the ground. I heard a voice that said to me, 'Saul, Saul, why do you attack me?'

**8** I answered, 'Who are you, Lord?' He said to me, 'I am Jesus of Nazareth. You attack me.'

**9** The men with me saw the light and were afraid. But they did not understand the voice that spoke to me.

**10** I said, 'What must I do, Lord?' The Lord said to me, 'Get up and go into Damascus. There someone will tell you all the things that you must do.'

**11** The bright light made me blind. So the men with me held my hand and led me into Damascus.

**12** A man with the name Ananias lived there. He was devout and obeyed the law. All the Jews who lived there spoke well of him.

**13** He came to me and stood near me. He said, 'Brother Saul, see again!' At that moment, I could see, and I looked at him.

**14** Ananias said, 'The God of our ancestors chose you. You will know what he wants. You will see the Righteous One and hear his voice.

**15** You will tell all people about the things that you saw and heard.

**16** Now, do not wait. Get up and receive baptism. Call on the name of the Lord, and he will wash away your sins.'

**17** I went back to Jerusalem. One day I prayed in the temple, and I had a vision.

**18** I saw the Lord. He said to me, 'Go quickly! Leave Jerusalem immediately. The people here will not accept what you say about me.'

**19** I said, 'Lord, these people know what I did. I went to each synagogue. I put the believers in prison and beat them.

**20** When the people killed Stephen your witness, I stood there and agreed with them. I guarded the coats of the men who killed him.'

**21** The Lord said to me, 'Go. I will send you far away to the Gentiles.'"

**22** The people listened to Paul until he said this. Then they shouted, "Kill him! He must not live!"

**23** They shouted and waved their coats. They threw dust into the air.

**24** The commander told the soldiers to take Paul into the fortress. He told them to whip Paul and question him. The commander wanted to know why the people shouted against Paul.

**25** The soldiers tied Paul with straps to whip him. Paul said to the centurion who stood there, "Is it legal for you to whip a Roman citizen? I did not have a trial."

**26** The centurion heard this. He went to the commander and said, "Be careful! This man is a Roman citizen."

**27** The commander came to Paul and said, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" Paul said, "Yes."

**28** The commander said, "I paid much money to become a citizen." Paul said, "But I was a citizen from my birth."

**29** Immediately the men who wanted to question Paul went away from him. The commander was also afraid. He knew that Paul was a Roman citizen, and the commander put him in chains.

**30** The commander wanted to know why the Jews accused Paul. So on the next day he took off the chains of Paul. He told the chief priests and all the council to meet. Then he brought Paul and put him in front of them.

## Chapter 23

**1** Paul looked directly at the council. He said, "Brothers, all my life I did what I thought was right before God. I do the same today."

**2** The high priest Ananias told the men near Paul to hit him on the mouth.

**3** Then Paul said to Ananias, "God will hit you! You are a false person, like a dirty wall with white paint. You sit there and judge me by the law. But you disobey the law when you tell them to hit me!"

**4** The men near Paul said, "Do you insult the high priest of God?"

**5** Paul said, "Brothers, I did not know that he was the high priest. The Scripture says, 'Do not speak evil about a leader of your people.'"

**6** Paul knew that some men in the council were Sadducees and some were Pharisees. So he shouted in the council, "Brothers, I am a Pharisee, and my father was a Pharisee. You judge me because I hope for the resurrection of the dead!"

**7** When Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees started to argue. The council separated into 2 groups.

**8** The Sadducees say that there is no resurrection. They also say that there are no angels and no spirits. But the Pharisees believe in all these things.

**9** There was a loud noise. Some teachers of the law from the Pharisees stood up and argued strongly. They said, "We find nothing wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel spoke to him."

**10** The argument became violent. The commander was afraid that they will pull Paul into pieces. So he told the soldiers to go down and take Paul away from them. He told them to take Paul into the fortress.

**11** On the next night, the Lord stood near Paul. He said, "Be brave! You told the people in Jerusalem about me. You must also tell the people in Rome about me."

**12** In the morning, some Jews made a plan. They made a strong promise. They said, "We will not eat or drink until we kill Paul."

**13** More than 40 men made this plan.

**14** They went to the chief priests and elders. They said, "We made a strong promise. We will not eat anything until we kill Paul.

**15** Now you and the council must send a message to the commander. Ask him to bring Paul down to you. Say that you want to learn more about his case. We will be ready to kill Paul before he arrives."

**16** But the son of the sister of Paul heard about this plan. He went into the fortress and told Paul.

**17** Paul called one of the centurions and said, "Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him."

**18** So the centurion took him to the commander. The centurion said, "The prisoner Paul called me. He asked me to bring this young man to you. The young man has something to tell you."

**19** The commander held the hand of the young man and took him to a private place. He asked, "What do you want to tell me?"

**20** The young man said, "The Jews agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the council tomorrow. They will say that they want to learn more about him.

**21** But do not agree with them. More than 40 of them wait to attack Paul. They promised not to eat or drink until they kill him. Now they are ready. They only wait for you to agree."

**22** The commander let the young man go. He said, "Do not tell anyone that you told me this."

**23** Then the commander called 2 of his centurions. He said, "Prepare 200 soldiers to go to Caesarea. Also prepare 70 horsemen and 200 men with spears. Be ready to leave at 9 o'clock tonight.

**24** Get horses for Paul. Take him safely to Felix the governor."

**25** The commander wrote a letter. The letter said:

**26** "From Claudius Lysias. To the most excellent governor Felix. Greetings.

**27** The Jews took this man and wanted to kill him. But I learned that he was a Roman citizen. So I went with my soldiers and saved him.

**28** I wanted to know why they accused him. So I brought him to their council.

**29** I learned that they accused him about questions of their own law. But he did nothing that deserves death or prison.

**30** Then someone told me that the Jews made a plan to kill the man. So I immediately sent him to you. I also told his accusers to tell you their complaints against him."

**31** The soldiers obeyed their orders. During the night, they took Paul to Antipatris.

**32** On the next day, the horsemen went with Paul, and the other soldiers went back to the fortress.

**33** The horsemen arrived in Caesarea. They gave the letter to the governor and put Paul in front of him.

**34** The governor read the letter. He asked Paul, "What province are you from?" Paul said, "Cilicia."

**35** The governor said, "I will hear your case when your accusers arrive." Then he told the soldiers to guard Paul in the palace of Herod.

## Chapter 24

**1** After 5 days, Ananias the high priest went down to Caesarea. Some of the elders and a lawyer with the name Tertullus went with him. They told the governor their complaints against Paul.

**2** The soldiers brought Paul in. Tertullus started to accuse Paul. He said, "Your Excellency, we have much peace because of you. Your wise decisions made many good changes for this nation.

**3** Most excellent Felix, we always and everywhere accept these things with much thanks.

**4** But I do not want to use too much of your time. So please, be kind and listen to our short statement.

**5** We found that this man causes much trouble. He causes Jews everywhere in the world to fight against the government. He is a leader of the group of the Nazarenes.

**6** He also tried to make the temple unclean. So we arrested him. We wanted to judge him by our law.

**7** But Lysias the commander came and used much force. He took Paul away from us.

**8** Lysias told the accusers of Paul to come to you. If you question Paul, you will learn the truth about all our complaints."

**9** The Jews also agreed and said that these things were true.

**10** The governor moved his hand to tell Paul to speak. Paul said, "I know that you were a judge of this nation for many years. Thus, I am glad to make my defense to you.

**11** You can learn that only 12 days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

**12** The Jews did not find me in an argument with any person in the temple. They did not find me when I caused trouble among the people in the synagogues or in the city.

**13** They cannot prove the things that they say against me now.

**14** But I tell you this: I worship the God of our ancestors in the Way. They say that the Way is a false religion. But I believe all things in the law and in the prophets.

**15** I have the same hope in God that these men have. I hope that God will raise all the dead people, good and bad.

**16** Thus, I always try to do what is right before God and before people.

**17** After many years, I came back to Jerusalem. I brought money to help the poor people of my nation and to make offerings.

**18** Some Jews from Asia found me in the temple when I made these offerings. I did the purification ceremony. There was no crowd with me, and I did not cause trouble.

**19** Those Jews must be here in front of you. They must accuse me, if they have something against me.

**20** Or these men here must say what crime they found. They must tell you what I did wrong when I stood in front of the council.

**21** I only said one thing when I stood in front of them. I shouted, 'You judge me today because I believe in the resurrection of the dead.'"

**22** Felix knew much about the Way. He stopped the trial. He said, "When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case."

**23** Felix told the centurion to guard Paul but to give him some freedom. He told the centurion to let the friends of Paul visit him and help him.

**24** After some days, Felix came with his wife Drusilla. She was a Jew. Felix sent for Paul. He listened to Paul speak about faith in Christ Jesus.

**25** Paul spoke about righteousness, self-control and the judgment that will come. Felix became afraid. He said, "Go away for now. When I have time, I will send for you."

**26** Felix also hoped that Paul will give him money to make him free. So he sent for Paul many times and talked with him.

**27** After 2 years, Porcius Festus became governor after Felix. Felix wanted to please the Jews. So he left Paul in prison.

## Chapter 25

**1** Festus arrived in the province. After 3 days he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

**2** There the chief priests and the Jewish leaders told Festus their complaints against Paul. They asked Festus for help.

**3** They asked Festus to do something for them. They asked him to send Paul to Jerusalem. They made a plan to kill Paul on the road.

**4** But Festus answered, "Paul will stay in Caesarea. I will go back there soon.

**5** Some of your leaders can go there with me. If the man did something wrong, they can accuse him there."

**6** Festus stayed with them for more than 10 days. Then he went down to Caesarea. On the next day, he sat on the judgment seat. He told the soldiers to bring Paul in.

**7** Paul came in. The Jews who came from Jerusalem stood around him. They said many serious things against Paul. But they could not prove these things.

**8** Paul made his defense. He said, "I did nothing wrong against the law of the Jews, against the temple or against Caesar."

**9** But Festus wanted to please the Jews. So he said to Paul, "Do you want to go to Jerusalem? There I will judge you about these things."

**10** Paul said, "I stand in front of the court of Caesar. I must have my trial here. I did no wrong to the Jews. You know this very well.

**11** If I did something wrong and I deserve to die, I do not refuse to die. But if their complaints against me are not true, nobody can give me to them. I appeal to Caesar!"

**12** Festus spoke with his advisers. Then he said, "You appealed to Caesar. So you will go to Caesar!"

**13** After some days, King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.

**14** They stayed there for many days. Festus told the king about the case of Paul. Festus said, "Felix left a man here in prison.

**15** When I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews told me about him. They asked me to condemn him.

**16** I told them, 'It is not the custom of the Romans to give a man to his accusers before his trial. He must first meet his accusers face to face. He must have a chance to defend himself against their complaints.'

**17** So the accusers came here with me. I did not wait. On the next day, I sat on the judgment seat. I told the soldiers to bring the man in.

**18** The accusers stood up. But they did not accuse him of the crimes that I expected.

**19** They only had some arguments with him about their own religion. They also argued about a dead man with the name Jesus. Paul says that Jesus is alive.

**20** I did not know how to investigate these questions. So I asked Paul, 'Do you want to go to Jerusalem? There you can have a trial about these things.'

**21** But Paul asked to stay in prison until the Emperor decides his case. So I told the soldiers to guard him until I can send him to Caesar."

**22** Agrippa said to Festus, "I also want to hear this man." Festus said, "Tomorrow you will hear him."

**23** On the next day, Agrippa and Bernice came with much ceremony. They went into the hall with the military commanders and the important men of the city. Festus gave an order, and the soldiers brought Paul in.

**24** Festus said, "King Agrippa and all the men here, you see this man. All the Jewish people complained to me about him in Jerusalem and here. They shouted that he must not live.

**25** But I found that he did nothing that deserves death. He appealed to the Emperor. So I decided to send him to Rome.

**26** But I do not have clear information about him to write to the Emperor. So I brought him in front of all of you, and particularly in front of you, King Agrippa. After this investigation, I will have something to write.

**27** I think that it is not reasonable to send a prisoner and not to tell the complaints against him."

## Chapter 26

**1** Agrippa said to Paul, "You can speak for yourself." Then Paul lifted his hand and started his defense.

**2** "King Agrippa, I am happy that I can make my defense to you today. I will answer all the complaints of the Jews against me.

**3** This is very good because you know all the customs and questions of the Jews. So please, listen to me patiently.

**4** All the Jews know how I lived from the time when I was young. From the start, I lived among my own people in Jerusalem.

**5** They knew me for a long time. If they want, they can tell you that I lived as a Pharisee. The Pharisees are the most strict group of our religion.

**6** Now I am on trial because I hope in the promise that God made to our ancestors.

**7** Our 12 tribes hope to receive this promise. Thus, they serve God with much enthusiasm, day and night. King Agrippa, the Jews accuse me because of this hope.

**8** Why do you think that it is not possible for God to raise the dead?

**9** In the past, I also thought that I must do many things against the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

**10** I did these things in Jerusalem. The chief priests gave me authority, and I put many of the holy people in prison. When the people killed them, I agreed with that decision.

**11** Many times I punished the believers in all the synagogues. I tried to force them to speak against God. I was very angry with them. I went to cities in other countries to attack them.

**12** For this purpose, I went to Damascus. The chief priests gave me authority and orders.

**13** King Agrippa, at noon on the road I saw a light from heaven. The light was brighter than the sun. It shone around me and the men who traveled with me.

**14** We all fell to the ground. I heard a voice that spoke to me in the Hebrew language. The voice said, 'Saul, Saul, why do you attack me? When you fight against me, you only hurt yourself.'

**15** I said, 'Who are you, Lord?' The Lord said, 'I am Jesus. You attack me.

**16** But get up and stand on your feet. I appeared to you for this purpose: I chose you to be my servant and my witness. You will tell people what you saw today. You will also tell them what I will show you in the future.

**17** I will save you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I send you to them.

**18** You will open their eyes. You will help them turn from darkness to light. You will help them turn from the power of Satan to God. Then God will forgive their sins. They will have a place among the people that God made holy through faith in me.'

**19** So, King Agrippa, I obeyed the vision from heaven.

**20** First I preached to the people in Damascus. Then I preached in Jerusalem and in all of Judea. Then I preached to the Gentiles. I told them to repent and turn to God. I told them to do actions that show that they repented.

**21** For this reason, the Jews took hold of me in the temple and tried to kill me.

**22** But God helped me until today. So I stand here and speak to all people, important and not important. I say only the things that the prophets and Moses said will occur.

**23** They said that the Christ must suffer. They said that he will be the first to rise from the dead. He will bring the light of God to the Jews and to the Gentiles."

**24** While Paul made his defense, Festus shouted, "Paul, you are crazy! Too much study made you crazy!"

**25** But Paul said, "Most excellent Festus, I am not crazy. My words are true and reasonable.

**26** The king knows about these things, and I can speak freely to him. I am sure that he knows about all these things. These things did not occur in a secret place.

**27** King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe."

**28** Agrippa said to Paul, "Do you think that you can make me a Christian so quickly?"

**29** Paul said, "Quickly or slowly, I pray to God for you and for all the people who listen to me today. I pray that you will become as I am, but without these chains."

**30** Then the king, the governor, Bernice and all the people with them stood up.

**31** They went out of the room and talked together. They said, "This man did nothing that deserves death or prison."

**32** Agrippa said to Festus, "We can make this man free. But he appealed to Caesar."

## Chapter 27

**1** The officials decided that we must sail to Italy. They gave Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion with the name Julius. Julius was an officer in the Imperial Regiment.

**2** We went on a ship from Adramyttium. The ship was ready to sail to the ports along the coast of Asia. Then we sailed. Aristarchus, a man from Thessalonica in Macedonia, was with us.

**3** On the next day, we arrived in Sidon. Julius was kind to Paul. He let Paul go to his friends so that they could give him the things that he needed.

**4** We sailed from Sidon. The wind blew against us. So we sailed near the island of Cyprus, on the side away from the wind.

**5** We sailed across the sea near Cilicia and Pamphylia. Then we arrived at Myra in Lycia.

**6** There the centurion found a ship from Alexandria that sailed to Italy. He put us on that ship.

**7** We sailed slowly for many days. With much difficulty we arrived near Cnidus. The wind did not let us go farther. So we sailed near Crete, on the side away from the wind. We went past Salmone.

**8** We sailed along the coast of Crete with much difficulty. We came to a place with the name Fair Havens. It was near the city of Lasea.

**9** We lost much time. Sailing was now dangerous because the Day of Atonement (the Fast) was already past. So Paul warned the people on the ship.

**10** He said, "Men, I see that our journey will be dangerous. We will lose the cargo and the ship. We can also lose our lives."

**11** But the centurion believed the captain and the owner of the ship. He did not believe what Paul said.

**12** The harbor was not a good place to stay for the winter. So most of the men decided to sail again. They hoped to arrive at Phoenix and stay there for the winter. Phoenix is a harbor in Crete. It opens to the southwest and to the northwest.

**13** A gentle wind started to blow from the south. The men thought that they could do what they wanted. So they pulled up the anchor and sailed along the coast of Crete.

**14** But soon a very strong wind came down from the island. People call this wind "the Northeaster."

**15** The wind caught the ship. The ship could not sail against the wind. So we let the wind push the ship.

**16** We went past a small island with the name Cauda. The island gave us some protection from the wind. There we got control of the small boat with much difficulty.

**17** The men pulled the small boat up onto the ship. Then they put ropes under the ship to hold it together. They were afraid that the ship will hit the sandbanks near Syrtis. So they lowered the sails and let the wind push the ship.

**18** The storm hit us very strongly. On the next day, the men started to throw the cargo into the sea.

**19** On the third day, they threw the equipment of the ship into the sea with their own hands.

**20** For many days we did not see the sun or the stars. The storm continued to be very strong. At last we lost all hope that we will live.

**21** The men did not eat for a long time. Then Paul stood up among them and said, "Men, you did not listen to me. You sailed from Crete. Thus, you have this damage and loss.

**22** But now I tell you to be brave. None of you will die. We will lose only the ship.

**23** Last night an angel of God stood near me. I am his servant, and I worship him.

**24** The angel said, 'Paul, do not be afraid. You must stand in front of Caesar. God will save the lives of all the people who sail with you.'

**25** So, men, be brave! I believe God. All will occur as he told me.

**26** But the storm will push our ship onto an island."

**27** On the fourteenth night, the storm pushed us across the Adriatic Sea. At about midnight, the sailors thought that we were near land.

**28** They measured the depth of the water. It was 20 fathoms (about 37 meters) deep. After a short time, they measured it again. It was 15 fathoms (about 28 meters) deep.

**29** The sailors were afraid that the ship will hit the rocks. So they lowered 4 anchors from the back of the ship. They prayed for the morning to come.

**30** The sailors tried to escape from the ship. They lowered the small boat into the sea. They said that they wanted to lower anchors from the front of the ship.

**31** But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "If these men do not stay in the ship, you cannot live."

**32** So the soldiers cut the ropes of the small boat and let it fall into the sea.

**33** Before the morning, Paul told all the people to eat. He said, "For 14 days you waited and did not eat. You ate nothing.

**34** So I ask you to eat some food. You need food to live. None of you will lose even 1 hair from your head."

**35** After Paul said this, he took some bread. He thanked God in front of all of them. He broke the bread and started to eat.

**36** Then all the people became brave again, and they also ate some food.

**37** There were 276 people on the ship.

**38** They ate as much as they wanted. Then they threw the wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter.

**39** In the morning, the sailors did not know the land. But they saw a bay with a beach. They decided to try to sail the ship onto the beach.

**40** They cut the anchors and left them in the sea. They also untied the ropes that held the rudders. Then they lifted the front sail to the wind and moved toward the beach.

**41** But the ship hit a sandbank where 2 currents met. The front of the ship stuck in the sand and could not move. The large waves broke the back of the ship into pieces.

**42** The soldiers wanted to kill the prisoners. They did not want any prisoner to swim away and escape.

**43** But the centurion wanted to save Paul. So he did not let the soldiers do this. He told the people who could swim to jump into the sea first and go to land.

**44** He told the other people to follow on boards or on pieces of the ship. In this way, all the people arrived safely on land.

## Chapter 28

**1** We arrived safely on land. Then we learned that the name of the island was Malta.

**2** The people of the island were very kind to us. It rained and it was cold. So they made a fire and welcomed all of us.

**3** Paul got some sticks and put them on the fire. The heat caused a poisonous snake to come out. The snake bit the hand of Paul and held on.

**4** The people of the island saw the snake on his hand. They said to each other, "This man must be a murderer. He escaped from the sea, but Justice does not let him live."

**5** But Paul shook the snake off into the fire. He was not hurt.

**6** The people waited for Paul to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. They waited for a long time. But they saw that nothing bad occurred to him. So they changed their minds and said, "He is a god."

**7** Near that place there was land that the chief official of the island owned. His name was Publius. He welcomed us into his house. For 3 days he was kind to us.

**8** The father of Publius was sick in bed. He had a fever and dysentery (a disease of the intestines). Paul went to see him. Paul prayed and put his hands on him. Then Paul healed him.

**9** After this, the other sick people on the island came to Paul. He healed them too.

**10** The people gave us many gifts to honor us. When we were ready to sail, they put on the ship all the things that we needed.

**11** After 3 months, we sailed on a ship from Alexandria. The ship stayed at the island during the winter. On the front of the ship were the images of the twin gods Castor and Pollux.

**12** We arrived at Syracuse and stayed there for 3 days.

**13** From there we sailed around the coast and arrived at Rhegium. After 1 day, a wind started to blow from the south. On the next day, we arrived at Puteoli.

**14** There we found some brothers. They asked us to stay with them for 7 days. Then we went to Rome.

**15** The brothers in Rome heard about us. They came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Taverns. Paul saw them. He thanked God and became brave.

**16** We arrived in Rome. The centurion gave the prisoners to the captain of the guard. But the officials let Paul live by himself with a soldier who guarded him.

**17** After 3 days, Paul called the Jewish leaders together. When they came, he said to them, "Brothers, I did nothing against our people or against the customs of our ancestors. But the Jews in Jerusalem arrested me. They gave me to the Romans.

**18** The Romans questioned me. They wanted to let me go because I did nothing that deserves death.

**19** But the Jews spoke against this. So I had to appeal to Caesar. But I do not accuse my own nation of anything.

**20** For this reason, I asked to see you and speak with you. I wear this chain because I believe in the hope of Israel."

**21** The Jewish leaders said to Paul, "We did not receive letters about you from Judea. None of the brothers who came from there told us anything bad about you.

**22** But we want to hear what you think. We know that people everywhere speak against this group."

**23** The Jewish leaders chose a day to meet with Paul. On that day, many of them came to the house where Paul stayed. From morning until evening, Paul explained the kingdom of God to them. He used the law of Moses and the books of the prophets. He tried to make them believe in Jesus.

**24** Some of them believed the things that Paul said. But other people did not believe.

**25** They did not agree with each other, and they started to leave. Paul told them this last message: "The Holy Spirit spoke the truth to your ancestors through the prophet Isaiah. He said,

**26** 'Go to this people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but you will not understand. You will look and look, but you will not see.

**27** The hearts of this people became hard. They do not hear well with their ears. They closed their eyes. They do not want to see with their eyes or hear with their ears. They do not want to understand with their hearts. They do not want to turn to me so that I heal them.'

**28** Thus, you must know this: God sent his salvation to the Gentiles. They will listen!"

**29** After Paul said these words, the Jews left. They argued strongly among themselves.

**30** For 2 full years, Paul lived in a house that he rented. He welcomed all the people who came to see him.

**31** He preached about the kingdom of God. He taught about the Lord Jesus Christ. He spoke very boldly, and nobody stopped him.

---

# Romans

## Chapter 1

**1** I am Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ. God called me to be an apostle. God chose me to tell the gospel of God.

**2** God promised this gospel at an earlier time. He gave the promise through his prophets in the holy scriptures.

**3** The gospel is about his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. As a human, he came from the family of David.

**4** By the Spirit of holiness, God showed with power that Jesus is the Son of God. God did this when Jesus came back to life from the dead.

**5** Through Jesus, we got grace and the work of an apostle. Our work is to cause people from all nations to obey through faith. We do this for the name of Jesus.

**6** You are also among these nations. Jesus Christ called you to be his people.

**7** I write to all the people in Rome whom God loves and calls to be holy people. I ask God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ to give you grace and peace.

**8** First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you. People in all the world speak about your faith.

**9** I serve God with all my spirit when I tell the gospel of his Son. God knows that I always speak about you in my prayers.

**10** In my prayers, I ask God for a way to come to you at last. I ask that he will permit this.

**11** I want very much to see you. I want to give you a spiritual gift. This gift will make you strong.

**12** Thus, you and I can help each other. Your faith will help me, and my faith will help you.

**13** Brothers, I want you to know this. Many times I made a plan to come to you, but something always stopped me. I want to see good results among you. I saw such results among the other Gentiles.

**14** I have a duty to Greeks and to foreign people. I have a duty to wise people and to foolish people.

**15** Thus, I am ready to tell the gospel to you in Rome also.

**16** I do not feel shame about the gospel. The gospel is the power of God that saves each person who believes. It is first for the Jew, and also for the Greek.

**17** The gospel shows how God makes a person righteous. This starts with faith and ends with faith. The scripture says, "The righteous person will live by faith."

**18** God shows his anger from heaven against all the sin and evil of people. These people use their evil to hide the truth.

**19** People can know some things about God. These things are clear to them, because God showed these things to them.

**20** People cannot see the qualities of God. But since God made the world, people can see these qualities clearly in the things that he made. They see his eternal power and that he is God. Thus, people have no excuse.

**21** They knew God, but they did not honor him as God. They did not thank him. Their thoughts became useless, and their foolish minds became dark.

**22** They said that they were wise, but they became fools.

**23** God lives forever and is glorious. But they changed the glory of God for statues. These statues looked like humans who die, and like birds, animals and snakes.

**24** Thus, God let them follow the bad desires of their hearts. They did impure things, and they brought shame to their bodies with each other.

**25** They changed the truth of God for a lie. They worshipped and served the things that God made, not God himself. God is the Creator, and people must praise him forever. Amen.

**26** Thus, God let them follow their shameful desires. Their women changed the natural use of their bodies for a use that is not natural.

**27** Also, the men stopped the natural relations with women. They had a strong desire for each other. Men did shameful things with other men. They got the correct punishment in their bodies for their wrong actions.

**28** They did not think it important to know God. Thus, God let them have a bad mind. They did things that people must not do.

**29** They are full of all kinds of sin, sexual sin, evil, greed and hate. They are full of jealousy, murder, fights, lies and bad thoughts. They tell secrets about other people.

**30** They say bad things about other people. They hate God. They are rude, proud and boastful. They find new ways to do evil. They do not obey their parents.

**31** They have no sense. They do not keep their promises. They have no love and no mercy.

**32** They know the law of God. The law says that people who do these things must die. But they do these things, and they also approve of other people who do them.

## Chapter 2

**1** Thus, you have no excuse when you judge other people. When you judge another person, you also judge yourself. You do the same things that you judge.

**2** We know that God judges correctly the people who do such things.

**3** You judge the people who do such things, but you do the same things. Do you think that you will escape the judgment of God?

**4** God is very kind and patient with you. Do you think that his kindness is not important? Do you not know that God is kind to you because he wants you to repent?

**5** But your heart is hard, and you do not repent. Thus, you cause more anger of God against yourself. God will show his anger on the day when he judges correctly.

**6** God will give to each person the result of what that person did.

**7** Some people continue to do good things and look for glory, honor and life that does not end. God will give them eternal life.

**8** Other people are selfish. They do not obey the truth, but they obey evil. God will show his anger to them.

**9** Each person who does evil will have trouble and pain. This is first for the Jew, and also for the Gentile.

**10** But each person who does good will get glory, honor and peace. This is first for the Jew, and also for the Gentile.

**11** God treats all people equally.

**12** Some people sin, but they do not have the law of Moses. They will die without the law. Other people sin, and they have the law. The law will judge them.

**13** God does not make people righteous because they hear the law. God makes people righteous when they obey the law.

**14** The Gentiles do not have the law. But sometimes they do naturally what the law says. Thus, they show that they know the law, although they do not have it.

**15** They show that the law is in their hearts. Their conscience also agrees. Their thoughts sometimes say that they are guilty and sometimes say that they are not guilty.

**16** This will occur on the day when God judges the secret things of people through Jesus Christ. My gospel tells this.

**17** You say that you are a Jew. You trust in the law, and you are proud of your relation with God.

**18** You know what God wants. The law teaches you, and you know what is best.

**19** You are sure that you can lead blind people. You think that you are a light for people in the dark.

**20** You think that you can teach foolish people and children. You think that the law gives you all knowledge and truth.

**21** You teach other people, but do you not teach yourself? You say that people must not steal, but do you steal?

**22** You say that people must not commit adultery, but do you commit adultery? You hate idols, but do you steal from temples?

**23** You are proud of the law, but you disobey the law. Thus, you bring shame to God.

**24** The scripture says, "Because of you, the Gentiles say bad things about the name of God."

**25** Circumcision is of value if you obey the law. But if you disobey the law, your circumcision has no value.

**26** A man who did not receive circumcision can obey the law. Then God will think of him as a man who received circumcision.

**27** Some men did not receive circumcision, but they obey the law. These men will judge you. You have the written law and circumcision, but you disobey the law.

**28** A person is not a true Jew only because of the outside of his body. True circumcision is not only on the body.

**29** A true Jew is a Jew on the inside. True circumcision is a change in the heart. The Spirit makes this change, not the written law. Such a person gets praise from God, not from people.

## Chapter 3

**1** Then what is the advantage of a Jew? What is the value of circumcision?

**2** The advantage is large in all ways. First, God gave his words to the Jews.

**3** Some Jews did not believe. Can their unbelief stop the faithfulness of God?

**4** No! God is always true, although each human is a liar. The scripture says to God, "Your words show that you are right. When people judge you, you will win."

**5** Our evil shows clearly that God is righteous. Then what can we say? Is God wrong when he punishes us? I speak as humans speak.

**6** No! If God is wrong, then he cannot judge the world.

**7** My lie can show more clearly that God is true. Then God gets more glory. Why then does God judge me as a sinner?

**8** Some people tell lies about us. They say that we teach, "Let us do evil, so that good things can come." God will judge these people correctly.

**9** What then? Are we Jews better than other people? No! We showed that Jews and Gentiles are all under the power of sin.

**10** The scripture says, "No person is righteous, not even one.

**11** No person understands. No person looks for God.

**12** All people went away from God. All people became useless. No person does good, not even one.

**13** Their mouths are like an open grave. They use their tongues to tell lies. Their lips have poison like the poison of snakes.

**14** Their mouths are full of curses and bitter words.

**15** They go quickly to kill people.

**16** They cause damage and pain wherever they go.

**17** They do not know the way of peace.

**18** They do not respect God."

**19** We know that the law speaks to the people who are under the law. Thus, no person can make an excuse. All the world is guilty before God.

**20** No person becomes righteous before God because he obeys the law. The law only shows us what sin is.

**21** But now God shows how he makes people righteous without the law. The law and the prophets tell about this.

**22** God makes people righteous through faith in Jesus Christ. He does this for all people who believe. There is no difference between people.

**23** All people sinned, and all people fail to have the glory of God.

**24** But God makes them righteous as a free gift through his grace. He does this because Christ Jesus paid to make them free.

**25** God gave Christ as a sacrifice that takes away sin. People get this through faith in his blood. Thus, God showed that he is righteous. In the past, God was patient and did not punish sins.

**26** Now God shows that he is righteous. He is just, and he makes righteous the person who has faith in Jesus.

**27** Then can we be proud of ourselves? No! What law stops us? Is it the law of works? No! The law of faith stops us.

**28** Thus, we say that God makes a person righteous through faith. The person does not need to obey the law for this.

**29** Is God only the God of the Jews? Is he not also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is also the God of the Gentiles.

**30** There is only one God. He makes righteous the circumcised people through faith. He also makes righteous the uncircumcised people through faith.

**31** Do we then stop the law because of faith? No! We make the law strong.

## Chapter 4

**1** Then what can we say about Abraham, our human ancestor? What did he find?

**2** If Abraham became righteous because of his works, then he can be proud. But he cannot be proud before God.

**3** The scripture says, "Abraham believed God. Thus, God thought of him as righteous."

**4** When a person works, his pay is not a gift. His employer must pay him.

**5** But think about a person who does not work for it. He only believes God, who makes evil people righteous. God thinks of the faith of that person as righteousness.

**6** David also speaks about the happiness of a person whom God thinks of as righteous without works.

**7** David says, "The people whose wrong actions God forgives are happy. The people whose sins God covers are happy.

**8** The man whose sin the Lord does not count is happy."

**9** Is this happiness only for the circumcised people? Or is it also for the uncircumcised people? We say that God thought of the faith of Abraham as righteousness.

**10** When did God do this? Was it after Abraham received circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.

**11** Abraham got circumcision as a sign. It showed that God thought of him as righteous through faith before his circumcision. Thus, Abraham is the father of all people who believe but did not receive circumcision. God also thinks of them as righteous.

**12** Abraham is also the father of circumcised people. But these people must also follow the faith of Abraham. Abraham had this faith before his circumcision.

**13** God promised Abraham and his descendants, "The world will be yours." God did not give this promise through the law. He gave it through the righteousness that comes from faith.

**14** If the people who obey the law get the promise, then faith is useless. Then the promise has no value.

**15** The law causes the anger of God. But where there is no law, there is no disobedience.

**16** Thus, the promise comes through faith, and it is a gift of grace. Thus, the promise is sure for all the descendants of Abraham. It is not only for the people who have the law. It is also for the people who have the faith of Abraham. Abraham is the father of all of us.

**17** The scripture says, "I made you the father of many nations." Abraham is our father before God, whom he believed. God gives life to the dead. God speaks about things that do not exist as if they exist.

**18** Abraham had no reason to hope, but he continued to hope and believe. Thus, he became the father of many nations. God told him, "Your descendants will be very many."

**19** Abraham was almost 100 years old. He knew that his body was almost dead. He knew that Sarah could not have children. But his faith did not become weak.

**20** Abraham did not doubt the promise of God. His faith became strong, and he gave glory to God.

**21** He was sure that God can do what he promised.

**22** Thus, God thought of Abraham as righteous.

**23** The words "God thought of him as righteous" are not only for Abraham.

**24** These words are also for us. God will think of us as righteous if we believe in God. God raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.

**25** God gave Jesus to die because of our sins. God raised Jesus to life to make us righteous.

## Chapter 5

**1** God made us righteous through faith. Thus, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**2** Through Christ, we can come by faith into this grace. We stand in this grace now. We are happy because we hope for the glory of God.

**3** Also, we are happy when we have troubles. We know that troubles teach us patience.

**4** Patience makes our character strong, and a strong character gives us hope.

**5** This hope will not fail us. God gave us the Holy Spirit, and the Holy Spirit filled our hearts with the love of God.

**6** We were weak and could not help ourselves. At the correct time, Christ died for evil people.

**7** It is rare for a person to die for a righteous person. Possibly a person will dare to die for a good person.

**8** But God shows his love for us in this way. Christ died for us while we were still sinners.

**9** Now the blood of Christ made us righteous. Thus, it is much more sure that Christ will save us from the anger of God.

**10** We were enemies of God. But the death of his Son made us friends with God. Now we are his friends. Thus, it is much more sure that the life of his Son will save us.

**11** Also, we are happy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ. Through Christ, we are now friends with God.

**12** Sin came into the world through one man, Adam. Death came through sin. Thus, death came to all people, because all people sinned.

**13** Before God gave the law, sin was in the world. But when there is no law, God does not count sin.

**14** But death had power over all people from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. Death had power also over people who did not disobey a command like Adam. Adam was a picture of the one who was to come.

**15** But the gift of God is not like the sin of Adam. Many people died because of the sin of one man. But the grace of God is much greater. The gift of grace came through one man, Jesus Christ. This gift came to many people.

**16** The gift is not like the result of the sin of one man. After one sin, the judgment caused punishment. But after many sins, the free gift made people righteous.

**17** Death had power because of the sin of one man. But Jesus Christ is much greater. Some people get the large gift of grace and of righteousness. They will rule in life through the one man, Jesus Christ.

**18** One sin caused punishment for all people. In the same way, one righteous act makes all people righteous and gives them life.

**19** One man disobeyed God, and many people became sinners. In the same way, one man obeyed God, and many people will become righteous.

**20** The law came so that sin became larger. But where sin became larger, grace became much larger.

**21** Sin had power, and it caused death. In the same way, grace has power through righteousness. Grace gives eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

## Chapter 6

**1** Then what can we say? Must we continue to sin, so that grace becomes larger?

**2** No! We died to sin. Then how can we continue to live in sin?

**3** You know that all of us who received baptism into Christ Jesus received baptism into his death.

**4** When we received baptism, we shared in the death and burial of Christ. The glory of the Father raised Christ from the dead. In the same way, we also must live a new life.

**5** We share in the death of Christ. Thus, we will also share in his resurrection.

**6** We know that our old self died on the cross with Christ. Thus, the power of sin in our body is gone. We are no longer slaves to sin.

**7** A person who died is free from sin.

**8** We died with Christ. Thus, we believe that we will also live with him.

**9** We know that God raised Christ from the dead. Christ will not die again. Death has no power over him now.

**10** Christ died one time to stop the power of sin. Now he lives for God.

**11** In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to sin. But you are alive for God through Christ Jesus our Lord.

**12** Do not let sin rule in your body, which will die. Do not obey the bad desires of your body.

**13** Do not give the parts of your body to sin as tools for evil. Give yourselves to God, as people who came back to life from death. Give the parts of your body to God as tools for righteousness.

**14** Sin will not rule you. You are not under the law, but under grace.

**15** What then? Must we sin because we are not under the law, but under grace? No!

**16** You know this. When you give yourselves to obey a person, you become the slaves of that person. You can be slaves of sin, which causes death. Or you can be slaves of obedience, which causes righteousness.

**17** In the past, you were slaves of sin. But now you obey with all your heart the true message that people gave you. I thank God for this.

**18** You are free from sin. You became slaves of righteousness.

**19** I use an example from human life, because your human nature is weak. In the past, you gave the parts of your body as slaves to impure things and to evil. Now give them as slaves to righteousness. This will make you holy.

**20** When you were slaves of sin, righteousness did not control you.

**21** What result did you get from those things then? Now you feel shame about those things. The result of those things is death.

**22** But now you are free from sin, and you are slaves of God. The result is that you become holy. At the end, you will get eternal life.

**23** The payment for sin is death. But the gift of God is eternal life through Christ Jesus our Lord.

## Chapter 7

**1** Brothers, I speak to people who know the law. You know that the law has power over a person only while that person lives.

**2** For example, the law joins a married woman to her husband while he lives. But if her husband dies, the law of marriage does not hold her.

**3** If she marries another man while her husband lives, people will call her an adulteress. But if her husband dies, that law does not hold her. Then she is not an adulteress if she marries another man.

**4** My brothers, in the same way, you died to the law through the body of Christ. Now you can belong to another person. You belong to Christ, whom God raised from the dead. Thus, we can make good results for God.

**5** When our human nature controlled us, the law caused sinful desires to start in our bodies. These desires caused results that end in death.

**6** But now we are free from the law. We died to the law that held us. Thus, we serve God in the new way of the Spirit. We do not serve in the old way of the written law.

**7** What can we say then? Is the law sin? No! But without the law, I did not know what sin is. The law said, "Do not want things that belong to other people." Without this law, I did not know that such a desire is wrong.

**8** But sin used this commandment as an opportunity. Sin caused all types of wrong desires in me. Without the law, sin had no power.

**9** At one time I lived without the law. But when the commandment came, sin became alive, and I died.

**10** The commandment had the purpose to give life. But I found that the commandment caused my death.

**11** Sin used the commandment as an opportunity. Sin deceived me, and through the commandment sin killed me.

**12** Thus, the law is holy. The commandment is holy, fair and good.

**13** Then did the good thing cause my death? No! Sin caused my death. Sin used the good thing to cause my death. Thus, people can see that sin is truly sin. Through the commandment, sin shows how very bad it is.

**14** We know that the law is spiritual. But I am human, and sin controls me like a slave.

**15** I do not understand the things that I do. I do not do the things that I want to do. I do the things that I hate.

**16** I do the things that I do not want to do. Thus, I agree that the law is good.

**17** Thus, I am not the person who does these things. The sin that lives in me does them.

**18** I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my human nature. I want to do good, but I cannot do it.

**19** I do not do the good things that I want to do. I do the evil things that I do not want to do.

**20** I do the things that I do not want to do. Thus, I am not the person who does them. The sin that lives in me does them.

**21** Thus, I find this rule in me. When I want to do good, evil is there with me.

**22** In my inner self, I am happy with the law of God.

**23** But I see a different law in the parts of my body. This law fights against the law of my mind. It makes me a prisoner of the law of sin in my body.

**24** I am a very unhappy man! Who will make me free from this body, which causes death?

**25** I thank God! He makes me free through Jesus Christ our Lord. Thus, with my mind, I serve the law of God. But with my human nature, I serve the law of sin.

## Chapter 8

**1** Thus, God does not now find guilty the people who are in Christ Jesus. These people do not live by their human nature, but by the Spirit.

**2** The law of the Spirit gives life in Christ Jesus. This law made me free from the law of sin and death.

**3** The law could not save us, because our human nature made the law weak. But God did what the law could not do. He sent his own Son with a human body like the body of a sinful person. God sent him as an offering for sin. Thus, God gave the punishment for sin in the human body of Jesus.

**4** God did this so that we can obey what the law tells us to do. We do not live by our human nature, but by the Spirit.

**5** Some people live by their human nature. They think about the things that their human nature wants. Other people live by the Spirit. They think about the things that the Spirit wants.

**6** If a person lets human nature control the mind, the result is death. If a person lets the Spirit control the mind, the result is life and peace.

**7** The mind that human nature controls is an enemy of God. It does not obey the law of God. It cannot obey the law of God.

**8** Thus, people who live by their human nature cannot please God.

**9** But your human nature does not control you. The Spirit controls you, if the Spirit of God lives in you. If a person does not have the Spirit of Christ, that person does not belong to Christ.

**10** If Christ is in you, your body will die because of sin. But the Spirit gives you life because God made you righteous.

**11** God raised Jesus from the dead. If the Spirit of God lives in you, then God will also give life to your bodies, which will die. He will do this through his Spirit, who lives in you.

**12** Thus, brothers, we have a duty. But this duty is not to our human nature. We must not live by our human nature.

**13** If you live by your human nature, you will die. But through the Spirit, you can stop the evil things that your body does. If you do this, you will live.

**14** All people whom the Spirit of God leads are the sons of God.

**15** God did not give you a spirit that makes you slaves again. That spirit causes fear. God gave you the Spirit who makes you his children. Through the Spirit, we call out to God, "Abba, Father!"

**16** The Spirit himself speaks together with our spirit. He tells us that we are the children of God.

**17** If we are his children, then we will get what God promised to his children. We will get these things from God together with Christ. But we must suffer with Christ. Then we will also have glory with him.

**18** I think that our pain at this time is small. It is small when we compare it with the glory that God will show in us.

**19** All the things that God made wait with a strong desire. They wait for God to show who his sons are.

**20** God made the things that he made weak and useless. They did not choose this. God did this, but he gave hope with it.

**21** The hope is that God will make all things free from decay. All things will be free like the children of God. They will have the glory of the children of God.
